## `ArtAttack/ArtAttack.vcxproj`

_15 findings: 2 critical, 3 high, 8 medium, 2 low_

#### 1. There is no engine target: one Application project, 193 files flat in one directory, 2 filters

`ArtAttack/ArtAttack.vcxproj:29, 36, 43, 51 (and ArtAttack.vcxproj.filters:1-12)` — **critical** · `design` · confidence: certain

All four configurations set `<ConfigurationType>Application</ConfigurationType>` (lines 29, 36, 43, 51). The project emits an .exe and no .lib, so there is literally nothing another game could link against. All 193 first-party .h/.cpp files live in a single flat `ArtAttack/` directory, and `ArtAttack.vcxproj.filters` declares exactly two filters (`Common`, `Assets`) covering 6 of ~200 items — `Game.h`, `Level.h`, `Player.h`, `MattMath.h`, `weapon_consts.h` and `CollisionTools.h` are all siblings with no grouping.

The cost is already visible: `MattMathTests` cannot link the engine and instead `#include`s implementation .cpp files (MathTests.cpp:5-6 includes `..\ArtAttack\MattMath.cpp` and `EricsonMath.cpp`; CollisionToolsTests.cpp:3 includes `CollisionTools.cpp`). Only 3 of ~81 TUs are testable at all, precisely because there is no library boundary.

Every other finding in this sweep is downstream of this one: with no compilation boundary, nothing *stops* game concepts leaking into engine headers, so they all have.

**Fix:** Split into three MSBuild targets sharing a common `.props`: `MattMath` (StaticLibrary, zero deps), `ArtAttackEngine` (StaticLibrary, depends on MattMath + DirectXTK), `ArtAttackGame` (Application, depends on Engine). Mirror that on disk (see notes). The moment the engine is a static lib, a game include from an engine .cpp becomes a link/compile error instead of a silent coupling.

#### 2. The 'engine' is ConfigurationType=Application, so it can never be linked by anything - including its own tests

`ArtAttack/ArtAttack.vcxproj:29,36,43,51` — **critical** · `design` · confidence: certain

All four configurations declare <ConfigurationType>Application</ConfigurationType>. The project therefore emits no .lib, and there is no second project separating engine from game. The consequence is visible in the test project: MattMathTests/MattMathTests.vcxproj:173 declares a ProjectReference to ArtAttack.vcxproj, but because there is no library to link, MattMathTests/MathTests.cpp:5-6 does `#include "..\ArtAttack\MattMath.cpp"` and `#include "..\ArtAttack\EricsonMath.cpp"`, and MattMathTests/CollisionToolsTests.cpp:3 does `#include "..\ArtAttack\CollisionTools.cpp"`. The ProjectReference's only effect is to force a full game-EXE build before the tests run. Only 3 of the 81 translation units are reachable by tests at all, and the stated goal (a reusable 2D engine) is structurally impossible: there is nothing a second game could consume.

**Fix:** Split into three projects sharing one .props sheet: ArtAttackEngine (StaticLibrary - DeviceResources, StepTimer, MattMath, CollisionTools, ThreadPool, Partitioner, ResourceManager, SpriteSheet, State/StateContext, Drawer, ViewportManager), ArtAttackGame (Application - Level, Player, Weapon*, Projectile*, Menu*, TeamColour, collision_object_type), and Tests linking the engine lib. Delete the #include-a-.cpp hack once the lib exists.

#### 3. No <LanguageStandard> anywhere: the whole engine is stuck on /std:c++14

`ArtAttack/ArtAttack.vcxproj:86-180` — **high** · `build-config` · confidence: certain

None of the four ItemDefinitionGroup/ClCompile blocks (lines 87-98, 109-119, 130-143, 156-169) sets <LanguageStandard>, and neither does MattMathTests.vcxproj. MSVC's vcxproj default is /std:c++14, so despite the v145 toolset the codebase cannot use anything from C++17/20. This is confirmed by absence, not just by the project file: grepping all 197 first-party sources for std::optional, std::string_view, if constexpr, std::clamp, std::scoped_lock, structured bindings, and inline variables returns zero hits. It is the root enabler of several other findings here - notably that ~780 namespace-scope `const std::string`/`const Colour` objects in headers cannot be `inline constexpr`, that `std::string_view` cannot replace the stringly-typed resource keys, and that `[[nodiscard]]` is unavailable on the ~344 const getters. /Zc:__cplusplus is already passed (lines 97, 118, 142, 167), so __cplusplus reports 201402L honestly and nothing is masking the problem.

**Fix:** Add <LanguageStandard>stdcpp20</LanguageStandard> (and <LanguageStandard_C>stdc17</LanguageStandard_C>) to a shared .props sheet imported by both projects. Nothing in the codebase depends on C++14 semantics; the only C++17-ish construct in the tree today is std::size() in the vendor-supplied DeviceResources.cpp, which already compiles as an MSVC extension.

#### 4. No <LanguageStandard> in any configuration, so the whole engine compiles as C++14

`ArtAttack/ArtAttack.vcxproj:91-167` — **high** · `build-config`

All four ItemDefinitionGroup blocks set `WarningLevel=Level4`, `ConformanceMode=true` and `FloatingPointModel=Fast` (lines 91/94/96, 113/116/117, 134/139/141, 160/165/166) but none sets `<LanguageStandard>`, so MSVC v145 falls back to `/std:c++14`. Everything the platform layer needs is therefore unavailable: `std::clamp` (CameraTools.cpp:85-88 hand-rolls it via the out-param `clamp_ref` that causes the inverted-dead-zone bug), `[[fallthrough]]` (ViewportManager.cpp:183/207 fall through silently), `std::string_view` (ResolutionManager.cpp:94-121 heap-allocates up to four std::strings per lookup), `[[nodiscard]]`, `std::optional`, `inline` variables (so `viewport_consts` in ViewportManager.h:10-16 gets a dynamically-initialised copy per TU), and structured bindings.

There is also no `<TreatWarningAsError>` and no `<MultiProcessorCompilation>`, so /W4 findings such as the C4018 at DeviceResources.cpp:740 and the C4189 at Game.cpp:266 accumulate unnoticed, and 81 TUs compile serially.

**Fix:** Add `<LanguageStandard>stdcpp20</LanguageStandard>` and `<MultiProcessorCompilation>true</MultiProcessorCompilation>` in a shared `common.props` imported by all four configurations, instead of four hand-maintained copies. Turn on `<TreatWarningAsError>` once the existing /W4 backlog is cleared.

#### 5. /W4 with no TreatWarningAsError, and the test project silently compiles at /W3 with -permissive- off

`ArtAttack/ArtAttack.vcxproj:91,113,134,160` — **high** · `build-config` · confidence: certain

ArtAttack sets <WarningLevel>Level4</WarningLevel> and <ConformanceMode>true</ConformanceMode> in all four configs, but <TreatWarningAsError> appears nowhere in either project file (grep returns 0). /W4 is therefore purely advisory and warnings accumulate unnoticed - the recon sweep already identified live C4018 signed/unsigned comparisons at ArtAttack/MainMenu.cpp:50, ArtAttack/Level.cpp:386, ArtAttack/EndMenu.cpp:32, ArtAttack/MenuPage.cpp:140 and ArtAttack/ResultsMenu.cpp:266. Meanwhile MattMathTests.vcxproj:98,113,130,149 uses <WarningLevel>Level3</WarningLevel> and sets no <ConformanceMode> at all, so test code - which textually includes engine source - is checked under strictly weaker rules than the engine, and non-conforming constructs can pass the tests and fail the game build. There is also no <MultiProcessorCompilation> in either project, so all 81 TUs build serially.

**Fix:** Add <TreatWarningAsError>true</TreatWarningAsError>, <MultiProcessorCompilation>true</MultiProcessorCompilation>, ConformanceMode and WarningLevel Level4 to a shared .props. Fix the existing warnings first (they are a small, bounded list), then turn the switch on so the count can only go down.

#### 6. No LanguageStandard is set, so the project builds as C++14 and several correct fixes are unavailable

`ArtAttack/ArtAttack.vcxproj:86-180` — **medium** · `modern-cpp`

`ArtAttack.vcxproj` sets `WarningLevel` Level4, `ConformanceMode` true and `FloatingPointModel` Fast in all four configurations (:91/94/96, :113/116/117, :134/139/141, :160/165/166), but **never sets `<LanguageStandard>`** — a grep for it returns nothing. MSVC therefore falls back to `/std:c++14`.

That is not theoretical: I grepped all first-party `.cpp`/`.h` for `nodiscard`, `std::optional`, `string_view`, `if constexpr` and `[[fallthrough]]` and got **zero** hits. The codebase has never used a C++17 feature, and several of the right fixes in this module group are currently unavailable: `[[fallthrough]]` for the deliberate fall-through at GameStates.cpp:137-138, `std::optional<std::size_t>` for `check_for_pause_input`'s -1 sentinel (GameStates.cpp:348-359), `inline constexpr` for `team_colour_consts` (TeamColour.h:25-42), and `[[nodiscard]]` on the pure queries of `IGameObject`/`ICollisionGameObject`/`MovingObject`.

`TreatWarningAsError` is also set in neither project, so the /W4 warnings this code does generate (e.g. C4018 at GameStates.cpp:321) accumulate silently.

**Fix:** Add `<LanguageStandard>stdcpp20</LanguageStandard>` (or stdcpp17) to a shared `.props` sheet imported by both projects, replacing the four hand-maintained near-identical ItemDefinitionGroup blocks. Enable `TreatWarningAsError` at least for new code. Given `/fp:fast` is on everywhere, also confirm it is actually wanted — this codebase relies on float comparison helpers.

#### 7. No <LanguageStandard> is set, so the whole project silently builds as C++14 — which blocks most of the fixes above

`ArtAttack/ArtAttack.vcxproj:88-170` — **medium** · `design`

Verified: `grep LanguageStandard` over both vcxproj files returns nothing, while WarningLevel (Level4 on the engine, Level3 on the tests), FloatingPointModel (Fast, all four configs) and ConformanceMode (true) are all set explicitly. With MSVC v145 and no explicit standard, the project defaults to an old standard rather than anything current.

I am promoting this from the several candidates that mentioned it in passing because it is the blocking dependency for a large share of the other findings: inline constexpr variables (the Colour.h palette and every MattMath constant, which would eliminate the static-initialisation-order hazard), std::optional (the intersection sentinel and the six out-param overload pairs), std::clamp, std::string_view, std::variant (the Shape dispatch), and [[nodiscard]]. Also verified: TreatWarningAsError is set nowhere, so the C4244/C4018/C4505 warnings the other findings mention accumulate silently at /W4.

**Fix:** Set <LanguageStandard>stdcpp17</LanguageStandard> (or stdcpp20) in all four configurations of both projects, and enable TreatWarningAsError at least for the engine project so new narrowing and unreferenced-function warnings are caught.

#### 8. No <LanguageStandard> set, so the project builds as C++14 and every modern fix in this module is blocked

`ArtAttack/ArtAttack.vcxproj:88-170` — **medium** · `modern-cpp`

All four configurations set `<WarningLevel>Level4</WarningLevel>` and `<ConformanceMode>true</ConformanceMode>` but no `<LanguageStandard>` element appears anywhere in the file, so MSVC v145 falls back to its default (/std:c++14). `<TreatWarningAsError>` is likewise absent, which is why the C4100 unreferenced-parameter warnings in this module accumulate silently.

This single omission blocks most of the clean fixes the weapons module needs: `inline constexpr` constants (the per-TU duplication in weapon_consts.h), `std::string_view` members to make `WeaponDetails` a literal type, `std::clamp` for the two open-coded ammo clamps (Weapon.cpp:210-213, :221-224), and `[[nodiscard]]` on `WeaponBuilder::build_weapon` and `Weapon::update_and_get_projectiles` (discarding the latter silently drops the projectiles the player just fired - a plausible mistake given the name starts with `update_`).

**Fix:** Set `<LanguageStandard>stdcpp17</LanguageStandard>` (or stdcpp20) in all four configurations and turn on `<TreatWarningAsError>` so the dead-signature warnings cannot reaccumulate. Then apply `[[nodiscard]]` to the factory, `update_and_get_projectiles`, and the pure const accessors.

#### 9. No <LanguageStandard> is set, pinning the project to MSVC's C++14 default, and /W4 output is demonstrably unread

`ArtAttack/ArtAttack.vcxproj:88-170` — **medium** · `build-config`

I grepped the vcxproj: `WarningLevel>Level4` and `ConformanceMode>true` appear in all four configurations (lines 91/96, 113/117, 134/141, 160/166), but there is NO `<LanguageStandard>` element anywhere, so MSVC defaults to /std:c++14. That is why the codebase hand-rolls `MattMath::clamp` instead of `std::clamp`, cannot use `std::filesystem` for the path handling flagged elsewhere, cannot use `std::string_view` for directory_consts, cannot use `try_emplace`, and has no `[[nodiscard]]` (grep: zero hits across all first-party files).

There is also no `<TreatWarningAsError>`. The proof that /W4 output is being ignored is `GameData.cpp:142-146`, an unreachable duplicated `return` that C4702 would flag in optimised builds, sitting in committed code.

Also note both Debug configs define `_DEBUG` (lines 93, 115) and both Release configs define `NDEBUG` (138, 164) — which is what disarms every `RAPIDJSON_ASSERT` in the JSON findings above.

**Fix:** Set `<LanguageStandard>stdcpp20</LanguageStandard>` (or at minimum stdcpp17) in all four configurations, then sweep for the now-available replacements: std::clamp, std::filesystem::path, string_view constants, [[nodiscard]], try_emplace. Triage the current /W4 output once and turn on TreatWarningAsError for new code.

#### 10. No LanguageStandard is set, so the project silently builds as C++14 and the fixes several findings need are unavailable

`ArtAttack/ArtAttack.vcxproj:90-170` — **medium** · `build-config`

I grepped the vcxproj: `PlatformToolset` is `v145` and `ConformanceMode` is `true` in all four configurations, but there is no `<LanguageStandard>` element anywhere. MSVC therefore defaults to `/std:c++14`.

This is not cosmetic — it is why several natural fixes in this module are currently unavailable: `std::clamp` for the unclamped HUD bars, `std::optional<float>` for the `FLT_MIN` frame-time sentinel and the `respawn_timer`/`show_respawn_timer` pair, `inline` variables for the header constants above, `std::string_view` for asset names, and designated initialisers (C++20) for the giant defaulted constructor lists. A grep for `std::optional`, `string_view`, `if constexpr` and `std::clamp` across the first-party sources returns zero hits, so nothing depends on staying at C++14.

Also worth noting from the same file: `FloatingPointModel` is `Fast` in all four configurations, which the codebase then combines with exact float equality comparisons (`info.frame_time != FLT_MIN`, Player.cpp:66).

**Fix:** Set `<LanguageStandard>stdcpp20</LanguageStandard>` (or at minimum `stdcpp17`) in all four configurations and fix the fallout in one pass. Consider `TreatWarningAsError` for new code, since /W4 warnings are currently accumulating unread (the unused parameter in the `set_draw_rotation_by_rectangle_rotated` stub is one).

#### 11. Four hand-maintained copies of the compiler settings have visibly drifted apart

`ArtAttack/ArtAttack.vcxproj:95,140,115,164,168` — **medium** · `build-config` · confidence: certain

Lines 86-180 are four near-identical ItemDefinitionGroup blocks with no shared .props sheet (there is no .props file anywhere in the repo). They have drifted: (a) <EnableEnhancedInstructionSet>StreamingSIMDExtensions2</EnableEnhancedInstructionSet> appears at line 95 (Debug|Win32) and 140 (Release|Win32) but is absent from both x64 blocks; (b) <GuardEHContMetadata>true</GuardEHContMetadata> appears only at line 168 (Release|x64), so three of four configurations lack the hardening; (c) `WIN32` is defined in the x64 preprocessor lists at lines 115 and 164; (d) the identical AdditionalIncludeDirectories, AdditionalDependencies, Manifest DPI and /Zc:__cplusplus settings are each written out four times. The AdditionalDependencies list is also stale boilerplate - comdlg32.lib, advapi32.lib, shell32.lib and oleaut32.lib are not used by anything in this project. The project still declares ToolsVersion="14.0" (line 2) with no <VCProjectVersion>, while MattMathTests.vcxproj:22 declares <VCProjectVersion>17.0</VCProjectVersion>.

**Fix:** Create Directory.Build.props or a Common.props at the repo root holding everything the four blocks share (include dirs, warning level, conformance, /Zc:__cplusplus, /Zc:preprocessor, LanguageStandard, FloatingPointModel, MultiProcessorCompilation, TreatWarningAsError), import it from both .vcxproj files, and leave only genuinely per-config settings (Optimization, UseDebugLibraries) in the ItemDefinitionGroups. Drop ToolsVersion="14.0" and set VCProjectVersion to match the test project.

#### 12. Six source files that are 100% commented out are still compiled as part of the build

`ArtAttack/ArtAttack.vcxproj:252-254,348-350` — **medium** · `design` · confidence: certain

StructureRamp.h/.cpp, StructureRampLeft.h/.cpp and StructureRampRight.h/.cpp are listed as project items (ClInclude lines 252-254, ClCompile lines 348-350) and are in the filters file (lines 126-128, 211-213). I measured their content: the three headers have 0 non-comment non-blank lines and the three .cpp files have exactly 1 each - `#include "pch.h"`. StructureRamp.h opens with `//#ifndef STRUCTURE_RAMP_H` and every subsequent line is commented. So the build compiles three empty translation units, and the four headers among them are the only first-party headers with no include guard of any kind (because the guard is commented out too). Ramps are actually built as plain `Structure` objects with a TriangleRightAxisAligned shape in LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:144-177, so these files are not a work-in-progress that something depends on - they are abandoned.

**Fix:** Delete all six files and their vcxproj/filters entries. Git remembers them. The same applies to the ~840 lines of commented-out code elsewhere (MattMath.cpp ~254 lines, EricsonMath.cpp ~233, MattMath.h:303-352 dead Matrix/Vector templates, Player.cpp:307-335 and 391-420, Level.cpp:331-353, Main.cpp:39+).

#### 13. No asset deployment step: the built exe only runs under the VS debugger

`ArtAttack/ArtAttack.vcxproj:383-395` — **medium** · `build-config` · confidence: certain

directory_consts.h:9-13 uses relative paths `./textures/`, `./levels/`, `./fonts/`, `./save/save_data.json`, `./sounds/`. The vcxproj has no <OutDir> override, no PostBuildEvent, no <Content>/<CopyToOutputDirectory> items, and no asset ItemGroup beyond two <Image> entries (lines 386-389: directx.ico and textures\sprite_sheet_1.dds - one of the six top-level textures, and it is only there for the resource compiler). With the default OutDir the exe lands in $(SolutionDir)Debug\ or $(SolutionDir)x64\Debug\, where none of ./textures, ./levels, ./fonts, ./save or ./sounds exist. The app runs only because Visual Studio's debugger defaults the working directory to $(ProjectDir). Meanwhile the XAudio2 NuGet targets do copy xaudio2_9redist.dll next to the exe, so the output directory is half-populated and looks deployable.

**Fix:** Add a <Content Include="levels\**;textures\*.dds;fonts\*.spritefont;sounds\**"> group with <CopyToOutputDirectory>PreserveNewest</CopyToOutputDirectory>, or a PostBuildEvent robocopy. Then verify by running the exe directly from the output folder rather than F5.

#### 14. No LanguageStandard element, so the project silently builds as C++14 on toolset v145

`ArtAttack/ArtAttack.vcxproj:88-170` — **low** · `build-config`

Several candidates in this group proposed `std::optional`, `std::string_view`, `inline constexpr` and designated initialisers as fixes, all of which are unavailable. I grepped the vcxproj: `<PlatformToolset>v145</PlatformToolset>` in all four configurations, `<WarningLevel>Level4</WarningLevel>` ×4, `<ConformanceMode>true</ConformanceMode>` ×4, `<FloatingPointModel>Fast</FloatingPointModel>` ×4 — and no `<LanguageStandard>` element at all, so MSVC defaults to `/std:c++14`. There is also no `<TreatWarningAsError>`, which is why the C4189 at Player.cpp:271 and the C4062 at Player.cpp:1218 have gone unnoticed.

A 2026 toolset building a 2014 standard is leaving `optional`, `string_view`, `inline` variables, structured bindings, `if constexpr` and guaranteed copy elision on the table — several of which are the natural fix for findings above.

**Fix:** Add `<LanguageStandard>stdcpp20</LanguageStandard>` (or at minimum `stdcpp17`) to all four configurations, and turn on `<TreatWarningAsError>true</TreatWarningAsError>` once the existing /W4 backlog is cleared.

#### 15. No LanguageStandard set (defaults to C++14) and no TreatWarningAsError, so /W4 findings accumulate unseen

`ArtAttack/ArtAttack.vcxproj:91-166` — **low** · `tooling`

I grepped all four configurations. `WarningLevel` is `Level4` (lines 91, 113, 134, 160), `ConformanceMode` is `true` (96, 117, 141, 166), `FloatingPointModel` is `Fast` (94, 116, 139, 165), `PlatformToolset` is v145 (31, 38, 45, 53) — but there is **no** `LanguageStandard` element anywhere, so the compiler falls back to its default, `/std:c++14`. That blocks `[[nodiscard]]` (zero occurrences project-wide — I grepped), `inline` variables for the header constants, `std::string_view` for the parser comparisons, structured bindings, and `if constexpr` — every one of which is recommended by other findings in this review.

`TreatWarningAsError` is set nowhere, which is why the C4189 (unused `num_threads`, Level.cpp:599), C4101 (unused `e`, Level.cpp:727), C4018 (signed/unsigned at Level.cpp:386, StructurePaintable.cpp:189/191, GameStates.cpp:321) and C4100 (unused `other`, Structure.cpp:43/47) instances found in this review have survived.

`FloatingPointModel=Fast` also licenses the compiler to assume no NaN/inf, which interacts badly with the divide-by-zero in StructurePaintable.cpp:111/116 and the NaN in LevelEndInfo.cpp:115.

**Fix:** Add `<LanguageStandard>stdcpp20</LanguageStandard>` (or at least stdcpp17) to all four configurations, then enable `TreatWarningAsError` for Debug and fix the resulting list. Reconsider `/fp:fast` given the division guards this codebase does not have.

## `ArtAttack/DrawObject.h`

_8 findings: 1 critical, 3 high, 4 medium_

#### 1. Device-lost/restore destroys ResourceManager and the dt float, leaving every live drawable holding a freed pointer

`ArtAttack/DrawObject.h:36` — **critical** · `lifetime`

`DrawObject::_resource_manager` (DrawObject.h:36) and `Drawer::_resource_manager` / `Drawer::_dt` (Drawer.h:30-31) and `AnimationObject::_dt` (AnimationObject.h:49) are non-owning raw pointers captured at construction and never re-seated.

I read Game.cpp. `OnDeviceLost()` resets the sprite batches, resets `_states` (which is `CommonStates`, not the state machine) and calls `reset_all_textures/sprite_fonts/sounds`. It does NOT tear down `Game::_state` (Game.h:67, `std::unique_ptr<State>`), so the whole live object graph survives. `OnDeviceRestored()` then calls `create_device_dependent_resources()`, which at Game.cpp:238-245 does:
```cpp
this->_resource_manager = std::make_unique<ResourceManager>();  // old one destroyed
this->_dt = std::make_unique<float>(0.f);                       // old float destroyed
```
The `unique_ptr` assignments free the old objects. `GameData` is re-pointed; every already-constructed `Player`, `Visual`, `PaintTile`, `Text`, `TextDropShadow`, `InterfaceGameplay` and `DebugText` is not. The next `TextureObject::draw` → `SpriteSheetObject::get_sprite_sheet()` (SpriteSheetObject.cpp:33) dereferences freed memory, as does `Drawer::get_dt()` (Drawer.cpp:30).

The root cause is the design: nothing in `DrawObject`'s or `Drawer`'s API states that the pointer is non-owning, how long it must outlive the object, or who re-seats it. This is exactly the coupling that blocks the engine-reuse goal — every drawable holds a mutable back-pointer to a global service.

**Fix:** Short term: do not recreate `ResourceManager` and the dt float on device restore — keep the objects and only reload their GPU-side contents in place. Long term: delete `DrawObject::_resource_manager` entirely; drawables should hold resolved handles and receive whatever they need through the draw call, and frame time should be a `float` parameter to `update(float dt)` rather than a heap-allocated float whose address is threaded through ~26 headers.

#### 2. The render hierarchy is inheritance where composition belongs, and Player ends up with two complete copies of all render state

`ArtAttack/DrawObject.h:1-43` — **high** · `design`

`DrawObject` (colour/rotation/origin/effects/depth/`ResourceManager*`) → `SpriteSheetObject` (+ two name strings) → sibling leaves `TextureObject` and `AnimationObject`. These are pure state bags with no polymorphic behaviour, yet they are inherited rather than held.

The cost is visible at Player.h:63-64:
```cpp
class Player final : public MovingObject, public ICollisionGameObject,
                     public AnimationObject, public TextureObject
```
`AnimationObject` and `TextureObject` both derive `SpriteSheetObject` → `DrawObject` **non-virtually**, so every `Player` contains two independent copies of `_resource_manager`, `_colour`, `_draw_rotation`, `_origin`, `_effects`, `_layer_depth`, `_sheet_name`, `_element_name`. `Player::draw` keeps them in sync by hand — `TextureObject::set_effects(effects)` at :83 and `AnimationObject::set_effects(effects)` at :86, the same value written twice; the sheet name is set on the texture copy at :62-63 and on the animation copy at :65.

The two bases also declare `draw` overload sets with identical signatures (TextureObject.h:20-32 vs AnimationObject.h:34-46), so every call from `Player` must be explicitly qualified or it is ambiguous. Storing the non-owning `ResourceManager*` twice per player also doubles the dangling surface of the device-restore bug.

Same shape at Visual.h:8 (`IGameObject` + `TextureObject`), Projectile.h and Mh.h's menu widgets.

**Fix:** Make render state a value type held by composition: `struct Sprite { SheetHandle sheet; FrameId frame; Colour tint; Vector2F origin; float rotation; SpriteEffects effects; float depth; };` and `class SpriteAnimator { AnimationId clip; int frame; float elapsed; bool paused; };`. `Player` then *has* a `Sprite` and *has* a `SpriteAnimator` and iterates a small list of layers in `draw`. No diamond, no duplicated state, no qualified-call gymnastics, and the state becomes inspectable and serialisable.

#### 3. Including DrawObject.h drags RapidJSON, XAudio2, SoundBank and the game's level_stage enum into every renderable

`ArtAttack/DrawObject.h:1-6` — **high** · `design`

`DrawObject.h:5` includes `ResourceManager.h`. I read ResourceManager.h:1-10 — it includes `<map>`, `<string>`, `SpriteSheet.h`, `level_stage.h`, `LevelLoadedInfo.h`, `<Audio.h>` and `SoundBank.h`. And `SpriteSheet.h:6` includes `rapidjson/document.h`.

Since `DrawObject` is the root of the entire render hierarchy, every file that draws anything transitively compiles RapidJSON's document parser, the DirectXTK audio engine, the game's sound-bank type, and `level_stage` — an enum of game modes. A texture-drawing base class cannot be compiled without the game's mode list and an audio library.

The root cause is that `DrawObject` stores a `ResourceManager*` at all: every drawable holds a pointer to the god-object that also owns sounds and level metadata.

**Fix:** (1) Remove `ResourceManager*` from `DrawObject` — drawables hold resolved handles and receive what they need through the draw call, and the header dependency disappears. (2) Split `ResourceManager` along asset lines (`TextureCache`, `FontCache`, `SpriteSheetCache`, `SoundCache`, `LevelInfoCache`) behind narrow interfaces, and move JSON parsing out of `SpriteSheet.h` into a `SpriteSheetLoader.cpp` so RapidJSON never appears in a public header. Forward-declare `SpriteBatch`, `SpriteFont` and `ID3D11ShaderResourceView`.

#### 4. const accessors hand out a mutable ResourceManager*, so the entire const-marked draw path performs writes to shared containers

`ArtAttack/DrawObject.h:20` — **high** · `const-correctness`

```cpp
virtual ResourceManager* get_resource_manager() const;   // DrawObject.h:20
ResourceManager* Drawer::get_resource_manager() const;   // Drawer.h:17
```
A const member function returning a non-const pointer to a collaborator, and here it is load-bearing rather than incidental. `TextureObject::draw(...) const` (TextureObject.cpp:21-34) uses it to obtain a non-const `SpriteSheet*` and call the non-const `SpriteSheet::draw`, which does `_sprite_frames[frame_name]`. `TextObject::draw(...) const` uses it to call `ResourceManager::get_sprite_font`, which is non-const because it does `_sprite_fonts[font_name].get()`.

So every `const` marker on the draw path is a guarantee that is simply false, and it is exactly the guarantee that any future reasoning about the parallel renderer would rest on. Making these honest is a prerequisite for the threading being correct, not a tidiness exercise.

**Fix:** Make the four `ResourceManager` getters const, using `.at()`, returning `const SpriteFont*` / `const SpriteSheet*`. Then `DrawObject::get_resource_manager() const` returns `const ResourceManager*` and `_resource_manager` becomes `const ResourceManager*` in both `DrawObject` and `Drawer`.

#### 5. DrawObject declares a virtual destructor and none of the other four special members — the hierarchy is slice-prone and unmovable

`ArtAttack/DrawObject.h:10-11` — **medium** · `design`

```cpp
class DrawObject
{
public:
    virtual ~DrawObject() = default;   // :10
    DrawObject() = default;            // :11
```
Declaring the destructor suppresses the implicit move constructor and move assignment, so the whole hierarchy — `SpriteSheetObject`, `TextureObject`, `AnimationObject`, `TextObject`, `Text`, `TextDropShadow`, `Visual`, `Player` and the menu widgets — is non-movable; every apparent move silently degrades to a copy of two `std::string`s plus the rest.

Meanwhile copy construction and copy assignment stay implicitly public on a class with virtual functions and a public non-final base, so `Text& t = some_drop_shadow; t = some_text;` compiles and slices: the shadow's colour/offset/scale survive while the `Text`/`TextObject` subobject is overwritten.

`AnimationStrip` (AnimationStrip.h:6-27) has the mirror problem: implicitly copyable while handing out `&_frame_rects[i]` (AnimationStrip.cpp:34), so a copy-assignment invalidates every pointer previously returned.

Rule of five in the strictest sense — the base declares one of the five and none of the other four.

**Fix:** Apply the polymorphic-base recipe on `DrawObject` (and mirror it on `Drawer`, `SpriteSheet`, `AnimationStrip`): `virtual ~DrawObject() = default;` public, and `protected:` defaulted copy/move constructor and assignment. Protected copy/move keeps derived classes copyable while making slicing through a base reference ill-formed, and restores move semantics.

#### 6. Every class in the render hierarchy has a public defaulted constructor that produces a permanently unusable object

`ArtAttack/DrawObject.h:11` — **medium** · `design`

`DrawObject() = default` (DrawObject.h:11), `SpriteSheetObject() = default` (SpriteSheetObject.h:9), `TextureObject() = default` (TextureObject.h:9), `AnimationObject() = default` (AnimationObject.h:10), `TextObject() = default` (TextObject.h:9), `Text() = default` (Text.h:9), `TextDropShadow() = default` (TextDropShadow.h:9), `Visual() = default` (Visual.h:11), plus `PaintTileSplash() = default` (PaintTile.h:26).

All leave `DrawObject::_resource_manager == nullptr`, and `AnimationObject` additionally leaves `_dt == nullptr` and `_frame_time == 0.0f`. `DrawObject` exposes no setter for `_resource_manager` — `SpriteSheetObject` only has name setters — so such an object can never be brought into a valid state through the public or protected API. It is guaranteed to null-deref on first use: `TextureObject::draw` → `get_sprite_sheet()` → `get_resource_manager()->...` (SpriteSheetObject.cpp:33), and `AnimationObject::update` → `*this->_dt` (AnimationObject.cpp:88, reached because `_paused` defaults to false).

This is not purely theoretical plumbing. `PaintTile.h:83` declares `PaintTileSplash _splash;` by value, so every `PaintTile` passes through a state where its splash has a null `_dt`; PaintTile.cpp:25 move-assigns a real one over it in the constructor *body*, so the window is currently closed by luck rather than by construction.

Compare `Drawer`, which at least has `set_resource_manager`/`set_dt` — inconsistent, and those accept nullptr silently anyway.

**Fix:** Delete the defaulted constructors from the render hierarchy, and have `PaintTile` initialise `_splash` in its member-initialiser list rather than assigning in the body. Take the manager as `ResourceManager&` so "absent" is not representable. If a container needs default-constructibility, the container should hold `optional`/`unique_ptr`.

#### 7. Roughly 25 virtual accessors and draw overloads across the render bases, of which two are ever actually overridden

`ArtAttack/DrawObject.h:20-31` — **medium** · `design`

DrawObject.h:20-31 declares eleven `virtual` one-line accessors. SpriteSheetObject.h:19-23 adds five more. TextureObject.h:20-32 and AnimationObject.h:34-46 each declare five `virtual` `draw` overloads.

A grep for `override` on these signatures across the first-party tree finds only two: `set_colour` (Mh.h, PaintTile.h:40, Text.h:22 — and the `Text` one is the useless forwarder) and `get_resource_manager` (Weapon.h). No getter is ever overridden, and none of the ten `draw` overloads is overridden — `MTexture::draw`/`MText::draw` override `IGameObject::draw`, a different signature, and then call these qualified.

Cost: every `Player`, `Projectile`, `PaintTile`, `Structure` and menu widget carries vtable slots for accessors that return a float, and the per-sprite draw path makes indirect calls the optimiser cannot inline — on the hot loop in `draw_player_view_level`, a per-sprite tax for zero polymorphism.

**Fix:** Strip `virtual` from all of them, keeping it only where a real override exists (and reconsider even `Weapon::get_resource_manager` — that override suggests the dependency should be a constructor parameter, not a virtual hook). Mark the pure getters `[[nodiscard]]` while you are in there.

#### 8. The origin field has no defined coordinate space, and Weapon feeds world-space values into a texture-space parameter

`ArtAttack/DrawObject.h:39` — **medium** · `correctness`

`DrawObject::_origin` is an untyped `Vector2F` shared by two draw families with different geometry. `TextureObject::draw(batch, RectangleI dest)` forwards it to `SpriteBatch::Draw(texture, RECT destination, RECT const* source, color, rotation, origin, effects, depth)`, where DirectXTK interprets `origin` in **source-texture pixels** and rescales it by the destination/source ratio. The position overload also treats it as texture pixels, multiplied by `scale`.

Callers do not know this. I read `Weapon::draw` (Weapon.cpp:36-66):
```cpp
auto draw_rectangle = RectangleF(draw_pos, this->get_details().size);
Vector2F origin = this->calculate_sprite_origin(this->get_details().size, rotation_origin::LEFT_CENTER);
...
DrawObject::set_origin(origin);
TextureObject::draw(sprite_batch, draw_rectangle, camera);
```
`get_details().size` is world units, not atlas pixels, so the pivot is wrong by the world-to-texel ratio — correct only by coincidence when the two happen to match. Same pattern in WeaponRoller.cpp.

The camera-aware overloads compound it: `TextureObject::draw(..., const Camera&)` transforms the destination rectangle (TextureObject.cpp:59-60) but leaves `_origin` untouched, so the two end up in different spaces.

The root problem is design, not arithmetic: a bare `Vector2F` on a base class, set through an untyped setter, with the unit convention documented nowhere.

**Fix:** Make the pivot explicit and typed. Store it as a normalised `Vector2F` in [0,1] of the frame and convert to texel space in the single place that calls `SpriteBatch::Draw`, or take it from `SpriteFrame::_origin` — already parsed from the atlas and currently discarded — so it is authored in texture space by construction. Remove the untyped `set_origin` from the public surface.

## `ArtAttack/EricsonMath.cpp`

_10 findings: 1 critical, 1 high, 5 medium, 3 low_

#### 1. closest_pt_point_OBB loops over 3 axes in 2D and throws on every call; zero tests

`ArtAttack/EricsonMath.cpp:769-786` — **critical** · `test-coverage` · confidence: certain

`closest_pt_point_OBB(p, b, q)` — the only OBB support routine, added with the recent RectangleRotated/OBB work — contains `for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) { float dist = Vector2F::dot(d, b.get_axis(i)); ... }`. `RectangleRotated::get_axis` (ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:4315-4327) is `if (axis==0) ... else if (axis==1) ... throw std::invalid_argument("Axis must be 0 or 1")`. The third iteration therefore throws unconditionally: the function can never return normally, for any input. It is declared in EricsonMath.h:141, has zero call sites in the engine, and has zero tests. A single test asserting the closest point on an axis-aligned OBB would have caught this on the day it was written. This is the clearest evidence that the RectangleRotated/OBB work shipped without behavioural coverage of its own primitives.

**Fix:** Change the loop bound to 2. Add a test class for the OBB primitives: closest point for a point inside the box (returns p), outside along +x axis, outside past a corner (clamps on both axes), and on a 45-degree-rotated box where the answer differs from the AABB answer.

#### 2. closest_pt_point_OBB loops over 3 axes of a 2D OBB — throws std::invalid_argument on every call

`ArtAttack/EricsonMath.cpp:769-786` — **high** · `correctness`

```cpp
for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++)
{
	float dist = Vector2F::dot(d, b.get_axis(i));
	if (dist > b.get_half_width(i)) dist = b.get_half_width(i);
	...
}
```
An unedited copy of Ericson's 3D routine. `MattMath::OBB` is `typedef RectangleRotated OBB` (MattMath.h:1136) and has exactly two axes: `RectangleRotated::get_axis` (MattMath.cpp:4315-4327) and `get_half_width` (MattMath.cpp:4340-4352) both `throw std::invalid_argument("Axis must be 0 or 1")` for any other index. The third iteration therefore throws unconditionally — the function can never return normally, for any input — and it escapes after `q` has already been partially written, leaving the caller's out-param meaningless.

Grep confirms zero callers outside EricsonMath.{h,cpp} (including MattMathTests), which is the only reason it has not fired. It is also new code, added with the recent RectangleRotated/OBB work, and sits in the public header (EricsonMath.h:141-142). The sibling `closest_pt_point_AABB` (lines 421-449) was correctly hand-unrolled to two axes, so the 3-iteration loop is a straight porting miss.

**Fix:** `i < 2`, or unroll it explicitly like closest_pt_point_AABB does and drop the throwing integer-indexed accessors in favour of the existing get_x_axis()/get_y_axis()/get_half_x_width()/get_half_y_width(). MattMathTests already compiles EricsonMath.cpp directly, so one assertion would have caught this.

#### 3. MattMath::AABB is a typedef for RectangleF, so every AABB entry point re-derives min/max and the type name lies

`ArtAttack/EricsonMath.cpp:283-296, 391-395, 421-427, 567-570, 644-648` — **medium** · `design`

`typedef MattMath::RectangleF AABB;` (MattMath.h:301). RectangleF is position+size; every Ericson routine wants min/max corners, so five functions each open with the same two lines — test_AABB_AABB (286-289), sq_dist_point_AABB (394-395), closest_pt_point_AABB (426-427), intersect_moving_AABB_AABB (567-570), test_segment_AABB (647-648).

Worse, the two names are freely interchangeable with no compiler distinction, and the header uses both for the same type in adjacent declarations: `test_AABB_AABB` takes `const RectangleF&` (EricsonMath.h:77-78) while `intersect_moving_AABB_AABB` (113-114) and `test_segment_AABB` (119-120) take `const AABB&`.

**Fix:** Make `struct AABB { Point2F min, max; }` a real type in the types layer with explicit conversions to/from RectangleF. The intersection layer then takes AABB and does no conversion; the rendering/layout layer keeps RectangleF; the conversion happens once at the boundary.

#### 4. Three unguarded divisions produce NaN for degenerate geometry, and the downstream clamps and comparisons silently swallow it

`ArtAttack/EricsonMath.cpp:729-743, 756-767, 348` — **medium** · `robustness`

1. `barycentric` (729-743): `float denom = d00 * d11 - d01 * d01; v = (...)/denom; w = (...)/denom;` — zero for any collinear or zero-area triangle. `test_point_triangle` (746-752) then evaluates `v >= 0.0f && w >= 0.0f && (v + w) <= 1.0f` on NaNs, every comparison is false, and a degenerate triangle silently claims every point is outside it. This is live: MattMath.cpp:449 `triangle_point_intersect` forwards straight to `test_point_triangle`.

2. `closest_pt_point_segment` (756-767): `t = dot(c - a, ab) / dot(ab, ab);` — a zero-length segment gives 0/0 = NaN, and the clamps `if (t < 0.0f)` / `if (t > 1.0f)` are both false for NaN, so `d` becomes (NaN, NaN). Live via MattMath.cpp:333-340 `circle_segment_intersect`, whose `distance(...) <= radius` is then false — a degenerate segment silently reports no intersection.

3. `closest_pt_point_triangle` (line 348): `float denom = 1.0f / (va + vb + vc);` — same degeneracy, no guard.

Triangles and segments come from level JSON via LevelObjectBuilder with no non-degeneracy validation, so this is reachable by editing a level file, and the failure mode is a silent hole in the world rather than a diagnostic. /fp:fast is set in all four configs, which licenses the compiler to assume no NaNs, so the "silently false" behaviour is not even reliably reproducible across optimisation levels.

**Fix:** Guard each denominator against a near-zero magnitude and return a defined fallback (degenerate triangle → not contained; zero-length segment → t = 0, d = a). Better, validate geometry at load time in LevelObjectBuilder using the `signed_2D_tri_area` already implemented at line 688, and reject with a message naming the level file and object.

#### 5. intersect_moving_AABB_AABB reports a hit when the relative velocity is zero on a separating axis

`ArtAttack/EricsonMath.cpp:535-640` — **medium** · `correctness`

The per-axis blocks are gated on `if (v.x < 0.0f)` / `if (v.x > 0.0f)` (lines 572, 586) and the y equivalents (606, 620). When a component of `v = vb - va` is exactly zero, **no separation test runs on that axis at all**. With `tfirst = 0.0f` and `tlast = 1.0f` untouched (547-548), the `tfirst > tlast` checks never fire and the function returns 1.

Concrete: `a` at x∈[0,10], `b` at x∈[100,110], overlapping in y, `va == vb` so `v = (0,0)`. The early `test_AABB_AABB` at line 540 correctly says they do not overlap; both axis blocks are skipped; the function returns 1, claiming contact over [0,1]. Two boxes moving in lockstep 90 units apart are reported as colliding.

This is a faithful transcription of a known erratum in the 3D original, preserved by the hand-unrolling. It is also the engine's only swept-collision routine and has zero callers anywhere (verified by grep, including MattMathTests) — so fast projectiles tunnel with nothing to catch them, and the one routine that would fix that is both unused and wrong.

**Fix:** Add the zero-velocity case per axis: with no relative motion, any existing separation on that axis is permanent, so `else { if (b_max.x < a_min.x || b_min.x > a_max.x) return false; }`. Then either wire the function into projectile integration or delete it so it stops looking like available functionality.

#### 6. intersect_moving_AABB_AABB: the only swept-collision routine, zero tests and zero call sites

`ArtAttack/EricsonMath.cpp:535-640` — **medium** · `test-coverage` · confidence: certain

`intersect_moving_AABB_AABB` is 105 lines of continuous-collision maths, half of it commented-out 3D source from the book (lines 551-565), returning `int` literals `0`/`1` through a `bool`. `grep -rn intersect_moving_AABB_AABB ArtAttack/` finds only its declaration (EricsonMath.h:113) and definition — it has no callers. It is also the routine that would fix the engine's tunnelling problem, since `Level::update_level_logic` currently does discrete overlap tests only. It is untested, so nobody can tell whether it works well enough to adopt. Similarly untested and unreachable from the tests: `barycentric`, `test_point_triangle`, `sq_dist_point_AABB`, `test_circle_circle`, `EricsonMath::clamp`, and the 2-arg overloads of `rectangle_circle_intersect`, `circle_triangle_intersect`, `circle_segment_intersect` (only the 3-arg out-param versions are exercised), plus `circle_point_intersect` and `triangle_point_intersect` which have no coverage at all.

**Fix:** Either test it (two boxes approaching head-on: assert tfirst; two boxes moving apart: assert false; already-overlapping: assert tfirst==tlast==0) and wire it into the projectile path, or delete it. Dead untested code in a collision library is a liability either way.

#### 7. closest_pt_point_OBB loops over three axes of a 2D OBB, so get_axis(2) throws on every call

`ArtAttack/EricsonMath.cpp:769-786` — **medium** · `correctness`

Merges 2 candidates. `for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) { float dist = Vector2F::dot(d, b.get_axis(i)); ... }` -- `OBB` is a typedef for `MattMath::RectangleRotated` (MattMath.h:1136), which is 2D. `RectangleRotated::get_axis` (MattMath.cpp:4315-4327) and `get_half_width` (4340-4352) accept only 0 and 1 and otherwise `throw std::invalid_argument("Axis must be 0 or 1")`. The third iteration therefore always throws; the function cannot complete for any input. A straight port of Ericson's 3D routine with the loop bound left at 3. Grep confirms it has no callers (only the declaration at EricsonMath.h:141), so this is a landmine rather than a live bug -- but it is the natural building block for the OBB collision response the recent work is heading towards.

**Fix:** Change the bound to `i < 2`. Better, unroll the two axes using `get_x_axis`/`get_y_axis` and `get_half_x_width`/`get_half_y_width` and delete the throwing integer-indexed accessors. Add a test -- MathTests.cpp covers neither.

#### 8. Roughly 40% of the EricsonMath module is commented-out dead code, including a competing type system

`ArtAttack/EricsonMath.cpp:1-281, 451-479, 494-530, 551-565` — **low** · `design`

EricsonMath.h lines 13-74 are a commented-out parallel math library — `struct Vector`, `typedef Vector Point`, `struct AABB`, `struct Sphere`, `struct OBB`, plus eleven commented declarations. EricsonMath.cpp lines 1-281 are one contiguous commented block, with further blocks at 451-479 (a duplicate sq_dist_point_AABB), 494-530 (test_triangle_AABB, which contains literal `...` and could never have compiled) and 551-565 (the 3-axis loop that lines 572-638 replace by hand). The trailing `// 132` at line 788 is a page number from the book.

This is not just untidiness: a reader opening the intersection module sees two definitions of AABB (a commented struct here, a live typedef in MattMath.h:301) and two Vector types, and has to work out which is real. The commented 3-axis loop at 551-565 is also the template that produced the still-live `i < 3` bug in closest_pt_point_OBB.

On top of that, four declared functions have zero callers anywhere including MattMathTests: test_circle_circle (which uses the correct squared-distance form, while the live MattMath::circles_intersect uses a sqrt), intersect_moving_AABB_AABB, clamp, closest_pt_point_OBB.

**Fix:** Delete the commented blocks — git is the archive. Delete the four unreferenced functions, or fix and test them. If intersect_moving_AABB_AABB is kept, note its x and y blocks (572-604, 606-638) are the same 30 lines with .x/.y swapped.

#### 9. bool-returning functions return integer literals 0 and 1 throughout

`ArtAttack/EricsonMath.cpp:292-295, 541, 575, 589, 603, 623, 637, 639, 657, 659, 680, 683, 720, 724` — **low** · `modern-cpp`

The signatures were modernised to `bool` but the bodies kept the book's C-style int returns — e.g. test_AABB_AABB ends `if (...) return 0; if (...) return 0; return 1;` (292-295). Every site listed above does the same. This survives /W4 silently and reads as if the functions still return counts. Line 541 compounds it: `tfirst = tlast = 0.0f; return 1;` — chained assignment plus int return in one statement.

**Fix:** Mechanical replace with `false`/`true` across the file.

#### 10. CONFIRMED - closest_pt_point_OBB iterates 3 axes on a 2D OBB and throws on i==2, but it has zero callers

`ArtAttack/EricsonMath.cpp:769-786` — **low** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

```
for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++)
{
    float dist = Vector2F::dot(d, b.get_axis(i));
    ...
}
```
`OBB` is `typedef RectangleRotated OBB` (MattMath.h:1136), a 2D type. `RectangleRotated::get_axis` (MattMath.cpp:4315-4327) handles axis 0 and 1 and then `throw std::invalid_argument("Axis must be 0 or 1");`. `get_half_width` (4340-4352) is identical. So the third loop iteration throws at line 779 unconditionally. The loop bound is an un-adapted copy from Ericson's 3D original (the book's version is `for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++)` over a 3D OBB). CONFIRMED.

Reachability: DEAD, and the function is dead everywhere including tests. Repo-wide grep for `closest_pt_point_OBB` returns exactly two hits — the declaration (EricsonMath.h:141) and the definition (EricsonMath.cpp:769). No call site in ArtAttack/ and none in MattMathTests/MathTests.cpp.

To answer the broader question: EricsonMath as a whole is NOT dead. MattMath.cpp calls into it live — `test_AABB_AABB` (MattMath.cpp:179), `test_circle_AABB` (:185, :190), `test_segment_AABB` (:249), `test_circle_triangle` (:308, :315), `closest_pt_point_segment` (:336), `test_point_triangle` (:449), `test_2D_segment_segment` (:572) — all on the live `Shape::intersects` path used by every `is_colliding`. It is only `closest_pt_point_OBB` (and the ~233 lines of commented-out code around it) that never runs.

**Fix:** Change the bound to 2, or better delete the function until something needs it. While in this file: EricsonMath.h is roughly 50% commented-out declarations (lines 13-73, 102-111) and EricsonMath.cpp ~233 lines of commented-out bodies. Delete them; git has them. A dead function that throws is worse than no function, because a future caller gets a runtime abort instead of a compile error.

## `ArtAttack/Game.cpp`

_26 findings: 5 critical, 11 high, 7 medium, 3 low_

#### 1. Device restore rebuilds SpriteBatches on the 16 deferred contexts of the destroyed device

`ArtAttack/Game.cpp:282-287, 52, 229` — **critical** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

`create_deferred_contexts` is called exactly once, from `Game::initialize` (Game.cpp:52) — grep confirms no other call site. `DeviceResources::HandleDeviceLost` (DeviceResources.cpp:418-453) does `m_d3dContext.Reset(); ... m_d3dDevice.Reset(); m_dxgiFactory.Reset(); CreateDeviceResources(); CreateWindowSizeDependentResources();` and then calls `OnDeviceRestored`. `Game::OnDeviceRestored` (Game.cpp:282-287) calls `create_device_dependent_resources()`, which at Game.cpp:226-232 does `std::make_unique<SpriteBatch>(this->_device_resources->get_deferred_context(i))` for i in 0..15 — i.e. it builds brand-new SpriteBatches, and `_states = make_unique<CommonStates>(device)` at line 252 on the NEW device, on top of the OLD deferred contexts, which still belong to the removed device. `DeviceResources::_deferred_contexts` (DeviceResources.h:128) is never cleared or recreated on device loss.

Every frame after a restore, `Game::clear()` (Game.cpp:136-149) then does `deferred_context->OMSetRenderTargets(1, &renderTarget, nullptr)` with the NEW device's RTV on an OLD device's context, and `GameLevel::draw` (GameStates.cpp:328) / `MenuPage::draw_mobjects_in_viewports` (MenuPage.cpp:161) call `immediate_context->ExecuteCommandList(...)` on the new immediate context with command lists produced by the old device. Cross-device resource use is invalid in D3D11.

In Debug this trips the info-queue break installed at DeviceResources.cpp:238-239 (`SetBreakOnSeverity(D3D11_MESSAGE_SEVERITY_ERROR, true)`) — a hard debug break. In Release it is silent corruption: black or garbage frames for the rest of the session. This is reachable from the two normal device-loss paths, `Present` (DeviceResources.cpp:485-494) and `ResizeBuffers` (DeviceResources.cpp:290-304).

**Fix:** Move deferred-context creation into `DeviceResources::CreateDeviceResources()` (so it is redone by `HandleDeviceLost`), release the old ones first, and store them as `Microsoft::WRL::ComPtr<ID3D11DeviceContext>` so the reference is dropped when the device is torn down. Longer term, a `TryEnableDeviceLossHandling`-style test path or at least a manual `DXGIGetDebugInterface`-triggered device removal should be exercised once — this code has clearly never been run.

#### 2. OnDeviceRestored reconstructs every subsystem, turning the entire live object graph into dangling pointers

`ArtAttack/Game.cpp:218-261, 282-287` — **critical** · `resource-lifetime`

`Game::OnDeviceRestored()` (Game.cpp:282-287) unconditionally re-runs `create_device_dependent_resources()`, which is not a GPU-resource hook at all — it reassigns `_thread_pool` (:236), `_resource_manager` (:239), `_resource_loader` (:241), `_dt = std::make_unique<float>(0.f)` (:244), `_viewport_manager` (:247), `_states` (:252), `_partitioner` (:255), each assignment destroying the previous object, then republishes the new addresses into `GameData`.

Nothing in the live world re-reads GameData. Raw pointers are snapshotted once at construction: `Level.h:118 ViewportManager*`, `:119 ResourceManager*`, `:140 const float* _dt`, `:141 ID3D11SamplerState* _sampler_state` (obtained from the `CommonStates` that `OnDeviceLost` destroys at Game.cpp:276), `:146 ThreadPool*`, `:147 const Partitioner*`. Eleven headers cache `const float* _dt` (AnimationObject.h, AnimatedSprite.h, Drawer.h, LevelBuilder.h, Level.h, LevelObjectBuilder.h, PaintTile.h, Player.h, Projectile.h, StructurePaintable.h, Weapon.h). A single TDR/driver-update during gameplay therefore frees the float that every one of them reads on the next update, plus the thread pool the render path is mid-flight in.

**Fix:** Split into (a) device-dependent GPU objects recreated on restore (SpriteBatches, CommonStates, textures) and (b) device-independent services created exactly once in `initialize()` and never reassigned (ThreadPool, ResourceManager registry, ViewportManager, Partitioner, frame delta). Services that must be recreated should be repaired in place (`_resource_manager->recreate_gpu_resources(device)`) so their identity is stable, or reached through an accessor rather than a snapshotted raw pointer.

#### 3. Device-lost recovery destroys the ResourceManager, ThreadPool and dt that every live object holds by raw pointer

`ArtAttack/Game.cpp:218-287` — **critical** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

`Game::create_device_dependent_resources()` is called from two places: `Game::initialize()` (Game.cpp:54) and `Game::OnDeviceRestored()` (Game.cpp:284). It unconditionally re-creates the owning `unique_ptr` members:

```cpp
this->_resource_manager = std::make_unique<ResourceManager>();   // :239
this->_resource_loader  = std::make_unique<ResourceLoader>(...); // :241
this->_dt               = std::make_unique<float>(0.f);          // :244
this->_viewport_manager = std::make_unique<ViewportManager>(...);// :247
this->_thread_pool      = std::make_unique<ThreadPool>(...);     // :236
this->_partitioner      = std::make_unique<Partitioner>();       // :255
this->_resource_loader->load_all_resources();                    // :258
```

Every live game object captured raw pointers to the *old* instances at construction time: `Level::_sound_bank` and `_resource_manager` (Level.cpp:59), `Player::_sound_bank` (Player.cpp:44), `StructurePaintable::_sound_bank` (StructurePaintable.cpp:34), `Weapon::_sound_bank` (Weapon.cpp:33), `DrawObject::_resource_manager` on every drawable, and the `const float* _dt` threaded through ~26 headers. After a device-lost/restore (driver reset, TDR, Alt-Tab on some drivers) every one of those pointers dangles — guaranteed use-after-free on the next frame if a level is in progress.

`OnDeviceLost` (Game.cpp:269-280) also calls `reset_all_textures/sprite_fonts/sounds` on a ResourceManager that is about to be thrown away entirely, so that work is pointless, and `load_all_resources()` re-reads every DDS and JSON from disk from scratch.

**Fix:** Split device-dependent GPU resource creation from the service objects. `ResourceManager`, `ThreadPool`, `Partitioner`, `_dt` and `ViewportManager` should be created once in `initialize()` and never re-created; only the D3D objects (SpriteBatches, CommonStates, textures, SpriteFonts) should be torn down and rebuilt on device loss, with the ResourceManager re-populating its existing map entries in place so the borrowed pointers stay valid.

#### 4. OnDeviceLost/OnDeviceRestored replace every shared service, leaving all live game objects with dangling pointers

`ArtAttack/Game.cpp:269-287` — **critical** · `memory-safety` · confidence: certain

`Game::OnDeviceRestored` (Game.cpp:282-287) calls `create_device_dependent_resources()`, which does not "recreate device-dependent resources" — it reconstructs the entire service graph: `_thread_pool` (Game.cpp:236), `_resource_manager` (239), `_resource_loader` (241), `_dt = std::make_unique<float>(0.f)` (244), `_viewport_manager` (247), `_states` (252), `_partitioner` (255), each republished into `GameData` (237, 240, 243, 245, 250, 253, 256). `GameData` is only a bag of raw pointers (GameData.h:49-61); every consumer copied those pointers into its own members at construction and is never notified. Confirmed consumers: `Level::_resolution_manager/_viewport_manager/_resource_manager` (Level.h:117-119), `Level::_dt` (Level.h:140), `Level::_thread_pool/_partitioner` (Level.h:146-147), `Player::_dt` (Player.h:170). After one device restore mid-match, `Level::update` dereferences six freed objects.

Worse, the crash arrives before the restore: `Game::OnDeviceLost` (Game.cpp:277-279) calls `_resource_manager->reset_all_sounds()`, which is `sound_bank.second->reset_all_instances(); sound_bank.second.reset();` (ResourceManager.cpp:119-126) — it destroys every `SoundBank`. `Player::_sound_bank` (Player.h:168) and `Level::_sound_bank` (Level.h:107) are raw pointers into those destroyed banks, and the next `play_wave` (SoundBank.cpp:16-21) is a use-after-free. Audio is not a D3D device resource at all — tearing down sound on D3D device loss is gratuitous.

**Fix:** Split `create_device_dependent_resources` into (a) genuinely device-dependent GPU objects (SpriteBatches, CommonStates, textures/fonts) and (b) one-time services (`_dt`, thread pool, partitioner, resource manager, viewport manager) that must survive device loss; only (a) may be re-run from `OnDeviceRestored`. Stop resetting sounds on device loss. Frame time should be a `float` passed as an argument, not a heap `float*` handed out to 26 headers.

#### 5. OnDeviceRestored reallocates the shared frame-time float, dangling every const float* _dt in the engine

`ArtAttack/Game.cpp:282-287` — **critical** · `memory-safety` · confidence: certain

`Game::OnDeviceRestored()` calls `create_device_dependent_resources()`, which at ArtAttack/Game.cpp:244-245 does:

```
this->_dt = std::make_unique<float>(0.f);
this->_data->set_dt(this->_dt.get());
```

Assigning a new `unique_ptr` frees the old float. Every live object took a copy of the OLD raw pointer at construction time and keeps it forever: `Level::_dt` (ArtAttack/Level.h:140), `Player::_dt` (ArtAttack/Player.h:170), `Weapon::_dt` (ArtAttack/Weapon.h:123), `Projectile::_dt` (ArtAttack/Projectile.h:79), `PaintTile::_dt` (ArtAttack/PaintTile.h:82), `StructurePaintable::_dt` (ArtAttack/StructurePaintable.h:57), `AnimationObject::_dt` (ArtAttack/AnimationObject.h:49), `AnimatedSprite::_dt` (ArtAttack/AnimatedSprite.h:42), `Drawer::_dt` (ArtAttack/Drawer.h:31), `LevelBuilder`/`LevelObjectBuilder` (:32/:31). After a device-lost/restore (driver update, TDR, GPU hot-swap, remote-desktop transition) every `*this->_dt` read — e.g. `Player::get_dt()` ArtAttack/Player.cpp:692-694, `AnimationObject.cpp:88` — is a use-after-free that then multiplies velocities by garbage.

The same function also replaces `_thread_pool`, `_resource_manager`, `_resource_loader`, `_viewport_manager`, `_partitioner` and republishes them into `GameData`, while the live `Level` holds raw pointers to the old ones (ArtAttack/Level.h:117-119, 146-147) — so device restore during gameplay is a use-after-free across the whole object graph, not just for `_dt`.

**Fix:** Split `create_device_dependent_resources()` into genuinely device-dependent GPU objects (SpriteBatch, CommonStates, textures) and device-INdependent services (`_dt`, ThreadPool, Partitioner, ResourceManager instance) so restore only recreates the former. Better still: stop passing frame time as a heap-allocated `float*` at all — pass `float dt` down through `update(float dt)`, which removes 11 dangling-pointer members and the whole aliasing problem in one change.

#### 6. Controller polling lives inside the fixed-step update, so sampling rate is welded to 60 Hz and varies 0..6 per displayed frame

`ArtAttack/Game.cpp:75-98` — **high** · `design` · confidence: certain

```
void Game::tick()
{
    _timer.Tick([&]() { update(_timer); });
    render();
}
```

`Tick` invokes the lambda 0..6 times per call (ArtAttack/StepTimer.h:134-142), and `update()` → `StateContext::update()` is the *only* thing that ever touches the pad. Every poll site is downstream of it: `GameLevel::update` ACTIVE branch calls `_player_input->update_and_get_player_inputs()` (ArtAttack/GameStates.cpp:141-142), and every menu page calls `MenuPage::get_menu_inputs()` → `get_input()->update_and_get_menu_inputs()` (ArtAttack/MenuPage.cpp:185-188). Each of those loops `for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) get_raw_input(i)` → `_gamepad->GetState(i, ...)` (ArtAttack/PlayerInput.cpp:119-125, ArtAttack/MenuInput.cpp:131-137), so one update = 4 XInput/WGI reads, and one displayed frame = 0, 4 or up to 24 reads.

Consequences:
- The pad is sampled at exactly 60 Hz no matter the display. All edge detection is a two-sample comparison — `jump_pressed = current.jump_button && !previous.jump_button` (PlayerInput.cpp:45-48), `pause_menu = !current.pause_menu && previous.pause_menu` (:53), `proceed = prev_proceed && no_press_current` (MenuInput.cpp:40-46). A press-and-release that fits inside one 16.7 ms window is invisible to both classes — it never appears in `previous`, so the whole press is dropped. There is no latching anywhere.
- On a 120/144 Hz display `update()` runs 0 times on the majority of ticks, adding up to a full 16.7 ms of input latency on top of the pipeline, while `render()` still runs.
- During catch-up the same physical pad state is read 6 times in under a millisecond, so 100 ms of simulated gameplay is driven by one instant of input.

**Fix:** Poll input once per `tick()`, before `_timer.Tick(...)`, into a per-frame snapshot with sticky `pressed`/`released` bits that are latched on poll and cleared after the update loop has consumed them. That decouples sample rate from simulation rate, makes taps unmissable regardless of refresh, and makes catch-up steps consume the same latched edge exactly once.

#### 7. Game keeps simulating, presenting and playing audio while unfocused; while minimised it spins at unbounded frame rate

`ArtAttack/Game.cpp:75-98, 157-184` — **high** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

The message loop is `if (PeekMessage(...)) {...} else { g_game->tick(); }` (Main.cpp:213-224) with no focus/minimise gate, and `Game::tick` (Game.cpp:75-84) unconditionally runs `update` then `render`.

Alt-tab out (WM_ACTIVATEAPP, Main.cpp:329-341): `on_deactivated` (Game.cpp:165-169) suspends only the gamepad. The audio engine is untouched — `_audio_engine->Suspend()` appears only in `on_suspending` (Game.cpp:175) and the destructor (line 27) — so background music keeps playing over whatever the user switched to. `_timer` is not reset and `update()` keeps running, so `Level::_timer` (Level.h:121) keeps counting down and the match can end while the player is in another app; the gamepad being suspended just means the player cannot react.

Minimise (WM_SIZE/SIZE_MINIMIZED, Main.cpp:282-291) does call `on_suspending`, which suspends gamepad and audio — but still does not stop `tick()`. `render()` runs, and `DeviceResources::Present` (DeviceResources.cpp:456-504) calls `m_swapChain->Present(1, 0)`, which on an occluded/minimised window returns DXGI_STATUS_OCCLUDED (0x087A0001). That is a SUCCESS code, so `ThrowIfFailed(hr)` at line 497 passes silently and DXGI does not block for vsync — the minimised game busy-loops the CPU and GPU at maximum rate on a clear+present cycle that is never displayed.

**Fix:** Track a `m_suspended`/`m_minimized` flag in `Game`, skip `render()` (and optionally `update()`) while it is set, and handle DXGI_STATUS_OCCLUDED in `Present` by switching to `Present(0, DXGI_PRESENT_TEST)` until it clears. Suspend audio on deactivation too, or at least duck it.

#### 8. Audio device loss is explicitly caught and discarded: game is permanently silent after any default-device change

`ArtAttack/Game.cpp:93-97` — **high** · `robustness` · confidence: certain

if (!_audio_engine->Update())
    {
        // more about this below...
    }

The comment is copied verbatim from the DirectXTK audio tutorial, where the next paragraph tells you to write `if (_audio_engine->IsCriticalError()) { m_retryAudio = true; }` and later call `_audio_engine->Reset()`. Neither `IsCriticalError` nor any `AudioEngine::Reset` call exists anywhere in the codebase (grep over ArtAttack/ returns zero hits; the only `_audio_engine` uses are Game.cpp:27, 47, 93, 175, 182, 242).

Concrete consequence: unplug a headset, switch the default playback device, or have Windows re-enumerate the endpoint, and `AudioEngine` enters its critical-error state. `Update()` returns false forever, `AllocateVoice` starts returning null, and every `SoundBank::play_wave` (SoundBank.cpp:16-21) and `play_effect` (SoundBank.cpp:29-37) becomes a no-op. The game runs on with no sound at all until it is restarted, and never tells the user. There is also no `AudioEngine_EnvironmentalReverb`/retry path and no `AudioEngine::Update` return check anywhere else.

**Fix:** Implement the standard retry: on `!Update() && IsCriticalError()` set a retry flag, and each subsequent frame attempt `_audio_engine->Reset()`; on success, re-create the sound effect instances held by `SoundBank`. This also needs to be a documented engine-level service, not a `// more about this below...` in `Game::update`.

#### 9. clear() records into all 16 deferred contexts every frame; 12 of them are never flushed, so their command buffers grow unbounded

`ArtAttack/Game.cpp:124-152` — **high** · `performance`

`Game::clear()` loops over every deferred context and records `OMSetRenderTargets` (:136-140) and `RSSetViewports` (:146-149) into it, every frame. But only contexts `[0, partition_count)` ever get `FinishCommandList`: `Level::draw_active_level` (Level.cpp:379-399) partitions `_player_objects` (max 4) over `get_max_num_threads()` = 16, and `Partitioner::partition` caps the partition count at `num_elements` (Partitioner.cpp:10 — `i < num_partitions && i < num_elements`), so only those tasks reach `deferred_contexts->at(i)->FinishCommandList(...)` (Level.cpp:587).

A deferred context's recorded command buffer is only handed off and freed by `FinishCommandList`. Contexts 4..15 therefore accumulate two recorded commands per frame — 7,200 per minute — for the entire session, and every one is wasted since nothing executes them. In a 1-player level that is 15 of 16 contexts growing forever.

**Fix:** Do not touch deferred contexts in `clear()` at all. Bind the render target and viewport inside the recording function, on the specific context that thread is about to `FinishCommandList` (`Level::draw_player_view_level`, `MenuPage::draw_mobject_in_viewports`). `clear()` should only clear the RTV on the immediate context.

#### 10. ResetElapsedTime() exists at exactly one site; every real stall path (level load, device restore, drag) is missing it

`ArtAttack/Game.cpp:178-184` — **high** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

`_timer.ResetElapsedTime()` is called once in the entire program, in `Game::on_resuming()`. `m_qpcMaxDelta` is fixed at 1/10 s (ArtAttack/StepTimer.h:39-40 `m_qpcMaxDelta = m_qpcFrequency.QuadPart / 10`) and `m_targetElapsedTicks = SecondsToTicks(1.0/60) = 166666`, so after any stall longer than 100 ms the next `Tick()` runs exactly `1000000 / 166666 = 6` back-to-back `update()` calls (ArtAttack/StepTimer.h:132-142) with no `render()` between them, and the excess wall-clock time is silently discarded.

Paths that stall for far more than 100 ms and do NOT reset the timer:
- `GameLevel::init()` — ArtAttack/GameStates.cpp:105-127: builds `LevelBuilder`, parses the level JSON and constructs every `PaintTile`. Worse, this runs *inside* the timer's update lambda: Main.cpp:222 `tick()` → Game.cpp:77 `_timer.Tick(...)` → Game.cpp:91 `StateContext::update()` → GameStates.cpp:73-77 `GameMenu::update` → `order_level_creation()` → `StateContext::transition_to` (ArtAttack/StateContext.cpp:20-25) → `init()`. Blocking file I/O is being performed from inside `while (m_leftOverTicks >= m_targetElapsedTicks)`.
- level rebuild on restart — ArtAttack/GameStates.cpp:202-204 (`pause_menu_action::RESTART`) and :279-282 (`end_menu_action::RESTART`).
- `Game::initialize()` — ArtAttack/Game.cpp:32-66; the `StepTimer` is constructed when `Game` is (`DX::StepTimer _timer = DX::StepTimer();` ArtAttack/Game.h:60, i.e. at Main.cpp:109), then `create_device_dependent_resources()` runs `_resource_loader->load_all_resources()` (Game.cpp:258) — the entire texture/font/audio load sits between the timer's first QPC sample and the first `Tick()`.
- `Game::OnDeviceRestored()` — Game.cpp:282-287, which re-runs the full resource load.
- WM_EXITSIZEMOVE — ArtAttack/Main.cpp:309-318; the window-drag modal loop only ticks on WM_PAINT.
- `Game::on_activated()` — Game.cpp:157-163; only the minimize/power path (`on_resuming`) resets.

Observable effect: after a level loads, six 1/60 physics steps execute invisibly — collision resolution, projectile spawning, camera follow and the countdown/music start (ArtAttack/Level.cpp:65-124) all advance ~100 ms of simulated time before one pixel is drawn, driven by a single input snapshot. `Level::update_level_logic` also `throw std::exception("Player out of bounds")` (Level.cpp:312, 319) during that invisible burst.

**Fix:** Call `_timer.ResetElapsedTime()` immediately after every blocking operation: at the end of `GameLevel::init()`, after each `build_level()` call, at the end of `Game::initialize()` and `Game::OnDeviceRestored()`, and in the WM_EXITSIZEMOVE handler. Structurally, `GameData` should expose the timer (or a `request_timer_reset()` flag) so states can reset it without reaching into `Game`. Longer term, move level loading off the update thread entirely so the fixed-step loop never contains disk I/O.

#### 11. create_window_size_dependent_resources is an empty stub, so any window resize desyncs viewports from the backbuffer

`ArtAttack/Game.cpp:264-267, 197-205` — **high** · `correctness`

```
void Game::create_window_size_dependent_resources() const
{
    auto size = _device_resources->GetOutputSize();   // computed, never used
}
```
The entire body is an unused local (C4189 under /W4, silently accumulating because `TreatWarningAsError` is unset). It is called from three places (Game.cpp:57, 202, 286) and does nothing.

Meanwhile `WndProc` WM_SIZE / WM_EXITSIZEMOVE (Main.cpp:299-318) → `on_window_size_changed` → `DeviceResources::WindowSizeChanged` DOES resize the swap chain and rebuild `m_screenViewport` (DeviceResources.cpp:395-415, 381), and the windowed style is `WS_OVERLAPPEDWINDOW` so the user can resize freely down to 320x200 (`WM_GETMINMAXINFO`, Main.cpp:320-326). But nothing updates `ResolutionManager` — `set_resolution` is only ever called from Main.cpp:100 and MainMenu.cpp:324. Every viewport (`ViewportManager.cpp:19, 49, 58, 66, 87, 126`), the camera dead zone, split-screen dividers, `MenuPage::get_float_resolution` (:190-193) and `Level` (Level.cpp:90, 152, 156) still compute against the stale saved enum. After a resize the split-screen geometry is clipped off the backbuffer with no diagnostic. There are two conflicting sources of truth for 'screen size' and the empty stub makes it look like the resize path is handled.

**Fix:** Pick one authority. Either drop WS_THICKFRAME|WS_MAXIMIZEBOX so the client size cannot change behind the engine's back, or make the swap chain the authority: a Display service exposing `backbuffer_size()` plus a resize event that ViewportManager, cameras and UI subscribe to, with the resolution enum used only as an input when creating/resizing the window.

#### 12. OnDeviceRestored rebuilds ThreadPool / ResourceManager / ResourceLoader / _dt, leaving every cached raw pointer in the live scene dangling

`ArtAttack/Game.cpp:218-261, 282-287` — **high** · `lifetime`

Merged from 3 candidates. `Game::OnDeviceRestored()` (Game.cpp:282-287) just calls `create_device_dependent_resources()`, which is not a device-resource function — it unconditionally REPLACES every long-lived service:

    _thread_pool      = std::make_unique<ThreadPool>(NUM_THREADS_MIN, NUM_THREADS_MAX); // :236
    _resource_manager = std::make_unique<ResourceManager>();                            // :239
    _resource_loader  = std::make_unique<ResourceLoader>(...);                          // :241
    _dt               = std::make_unique<float>(0.f);                                   // :244
    _viewport_manager = std::make_unique<ViewportManager>(...);                         // :247
    _states           = std::make_unique<CommonStates>(device);                         // :252
    _partitioner      = std::make_unique<Partitioner>();                                // :255

Each assignment destroys the previous object. The new addresses are republished into the root `GameData`, but `OnDeviceLost` (269-280) does NOT tear down the state tree, so every live object still holds the address it cached at construction: `SoundBankObject::_resource_manager` (SoundBankObject.h:35), `Level::_sound_bank` (Level.cpp:59), and every `MenuData`-family object, which is a by-value SNAPSHOT of the 13-pointer bag taken via `GameData::GameData(const GameData*)` (GameData.cpp:4-20).

The `_dt` case is the cleanest proof: `Game::update` writes `*this->_dt = elapsedTime;` (Game.cpp:90) into the NEW float while every consumer still reads the OLD, freed one. Verified by grep: only lines 89-90, 244-245 touch `_dt`.

I graded this high rather than critical because it needs a device-lost event (TDR, driver reset, RDP session change) to trigger — but when it does, the entire scene is on freed memory.

**Fix:** Split `create_device_dependent_resources()` into a one-time `create_services()` called only from `initialize`, and a `recreate_device_resources()` called on restore that reloads GPU CONTENTS into the existing manager, preserving object identity. Independently, stop passing frame time as `float*` — pass it by value into `update(float dt)`.

#### 13. Device restore re-creates every engine service while live objects hold stale raw pointers to the old ones

`ArtAttack/Game.cpp:218-261` — **high** · `memory-safety` · confidence: certain

`Game::OnDeviceRestored()` (Game.cpp:282-287) calls `create_device_dependent_resources()` a second time. That function reallocates essentially the whole service layer and republishes it into `GameData`:

```cpp
this->_thread_pool = std::make_unique<ThreadPool>(...);      // :236  old pool freed
this->_resource_manager = std::make_unique<ResourceManager>(); // :239 old cache freed
this->_dt = std::make_unique<float>(0.f);                     // :244 old float freed
this->_viewport_manager = std::make_unique<ViewportManager>(...); // :247
this->_partitioner = std::make_unique<Partitioner>();          // :255
```

But every consumer cached a raw copy at construction time, not a handle to `GameData`. `Level` alone caches five of them (Level.h:117-119, 140, 146-147): `_viewport_manager`, `_resource_manager`, `_dt`, `_thread_pool`, `_partitioner`. `MenuData`/`GameData(const GameData*)` (GameData.cpp:4-20) takes a *snapshot copy* of all twelve pointers, so every menu page holds a second stale set. `const float* _dt` is threaded into ~26 headers (Player.h, Drawer.h, AnimationObject.h:49, ...).

After any device reset (driver update, TDR, `DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED` from `Present`, DeviceResources.cpp:485-493) the running `Level` dereferences a freed `float` every frame and calls into a freed `ThreadPool` and `ResourceManager`. Nothing in the codebase re-seeds those cached pointers.

The root cause is architectural: `GameData` (GameData.h:49-61) is a bag of 12 raw non-owning pointers used as a service locator, with no lifetime contract and no indirection through which owners can be swapped.

**Fix:** Split `create_device_dependent_resources` so that only genuinely device-dependent objects (SpriteBatches, CommonStates, textures) are recreated on restore; `_dt`, `_thread_pool`, `_partitioner`, `_resource_manager` and `_viewport_manager` must be created once in `initialize`. Better: stop passing frame time as `const float*` entirely (pass `float dt` to `update`), and hand out services as references resolved per-call from a single owner rather than cached raw pointers.

#### 14. create_window_size_dependent_resources is an empty stub, so every viewport, camera and UI layout stays pinned to the saved resolution after any resize

`ArtAttack/Game.cpp:264-267` — **high** · `design` · confidence: certain

`void Game::create_window_size_dependent_resources() const { auto size = _device_resources->GetOutputSize(); }` — the local `size` is unused (also an unreported /W4 C4189, since `TreatWarningAsError` is set nowhere). This is the only hook that fires on a resize (`Game::on_window_size_changed`, Game.cpp:197-205), so nothing outside `DeviceResources` ever learns the new size.

Everything that positions pixels reads `ResolutionManager` instead, i.e. the value loaded from save_data.json: `ViewportManager::get_fullscreen_viewport` (ViewportManager.cpp:19), all three `apply_player_viewport` overloads (ViewportManager.cpp:49, 58, 66 — note line 60/69 also feed it to `SpriteBatch::SetViewport`, so the sprite projection matrix is built from it), `get_player_viewport` (:87), `get_viewport_dividers` (:126), `MenuPage::get_float_resolution` (MenuPage.cpp:190-193), and the gameplay cameras: `Level.cpp:80-84` and `196-200` feed `CameraTools::calculate_camera` a `viewport_size` from `_viewport_manager->get_player_viewport(...)`, and `Level.cpp:150-156` builds the zoom-out camera from `_resolution_manager->get_resolution_vec()`. `get_fullscreen_d3d11_viewport()` (ViewportManager.h:43), the one function that could have been backbuffer-driven, is dead — grep shows no caller.
