Concrete first visible consequence of dragging a window corner: WM_EXITSIZEMOVE (Main.cpp:309-318) resizes the swapchain to, say, 800x600, `Game::clear` sets the correct 800x600 viewport (Game.cpp:143-149), and then the draw path immediately overrides it with `RSSetViewports` at 1920x1080 (ViewportManager.cpp:50/59). D3D clamps to the render target, so you see only the top-left 800x600 corner of the scene and the HUD/menu is mostly off-screen. Enlarge the window instead and the game renders into the top-left corner surrounded by the black clear colour. No crash, permanent wrong output.

**Fix:** Either make the render size authoritative — have `create_window_size_dependent_resources` push `GetOutputSize()` into `ResolutionManager` (renamed to something like `RenderTargetSize`) and have ViewportManager/MenuPage read that — or render to a fixed-size offscreen target at the design resolution and blit it letterboxed. Do not keep two independent notions of "the resolution".

#### 15. OnDeviceLost frees SpriteBatches and CommonStates but leaves the raw-pointer mirrors GameData published

`ArtAttack/Game.cpp:269-280` — **high** · `memory-safety`

```
void Game::OnDeviceLost()
{
    for (auto& sprite_batch : this->_sprite_batches) { sprite_batch.reset(); }
    _states.reset();
    this->_resource_manager->reset_all_textures();
    ...
}
```
It resets the 16 owning `unique_ptr<SpriteBatch>`s but never touches `_sprite_batches_ptrs` (Game.h:73), the hand-maintained parallel `std::vector<SpriteBatch*>` whose **address** was published to GameData at Game.cpp:234 and which every draw path dereferences (GameStates.cpp:317, MenuPage.cpp:129, Level.cpp:513). Same for `_states.reset()`: `GameData::_common_states` (GameData.h:58) still points at the freed `CommonStates`, and `Level::_sampler_state` (Level.h:141) still holds the `ID3D11SamplerState*` that CommonStates owned and has now released. `this->_resource_manager->reset_all_textures()` is also unguarded against a null `_resource_manager`.

The lost/restored pair is asymmetric: `OnDeviceLost` clears three things, `OnDeviceRestored` recreates ten.

**Fix:** Delete the parallel `vector<SpriteBatch*>` mirror entirely — expose `const std::vector<std::unique_ptr<SpriteBatch>>&` or build the raw view on demand — so there is no second copy to forget. Until then, clear `_sprite_batches_ptrs` and null every observer GameData published in `OnDeviceLost`.

#### 16. OnDeviceRestored rebuilds ThreadPool, Partitioner, _dt, CommonStates and ResourceManager, but the live Level keeps the old raw pointers

`ArtAttack/Game.cpp:269-287` — **high** · `memory-safety` · confidence: certain

`OnDeviceRestored` simply re-runs the full construction path:

```cpp
void Game::OnDeviceRestored()
{
    create_device_dependent_resources();   // Game.cpp:284
    create_window_size_dependent_resources();
}
```

and `create_device_dependent_resources` (Game.cpp:218-261) **replaces** objects that are already published to, and cached by, live gameplay code:

```cpp
this->_thread_pool = std::make_unique<ThreadPool>(NUM_THREADS_MIN, NUM_THREADS_MAX);  // :236 destroys the old pool
this->_data->set_thread_pool(this->_thread_pool.get());                                // :237
this->_resource_manager = std::make_unique<ResourceManager>();                          // :239
this->_dt = std::make_unique<float>(0.f);                                               // :244 old float freed
this->_viewport_manager = std::make_unique<ViewportManager>(...);                       // :247
_states = std::make_unique<CommonStates>(device);                                       // :252
this->_partitioner = std::make_unique<Partitioner>();                                   // :255
```

Republishing into `GameData` is not enough, because `Level` and the objects under it snapshot those raw pointers **once**, at construction. `GameLevel::init` (GameStates.cpp:113-120) passes `get_thread_pool()`, `get_partitioner()`, `get_dt()`, `get_resource_manager()` and `get_common_states()->PointClamp()` into `LevelBuilder`, which stores them in `Level` as `ThreadPool* _thread_pool` (Level.h:146), `const Partitioner* _partitioner` (:147), `const float* _dt` (:140), `ID3D11SamplerState* _sampler_state` (:141), `ViewportManager* _viewport_manager` (:118), `ResourceManager* _resource_manager` (:119). The same `const float* _dt` is copied into ~26 other classes (Player, Weapon, AnimationObject — see `*this->_dt` at AnimationObject.cpp:88).

So the first frame after any device reset (fullscreen alt-tab, driver TDR, GPU hot-swap, `HandleDeviceLost` at DeviceResources.cpp:493), `Level::draw_active_level` calls `this->_thread_pool->get_max_num_threads()` (Level.cpp:379) on a destroyed `ThreadPool`, `Level::get_dt()` reads a freed `float`, and `_sampler_state` points at an `ID3D11SamplerState` released by `_states.reset()` (Game.cpp:276). All four are use-after-free.

Note also that nothing drains the pool before it is replaced: line 236 destroys the old `ThreadPool` while, in principle, its callbacks could still be outstanding. `~ThreadPool` blocks (see the `CloseThreadpoolCleanupGroupMembers` finding), so it would deadlock-or-crash rather than silently corrupt, but the ordering is unguarded either way.

**Fix:** Split `create_device_dependent_resources` into (a) genuinely device-dependent GPU objects that must be recreated — SpriteBatches, CommonStates, textures — and (b) device-independent services that must NOT be — ThreadPool, Partitioner, the frame-time value, the resource *manager* (as opposed to its GPU payloads). Only (a) should run in `OnDeviceRestored`. Then stop distributing raw snapshots: pass frame time as a `float` parameter to `update(float dt)` instead of a `const float*` member, and have long-lived objects reach services through the `GameData` accessor at point of use rather than caching the pointer at construction — or, better for the reusable-engine goal, inject an interface reference whose implementation can be swapped behind the callers' backs.

#### 17. Blocking vsync Present + fixed 60 Hz update, no interpolation, no tearing option: judder on >60 Hz and full redraw of unchanged frames

`ArtAttack/Game.cpp:12-19` — **medium** · `performance` · confidence: certain

`DeviceResources` is constructed with default flags:

```
_device_resources = std::make_unique<DX::DeviceResources>(
    DXGI_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_UNORM, DXGI_FORMAT_UNKNOWN);
// TODO: ... Add DX::DeviceResources::c_AllowTearing to opt-in to variable rate displays.
```

The TODO was never actioned, so `c_AllowTearing` is off and `DeviceResources::Present()` takes the blocking branch `m_swapChain->Present(1, 0)` (ArtAttack/DeviceResources.cpp:464-470). Meanwhile `Game::render()` runs unconditionally after `Tick` (Game.cpp:82) and the simulation is pinned to 60 Hz.

Observable symptoms:
- 144 Hz display: `render()` presents 144 frames/s; `update()` runs 60 times/s, so state changes land on a 2-3-2-3 refresh pattern. Nothing interpolates between simulation states (there is no alpha anywhere; `Camera` positions come straight from `Player::get_camera()` at Level.cpp:508), so motion visibly judders — the game looks *worse* on the faster monitor.
- ~58% of those 144 frames are byte-identical redraws, yet each one still runs `clear()` re-binding RTV+viewport across all 16 deferred contexts (Game.cpp:136-149), re-partitions the players and dispatches thread-pool tasks that re-record every command list (`Level::draw_active_level` ArtAttack/Level.cpp:375-400). All of that CPU work produces no pixel change.
- Display that cannot do 60 (e.g. 50 Hz): each 20 ms tick alternates 1 and 2 update steps, so the simulation runs correct wall-clock speed but at an uneven cadence with no interpolation to hide it.
- Minimised/occluded: `Present` returns `DXGI_STATUS_OCCLUDED`, which is a SUCCESS code, so `ThrowIfFailed` passes and there is no early-out (DeviceResources.cpp:495-497). The vsync block disappears and the loop busy-spins re-rendering invisible frames at 100% of a core.

**Fix:** Three separable fixes: (1) pass `DX::DeviceResources::c_AllowTearing` and let the render rate float; (2) expose the fixed-step remainder (`m_leftOverTicks / m_targetElapsedTicks`) from `StepTimer` as an interpolation alpha and lerp camera/sprite transforms in `draw`, which is the standard fix and the one a reusable engine needs; (3) skip `render()` when no `update()` ran and the swap chain is occluded — track whether `GetFrameCount()` changed since the last present.

#### 18. Audio device loss is detected and then deliberately discarded

`ArtAttack/Game.cpp:93-96` — **medium** · `robustness`

```
if (!_audio_engine->Update())
{
    // more about this below...
}
```
The DirectXTK template's placeholder comment, never filled in. `AudioEngine::Update()` returns false when the audio graph has stopped — either a lost device or no audio device at all. The documented handling is `if (_audio_engine->IsCriticalError()) { _audio_engine->Reset(); }` to re-acquire the new default endpoint. As written, unplugging headphones or switching output device silently mutes the game for the rest of the session while `Update()` keeps being called 60 times a second on a dead engine, and the empty `if` body is compiled away.

**Fix:** Implement the standard recovery, or — if ignoring it is genuinely intended — delete the `if` and write a comment saying why. An empty conditional body reads as unfinished work. For a reusable engine, surface it as an `on_audio_device_lost()` hook.

#### 19. Window message handlers dereference _gamepad and _audio_engine unguarded, and messages arrive before initialize()

`ArtAttack/Game.cpp:157-184` — **medium** · `robustness`

`on_activated()` checks the pointer (`if (this->_gamepad)`, :161) but its three siblings do not:
```
void Game::on_deactivated() const { this->_gamepad->Suspend(); }                          // :165-169
void Game::on_suspending()  const { this->_gamepad->Suspend(); _audio_engine->Suspend(); } // :171-176
void Game::on_resuming()          { _timer.ResetElapsedTime(); _gamepad->Resume(); _audio_engine->Resume(); } // :178-184
```
The ordering makes this reachable: WM_CREATE installs the `Game*` into GWLP_USERDATA (Main.cpp:246-252) *inside* `CreateWindowExW` (:156/162), `ShowWindow` runs at :191/195 and synchronously delivers WM_ACTIVATEAPP and WM_SIZE, but `_audio_engine` is not created until `initialize` (Game.cpp:47) and `_gamepad` until :59 — and `initialize` is not called until Main.cpp:207. A WM_ACTIVATEAPP with `wParam == 0` (window created behind another app) or WM_SIZE(SIZE_MINIMIZED) during startup is an immediate null dereference. `WM_POWERBROADCAST`/PBT_APMQUERYSUSPEND (Main.cpp:343-350) has the same exposure. The lone guard in `on_activated` is evidence that this was hit once and only the branch that fired was patched.

`on_window_size_changed` survives the same window purely by luck: `WindowSizeChanged` early-returns on `!m_window` (DeviceResources.cpp:397-398).

**Fix:** Do not publish `this` to GWLP_USERDATA until the object is usable — create the window with `lpCreateParams = nullptr`, call `initialize()`, then `SetWindowLongPtr`. That eliminates the whole class of half-constructed-callback bugs rather than sprinkling null checks. Failing that, guard every handler uniformly with one `_initialized` flag.

#### 20. on_deactivated/on_suspending dereference _gamepad and _audio_engine with no null check, and WndProc routes messages to Game before initialize() runs

`ArtAttack/Game.cpp:157-184` — **medium** · `robustness` · confidence: likely

`on_activated` (Game.cpp:157-163) guards with `if (this->_gamepad)`, but `on_deactivated` (165-169) is a bare `this->_gamepad->Suspend();`, `on_suspending` (171-176) is `this->_gamepad->Suspend(); _audio_engine->Suspend();`, and `on_resuming` (178-184) is `_timer.ResetElapsedTime(); this->_gamepad->Resume(); _audio_engine->Resume();`.

The `Game*` becomes reachable from WndProc inside `CreateWindowExW` itself: WM_CREATE stores `params->lpCreateParams` in GWLP_USERDATA (Main.cpp:246-252), and CreateWindowEx then synchronously sends WM_SIZE/WM_MOVE. So from Main.cpp:156/162 onwards every message handler is live — but `_audio_engine` is not constructed until Game.cpp:47 and `_gamepad` not until Game.cpp:59, after `create_device_dependent_resources()` (line 54) has run `_resource_loader->load_all_resources()` (line 258), i.e. after all textures, fonts and sound banks have been loaded from disk. A WM_SIZE/SIZE_MINIMIZED or a deactivation delivered during that window is a null dereference. The equivalent hazard on the size path is masked only by chance, by `if (!m_window) return false;` at DeviceResources.cpp:397-398.

These three handlers are also declared `const` (Game.h:39-45) while mutating the gamepad, the audio engine and the timer through owned pointers — const that means nothing.

**Fix:** Guard all four handlers uniformly (or better, add an `_initialized` flag checked once at the top of each), and drop the meaningless `const` on handlers that change engine state.

#### 21. on_deactivated/on_suspending dereference _gamepad and _audio_engine without the null guard on_activated has

`ArtAttack/Game.cpp:157-176` — **medium** · `robustness` · confidence: likely

The three handlers sit next to each other and only one of them checks:

```cpp
void Game::on_activated() const
{
    if (this->_gamepad)          // Game.cpp:161 - guarded
        this->_gamepad->Resume();
}

void Game::on_deactivated() const
{
    this->_gamepad->Suspend();   // Game.cpp:168 - NOT guarded
}

void Game::on_suspending() const
{
    this->_gamepad->Suspend();   // Game.cpp:174 - NOT guarded
    _audio_engine->Suspend();    // Game.cpp:175 - NOT guarded
}
```

`_gamepad` and `_audio_engine` are `= nullptr` members (Game.h:68, Game.h:74) created only inside `Game::initialize` (Game.cpp:59 and Game.cpp:47). Main.cpp calls `initialize` at line 207 - *after* `CreateWindowExW` (Main.cpp:156/162) and `ShowWindow` (Main.cpp:191/195), both of which synchronously dispatch `WM_ACTIVATEAPP` into `WndProc`. `GWLP_USERDATA` is already populated by `WM_CREATE` (Main.cpp:246-252), so the `if (game)` check at Main.cpp:330 passes and the only thing between the message and a null dereference is the guard that `on_deactivated` lacks.

The presence of the guard on `on_activated` shows the author already hit this on the activate path and patched only that one.

The same asymmetry means `on_suspending` (reached via `WM_SIZE`/`SIZE_MINIMIZED`, Main.cpp:282-291, and `PBT_APMQUERYSUSPEND`, Main.cpp:346-350) is a double null-deref during the startup window.

**Fix:** Guard all three consistently, or better, move `_gamepad`/`_audio_engine` construction into the `Game` constructor (they have no window or device dependency) so they are non-null for the entire lifetime of the object that receives window messages. Suppressing the symptom with `if (x)` in three places is the weaker fix.

#### 22. WM_DISPLAYCHANGE only updates the colour space; nothing re-derives the render size on a monitor or mode change

`ArtAttack/Game.cpp:186-205` — **medium** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

`Game::on_display_change` (Game.cpp:192-195) is `_device_resources->UpdateColorSpace();` and nothing else — it does not consult the new display mode, does not re-check whether the saved resolution is still meaningful, and does not touch `ResolutionManager`. `Game::on_window_moved` (186-190) calls `WindowSizeChanged(r.right, r.bottom)` using the *cached* `m_outputSize` (DeviceResources.h:50), so the compare at DeviceResources.cpp:404-410 always matches and it degenerates to `UpdateColorSpace()` — dragging the window to another monitor changes nothing about how the game renders.

So: change the desktop resolution from 1920x1080 to 1280x720 while running borderless-fullscreen, and Windows resizes the maximized window, producing a WM_SIZE that resizes the swapchain to 1280x720 — while `ResolutionManager` still says 1920x1080 and drives every viewport (ViewportManager.cpp:49, 58, 66, 87, 126). The divergence described in the `create_window_size_dependent_resources` finding becomes permanent and is not recoverable without editing the save file. There is no validation anywhere that the saved `screen_resolution` (ResolutionManager.cpp:47-63, four hardcoded 16:9 sizes) is supported by, or even smaller than, the current monitor — no `EnumDisplayModes`, no `GetSystemMetrics(SM_CXSCREEN)`, no `IDXGIOutput::GetDisplayModeList` call exists in the codebase.

**Fix:** Have WM_DISPLAYCHANGE (and the resize path) re-read the client rect and republish it as the layout resolution; validate the saved resolution against the current output on startup and clamp it, rather than trusting save_data.json.

#### 24. The DirectXTK project template's TODO comments were never cleaned up and now misdescribe the code

`ArtAttack/Game.cpp:17, 62, 159, 167, 173, 183, 204, 222, 271` — **low** · `dead-code` · confidence: certain

Twelve of the fifteen TODOs in the codebase are untouched boilerplate from the DirectX 11 VS template: `Game.cpp:17` ('TODO: Provide parameters for swapchain format...'), `:62` ('TODO: Change the timer settings if you want something other than the default variable timestep mode' — the line above it *does* set fixed timestep, so the comment is now false), `:159, :167, :173, :183` (in `on_activated`/`on_deactivated`/`on_suspending`/`on_resuming`, all of which are implemented), `:204, :222, :271`; `Main.cpp:181, :200, :240`. They make it impossible to tell template scaffolding from real work items.

The three TODOs that *are* real all mark unimplemented functions: `DrawObject.cpp:68` (`set_draw_rotation_by_rectangle_rotated`, empty, never called), `Level.cpp:698` (`draw_end_screen`, empty, never called), `Mh.cpp:280` and `:345` ('TODO: implement text bounding box' — which is why `MWidget` size queries on text are unreliable). `Player.cpp:276` is the left-ramp gap reported separately.

**Fix:** Delete the twelve template TODOs. Keep only real work items, and where the work item is 'this function does nothing', delete the function instead of the comment.

#### 25. const member functions across Game mutate device, audio and input state; the const is meaningless and inconsistently applied

`ArtAttack/Game.cpp:157-205, 124-152, 264-267` — **low** · `design`

`on_activated() const` resumes the gamepad, `on_deactivated() const` and `on_suspending() const` suspend gamepad and audio, `clear() const` issues `ClearRenderTargetView`/`OMSetRenderTargets`/`RSSetViewports` on the device and all 16 deferred contexts, `on_window_moved() const` and `on_window_size_changed(...) const` call `_device_resources->WindowSizeChanged(...)` which resizes the swap chain. All compile because `const std::unique_ptr<T>::operator->` still yields a non-const `T*` — const on Game does not propagate through the pointers.

The tell is `on_resuming()` (Game.cpp:178), which is NOT const and does the exact mirror of `on_suspending() const`, differing only by `_timer.ResetElapsedTime()`. The qualifiers communicate nothing and actively mislead — they say 'this does not change the game' about the functions that reconfigure the swap chain.

**Fix:** Drop `const` from all of these; they are commands. Reserve `const` for genuine observers. If you want the compiler to help, hold non-owning dependencies through a propagate_const-style wrapper rather than relying on convention.

#### 26. Redundant std::move around make_unique, plus the hand-maintained parallel sprite-batch vector

`ArtAttack/Game.cpp:224-232` — **low** · `modern-cpp`

```
this->_sprite_batches[i] = std::move(
    std::make_unique<SpriteBatch>(this->_device_resources->get_deferred_context(i)));
```
`std::make_unique` already returns a prvalue; wrapping it in `std::move` is a no-op at best and pessimising where copy elision would otherwise apply. The loop also maintains `_sprite_batches_ptrs` in lockstep (`:231`) purely so `:234` can publish `&this->_sprite_batches_ptrs` as a `std::vector<SpriteBatch*>*` through `GameData::set_sprite_batches` — handing every consumer a mutable pointer to a Game member container (and the source of the dangling-mirror bug reported separately).

Same file, `float elapsedTime = float(timer.GetElapsedSeconds());` (Game.cpp:89) is a C-style functional cast where the codebase uses `static_cast` everywhere else (ResolutionManager.cpp:71-72, Main.cpp:148), and `elapsedTime` is the only camelCase local in the file.

**Fix:** Drop the `std::move` and use `static_cast<float>`. Replace the parallel vector with a single accessor returning `const std::vector<std::unique_ptr<SpriteBatch>>&` or a span-like view so there is nothing to keep in sync.

## `ArtAttack/Game.h`

_20 findings: 1 critical, 6 high, 9 medium, 4 low_

#### 1. AudioEngine is destroyed before the ResourceManager that owns its WaveBanks and SoundEffectInstances

`ArtAttack/Game.h:65-74` — **critical** · `resource-lifetime`

Members destruct in reverse declaration order. `_resource_manager` is declared at Game.h:65 and `_audio_engine` at Game.h:74, so on every shutdown `_audio_engine` dies FIRST and `_resource_manager` second. `ResourceManager::_sound_banks` (ResourceManager.h:53) is `std::map<std::string, std::unique_ptr<SoundBank>>`; `SoundBank` owns `std::unique_ptr<DirectX::WaveBank> _wave_bank` (SoundBank.h:39) and `std::map<std::string, std::unique_ptr<DirectX::SoundEffectInstance>>` (SoundBank.h:41). DirectXTK requires the AudioEngine to outlive every WaveBank / SoundEffectInstance — their destructors unregister themselves from the engine. So `g_game.reset()` (Main.cpp:226) runs ~WaveBank and ~SoundEffectInstance against a freed AudioEngine on every normal exit. `Game::~Game()` (Game.cpp:23-29) calling `_audio_engine->Suspend()` does not help: the destructor body runs BEFORE member destruction, not after.

**Fix:** Declare `_audio_engine` first (before `_resource_manager`/`_resource_loader`) so it dies last, and better, stop relying on declaration order: add an explicit `Game::shutdown()` that does `_resource_manager.reset(); _resource_loader.reset();` and only then `_audio_engine.reset()`, with a comment stating the DirectXTK constraint.

#### 2. Game is a god object: platform host, device-lost sink, root state machine and owner of twelve unrelated subsystems

`ArtAttack/Game.h:16-76` — **high** · `design`

`class Game final : public DX::IDeviceNotify, public StateContext` simultaneously is (1) the Win32/D3D host (DeviceResources, StepTimer, clear/present), (2) the device-lost listener, (3) the root application state machine — by *inheriting* StateContext, an is-a claim that is false and that makes `transition_to` public on any `Game*` — and (4) the owner of CommonStates, ResourceLoader, ResourceManager, a heap `float`, GamePad, ViewportManager, ThreadPool, a `vector<unique_ptr<SpriteBatch>>` plus a hand-maintained parallel `vector<SpriteBatch*>` (Game.h:72-73), AudioEngine, Partitioner, and a `GameData*` service locator it populates with pointers to all of the above (Game.cpp:36, 60, 234, 237, 240, 243, 245, 250, 253, 256).

Nothing here is reusable: taking the platform layer to another game means taking the audio engine, the sprite-batch pool and the resource loader with it. `Main.cpp:208` then hardcodes the game's first screen into the entry point (`transition_to(std::make_unique<GameMenu>(...))`). Most of the lifetime bugs in this module — the audio destruction order, the OnDeviceRestored subsystem churn, the dangling `_sprite_batches_ptrs` — are direct consequences of this one class owning everything.

**Fix:** Split into an `Engine`/`Application` (window + device + timer + frame loop + present, nothing else), a `Services` container of subsystem interfaces constructed and injected explicitly, and a `StateMachine` **member** rather than a base class. The game supplies its initial state; the engine never names GameMenu or any game type.

#### 3. Game frees every service before its StateContext base destroys the State that points at them

`ArtAttack/Game.h:16, 59-76` — **high** · `lifetime`

`class Game final : public DX::IDeviceNotify, public StateContext` (Game.h:16). C++ destroys members first, base subobjects last. So `g_game.reset()` (Main.cpp:226) runs `~Game()`, then members in reverse declaration order (`_partitioner`, `_audio_engine`, `_sprite_batches`, `_thread_pool`, `_viewport_manager`, `_gamepad`, `_state`, `_dt`, `_resource_manager`, `_resource_loader`, `_states`, `_device_resources`), and only THEN `~StateContext()`, which destroys `StateContext::_state` (StateContext.h:16) — the live scene graph.

So the entire game state tree is torn down AFTER the ResourceManager, ThreadPool, AudioEngine, SpriteBatches, CommonStates and DeviceResources it points at have been freed. `Level::_sound_bank` (cached at Level.cpp:59), `Level::_thread_pool`, `SoundBankObject::_resource_manager` are all dangling at that moment.

It does not crash today only because nothing dereferences during teardown. `Level::stop_music()` already exists at Level.cpp:61-64 and does `this->_sound_bank->stop_effect(...)`; the day someone writes the obvious `~Level() { stop_music(); }` this becomes a use-after-free at every exit. For a project whose goal is a reusable engine, "shutdown works because no destructor does anything" is not a shutdown design.

**Fix:** Destroy the state tree explicitly and FIRST: give `StateContext` a `clear_state()` and call it at the top of `~Game()`, or stop inheriting `StateContext` and hold it as the last-declared member. Document the required teardown order in the header either way.

#### 4. Game inherits StateContext, so subsystems die before the live state tree — and the audio engine dies before the sounds it owns

`ArtAttack/Game.h:16, 59-76` — **high** · `lifetime`

`class Game final : public DX::IDeviceNotify, public StateContext` (Game.h:16) owns every engine subsystem as *members* (`_device_resources`:59, `_states`:62, `_resource_loader`:64, `_resource_manager`:65, `_dt`:66, `_gamepad`:68, `_viewport_manager`:69, `_thread_pool`:71, `_sprite_batches`:72, `_audio_engine`:74, `_partitioner`:75), while the live `GameLevel`/`Level`/`Player` tree is owned by the *base* `StateContext::_state` (StateContext.h:16).

C++ destroys derived members first, then base subobjects. At `g_game.reset()` (Main.cpp:226) the order is: `~Game()` body (Game.cpp:23-29, only suspends audio) → all 15 members in reverse declaration order → `~StateContext()` → the whole GameLevel/Level/Player/Weapon/Projectile graph. Every one of those objects holds raw non-owning `ResourceManager*`, `ThreadPool*`, `ViewportManager*`, `const float* _dt` pointers into members that are already gone. This part is latent — it survives only because no game object has a user-written destructor.

The **second half is not latent**: `_audio_engine` (:74) is destroyed before `_resource_manager` (:65), and `ResourceManager::_sound_banks` (ResourceManager.h:53) owns `std::unique_ptr<SoundBank>`, each of which owns a `std::unique_ptr<DirectX::WaveBank>` and a set of `SoundEffectInstance`s (SoundBank.h:33-40). DirectXTK requires all WaveBank/SoundEffect/SoundEffectInstance objects to be destroyed *before* the owning AudioEngine — `~SoundEffectInstance` calls back into the engine to return its voice. This happens on every clean exit.

**Fix:** (1) Give `StateContext` a `clear_state()` and call it as the first statement of `~Game()` so the state tree dies while its dependencies are alive; better, stop inheriting `StateContext` and hold one by composition declared *before* all subsystems. (2) Move `_audio_engine` to be declared before `_resource_manager`, or reset the resource manager explicitly at the top of `~Game()`.

#### 5. The root State is owned by a base class, so on app exit it outlives every service it borrows; Game::_state is dead code

`ArtAttack/Game.h:16-76` — **high** · `lifetime` · confidence: certain

class Game final : public DX::IDeviceNotify, public StateContext
    { ...
        std::unique_ptr<DX::DeviceResources> _device_resources;   // 59
        std::unique_ptr<ResourceManager> _resource_manager;       // 65
        std::unique_ptr<State> _state = nullptr;                  // 67  <-- never used
        std::unique_ptr<ThreadPool> _thread_pool;                 // 71
        std::unique_ptr<DirectX::AudioEngine> _audio_engine;      // 74

Two problems.

1. `Game::_state` (line 67) is referenced nowhere in Game.cpp (grep for `_state` in Game.cpp returns only `_states`, the `CommonStates`). The live state actually lives in the private `StateContext::_state` base member. It is a dead, misleading member that also collides visually with `_states`.

2. Base-class subobjects are destroyed *after* members. So `g_game.reset()` (Main.cpp:226) destroys, in order, `_partitioner`, `_audio_engine`, `_thread_pool`, `_viewport_manager`, `_resource_manager`, `_device_resources` ... and only then `~StateContext()` destroys the live `GameLevel`, its `Level`, `Player`s and `Weapon`s — every one of which holds raw pointers into the already-destroyed `ResourceManager`/`SoundBank`/`ThreadPool`. Destroying `AudioEngine` before the `SoundEffect`/`SoundEffectInstance` objects it owns notifications for is explicitly unsupported by DirectXTK. Nothing crashes today only because none of those destructors dereference anything.

This is the app-exit branch of the teardown path: quitting from a live match tears the world down in exactly the wrong order.

**Fix:** Delete the dead `_state` member. Make `Game` *hold* a `StateContext` rather than inherit one (`std::unique_ptr<StateContext> _root_state;` declared first among the members, so it is destroyed first), or add an explicit `~Game()` body that does `StateContext::transition_to(nullptr)`-equivalent teardown of the state tree before any service is released. `Game` also declares `Game(Game&&) = default` (line 22) while the constructor calls `_device_resources->RegisterDeviceNotify(this)` (Game.cpp:20) — a move leaves DeviceResources pointing at a moved-from Game; that move should be deleted.

#### 6. Destruction order is inverted: the live State outlives every Game member, and the ThreadPool is destroyed after the SpriteBatches its tasks use

`ArtAttack/Game.h:16-76` — **high** · `design` · confidence: certain

`class Game final : public DX::IDeviceNotify, public StateContext` (Game.h:16) and the members are declared:

```
:59 _device_resources   :62 _states       :64 _resource_loader  :65 _resource_manager
:66 _dt                 :67 _state        :68 _gamepad          :69 _viewport_manager
:70 _data               :71 _thread_pool  :72 _sprite_batches   :73 _sprite_batches_ptrs
:74 _audio_engine       :75 _partitioner
```

C++ destroys members in reverse declaration order, then base classes. At `g_game.reset()` (Main.cpp:226) the actual sequence is therefore:

`_partitioner` → `_audio_engine` → `_sprite_batches_ptrs` → **`_sprite_batches`** → **`_thread_pool`** → `_viewport_manager` → `_dt` → `_resource_manager` → `_states` → `_device_resources` → **then the `StateContext` base, which finally destroys the live `GameMenu`/`GameLevel` and the whole `Level` under it.**

Two concrete problems:

1. **`_sprite_batches` is destroyed one step before `_thread_pool`.** `~ThreadPool` (ThreadPool.cpp:30-36) calls `CloseThreadpoolCleanupGroupMembers(_cleanup_group, FALSE, nullptr)`, and `FALSE` means *do not cancel — wait for outstanding callbacks to run to completion*. So the one place in the program that actually drains the pool runs **after** the `SpriteBatch` objects those callbacks write into (`sprite_batches->at(i)->Begin(...)`, Level.cpp:513) have already been destroyed, and after `_sprite_batches_ptrs` — the very vector `GameData` hands to the tasks — has been destroyed. Any task still outstanding is guaranteed to use freed memory on a background thread.

2. **The active `State` is destroyed dead last**, after `_device_resources`, `_resource_manager` and `_states`. `Level` and everything it owns (players, projectiles, sprite sheets holding raw `ID3D11ShaderResourceView*`, `SoundBank*` into the already-destroyed `ResourceManager`) is torn down when the D3D device, the resource manager and the sampler states are already gone. `Game::_state` at line 67 is a *third* problem: it is a dead member that never appears anywhere in Game.cpp — the real state lives in the private `StateContext::_state` (StateContext.h:16). It reads as though `Game` owns its state in member position, which is exactly the ordering guarantee it does *not* provide.

The only reason this does not crash today is that no draw ever leaves work outstanding — which is an accident of every draw calling `wait_for_tasks_to_complete` before returning, not a guarantee the design enforces.

**Fix:** Give `Game` an explicit teardown that runs before any member is destroyed: `Game::~Game()` should first `transition_to(nullptr)` (or add a `StateContext::clear_state()`) to drop the active State while all services are still alive, then `_thread_pool->wait_for_tasks_to_complete()` / reset the pool, then let the members go. Delete the dead `_state` member at Game.h:67. Better still, stop relying on declaration order for lifetime at all: make the pool the first thing constructed and the first thing shut down, and hold the state machine by composition (`StateContext _states;` as a member) rather than by inheritance, so its position in the destruction order is visible and controllable.

#### 7. Frame delta is a heap-allocated unique_ptr<float> whose raw pointer is threaded through eleven classes

`ArtAttack/Game.h:66` — **high** · `design`

`std::unique_ptr<float> _dt = nullptr;` — allocated at Game.cpp:244, published as a raw `float*` via `_data->set_dt(this->_dt.get())` (:245), written each update by `*this->_dt = elapsedTime;` (:90). Eleven headers cache it as `const float* _dt`: AnimationObject.h, AnimatedSprite.h, Drawer.h, LevelBuilder.h, Level.h, LevelObjectBuilder.h, PaintTile.h, Player.h, Projectile.h, StructurePaintable.h, Weapon.h. None documents the pointer as non-owning, none can tell whether it is still valid, and reassigning `_dt` on device restore (Game.cpp:244) frees it out from under all eleven.

The root cause is that `State::update()`/`draw()` are nullary (State.h) and `StateContext::update()/draw()` forward without arguments (StateContext.h:12-13), so frame time has nowhere to travel except as ambient global state. The same shape forces the renderer to be looked up through GameData: `GameLevel::draw` fetches `get_deferred_contexts()` and `get_sprite_batches()` from the locator (GameStates.cpp:311-317) because `draw()` cannot be handed a render target.

**Fix:** Change the interface to `virtual void update(float dt) = 0;` and `virtual void draw(Renderer& r) = 0;` and thread both down explicitly. dt then has no lifetime at all and the renderer becomes an injected parameter rather than something any object can reach.

#### 8. NUM_THREADS_MAX = 16 is an unnamespaced header constant that fixes four unrelated decisions, with no reference to hardware

`ArtAttack/Game.h:12-14` — **medium** · `design`

`constexpr int TARGET_FPS = 60; constexpr int NUM_THREADS_MIN = 1; constexpr int NUM_THREADS_MAX = 16;` sit at global namespace scope in a header included by most of the project, and `NUM_THREADS_MAX` simultaneously means: the deferred-context count (Game.cpp:52), the SpriteBatch pool size (Game.cpp:224-232), and the ThreadPool ceiling (Game.cpp:236). `std::thread::hardware_concurrency()` appears nowhere in the codebase (grepped).

The real parallelism is bounded by player count (max 4), because `Partitioner::partition` caps the partition count at `num_elements` (Partitioner.cpp:10). So on any machine running a 1-player level, 15 deferred contexts and 15 DirectXTK SpriteBatch objects are constructed and never used — each SpriteBatch carries its own dynamic vertex buffer (4096 sprites), so several MB of GPU-visible memory is allocated to serve at most 4 of them. `Game::clear()` then re-binds state on all 16 every frame (see the separate finding).

**Fix:** Compute the worker count once as `std::clamp(std::thread::hardware_concurrency(), 1u, MAX_VIEWS)` and size contexts, batches and pool from it. Make it a constructor parameter of the engine rather than a header constant — a reusable engine cannot know the game's player cap. Wrap `TARGET_FPS` and friends in a namespace or an engine config struct.

#### 9. Thread count hardcoded to 16 at global namespace scope; real parallelism is capped at 4 and never measured

`ArtAttack/Game.h:12-14` — **medium** · `design` · confidence: certain

```cpp
constexpr int TARGET_FPS = 60;
constexpr int NUM_THREADS_MIN = 1;
constexpr int NUM_THREADS_MAX = 16;
```

Three unnamespaced global constants in an engine header (the same pollution appears at CollisionTools.h:7-8 with `BRACKET_ITERATIONS` / `ITERATION_POWER`). Consequences:

- `create_deferred_contexts(NUM_THREADS_MAX)` (Game.cpp:52) always allocates 16 D3D11 deferred contexts, and Game.cpp:224-232 always allocates 16 `SpriteBatch` objects (each with its own dynamic vertex buffer), regardless of machine or player count.
- The actual concurrency is `Partitioner::partition(num_players, 16)` (Level.cpp:382-383), and `Partitioner::partition` caps its output at `num_elements` (Partitioner.cpp:10 `i < num_partitions && i < num_elements`). With at most 4 players, at most 4 of the 16 contexts/batches are ever used. Menus use exactly 2 (all `draw()` overloads push exactly two mobjects, e.g. MainMenu.cpp:38-45, EndMenu.cpp:234-241).
- `std::thread::hardware_concurrency()` is never consulted; nothing appears in `Save`/config.
- `Partitioner::partition` divides by `num_partitions` with no zero guard (Partitioner.cpp:7-8), and `num_partitions` comes from `ThreadPool::get_max_num_threads()`, whose backing member defaults to `-1` (ThreadPool.h:26) and whose constructor argument is never validated before being cast to `DWORD` (ThreadPool.cpp:14-18) — a negative max would become a huge `DWORD`.

**Fix:** Move these into a namespaced engine-config struct supplied at init (default `std::thread::hardware_concurrency()`), size the deferred-context/SpriteBatch pool to the actual number of parallel render targets needed, and validate/clamp the ThreadPool constructor arguments. Guard `Partitioner::partition` against `num_partitions <= 0`.

#### 10. NUM_THREADS_MAX = 16 is hardcoded and drives three unrelated quantities regardless of hardware or workload

`ArtAttack/Game.h:13-14` — **medium** · `performance`

constexpr int TARGET_FPS = 60;
    constexpr int NUM_THREADS_MIN = 1;
    constexpr int NUM_THREADS_MAX = 16;

One constant drives: the thread pool maximum (Game.cpp:236), sixteen deferred contexts, and sixteen `SpriteBatch` objects each with its own vertex/index buffers (Game.cpp:224-232). None of it derives from `std::thread::hardware_concurrency()`.

On a 4-core machine `MenuPage::draw_mobjects_in_viewports` (MenuPage.cpp:131) genuinely submits up to 16 concurrent tasks — oversubscription. The gameplay path is the opposite problem: `Level::draw_active_level` (Level.cpp:379-383) partitions at most 4 players across 16 partitions, so 12 of the 16 SpriteBatches and deferred contexts are allocated and kept alive for nothing.

**Fix:** Derive from `std::max(1u, std::thread::hardware_concurrency())` capped by the actual maximum parallel work, and allocate deferred contexts + SpriteBatches to match. If a fixed cap is wanted, name it for what it bounds instead of reusing one constant for three unrelated quantities.

#### 11. Game owns its managers as members but the active State lives in a base subobject destroyed last

`ArtAttack/Game.h:16-76` — **medium** · `design`

`class Game final : public DX::IDeviceNotify, public StateContext` (Game.h:16). The active `State` — `GameLevel`, which owns `std::unique_ptr<Level> _level` (GameStates.h:57) — lives in the `StateContext` **base** subobject. Every manager `Level` points at is a **member** of `Game`: `_resource_manager` (Game.h:65), `_dt` (:66), `_viewport_manager` (:69), `_thread_pool` (:71), `_sprite_batches` (:72), `_audio_engine` (:74), `_partitioner` (:75).

C++ destruction order is body, then members in reverse declaration order, then base classes. So on shutdown every manager is destroyed **before** the StateContext base destroys GameLevel and Level. During `~Level`, `_sound_bank`, `_resolution_manager`, `_viewport_manager`, `_resource_manager`, `_thread_pool`, `_partitioner` and `_dt` (Level.h:107-147) all point at freed memory, as do the equivalents in every Player, Weapon, Structure and PaintTile it transitively owns. It survives only because none of those destructors happens to touch its back-pointers — an invariant nobody wrote down.

Two smaller things in the same header: `std::unique_ptr<State> _state = nullptr;` (Game.h:67) duplicates the base's state pointer and is dead — I grepped Game.cpp and the only `_state` hits are the unrelated `_states` (CommonStates). And Game.h:22-23 defaults the move operations while the constructor publishes `this` via `RegisterDeviceNotify`, so a moved-from Game leaves DeviceResources holding a stale `IDeviceNotify*`.

**Fix:** Make `Game` *contain* a `StateContext` member declared after all the managers it depends on, rather than inheriting from it — reverse-order destruction then tears the state machine down first. Delete the unused `_state` member and the defaulted move operations.

#### 12. The active State is destroyed after every service it borrows, because it lives in a base subobject

`ArtAttack/Game.h:16, 59-76` — **medium** · `correctness`

C++ destroys derived-class members first (reverse declaration order) and base subobjects last. On `g_game.reset()` (Main.cpp:226) the order is: `_partitioner`, `_audio_engine`, `_sprite_batches_ptrs`, `_sprite_batches`, `_thread_pool`, `_data`, `_viewport_manager`, `_gamepad`, `_state` (the dead one), `_dt`, `_resource_manager`, `_resource_loader`, `_states`, `_timer`, `_device_resources` — and only THEN `~StateContext` → `~GameLevel` → `~Level` → `~Player`.

So the entire live object graph is destructed after every service it points at has been freed: `Level` holds `ThreadPool*` (Level.h:146), `const Partitioner*` (:147), `ViewportManager*` (:118), `ResourceManager*` (:119), `const float* _dt` (:140), `ID3D11SamplerState*` (:141). Today the game-object destructors are implicit and happen not to touch those pointers, so it does not crash — but it becomes UB the first time a `Level` or `Player` destructor logs, stops a sound, or releases a GPU resource, which is a normal thing to add.

**Fix:** Explicitly tear the state machine down first: reset the state at the top of `Game::~Game()` (Game.cpp:23), before any member destructor runs. Longer term `Game` should HOLD a `StateContext` rather than BE one — composition makes this ordering explicit and expressible.

#### 13. Game explicitly defaults move operations while three external observers hold pointers into it

`ArtAttack/Game.h:22-23` — **medium** · `correctness`

`Game(Game&&) = default; Game& operator= (Game&&) = default;` — meanwhile `Game` hands out three pointers into itself:
- `Game::Game()` calls `_device_resources->RegisterDeviceNotify(this)` (Game.cpp:20), stored as `IDeviceNotify* m_deviceNotify` (DeviceResources.h:126, whose comment 'can be held directly as it owns the DeviceResources' is only true if the owner never moves);
- `create_device_dependent_resources` publishes `&this->_sprite_batches_ptrs` — the address of a member vector — into GameData (Game.cpp:234);
- `StateContext::transition_to` stores `this` into the State, and `Game` is the root StateContext (Game.h:16).

Moving a `Game` leaves all three pointing at the moved-from husk. The user-declared destructor at Game.h:20 would already have suppressed the implicit move, so these two lines were added deliberately and are pure hazard — `Game` is only ever held in a `unique_ptr` (Main.cpp:20), so nothing needs them.

**Fix:** `Game(Game&&) = delete; Game& operator= (Game&&) = delete;` alongside the already-deleted copies. Longer term, move `RegisterDeviceNotify(this)` out of the constructor into `initialize()` so a half-constructed Game is never published, and stop publishing the address of a member container.

#### 14. Game::update(StepTimer const&) hides the inherited public StateContext::update() behind a private overload

`ArtAttack/Game.h:51` — **medium** · `design`

`StateContext` exposes `void update() const;` (StateContext.h:12). `Game` declares `void update(DX::StepTimer const& timer);` in its **private** section (Game.h:51). Name lookup in a derived class stops at the first scope containing the name, so `StateContext::update()` is entirely hidden on any `Game` object — and hidden behind a private overload, so an external `game.update()` is an access error rather than a call to the base. Game.cpp:91 has to work around its own hiding by writing `StateContext::update();` explicitly inside `Game::update`. The same shape almost recurs with `Game::render()` vs `StateContext::draw()` (Game.cpp:115).

**Fix:** Rename the private one to `update_frame(DX::StepTimer const&)` or `step`, or add `using StateContext::update;` if the overload set is intended. `StateContext::update()/draw()` are the polymorphic entry points and would be better as virtuals on StateContext than as names shadowed by a derived class.

#### 15. Member declaration order destroys the ThreadPool after the resources its tasks use, and before the objects that hold pointers to it

`ArtAttack/Game.h:59-76` — **medium** · `memory-safety` · confidence: likely

Members are destroyed in reverse declaration order. Declared order is `_device_resources`(59) … `_state`(67) … `_thread_pool`(71), `_sprite_batches`(72), `_sprite_batches_ptrs`(73), `_audio_engine`(74), `_partitioner`(75). So destruction is:

`_partitioner` → `_audio_engine` → `_sprite_batches_ptrs` → `_sprite_batches` → **`_thread_pool`** → `_data` → `_viewport_manager` → `_gamepad` → **`_state`** → `_dt` → `_resource_manager` → … → `_device_resources`.

Two inversions:
1. `_sprite_batches` (and `_partitioner`, `_audio_engine`) are destroyed **before** `~ThreadPool`. `~ThreadPool` calls `CloseThreadpoolCleanupGroupMembers(_cleanup_group, FALSE, nullptr)` (ThreadPool.cpp:32), i.e. it *waits* for outstanding callbacks — callbacks that would be running against already-freed SpriteBatches. The class provides no "is idle" invariant, so this is safe only because every current call site happens to call `wait_for_tasks_to_complete()` synchronously.
2. `_state` (which owns `GameMenu`/`GameLevel` → `Level`, and `Level` caches `ThreadPool* _thread_pool`, Level.h:146) is destroyed **after** `_thread_pool`. Any future cleanup in `~Level` that touches the pool is a use-after-free.

Separately, `Game(Game&&) = default;` / `Game& operator=(Game&&) = default;` (Game.h:22-23) are wrong for this class: the constructor registers `_device_resources->RegisterDeviceNotify(this)` (Game.cpp:20) and `Main.cpp:250` stores the `Game*` in `GWLP_USERDATA`. A move leaves both back-references pointing at the moved-from object.

**Fix:** Declare `_thread_pool` **last** so it is destroyed first, and declare `_state` before it. Delete the move operations on `Game` (it is a `final` class registered by address; it should be neither copyable nor movable).

#### 16. AudioEngine is declared after ResourceManager, so it is destroyed BEFORE the SoundBanks that own its WaveBank and voices

`ArtAttack/Game.h:65, 74` — **medium** · `lifetime`

Member order puts `_resource_manager` at Game.h:65 and `_audio_engine` at Game.h:74. Reverse-order destruction therefore frees the AudioEngine FIRST and the ResourceManager — which owns the SoundBanks, which own `unique_ptr<DirectX::WaveBank>` and `unique_ptr<SoundEffectInstance>` (SoundBank.h:39, 41) — second.

Those DirectXTK objects are constructed with a raw `AudioEngine*` (Audio.h:320 `WaveBank(AudioEngine*, const wchar_t*)`) and unregister from the engine in their destructors. This is precisely the ordering DirectXTK warns against.

It survives today only because DirectXTK defends itself — `AudioEngine`'s destructor notifies every registered object and nulls their engine pointer. So this is a latent bug rescued by a third-party defensive path, with nothing in this codebase documenting the dependency. `~Game()` (Game.cpp:23-29) only calls `_audio_engine->Suspend()`, which does not address it.

**Fix:** Move `_audio_engine` above `_resource_manager` in Game.h so it outlives it, and add a comment stating the invariant. Better, release the resource manager's sound banks explicitly in `~Game()` so the ordering is expressed in code rather than in declaration position.

#### 17. Game.h relies on transitive includes and offers two entry points for setting the same GameData pointer

`ArtAttack/Game.h:29, 47, 64, 69, 75` — **low** · `design`

Header hygiene: Game.h declares `std::unique_ptr<ResourceLoader>` (:64), `std::unique_ptr<ViewportManager>` (:69) and `std::unique_ptr<Partitioner>` (:75) but includes none of ResourceLoader.h / ViewportManager.h / Partitioner.h. It compiles only because GameData.h (included at Game.h:6) happens to pull all three in (GameData.h:6, 9, 11); reordering the includes breaks the build.

API duplication: `initialize(GameData*)` (:29) sets `_data` at Game.cpp:34, and `set_game_data(GameData*)` (:47) sets the same field at Game.cpp:70. Main.cpp calls both — `set_game_data` at :110, `initialize` at :207 — so there are two entry points for one invariant and no way to tell which is authoritative.

**Fix:** Include the three headers explicitly, or forward-declare the classes (Game's destructor is already out-of-line, so forward declarations work for the unique_ptr members). Delete `set_game_data` and take GameData in the constructor or in `initialize` only.

#### 18. Game declares a dead unique_ptr<State> _state duplicating the one StateContext already owns

`ArtAttack/Game.h:67` — **low** · `design`

`std::unique_ptr<State> _state = nullptr;` — `Game` inherits `StateContext` (Game.h:16), which owns the real `std::unique_ptr<State> _state` privately (StateContext.h:16) and manages it through `transition_to` (called from Main.cpp:208). I grepped Game.cpp for `_state\b`: zero hits — the member is never assigned, read, or reset. It is a leftover that makes the header lie about where the current state lives, in the exact class a reader opens to answer 'who owns the current state?'. (It does not shadow — the base member is private — it is a silently unused duplicate.)

**Fix:** Delete the line. If derived classes genuinely need to inspect the active state, give `StateContext` a `const State* get_state() const` rather than a second member. While there, the `= nullptr` initialisers on every `unique_ptr` member (Game.h:59, 62, 64-69, 71, 74-75) are redundant.

#### 19. Game declares a second, unused `_state` member that shadows the one its StateContext base owns

`ArtAttack/Game.h:67` — **low** · `design`

`class Game final : public DX::IDeviceNotify, public StateContext` (Game.h:16), and `StateContext` already owns the current state as a private `std::unique_ptr<State> _state = nullptr;` (StateContext.h:16). Game.h:67 then declares its own `std::unique_ptr<State> _state = nullptr;`.

I grepped Game.cpp for `_state`: the only hits are lines 252, 253 and 276, all of which are `_states` (the CommonStates member). Game's own `_state` is never read or written anywhere. The real state is managed entirely through the inherited `StateContext::transition_to`. Two same-named, same-typed members owned by different subobjects of one class make it impossible to tell from the header who owns the current state — which is what makes the destruction-order finding above hard to see.

**Fix:** Delete Game.h:67.

#### 20. Dead duplicate member Game::_state, one character away from the live member _states

`ArtAttack/Game.h:67` — **low** · `ownership`

`std::unique_ptr<State> _state = nullptr;` is declared as a private member of `Game`, but `Game` already inherits `StateContext` (Game.h:16), which owns the one and only real state in `StateContext::_state` (StateContext.h:16). Grepping `_state` in Game.cpp returns exactly three hits — lines 252, 253 and 276 — and all three are the *unrelated* member `_states` (the `CommonStates`). `Game::_state` is never assigned, never read, never reset; it is a leftover from before Game was refactored to inherit StateContext.

Severity is `low` because it has no behavioural effect (three reviewers graded it high/medium). It is worth fixing because a reader of Game.h concludes Game owns the state directly (it does not), and because a member named `_state` sitting one character from a live member named `_states` is a typo waiting to compile silently.

**Fix:** Delete Game.h:67. While you are there, rename `_states` to `_common_states` so no member differs from another only by a trailing `s`.

## `ArtAttack/GameStates.cpp`

_18 findings: 2 critical, 4 high, 7 medium, 5 low_

#### 1. Gamepad input vector is compacted by connection state, then indexed by player number — out-of-bounds read on controller disconnect

`ArtAttack/GameStates.cpp:141-157, 185` — **critical** · `correctness`

`GameLevel::update` does `std::vector<PlayerInputData> player_inputs = this->_player_input->update_and_get_player_inputs();` (:141-142) and passes it unvalidated to `_level->update(player_inputs)` (:185).

`PlayerInput::update_and_get_player_inputs` (PlayerInput.cpp:119-138) only pushes an entry for pads that are currently connected:
```cpp
for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
    if (current[i].connected) { ... result.push_back(input); }
    this->_prev_inputs[i] = current[i];
}
```
But `Level::update_level_logic` (Level.cpp:189-192) indexes it positionally by player object:
```cpp
int player_index = 0;
for (const auto& object : *this->_player_objects) {
    object->set_player_input(player_inputs[player_index]);
```
In a 3-player match, unplugging pad 0 shrinks the vector to 2 while `_player_objects` still holds 3 → `player_inputs[2]` is an unchecked `std::vector::operator[]` past the end. Before it goes out of bounds it also silently remaps every surviving player's input to the wrong Player object.

The same defect flows through `check_for_pause_input` (:348-359), which returns an index into the compacted vector; that index is handed to `PauseMenuData` as the player number (:156) and then used as an unchecked subscript into `MenuInput`'s separately-compacted vector — `inputs[player_num]` at PauseMenu.cpp:53, 54, 59, 82, 98, 222, 229, 256 (MenuInput::update_and_get_menu_inputs compacts identically, MenuInput.cpp:131-150). A pad disconnecting while the pause menu is open is a second out-of-bounds read.

`PlayerInputData` already carries a `connection` field for exactly this, but PlayerInput.cpp:111 hardcodes `result.connection = connection_state::CONNECTED;` and DISCONNECTED is never written.

**Fix:** Return a fixed 4-element array (or a vector always sized to the max player count) indexed by pad slot, with `connection` correctly set for absent pads, so slot index == player identity is an invariant across both input types and across frames. Then `check_for_pause_input` returns a real player number and every `inputs[n]` is safe. Until then use `.at()` in Level::update_level_logic and PauseMenu so the failure is loud.

#### 2. End-menu "Restart" replays the match with the wrong viewport layout and no split-screen dividers

`ArtAttack/GameStates.cpp:276-283` — **critical** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

`Level::draw_zoom_out_level_component` permanently mutates the shared ViewportManager at the end of every match:

    // Level.cpp:619 (inside a `const` draw helper, run on a thread-pool worker)
    this->_viewport_manager->set_layout(screen_layout::ONE_PLAYER);

Grep confirms `ViewportManager::set_layout` has exactly two call sites: `GameStates.cpp:123` (`GameLevel::init`) and `Level.cpp:619`. The end-menu RESTART branch rebuilds the level but never restores the layout:

    // GameStates.cpp:276-283
    case end_menu_action::RESTART:
    {
        this->_level->stop_music();
        this->_level = std::move(this->_level_builder->build_level(this->_settings));
        this->_state = game_level_state::FIRST_UPDATE;
        break;
    }

`GameLevel::init()` is not re-run (it is only called by `StateContext::transition_to`), so match 2 of a 2/3/4-player game renders every player's camera into one fullscreen viewport stacked on top of each other. Worse, `LevelBuilder::build_level` builds the split-screen dividers *from the current layout* (`LevelBuilder.cpp:55-56` -> `LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:232-233` -> `ViewportManager::get_viewport_dividers`), and `ViewportManager.cpp:129-132` returns an empty vector for ONE_PLAYER — so the rebuilt level also has zero viewport dividers baked in permanently. Both symptoms persist for every subsequent restart. `PlayerBuilder::build_players` is likewise handed the stale `_viewport_manager` (LevelBuilder.cpp:50-53).

**Fix:** Two separate fixes. (a) Stop mutating global render state from a draw path: `draw_zoom_out_level_component` should compute the fullscreen viewport locally (`ViewportManager::get_fullscreen_d3d11_viewport()` already exists) and apply it to the deferred context, instead of calling `set_layout`. Note the method is declared `const` (Level.h:173) yet mutates the manager — that const is a lie. (b) Make rematch go through one code path: extract a `GameLevel::build_and_enter_level()` that calls `set_layout(_settings.get_screen_layout())` and then `build_level`, and call it from `init()`, from `pause_menu_action::RESTART` (GameStates.cpp:200-205) and from `end_menu_action::RESTART`.

#### 3. No exception handler exists anywhere on the path; a malformed level file or an out-of-bounds object terminates the process

`ArtAttack/GameStates.cpp:105-127` — **high** · `robustness`

`GameLevel::init()` calls `this->_level = std::move(this->_level_builder->build_level(this->_settings));` (:125-126) with no try/catch. I traced the entire stack and there is no handler at any level: GameStates.cpp:125 → `StateContext::transition_to` (StateContext.cpp:20-25) → `Game::update` (Game.cpp:87-98) → `Game::tick` (Game.cpp:75-84) → `wWinMain` (Main.cpp:211-224). A grep of Main.cpp for `try`/`catch` returns exactly one hit, and it is the word "Entry point" in a comment on line 83.

The codebase throws liberally on this path — 58 `throw std::exception` sites project-wide, including `Level::update_level_logic` throwing `"Player out of bounds"` / `"Collision object out of bounds"` during *normal play* (Level.cpp:312, 319). So a player clipping out of the level, or a missing/malformed `levels/*.json`, produces `std::terminate` — instant process death, no message box, no log.

Worse: `Level::draw_player_view_level` throws `"Deferred context not created"` (Level.cpp:500) and `"Failed to finish command list"` (:590, :649) from *inside thread-pool worker lambdas*, and `ThreadPool::work_callback` (ThreadPool.cpp:60-65) is `void CALLBACK` with no try/catch — an exception escaping there is unconditionally `std::terminate`, and it can never be caught by the caller no matter what handlers are added upstream.

**Fix:** Wrap `build_level` in a try/catch in `GameLevel::init()` and fail back to the main menu with an on-screen error. Add a top-level try/catch around the message loop in `wWinMain`. Add a try/catch inside `ThreadPool::work_callback` that captures the exception into the work item so `wait_for_tasks_to_complete()` can rethrow on the calling thread. For an engine, unrecoverable termination on bad content is the worst possible failure mode.

#### 4. GameLevel::init captures device-dependent raw pointers for the whole life of the level and never refreshes them on device restore

`ArtAttack/GameStates.cpp:113-127` — **high** · `lifetime`

```cpp
this->_level_builder = std::make_unique<LevelBuilder>(
    this->get_data()->get_viewport_manager(),
    this->get_data()->get_dt(),                            // float* owned by Game::_dt
    this->get_data()->get_resource_manager(),
    this->get_data()->get_common_states()->PointClamp(),   // borrowed, un-AddRef'd
    ...);
```
`CommonStates::PointClamp()` returns a borrowed `ID3D11SamplerState*` whose lifetime is the `CommonStates` object. It is stored in the LevelBuilder, copied into the `Level`, and used every frame. `Game::OnDeviceLost` (Game.cpp:269-280) does `_states.reset()`; `Game::OnDeviceRestored` (Game.cpp:282-287) re-runs `create_device_dependent_resources()`, which allocates a brand-new `CommonStates` at a new address (Game.cpp:252) **and a brand-new `_dt` float** (Game.cpp:244), republishing both into the real `GameData`.

`GameLevel` implements no device-lost notification and `Game::OnDeviceRestored` does not re-`init()` the current state. After a device reset (driver update, TDR, some Alt-Tab paths) the running level draws with a freed sampler and integrates physics against a freed `float`.

The same snapshot problem exists one level up: `class MenuData : public GameData` (MenuData.h:7) and `GameData::GameData(const GameData*)` (GameData.cpp:4-20) copies all thirteen raw pointers by value, so `MainMenuData` (:6, :13), `PauseMenuData` (:153), `ResultsMenuData` (:172) and `EndMenuData` (:228) each hold their own frozen copy of `_common_states`, `_dt`, `_sprite_batches` and `_device_resources` taken at construction time.

**Fix:** Do not cache device-dependent handles in simulation objects — look them up through the resource manager at draw time, or hold a `ComPtr` and re-acquire on restore. Stop passing `const float*` for delta time entirely: pass `float dt` as an argument to `update(float)`. Route `IDeviceNotify` down to the active `State` so it can re-init. And make `MenuData` hold a `const GameData*` by composition rather than copy-inheriting the service bag.

#### 5. FIRST_UPDATE/SECOND_UPDATE is a hand-rolled workaround for the missing timer reset, and it under-shoots

`ArtAttack/GameStates.cpp:128-142` — **high** · `design` · confidence: certain

```
switch (this->_state)
{
case game_level_state::FIRST_UPDATE:
    this->_state = game_level_state::SECOND_UPDATE;
    return;
case game_level_state::SECOND_UPDATE:
    this->_state = game_level_state::ACTIVE;
    //no break here so it goes to active
```

Two extra enumerators were bolted onto the level state machine (ArtAttack/GameStates.h:38-39) purely to swallow update calls after a load. It absorbs exactly ONE update (FIRST returns; SECOND falls through and immediately simulates), but the missing `ResetElapsedTime()` produces up to SIX. So five full simulation steps still run unseen. The mechanism treats a symptom whose cause is one missing line.

It also produces a refresh-rate-dependent black flash. `Game::render()` (ArtAttack/Game.cpp:103-121) runs unconditionally every tick and always does `clear()` + `Present()`, but `GameLevel::draw()` (GameStates.cpp:305-309) returns before drawing anything while in FIRST_UPDATE/SECOND_UPDATE. On a 60 Hz vsync display that is ~2 black frames on level entry. On a 144 Hz display `update()` runs on only ~42% of ticks, so the same two state transitions take ~5-6 presented frames — the black flash is over twice as long purely because the monitor is faster.

**Fix:** Delete `FIRST_UPDATE`/`SECOND_UPDATE` and call `_timer.ResetElapsedTime()` at the end of `GameLevel::init()` instead. If a "level is not ready to draw" concept is genuinely wanted, make it an explicit `bool _ready` that `draw()` uses to render a loading screen rather than presenting a cleared black buffer.

#### 6. GameLevel::draw does raw D3D11 command-list submission — GPU backend code inside a flow-control State

`ArtAttack/GameStates.cpp:303-346` — **high** · `design`

A `State` — an object whose job is "which screen am I on" — reaches through the service locator for deferred contexts, allocates a raw `std::vector<ID3D11CommandList*>`, hands it to `Level::draw` as an out-param, then fetches the immediate context and hand-loops `ExecuteCommandList` / `Release`:
```cpp
std::vector<ID3D11CommandList*> command_lists(deferred_contexts->size(), nullptr);
...
for (int i = 0; i < command_lists.size(); i++) {
    if (command_lists[i] == nullptr) continue;
    immediate_context->ExecuteCommandList(command_lists[i], TRUE);
    command_lists[i]->Release();
}
```
This is the only place in the codebase where command lists are executed, so any other state wanting multithreaded drawing must copy this block verbatim, and swapping D3D11 means editing the state machine.

Four concrete defects in the same block:
- **Ownership crosses a thread boundary as a raw pointer.** The references are created with refcount 1 by `FinishCommandList` on thread-pool workers (Level.cpp:587, 646) and released by hand here. Nothing in `Level::draw`'s signature communicates the handover.
- **Signed/unsigned compare** at :321 (`int i < command_lists.size()`) — C4018 under the project's /W4, accumulating silently since `TreatWarningAsError` is set in neither project. The sibling `check_for_pause_input` (:351) casts correctly, so the file disagrees with itself.
- **Per-frame heap allocation, 4× oversized.** `deferred_contexts->size()` is `NUM_THREADS_MAX` = 16 (Game.h:14, Game.cpp:52), but `Partitioner::partition` caps its loop at `i < num_elements` (Partitioner.cpp:10) and it is partitioning `_player_objects->size()` (max 4, Level.cpp:383). Slots 4-15 are always null. 16 deferred contexts and 16 SpriteBatches exist to service at most 4 recorders.
- **`ExecuteCommandList(..., TRUE)`** forces a full save/restore of the immediate-context state once per player per frame; the paired `FinishCommandList(TRUE, ...)` at Level.cpp:587/646 does the same.
- `get_deferred_contexts()` is fetched twice (:311 and :315) for the same value.

**Fix:** Introduce a Renderer that owns the deferred contexts, the SpriteBatch pool, and command-list recording+submission; `State::draw(Renderer&)` should only record. `ID3D11CommandList*` and `ExecuteCommandList` must not appear above the platform layer. In the interim: use `std::vector<Microsoft::WRL::ComPtr<ID3D11CommandList>>` (the project already uses ComPtr at ResourceManager.h:48), make it a member sized to the max player count and `assign(n, nullptr)` each frame, use a range-for, pass the cached local, and pass FALSE for RestoreContextState.

#### 7. MainMenuData is constructed with three null pointers and only becomes usable after a separate init() call

`ArtAttack/GameStates.cpp:4-24, 64-70` — **medium** · `lifetime`

Both `GameMenu` constructors (GameStates.cpp:4-17) build `_menu_data` with the one-argument `MainMenuData(GameData*)` ctor, which leaves `_menu_level_settings`, `_is_ready_to_load_level` (MainMenuData.h:20-21) and `MenuData::_input` (MenuData.h:16) all null. They are filled only later by `GameMenu::init()` -> `set_main_menu_data_ptrs()` (19-24, 63-70), which must run before `transition_to` creates the first page at line 26. Between construction and `init()` the object is a live, publicly reachable `MainMenuData` whose three getters return nullptr, and every consumer dereferences them unchecked: `MainMenuPage::get_player_count()` does `get_level_settings()->get_player_count()` (MainMenu.cpp:22-26), `MenuPage::get_menu_inputs()` dereferences `get_input()` (MenuPage.cpp:185-188), `MainMenuStageSelect::update` writes `*get_is_ready_to_load_level() = true` (MainMenu.cpp:1821-1822), and `GameMenu::update()` dereferences `*this->_is_ready_to_load_level` unconditionally (GameStates.cpp:72-77). Calling `update()` before `init()` is an immediate null dereference. The four-argument ctor that would avoid all of this already exists and is never used (MainMenuData.h:12-13).

**Fix:** Construct `_menu_input`, `_menu_level_settings` and `_is_ready_to_load_level` in `GameMenu`'s constructor and use the existing four-argument `MainMenuData` ctor, so the object is never observable half-built. Delete the one-argument ctor and the `set_*` mutators.

#### 8. Two-phase construction with no guard: update() and draw() dereference members that only init() creates

`ArtAttack/GameStates.cpp:19-26, 71-78, 105-127` — **medium** · `robustness`

`GameMenu`'s constructors (:4-18) create only `_game_data`, `_menu_data` and `_menu_level_settings`. `_menu_input`, `_is_ready_to_load_level` and `_menu` exist only after `init()` (:21-26). But `update()` dereferences unconditionally:
```cpp
this->_menu->update();                 // null unique_ptr if init() did not run
if (*this->_is_ready_to_load_level)    // null deref
```
and `draw()` (:87) does the same. `GameLevel` is identical: the constructor (:95-99) sets only `_game_data` and `_settings`; `_player_input`, `_menu_input`, `_level_builder` and `_level` all come from `init()` (:107-126), yet `update()` dereferences `_player_input` at :142 and `draw()` dereferences `_level` at :315. `_pause_menu_action`, `_results_menu_action` and `_end_menu_action` are dereferenced without a guard at :193, :220 and :243.

Nothing enforces the ordering. `State::init()` is a public pure virtual peer of `update`/`draw` (State.h:11-13) with no stated ordering; the only thing that makes it work is that `StateContext::transition_to` happens to call it (StateContext.cpp:24) — which is also the line that leaves a half-built state installed when it throws.

Worse, `GameMenu`'s constructor builds `_menu_data` (:6) whose three back-pointers stay null until `set_main_menu_data_ptrs()` patches them at :24. And `GameLevel::init` needs nothing that is not already available in the constructor — it only reads `get_data()` and `_settings` — so the two-phase split buys literally nothing there.

**Fix:** Do the work in the constructors and delete `init()` from the `State` interface; the context then constructs a fully valid state before publishing it, which also fixes the exception hole in `transition_to`. If a post-construction hook is genuinely needed to know the context, pass the `StateContext&` to the constructor instead of `set_context`.

#### 9. GameLevel::update is a 174-line nested switch containing five copy-pasted return-to-menu blocks

`ArtAttack/GameStates.cpp:128-301` — **medium** · `design`

One method holds the application's entire flow graph: `switch (_state)` with a nested `switch (action)` inside three of its cases, spanning :128-301. Within it the same five-line block is pasted five times (:206-213, :246-254, :256-265, :266-275, :284-293), differing only in one enum value:
```cpp
this->_level->stop_music();
MainMenuMidwayLoadSettings settings;
settings.settings = <this->_settings | MenuLevelSettings()>;
settings.screen   = main_menu_screen::<HOME|TEAM_SELECT|WEAPON_SELECT|STAGE_SELECT>;
this->get_context()->transition_to(std::make_unique<GameMenu>(this->get_data(), settings));
```
The restart path is pasted twice more (:200-205, :276-283). Every one of the seven copies is a place a future edit can be forgotten, and two of them already differ subtly (the QUIT copy lacks the braces its siblings have; the EXIT copy is indented with tabs where the others use spaces).

**Fix:** Extract `void GameLevel::return_to_menu(main_menu_screen screen, const MenuLevelSettings& settings)` and `void GameLevel::restart_level()`. Once transitions are values rather than side effects (see the transition_to finding), each menu-action case collapses to a single returned transition request and the nested switch disappears entirely.

#### 10. FIRST_UPDATE/SECOND_UPDATE warm-up hack is defeated by the fixed-timestep loop and causes a black flash

`ArtAttack/GameStates.cpp:131-139, 303-309` — **medium** · `correctness`

```cpp
case game_level_state::FIRST_UPDATE:
    this->_state = game_level_state::SECOND_UPDATE;
    return;
case game_level_state::SECOND_UPDATE:
    this->_state = game_level_state::ACTIVE;
    //no break here so it goes to active
```
with `draw()` early-returning for both states (:305-309). No comment explains what the two dead updates are waiting for; the evident intent is to swallow the huge first frame delta after `init()` loads a level. It does not work, for three reasons:

1. `Game::tick` uses a fixed timestep (`_timer.SetFixedTimeStep(true)`, Game.cpp:64) and `StepTimer::Tick` runs `while (m_leftOverTicks >= m_targetElapsedTicks) { ...; update(); }` (StepTimer.h:132-141) with the raw delta clamped to `m_qpcMaxDelta` (StepTimer.h:104-108, default 1/10s) — up to 6 `update()` calls per single `tick()` at a 1/60 target. After a slow `init()`, FIRST_UPDATE → SECOND_UPDATE → ACTIVE all fire inside one tick and the first real `_level->update()` still runs against the backlog.
2. Under fixed timestep `*this->_dt = float(timer.GetElapsedSeconds())` (Game.cpp:89-90) is always the fixed step anyway, so the large-delta problem the hack guards against cannot reach the simulation through `_dt` in the first place.
3. Despite two states, only *one* update is actually skipped — SECOND_UPDATE deliberately falls through into ACTIVE.

Meanwhile `draw()` returning early means `Game::render` clears and presents nothing: a black flash on every level start and on every RESTART, since `_state` is reset to FIRST_UPDATE at :204 and :281.

**Fix:** Delete both states and fix the root cause: call `_timer.ResetElapsedTime()` after `GameLevel::init()` and after each rebuild at :202 and :279 — that is exactly what `StepTimer::ResetElapsedTime()` exists for. It also removes the two special cases from `GameLevel::draw` and the black flash with them.

#### 11. State has init() but no on_exit(), so _level->stop_music() is hand-duplicated at seven sites and skipped on app exit

`ArtAttack/GameStates.cpp:201, 207, 248, 258, 268, 278, 286` — **medium** · `design`

`State` (State.h:11-13) declares `update`, `draw`, `init` — an entry hook with no matching exit hook. So every path that leaves the level must remember `this->_level->stop_music();` by hand: seven copies at the lines above. Forgetting an eighth when a transition is added later leaks a playing music instance over the menu.

More importantly, `Level` declares no destructor (I checked Level.h — only `void stop_music() const;` at :92, no `~Level`), so the one exit path that cannot be hand-patched is skipped: quitting the app mid-level. `Main.cpp:213-224` breaks out on WM_QUIT, `g_game.reset()` (:226) destroys `Game`, `_audio_engine` (Game.h:74) is destroyed before `_resource_manager` (Game.h:65) which owns the still-playing `SoundEffectInstance`s, and the `Level` that started them is destroyed after both via the StateContext base. Releasing a resource is the destructor's job, not seven call sites'.

**Fix:** Two independent fixes; do both. (1) Add `virtual void on_enter() {}` / `virtual void on_exit() {}` to `State`, invoked by `StateContext` around the transition — engine-level lifecycle, not a per-state convention. (2) Stop the music in `~Level()`; the sound instance it started is its resource. With (2) all seven call sites vanish immediately and the app-exit path becomes correct too.

#### 12. Missing break after case END_MENU, and case QUIT declares a non-trivial local with no braces

`ArtAttack/GameStates.cpp:240-300` — **medium** · `correctness`

Two switch defects in `GameLevel::update`, plus one that makes them hard to spot.

1. The `case game_level_state::END_MENU:` compound block closes at :297 with **no `break;`** and falls straight into `default: break;` at :298-299. Every other case in that switch terminates explicitly (FIRST_UPDATE `return` :135, ACTIVE `break` :187, PAUSE_MENU :215, RESULTS :238), so this is an inconsistency rather than a deliberate fallthrough — and it becomes a real bug the moment a `game_level_state` is inserted between END_MENU and `default`.

2. `case pause_menu_action::QUIT:` (:206-213) declares `MainMenuMidwayLoadSettings settings;` at :208 with no braces around the case body. `MainMenuMidwayLoadSettings` (MainMenu.h:104-109) contains a `MenuLevelSettings`, which contains `std::vector<MenuPlayerSettings> _player_settings` (MenuLevelSettings.h:33) — a non-trivially-initialised local inside a switch scope. It compiles only because QUIT is the last label in that switch; adding any case after it is an immediate hard error C2360. The structurally identical END_MENU cases at :246-293 all correctly brace their bodies.

3. The *deliberate* fallthrough at :137-138 (`SECOND_UPDATE` → `ACTIVE`) is marked only by the comment `//no break here so it goes to active`. MSVC has no `-Wimplicit-fallthrough`, so nothing distinguishes the intentional one from the accidental one at :297.

**Fix:** Add `break;` at :297. Brace the QUIT case body like its siblings. Once the project moves off C++14 (see the LanguageStandard finding), mark :138 `[[fallthrough]];` so the deliberate case is machine-checkable.

#### 13. check_for_pause_input returns a magic -1 and hand-rolls a search the standard library already provides

`ArtAttack/GameStates.cpp:348-359` — **medium** · `design`

```cpp
int GameLevel::check_for_pause_input(const std::vector<PlayerInputData>& player_inputs)
{
    for (int i = 0; i < static_cast<int>(player_inputs.size()); i++)
        if (player_inputs[i].toggle_pause_menu) return i;
    return -1;
}
```
The caller must know that -1 is the magic "nobody" value and compares against a bare literal (`if (pause_menu_player != -1)`, :146). The `static_cast<int>` on `size()` exists purely to make the sentinel expressible in the loop's signed index. And the codebase contains **zero** uses of any `<algorithm>` header — this is a textbook `std::find_if`.

This is the design half of the critical input-indexing finding: the returned value is also semantically wrong (an index into a compacted vector used as a player number). Fixing the sentinel without fixing the indexing leaves the real bug in place.

**Fix:** Return `std::optional<int>` (C++17) or at minimum introduce `constexpr int NO_PAUSING_PLAYER = -1;` instead of the bare literal. Implement with `std::find_if` + `std::distance`. Make the returned value a genuine player number by fixing the input vector to be slot-indexed (see the critical finding).

#### 14. GameMenu::init's screen switch has no default; an unmatched value leaves a null inner state that renders nothing forever

`ArtAttack/GameStates.cpp:28-62` — **low** · `robustness`

`init()` creates `this->_menu = std::make_unique<StateContext>();` (:26) and relies on the switch at :28-62 to populate it. The switch currently covers all eight `main_menu_screen` enumerators (MainMenu.h:92-102) but has no `default:` and no post-condition check. If `_screen` ever holds a value not listed — a new enumerator, or a garbage value read back from `MainMenuMidwayLoadSettings::screen` — `_menu` is left with a null `_state`. `StateContext::update()`/`draw()` then hit their null guards (StateContext.cpp:6, 14) and return silently, giving a game that runs at full framerate showing a cleared screen with no exception, no log and no assert.

Graded `low` rather than medium because all eight enumerators *are* currently handled, and MSVC's C4062 ("enumerator in switch is not handled", level 4, active when there is no default label) would fire at /W4 if one were added — though warnings are not errors in this project.

The switch also has inconsistent arity: five branches pass only `_menu_data.get()`, three (TEAM_SELECT :51-52, WEAPON_SELECT :55-56, STAGE_SELECT :59-60) also pass `_menu_level_settings.get()` — despite `MainMenuData` already carrying the settings pointer via `set_level_settings` at :66, making the second argument redundant.

**Fix:** Add `default: throw std::logic_error("unhandled main_menu_screen");`, or assert in debug with a fallback to TITLE.
