Better: give every page a uniform constructor taking one `MainMenuData*` (which already carries the settings) and replace the switch with a registry keyed by `main_menu_screen`, so adding a screen without wiring it fails at startup rather than rendering a blank screen.

#### 15. std::move applied to a prvalue return value, defeating copy elision

`ArtAttack/GameStates.cpp:125-126, 202-203, 279-280` — **low** · `modern-cpp`

Three sites do `this->_level = std::move(this->_level_builder->build_level(this->_settings));`. `LevelBuilder::build_level` already returns `std::unique_ptr<Level>` **by value** (LevelBuilder.h:26), so the expression is already a prvalue. Wrapping it in `std::move` turns it into an xvalue and blocks elision into the assignment. MSVC /W4 does not diagnose this; clang and gcc emit `-Wpessimizing-move`.

**Fix:** `this->_level = this->_level_builder->build_level(this->_settings);` at all three sites.

#### 16. Menu sub-objects are rebuilt in reverse dependency order and are never released when the overlay closes

`ArtAttack/GameStates.cpp:150-162, 169-181, 225-236` — **low** · `lifetime`

```cpp
this->_pause_menu_action = std::make_unique<pause_menu_action>(NONE);  // :150 frees the OLD action
this->_pause_menu_data   = std::make_unique<PauseMenuData>(..., _pause_menu_action.get()); // :153 frees the OLD data
this->_pause_menu        = std::make_unique<StateContext>();           // :159 frees the OLD menu
```
The assignments are the exact reverse of the dependency order. At :150 the previous `pause_menu_action` is deleted while the previous `_pause_menu_data` — still alive — holds a pointer to it, and the previous `_pause_menu`'s page still holds a pointer to that data. Only at :159 is the top of the chain released. Identical shape at :169-181 (results) and :225-236 (end menu). I checked and nothing dereferences through the stale pointers in that window, so this is a latent hazard rather than an active bug — hence `low`.

The related lifetime sloppiness is more visible: on `RESUME` (:197-199) the code sets `_state = ACTIVE` and nothing else, so the whole pause-menu tree, its data and its stale `RESUME` action stay alive until the next pause press — which then rebuilds a `StateContext`, a `PauseMenuData` and a `PauseMenuInitial` (loading its widget tree) mid-frame, a visible hitch at the exact moment the player pauses. The RESULTS objects are likewise never freed once END_MENU is entered. `GameMenu::_is_ready_to_load_level` is never reset to false either.

**Fix:** Tear down top-down before rebuilding bottom-up (`_pause_menu.reset(); _pause_menu_data.reset(); _pause_menu_action.reset();`), or better: build the overlay objects once in `init()` and `reset()` them on entry, and release them explicitly on exit so ownership matches lifetime.

#### 17. END_MENU case has no break and one pause case declares a local without braces

`ArtAttack/GameStates.cpp:240-300` — **low** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

Two latent landmines in the same switch.

1. The `game_level_state::END_MENU` case block (lines 240-297) ends without a `break;`. It currently falls into `default: break;` at lines 298-299, so behaviour is correct today — but it is the only case in the switch missing its break (FIRST_UPDATE returns at 135, SECOND_UPDATE falls through *deliberately* with a comment at 138, ACTIVE breaks at 187, PAUSE_MENU at 215, RESULTS at 238), and inserting any new case between END_MENU and `default` silently changes behaviour.

2. `case pause_menu_action::QUIT:` (lines 206-213) declares a local with a non-trivial constructor directly under a case label with no enclosing braces:

        case pause_menu_action::QUIT:
            this->_level->stop_music();
            MainMenuMidwayLoadSettings settings;   // MenuLevelSettings member -> non-trivial init
            settings.settings = MenuLevelSettings();

   This only compiles because QUIT is the last label in that switch. Adding any case after it makes MSVC reject the whole function with C2361 ("initialization of 'settings' is skipped by 'default' label"). Every other case that declares this same local wraps itself in braces (247, 257, 267, 277, 285) — this one was missed.

The wider issue is that `GameLevel::update` is a 170-line nested switch (lines 128-301) mixing frame skipping, input polling, level ticking and five different menu constructions; the missing brace and missing break are symptoms of that.

**Fix:** Add the `break;` and the braces. Then split the body: one small handler function per `game_level_state` (`update_active()`, `update_pause_menu()`, `update_results()`, `update_end_menu()`), each returning the next state. The FIRST_UPDATE/SECOND_UPDATE pair (a two-frame warm-up implemented as two enum values that just fall forward) should be a named `int _warmup_frames` or removed entirely once the cause of needing it is understood.

#### 18. ExecuteCommandList/FinishCommandList request full state restore in the level path and not in the menu path

`ArtAttack/GameStates.cpp:321-330` — **low** · `performance`

`immediate_context->ExecuteCommandList(command_lists[i], TRUE)` (GameStates.cpp:328) passes `RestoreContextState = TRUE`, the documented expensive path, once per player per frame. `Level::draw_player_view_level` (Level.cpp:587) and `draw_zoom_out_level_component` (Level.cpp:646) likewise pass `TRUE` to `FinishCommandList`. The identical operation in the menu path passes `FALSE` (MenuPage.cpp:117 and :161), so the two halves of the engine disagree about whether the restore is needed.

Nothing depends on it: `Game::clear()` re-binds the render target and viewport on every context at the start of every frame (Game.cpp:129-149), so the saved state is discarded immediately.

**Fix:** Pass `FALSE` everywhere and set state explicitly at the start of each recording, which the code already does. Wrap the execute-and-release loop in one helper so the flag exists in a single place.

## `ArtAttack/ICollisionGameObject.h`

_7 findings: 1 critical, 3 high, 1 medium, 2 low_

#### 1. The core collision interface identifies objects with an enum of this game's content

`ArtAttack/ICollisionGameObject.h:5, 14 (with collision_object_type.h:4-88)` — **critical** · `design` · confidence: certain

`ICollisionGameObject` — the engine's fundamental collidable abstraction — includes `collision_object_type.h` (line 5) and exposes `virtual collision_object_type get_collision_object_type() const = 0;` (line 14). That enum (collision_object_type.h:4-29) is a flat cross-product of class x team x weapon: `PLAYER_TEAM_A`, `PLAYER_TEAM_B_DEAD`, `PROJECTILE_SPRAY_TEAM_A`, `PROJECTILE_MIST_TEAM_B`, `PAINT_TILE`, `STRUCTURE_RAMP_LEFT`, ... The header then ships 8 free predicates (`is_team_a_projectile`, `is_dead_player`, ...) at lines 31-88 that hardcode the same content.

Consequence: every collidable in any future game must declare itself as one of *this* game's 23 types. Adding a weapon means editing an engine header and recompiling every TU that touches collision. Adding a third team is a combinatorial edit. It also forces the same if/else identity ladder to be rewritten in every object (Player.cpp:186-244, PaintTile.cpp:114-140, StructurePaintable.cpp:64-102, Level.cpp:238, Level.cpp:713-715).

This is the single most pervasive engine/game inversion in the repo: the game's content model *is* the engine's type system.

**Fix:** Replace the enum with data the engine does not interpret: a `CollisionLayer`/`CollisionMask` bitset plus an opaque game-owned tag (e.g. `uint32_t user_type` or a `void*`/`std::any` payload). The engine filters pairs by layer/mask; the *game* decides what `PROJECTILE_SPRAY_TEAM_A` means by casting/inspecting its own tag in its own `on_collision`. Move `collision_object_type.h` out of the engine entirely into game/ as `game_collision_tags.h`.

#### 2. is_colliding lives on the interface, so every object implements the whole narrow phase — and the relation is not symmetric

`ArtAttack/ICollisionGameObject.h:12-13` — **high** · `design`

Because the interface asks each object "are you colliding with this other object?", the same four-step algorithm (type filter → AABB test → shape test) is written out separately in Player.cpp:148-185, PaintTile.cpp:84-109, ProjectileSpray.cpp:56, ProjectileJet.cpp:54, ProjectileBall.cpp:55, ProjectileMist.cpp:56 and ProjectileRolling.cpp:48.

Worse, `Structure::is_colliding` (Structure.cpp:43-46) is:
```cpp
bool Structure::is_colliding(const ICollisionGameObject* other) const
{
	return false;
}
```
So the answer to "are these two colliding" depends on which one you ask. `Level::update_level_logic` therefore has to ask both orderings and dispatch `on_collision` to each participant twice per frame (Level.cpp:222-293, three overlapping loop nests with the same pairs tested twice and only an `object == object_2` self-check).

Every cheap rejection also costs 5+ virtual calls, because everything a pair needs (`get_for_deletion`, `get_collision_object_type`, `get_shape`, and `get_bounding_box` inside the shape test) is behind a pure virtual. There is no broad phase at all, and the `ThreadPool`/`Partitioner` the project already owns are used only for drawing (Level.cpp:379-400) — collision is single-threaded and unaccelerated over a list that grows with every projectile fired (Level.cpp:204-210).

**Fix:** Remove `is_colliding` from the interface. Leave `get_shape()` plus a layer mask and a cached AABB the level can read without dispatch; a `CollisionSystem` computes intersection once per pair and calls `on_collision` on each participant with the contact. Intersection logic then lives in exactly one place (`MattMath::Shape::intersects`, where it already is) and symmetry is structural rather than a convention each class must remember.

#### 3. Splatoon rules are welded into the engine's core collision interface via collision_object_type

`ArtAttack/ICollisionGameObject.h:14` — **high** · `design`

`virtual collision_object_type get_collision_object_type() const = 0;` makes a 23-value enum that cross-multiplies class × team × weapon part of the fundamental collision contract. `collision_object_type.h:4-29` literally enumerates `PROJECTILE_MIST_TEAM_B`, `PROJECTILE_ROLLING_TEAM_A`, `PLAYER_TEAM_A_DEAD`, `STRUCTURE_RAMP_LEFT`, `PAINT_TILE`. Adding a sixth weapon adds two enumerators and forces edits to every if/else chain keyed on it; adding a third team is a combinatorial rewrite.

The header also ships the game's classification rules as eight inline free functions (`is_player`, `is_projectile`, `is_team_a_projectile`, `is_structure_ramp`, …, collision_object_type.h:31-88) — game rules living in an engine header — and those rules are then re-derived by hand anyway at the use sites (Player::on_collision, PaintTile::on_collision, StructurePaintable::on_collision, Level::count_projectiles).

For a project whose stated goal is a reusable 2D engine, this is the single largest obstacle to reusing the collision layer for anything else: the engine cannot describe a collision without naming Splatoon's weapons and teams.

**Fix:** The engine interface should carry only `get_shape()` and a numeric collision layer/mask bitfield used for broad-phase filtering; the game supplies the layer meanings. Identity ("is this an enemy projectile?") belongs to game-side data on the entity (team id, damage source), and the branching should be a response table or double dispatch rather than a type-tag ladder.

#### 4. Boolean accessors split between `get_x()` and `is_x()` with no rule; the worst offender is on a core engine interface

`ArtAttack/ICollisionGameObject.h:16` — **high** · `naming` · confidence: certain

`virtual bool get_for_deletion() const = 0;` (ICollisionGameObject.h:16) reads as "fetch the for-deletion" rather than a question, and it sits on the interface every collidable object in the engine implements. It is not an isolated slip - the codebase has two competing conventions for bool accessors:
  `get_` form: `ICollisionGameObject.h:16` / `Player.h:97` / `Projectile.h:47` / `PaintTile.h:76` / `Structure.h:33` (`get_for_deletion`), `AnimationStrip.h:16` (`get_looping`), `Mh.h:18` (`get_hidden`), `Save.h:26` (`get_fullscreen`), `Player.h:109-111,115,227` (`get_input_primary_shoot`, `get_input_jump_pressed`, `get_input_jump_held`, `get_showing_debug`, `get_facing_right`), `Weapon.h:73,75,79` (`get_invert_x`, `get_invert_y`, `get_gun_player_aligned`).
  `is_` form: `AnimatedSprite.h:35` / `AnimationObject.h:28` (`is_paused`), `IGameObject.h:13` (`is_visible_in_viewport`), `ICollisionGameObject.h:12` (`is_colliding`), `Player.h:250-251` (`is_on_ground`, `is_on_ramp`), `SoundBank.h:32` (`is_effect_looping`).
So `AnimationStrip::get_looping()` and `SoundBank::is_effect_looping()` ask the same question two ways.

**Fix:** One rule: bool accessors read as predicates. `get_for_deletion` -> `is_flagged_for_deletion`, `get_looping` -> `is_looping`, `get_hidden` -> `is_hidden`, `get_fullscreen` -> `is_fullscreen`, `get_facing_right` -> `is_facing_right`, `get_showing_debug` -> `is_showing_debug`, `get_invert_x/y` -> `is_x/y_inverted`, `get_gun_player_aligned` -> `is_gun_player_aligned`, `get_input_jump_pressed` -> `is_jump_pressed`.

#### 5. get_for_deletion is a read-only self-destruct flag with no way to request destruction and no owner of lifetime

`ArtAttack/ICollisionGameObject.h:16` — **medium** · `design`

`virtual bool get_for_deletion() const = 0;` — an object can only be *asked* whether it wants to die. There is no interface to tell one to die and no reason attached. `Level` polls it and does a hand-written swap-with-back erase using a decrementing `size_t` index (Level.cpp:296-305):
```cpp
for (size_t i = 0; i < this->_collision_objects->size(); i++)
    if (this->_collision_objects->at(i)->get_for_deletion()) {
        this->_collision_objects->at(i) = std::move(this->_collision_objects->back());
        this->_collision_objects->pop_back();
        i--;   // wraps to SIZE_MAX when i == 0, then ++ brings it back to 0
    }
```
Meanwhile other lifetime conditions in the same function are signalled by throwing instead (Level.cpp:312, 319, `"Player out of bounds"`). So object lifetime is split across a per-object boolean, one hand-rolled erase loop hardcoded to one specific container, and exceptions — three mechanisms for one concern, none of them owned by anything.

The name is also wrong for a bool predicate: `get_for_deletion()` should be `is_marked_for_deletion()`.

**Fix:** The world owns lifetime. Give the engine an entity handle and a `World::destroy(Handle)` command queue drained at a defined point in the frame; anything — the object itself, a collision response, an out-of-bounds check — can enqueue a destroy. `get_for_deletion` then disappears from the interface entirely.

#### 6. Duplicate MattMath.h include, raw pointers where references are meant, no [[nodiscard]] on any query, misnamed predicate

`ArtAttack/ICollisionGameObject.h:4-6, 12-16` — **low** · `modern-cpp`

Four small header hygiene issues on the collision interface.

1. **Duplicate include.** `ICollisionGameObject.h:4` includes `IGameObject.h`, which already includes `MattMath.h` at IGameObject.h:4; line 6 then includes `"MattMath.h"` again. MattMath.h is 1139 lines and pulls `SimpleMath.h`, `<d3d11.h>` and `<vector>`, while nothing in these interfaces needs more than `RectangleF`, `Camera` and `Shape`. `DirectX::SpriteBatch` is used only as a pointer and could be forward-declared.

2. **Pointers where references are meant.** `is_colliding(const ICollisionGameObject* other)` and `on_collision(const ICollisionGameObject* other)` take pointers, but null is not a meaningful argument and not one of the ~10 implementations checks for it (Player.cpp:148-185, PaintTile.cpp:84-109, ProjectileSpray.cpp:56, ProjectileJet.cpp:54, ProjectileBall.cpp:55, ProjectileMist.cpp:56, ProjectileRolling.cpp:48). Same for `DirectX::SpriteBatch*` in IGameObject.h:11-12.

3. **No `[[nodiscard]]` anywhere.** I grepped all first-party sources: zero occurrences. Pure queries like `is_colliding`, `get_collision_object_type`, `get_shape`, `get_for_deletion`, `is_visible_in_viewport` and all 27 MovingObject getters can be called and silently discarded. (Requires C++17 — see the LanguageStandard finding.)

4. **Misnamed predicate.** `get_for_deletion()` returns a bool; it should be `is_marked_for_deletion()`.

5. **Copy not suppressed.** `IGameObject`, `ICollisionGameObject`, `State` and `MovingObject` all declare a virtual destructor and stop there, which suppresses implicit *move* but leaves implicit *copy*. Given two `ICollisionGameObject&`, `a = b;` compiles and slices. For `MovingObject`, which carries `_velocity`/`_dx`/`_rotation`, that would half-copy physics state.

**Fix:** Remove the duplicate MattMath.h include; split MattMath.h into per-type headers and include only what each interface needs; forward-declare `namespace DirectX { class SpriteBatch; }`. Take `const ICollisionGameObject&` and `SpriteBatch&`. Add `[[nodiscard]]` to every pure query. Rename `get_for_deletion`. Add protected/deleted copy and move to every abstract base.

#### 7. get_shape() hands out a raw interior pointer with no lifetime contract, while the same interface defines the deletion protocol

`ArtAttack/ICollisionGameObject.h:15` — **low** · `ownership`

`virtual const MattMath::Shape* get_shape() const = 0;` returns the address of a member shape (e.g. `Player::get_shape` returns `this->get_collision_rectangle()`, Player.cpp:128-131). Nothing in the signature or a comment says how long it is valid, whether it may be stored, whether it survives `update()`, or whether it can be null.

The *same interface* declares `get_for_deletion()` at :16, and `Level::update_level_logic` acts on it by swap-erasing entries out of `_collision_objects` mid-frame (Level.cpp:296-305) — which destroys the object and would dangle any `Shape*` obtained from it earlier. `Level` also `push_back`s newly spawned projectiles into that same vector while the frame is in progress (Level.cpp:209), invalidating references into it.

I checked and no current caller holds a `Shape*` across either operation, so this is an undocumented contract rather than a live bug — hence `low`. `CollisionTools::resolve_object_collision` taking a *mutable* `Shape*` and mutating it in place makes the contract genuinely ambiguous, though.

**Fix:** Return `const Shape&` so it cannot be null and is harder to store casually, and document the validity window on the interface. Longer term, separate collision geometry from the object so the broad phase can own it in a contiguous array with stable handles rather than pointers into scattered heap objects.

## `ArtAttack/Level.cpp`

_33 findings: 5 critical, 12 high, 7 medium, 9 low_

#### 1. player_inputs is compacted to connected pads but indexed by player-object index (OOB read)

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:188-193` — **critical** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

`PlayerInput::update_and_get_player_inputs()` (ArtAttack/PlayerInput.cpp:126-137) builds its result with `if (current[i].connected) { ... result.push_back(input); }` — the vector is COMPACTED, so its indices are "nth connected pad", not "player number". `Level::update_level_logic` then does:

```
int player_index = 0;
for (const auto& object : *this->_player_objects)
{
    object->set_player_input(player_inputs[player_index]);
```

`_player_objects` is fixed at level-build time. The moment any pad disconnects, `player_inputs.size() < _player_objects->size()` and `operator[]` reads past the end — and the players that survive are driven by the WRONG controller (unplug pad 0 in a 2-player match and player 0 is now steered by pad 1). If *all* pads go away the vector is empty and `player_inputs[0]` is an out-of-bounds read on an empty vector on the very first iteration.

That last case is not hypothetical and is reachable without touching any hardware: minimising the window sends WM_SIZE/SIZE_MINIMIZED (ArtAttack/Main.cpp:281-291) → `Game::on_suspending()` (ArtAttack/Game.cpp:171-176) → `_gamepad->Suspend()`, while the main loop keeps calling `tick()` (ArtAttack/Main.cpp:213-224) → `GameLevel::update()` ACTIVE branch → `_player_input->update_and_get_player_inputs()` on a suspended GamePad, which reports every pad disconnected. So minimising during a match walks straight into the empty-vector index.

The same index-confusion exists in the pause menu: `GameLevel::check_for_pause_input` (ArtAttack/GameStates.cpp:348-358) returns `i`, an index into the compacted `player_inputs`, which is stored as `player_num` and later used as a direct subscript into a *different* compacted vector — `inputs[player_num]` at ArtAttack/PauseMenu.cpp:48-53 and 217-222. Note that every other menu iterates `for (i = 0; i < inputs.size(); i++)` correctly (ArtAttack/MainMenu.cpp:49-51, ArtAttack/EndMenu.cpp:32, ArtAttack/ResultsMenu.cpp:266) — only the gameplay and pause paths get it wrong.

**Fix:** Stop compacting. Return a fixed `std::array<PlayerInputData, 4>` (or a vector sized to the player count) indexed by player slot, and use the already-present but currently dead `PlayerInputData::connection` field (ArtAttack/PlayerInputData.h:19; `calculate_player_input` unconditionally writes `connection_state::CONNECTED` at ArtAttack/PlayerInput.cpp:111, so DISCONNECTED is never produced) to mark absent pads. Then `Level::update_level_logic` looks up by `player->get_player_num()` and treats a disconnected pad as neutral input / auto-pause instead of indexing off the end.

#### 2. Level indexes the connection-compacted input vector by player ordinal - OOB read on any pad dropout

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:189-192` — **critical** · `memory-safety` · confidence: certain

`Level::update_level_logic` walks `*this->_player_objects` with a running counter and uses it as a subscript into the input vector:

```cpp
int player_index = 0;
for (const auto& object : *this->_player_objects)
{
    object->set_player_input(player_inputs[player_index]);   // Level.cpp:192
    ...
    player_index++;
}
```

`_player_objects->size()` is fixed at level build time and equals the menu's player count (`PlayerBuilder::build_players`, PlayerBuilder.cpp:27, iterates `settings.get_player_settings()`, whose size is forced to `_player_count` by `MenuLevelSettings::set_player_count`, MenuLevelSettings.cpp:9-25).

`player_inputs.size()` is NOT the player count. `PlayerInput::update_and_get_player_inputs` (PlayerInput.cpp:126-137) only `push_back`s entries for slots that reported `IsConnected()`, so its size is the number of *currently connected* pads.

Mid-match trace (2 players, pads in XInput slots 0 and 1, player 2's pad unplugged):
1. PlayerInput.cpp:124 `get_raw_input(1)` -> `pad.IsConnected()` false -> `current[1].connected` stays false (PlayerInput.h:25 default).
2. PlayerInput.cpp:129 skips the push_back, so `result.size() == 1`.
3. GameStates.cpp:141-142 hands that 1-element vector to `Level::update`, GameStates.cpp:185.
4. Level.cpp:192 with `player_index == 1` reads `player_inputs[1]` on a size-1 vector - out of bounds. `std::vector::operator[]` is unchecked in Release; in Debug MSVC's `_ITERATOR_DEBUG_LEVEL` assert fires and the process aborts.

Observable effect in Release: player 2 is fed ~48 bytes of whatever follows the vector buffer, reinterpreted as `PlayerInputData`. `x_movement` becomes a garbage float that is multiplied straight into velocity (`X_INITIAL_VELOCITY * x_input`, Player.cpp:769; `X_ACCELERATION * dt * x_input`, Player.cpp:774) - so the abandoned player teleports or accelerates unboundedly, which then trips `throw std::exception("Player out of bounds")` at Level.cpp:312. Nothing catches it; the app terminates.

The *all* pads case is worse and does not need an unplug: if the vector is empty, `player_inputs[0]` is dereferencing a null/garbage `_Myfirst` pointer.

Note `Level.h:143` declares `std::vector<PlayerInputData> _player_inputs` which is never read or written anywhere - a vestige of the design that would have avoided this.

**Fix:** Stop compacting. Have `PlayerInput::update_and_get_player_inputs()` return a fixed 4-element (`GamePad::MAX_PLAYER_COUNT`) array/vector where disconnected slots carry `connection_state::DISCONNECTED` and zeroed axes - the `connection` field in `PlayerInputData` already exists for exactly this and is currently dead. Then store the owning XInput slot on `Player` (it already has `_player_num`, Player.cpp:1077) and look up `player_inputs[player->get_pad_slot()]`, treating DISCONNECTED as "no input this frame" rather than as a shorter vector. As a stopgap, guard the loop with `if (player_index >= player_inputs.size()) { object->set_player_input(PlayerInputData()); }`.

#### 3. Every render worker draws every object, and draw() mutates the object — guaranteed data race

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:491-592` — **critical** · `concurrency` · confidence: certain

`Level::draw_active_level` (Level.cpp:375-400) partitions *players* across thread-pool tasks:

```
auto partitioned_players = this->_partitioner->partition(this->_player_objects->size(), num_threads);
for (int i = 0; i < partitioned_players.size(); i++)
    this->_thread_pool->add_task([this, i, partitioned_players, ...]{ this->draw_player_view_level(...); });
```

But inside `draw_player_view_level` each task iterates the *entire* world, not its slice (Level.cpp:516-540):

```
for (auto& object : *this->_non_collision_objects) { ... object->draw(sprite_batches->at(i), camera); }
for (auto& object : *this->_collision_objects)     { ... object->draw(sprite_batches->at(i), camera); }
for (auto& object : *this->_player_objects)        { ... object->draw(sprite_batches->at(i), camera); }
```

So in a 2-4 player match, 2-4 threads call `draw()` on the *same* object concurrently. `IGameObject::draw` is non-const (IGameObject.h:11-12) and the implementations write member state:

- `Player::draw` (Player.cpp:54-86): `this->_animation_state = new_animation_state;`, `TextureObject::set_sprite_sheet_name(info.sprite_sheet);`, `TextureObject::set_element_name(info.uniform_texture);`, `set_animation_strip_and_reset(...)` (which resets `_frame_index`/`_time_elapsed`, AnimationObject.cpp:108-112), `set_frame_time(...)`, `TextureObject::set_effects(effects)`, `AnimationObject::set_effects(effects)`.
- `Weapon::draw` (Weapon.cpp:61-64, 71-76): `set_element_name(...)`, `set_origin(...)`, `set_effects(...)`, `set_draw_rotation(...)`.
- `PaintTile::draw` (PaintTile.cpp:34-53): `this->set_colour(...)`, `this->_splash.set_colour(...)`, `this->_splash.set_rectangle_center(...)` — and `StructurePaintable::draw` (StructurePaintable.cpp:45-52) loops every tile, from every thread.

`set_element_name`/`set_sprite_sheet_name` assign `std::string` members (SpriteSheetObject.h:25-26). Concurrent `std::string::operator=` on the same object is not merely a torn value — it is concurrent free/allocate on the same control block, i.e. heap corruption. This is the single most serious defect found in the sweep and it fires on every multiplayer frame. Note the codebase contains **zero** uses of `std::mutex`, `std::atomic`, or any synchronisation primitive (grepped across all first-party sources).

**Fix:** Split the render pass into a lock-free shape: (1) make `draw` a `const` operation on immutable per-frame state — move all the animation/effect/name mutation out of `draw` and into `update`, which runs single-threaded; (2) have each task record only its own slice, i.e. per-viewport visibility should not require re-walking global containers from N threads mutating shared objects. Longer term, produce an immutable per-frame render packet list during update and let workers consume it read-only.

#### 4. Every draw task mutates the same shared game objects: unsynchronised data race on Player/PaintTile state

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:516-540` — **critical** · `concurrency` · confidence: certain

`Level::draw_active_level` (Level.cpp:386-397) submits one task per *partition of players*, and each task runs `draw_player_view_level`, which iterates **all** objects, not just its own partition:

```cpp
for (auto& object : *this->_non_collision_objects)  // Level.cpp:516
    if (object->is_visible_in_viewport(camera_view)) object->draw(sprite_batches->at(i), camera);
for (auto& object : *this->_collision_objects)      // Level.cpp:525
    ...
for (auto& object : *this->_player_objects)         // Level.cpp:534
    ...
```

With 4 players there are 4 concurrent tasks and every task calls `draw()` on every one of those objects. `IGameObject::draw` is declared **non-const** (IGameObject.h:11-12) and the implementations write member state:

`Player::draw` (Player.cpp:47-88):
```cpp
this->_animation_state = new_animation_state;          // :59
TextureObject::set_sprite_sheet_name(info.sprite_sheet); // :62  (std::string assignment)
TextureObject::set_element_name(info.uniform_texture);   // :63  (std::string assignment)
set_animation_strip_and_reset(...); set_frame_time(...);  // :65-72
TextureObject::set_effects(effects);                     // :83
AnimationObject::set_effects(effects);                   // :86
```

`PaintTile::draw` (PaintTile.cpp:34-53) does the same: `this->set_colour(...)`, `this->_splash.set_colour(...)`, `this->_splash.set_rectangle_center(...)` — and every `StructurePaintable` forwards `draw` to its whole tile grid (StructurePaintable.cpp:45-52), so thousands of tiles are concurrently written by 4 threads.

These are plain non-atomic member writes, including `std::string` assignment (which reallocates). Four threads writing the same `std::string` is heap corruption, not just a torn value. There is no mutex, no atomic, no per-thread copy anywhere in the codebase.

This is the root design error behind the whole parallel-draw scheme: `draw` was allowed to be a mutating operation, so it can never be run concurrently over a shared scene.

**Fix:** Make `IGameObject::draw` (and every override) `const`, and move all the state changes it currently performs — animation-state selection, sprite-sheet/element switching, effects flags, paint-tile colour — into `update()`, which runs single-threaded. The compiler will then enforce that a draw task cannot mutate shared scene state. Until that refactor lands, the parallel draw path is not safe and `draw_active_level` should fall back to the serial loop that is still sitting commented out at Level.cpp:402-490.

#### 5. draw_zoom_out_level_component runs on a worker thread but mutates ViewportManager and touches the IMMEDIATE device context

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:595-651` — **critical** · `concurrency` · confidence: certain

`draw_zoom_out_level` pushes the whole zoom-out draw onto the pool:

```cpp
void Level::draw_zoom_out_level(...) const
{
    int num_threads = this->_thread_pool->get_max_num_threads();   // :599  never used (C4189 under /W4)
    this->_thread_pool->add_task([this, deferred_contexts, command_lists, sprite_batches]()
        { this->draw_zoom_out_level_component(deferred_contexts, command_lists, sprite_batches); });  // :601
    this->_thread_pool->wait_for_tasks_to_complete();               // :606
}
```

The callback body then does, **on a background thread**:

```cpp
this->_viewport_manager->set_layout(screen_layout::ONE_PLAYER);  // :619
this->_viewport_manager->apply_player_viewport(0);               // :620
```

Two separate defects:

1. `ViewportManager::set_layout` (ViewportManager.cpp:79-82) is a **non-const mutator** writing the shared `_layout` member that the main thread reads from `get_all_viewports`, `get_player_viewport`, `get_viewport_dividers`. It is reached from a `const` member function through the non-const raw pointer `ViewportManager* _viewport_manager` (Level.h:118) — the `const` on `draw_zoom_out_level` is decoration only. It is also a permanent side effect hidden inside a draw call: the layout is clobbered to ONE_PLAYER and never restored.

2. `apply_player_viewport(int)` — the one-argument overload (ViewportManager.cpp:63-70) — does:
```cpp
auto context = this->_device_resources->GetD3DDeviceContext();  // the IMMEDIATE context
context->RSSetViewports(1, &vp);
this->_sprite_batch->SetViewport(vp);                            // sprite batch #0, owned by deferred ctx 0
```
So a worker thread issues a command on the immediate context and reconfigures SpriteBatch 0 while the main thread is inside `Game::render`/`Present`. `ID3D11DeviceContext` is explicitly not thread-safe; the whole point of the 16 deferred contexts (Game.cpp:52, DeviceResources.cpp:716-730) is that workers must never touch the immediate one. The three-argument overload that takes an explicit context exists (ViewportManager.cpp:53-61) and is what the rest of the worker code correctly uses (Level.cpp:506, MenuPage.cpp:107).

Submitting exactly one task and then immediately blocking on it also means this path pays a full thread-pool round trip to gain zero parallelism.

**Fix:** Do not run this on the pool at all — call `draw_zoom_out_level_component` directly on the calling thread and delete the unused `num_threads`. Hoist `set_layout` out of the draw path into `Level::update` (draw must not change simulation/presentation state). Replace `apply_player_viewport(0)` with the three-arg overload `apply_player_viewport(0, deferred_contexts->at(0), sprite_batches->at(0))` so the immediate context is never touched off the main thread, and delete the one-argument overload so it cannot be reached again.

#### 6. Quit-to-main-menu from the pause menu leaves weapon loop sounds playing forever

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:61-64` — **high** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

`Level::stop_music()` stops exactly one instance:

    void Level::stop_music() const
    {
        this->_sound_bank->stop_effect(this->_music_name, true);
    }

Player weapon sounds are separate *looping* `SoundEffectInstance`s started by `Weapon::handle_shoot_sound` (Weapon.cpp:240-246, `play_effect(sound_name, true, ...)`). They are only stopped by `Level::stop_player_sounds()` (Level.cpp:323-330), which is reached from exactly one place — the natural ACTIVE -> ZOOM_OUT transition at Level.cpp:135. The pause-menu exits never reach it:

    // GameStates.cpp:206-213
    case pause_menu_action::QUIT:
        this->_level->stop_music();          // music only
        ... transition_to(GameMenu)
    // GameStates.cpp:200-205
    case pause_menu_action::RESTART:
        this->_level->stop_music();          // music only
        this->_level = std::move(... build_level ...);

The instances live in the shared `SoundBank` owned by `ResourceManager` (SoundBank.h:41, `_sound_effect_instances`), not in the `Weapon`, so destroying the `Level` does not stop them. Pausing mid-fire and quitting therefore drops you into the main menu with the sprayer/roller/mister loop still playing, over the main-menu music (MainMenu.cpp:276 `play_effect(MUSIC, true, ...)`). On RESTART the stale loop only stops if match 2 happens to contain a player with the identical (team, player_num) weapon sound name.

**Fix:** Add `void Level::stop_all_sounds() const { stop_music(); stop_player_sounds(); }` and call that from every exit branch instead of `stop_music()`. Better still, give `Level` an actual destructor that stops everything it started, so no caller has to remember — the current design duplicates the teardown call at seven sites in `GameLevel::update` and gets it wrong at two of them.

#### 7. player_inputs is indexed by player-object position but the vector only contains connected pads

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:189-201` — **high** · `correctness`

`update_level_logic` walks `_player_objects` and indexes the input vector by loop position:
```cpp
int player_index = 0;
for (const auto& object : *this->_player_objects)
{
    object->set_player_input(player_inputs[player_index]);
```
`PlayerInput::update_and_get_player_inputs()` (PlayerInput.cpp:119-138) **compacts** — it only `push_back`s for pads where `current[i].connected`:
```cpp
for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++)
    if (current[i].connected) result.push_back(calculate_player_input(current[i], _prev_inputs[i]));
```
Two bugs follow. (1) If any pad disconnects mid-match, `player_inputs.size() < _player_objects->size()` and `player_inputs[player_index]` reads past the end — `operator[]` is unchecked, so silent UB. (2) Even without a size mismatch, if pad 1 of 0..3 drops while 0, 2, 3 stay connected, entries shift down and player object 1 is driven by pad 2.

The same loop also uses `player_index` for `_viewport_manager->get_player_viewport(player_index)` (Level.cpp:198), while `draw_player_view_level` uses `object->get_player_num()` for the same lookup (Level.cpp:503-511). Two indexing schemes that agree only by coincidence.

**Fix:** Have PlayerInput return a fixed 4-element array indexed by pad slot with a `connected` flag, and look it up as `player_inputs[object->get_player_num()]` with a neutral-input fallback when that pad is absent. Switch Level.cpp:198 to `get_player_num()` so update and draw agree.

#### 8. "Still on the ground" is inferred from any structure overlap, so wall and jump-through contact suppresses on_no_collision()

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:221-249` — **high** · `correctness`

```cpp
bool player_colliding_with_structure = false;
for (auto& other_object : *this->_collision_objects) {
    if (other_object->get_for_deletion()) continue;
    if (player->is_colliding(other_object.get())) {
        player->on_collision(other_object.get());
        other_object->on_collision(player.get());
        if (is_structure(other_object->get_collision_object_type()))
            player_colliding_with_structure = true;
    }
}
if (!player_colliding_with_structure) player->on_no_collision();
```
`Player::on_no_collision` (Player.cpp:1252-1263) is the *only* thing that moves the player out of ON_GROUND/ON_DROP_DOWN_GROUND/ON_RAMP_* into IN_AIR. But the flag is set for any structure that merely overlaps, regardless of how the collision resolved:
- `Player::on_left_collision` / `on_right_collision` (Player.cpp:562-575) zero velocity_x and push out but deliberately never touch move_state. A player who walks off a ledge while still brushing a wall keeps move_state == ON_GROUND and can jump in mid-air while hugging the wall.
- `Player::on_structure_jump_through_collision` (Player.cpp:360-382) returns without resolving when the player is rising through or dropping through the platform — yet `is_structure(STRUCTURE_JUMP_THROUGH)` is true, so the flag is set and the player is treated as grounded while passing *through* a one-way platform.

The flag is also computed over the pre-resolution overlap set, so an object that only overlapped before push-out still counts. Ground state is game logic; it should be produced by the collision responses, not inferred by the loop driver.

**Fix:** Have `Player` track a per-frame `_grounded_this_frame` flag that only `on_bottom_collision` and the ramp handlers set, and call `on_no_collision()` at the end of the player's collision pass when it is still false. `Level` should not be classifying collision types at all.

#### 9. O(n²) collision inlined into Level with no broad phase, and object-object pairs visited in both orderings

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:221-293` — **high** · `performance`

Three hand-written nested loops with no abstraction between them and the object list:
- loop 1 (:222-249): for each player, for each collision object
- loop 2 (:259-273): for each collision object, for each player
- loop 3 (:277-292): for each object, for each *other* object — the pair (a,b) is visited as (a,b) and again as (b,a), so `is_colliding` is evaluated twice per pair every frame

`_collision_objects` holds all 24-40 level structures plus every live projectile, so a busy frame is tens of thousands of virtual `is_colliding` calls, each doing two virtual `get_bounding_box()` calls that return `RectangleF` **by value** and, on an AABB hit, a `Shape::intersects` dynamic_cast chain (MattMath.cpp:119-136). The `ThreadPool` and `Partitioner` that exist in this very class are used only for drawing (Level.cpp:379-399), never here.

Storage compounds it: `unique_ptr<vector<unique_ptr<T>>>` means every candidate test chases two levels of indirection.

Note: I explicitly checked and **rejected** the related claim that response callbacks fire 2-4 times per pair (see the separate rejected finding) — that does not happen. The redundant *detection* work is real; the double *response* is not.

**Fix:** Collapse to one pass over unique pairs (`for i, for j > i`) and dispatch once. Add a broad phase — a uniform grid or sweep-and-prune over AABBs cached in a flat `std::vector<RectangleF>` parallel to the object list, rebuilt once per frame (structures are static and only need inserting once). Add a collision layer/mask so structure-vs-structure pairs are never generated.

#### 10. An object leaving the play area throws an unhandled exception instead of being despawned

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:307-321` — **high** · `robustness`

```cpp
for (auto& player : *this->_player_objects)
    if (this->is_object_out_of_bounds(player.get()))
        throw std::exception("Player out of bounds");
for (auto& object : *this->_collision_objects)
    if (this->is_object_out_of_bounds(object.get()))
        throw std::exception("Collision object out of bounds");
```
Nothing catches this. I grepped Main.cpp: it has no `try` or `catch` anywhere, and neither `Game::tick` nor `GameLevel::update` wraps the call. So a projectile clearing the out-of-bounds rectangle terminates the process mid-match. `is_object_out_of_bounds` (Level.cpp:689-694) fires the moment an object's AABB stops intersecting the level's out-of-bounds rect — an entirely ordinary event for a fast projectile in a shooter.

The engine already has a despawn mechanism (`get_for_deletion` + the swap-erase at Level.cpp:296-305) that this check declines to use. It is also a redundant second O(n) traversal of `_collision_objects` immediately after that sweep.

Note the two stored-but-never-read spawn vectors (`_team_a_spawns`/`_team_b_spawns`, Level.h:136-137) are exactly what the player case should use to respawn instead of throwing.

**Fix:** Make out-of-bounds a policy: mark projectiles for deletion, respawn players at their team spawn. Fold the test into the existing deletion sweep so the list is walked once. Reserve exceptions for programmer errors and add a top-level handler regardless.

#### 11. Out-of-bounds objects throw instead of being despawned, turning a routine event into a process abort

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:307-321` — **high** · `robustness` · confidence: certain

```
for (auto& object : *this->_collision_objects)
{
    if (this->is_object_out_of_bounds(object.get()))
    {
        throw std::exception("Collision object out of bounds");
    }
}
```
(and the same for players at 308-314). `is_object_out_of_bounds` (Level.cpp:689-694) returns true as soon as an object's AABB stops intersecting `_out_of_bounds`, which for king_of_the_hill is `{-100, -100, 6200, 6200}` (levels/king_of_the_hill.json:52-58).

This is the natural despawn condition for a projectile — the engine's response should be `set_for_deletion(true)`, not termination. Today the level survives only because king_of_the_hill happens to be fully walled (structures at x=-100 w=100 h=7000, x=6000 w=100 h=7000, y=-100 w=6200 h=100; levels/king_of_the_hill.json:85-133), so projectiles collide with a wall and are deleted before they can leave the box. Any level authored without a complete wall ring, or any projectile that clips a corner, aborts the process.

REACHABILITY: LIVE every frame. Game::tick → Level::update (Level.cpp:128) → update_level_logic (Level.cpp:315).

This interacts directly with the `get_delete_timer()` bug above: with lifetimes broken, projectiles rely entirely on geometry to be removed, so the out-of-bounds path is being leaned on far harder than intended.

**Fix:** For collision objects, replace the throw with deletion (set the for-deletion flag and let the existing sweep at Level.cpp:296-305 remove it), and run the out-of-bounds pass *before* that sweep so it happens in one place. A player leaving bounds is a game rule (respawn / kill), not an engine error — it should call the respawn path, not throw. Also note the sweep at 296-305 relies on `size_t i` wrapping to SIZE_MAX on `i--` at index 0; use `std::remove_if` + `erase` instead.

#### 12. Split-screen is hardwired: render-slot index == player index, and there is no View concept

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:491-593` — **high** · `design`

`draw_player_view_level(int start, int end, ...)` uses one loop variable `i` as (a) the index into `_player_objects`, (b) the index into `deferred_contexts`, (c) the index into `sprite_batches`, and (d) the index into `command_lists` (Level.cpp:496-591). The camera comes from `_player_objects->at(i)->get_camera()`, the viewport from that player's `get_player_num()`, and the HUD is drawn from the same player's health/ammo/team (Level.cpp:560-569). `draw_active_level` partitions `_player_objects->size()` across threads (Level.cpp:382-383).

The engine therefore cannot render a spectator view, a minimap, a render-to-texture pass, a level with zero players, or any view not owned by a `Player`. "A thing we render the scene from" does not exist as a concept — `Player` *is* the camera, the viewport and the HUD owner. The zoom-out path had to be written as a completely separate function (Level.cpp:609-651) for exactly this reason, and it is where two other bugs in this review live.

**Fix:** Introduce a first-class `View` (camera + viewport + optional HUD overlay) and have the renderer iterate `std::vector<View>`. Player contributes a View; the zoom-out sequence contributes a View; a minimap contributes a View. Partition views, not players.

#### 13. Multithreaded draw calls non-const draw() on shared objects — concurrent writes to the same PaintTile

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:496-540` — **high** · `concurrency`

`draw_active_level` (Level.cpp:379-399) partitions **players** across thread-pool tasks, but each task's `draw_player_view_level` iterates over **all** shared lists: `_non_collision_objects` (:516), `_collision_objects` (:525), `_player_objects` (:534), calling `object->draw(...)`.

`IGameObject::draw` is non-const (IGameObject.h:11-12) and `PaintTile::draw` genuinely mutates the object (PaintTile.cpp:34-53):
```cpp
this->set_colour(this->_team_colours.get_team_colour(player_team::A));
this->_splash.set_colour(...);
this->_splash.set_rectangle_center(this->_rectangle.get_center());
```
`set_colour` writes `DrawObject::_colour`; `set_rectangle_center` writes `PaintTileSplash::_rectangle` (PaintTile.cpp:172-175). With 2+ players there are 2+ worker threads executing `StructurePaintable::draw` → `PaintTile::draw` on the *same* tile objects. Non-atomic concurrent writes, no synchronisation anywhere on the path.

Secondary race on the same path: `SpriteSheet::draw` uses `this->_sprite_frames[frame_name]` (SpriteSheet.cpp:105 and :126) — `std::map::operator[]`, which **inserts** on a miss and can restructure the tree while other threads read it.

Note this is entirely avoidable: `TextureObject`'s draw primitives are already `const` (TextureObject.h:20-32). `PaintTile::draw` is the reason the interface is non-const, and the colour it recomputes every frame is fully determined by `_team`, which only changes in `on_collision` (PaintTile.cpp:138). Candidates 59 and 77 merged.

**Fix:** Set the tile colour once in `PaintTile::on_collision`, pass the splash rectangle as a local rather than storing it, then make `IGameObject::draw` const-qualified. Change `SpriteSheet::draw` to `.at(name)` on a const SpriteSheet, or better resolve sheet/frame handles at load time so the render loop touches no string-keyed maps.

#### 14. Exceptions thrown inside thread-pool draw tasks escape a Win32 callback and terminate the process

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:498-501` — **high** · `robustness`

`draw_player_view_level` throws from inside a worker task at Level.cpp:500 (`throw std::exception("Deferred context not created")`) and :590 (`FinishCommandList` failed); `draw_zoom_out_level_component` does the same at :616 and :649. The `.at()` calls on all three vectors can also throw `std::out_of_range`.

The task body is invoked from `ThreadPool::work_callback` (ThreadPool.cpp:60-65):
```cpp
std::function<void()>* task = static_cast<std::function<void()>*>(parameter);
(*task)();      // no try/catch
delete task;    // skipped if it throws
```
This is a `void CALLBACK` Win32 thread-pool entry point. An exception escaping it calls `std::terminate` — no message, no log. `wait_for_tasks_to_complete()` (ThreadPool.cpp:50-58) never observes it and the task object leaks.

There is no top-level handler either: I grepped Main.cpp and it contains no `try` or `catch` at all, so the same is true of the `throw std::exception("Player out of bounds")` at Level.cpp:312. `FinishCommandList` failing on device-removal/OOM is a realistic path. Candidates 7, 23 and 80 merged.

**Fix:** Wrap the body in `work_callback` in `try { (*task)(); } catch (...) { store std::exception_ptr on the work item; }` and rethrow from `wait_for_tasks_to_complete()` on the calling thread. Put a top-level try/catch around the message loop in Main.cpp. In the draw path, prefer returning HRESULT/bool; the `GetType()` check is an invariant assertion, not a runtime error.

#### 15. Zoom-out draw spawns one task then immediately waits — and that worker drives the immediate context and mutates ViewportManager

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:595-651` — **high** · `concurrency` · confidence: certain

```cpp
void Level::draw_zoom_out_level(...) const
{
    int num_threads = this->_thread_pool->get_max_num_threads();   // :599  never used (/W4 C4189)
    this->_thread_pool->add_task([this, deferred_contexts, command_lists, sprite_batches]()
        { this->draw_zoom_out_level_component(...); });
    this->_thread_pool->wait_for_tasks_to_complete();
}
```

One task, submitted and immediately blocked on — pure thread-pool overhead with zero parallelism, plus a dead local. But the real problem is what the worker then does (Level.cpp:619-620):

```cpp
this->_viewport_manager->set_layout(screen_layout::ONE_PLAYER);   // mutates shared ViewportManager::_layout
this->_viewport_manager->apply_player_viewport(0);
```

`set_layout` is a non-const write to shared engine state (ViewportManager.cpp:79-82) performed off the main thread. And the no-context overload of `apply_player_viewport` (ViewportManager.cpp:63-70) reaches for the **immediate** context and the ViewportManager's own cached `SpriteBatch`:

```cpp
auto context = this->_device_resources->GetD3DDeviceContext();
context->RSSetViewports(1, &vp);
this->_sprite_batch->SetViewport(vp);
```

D3D11 immediate contexts are explicitly not free-threaded; issuing `RSSetViewports` on it from a pool thread is undefined behaviour even though the main thread happens to be blocked. `_sprite_batch` here is SpriteBatch 0 (Game.cpp:248) — the same object worker 0 uses.

Side effect worth noting separately: `set_layout(ONE_PLAYER)` is a permanent global change made from a draw call, so the level's screen layout is silently clobbered for everything that reads it afterwards.

**Fix:** Run the zoom-out path inline on the calling thread (no pool involvement), pass the deferred context explicitly so the immediate-context overload of `apply_player_viewport` is never reachable from a worker, and delete the unused `num_threads`. Move `set_layout` out of the draw path into the state transition that actually changes the layout.

#### 16. Zoom-out worker task drives the immediate D3D context and the main thread's SpriteBatch

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:614-626` — **high** · `concurrency`

Same function as the layout finding, different defect. `draw_zoom_out_level_component` runs inside a thread-pool task (queued at Level.cpp:601-604) and calls the **single-argument** `apply_player_viewport(0)`. That overload (ViewportManager.cpp:63-70) does:
```cpp
auto context = this->_device_resources->GetD3DDeviceContext();
context->RSSetViewports(1, &vp);
this->_sprite_batch->SetViewport(vp);
```
i.e. it touches the **immediate** context and ViewportManager's own shared `SpriteBatch` — while the main thread owns that immediate context inside `Game::render()`. `ID3D11DeviceContext` is explicitly not free-threaded.

Worse, neither of those objects is the one being recorded into: every draw in the function goes to `sprite_batches->at(0)` on `deferred_contexts->at(0)` (Level.cpp:624-646). So the viewport the function intends to establish never reaches the command list it produces. It renders correctly today only because `Game::clear` sets the fullscreen viewport on every deferred context each frame (Game.cpp:136-148) and the overview happens to want fullscreen.

Contrast the per-player path, Level.cpp:505-506, which correctly uses `apply_player_viewport(player_num, deferred_contexts->at(i), sprite_batches->at(i))`.

**Fix:** Use the three-argument overload here too, and delete the single-argument `apply_player_viewport(int)` plus ViewportManager's `_sprite_batch` member so the broken call cannot be written again.

#### 17. Zoom-out draw permanently forces ONE_PLAYER layout on the shared ViewportManager; Restart then renders every player fullscreen

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:619-620` — **high** · `correctness`

`draw_zoom_out_level_component` begins with:
```cpp
this->_viewport_manager->set_layout(screen_layout::ONE_PLAYER);
this->_viewport_manager->apply_player_viewport(0);
```
`_layout` is a member of the shared `ViewportManager` (ViewportManager.cpp:79-82), it is never restored, and the only place it is set from the match settings is `GameLevel::init` (GameStates.cpp:122-123). Neither restart path re-runs `init` — both just rebuild the level: `pause_menu_action::RESTART` (GameStates.cpp:200-205) and `end_menu_action::RESTART` (GameStates.cpp:276-283).

Every match reaches ZOOM_OUT before the results/end menu appears (`level_state::FINISHED` is only reachable via ZOOM_OUT → OVERVIEW, Level.cpp:133-167), so by the time the end-menu Restart is available the layout is *always* ONE_PLAYER. The rebuilt level then takes each player's viewport from `get_player_viewport(...)` (which returns fullscreen for every player_num under ONE_PLAYER, ViewportManager.cpp:160-165) and `build_viewport_dividers` gets an empty list (ViewportManager.cpp:129-132). Every player renders fullscreen on top of everyone else with no dividers.

This is also mutation of shared presentation state from inside a `const` method running on a thread-pool worker.

**Fix:** Do not mutate ViewportManager here — render the overview through the deferred-context overload with an explicitly-constructed fullscreen viewport. Independently, make GameLevel re-apply `set_layout(_settings.get_screen_layout())` on both restart paths, or move level construction into one helper that always does it.

#### 18. Three includes have the wrong case and only compile because NTFS is case-insensitive

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:2` — **medium** · `portability` · confidence: certain

`Level.cpp:2` is `#include "level.h"` — the file is `Level.h`. `InterfaceGameplay.h:7` and `TeamColour.h:5` are both `#include "colour.h"` — the file is `Colour.h`. These resolve on Windows and fail on any case-sensitive filesystem. For a project whose stated goal is a reusable engine, this is a hard block on ever building it anywhere but Windows, and it is the kind of thing that only surfaces after someone has invested a day in a port.

**Fix:** Fix the three include spellings. Worth a one-off audit: `grep -rn '#include "[a-z]' ArtAttack/` and check each hit against the actual filename.

#### 19. _countdown_text is created lazily in update() but dereferenced unconditionally in draw()

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:95-115` — **medium** · `robustness`

`_countdown_text` (Level.h:111) is null after construction. It is allocated only inside the `_start_timer >= START_TIMER` branch of the first `update()` (Level.cpp:95-104) — a condition true exactly once — and dereferenced with no guard at :109, :114 and, crucially, from the draw path:
```cpp
// draw_player_view_level, Level.cpp:581-585
if (_state == level_state::START_COUNTDOWN || _start_timer > -1.0f)
    this->draw_countdown_text(sprite_batches->at(i), viewport_camera);
// draw_countdown_text, Level.cpp:742
this->_countdown_text->draw(sprite_batch, viewport_camera);
```
The only thing preventing a null deref on the first rendered frame is `game_level_state::FIRST_UPDATE`/`SECOND_UPDATE` (GameStates.h:38-39) — two enum values whose entire bodies are "advance to the next state" (GameStates.cpp:133-138) paired with an early return in draw (GameStates.cpp:305-309). That is an undocumented ordering contract expressed as dummy FSM states, and it must be re-established by hand on every restart (GameStates.cpp:204, :281).

The public `Level::set_state(level_state)` (Level.h:88, zero callers) additionally lets any client put the object back into START_COUNTDOWN, re-entering the branch at :67 without re-satisfying the `_start_timer` condition.

I checked the specific crash scenario one reviewer proposed (pause pressed on the SECOND_UPDATE frame) — see the rejected finding; it is not reachable as described. Downgraded from high to medium accordingly: this is a latent precondition, not a demonstrated crash.

**Fix:** Build `_countdown_text` in the constructor — resolution, resource manager and the constants are all available there — and delete the `_start_timer >= START_TIMER` sentinel. Move the one-shot music/sound/camera work into an explicit `init()`/`on_enter()` called once by GameLevel::init, then delete FIRST_UPDATE/SECOND_UPDATE and the public `set_state`.

#### 20. Scene-drawing loops exist in three copies, one of which is 88 lines of commented-out code

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:375-489` — **medium** · `design` · confidence: certain

`Level` draws the same object lists three times:

- `Level::draw_player_view_level` (:491-589) — three `for (object : *this->_X) if (object->is_visible_in_viewport(camera_view)) object->draw(sprite_batch, camera);` loops over `_non_collision_objects`, `_collision_objects`, `_player_objects`.
- `Level::draw_zoom_out_level_component` (:609-650) — the same three loops with the visibility test dropped.
- `Level.cpp:402-489` — an 88-line commented-out earlier `draw_active_level` containing a third copy of the same three loops plus the interface/debug/countdown draw sequence. It is stale (it calls `object->draw(camera)` with a signature that no longer exists) and is the kind of dead duplicate that makes the live code hard to trust.

Separately, the D3D command-list boilerplate `if (ctx->GetType() != D3D11_DEVICE_CONTEXT_DEFERRED) throw ...` + `FinishCommandList` + `if (FAILED(hr)) throw ...` is copy-pasted into three functions across two files: MenuPage.cpp:156-159 & 179-183, Level.cpp:498-501 & 583-588, Level.cpp:614-617 & 646-650. `MenuPage::draw_mobjects_in_viewports` (MenuPage.cpp:186-226) and `Level::draw_active_level` (Level.cpp:375-399) are also the same partition-then-thread-pool-then-wait dance twice.

**Fix:** Extract `draw_objects(SpriteBatch*, const Camera&, const RectangleF* cull_view)` taking the cull rect as optional, and call it three times from each draw path. Delete the commented-out block at :402-489 (git has it). Extract the deferred-context/FinishCommandList boilerplate into one RAII `DeferredRecording` helper in an engine-level header that both `Level` and `MenuPage` use, and extract the partition+dispatch+wait sequence into one `ThreadPool::parallel_for(count, fn)`.

#### 21. Thread-pool lambda copies the whole partition vector per task, every frame

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:379-399` — **medium** · `performance`

```cpp
auto partitioned_players = this->_partitioner->partition(this->_player_objects->size(), num_threads);
for (int i = 0; i < partitioned_players.size(); i++)
{
    this->_thread_pool->add_task([this, i, partitioned_players,   // captured BY VALUE
        deferred_contexts, command_lists, sprite_batches]() {
            this->draw_player_view_level(partitioned_players[i].first, partitioned_players[i].second, ...);
        });
}
```
`partitioned_players` is a `std::vector<std::pair<int,int>>` (Partitioner.h:11) captured by value, so a full vector copy is heap-allocated per task per frame — and each lambda only reads element `i`. `ThreadPool::add_task` then heap-allocates the closure again (`new std::function<void()>(task)`, ThreadPool.cpp:41). `Partitioner::partition` (Partitioner.cpp:4-22) also `push_back`s with no `reserve`. That is roughly 1 + 2N allocations per frame on the render path for data identical every frame while the player count is unchanged.

The callee side compounds it: `GameLevel::draw` allocates a 16-element `std::vector<ID3D11CommandList*>` every frame (GameStates.cpp:313) because of Level::draw's out-parameter signature.

Also `int i < partitioned_players.size()` is a signed/unsigned comparison — C4018 under /W4, which is enabled (ArtAttack.vcxproj:91 etc.) but not treated as an error anywhere. Same at StructurePaintable.cpp:189/191 and GameStates.cpp:321.

**Fix:** Capture the two ints for this task only, not the vector. Cache the partition as a member and recompute it only when the player count changes. Hoist the command-list vector into a member of GameLevel reused across frames. Replace `std::pair<int,int>` with a named `struct PartitionRange { int begin, end; }`.

#### 22. Results and end-menu frames re-draw the entire level, unculled, on one worker thread, for as long as the menus are open

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:595-651` — **medium** · `performance` · confidence: certain

Once the level reports FINISHED, `GameLevel::update` stops updating it (GameStates.cpp:164-186 takes the RESULTS branch instead), but `GameLevel::draw` unconditionally re-draws it every frame (GameStates.cpp:315-317) for the whole results screen (a scripted ~4 second sequence, ResultsMenu.h:27-30) and then for as long as the player sits on the end menu.

    void Level::draw_zoom_out_level(...) const
    {
        int num_threads = this->_thread_pool->get_max_num_threads();   // 599: assigned, never used
        this->_thread_pool->add_task([...]{ this->draw_zoom_out_level_component(...); });
        this->_thread_pool->wait_for_tasks_to_complete();
    }

That is a thread-pool dispatch + join per frame to run exactly one task, and the task itself has no viewport culling at all — compare `draw_player_view_level`, which tests `object->is_visible_in_viewport(camera_view)` for every object (Level.cpp:518, 527, 536), whereas `draw_zoom_out_level_component` draws every non-collision object, every collision object (including every live projectile) and every player unconditionally (Level.cpp:628-642).

Line 599's `num_threads` is a genuine `/W4` C4189 ("local variable is initialized but not referenced") sitting in shipped code — a concrete demonstration that the project's `/W4` output is being ignored because `TreatWarningAsError` is set nowhere in the vcxproj.

**Fix:** Draw the frozen level once into a cached command list (or a render target) when the level enters ZOOM_OUT/FINISHED and re-execute that while the menus are up, instead of re-recording it every frame. Delete the unused `num_threads`, and call `draw_zoom_out_level_component` directly rather than round-tripping through the pool for a single task. Then turn on `TreatWarningAsError` for at least a warning subset so this class of thing cannot accumulate.

#### 23. Zoom-out/overview draw path has no visibility culling at all, and runs single-threaded exactly when the map is most painted

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:609-642` — **medium** · `performance` · confidence: certain

`draw_zoom_out_level_component` iterates `_non_collision_objects`, `_collision_objects` and `_player_objects` and calls `object->draw(sprite_batch, camera)` with no `is_visible_in_viewport` check (lines 628-642), unlike the active path at 516-540. This is the state used for `ZOOM_OUT`, `OVERVIEW` and `FINISHED` (Level.cpp:365-372) - i.e. the end-of-match survey of the painted map. It is dispatched as a single ThreadPool task (lines 601-606) onto deferred context 0 with one SpriteBatch.
Worst case on turbulence, fully painted: 5,574 tiles x 2 sprites = 11,148 SpriteBatch::Draw plus ~27,870 string-keyed map lookups, all in one batch on one thread, at the exact moment tile paint coverage peaks. The active 4-way split path at least spreads its work across 4 deferred contexts.

**Fix:** Apply the same `is_visible_in_viewport(camera_view)` gate the active path uses, computing the view rect from `_zoom_out_camera`, and cull per tile (see the StructurePaintable::draw finding). The overview camera is zoomed out so most objects will pass, which is exactly why the per-tile merge into a few quads matters more here than anywhere else.

#### 24. try/catch around a pointer dynamic_cast is dead code; a failed cast null-derefs instead

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:711-732` — **medium** · `correctness`

```cpp
if (type == collision_object_type::STRUCTURE_PAINTABLE)
{
    try {
        auto paintable_object = dynamic_cast<IPaintableGameObject*>(object.get());
        PaintTotal paint = paintable_object->get_paint_total();   // :722, unguarded
        ...
    }
    catch (const std::bad_cast& e) { throw std::exception("Could not cast to IPaintableGameObject"); }
}
```
The **pointer** form of `dynamic_cast` returns `nullptr` on failure; only the reference form throws `std::bad_cast`. The catch block is unreachable, `e` is an unused variable (C4101 under /W4), and the failure it was written to handle — an object tagged STRUCTURE_PAINTABLE that isn't a StructurePaintable — is an unchecked null dereference at line 722.

The guard is only the enum tag from `Structure::get_collision_object_type()` (Structure.cpp:51-54), which is just whatever `collision_type` the constructor was handed. LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:71-78 happens to pair them correctly today, so this is not currently triggerable — hence medium, not high — but the enum is being used as a substitute for the type system with a null-unsafe cast to recover the type. This is also the whole scoring path: a failure here loses the match result. Candidates 4, 22, 40, 61 and 84 merged.

**Fix:** `if (auto* paintable = dynamic_cast<IPaintableGameObject*>(object.get())) { ... }` — no enum check, no try/catch, no null deref, and a future paintable type is picked up automatically. Better still, have the builder collect a `std::vector<IPaintableGameObject*>` at construction so the query is a straight loop with no RTTI.

#### 25. _zoom_out_camera is one frame stale at the ACTIVE→ZOOM_OUT transition, producing a visible camera pop

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:139-160` — **low** · `correctness`

The transition to ZOOM_OUT happens inside the `if (_state == level_state::ACTIVE)` branch (Level.cpp:126-138), and the branch that computes `_zoom_out_camera` is `else if (_state == level_state::ZOOM_OUT)` (:139) — chained off the same if. So on the frame the match timer expires, the state flips to ZOOM_OUT but the else-if is not evaluated.

`Level::draw` (:365-372) then routes that frame to `draw_zoom_out_level`, which renders with `_zoom_out_camera` still holding its declared initial value `MattMath::Camera::DEFAULT_CAMERA` (Level.h:126). One frame rendered with the identity camera before the interpolation starts on the following frame — a snap at the exact moment the whistle blows.

This is the generic hazard of an if/else-if ladder over a state enum with no entry hooks: any state entered in this tick has its handler skipped until the next tick.

**Fix:** Compute the zoom-out camera at ratio 0 when entering the state, or restructure `update()` as a `switch` with explicit `enter_state()` hooks so the handler for a newly-entered state runs in the same frame.

#### 26. Zoom-out start and finish cameras are rebuilt every frame from frame-invariant inputs

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:150-159` — **low** · `performance`

`_zoom_out_start_bounds` and `_zoom_out_finish_bounds` are set once in the constructor (Level.cpp:45-46) from the level JSON and never change, and the screen resolution does not change mid-zoom. Only `zoom_out_camera_ratio()` (Level.cpp:176-179) varies per frame. Yet both endpoint cameras -- including two `RectangleF` constructions, two `get_resolution_vec()` calls through a raw pointer, and two divisions -- are recomputed every frame to produce identical values. Small in absolute cost, but it is the only per-frame use of the Camera API and it illustrates the wider pattern of recomputing derived values at the point of use rather than caching them where their inputs change.

**Fix:** Compute `start_camera` and `finish_camera` once when the level enters `level_state::ZOOM_OUT` (or in the constructor) and store them; the per-frame work then reduces to the single `calculate_intermediate_camera` lerp.

#### 27. Dead code on the end-of-match path: unreachable FINISHED branch, empty draw_end_screen, unused Level member

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:169-175` — **low** · `dead-code` · confidence: certain

Three pieces of dead code in the code that runs when a match ends.

1. `Level::update`'s FINISHED branch is unreachable:

        else if (this->_state == level_state::FINISHED)
        {
            this->_sound_bank->stop_effect(this->_music_name, true);
            return;
        }

   `_state` becomes FINISHED inside the OVERVIEW branch at line 166, and because the chain is `else if` the FINISHED branch is not evaluated in that same call. From the next frame on, `GameLevel::update` takes the RESULTS branch (GameStates.cpp:164) and never calls `Level::update` again. So the only place the level would stop its own music is never executed — which is exactly why `stop_music()` has to be hand-duplicated at seven sites in `GameLevel::update`.

2. `void Level::draw_end_screen() { /* TODO */ }` (Level.cpp:696-699), declared private at Level.h:152, has no callers.

3. `std::vector<PlayerInputData> _player_inputs` (Level.h:143) is never read or written anywhere in Level.cpp — `update` takes the inputs by const reference and forwards them.

Also in the same area, `Level::stop_music()` is declared `const` (Level.h:92) while stopping audio, and `draw_zoom_out_level_component` is `const` (Level.h:173) while calling `ViewportManager::set_layout` — the `const` qualifiers on this class carry no information.

**Fix:** Delete all three. Then move the music/sound teardown into `~Level` (or a single `Level::end()` called from one place) so the seven duplicated `stop_music()` calls in `GameLevel::update` collapse to zero, which also fixes the two branches that currently forget `stop_player_sounds()`.

#### 28. A fresh vector is allocated per player per frame to carry projectiles that usually don't exist

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:204-213` — **low** · `performance`

```cpp
std::vector<std::unique_ptr<ICollisionGameObject>> new_projs =
    object->update_weapon_and_get_projectiles();
for (auto& proj : new_projs)
    this->_collision_objects->push_back(std::move(proj));
```
This runs for every player every frame. In the great majority of frames the weapon fires nothing, but the call still constructs and destroys a `std::vector`, and when it is non-empty it allocates one heap block for the vector plus one per projectile. The elements are then moved out one at a time rather than in bulk.

It also appends into the container that the surrounding loops immediately go on to iterate (Level.cpp:227, 259, 277), which is the kind of mid-iteration mutation that is safe only by accident of the loop ordering.

**Fix:** Change the weapon API to append into a caller-supplied container so the common case is zero allocations. If the by-value return stays, at least use `insert` with `std::make_move_iterator` so the destination grows once. Longer term, pool projectiles. And route spawns through a deferred queue drained at end of tick rather than into the live container.

#### 29. Hand-rolled swap-erase relies on unique_ptr self-move-assignment and unsigned wraparound; the codebase uses zero standard algorithms

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:296-305` — **low** · `modern-cpp`

```cpp
for (size_t i = 0; i < this->_collision_objects->size(); i++)
{
    if (this->_collision_objects->at(i)->get_for_deletion())
    {
        this->_collision_objects->at(i) = std::move(this->_collision_objects->back());
        this->_collision_objects->pop_back();
        i--;
    }
}
```
Two things are load-bearing and neither is stated: when `i == size()-1`, `at(i)` and `back()` are the same `unique_ptr`, so line 300 is a **self-move-assignment** (survivable on every mainstream implementation, but it reads like a use-after-move); and when `i == 0` the `i--` wraps a `size_t` to `SIZE_MAX` before `i++` returns it to 0. Defined behaviour, written as if signed. It also uses bounds-checked `at()` inside a loop already guarded by `size()`. No leak — `pop_back()` destroys correctly — so this is fragility, not a bug.

One reviewer claimed no file includes `<algorithm>`; that is **wrong** — pch.h:42 includes it. But I grepped the entire first-party tree for `std::find`, `std::count_if`, `std::remove_if`, `std::accumulate`, `std::any_of`, `std::sort`, `std::for_each` and got **zero** matches, so the underlying point stands: the algorithms are available and simply never used. Other sites that want them: Level.cpp:658-682 (count_if), StructurePaintable.cpp:189-213 (find/any_of — where the face bug lives), StructurePaintable.cpp:303-317 (accumulate; note the stray `;` after the switch's closing brace at :316).

Also in `draw_player_view_level`, `this->_player_objects->at(i)` is repeated nine times inside one loop body (Level.cpp:503, 508, 555, 563, 564, 566, 568, 572, 577) instead of binding a reference once.

**Fix:** `objs.erase(std::remove_if(objs.begin(), objs.end(), [](const auto& o){ return o->get_for_deletion(); }), objs.end());` — order-preserving, one pass, no index arithmetic. Convert the other sites too, and bind `Player& player = *(*_player_objects)[i];` at the top of the draw loop.

#### 30. ID3D11CommandList COM objects held as raw pointers with manual Release — leaked on any throwing path

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:587` — **low** · `memory-safety`

`FinishCommandList(TRUE, &command_lists->at(i))` (Level.cpp:587, and :646 in the zoom-out path) hands back a COM object with refcount 1 into a raw `ID3D11CommandList*` slot. The only `Release()` is the manual loop in the caller (GameStates.cpp:321-330).

Everything between is a leak window. `draw_player_view_level` processes a whole partition in one loop and throws at :500 and :590, so a failure on partition element 2 leaks the list already produced for element 1; unwinding past GameStates.cpp:321 leaks every list produced by the other workers. (In practice the throw terminates the process anyway — see that finding — so the leak is academic today, hence low.)

Relatedly, the `add_task` loop at Level.cpp:386-397 is not exception-safe: `command_lists` points at a stack local in `GameLevel::draw` (GameStates.cpp:313), and `ThreadPool::add_task` can throw (`new std::function` bad_alloc, or `CreateThreadpoolWork` failure at ThreadPool.cpp:44). If task 0 is submitted and task 1's `add_task` throws, the unguarded `wait_for_tasks_to_complete()` at :399 is skipped and the stack frame is destroyed while worker 0 is still writing into it.

`Microsoft::WRL::ComPtr` is already available and used elsewhere in the project, so this is inconsistency, not a constraint.

**Fix:** Change the parameter to `std::vector<Microsoft::WRL::ComPtr<ID3D11CommandList>>*` and pass `ReleaseAndGetAddressOf()`; the caller then does `ExecuteCommandList(list.Get(), TRUE)` and the vector's destructor releases. Have `ThreadPool` hand back a scope guard whose destructor waits, so the wait cannot be skipped.

#### 31. draw_zoom_out_level dispatches one task to the thread pool and immediately blocks on it; num_threads is dead

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:595-607` — **low** · `performance`

```cpp
void Level::draw_zoom_out_level(...) const
{
    int num_threads = this->_thread_pool->get_max_num_threads();   // :599 — never used
    this->_thread_pool->add_task([this, deferred_contexts, command_lists, sprite_batches]()
        { this->draw_zoom_out_level_component(deferred_contexts, command_lists, sprite_batches); });
    this->_thread_pool->wait_for_tasks_to_complete();
}
```
One task, then an immediate join. Net effect is a `new std::function` allocation (ThreadPool.cpp:41), a CreateThreadpoolWork/SubmitThreadpoolWork/WaitForThreadpoolWorkCallbacks/CloseThreadpoolWork round trip and a thread hand-off, all to run work the calling thread then waits for anyway — strictly worse than calling the function. It also moves the work onto a thread where it must not be (see the immediate-context finding) and onto the wrong side of the terminate-on-throw boundary.

`num_threads` is an unreferenced local — C4189 under /W4, which is enabled but with `TreatWarningAsError` set nowhere in ArtAttack.vcxproj, so it accumulated unseen.

**Fix:** Call `draw_zoom_out_level_component` directly and delete both the pool round trip and the unused local. Turn on TreatWarningAsError for at least the Debug configuration so the next one of these is caught at the point of writing.

#### 32. Dead code in the module: unused local, empty never-called method, uncalled public mutator, 110 lines of commented-out drafts

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:599` — **low** · `dead-code`

Consolidating the dead-code items, all verified by reading and grep:
- Level.cpp:599 — `int num_threads = ...` in `draw_zoom_out_level`, never used (C4189).
- Level.h:152 / Level.cpp:696-699 — `void Level::draw_end_screen() { // TODO }`: private, empty, zero call sites.
- Level.h:88 / Level.cpp:701-704 — `Level::set_state(level_state)` is public with zero callers and bypasses every transition side-effect in `update()` (music stop, sound stop, camera setup at :130-160).
- Level.cpp:331-353 and 402-490 — ~110 lines of commented-out earlier `draw`/`draw_active_level` implementations; line 402-404 is a stray fragment with no matching body.
- Structure.cpp:43-50 — both `is_colliding` and `on_collision` ignore their `other` parameter entirely (C4100).
- Level.cpp:727 — `catch (const std::bad_cast& e)` binds `e` and never uses it (C4101).
- StructurePaintable.cpp:118-180 — 60 lines of a commented-out earlier `generate_paint_tiles` implementation, plus the commented `PaintableFaces` struct at StructurePaintable.h:17-23 and LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:101-105 (which, ironically, is the correct design the working code should return to).
- LevelObjectBuilder.h:10-11 — commented-out includes for the fully-commented ramp headers.

**Fix:** Delete all of it. Version control is the archive for old implementations; commented-out code in the file is a maintenance tax and, in the PaintableFaces case, actively misleading about which design is live.

#### 33. The projectile/team type-enum chain is hand-rewritten in four places instead of using the predicates that already exist

`ArtAttack/Level.cpp:658-682` — **low** · `design`

`Level::count_projectiles` (Level.cpp:663-675) writes a 10-way `type == PROJECTILE_*_TEAM_*` disjunction that is character-for-character the body of `is_projectile()` at collision_object_type.h:43-55 — and the local variable even shadows its name.

The same shape appears three more times: `StructurePaintable::on_collision` (StructurePaintable.cpp:68-78, another 10-way chain equal to `is_projectile`) and `PaintTile::on_collision` (PaintTile.cpp:118-133, which is `is_team_a_projectile` / `is_team_b_projectile` from collision_object_type.h:57-73 split in two).
