Every new weapon adds two enum values and requires editing all four chains plus the predicate helpers; missing one fails silently — a projectile that paints nothing, or a debug counter that under-reports.

The root cause is that the enum cross-multiplies class × team × weapon into 23 flat values (collision_object_type.h:4-29), so "what kind of thing is this" and "whose team is it" can only be answered by enumeration.

`count_projectiles` is also called from inside the per-player draw loop (Level.cpp:574) whenever a player has debug enabled — recomputed per viewport, from multiple threads, over a list unchanged since `update`, for a value identical for every player.

**Fix:** At minimum call the existing `is_projectile` / `is_team_a_projectile` / `is_team_b_projectile` helpers. Properly: split the axes — an `object_kind`, a separate `TeamId`, and a weapon id — and expose `get_team()` on `ICollisionGameObject` so `PaintTile::on_collision` becomes `_team = other->get_team();` with no chain and no throw. Compute the projectile count once at the end of update and cache it.

## `ArtAttack/Level.h`

_10 findings: 1 critical, 5 high, 4 medium_

#### 1. `Level` is both the only scene abstraction and the complete paint-battle ruleset

`ArtAttack/Level.h:22-52, 54-80, 128-137 (impl Level.cpp:706-735)` — **critical** · `design` · confidence: certain

There is no engine-level `Scene`/`World` type; `Level` is it, and it is entirely this game. Its constructor (Level.h:58-80) takes `const TeamColour&`, `level_stage stage`, `const std::vector<Vector2F>& team_a_spawns`, `const std::vector<Vector2F>& team_b_spawns`. Its members include `TeamColour _team_colours` (:128), `level_stage _stage = level_stage::KING_OF_THE_HILL` (:129), `_team_a_spawns`/`_team_b_spawns` (:136-137). `level_consts` (:31-52) hardcodes a 240-second match timer, a 3-second countdown, the countdown font `gill_sans_mt_bold_144`, and the sound cue names `"smash_countdown"`/`"slide_whistle_up"`.

`level_state` (:22-29) — `START_COUNTDOWN/ACTIVE/ZOOM_OUT/OVERVIEW/FINISHED` — is this game's match flow, not a generic scene lifecycle. And `Level::get_level_end_info()` (Level.cpp:706-735) is the win condition: it walks `_collision_objects`, filters `type == STRUCTURE_PAINTABLE`, `dynamic_cast<IPaintableGameObject*>`, and sums `paint.team_a`/`paint.team_b`.

So the generic responsibilities that *should* be engine (own the object lists, step them, run broad/narrow phase, dispatch collisions, cull, draw through viewports, delete dead objects) are welded to the game responsibilities (two teams, spawns, paint scoring, match timer, zoom-out celebration).

**Fix:** Extract an engine `Scene` owning `std::vector<std::unique_ptr<IGameObject>>` + the collision/update/draw pipeline, with virtual (or callback) hooks `on_pre_update/on_post_collision/is_finished/get_result`. Then `PaintBattleScene : Scene` in game/ holds `TeamColour`, spawns, the match timer and `get_level_end_info()`. The engine must not know the word 'team'.

#### 2. Level is a god class: object storage, simulation, collision, camera, HUD, audio, match rules and the D3D11 render backend

`ArtAttack/Level.h:54-179` — **high** · `design`

`Level` carries ~30 data members and mixes at least eight unrelated responsibilities: object ownership (Level.h:95-105), simulation tick (update_level_logic, Level.cpp:180-322), collision iteration and response (Level.cpp:221-293), deletion/out-of-bounds culling (Level.cpp:296-321), camera control (`_camera_tools`, `_zoom_out_camera`), HUD (`_interface_gameplay`, `_debug_text`, `_countdown_text`), audio policy (`_sound_bank`, `_music_name`, `stop_music`, `stop_player_sounds`), match rules and scoring (`_timer`, `_state`, `get_level_end_info`), and the multithreaded D3D11 render backend (`_thread_pool`, `_partitioner`, `_sampler_state`, `FinishCommandList` at Level.cpp:587).

Nothing here can be reused or tested independently, and none of it can run without a live D3D11 device. Given the stated goal of a reusable engine with the game as a proof, this is the single largest structural obstacle in the module: everything reusable is welded to everything game-specific.

**Fix:** Split into: `Scene`/`World` (owns and updates objects), `CollisionSystem` (unique pairs, dispatch), `SceneRenderer` (the only piece that knows SpriteBatch/deferred contexts), `GameMode`/`RuleSet` (timer, countdown, win condition, scoring — game code, not engine), and `Hud`. `Level` then becomes a thin composition root the game supplies.

#### 3. 23-parameter constructor, five of whose members are written and never read

`ArtAttack/Level.h:58-80` — **high** · `design`

`Level::Level` takes 23 positional parameters (Level.h:58-80; several reviewers said 24 — I counted, it is 23). The call site (LevelBuilder.cpp:59-82) cannot be read without counting commas, and there are four adjacent `const MattMath::RectangleF&` parameters (out_of_bounds, camera_bounds, zoom_out_start_bounds, zoom_out_finish_bounds) plus two adjacent `const std::vector<Vector2F>&` spawn parameters — transposable at a call site with no diagnostic.

I grepped every member across the whole first-party tree. Five are written and never read:
- `_stage` (Level.h:129, written Level.cpp:42) — the only other hits are MenuLevelSettings' unrelated member.
- `_team_a_spawns` / `_team_b_spawns` (Level.h:136-137, written Level.cpp:47-48) — two whole `std::vector<Vector2F>` copies per level build, per Restart. Spawns are actually consumed by PlayerBuilder (LevelBuilder.cpp:50-53).
- `_level_name` (Level.h:116, written Level.cpp:37) — a `std::string` copy for nothing.
- `_player_inputs` (Level.h:143) — never written *or* read anywhere; `update()` takes inputs by reference and forwards them.

Related dead surface in the same class: `void set_state(level_state)` (Level.h:88, Level.cpp:701-704) is public with zero callers and lets any client jam the FSM into an arbitrary state, bypassing every transition side-effect in `update()`; `void draw_end_screen()` (Level.h:152, Level.cpp:696-699) is an empty `// TODO` with zero callers.

**Fix:** Delete the five dead members, their four constructor parameters, `set_state` and `draw_end_screen` (or wire the spawn vectors into a respawn path — see the out-of-bounds finding). Then collapse the remainder into a `LevelDescription` value struct plus an engine-services struct, so designated-initialiser construction names every field at the one call site.

#### 4. Level's public draw API is three raw pointers to vectors of D3D11 objects

`ArtAttack/Level.h:83-85` — **high** · `design`

`void draw(std::vector<ID3D11DeviceContext*>*, std::vector<ID3D11CommandList*>*, std::vector<DirectX::SpriteBatch*>*) const;` — a simulation type whose public signature exposes the deferred-context/command-list scheme. The same triple is repeated on `draw_active_level` (Level.h:156-158), `draw_zoom_out_level` (160-162), `draw_player_view_level` (168-171) and `draw_zoom_out_level_component` (173-175).

The implementation does the graphics work itself: `deferred_contexts->at(i)->GetType() != D3D11_DEVICE_CONTEXT_DEFERRED` with a throw (Level.cpp:498-501), `sprite_batches->at(i)->Begin(SpriteSortMode_Deferred, nullptr, _sampler_state)` (Level.cpp:513), `FinishCommandList(TRUE, &command_lists->at(i))` (Level.cpp:587). The caller then has to `ExecuteCommandList` and `Release` them by hand (GameStates.cpp:321-330).

Additional problems in the one signature: `command_lists` is a pure out-parameter mixed in among inputs with nothing in the type saying so; the three vectors must be index-aligned and at least `_player_objects->size()` long, which is neither stated nor checked; and the meaning of the index differs between the two paths (`draw_player_view_level` uses partition indices, `draw_zoom_out_level_component` hard-codes 0 at Level.cpp:614/620/624/646). Candidates 37 and 67 merged.

**Fix:** Define an engine-level `IRenderer`/`RenderContext` and make `Level::draw(IRenderer&)` the whole API. Command-list recording, deferred contexts, sampler state and the parallel-recording strategy become the renderer's private business. Until then, at minimum pass one `RenderTargets` struct by const reference with a single invariant check.

#### 5. Level caches raw SoundBank* and ResourceManager* that device-loss destroys and replaces

`ArtAttack/Level.h:107-119` — **high** · `memory-safety`

`SoundBank* _sound_bank` (Level.h:107, assigned Level.cpp:59) and `ResourceManager* _resource_manager` (Level.h:119). `StructurePaintable.h:59` caches a `SoundBank*` too (assigned StructurePaintable.cpp:34).

The pointees are owned by `ResourceManager::_sound_banks`. `Game::OnDeviceLost()` (Game.cpp:269-280) calls `_resource_manager->reset_all_sounds()`, which at ResourceManager.cpp:119-126 does `sound_bank.second.reset()` on every entry — the SoundBanks are **destroyed**. `Game::OnDeviceRestored()` (Game.cpp:282-287) then calls `create_device_dependent_resources()`, which at Game.cpp:239 does `this->_resource_manager = std::make_unique<ResourceManager>();` — the entire ResourceManager is replaced with a new object. Nothing notifies the live `Level`, and the state machine is not rebuilt.

So after any device-lost event (Alt-Tab, driver reset, TDR), the surviving `Level` holds dangling `_sound_bank` **and** `_resource_manager`. The next frame dereferences them: Level.cpp:63, :73-74, :134, :136, :147, :171, and `StructurePaintable::on_collision` at :97 on every paint hit.

**Fix:** Either don't cache — look the bank up by name at each use through a null-checked accessor — or, for a reusable engine, give resources generation-counted handles so a stale handle is detectable rather than dangling. Whatever you pick, document every raw pointer member with its owner and its validity window.

#### 6. Level has four write-only members, including a complete spawn-point pipeline that terminates in nothing

`ArtAttack/Level.h:116, 136-137, 143` — **high** · `dead-code` · confidence: certain

`Level.h:136-137` declare `std::vector<Vector2F> _team_a_spawns` / `_team_b_spawns`. They are initialised at `Level.cpp:47-48` from constructor parameters (`Level.cpp:18-19`), which are fed by `LevelBuilder.cpp:70-71` from `LevelLoadedInfo::get_team_a_spawns()/get_team_b_spawns()` (`LevelLoadedInfo.cpp:19-27`), which parse `"spawn_locations"` out of the level JSON via `decode_team_spawns_json` (`LevelLoadedInfo.cpp:86-93`). Neither member is ever read — grep for `_team_a_spawns` returns exactly the ctor-init and the declaration. A whole JSON→builder→object data path exists to populate two vectors nobody looks at (players actually respawn from `Player::_respawn_position`, set in PlayerBuilder). Same file: `_level_name` (`Level.h:116`, set at `Level.cpp:37`) is never read, and `std::vector<PlayerInputData> _player_inputs` (`Level.h:143`) is never touched at all — not written, not read.

**Fix:** Either wire spawn points into respawn (the obviously intended behaviour) or delete the member, the ctor parameters, the LevelBuilder plumbing, and LevelLoadedInfo::get_team_a_spawns/get_team_b_spawns/decode_team_spawns_json. Delete `_level_name` and `_player_inputs` outright.

#### 7. Level.h pulls 17 headers into every consumer; one is unused and six are needed only for pointer members

`ArtAttack/Level.h:4-20` — **medium** · `design`

Level.h includes ICollisionGameObject.h, TeamColour.h, level_stage.h, PlayerInput.h, Player.h, ResolutionManager.h, ViewportManager.h, DebugText.h, CameraTools.h, InterfaceGameplay.h, LevelEndInfo.h, TextDropShadow.h, SoundBank.h, IPaintableGameObject.h, ResourceManager.h, ThreadPool.h, Partitioner.h. Because LevelBuilder.h:4 includes Level.h, that whole graph lands in LevelBuilder.cpp, GameStates.cpp and everything downstream.

- `IPaintableGameObject.h` (line 17) is referenced nowhere in Level.h — I grepped for `PaintTotal` and `IPaintable` and the include is the only hit. Its only user is Level.cpp:720.
- `SoundBank`, `ResolutionManager`, `ViewportManager`, `ResourceManager`, `ThreadPool`, `Partitioner` appear only as raw pointer members (Level.h:107, 117-119, 146-147) — forward declarations suffice.
- `DebugText`, `CameraTools`, `InterfaceGameplay`, `TextDropShadow` are `unique_ptr` members; declaring `~Level();` out-of-line in Level.cpp lets all four become forward declarations too.
- `level_stage.h` (line 6) supports `_stage`, which is dead.

Same issue at LevelObjectBuilder.h:7, which includes StructurePaintable.h although the header only mentions `ICollisionGameObject` and `IGameObject`; and LevelObjectBuilder.h:6 / LevelLoadedInfo.h:5 both pull rapidjson into every consumer.

**Fix:** Forward-declare the pointer-member types, declare `~Level();` out-of-line, move IPaintableGameObject.h and StructurePaintable.h into the .cpp files, and delete level_stage.h along with the dead `_stage`. This is a prerequisite for the engine ever shipping as a library with a public header surface.

#### 8. Match rules, asset names and UI styling for one specific game are compile-time constants inside Level.h

`ArtAttack/Level.h:31-52` — **medium** · `design`

`namespace level_consts` hardcodes, in the level class's own header: the match length `TIMER = 240.0f`, `START_TIMER = 3.0f`, the countdown font `"gill_sans_mt_bold_144"`, the countdown string `"3"`, two colours, a shadow offset, a text scale, the cue names `"smash_countdown"` and `"slide_whistle_up"` with their volumes, and `ZOOM_OUT_TIMER`/`OVERVIEW_TIMER`.

Every one is game content, not engine behaviour, and none is overridable per level — even though the level JSON already carries `sound.music_name`, `sound.music_volume` and the four bounds rectangles, so the data path exists and was simply not used for these.

Separately, these are namespace-scope `const std::string`/`const Colour` objects in a header. `const` at namespace scope gives internal linkage, so every TU including Level.h gets its own copy with a dynamic initialiser at startup and a destructor at exit. The `static` on some (line 35-40) and not others (line 47, 50) changes nothing. Same pattern at PaintTile.h:15-20 and StructurePaintable.h:12-14 — including `SOUND_BANK_NAME = "sound_bank_1"`, a hardcoded asset name inside a wall class.

**Fix:** Move match length, countdown length and the post-match timings into a GameModeConfig loaded from level/mode JSON; move cue names and font/colour styling into a HUD/UI theme resource. For the storage issue, use `inline constexpr std::string_view` (needs the language standard raised — see the separate finding) or move definitions to a .cpp with `extern const` declarations.

#### 9. Public `= default` constructors produce half-built objects that the very next call dereferences — and one of them is silently deleted

`ArtAttack/Level.h:57` — **medium** · `design`

Five classes in this module declare a defaulted default constructor alongside a real one, none of which is called anywhere:
- `Level() = default;` (Level.h:57) leaves all four object-list `unique_ptr`s null (Level.h:95-105) and every service pointer null; `Level::update` dereferences immediately (`*this->_player_objects` at Level.cpp:78, `*this->_collision_objects` at :183).
- `Structure() = default;` (Structure.h:10) leaves `_collision_shape = nullptr` (Structure.h:40), so `get_shape()` (Structure.cpp:55-58) returns null and `Level::is_object_out_of_bounds` does `object->get_shape()->get_bounding_box()` unguarded (Level.cpp:692) for every collision object every frame.
- `PaintTile() = default;` (PaintTile.h:54) leaves `_dt` null.
- `PaintTileSplash() = default;` (PaintTile.h:26) exists only because `PaintTile::_splash` is default-constructed then reassigned in the ctor *body* (PaintTile.cpp:25-28) instead of in the init list.
- `StructurePaintable() = default;` (StructurePaintable.h:28) is implicitly **deleted**, because `_paintable_edges` is a reference member with no initialiser. The declaration reads as "you may default-construct this" and means the opposite; it compiles only because nobody calls it.

Each one widens the null surface of the whole level pipeline for no benefit.

**Fix:** Delete all five — the user-provided constructors already suppress the implicit ones. Move `_splash` into PaintTile's member-init list, which removes the need for `PaintTileSplash()` too. Add asserts/throws on the injected pointers in the real constructors.

#### 10. unique_ptr<vector<unique_ptr<T>>> adds an owning indirection with no owner semantics — and it is what lets const methods mutate the world

`ArtAttack/Level.h:95-105` — **medium** · `design`

All four object lists are double-owned:
```cpp
std::unique_ptr<std::vector<std::unique_ptr<IGameObject>>>            _non_collision_objects = nullptr;
std::unique_ptr<std::vector<std::unique_ptr<ICollisionGameObject>>>   _collision_objects = nullptr;
std::unique_ptr<std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Player>>>                 _player_objects = nullptr;
std::unique_ptr<std::vector<std::unique_ptr<IGameObject>>>            _viewport_dividers = nullptr;
```
The same types are the constructor parameters (Level.h:58-61) and the return types of `LevelObjectBuilder::build_collision_objects`/`build_non_collision_objects`/`build_viewport_dividers` (LevelObjectBuilder.h:19-27).

`std::vector` already is the sole, cheaply-movable owner of its buffer. The outer `unique_ptr` buys an extra heap allocation and indirection on every access, plus a nullable state that ~20 dereference sites in Level.cpp assume away (:183, 190, 216, 222, 259, 277, 296, 308, 315, 516, 525, 534, 548, 629, 634, 639, 661, 711).

Most importantly it is what makes the `const` on `update_level_logic(...) const` (Level.cpp:180) meaningless: the method mutates every object, moves players, and appends spawned projectiles at Level.cpp:209 (`this->_collision_objects->push_back(std::move(proj))`) — the outer pointer being const says nothing about the vector. `draw_active_level(...) const` (Level.cpp:375) likewise queues thread-pool work. `const` here conveys nothing to a reader and nothing to the compiler. Candidates 30, 53 and 68 merged.

**Fix:** Hold and return `std::vector<std::unique_ptr<T>>` by value throughout — members, ctor params (by value + move), builder returns. Four heap allocations and four null states disappear, and `update_level_logic`/`draw_active_level` correctly stop compiling as `const`, which is the point. Route spawned projectiles through a deferred queue drained at end of tick rather than push_back into the container being walked.

## `ArtAttack/LevelLoadedInfo.cpp`

_5 findings: 2 critical, 1 high, 2 medium_

#### 1. Level JSON parsed through a 1-byte heap buffer declared as 8 bytes — heap overflow on every level load

`ArtAttack/LevelLoadedInfo.cpp:96-110` — **critical** · `memory-safety`

```cpp
FILE* fp = fopen(json_path, "rb");                            // unchecked
std::unique_ptr<char> readBuffer = std::make_unique<char>();  // ONE char
FileReadStream is(fp, readBuffer.get(), sizeof(readBuffer));  // sizeof(unique_ptr) == 8
Document d;
d.ParseStream(is);                                            // return value discarded
fclose(fp);
readBuffer.release();                                          // leaks the allocation
```
Four independent defects. (1) `make_unique<char>()` allocates one byte; `sizeof(readBuffer)` is the size of the `unique_ptr` object, 8 on x64. I read the vendored rapidjson (external/rapidjson/include/rapidjson/filereadstream.h:66-81): `Read()` does `readCount_ = std::fread(buffer_, 1, bufferSize_, fp_)` and, on the final short read, `buffer_[readCount_] = '\0'` — so it writes up to 8 bytes, plus a terminator at offset up to 8, into a 1-byte allocation. king_of_the_hill.json is 21,955 bytes, so the refill loop runs ~2,700 times per load, each time overwriting the allocator's block header. (2) `readBuffer.release()` relinquishes ownership without deleting. (3) `fopen` is unchecked; `RAPIDJSON_ASSERT(fp_ != 0)` compiles out under NDEBUG and `fclose(nullptr)` is UB. (4) `d.HasParseError()` is never queried, so a malformed file yields a null Document and every later `_json_doc["level_name"]` (line 17) etc. is UB in Release.

Candidates 3, 19, 58 and 72 all report this; merged. The same `sizeof(unique_ptr)` idiom also exists at SpriteSheet.cpp:74-81 (I confirmed `read_buffer.release()` there), and reviewers cite Save.cpp and SoundBank.cpp — treat it as one shared helper to fix.

**Fix:** Write one `rapidjson::Document parse_json_file(const std::string& path)` helper that checks `fopen`, uses a real `std::vector<char> buffer(65536)`, closes the FILE* with an RAII guard, and throws a message naming the path and `GetParseError()`/`GetErrorOffset()` on failure. Replace all four copy-pasted loaders with it.

#### 2. All four JSON loaders overflow a 1-byte heap buffer on every read (sizeof(unique_ptr) as size)

`ArtAttack/LevelLoadedInfo.cpp:96-110` — **critical** · `memory-safety` · confidence: certain

Every JSON loader in the codebase uses the identical idiom:

    std::unique_ptr<char> readBuffer = std::make_unique<char>();
    FileReadStream is(fp, readBuffer.get(), sizeof(readBuffer));

`make_unique<char>()` allocates exactly ONE byte. `sizeof(readBuffer)` is `sizeof(std::unique_ptr<char>)` = 8 on x64 (4 on Win32), not the buffer size. The vendored rapidjson does `readCount_ = std::fread(buffer_, 1, bufferSize_, fp_)` (external/rapidjson/include/rapidjson/filereadstream.h:71) and then `buffer_[readCount_] = '\0'` (line 76) — so it writes up to 8, and indexes up to buffer_[8], on a 1-byte allocation. This is a heap buffer overflow on every single refill, repeated for the whole file.

The shipped data makes the scale concrete: ArtAttack/textures/sprite_sheet_1.json is 14,165 bytes and ArtAttack/levels/king_of_the_hill.json is 21,955 bytes, so startup performs roughly 1,771 + 2,745 + (turbulence 21,493) + (close_quarters 12,730) + (sound_bank_1.json 3,166) + (save_data.json 53) / 8 overflowing freads — about 9,000 out-of-bounds writes before the main menu appears. It happens to "work" only because MSVC's heap allocates a padded block for a 1-byte request.

All four sites, identical bug:
- ArtAttack/LevelLoadedInfo.cpp:100-101 (runs 3× — one per level)
- ArtAttack/SpriteSheet.cpp:74-75
- ArtAttack/SoundBank.cpp:154-155
- ArtAttack/Save.cpp:16-17

All four also then call `readBuffer.release()` (LevelLoadedInfo.cpp:107, SpriteSheet.cpp:81, SoundBank.cpp:161, Save.cpp:23), deliberately leaking the allocation — presumably a misunderstanding of `release()` vs `reset()`. And none of the four checks `fopen` for NULL, which rapidjson only guards with `RAPIDJSON_ASSERT(fp_ != 0)` — a no-op under NDEBUG (defined in both Release configs, ArtAttack.vcxproj:138,164).

**Fix:** Replace the whole idiom with a shared helper that reads the file into a `std::string`/`std::vector<char>` and parses via `rapidjson::MemoryStream`/`StringStream`, or if FileReadStream is kept: `std::array<char, 65536> buf;` and pass `buf.size()`. Check `fopen` for null and throw a diagnostic naming the path. Drop the `release()` calls. Fix all four sites together.

#### 3. No JSON access anywhere is guarded: zero HasParseError checks, zero type checks, ~60 raw operator[] + GetFloat/GetString

`ArtAttack/LevelLoadedInfo.cpp:15-94` — **high** · `robustness` · confidence: certain

A repo-wide grep for `HasParseError`, `IsObject()`, `IsArray()`, `IsInt`, `IsString` returns **zero** hits in first-party code. `HasMember` appears exactly 7 times, all in LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:38,45,81,88,108 and SpriteSheet.cpp:34,39.

So `d.ParseStream(is)` at Save.cpp:20, LevelLoadedInfo.cpp:104, SoundBank.cpp:158 and SpriteSheet.cpp:78 is never checked, and every subsequent access is unguarded. LevelLoadedInfo is the worst offender — the whole class is unguarded chained subscripts:

```cpp
return this->_json_doc["level_name"].GetString();                       // :17
this->_json_doc["level_bounds"]["out_of_bounds"]["x"].GetFloat()        // :33-36, x4 rects
return this->_json_doc["collision_objects"];                            // :66
return this->_json_doc["sound"]["music_volume"].GetFloat();             // :82
for (auto& spawn : json.GetArray())  spawn["x"].GetFloat()              // :89-91
```

rapidjson's `operator[](name)` on a missing key hits `RAPIDJSON_ASSERT(false)` (document.h:1231) and, with asserts compiled out in Release, returns a static `kNullType` value. `GetFloat()`/`GetString()` on that null then reinterpret the union with the corresponding `RAPIDJSON_ASSERT(IsNumber())` also compiled out — so a renamed or misspelled key yields **garbage geometry** in Release and `std::string(garbage_pointer)` for the string accessors. A truncated save/level file (interrupted write) does the same via the unchecked parse.

Other unguarded sites: Save.cpp:25-26, SoundBank.cpp:125,126,163,164,166, SpriteSheet.cpp:26,30-33,55,57-63,83,84, LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:19,23,40-43,59,60,65,133-134,142,162-167,170-171,176,185,189-196.

**Fix:** Add a small guarded-access layer (`get_float(v, "x")`, `require_object(v, "level_bounds")`, …) that throws a descriptive exception naming the file and JSON pointer path, and check `d.HasParseError()` / `GetParseError()` / `GetErrorOffset()` immediately after every `ParseStream`. Do not rely on RAPIDJSON_ASSERT — it does not exist in Release.

#### 4. The same rectangle/vector decode is hand-written ~10 times in three mutually inconsistent JSON dialects

`ArtAttack/LevelLoadedInfo.cpp:30-62` — **medium** · `design` · confidence: certain

There is no shared decoding layer; each class writes its own. The same concept — a rectangle — is spelled three different ways in the data and decoded three different ways in code:

- `{"x","y","width","height"}` — LevelLoadedInfo.cpp:32-36, 40-44, 48-52, 57-61 (four copies) and LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:40-43, 83-86, 191-194 (three more).
- `{"left","top","right","bottom"}` — LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:47-51 and 90-94 (two copies of a `rectangle_tlbr` branch that **no shipping level uses** — verified: zero occurrences across all three level JSONs).
- `{"position":{"x","y"},"size":{"w","h"}}` — SpriteSheet.cpp:29-33, and `{"x","y","w","h"}` at SpriteSheet.cpp:56-60.

Likewise `Vector2F` decode is written out at LevelLoadedInfo.cpp:91, LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:47-50, SpriteSheet.cpp:36-37. The file-open-and-parse block is copy-pasted four times (see the heap-overflow finding) — meaning the single most serious bug in the pipeline has to be fixed in four places.

Also dead data: every one of the 91 collision/non-collision objects in the level JSONs carries a `"name"` field that `build_collision_object`/`build_non_collision_object` never read; and `sprite_sheet_1.json`'s `origin`/`rotated` are parsed into `SpriteFrame::_origin` and `_rotated` (SpriteSheet.cpp:36-41) which have no getter and are read by nothing (`_source_rectangle2` likewise) — parsed and discarded.

**Fix:** Add a `json_util` (or `JsonReader`) with `read_rect`, `read_vec2`, `read_float`, `read_string`, `read_array`, each taking the value plus a key and throwing a message that names the file and path. Pick one rectangle spelling and migrate the data files. Either consume `name`/`origin`/`rotated` or remove them from the schema.

#### 5. No parse-error check on any of the four ParseStream calls; rapidjson's own guards are compiled out in Release

`ArtAttack/LevelLoadedInfo.cpp:96-110` — **medium** · `robustness` · confidence: certain

All four loaders do `d.ParseStream(is);` and immediately dereference members, with zero error handling: LevelLoadedInfo.cpp:104, SpriteSheet.cpp:78, SoundBank.cpp:158, Save.cpp:20. Grepping the whole first-party tree for `HasParseError` / `GetParseError` returns nothing.

On a truncated or empty file the `Document` is left as `kNullType`, and the very next line (`this->_json_doc["level_name"]`, `d["resolution"]["x"].GetInt()`, `d["waves"]`, …) hits `GenericValue::operator[]`, whose only protection is `RAPIDJSON_ASSERT(IsObject())`. That macro is `assert(x)` (external/rapidjson/include/rapidjson/rapidjson.h:437), and both Release configurations define NDEBUG (ArtAttack.vcxproj:138,164) — so in a shipping build the assert vanishes and rapidjson walks `data_.o.members` on a null value. Undefined behaviour, not an exception.

This is directly reachable for the save file, which is the one JSON the *program itself* rewrites at runtime (`Save::write_save_file`, Save.cpp:58-83): an interrupted write or a hand-edited `ArtAttack/save/save_data.json` (currently 53 bytes: `{"resolution":{"x":1920,"y":1080},"fullscreen":false}`) yields a Release-mode crash with no message. It is also reachable for a fresh copy of the built exe: there is no post-build asset copy step and paths are relative (`"./save/save_data.json"`, ArtAttack/directory_consts.h:11), so if `./save/` is absent, `write_save_file`'s `fopen` returns nullptr → returns false → `load_from_json` then `fopen`s NULL → `fread(buf,1,8,NULL)`.

**Fix:** Check `d.HasParseError()` and `fp != nullptr` at all four sites and throw an exception naming the file and `GetParseErrorCode()`/`GetErrorOffset()`. Factor the shared open/read/parse into one function so the fix lands once. Also define `RAPIDJSON_ASSERT` to something that survives NDEBUG if you intend to rely on it.

## `ArtAttack/LevelObjectBuilder.cpp`

_9 findings: 1 critical, 2 high, 4 medium, 2 low_

#### 1. StructurePaintable stores a reference to a builder local; it dangles for the object's entire lifetime

`ArtAttack/LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:107-142` — **critical** · `memory-safety` · confidence: certain

```cpp
std::vector<Segment> paintable_edges;                 // :107  function-local
if (json.HasMember("paintable_faces")) { ... paintable_edges.push_back(...); }
return std::make_unique<StructurePaintable>(..., paintable_edges, ...);  // :140
```

`StructurePaintable` binds that argument to a **reference member**: `const std::vector<MattMath::Segment>& _paintable_edges;` (StructurePaintable.h:56). `build_collision_object` returns immediately afterwards, destroying the vector, so the member dangles for the whole life of the level. `StructurePaintable` reads it during paint-tile generation (StructurePaintable.cpp:189-193). 24 objects across the three shipping levels are `StructurePaintable`.

Secondary: that reference member also implicitly deletes the `StructurePaintable() = default;` declared on line 28 of the same header.

**Fix:** Change the member to `std::vector<MattMath::Segment> _paintable_edges;` (by value) and move the argument in. If the edges are only needed during construction (they appear to be — tiles are generated in the ctor), take the parameter and drop the member entirely.

#### 2. Level loading is a closed if/else over four hardcoded type strings — no registration point

`ArtAttack/LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:15-180, 182-200` — **high** · `design` · confidence: certain

`build_collision_object` (lines 15-180) is `std::string type = json["type"].GetString();` followed by `if (type == "Structure")`, `if (type == "StructurePaintable")`, `if (type == "StructureRamp")`, then `throw std::exception("Invalid collision object type")`. `build_non_collision_object` (182-200) is the same shape with a single `"Visual"` branch. Each branch also re-parses the rectangle with a copy-pasted `HasMember("rectangle") / HasMember("rectangle_tlbr")` block (lines 37-56 duplicated at 80-99), and does a nested string->enum if/else for `collision_type` (24-35, 70-78, 148-159).

So the level loader — which is the one piece of the engine a content-driven game most needs to extend — cannot be extended without editing it. A second game shipping a `Ladder` or `MovingPlatform` object has to modify engine source. The builder is also already coupled to game types by include: `LevelObjectBuilder.h:7` includes `StructurePaintable.h`, and the signature takes `const TeamColour& team_colours` (:20-21, :34-35).

**Fix:** Invert it into a registry: `LevelObjectBuilder` holds `std::map<std::string, std::function<std::unique_ptr<ICollisionGameObject>(const rapidjson::Value&, const BuildContext&)>>` and exposes `register_type(name, factory)`. The game registers `"StructurePaintable"` at startup; the engine registers only truly generic types. Factor the rectangle/`rectangle_tlbr` parsing into one `parse_rectangle(const Value&)` helper. Drop `TeamColour` from the signature — pass it inside a game-owned `BuildContext`.

#### 3. Every level JSON field is read with unchecked rapidjson accessors — missing or mistyped fields are UB in Release

`ArtAttack/LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:19-199` — **high** · `robustness`

Every read goes straight through rapidjson's precondition-asserting accessors: `json["type"].GetString()` (:19), `json["rectangle"]["x"].GetFloat()` (:40-43), `json["paintable_faces"]["left"].GetBool()` (:110), `json["triangle"]["x1"].GetFloat()` (:161-167), `json["sheet_name"].GetString()` (:59). `operator[](const char*)` and the typed getters enforce their preconditions with `RAPIDJSON_ASSERT`, which is `assert` and compiles out under NDEBUG. A level file missing `sheet_name`, or with `"width": "100"` as a string, is undefined behaviour in Release.

Only two things are checked at all, both via `HasMember`: `rectangle`/`rectangle_tlbr` (:38-56, :81-99) and `paintable_faces` (:108-130).

The one field looked up by name degrades silently instead: `colour_consts::colour_from_name` falls back to WHITE on an unknown name, so a typo'd colour produces a white object with no diagnostic.

There is no value validation either: nothing rejects negative or zero width/height, which is the precondition the paint-tile divide-by-zero (separate finding) depends on. Combined with the unchecked parse-error in `LevelLoadedInfo::load_from_json`, a bad level file has no failure mode that produces a usable message.

**Fix:** Add `require_float(json, "x")` / `require_string(json, "type")` / `require_object(json, "rectangle")` helpers that check `HasMember` **and** the type and throw a message naming the file, object index and field. Validate ranges (width/height > 0, spawns inside out_of_bounds) at build time. Make `colour_from_name` return a failure the caller must handle.

#### 4. Object factory is a closed if/else chain over hardcoded strings, with duplicated parsing and rapidjson in the public API

`ArtAttack/LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:15-200` — **medium** · `design`

`build_collision_object` is a 165-line chain of `if (type == "Structure") ... if (type == "StructurePaintable") ... if (type == "StructureRamp") ... throw std::exception("Invalid collision object type")` (:19, :67, :144, :179). `build_non_collision_object` (:182-200) knows exactly one type, `"Visual"`. Every new object type in any game built on this engine requires editing this engine-side file — there is no registration point.

The rectangle-parsing block is copy-pasted verbatim: lines 37-56 and 80-99 are byte-identical apart from indentation, and a third partial copy is inlined at :191-194. Any fix to rectangle parsing (e.g. the width/height validation the paint-tile divide needs) has to be made three times.

The public API leaks the parser: `build_collision_objects(const rapidjson::Value& json, ...)` (LevelObjectBuilder.h:20) and `LevelLoadedInfo::get_collision_objects_json()` returning `const rapidjson::Value&` (LevelLoadedInfo.h:26) weld the engine's level format to rapidjson forever, and LevelObjectBuilder.h:6 pulls `rapidjson/document.h` into every consumer.

Parsing is also split with no shared schema: bounds/spawns/audio in LevelLoadedInfo, objects here.

Minor but pervasive: every `if (type == "...")` heap-allocates a `std::string` from a `const char*` rapidjson already owns (:19, 23, 70, 147, 185), and `colour_from_name(json["colour"].GetString())` builds another and linear-scans ~150 string comparisons per object.

**Fix:** Replace the chain with a registry `std::unordered_map<std::string, factory_fn>` populated by the *game* at startup. Parse JSON once into engine-neutral `ObjectDesc`/`LevelDesc` PODs so rapidjson never appears in a header. Factor out `parse_rectangle(const Value&)`. Use `std::string_view` for the type comparisons.

#### 5. throw std::exception("literal") is an MSVC-only extension, used 54 times project-wide

`ArtAttack/LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:34` — **medium** · `portability`

The `std::exception(const char*)` constructor does not exist in the C++ standard; it is a Microsoft extension. libstdc++ and libc++ provide only the default constructor, so none of these compile off MSVC.

In this module: LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:34, 55, 77, 98, 129, 158, 179, 199 (eight in one file); Level.cpp:312, 319, 500, 590, 616, 649, 729; LevelEndInfo.cpp:77, 94, 111; PaintTile.cpp:136. I grepped the tree and counted 54 `std::exception("` sites across first-party .cpp files.

For a project whose stated purpose is a reusable engine, this pins it to one toolchain for no benefit. Several of the messages are also load-bearing diagnostics for level authors (`"Invalid collision type"`, `"Invalid rectangle type"`, `"Invalid paintable edges"`) but carry no context — no file, no object index — so a typo in a level JSON produces an unattributable abort.

**Fix:** Use `std::runtime_error` / `std::invalid_argument` from `<stdexcept>` (already in pch.h). For the builder, include the offending object's index and type string: `throw std::invalid_argument("collision_objects[" + std::to_string(i) + "]: unknown collision_type '" + collision_type + "'");`.

#### 6. JSON rectangle-parsing block duplicated verbatim; ProjectileBuilder repeats the same make_unique 9 times

`ArtAttack/LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:120-139` — **medium** · `design` · confidence: certain

Two builder duplications:

(a) `LevelObjectBuilder::build_collision_object` contains the same 20-line `rectangle` / `rectangle_tlbr` parsing block twice, byte-identical including the `throw std::exception("Invalid rectangle type")` fallthrough: lines 120-139 (Structure branch) and 163-182 (StructurePaintable branch). The surrounding per-type blocks also repeat `json["sheet_name"].GetString(), json["frame_name"].GetString(), ..., colour_consts::colour_from_name(json["colour"].GetString())` four times (:141-148, :215-225, :252-259, and `build_non_collision_object` :271-279). `build_collision_objects` (:285-296) and `build_non_collision_objects` (:298-307) are the same loop twice.

(b) `ProjectileBuilder::build_projectiles` (ProjectileBuilder.cpp:23-113) has four `case` blocks (SPRAY/JET/ROLLING/BALL) that are identical 16-line `vector + push_back(make_unique<ProjectileX>(RectangleF(position, DETAILS_X.col_rect_size), velocity, team, player_num, team_colour, dt, resource_manager, rotation, origin, effects, layer_depth)); return` bodies. `build_mist_projectiles` (:116-201) then repeats the same 14-line `push_back` five more times, differing only in the rotation applied to the velocity (`0`, `+PI/12`, `-PI/12`, `+PI/6`, `-PI/6`). ~200 duplicated lines across the two functions.

Note also line 145 and 219 pass `&rectangle` — the address of a function-local — into the object constructors.

**Fix:** (a) Extract `static RectangleF parse_rectangle(const rapidjson::Value&)` and a `SpriteSpec parse_sprite(const rapidjson::Value&)` for the sheet/frame/colour triple; make `build_collision_objects`/`build_non_collision_objects` one template. (b) In `ProjectileBuilder`, once the Projectile family is collapsed (see that finding) the whole switch becomes one `make_unique<Projectile>(details_for(type), ...)`; the mist spread becomes `for (float a : {0.0f, PI/12, -PI/12, PI/6, -PI/6})`.

#### 7. Ramps are built with collision types no projectile recognises, so projectiles pass straight through them

`ArtAttack/LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:144-177` — **medium** · `correctness`

The `"StructureRamp"` branch produces a plain `Structure` tagged `STRUCTURE_RAMP_LEFT` or `STRUCTURE_RAMP_RIGHT` (LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:148-155, 169-176).

`Projectile::is_matching_collision_object_type` (Projectile.cpp:93-118) only accepts three structure types:
```cpp
bool structure_collision =
    other_type == collision_object_type::STRUCTURE ||
    other_type == collision_object_type::STRUCTURE_PAINTABLE ||
    other_type == collision_object_type::STRUCTURE_JUMP_THROUGH;
```
Ramp types are absent, so projectiles never register a collision with a ramp — they fly through and are never marked for deletion by it. `Projectile::on_collision` (Projectile.cpp:120-132) repeats the same three-way list, so even if detection were fixed the despawn would still miss ramps.

Players *do* collide with ramps: `Player::is_matching_collision_object_type` (Player.cpp:145-147) is `return is_structure(other_type);`, and `is_structure` includes both ramp types (collision_object_type.h:75-82). So the two systems disagree about what a ramp is.

The root cause is that "is this thing solid" is spelled out in three hand-written type lists that have already drifted: collision_object_type.h:75-88, Projectile.cpp:98-101 and Projectile.cpp:124-127.

**Fix:** Replace the hand-rolled lists in `Projectile::is_matching_collision_object_type` and `Projectile::on_collision` with the shared `is_structure(other_type)` predicate. Long term, replace the type-tag enum with per-object collision layer/mask flags so there is exactly one definition of "solid".

#### 8. Two of the four levels/unused/*.json files cannot be loaded at all; nothing marks them as unloadable

`ArtAttack/LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:15-19` — **low** · `robustness` · confidence: certain

`ResourceLoader::load_level_info` (ArtAttack/ResourceLoader.cpp:38-43) currently loads only king_of_the_hill, turbulence and close_quarters, but four more level files sit in `ArtAttack/levels/unused/` and are one line away from being selected. Two of them would fail, in different ways:

- ArtAttack/levels/unused/test_1.json uses `"collision_type": "STRUCTURE_FLOOR_PAINTABLE"` (lines 94, 115) and `"STRUCTURE_WALL"` (lines 136, 150). Neither string exists in the builder's ladders (LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:24-35 accepts only STRUCTURE / STRUCTURE_JUMP_THROUGH; :71-78 only STRUCTURE_PAINTABLE), so it throws `std::exception("Invalid collision type")` — a message that names neither the file, the object, nor the offending string.
- ArtAttack/levels/unused/level_0.json is a completely different schema: its top-level keys are `level_name`, `spawn_locations`, `tile_types` — no `sound`, no `level_bounds`, no `collision_objects`, no `non_collision_objects`. Every `LevelLoadedInfo` accessor (`_json_doc["sound"]["music_name"]` at :78, `_json_doc["level_bounds"][...]` at :33-61, `_json_doc["collision_objects"]` at :66) would hit a missing member with the NDEBUG-disabled rapidjson assert described elsewhere.

Both also carry the `"grsquare_white_4ass"` frame-name typo (test_1.json:159, structure_test_old.json:261).

**Fix:** Delete `ArtAttack/levels/unused/` from the repo — it is dead content in an incompatible schema. If it is kept as reference, at minimum make the builder's exception messages include the file path, object `name` and the unrecognised string, so a bad level is diagnosable rather than a bare 'Invalid collision type'.

#### 9. The 'name' field on every level object is never read, and duplicate names in the data prove nobody would notice

`ArtAttack/LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:15-200` — **low** · `design` · confidence: certain

Every object in every level file carries a `"name"` field — 33 collision objects + 6 visuals in king_of_the_hill.json alone (json:84, 99, 114, 134, …). `LevelObjectBuilder::build_collision_object` and `build_non_collision_object` read only `type`, `collision_type`, `sheet_name`, `frame_name`, `colour`, and `rectangle`/`rectangle_tlbr`/`triangle`/`paintable_faces`. `json["name"]` appears nowhere in the codebase.

Evidence that this silently rots: king_of_the_hill.json:164 and king_of_the_hill.json:209 are both named `"spawn_a_ceiling"` — the second is actually team B's ceiling (x = 5700). The identical duplication exists in close_quarters.json and turbulence.json. Nothing surfaced it because nothing consumes the field.

Also unread: `"rectangle_tlbr"` is supported by the parser (LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:45-52, :88-95) but no level file on disk uses it — a whole code path with zero coverage from either data or tests.

**Fix:** Either use the name (store it on the object and include it in the builder's exception messages — 'Invalid collision type "STRUCTURE_WALL" for object "floor_2" in test_1.json' is worth far more than the current bare string), or drop it from the schema. Duplicate names should then be a load-time error.

## `ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp`

_69 findings: 1 critical, 14 high, 43 medium, 11 low_

#### 1. RectangleRotated(Segment, thickness) constructor always throws; no test constructs it

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:4201-4215` — **critical** · `test-coverage` · confidence: certain

The constructor does `this->_x_axis = center_line.get_direction();` then `this->_y_axis = Vector2F::normal(this->_x_axis);` and then `if (!this->is_valid()) throw std::invalid_argument(...)`. But `Segment::get_direction()` (ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:4063-4066) returns `point_1 - point_0` — un-normalised — while `axes_valid()` (4522-4537) requires `are_equal(_x_axis.length(), 1.0f, EPSILON)`. So this constructor throws for every segment whose length is not within 1e-4 of 1.0. Note the sibling 4-arg constructor at 4186 does call `_x_axis.normalize()`, so the two constructors disagree. Every RectangleRotated test in MattMathTests/MathTests.cpp (lines 356-403, 491-515, 629-662, 736-765, 783-830, 831-873) uses only the 4-arg constructor; the Segment overload has zero tests. This is the overload intended for paint trails / thick line segments, i.e. the reason OBBs were added.

**Fix:** Normalise in the Segment ctor (`_x_axis = Vector2F::unit_vector(center_line.get_direction())`) and add tests: construct from a segment of length 10 with thickness 2, assert `get_half_extents()`, `get_angle()`, the four corner points, and that a zero-length segment throws (`Assert::ExpectException<std::invalid_argument>`).

#### 2. The Shape dispatch layer every in-game collision goes through has zero tests

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:119-175` — **high** · `test-coverage` · confidence: certain

`Shape::intersects(const Shape* other)` is a `switch` on `other->get_shape_type()` doing `dynamic_cast` to the concrete type and re-dispatching (lines 119-136), with `default: throw std::invalid_argument("Shape type not recognized")`. `shape_type` includes a `NONE` member (ArtAttack/shape_type.h:11) which has no case, so any shape reporting NONE throws mid-frame. `Shape::AABB_intersects` (143-151) and the four free `shapes_intersect` / `shapes_AABB_intersect` wrappers (157-175) are equally untested. Every test in the suite calls the concrete free functions (`rectangle_triangle_intersect`, `quad_rectangle_rotated_intersect`, …) directly and bypasses this layer entirely — yet this layer is what `Player::is_colliding`, `CollisionTools::calculate_object_collision_direction` and `bracket_object_collision_generic` actually call. The suite tests the leaves and skips the trunk.

**Fix:** Add a `Shape*`-based matrix test: for all 25 ordered pairs of the five concrete shape types, construct one overlapping and one separated pair, call `shapes_intersect(a.get(), b.get())`, and assert symmetry (`a->intersects(b) == b->intersects(a)`) — symmetry alone is a strong oracle and needs no hand-derived expected values.

#### 3. triangles_intersect only tests 4 of the 9 edge pairs — two triangles can cross and be reported as disjoint

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:381-407` — **high** · `correctness`

Verified, and this is the most serious live defect the reviewers surfaced (it was buried inside a design candidate about copy-pasted algorithms). MattMath.cpp:393-404:
```cpp
std::vector<Segment> a_edges = a.get_edges();  // 3 edges
std::vector<Segment> b_edges = b.get_edges();  // 3 edges
for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++)
{
    if (segments_intersect(a_edges[i], b_edges[0]) ||
        segments_intersect(a_edges[i], b_edges[1]))
```
`i < 2` skips a_edges[2], and b_edges[2] is never tested at all. Only 4 of the 9 pairs are checked. Two triangles that overlap edge-on with no vertex of either inside the other (the vertex checks at 384-390 fail) and whose only crossings involve edge 2 return false. This is not dead code: Triangle::intersects(Triangle) forwards here, and triangle_quad_intersect (409-424), quads_intersect (492-511) and quad_rectangle_rotated_intersect (545-561) are all built on it. The function also has no AABB early-out, unlike its siblings at 196 and 264.

**Fix:** Replace the double loop with a full `for (i in 0..2) for (j in 0..2)` over both edge lists, or — better — write one convex-vs-convex separating-axis test against get_points()/get_edges() and delete the six near-identical hand-written copies at 193-229, 260-298, 381-407, 426-445, 453-490 and 619-661.

#### 4. triangles_intersect tests only 4 of the 9 edge pairs and is asymmetric in its arguments

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:381-407` — **high** · `correctness`

Verified verbatim at 397-404: `for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++) { if (segments_intersect(a_edges[i], b_edges[0]) || segments_intersect(a_edges[i], b_edges[1])) return true; }`. Outer bound is 2 instead of 3 and `b_edges[2]` is never tested, so pairs (a0,b2), (a1,b2), (a2,b0), (a2,b1), (a2,b2) are skipped -- `triangles_intersect(a,b)` can disagree with `triangles_intersect(b,a)`. This is the workhorse behind `triangle_quad_intersect` (409-424), `quads_intersect` (492-511), `quad_segment_intersect`, `quad_point_intersect` and `quad_rectangle_rotated_intersect`, so the miss propagates through the entire quad/OBB path -- a projectile can pass through a structure with no diagnostic. The vertex-containment pre-pass at 384-390 hides most cases but not a hexagram configuration, and not a degenerate triangle: `test_point_triangle` -> `barycentric` (EricsonMath.cpp:729-743) divides by `denom = d00*d11 - d01*d01`, which is 0 for collinear points, giving NaN and all-false comparisons. `Triangle` has no validity check, so degenerate triangles are constructible. The function also has no AABB early-out, unlike every neighbouring routine.

**Fix:** `for (int i=0;i<3;i++) for (int j=0;j<3;j++) if (segments_intersect(a_edges[i], b_edges[j])) return true;` -- or replace the whole point-in/edge-cross approach with SAT over the six edge normals, which is correct and allocation-free. Add an `a.get_bounding_box().intersects(b.get_bounding_box())` early-out.

#### 5. Point-in-OBB does 3 heap allocations, a full Quad validity check and 2 barycentric solves instead of 2 dot products

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:611-617, 4265-4268, 4450-4455` — **high** · `performance`

Merges 3 candidates. `RectangleRotated::contains(p)` (4265-4268) forwards to `point_rectangle_rotated_intersect` (611-617), which is `Quad quad = rect_rotated.get_quad(); return quad_point_intersect(quad, point);`. `get_quad()` (4450-4455) calls `calculate_points()` -- allocation #1 -- even though the identical corners are already cached in `_points`. `Quad(const std::vector<Point2F>&)` (3716-3732) then runs `is_valid()` (3832-3849), which calls `get_edges()` -- allocation #2 -- and does 6 pairwise `segments_intersect`. Then `quad_point_intersect` (530-543) calls `get_triangles()` (3965-3973) -- allocation #3 -- and runs up to 2 barycentric solves (EricsonMath.cpp:729-752). The correct test is two dots and two compares. This is not cold: `rectangles_rotated_intersect` (619-661) calls `contains()` 8 times before it even looks at edges, `triangle_rectangle_rotated_intersect` 3 times (463-474), `rectangle_rotated_rectangle_intersect` 4 times (270-273), `segment_rectangle_rotated_intersect` twice (593), and `CollisionTools::bracket_object_collision_generic` (CollisionTools.cpp:53-68) re-runs the whole narrow phase `BRACKET_ITERATIONS` times per resolved contact. As a bonus, because `Quad`'s ctor throws on invalid input, this read-only query can throw.

**Fix:** Implement `RectangleRotated::contains` directly in the OBB local frame (`Vector2F d = point - _center; return std::abs(Vector2F::dot(d,_x_axis)) <= _hw_extents.x && std::abs(Vector2F::dot(d,_y_axis)) <= _hw_extents.y;`) and have `point_rectangle_rotated_intersect` forward to it. Make `get_quad()` build from the cached `_points`.

#### 6. RectangleRotated exposes a full OBB interface (axes, half-extents, indexed accessors) that no intersection routine uses; the OBB path is brute-force point/edge enumeration instead of SAT

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:619-661` — **high** · `design`

`get_axis(int)` (4315-4327), `get_half_width(int)` (4340-4352), `get_half_extents()` and `get_center()` are exactly the interface Ericson's OBB SAT consumes, and `EricsonMath.h:141` already declares `closest_pt_point_OBB(const Point2F&, const OBB&, Point2F&)`. Yet `rectangles_rotated_intersect` (619-661) does an AABB pre-check, then 8 `contains()` calls (each the 3-allocation path above), then a 4x4 = 16 segment-segment loop -- where 2D OBB-vs-OBB SAT is 4 axis projections and no allocation. `circle_rectangle_rotated_intersect` (353-379) likewise enumerates edges rather than using `closest_pt_point_OBB`. The class stores exactly the right data and then never uses it.

**Fix:** Implement `rectangles_rotated_intersect` as 4-axis SAT over `get_axis(0/1)` of both boxes, `contains` as the two-dot-product test, and `circle_rectangle_rotated_intersect` as `distance_squared(circle.center, closest_pt_point_OBB(...)) <= r*r`. This is also the general answer to the fat-interface finding: convex shapes should expose projection/support and one SAT routine should serve them all.

#### 7. RectangleF::get_edges() returns {top, bottom, left, right} while its only consumer indexes it as clockwise

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:808-818` — **high** · `correctness`

Verified. MattMath.cpp:808-818 returns `{get_top_edge(), get_bottom_edge(), get_left_edge(), get_right_edge()}`. Every other shape is cyclic: Triangle::get_edges (3502-3511) is p0->p1, p1->p2, p2->p0; RectangleRotated::get_edges (4284-4293) is edge_0..edge_3 built from _points[i],_points[i+1]; RectangleRotated::edges_valid (4539-4555) does `edges[(i+1)%4]`, which only makes sense for a cyclic list. The sole consumer, StructurePaintable.cpp:188-212, maps i==0->top, i==1->right, i==2->bottom, i==3->left. Only index 0 agrees. LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:104-124 builds _paintable_edges from rectangle.get_left_edge()/get_top_edge()/get_right_edge()/get_bottom_edge() driven by the `paintable_faces` JSON block, and the match at StructurePaintable.cpp:193 is Segment==Segment. So a level marking `"right": true` matches edges[3] (the right edge) and sets left_edge=true, painting the LEFT face. Mapping is bottom->right, left->bottom, right->left. All three shipped levels use paintable_faces (close_quarters.json:258,280; king_of_the_hill.json:242+; turbulence.json:242+).

**Fix:** Return cyclic order {top, right, bottom, left} and document on Shape::get_edges() that edge i joins point i to point i+1. Then re-verify StructurePaintable.cpp:195-210 against the new order. Better: delete the Segment-equality index matching entirely and pass the paintable faces as the PaintableFaces flags struct that is already commented out at LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:100-105 and StructurePaintable.cpp:216-280.

#### 8. Shape::get_edges() has no documented ordering and RectangleF's differs from every other shape's; StructurePaintable indexes it as if it didn't

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:808-818` — **high** · `correctness`

Merges 2 candidates. `RectangleF::get_edges()` returns `{ top, bottom, left, right }` (808-818). `Quad::get_edges()` (3943-3953) and `RectangleRotated::get_edges()` (4284-4294) return perimeter order p0->p1, p1->p2, p2->p3, p3->p0. `Triangle::get_edges()` (3502-3511) returns three. `Circle::get_edges()` (3340-3344) returns an empty vector. StructurePaintable.cpp:188-212 consumes the polymorphic result and hard-codes `i==0 -> top, i==1 -> right, i==2 -> bottom, i==3 -> left`. I confirmed the shape really is a `RectangleF`: LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:80-141 builds a `RectangleF rectangle` and passes `&rectangle` as the collision shape, and builds `_paintable_edges` from `rectangle.get_left_edge()/get_top_edge()/get_right_edge()/get_bottom_edge()`. So three of four mappings are wrong: a level whose JSON declares only `paintable_faces.bottom` matches `edges[1]` (the bottom edge) and sets `right_edge = true`, painting the right face instead. Only index 0 (top) is correct.

**Fix:** Document `Shape::get_edges()` as perimeter order starting at `get_points()[0]` and reorder `RectangleF::get_edges()` to `{ top, right, bottom, left }`. Better: key paintable edges by geometry (they are already compared with `operator==` at StructurePaintable.cpp:193) rather than re-deriving a face name from a positional index.

#### 9. An entire unused linear-algebra sublibrary (MatrixF / Matrix3x3F / Vector4F) lives in the core math header

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:2142-2183, 2476-3050` — **high** · `dead-code` · confidence: certain

`MattMath.h:567-584` (Vector4F), `:684-748` (MatrixF + free functions `add/subtract/multiply/divide/gaussian_elimination/transpose/identity/zero/determinant/equal_dimensions`) and `:750-765` (Matrix3x3F) are implemented in `MattMath.cpp` `#pragma region Vector4F` (2142-2183), `#pragma region MatrixF` (2476-2983) and `#pragma region Matrix3x3F` (2985-3050) — roughly 615 lines of live code. I grepped every first-party file: `MatrixF`, `Matrix3x3F`, `VectorF`, `Vector4F`, `gaussian_elimination`, `determinant`, `transpose`, `identity`, `eigenvectors` have **zero** references outside MattMath.h/.cpp, including in MattMathTests. Immediately above it sits `#pragma region Matrix` (MattMath.cpp:1138-1306) and `#pragma region Vector` (:1308-1366) — 231 further lines that are entirely commented out, matching the commented-out `template<typename T> struct Matrix`/`struct Vector` declarations at `MattMath.h:303-352`. So the same abandoned idea exists in the file twice, once dead-by-comment and once dead-by-disuse. MattMath.h is the header every engine type includes, so this is compile cost paid by all 81 TUs.

**Fix:** Delete Vector4F, MatrixF, Matrix3x3F, the commented Matrix/Vector template blocks, and the `#pragma region Matrix`/`Vector` blocks in the .cpp. If a general matrix type is wanted for the engine later, it belongs in its own header with tests, not welded into the 1139-line MattMath.h that every game object pulls in.

#### 10. MatrixF(int, int) never sizes _elements, so every matrix factory writes out of bounds on an empty vector

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:2478-2513, 2995-3048` — **high** · `memory-safety`

Verified exactly as described:
```cpp
MatrixF::MatrixF(int rows, int columns)
{
    this->_rows = rows;
    this->_columns = columns;
}   // _elements (MattMath.h:723) stays empty
```
`get_element`/`set_element` (2494-2513) validate only via `row_valid`/`column_valid` (2701-2708), which test against `_rows`/`_columns`, never `_elements.size()`. So `_elements[calculate_index(row, column)]` indexes an empty vector. Every producer uses this constructor: add (2742), subtract (2761), multiply (2778), divide (2800), multiply(a,float) (2819), divide(a,float) (2833), transpose (2901), identity (2916), zero (2925), determinant's cofactor submatrix (2956), and `Matrix3x3F(float e11..e33)` (2995-3008), which delegates to MatrixF(3,3) and then performs nine out-of-bounds writes. `Matrix3x3F::rotation/scale/translation` (3010-3048) are therefore all memory-unsafe.

What keeps this from being 'critical': a repo-wide grep finds zero references to MatrixF or Matrix3x3F outside MattMath.h/.cpp. It is unreachable dead code — but it is shipped in the public engine header, so the first consumer to touch it corrupts memory.

**Fix:** Delete MatrixF, Matrix3x3F and the free add/subtract/multiply/divide/gaussian_elimination/transpose/identity/zero/determinant functions (MattMath.h:684-765, MattMath.cpp:2476-3050). A 2D engine has no use for a dynamically-sized dense matrix class with a recursive determinant. If it must stay, `_elements.assign(size_t(rows)*columns, 0.0f)` in the constructor and validate against _elements.size().

#### 11. Triangle::get_angle_N returns the supplement of the interior angle

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:3512-3527` — **high** · `correctness`

`get_angle_0()` is `angle_between(get_edge_0().get_direction(), get_edge_2().get_direction())`. edge_0 direction is `p1 - p0`; edge_2 direction is `p0 - p2` -- head-to-tail, not both emanating from p0. The interior angle at p0 is between `(p1 - p0)` and `(p2 - p0)`, so the code computes pi minus that. `get_angle_1` and `get_angle_2` have the same defect, so `get_angles()` (3528-3537) sums to 2*pi instead of pi. Worked example: p0=(0,0), p1=(4,0), p2=(1,1) -> interior 45 deg, code returns acos(-4 / (4*sqrt(2))) = 135 deg. Masked at the only consumer (`find_hypotenuse`) purely because 90 degrees is its own supplement; every other use is wrong.

**Fix:** `get_angle_0 = angle_between(points[1] - points[0], points[2] - points[0])` and equivalently for vertices 1 and 2. Add a test asserting the three angles sum to pi.

#### 12. find_hypotenuse returns a VERTEX index that both callers use as an EDGE index, so get_hypotenuse() returns a leg

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:3633-3652, 3665-3684` — **high** · `correctness`

`find_hypotenuse` (3665-3684) tests `get_angle_0/1/2` -- the angles at vertices 0, 1, 2 -- and returns 0/1/2 accordingly. `get_hypotenuse()` (3641) then does `return this->get_edges()[hypotenuse];` and `get_hypotenuse_gradient()` (3651) does `return this->calculate_gradient(hypotenuse);`. Edge indices are edge_0 = p0->p1, edge_1 = p1->p2, edge_2 = p2->p0 (3490-3501). The hypotenuse is the edge OPPOSITE the right angle: a right angle at vertex i means hypotenuse index (i+1) % 3. With the right angle at p0 the code returns edge p0->p1, a leg. Wrong for every right triangle. Only reachable from commented-out code (StructureRamp.cpp:24-26), but that is the ramp feature actively being worked on.

**Fix:** Return `(i + 1) % 3` from `find_hypotenuse`, or rename it `find_right_angle_vertex` and adjust both call sites. Replace the angle search with three `length_squared` comparisons (no acos, no sqrt) and add a test asserting `get_hypotenuse()` on TriangleRightAxisAligned((0,0),(1,0),(0,1)) is the segment (1,0)-(0,1).

#### 13. calculate_camera_from_view_rectangle is not the inverse of calculate_view_rectangle; its parameters are named backwards and its divisor is unguarded

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:4156-4169` — **high** · `correctness`

Merges 3 candidates (correctness / design / robustness). Body verified at 4165-4167: `Camera(view_rectangle.x - world_rectangle.x, view_rectangle.y - world_rectangle.y, world_rectangle.width / view_rectangle.width)`. The forward transform (4116-4123) is `view = (world - t) * s`; the true inverse is `s = view.w / world.w`, `t = world.x - view.x / s`. The code returns the RECIPROCAL scale and a translation that drops the `/s` and flips the sign. It only works at its sole call site because Level.cpp:150-156 passes the arguments swapped relative to their names: `_zoom_out_start_bounds` (a world-space level rect, Level.h:133, loaded from JSON at LevelLoadedInfo.cpp:46-52) goes into the `view_rectangle` slot and `RectangleF(Vector2F::ZERO, resolution)` (the screen rect) into `world_rectangle` -- so `s = screen.w / level.w` and `t = level.pos - 0`, which happens to be right only because the screen rect's origin is (0,0). Anyone calling it per its parameter names gets a garbage camera. There is also no guard on `view_rectangle.width == 0`, and that width comes straight from `_json_doc["level_bounds"]["zoom_out_start_bounds"]["width"].GetFloat()` with no validation, so a data typo yields an infinite scale and a blank frame with no diagnostic. A stale commented-out alternative sits at 4160-4162, evidence the semantics were never pinned down.

**Fix:** Rename the parameters to match reality, or fix the body to be the true inverse and fix Level.cpp. Guard the zero divisor and validate the rectangle at load time with a message naming the level file. Delete the commented-out alternative. Add a round-trip test: `calculate_view_rectangle(w, calculate_camera_from_view_rectangle(v, w)) == v`.

#### 14. RectangleRotated::is_valid() is a no-op during construction and no test exercises the invalid path

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:4186-4200, 4464-4480, 4539-4565` — **high** · `test-coverage` · confidence: certain

The 4-arg ctor calls `this->is_valid()` at line 4194 and only assigns `this->_points = this->calculate_points()` at line 4199 — after the check. `is_valid()` calls `edges_valid()` (4539), which does `std::vector<Segment> edges = this->get_edges();` built from `_points`, which at that moment is still the header's default-member-initialiser `{ Point2F::ZERO, Point2F::ZERO, Point2F::ZERO, Point2F::ZERO }` (ArtAttack/MattMath.h:1119-1120). Four zero-length edges: every `dot(...) == 0` perpendicularity check passes and every `get_length()` pair compares 0 == 0, so `edges_valid()` returns true unconditionally at construction time. Two thirds of the validation is dead. Zero tests call `is_valid()`, and there is no test that a malformed RectangleRotated is rejected — the suite only ever builds valid ones.

**Fix:** Compute `_points` before validating, then add tests for the rejection paths: non-perpendicular axes, zero half-extents, negative half-extents, and a valid case. Use `Assert::ExpectException<std::invalid_argument>`.

#### 15. RectangleRotated(Segment, thickness) never normalises its axes, so it throws for every segment whose length != 1

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:4201-4215` — **high** · `correctness`

Merges 5 duplicate candidates (all four "segment ctor" reports plus the "three divergent construction paths" report). Verified verbatim: line 4205 `this->_x_axis = center_line.get_direction();` and 4206 `this->_y_axis = Vector2F::normal(this->_x_axis);`. `Segment::get_direction()` (4063-4066) returns `point_1 - point_0` raw; `Vector2F::normal` (1865-1868) returns `(-y, x)` and does not normalise. `axes_valid()` (4522-4529) requires `are_equal(_x_axis.length(), 1.0f, EPSILON)` with EPSILON=1e-4 (MattMath.h:46). So the ctor at 4209-4212 throws unless the centre line is 1.0 +/- 1e-4 long. The sibling ctor at 4191-4192 does call `normalize()` on both axes -- a straight copy-paste omission. Two further defects hide behind the throw: (a) `_hw_extents = (length/2 + thickness, thickness)` makes the box 2*thickness LONGER than the centre line while `thickness` doubles as a half-width -- an undocumented asymmetry; (b) `normal((1,0)) = (0,1)` = DIRECTION_DOWN, whereas the other ctor's default `_y_axis` is DIRECTION_UP (MattMath.h:1116), so the two constructors wind opposite ways. Severity downgraded from the reported "critical": nothing crashes or corrupts, and there is no first-party caller, so this is a dead-on-arrival public API rather than a live crash.

**Fix:** Delegate: `RectangleRotated(const Segment& l, float t) : RectangleRotated(l.get_center(), l.get_direction(), Vector2F::normal(l.get_direction()), Vector2F(l.get_length()/2.0f, t)) {}` -- the 4-arg ctor already normalises. Decide and document whether the box should overhang the endpoints. Pick one y-axis convention for both ctors. Add a MathTests case; MathTests.cpp only ever calls the 4-arg form (lines 359, 376, 493, 631, 738, 785, 801, 833-866).

#### 16. MattMath::sign truncates a float determinant to int, returning 0 for any |cross| < 1

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:86-91` — **medium** · `correctness`

Verified:
```cpp
int MattMath::sign(const Vector2F& p1, const Vector2F& p2, const Vector2F& p3)
{
    return static_cast<int>((p1.x - p3.x) * (p2.y - p3.y) -
        (p2.x - p3.x) * (p1.y - p3.y));
}
```
This is the standard half-plane/orientation predicate, whose whole purpose is the *sign* of the determinant. `static_cast<int>` truncates toward zero, so every configuration with |determinant| < 1 — every small or thin triangle, and every near-collinear case, which is precisely what the predicate exists to resolve — returns 0. Callers written as `sign(...) < 0` / `> 0` both take the false branch. Callers comparing two sign() results for equality (the standard barycentric point-in-triangle idiom) compare magnitudes, not signs. Declared at MattMath.h:56-57, zero call sites.

**Fix:** Delete it, or rename to `float orient2d(...)` returning the raw determinant (the standard name and contract) and add a separate `int sign_of(float)` with an epsilon band. Express it in terms of a fixed Vector2F::cross so the operation exists once.

#### 17. Shape::intersects dynamic_casts after already switching on the shape_type tag, and dereferences both results unchecked

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:119-136` — **medium** · `design`

Verified:
```cpp
switch (other->get_shape_type())
{
case shape_type::RECTANGLE:
    return this->intersects(*dynamic_cast<const RectangleF*>(other));
...
default: throw std::invalid_argument("Shape type not recognized");
```
Three issues, in descending order of how much I believe them:
1. The switch has already established the dynamic type, so the dynamic_cast buys nothing and costs an out-of-line MSVC RTTI walk on the innermost call of the collision system. static_cast is correct here.
2. Hand-rolled double dispatch: Shape declares seven intersects overloads (MattMath.h:73-79) but shape_type enumerates five, because Segment and Point2F are not Shapes — so two of the seven pure virtuals every shape must implement can never be reached through the dispatcher. Adding a shape means editing a shape_type value, a pure virtual, five overrides, a switch case and ~6 free functions.
3. `other` is dereferenced with no null check and the dynamic_cast result is dereferenced with no null check. Not reachable today (all get_shape() implementations return member addresses or unique_ptr::get()), but the author clearly intended defensiveness here — the default case throws — and only half-implemented it. This part is speculative rather than a live defect.

**Fix:** Replace the dynamic_casts with static_cast immediately. Longer term, replace the hierarchy with a closed sum type (std::variant over the concrete shapes) and a single `intersects(const Shape&, const Shape&)` via std::visit over a symmetric overload set, so the compiler enforces exhaustiveness. Also fix the misleading free-function name at MattMath.h:117: rectangle_rotated_rectangle_intersect(const RectangleF&, const RectangleRotated&) reads as (rotated, rect) but takes the opposite order.

#### 18. Shape::intersects switches on a hand-maintained type tag and then dynamic_casts anyway, dereferencing the result unchecked

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:119-151` — **medium** · `design`

Merges 4 candidates. The switch at 121-135 has already established the concrete type from `get_shape_type()`, so each `*dynamic_cast<const RectangleF*>(other)` pays an MSVC RTTI walk for nothing -- on the hottest path in the engine (`Level::update_level_logic` runs pairwise `is_colliding`, and `CollisionTools::bracket_object_collision_generic` reruns the narrow phase `BRACKET_ITERATIONS` times per contact). The result is dereferenced immediately with no null test. Two consequences reported by reviewers are OVERSTATED and I am correcting them: (a) no current subclass can produce a null cast -- `TriangleRightAxisAligned` reports `shape_type::TRIANGLE` and `dynamic_cast<const Triangle*>` succeeds on it; (b) `other` itself is never null-checked and `Structure() = default` (Structure.h:10) leaves `_collision_shape = nullptr` (Structure.h:40), but I found no code path that actually default-constructs a `Structure`, so that is latent, not live. What is real today is the wasted RTTI plus a `default: throw std::invalid_argument` arm reachable only via `shape_type::NONE`, thrown from inside a query.

**Fix:** Pick one mechanism: trust the tag and use `static_cast` (with a debug assert on the dynamic_cast), or drop the tag and do proper double dispatch (`virtual bool intersects_with(const Shape&) const`). Take `const Shape&` rather than `const Shape*` throughout so null is not representable, and delete the pointer overloads and the free `shapes_*` wrappers.

#### 19. The convex-vs-convex intersection algorithm is retyped once per shape pair, and the copies have diverged

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:193-661` — **medium** · `design`

Verified. The same three-phase algorithm (AABB reject -> does A contain any vertex of B -> does B contain any vertex of A -> do any edges cross) appears with only the accessors changed at rectangle_triangle_intersect (193-229), rectangle_rotated_rectangle_intersect (260-298), triangle_rectangle_rotated_intersect (453-490), triangles_intersect (381-407), rectangles_rotated_intersect (619-661) and triangle_segment_intersect (426-445). A second family — 'split the quad into triangles and loop' — is typed six times at rectangle_quad_intersect (231-245), circle_quad_intersect (319-331), triangle_quad_intersect (409-424), quads_intersect (492-511), quad_segment_intersect (513-528), quad_point_intersect (530-543) and quad_rectangle_rotated_intersect (545-561).

The copies have already diverged in two verified ways: triangles_intersect is missing the AABB early-out its siblings have, and its edge loop is wrong (see the separate high finding). This is the concrete cost of the duplication, not a hypothetical one.

**Fix:** Every one of these shapes exposes get_points() and get_edges(). Write the convex-vs-convex test once against those two accessors — ideally as a separating-axis test over the union of both shapes' edge normals, an O(n+m) function correct for all convex pairs — and keep only the genuinely special cases (circle-vs-X) separate.

#### 20. The convex-polygon intersection algorithm is hand-copied four times, and 42 forwarding overloads implement an N x N dispatch matrix

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:193-227` — **medium** · `design` · confidence: certain

Two overlapping duplications in one file:

(a) The identical "AABB reject -> A contains any vertex of B -> B contains any vertex of A -> any edge pair intersects" algorithm is written out four times with only the vertex accessors changed:
- `rectangle_triangle_intersect` (:193-227)
- `rectangle_rotated_rectangle_intersect` (:260-297)
- `triangle_rectangle_rotated_intersect` (:453-487)
- `rectangles_rotated_intersect` (:619-660)
~150 lines. A further three functions (`rectangle_quad_intersect` :231-244, `triangle_quad_intersect` :409-423, `quad_rectangle_rotated_intersect` :545-560) are the same "split quad into triangles, loop" reduction copied three times.

(b) `MattMath.cpp` contains 42 `X::intersects(const Y&)` member definitions (RectangleF :888-918, Circle :3364-3390, Triangle :3549-3581, Quad :3988-4020, Segment :4054-4060, RectangleRotated :4237-4263), essentially all 3-line forwarders to the free function with the argument order flipped — e.g. `bool Triangle::intersects(const RectangleF& other) const { return rectangle_triangle_intersect(other, *this); }`. `MattMath.h` declares 48 `bool intersects(` overloads. On top of that sits `Shape::intersects` (:119-136), a `dynamic_cast`-per-branch dispatcher.

The pairwise matrix is what forces every new shape (RectangleRotated was added recently) to add ~7 new free functions plus ~7 overloads on every existing shape.

**Fix:** (a) Write one `bool convex_polygons_intersect(const Point2F* a, size_t na, const Point2F* b, size_t nb)` (or a proper SAT implementation) and have every polygon-vs-polygon case call it after an AABB reject; the quad cases become `for (tri : quad.get_triangles())` over that one function. (b) Give `Shape` a virtual `get_vertices()`/`get_edges()` and dispatch generically, or keep an explicit `shape_type x shape_type` function-pointer table, instead of an O(N^2) hand-written overload matrix.

#### 21. Circle intersection tests take a square root where a squared comparison is exact and free

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:300-304, 333-351` — **medium** · `performance`

`circles_intersect` (300-304) is `Vector2F::distance(a.center, b.center) <= a.radius + b.radius`, and `Vector2F::distance` (1820-1824) calls `sqrtf`. Same at `circle_segment_intersect` (339) and `circle_point_intersect` (348-351). `Vector2F::distance_squared` (1825-1829) already exists and is used by none of them, and `EricsonMath::test_circle_circle` (EricsonMath.cpp:298-306) already does the squared form correctly -- so the file contains both the right and the wrong implementation of the same test. Circles are the projectile shape, so these are among the highest-frequency calls in the engine, and the bracket search reruns them per iteration.

**Fix:** `float r = a.radius + b.radius; return Vector2F::distance_squared(a.center, b.center) <= r * r;` and the equivalent in the other two. No behaviour change for non-negative radii, one transcendental removed from the hottest path.

#### 22. The "cheap AABB early-out" in the OBB and triangle paths is more expensive than the test it guards

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:623, 457` — **medium** · `performance`

`rectangles_rotated_intersect` opens with `if (!a.intersects(b.get_bounding_box())) return false;` (623). `a.intersects(const RectangleF&)` (4237-4240) dispatches to `rectangle_rotated_rectangle_intersect` (260-298), which is a FULL OBB-vs-AABB test: its own bounding-box check, 4 `rotated_rect.contains()` calls, 4 `rect.contains()` calls, a `get_edges()` allocation and 4 segment-AABB tests -- roughly 15 heap allocations, strictly more work than the loop it is guarding. Same mistake at 457: `if (!triangle.intersects(rect_rotated.get_bounding_box()))` routes to the full `rectangle_triangle_intersect` (193-229). By contrast the guards at 264 and 587 do reduce to cheap tests, so the pattern is inconsistent as well as slow.

**Fix:** Use `a.get_bounding_box().intersects(b.get_bounding_box())` (which reaches `EricsonMath::test_AABB_AABB`, EricsonMath.cpp:283-296) at both sites.

#### 23. segments_intersect reports collinear overlapping segments as disjoint; the a == b patch only covers identically-ordered duplicates

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:563-581` — **medium** · `correctness`

`segments_intersect(a, b, t, p)` special-cases `if (a == b)` and otherwise delegates to `EricsonMath::test_2D_segment_segment` (EricsonMath.cpp:697-725), which requires `a1 * a2 < 0.0f` AND `a3 * a4 < 0.0f` -- strictly opposite signed areas. Collinear segments give zero areas and fall through to `// Segments not intersecting (or collinear) return 0`. Two segments lying on the same line and fully overlapping are reported disjoint. The `a == b` patch is narrow: `Segment::operator==` (4045-4049) compares componentwise, so `Segment((0,0),(10,0))` and `Segment((10,0),(0,0))` -- the same geometry reversed -- are not equal and the collinear miss stands; partial overlap is never handled. This is the primitive under `Quad::is_valid`, `triangles_intersect`, `triangle_segment_intersect`, `segment_rectangle_rotated_intersect` and `rectangles_rotated_intersect`, so two OBBs sharing a collinear face edge are reported as not colliding. Note the strict signs also mean endpoint-touching never counts, whereas `rectangle_point_intersect` (252-258) and `circle_point_intersect` (348-351) use `<=` so touching DOES count -- the codebase has no single convention.

**Fix:** Handle collinearity explicitly: when all four signed areas are ~0, project both segments onto the dominant axis and test 1D interval overlap. Then decide once whether touching counts and apply it uniformly across all primitives.

#### 24. RectangleF::intersection returns a zero rect at the origin as its no-overlap sentinel, and the collision resolver uses it unchecked

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:1099-1113` — **medium** · `correctness`
