Verified:
```cpp
if (x2 >= x1 && y2 >= y1) { return RectangleF(x1, y1, x2 - x1, y2 - y1); }
else                      { return RectangleF(); }   // (0,0,0,0)
```
The disjoint case returns a rectangle at the world origin, indistinguishable from a legitimate zero-area edge touch at (0,0) — and `>=` deliberately admits edge touches, so both states really occur. The instance overload (920-923) forwards and inherits it.

The consumer does not check. CollisionTools.cpp:214-217:
```cpp
RectangleF inter = RectangleF::intersection(collider->get_bounding_box(), collidee->get_bounding_box());
Vector2F amount = { inter.width, inter.height };
...
collider->offset(opposite_direction(direction) * amount);
```
The caller established a *shape* intersection, not an AABB one, so for triangles/circles/OBBs the AABBs can genuinely be disjoint; the push-out is then silently zero and the routine reports success. `union_of` (1114-1121) has no failure case and is fine.

**Fix:** Split query from computation: keep `bool intersects()` for the test and change intersection to `bool intersection(const RectangleF&, RectangleF& out) const`, or std::optional<RectangleF> once the project is on C++17. At minimum make the sentinel obviously invalid (negative width) and document it.

#### 25. RectangleF has no width/height >= 0 invariant, and from_top_left_bottom_right builds inverted rects straight from level JSON

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:1122-1133` — **medium** · `robustness`

Verified. `from_top_left_bottom_right` (1122-1128) subtracts without any ordering check, and LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:45-51 and 88-94 feed it directly from untrusted level JSON:
```cpp
Vector2F top_left = Vector2F(json["rectangle_tlbr"]["left"].GetFloat(), json["rectangle_tlbr"]["top"].GetFloat());
Vector2F bottom_right = Vector2F(json["rectangle_tlbr"]["right"].GetFloat(), json["rectangle_tlbr"]["bottom"].GetFloat());
rectangle = RectangleF::from_top_left_bottom_right(top_left, bottom_right);
```
Swap left/right in a level file and every predicate silently returns the wrong answer rather than failing: rectangle_point_intersect (252-258) tests `x >= rect.x && x <= rect.x + width` and can never be true with negative width; contains(RectangleF) (881-887) likewise; get_right() (764-767) returns a value left of get_left(); intersection (1099) reports no overlap. The object loads, draws, and is intangible. Same exposure via the direct RectangleF(x,y,w,h) path and set_width/set_height/scale, none of which validate. Quad::is_valid (MattMath.h:940) and RectangleRotated::is_valid (1108) already establish the validity-check pattern for the other shapes; RectangleF has none.

**Fix:** Normalise the two corners in from_top_left_bottom_right (std::minmax), add `bool RectangleF::is_valid() const { return width >= 0.0f && height >= 0.0f; }`, and have LevelObjectBuilder reject invalid rectangles at load with a message naming the offending object — rather than the current bare `throw std::exception("Invalid rectangle type")`.

#### 26. Every named constant is dynamically initialised, and DebugText.h reads one across TUs during static init

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:1134, 1495, 1907-1916, 2138, 4180` — **medium** · `design`

Verified. None of the constants is constant-initialised, because no constructor involved is constexpr: `RectangleF::ZERO` (1134), `Vector2I::ZERO` (1495), `Vector2F::ZERO/ONE/DIRECTION_RIGHT/DOWN/LEFT/UP` (1907-1912), `RectangleI::ZERO` (2138), `Camera::DEFAULT_CAMERA` (4180). The four diagonal directions (1913-1916) each run `unit_vector()` — a sqrtf and two divides — before main.

The cross-TU dependency is real and verified: DebugText.h:14 has, at namespace scope in a header, `const static MattMath::Vector2F DEBUG_POSITION = MattMath::Vector2F::ZERO;`. That object is dynamically initialised in every including TU from an object dynamically initialised in MattMath.obj, and the relative order across TUs is unspecified. It is benign today only because the correct value is bitwise zero, which zero-initialised static storage already holds. The same line written with Vector2F::ONE, DIRECTION_UP or Camera::DEFAULT_CAMERA (scale = 1.0f) would silently read zeros in a link order the author never tested. The same hazard spreads through ~20 default arguments (DrawObject.h:15, AnimatedSprite.h:17/25, MovingObject.h:14, Mh.h:86/125/154) and through the default member initialisers at MattMath.h:810, 844, 978-979, 984-985, 1114-1120.

One correction to the reviewers: they claimed all these constructors are written as body assignments. RectangleF(float,float,float,float) (MattMath.cpp:667-670) and all four Colour value constructors (2187-2206) do use member-init lists. The non-constexpr point stands regardless — they are out-of-line and RectangleF cannot be a literal type while it inherits Shape.

**Fix:** Make the constructors constexpr and inline in the header, and declare the constants `static constexpr` — under C++17 they become implicitly inline and the ordering question disappears. This depends on detaching RectangleF from Shape and on setting <LanguageStandard>. Failing that, use the Meyers-singleton accessor form. Compute the diagonal directions from literals rather than a runtime unit_vector() call.

#### 27. ~2000 commented-out lines across the tree, 7% of the whole first-party codebase

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:1138-1366` — **medium** · `dead-code` · confidence: certain

2007 of the 27,999 first-party lines are `//`-only. The large contiguous blocks, all of which are superseded implementations left in place beside their replacements:
- `EricsonMath.cpp:7-126` (120) and `:129-280` (152) — an old `Vector`/`AABB`/`Sphere` type set, plus `EricsonMath.h:13-73` (61 lines) of matching declarations.
- `MattMath.cpp:1138-1306` + `:1308-1366` (231) — the commented `Matrix`/`Vector` templates, matching `MattMath.h:303-352`.
- `Level.cpp:402-490` (89) — the previous single-threaded `draw_active_level`, sitting directly under the live deferred-context version at `:375-400`; and `Level.cpp:331-353` — the previous `Level::draw()`.
- `Player.cpp:391-483` (93) — the previous `on_structure_collision` body, above the live one at `:488`.
- `StructurePaintable.cpp:123-180` (58) — the previous edge-walking paint-tile generator.
- `Main.cpp:39-81` (43) — `get_adapters()`/`get_outputs()`/`get_adapter0_output0_rect()`; `Main.cpp:368-374+` — the ALT+ENTER fullscreen toggle.
- `MainMenu.cpp:55` — `//this->_music->Stop();`, the only reference to the member `MainMenu.h:138 std::unique_ptr<SoundEffectInstance> _music`, which is otherwise never assigned or used.
Having the old and new implementation of the same function adjacent in the same file is actively misleading when reading the code.

**Fix:** Delete all of it. It is in git. The specific hazard here is not disk space but that a reader of Level.cpp or Player.cpp cannot tell which of the two bodies is authoritative without checking indentation.

#### 28. Vector2I division has no zero guard, and Vector2I::scale(SimpleMath::Vector2) truncates the scale factor to int

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:1439-1456, 1470-1479, 1512-1519` — **medium** · `robustness`

Two verified defects in the same block, merged.

1. `operator/=(const Vector2I&)` (1439-1444), `operator/=(int)` (1451-1456) and the free forms (1512-1519) do raw integer division. Unlike the float equivalents, integer division by zero is UB and raises #DE on x86 — an instant process kill, not a quiet NaN. No guard, no documented precondition. Zero callers today, which is the only reason no crash has been seen; graded medium not high for that reason.

2. Worse and more concrete — `void Vector2I::scale(const DirectX::SimpleMath::Vector2& amount)` (1475-1479):
```cpp
this->x *= static_cast<int>(amount.x);
this->y *= static_cast<int>(amount.y);
```
The *scale factor* is truncated to int before multiplying, so `scale({1.5f, 1.5f})` multiplies by 1 (no-op) and `scale({0.5f, 0.5f})` multiplies by 0 (zeroes the vector). This is the one overload whose entire purpose is fractional scaling, and it cannot do it.

**Fix:** Delete the component-wise integer division operators — nothing calls them and the operation has no obvious meaning for a 2D point. Fix scale(const Vector2&) to multiply in float and round: `x = static_cast<int>(std::lround(x * amount.x))`, or delete it too.

#### 29. Every value type compares floats with exact ==, and two live code paths depend on bit-exactness under /fp:fast

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:1574-1577` — **medium** · `correctness`

Verified. Bit-exact operator== on Vector2F (1574-1577), RectangleF (863-869), Colour (2242-2248), Vector4F (2166-2172), Vector3F (3058-3063), Segment (4045-4049), Viewport (3287-3295), RectangleI (2053-2059). Meanwhile `MattMath::are_equal` (93-100) exists for exactly this and is used at only three sites outside MattMath.cpp (Player.cpp:767, 802, 811). FloatingPointModel=Fast is set in all four configurations.

Two live dependencies I verified:
- Player::on_structure_ramp_collision (Player.cpp:254-261) does `direction == Vector2F::DIRECTION_UP`, `== DIRECTION_UP_LEFT`, etc. This works only because direction_to_8_cardinal_direction (MattMath.cpp:1870-1904) returns copies of those exact global constants. Any refactor that recomputes the direction instead of returning the constant silently breaks ramp collision.
- StructurePaintable.cpp:193 does `edges[i] == this->_paintable_edges[j]`, comparing Segments whose endpoints were computed by get_left_edge()/get_top_edge()/etc. in two different translation units (LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:112-124 vs StructurePaintable.cpp:188). Both recompute `x + width`; under /fp:fast nothing guarantees identical contraction in both TUs.

**Fix:** Keep operator== exact (correct for a value type) but stop using it for geometric predicates. Have direction_to_8_cardinal_direction return the existing `MattMath::direction` enum (MattMath.h:12-23), and replace the Segment matching in StructurePaintable with the face-flags struct noted in the get_edges finding. Add are_equal overloads for RectangleF/Segment for cases that genuinely want tolerance.

#### 30. Vector2F::cross returns (x*b.y, y*b.x) — the two unsubtracted terms, not a cross product

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:1720-1723` — **medium** · `correctness`

Verified:
```cpp
Vector2F Vector2F::cross(const Vector2F& other) const
{
    return Vector2F(this->x * other.y, this->y * other.x);
}
```
The 2D perp-dot product is the scalar `x*b.y - y*b.x`. This returns a vector holding the two operands of that subtraction — meaningless under any interpretation; `a.cross(a)` returns a nonzero vector where the answer must be zero. It sits at MattMath.h:443 next to the (correct) `dot`, so it reads as a legitimate sibling. Zero callers, but this is exactly the primitive a separating-axis or winding test would reach for, and the collision code has no correct version of it (see the `sign` finding).

**Fix:** Change to `float cross(const Vector2F& other) const { return x*other.y - y*other.x; }` plus a static overload mirroring `dot`, and fold MattMath::sign into it. Add a unit test in MattMathTests/MathTests.cpp, which already covers dot/length.

#### 31. normalized()/normalize() divide by zero while the identical to_unit_vector()/unit_vector() guard against it

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:1724-1734` — **medium** · `robustness`

Verified. `normalized()` (1724-1728) and `normalize()` (1729-1734) divide by `length()` with no zero check; `to_unit_vector()` (1774-1787) and `static unit_vector()` (1852-1863) perform the same computation but test `length == 0.0f` and return (1,0). Four functions, two mutually incompatible zero-length contracts, no documentation of which is which.

I have to correct the reviewers on the consequences, which were overstated across several candidates:
- MovingObject::get_unit_velocity()/get_unit_dx() (MovingObject.cpp:52-55, 100-103) do call the unguarded `normalized()` on members that are zero at rest — but both have **zero callers**, so no NaN reaches gameplay today.
- RectangleRotated::set_x_axis/set_y_axis (4359-4380) normalise then call axes_valid(), which does are_equal(length, 1.0f) — false for NaN — and throws. NaN does not get stored. Same for the OBB constructor at 4186-4200. The claim that these 'silently store NaN and stop colliding' is wrong.
- What *is* genuinely unguarded: Triangle::inflate (3464-3466) and Quad::inflate (3821-3824) normalise centre-to-vertex vectors with no degenerate check, producing NaN points for a degenerate shape.
A separate real bug I found next door: `RectangleRotated(const Segment& center_line, float thickness)` (4201-4215) assigns `_x_axis = center_line.get_direction()` **without normalising** (unlike the other constructor at 4191-4192), so axes_valid() rejects any centre line whose length isn't 1 and the constructor always throws.

**Fix:** Collapse to two functions — `Vector2F normalized() const` and `void normalize()` — both with one documented zero-length policy, and delete to_unit_vector/unit_vector. Returning (1,0) is the worst option: it invents a direction the caller cannot distinguish from a real one. Separately, normalise the axes in the Segment-based RectangleRotated constructor.

#### 32. normalize()/normalized() have no zero-length guard while the sibling to_unit_vector()/unit_vector() do, and the shape code uses the unguarded pair

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:1724-1734` — **medium** · `correctness`

Merges 2 candidates. `normalized()` (1724-1728) and `normalize()` (1729-1734) divide by `length()` unconditionally; `to_unit_vector()` (1774-1787) and `unit_vector()` (1852-1863) both check `length == 0.0f` and fall back to (1,0). Four functions, one job, two degenerate-input policies, and no naming hint which is which. The shape code consistently picks the unguarded pair: `Triangle::inflate` (3464-3466) and `Quad::inflate` (3821-3824) normalise centre-to-vertex vectors, so a vertex coincident with the centroid writes NaN straight into `points[i]` -- and NaN comparisons are all false, so the shape silently stops colliding rather than throwing. `RectangleRotated` ctor (4191-4192) and `set_x_axis`/`set_y_axis` (4361, 4372) take the same path. `/fp:fast` is on in all four configurations, so the compiler may assume no NaNs and the downstream behaviour is unpredictable rather than merely wrong.

**Fix:** Give `normalize()`/`normalized()` the same zero guard (or an assert) and collapse the four near-duplicates into one. In Triangle/Quad::inflate, skip vertices whose offset from the centre is below EPSILON, and hoist the `(p - center).length()` that is recomputed after the normalise.

#### 33. rotate_vector_by_ref clobbers vec.x before using it to compute vec.y

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:1800-1807` — **medium** · `correctness`

Verified verbatim:
```cpp
void Vector2F::rotate_vector_by_ref(Vector2F& vec, float angle)
{
    float cos_angle = std::cos(angle);
    float sin_angle = std::sin(angle);
    vec.x = vec.x * cos_angle - vec.y * sin_angle;
    vec.y = vec.x * sin_angle + vec.y * cos_angle;   // reads the NEW x
}
```
Not a rotation for any angle but 0. Rotating (1,0) by 90 degrees gives (0,0). The two siblings are correct: `Vector2F::rotate(float)` (1757-1767) caches into locals, and the static `rotate_vector` (1792-1799) builds a new vector. Zero callers repo-wide (only the declaration at MattMath.h:464), which is why it has survived; `rotate_vector` is the one that is actually used (ProjectileBuilder.cpp:149,163,177,191; Weapon.cpp:150). Three reviewers reported this at severities from high to medium; graded medium because it is unreachable, but it is a public API of the engine's math library and looks like the efficient in-place variant.

**Fix:** Delete it. `vec.rotate(angle)` already covers the in-place case, and three spellings of one 4-multiply operation is why one of them rotted. If it must stay, compute both components into locals first.

#### 34. angle_between feeds an unclamped quotient to std::acos and has no zero-length guard

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:1808-1811` — **medium** · `robustness`

Verified: `return std::acos(Vector2F::dot(a, b) / (a.length() * b.length()));`. Two unguarded failures: (1) no clamp to [-1,1], so rounding on nearly parallel/antiparallel inputs yields 1.0000001 and acos returns NaN — and the project builds with FloatingPointModel=Fast in all four configurations (ArtAttack.vcxproj:94,116,139,165), which licenses reassociation of the dot product; (2) zero-length input divides by zero.

Downstream, verified: Triangle::get_angle_0/1/2 (3512-3527) are built on it, and TriangleRightAxisAligned::find_hypotenuse (3665-3684) tests `are_equal(angle, PI_OVER_2)` for each. Every comparison against NaN is false, so it returns -1 and get_hypotenuse()/get_hypotenuse_gradient() (3633-3652) throw 'Triangle is not a right triangle' about a triangle that is one.

I reject the escalation that this 'crashes level loading': LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:161-176 only calls `triangle.get_bounding_box()` on the TriangleRightAxisAligned, never get_hypotenuse, and every consumer of the hypotenuse API (StructureRamp.cpp) is commented out. RectangleRotated::get_angle() (4460-4463) has the same exposure and also has no callers.

**Fix:** Guard both ends: `const float denom = a.length()*b.length(); if (denom == 0.0f) return 0.0f; return std::acos(MattMath::clamp(dot(a,b)/denom, -1.0f, 1.0f));`. For find_hypotenuse specifically, test `are_equal(dot(e0, e2), 0.0f)` — far better conditioned near 90 degrees than an acos round-trip — and return bool+out-param instead of a magic -1 the caller turns into a throw.

#### 35. angle_between has no acos domain clamp and no zero-length guard

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:1808-1811` — **medium** · `correctness`

Merges 2 candidates. `return std::acos(Vector2F::dot(a, b) / (a.length() * b.length()));` -- the quotient is not clamped to [-1,1], so for nearly-parallel vectors float rounding gives 1.0000001 and acos returns NaN; and a zero-length input makes the denominator 0. Both are reachable from the shape API: `Triangle::get_angle_0/1/2` (3512-3527) feed it edge directions, and a degenerate triangle gives a zero direction. The NaN then propagates: `find_hypotenuse` (3665-3684) compares NaN against PI_OVER_2 with `are_equal` (93-96, `fabs(NaN - x) < eps` is false), so all three branches fail, it returns -1, and `get_hypotenuse()` throws "Triangle is not a right triangle" for a triangle that is one. `/fp:fast` in all four configurations makes the domain overshoot more likely, not less.

**Fix:** `float d = a.length() * b.length(); if (d <= 0.0f) return 0.0f; return std::acos(MattMath::clamp(Vector2F::dot(a,b) / d, -1.0f, 1.0f));` -- `MattMath::clamp` already exists at line 34. Prefer `atan2(cross, dot)`: signed, numerically stable, no epsilon.

#### 36. set_from_hex validates only the string length; a leading '#' silently yields black and a bad digit throws during static init

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:2359-2384` — **medium** · `robustness`

Verified. Three defects in one function:
1. Any length other than 6 or 8 falls to the else branch and becomes opaque black with no diagnostic. `"#ff0000"` is 7 characters, so the near-universal way of writing a hex colour silently produces black.
2. No digit validation. `std::stoi` throws std::invalid_argument on a non-hex character (e.g. "gg0000" passes the length check). Colour.h constructs 153 of these at namespace scope, so a single bad literal there propagates out of a dynamic initialiser and calls std::terminate before main, with no attributable diagnostic.
3. Cost: three or four substr temporaries plus three or four std::stoi calls (each doing strtol with locale handling) per colour, to decode 8 hex nibbles — multiplied by every Colour constant in every including TU.

**Fix:** Add `bool try_set_from_hex(std::string_view)` that strips an optional leading '#', validates every character with std::isxdigit and returns false on failure. Decode nibbles with a small lookup rather than substr+stoi. Once the palette is constexpr this function leaves the startup path entirely.

#### 37. Colour::saturate and Colour::desaturate are byte-identical; no Colour test exists to notice

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:2385-2404, 2359-2384` — **medium** · `test-coverage` · confidence: certain

```
void Colour::saturate(float amount) {
    float grey = this->r*0.3f + this->g*0.59f + this->b*0.11f;
    this->r = grey + amount * (this->r - grey); ... }
void Colour::desaturate(float amount) {
    float grey = this->r*0.3f + this->g*0.59f + this->b*0.11f;
    this->r = grey + amount * (this->r - grey); ... }
```
The two bodies are character-for-character the same, so `desaturate(2.0f)` saturates. Separately, `Colour::set_from_hex` (2359-2384) is fed strings from JSON level data: it silently produces opaque black for any length other than 6 or 8, rejects a leading `#`, and lets `std::stoi` throw `std::invalid_argument` out of the level loader on any non-hex character. Neither function — nor any other Colour member — has a test.

**Fix:** Add a Colour test class: `set_from_hex("FF0000")` -> (1,0,0,1); `"FF000080"` -> alpha 0.5; `"#FF0000"`, `"GG0000"`, `""` -> defined behaviour (assert the exception or the fallback, but assert *something*); `saturate(2)` and `desaturate(2)` must move in opposite directions.

#### 38. Colour::desaturate is a byte-identical copy of Colour::saturate

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:2385-2400` — **medium** · `correctness`

Verified — the two bodies at 2385-2392 and 2393-2400 are the same six statements, differing only in the function name:
```cpp
float grey = this->r * 0.3f + this->g * 0.59f + this->b * 0.11f;
this->r = grey + amount * (this->r - grey);
this->g = grey + amount * (this->g - grey);
this->b = grey + amount * (this->b - grey);
this->clamp_colours();
```
The shared formula lerps *away* from grey as `amount` grows, i.e. it is the saturate behaviour. So `desaturate(1.0f)` — the natural spelling of 'fully desaturate' — is a no-op, and `desaturate(0.0f)` is the only value that greys the colour. Two public API names (MattMath.h:630-631) with opposite meanings doing the same thing; a caller cannot tell which one is wrong. Graded medium rather than high because both have zero callers repo-wide. The Rec.601/NTSC luma weights 0.3/0.59/0.11 are also bare literals duplicated in both bodies.

**Fix:** Implement one primitive (`adjust_saturation(float factor)`) and express both in terms of it, so desaturate(1.0f) yields pure luminance and desaturate(0.0f) is a no-op. Hoist the luma weights to named constants.

#### 39. MatrixF(int,int) never sizes _elements, so every Matrix3x3F factory writes through a null vector - entirely dead code

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:2478-2482` — **medium** · `memory-safety` · confidence: certain

```
MatrixF::MatrixF(int rows, int columns)
{
	this->_rows = rows;
	this->_columns = columns;
}
```
`std::vector<float> _elements;` (MattMath.h:723) stays empty. `set_element` (2504-2513) validates only via `row_valid`/`column_valid` (2701-2708), which compare against `_rows`/`_columns` — never against `_elements.size()` — then does `this->_elements[index] = value;` with `index = row * _columns + column` (2709-2712).

So `Matrix3x3F::Matrix3x3F(float e11 ... e33)` (2995-3009) delegates to `MatrixF(3, 3)` and then performs **nine out-of-bounds writes** on a zero-length vector. In Release that is a write through `nullptr + index`; in Debug with `_ITERATOR_DEBUG_LEVEL=2` it trips 'vector subscript out of range'. Every factory built on that ctor is affected: `rotation` (3010-3017), `scale` ×3 (3018-3036), `translation` ×2 (3037-3048).

The claim is CONFIRMED. Reachability: DEAD. Grep for `MatrixF|Matrix3x3F|Vector4F` across the whole repo returns only MattMath.h, MattMath.cpp, Drawer.h and Drawer.cpp — and Drawer's hits are `Vector3F` only (Drawer.h:21/25, Drawer.cpp:34/43, where it is used as a packed camera x/y/zoom triple). `MatrixF`, `Matrix3x3F` and `Vector4F` have zero construction sites outside MattMath.cpp, including in MattMathTests. None of this ever executes.

**Fix:** Either fix it (`_elements.resize(static_cast<size_t>(rows) * columns, 0.0f);` and have `set_element` assert against `_elements.size()`) or, given the engine has DirectXMath available and uses `XMVECTOR`/`XMMATRIX` elsewhere, delete the hand-rolled `MatrixF`/`Matrix3x3F`/`Vector4F` hierarchy outright. A dynamically-sized matrix class carrying a heap allocation is the wrong tool for 3x3 transforms in a 2D engine. Also note `rows * columns != elements.size()` at 2487 compares `int` to `size_t` (/W4 C4018) — the whole class predates any review.

#### 40. MatrixF::operator== iterates rows over the column count and columns over the row count

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:2647-2666` — **medium** · `correctness`

Verified. `get_dimensions()` (2523-2526) returns `Vector2I(this->_columns, this->_rows)` and is documented at MattMath.h:697 as '// x = columns, y = rows'. But operator== does:
```cpp
for (int i = 0; i < dimensions.x; i++)      // i ranges over COLUMN count
    for (int j = 0; j < dimensions.y; j++)  // j ranges over ROW count
        if (this->get_element(i, j) != ...) // get_element(row, column)
```
So the row index ranges over the column count and vice versa. Square matrices work by accident; for a 2x3, `get_element(2, 0)` fails row_valid and throws std::invalid_argument out of an equality operator. Dead code (no MatrixF users), hence medium not high.

**Fix:** Compare `_rows`, `_columns` and `_elements` directly and delete get_dimensions(), whose x=columns/y=rows convention needs a comment to explain it and is a trap for exactly this reason. Or delete the whole matrix subsystem.

#### 41. Viewport::get_d3d_viewport_ptr reinterpret_casts `this` to an unrelated D3D11_VIEWPORT

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:3213-3216` — **medium** · `memory-safety`

Verified:
```cpp
const D3D11_VIEWPORT* Viewport::get_d3d_viewport_ptr() const
{
    return reinterpret_cast<const D3D11_VIEWPORT*>(this);
}
```
Strict-aliasing UB that works only because Viewport's six floats (MattMath.h:770-775) happen to be declared in the same order as D3D11_VIEWPORT's TopLeftX/TopLeftY/Width/Height/MinDepth/MaxDepth. No static_assert on size, offsets or standard-layout anywhere. Adding a member, reordering, or adding a base class silently produces garbage viewports with no diagnostic.

Graded medium rather than high because it has zero callers (grep across ArtAttack finds only the declaration at MattMath.h:790 and this definition), and the safe alternative `get_d3d_viewport()` sits three lines above at 3201-3212. So it is pure downside with no current upside.

**Fix:** Delete it. Callers needing a pointer for RSSetViewports should hold the value: `const D3D11_VIEWPORT vp = v.get_d3d_viewport(); ctx->RSSetViewports(1, &vp);`. If a zero-copy path is ever needed, make Viewport *contain* a D3D11_VIEWPORT and return &_vp rather than punning.

#### 42. Circle::get_edges() returns an empty vector -- a null-object hole in the Shape interface that silently no-ops callers

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:3340-3344` — **medium** · `design`

Merges 2 candidates. `get_edges()` is pure virtual on `Shape` (MattMath.h:87) because several intersection routines are written as "test my edges against yours" (MattMath.cpp:288-295, 369-376, 599-606, 646-657). A circle cannot honour that, so it returns nothing and every edge-driven algorithm silently reports "nothing to do" instead of failing. The real consumer is StructurePaintable.cpp:188 `std::vector<Segment> edges = this->get_shape()->get_edges();` followed by `for (int i = 0; i < edges.size(); i++)` -- a circular paintable structure would generate zero paint tiles and no diagnostic. This is interface segregation violated: `get_edges` belongs to polygons, not to all shapes.

**Fix:** Introduce a `ConvexPolygon` interface (`get_points()`/`get_edges()`/vertex count) implemented by RectangleF, Triangle, Quad and RectangleRotated but not Circle, and have edge-driven algorithms take `const ConvexPolygon&` so the type system rejects a circle at compile time.

#### 43. Circle::inflate allows a negative radius, after which the circle tests disagree with each other and its AABB is inside out

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:3346-3349` — **medium** · `correctness`

`void Circle::inflate(float amount) { this->radius += amount; }` -- no clamp, no validation, unlike `RectangleRotated::inflate` (4295-4305) which throws for non-positive extents. With radius -5: `EricsonMath::test_circle_AABB` (EricsonMath.cpp:368-375) and `test_circle_triangle` (483-492) compare against `radius * radius`, so -5 behaves exactly like +5 and the circle still collides; `circle_point_intersect` (348-351) and `circle_segment_intersect` (339) compare `distance <= radius` with the raw value, so nothing ever intersects; `circles_intersect` (300-304) compares against `a.radius + b.radius`, so a negative radius shrinks the other circle's reach; and `get_bounding_box()` (3318-3324) returns width/height of -10, which `test_AABB_AABB` (EricsonMath.cpp:283-296) turns into min > max, inverting the broad phase. One object, four mutually inconsistent answers.

**Fix:** Clamp (`radius = std::max(0.0f, radius + amount)`) or throw as RectangleRotated does -- and pick one policy across the hierarchy. Independently, make every circle test use `radius * radius` so the sign cannot leak into the result.

#### 44. Bounding boxes are recomputed from scratch on every call and never cached, plus two dead-store AABB locals in the bracket search

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:3427-3441, 3778-3792, 4217-4231` — **medium** · `performance`

`Triangle::get_bounding_box` (3427-3441) runs four nested min/max chains over three points; `Quad::get_bounding_box` (3778-3792) and `RectangleRotated::get_bounding_box` (4217-4231) do four chains over four points. None caches. `Shape::AABB_intersects` (143-146) calls `get_bounding_box()` on both operands every invocation, and every concrete `is_colliding` does AABB-then-narrow, so in `Level::update_level_logic`'s pairwise loop each object's AABB is rebuilt O(n) times per frame. I also confirmed both dead stores the candidate reported: `CollisionTools.cpp:35` and `CollisionTools.cpp:58` each do `RectangleF collider_aabb = collider->get_bounding_box();` and never use the variable -- a wasted virtual call plus min/max chain per bracket iteration, and a /W4 C4189 nobody sees because `TreatWarningAsError` is not set in either vcxproj. For `RectangleRotated` the AABB is a pure function of `_points`, which is already recomputed and cached on every mutation, so caching it there is free.

**Fix:** Cache the AABB alongside `_points` in `RectangleRotated` and invalidate it in the same setters. For Triangle/Quad, cache with a dirty flag, or have `Level` build a per-frame AABB array once and do broad phase against that. Delete the two unused `collider_aabb` locals.

#### 45. calculate_gradient divides by delta-x with no zero check, returning +/-inf for vertical edges

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:3594-3603` — **medium** · `correctness`

The index is validated (`if (edge < 0 || edge > 2) throw`) but the divisor is not: `(points[(edge+1)%3].y - points[edge].y) / (points[(edge+1)%3].x - points[edge].x)`. A vertical edge yields +/-inf; a zero-length edge yields NaN. No guard, no documented sentinel. Reachable from `get_hypotenuse_gradient()` (3643-3652), which is the value the ramp movement code is meant to consume -- a level author drawing a ramp with a vertical hypotenuse gets an infinite slope rather than an error. `/fp:fast` permits the compiler to assume this never happens.

**Fix:** Return the gradient through an out-param plus a bool, or return the edge direction vector and let callers handle the vertical case. Either way, do not hand an infinity to gameplay code.

#### 46. Every Quad constructor runs an O(n^2) self-intersection check and throws, including for input that is unconditionally valid, while accepting the genuinely broken cases

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:3700-3776` — **medium** · `robustness`

Merges 2 candidates. All five ctors end with `if (!this->is_valid()) throw std::invalid_argument("Quad is not valid");` (3710, 3728, 3741, 3756, 3772), and `is_valid()` (3832-3849) allocates a `vector<Segment>` and runs six segment-segment tests. `Quad(const RectangleF&)` (3734-3745) pays all of that to discover a rectangle is not self-intersecting. Meanwhile the documented invariant -- "ordered in a clockwise direction, starting from the top left" (MattMath.h:916-919) -- is never checked, nor is convexity, nor degeneracy: four identical points pass only because of the `a == b` short-circuit, and three collinear points pass because `test_2D_segment_segment` uses strict `< 0.0f` sign tests (EricsonMath.cpp:705, 712) and reports collinear as non-intersecting. So the class throws on the cheap-to-avoid case and accepts the genuinely broken ones -- and because `Quad`s are constructed inside const query paths (`get_quad()` -> `contains()`), the throw escapes into the per-frame collision loop where nothing catches `std::invalid_argument`. The exception message contains none of the offending coordinates.

**Fix:** Make constructors trivial and total. Expose `is_simple()`/`is_convex()` as opt-in queries or a `static bool try_make(points, Quad& out)` factory, and give `RectangleF`->`Quad` a direct path that skips validation. Include the four coordinates in any message that does survive.

#### 47. get_quad() recomputes cached corners and pays full Quad validation; Quad(RectangleRotated) then validates a second time, and 4 of the 6 validation tests are provably dead

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:4450-4455, 3832-3849` — **medium** · `performance`

`get_quad()` (4450-4455) calls `calculate_points()` although `_points` already holds exactly those corners, then constructs a `Quad` which runs `is_valid()` -- another allocation plus 6 segment-segment tests. `Quad::Quad(const RectangleRotated&)` (3747-3760) calls `get_quad()` (paying all of that), copies the four points out, and calls `is_valid()` AGAIN. I verified the dead-test claim: `is_valid()` loops i<j over four edges, so it tests pairs (0,1),(0,2),(0,3),(1,2),(1,3),(2,3). The four adjacent pairs share a vertex, and `EricsonMath::test_2D_segment_segment` (EricsonMath.cpp:697-725) requires `a1 * a2 < 0.0f` strictly -- for a shared endpoint one signed area is exactly 0, so the product is 0 and the test can never fire. Only the two diagonal pairs (0,2) and (1,3) can ever detect self-intersection; two-thirds of the work is provably useless.

**Fix:** Build the quad from the cached `_points`, give `Quad` a private non-validating constructor for input already known to be a rectangle, and reduce `is_valid()` to the two diagonal pairs.

#### 48. Quad fan-triangulates on the fixed 0-2 diagonal and is_valid() never rejects concave quads, so every quad query is wrong for concave input

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:3955-3973, 3832-3849` — **medium** · `correctness`

Merges 2 candidates. `get_triangle_0()` = (p0,p1,p2) and `get_triangle_1()` = (p0,p2,p3) always split on the p0-p2 diagonal. For a simple but concave quadrilateral whose reflex vertex is p1 or p3, that diagonal lies outside the shape and the two triangles cover area the quad does not occupy. `is_valid()` (3832-3849) only rejects self-intersection -- it says nothing about convexity -- so such quads construct successfully. Since `quad_point_intersect` (530-543), `quad_segment_intersect` (513-528), `quads_intersect` (492-511), `circle_quad_intersect` (319-331), `rectangle_quad_intersect` (231-245) and `quad_rectangle_rotated_intersect` (545-561) are all defined purely in terms of `get_triangles()`, every one reports false positives inside the concave notch. The header comment (MattMath.h:916-919) promises only clockwise-from-top-left ordering, never convexity -- an unchecked precondition.

**Fix:** Decide what `Quad` is. If it is the collider type (which is what every algorithm assumes), rename it `ConvexQuad`, enforce convexity in `is_valid()` via consistent cross-product sign across the four vertices, and replace the triangulation-based routines with SAT over the four edge normals -- faster and correct.

#### 49. Every RectangleRotated and Quad mutator writes the member first and validates second, so a throw leaves the object corrupt

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:4295-4413, 3883-3921` — **medium** · `robustness`

Merges 4 candidates. Pattern verified at all six RectangleRotated sites -- `inflate` (4295-4305), `set_x_axis` (4359-4369), `set_y_axis` (4370-4380), `set_half_extents` (4381-4391), `set_half_x_width` (4392-4402), `set_half_y_width` (4403-4413) -- and all four `Quad::set_point_N` (3883-3921). After the throw the primary field holds the rejected value while `_points` still describes the previous geometry, so `get_half_extents()` and `get_point_0()`/`get_bounding_box()`/`get_edges()` describe different rectangles. `set_x_axis`/`set_y_axis` are worse: `x_axis.normalized()` (1724-1728) has no zero guard, so `set_x_axis(Vector2F::ZERO)` writes NaN into `_x_axis` and then throws, leaving NaN axes forever. `Shape::inflate` is virtual and called through `Shape*`, so a caller that catches the exception has no way to know its shape is now garbage.

**Fix:** Compute the candidate value into a local, validate the local, throw before committing anything, then assign and recompute `_points`. That restores the strong exception guarantee for all ten setters. Guard `normalized()` against zero length.

#### 50. is_valid() runs before _points is populated, so edges_valid() is vacuously true for every input

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:4194-4199, 4209-4214, 4539-4565` — **medium** · `correctness`

Merges 3 duplicate candidates. Both ctors do `if (!is_valid()) throw; this->_points = this->calculate_points();` -- validation first, cache second. `is_valid()` (4464-4480) calls `edges_valid()` (4539-4565), which builds its edges from `get_edges()` (4284-4294) -> `get_edge_0..3()` (4434-4449) -> `_points`. At that moment `_points` is still the NSDMI `{ZERO, ZERO, ZERO, ZERO}` (MattMath.h:1119-1120). All four edges are `Segment(ZERO, ZERO)`: every `get_direction()` is (0,0) so every perpendicularity dot is exactly 0 and passes; every `get_length()` is 0 so both opposite-length checks pass. `edges_valid()` therefore returns true unconditionally during construction and has never rejected anything. The `if (edges.size() != 4) throw` at 4542-4545 is likewise unreachable -- `get_edges()` always builds exactly four. Severity downgraded from the reported "high": the consequence is a dead validator, not a wrong result, and no first-party code calls `is_valid()` (grep found zero callers outside MattMath.cpp).

**Fix:** Validate the primary state (`_center`, `_x_axis`, `_y_axis`, `_hw_extents`) directly and delete `edges_valid()` entirely -- for an OBB, orthonormal axes plus positive extents already imply perpendicular, pairwise-equal edges, so re-deriving the corners to check them is circular. Delete the unreachable size check.

#### 51. REJECTED AS WRITTEN, but a real adjacent bug: the Segment-based RectangleRotated constructor never normalises its axes

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:4201-4215` — **medium** · `correctness`

Several candidates cited 'MattMath.cpp:4191-4192' as the site where `RectangleRotated(const Segment& center_line, float thickness)` normalises the axes of a possibly-zero-length centre line. That is the wrong constructor: 4191-4192 belongs to the four-argument constructor at 4186. I am recording the rejection here rather than dropping it, because reading the real constructor turned up a worse defect the reviewers missed:
```cpp
RectangleRotated::RectangleRotated(const Segment& center_line, float thickness)
{
    this->_center = center_line.get_center();
    this->_x_axis = center_line.get_direction();   // NOT normalised
    this->_y_axis = Vector2F::normal(this->_x_axis);
    ...
    if (!this->is_valid()) { throw std::invalid_argument("RectangleRotated is not valid"); }
```
`get_direction()` (4063-4066) returns `point_1 - point_0`, unnormalised. `axes_valid()` (4522-4538) requires `are_equal(_x_axis.length(), 1.0f, EPSILON)`. So this constructor throws for every centre line whose length is not within 1e-4 of 1.0 — i.e. essentially always. The sibling constructor at 4186-4200 calls normalize() on both axes; this one does not.

**Fix:** Normalise both axes in the Segment constructor exactly as the four-argument one does, and add a MattMathTests case constructing an OBB from a centre line of realistic length — the existing RectangleRotated tests evidently do not cover this path.

#### 52. RectangleRotated(Segment, thickness) forgets to normalize its axes and throws for every segment of length != 1 - dead code, but the rejection of this finding was wrong

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:4201-4215` — **medium** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

Settling the disagreement: the constructor DOES throw for essentially every real input, and the agent who marked this 'REJECTED AS WRITTEN' was wrong. But 'always throws' is imprecise — here is the exact condition.

```
RectangleRotated::RectangleRotated(const Segment& center_line, float thickness)
{
    this->_center = center_line.get_center();
    this->_x_axis = center_line.get_direction();
    this->_y_axis = Vector2F::normal(this->_x_axis);
    this->_hw_extents = Vector2F(center_line.get_length() / 2.0f + thickness, thickness);
    if (!this->is_valid()) throw std::invalid_argument("RectangleRotated is not valid");
    this->_points = this->calculate_points();
}
```
`Segment::get_direction()` (MattMath.cpp:4063-4066) returns `point_1 - point_0`, **unnormalized**. `Vector2F::normal` (MattMath.cpp:1865-1868) returns `(-y, x)`, preserving that length. `is_valid()` (4464-4480) calls `axes_valid()` (4522-4538), which requires `are_equal(_x_axis.length(), 1.0f, EPSILON)` with `EPSILON = 0.0001f` (MattMath.h:46).

Exact throw condition: throws unless the segment's length is within 1e-4 of **1.0**, or `thickness <= 0` (half_widths_valid, 4512-4521). At this game's scale (segments are tens to thousands of pixels) that means every realistic input throws. The perpendicularity check passes trivially — `dot((x,y), (-y,x)) == 0` exactly.

The sibling 4-arg constructor at 4186-4192 gets this right: it explicitly calls `_x_axis.normalize(); _y_axis.normalize();` before validating. The Segment overload just omits those two lines.

REACHABILITY: DEAD. Repo-wide grep for `RectangleRotated(` finds zero first-party construction sites. `DrawObject::set_draw_rotation_by_rectangle_rotated` (DrawObject.cpp:66) and `Visual`'s overload (Visual.cpp:22-35) take one by const ref but nothing calls them with one. Even MattMathTests only ever uses the 4-arg form (MathTests.cpp:359, 376, 493, 631, 738, 785, 801, 833, 837, 842, 848, 854, 860, 866 — all `RectangleRotated(Vector2F::ZERO, ...)`). The Segment overload has no caller anywhere, test or game. Same for its private helper `calculate_points(const Segment&, float)` at 4501-4510.

**Fix:** Add `this->_x_axis.normalize(); this->_y_axis.normalize();` (or build from `center_line.get_direction().normalized()`), and add a test for the Segment overload — it currently has zero coverage, which is why nobody noticed. Also `_hw_extents.x = length/2 + thickness` looks wrong independently: it extends the box past the segment ends by `thickness` on the long axis, which is a capsule approximation, not a rectangle around the segment. Decide which is intended and document it.

#### 53. RectangleRotated mutators modify state, then validate, then throw — leaving the cached points inconsistent with the extents

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:4295-4413` — **medium** · `robustness`

Verified at six sites. inflate (4295-4305):
```cpp
this->_hw_extents += Vector2F(amount, amount);   // committed
if (!this->half_widths_valid()) { throw std::invalid_argument(...); }
this->_points = this->calculate_points();
```
On the throw path _hw_extents already holds the invalid value while _points still describes the previous extents — the object's cached corners no longer correspond to its stored state. Any later get_bounding_box() (4217-4232), contains() or intersects() silently reports geometry from the stale cache. No exception guarantee at all, not even basic. Same shape at set_x_axis (4359-4369), set_y_axis (4370-4380), set_half_extents (4381-4391), set_half_x_width (4392-4402), set_half_y_width (4403-4413).

This matters because Shape::inflate is invoked polymorphically from the collision path and nothing in CollisionTools catches std::invalid_argument — the object survives the unwind corrupted and keeps colliding.

**Fix:** Validate first, commit second: compute the candidate into a local, check it, then assign and recompute _points. That gives the strong guarantee for free. Make half_widths_valid/axes_valid take the value to check rather than reading members.

#### 54. get_rectangle_rotated_to_axis() is a renderer workaround welded onto a geometry primitive, and it silently discards the rotation

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:4456-4459` — **medium** · `design`

`RectangleF RectangleRotated::get_rectangle_rotated_to_axis() const { return RectangleF(this->_center, this->_hw_extents.x, this->_hw_extents.y); }` -- the OBB with its rotation thrown away. Its only caller is `Visual::Visual(..., const RectangleRotated&, ...)` (Visual.cpp:34), which needs an axis-aligned destination rect for `SpriteBatch`; the rotation was supposed to be recovered by `DrawObject::set_draw_rotation_by_rectangle_rotated`, which is an empty `// TODO: Implement this function` (DrawObject.cpp:66-69). So a sprite-batching detail lives in the math layer and currently drops rotation on the floor.

**Fix:** Delete the method from the shape. The renderer's job is to take a `RectangleRotated` and produce (destination rect, rotation, origin); put that adapter in the drawing layer, and implement it using `atan2(_x_axis.y, _x_axis.x)` rather than the unsigned `get_angle()`.

#### 55. RectangleRotated::get_angle() is acos-based and therefore unsigned, so +theta and -theta are indistinguishable

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:4460-4463` — **medium** · `correctness`

Merges 3 candidates. `return Vector2F::angle_between(this->_x_axis, Vector2F::DIRECTION_RIGHT);` -- `angle_between` (1808-1811) returns [0, pi], so an OBB rotated -30 degrees and one rotated +30 degrees both report 0.5236, and no orientation in the lower half plane is representable. The intended consumer is `DrawObject::set_draw_rotation_by_rectangle_rotated` (DrawObject.cpp:66-69), currently an empty `// TODO: Implement this function` stub, which would mirror half of all rotations. The class already stores the full basis and `Vector2F::angle()` (1749-1752) is already `std::atan2(y, x)`, so the signed angle is free. There is also no matching `set_angle`/`rotate` -- see the set_x_axis finding.

**Fix:** `return std::atan2(this->_x_axis.y, this->_x_axis.x);` -- signed, exact, cheaper, no epsilon. Document the sign convention for y-down screen space.

#### 56. RectangleRotated's corners come out counter-clockwise from bottom-left, contradicting the Quad contract they are fed into

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:4487-4499` — **medium** · `correctness`

With the class defaults `_x_axis = DIRECTION_RIGHT (1,0)` and `_y_axis = DIRECTION_UP (0,-1)` (MattMath.h:1115-1116) in y-down screen space, I evaluated `calculate_points` for center (0,0), extents (1,1): p0 = (-1, 1) bottom-left, p1 = (1, 1) bottom-right, p2 = (1, -1) top-right, p3 = (-1, -1) top-left -- counter-clockwise on screen, starting at the bottom-left. `Quad`'s header contract (MattMath.h:916-919) says "ordered in a clockwise direction, starting from the top left", and `Quad(const RectangleF&)` (3734-3739) does produce TL, TR, BR, BL. `get_quad()` (4450-4455) feeds the RectangleRotated corners straight into `Quad`, so `get_point_0()` is the bottom-left and the winding is opposite to every other quad in the system. The Segment constructor produces yet a third convention (its `normal()` y-axis points DOWN for a rightward segment). Nothing breaks today because triangulation and barycentric containment are winding-agnostic, but anything that assumes point 0 is the top-left -- sprite drawing, the positional edge mapping in StructurePaintable.cpp:189-212 -- will be wrong.

**Fix:** Pick one convention (clockwise from top-left in screen space), state it on `Shape`, and make `calculate_points`, `Quad(RectangleF)` and the Segment ctor all honour it. Add a test asserting `get_points()[0]` is the top-left for an axis-aligned RectangleRotated.

#### 57. edges_valid() validates stale _points, so it is a tautology in both constructors

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:4539-4565` — **medium** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

```
bool RectangleRotated::edges_valid() const
{
    std::vector<Segment> edges = this->get_edges();   // built from this->_points
    ...
}
```
`get_edges()` (4284-4294) reads `_points` via `get_edge_0..3` (4434-4449), which index `this->_points`. But both constructors call `is_valid()` **before** assigning `_points`:
- 4194-4199: check, then `_points = calculate_points()`
- 4209-4214: check, then `_points = calculate_points()`

At the moment `edges_valid()` runs, `_points` still holds its NSDMI value `{ZERO, ZERO, ZERO, ZERO}` (MattMath.h:1119-1120). All four edges are degenerate `(0,0)->(0,0)` segments: every `get_direction()` is `(0,0)`, every dot product is 0 (passes the perpendicularity test at 4550-4551), every length is 0 (passes the opposite-lengths test at 4558-4559). So `edges_valid()` unconditionally returns true from the constructor path and validates nothing.

In the mutators (`inflate` 4295-4305, `set_x_axis` 4359-4369, `set_y_axis`, `set_half_extents`, `set_half_x_width`, `set_half_y_width`) the same ordering means the validity check runs against the *previous* geometry, not the new one.

This is a separate defect from the missing normalize, and it is why the Segment constructor's other invariants were never caught: only `half_widths_valid` and `axes_valid` (which read the just-assigned members directly) actually do anything.

REACHABILITY: dead today (nothing constructs a RectangleRotated), but MattMathTests exercises the 4-arg ctor heavily and has been getting false confidence from these checks.

**Fix:** Compute the points first, then validate: `_points = calculate_points(); if (!is_valid()) throw ...;` — and do the same in every mutator. Better still, make `_points` a derived value computed on demand (or cached lazily) rather than a member that must be kept in sync by six separate setters, each of which currently repeats the same `if (!valid) throw; _points = calculate_points();` boilerplate.

#### 58. edges_valid() dots un-normalised edge vectors against an absolute epsilon, so validity depends on rectangle size

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:4548-4562` — **medium** · `correctness`

`Vector2F::dot(edges[i].get_direction(), edges[(i+1)%4].get_direction())` uses `Segment::get_direction()` (4063-4066), which is un-normalised, so the residual for two exactly-perpendicular edges scales with the product of the edge lengths while the tolerance is a fixed `EPSILON = 0.0001f` (MattMath.h:46). Same for `are_equal(edges[0].get_length(), edges[2].get_length(), EPSILON)` -- float carries ~7 significant digits, so two ~2000-unit lengths cannot be compared to 1e-4 (one ULP at 2048 is ~1.2e-4). `<FloatingPointModel>Fast</FloatingPointModel>` is set in all four ArtAttack configurations (ArtAttack.vcxproj:94, 116, 139, 165), which permits reassociation and enlarges the residual. This is latent today only because of the ordering bug above; fix that and large OBBs start throwing from a valid constructor.

**Fix:** Normalise the directions before dotting, or use a relative test: `std::abs(dot) <= EPSILON * len_a * len_b` and `std::abs(l0 - l2) <= EPSILON * std::max(l0, l2)`. Compare squared lengths to drop four sqrt calls. Better: delete the function per the previous finding.

#### 59. MattMath::sign truncates a float cross product to int, so it returns 0 ("collinear") for any triangle of area < 1

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:86-91` — **low** · `correctness`

`return static_cast<int>((p1.x - p3.x) * (p2.y - p3.y) - (p2.x - p3.x) * (p1.y - p3.y));` -- the name and the `int` return say -1/0/+1, but it actually returns the truncated signed area. For any three points whose signed area is in (-1, 1) it returns 0 regardless of which side the point is on, and truncation toward zero also destroys any magnitude ordering. It is declared in the public header next to the other geometry helpers (MattMath.h:56-57) and is a near-duplicate of `EricsonMath::signed_2D_tri_area` (EricsonMath.cpp:688-692) except for the cast. Severity kept low: grep confirms zero callers anywhere in the tree, so this is currently only a trap for whoever next writes a point-in-polygon test.

**Fix:** Delete it and use `EricsonMath::signed_2D_tri_area`. If a true sign is wanted: `float a = signed_2D_tri_area(...); return (a > EPSILON) - (a < -EPSILON);`

#### 60. circle_segment_intersect silently returns false for a zero-length segment because the projection yields NaN

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:333-346` — **low** · `correctness`

`closest_pt_point_segment` (EricsonMath.cpp:756-767) computes `t = dot(c - a, ab) / dot(ab, ab)`. For a degenerate segment the divisor is 0, `t` becomes NaN, both clamps (`if (t < 0)`, `if (t > 1)`) are false for NaN so it stays NaN, and `d = a + NaN * ab` is NaN. `Vector2F::distance(...) <= circle.radius` is then false: a circle sitting exactly on a degenerate segment is reported as not intersecting. Degenerate segments are reachable -- a default-constructed RectangleRotated produces four, and `RectangleF::get_edges()` on a zero-height rect produces two. The no-out-param overload (342-346) also declares an uninitialised `Point2F point` purely to discard it, so nothing signals that the query was meaningless.

**Fix:** Guard in `closest_pt_point_segment`: if `dot(ab, ab) < EPSILON` set `t = 0` and `d = a`. Circle-vs-point then falls out correctly.

#### 61. Float-to-int rectangle conversions truncate toward zero with no rounding, NaN check or range check

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:823-846` — **low** · `robustness`

Verified. get_rectangle_i (823-829), get_sm_rectangle (830-836) and get_win_rect (837-846) all use bare static_cast on x, y, width, height. static_cast truncates toward zero, not toward negative infinity, so the mapping is discontinuous at 0: both -0.5f and 0.5f become 0. For rectangles at negative coordinates — and the levels do use them, close_quarters.json out_of_bounds starts at (-100, -100) — this is a systematic off-by-one on the left and top edges. The same pattern repeats in RectangleI's float constructors (1967-1981) and Vector2I's (1375-1384).

The NaN part of the reviewers' claim is technically correct (converting NaN or an out-of-int-range float to an integer type is UB) but I am grading it low rather than higher because the NaN sources in this module are all in unreachable code paths (see the normalize and angle_between findings).

**Fix:** Introduce one `int to_pixel(float)` helper using std::lround with a debug assert on std::isfinite and a clamp to int range, and route all of these through it. Pick and document a single convention (floor for positions, ceil for sizes is usual for rectangles) instead of letting truncation choose implicitly.

#### 62. Four names for unitisation and a `normal()` one character from `normalize()` that means something entirely different

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:1724-1787, 1852-1868` — **low** · `design`

Verified. Unitisation exists four times: normalized() (1724-1728), normalize() (1729-1734), to_unit_vector() (1774-1787), static unit_vector() (1852-1863) — with two incompatible zero-length contracts (see the separate robustness finding). Independently, `void Vector2F::normal()` (1768-1773) rotates the vector 90 degrees in place:
```cpp
float temp = x; x = -y; y = temp;
```
It is one character from normalize() and means a completely different thing. There is also a static `normal(vec)` (1865-1868).

Usage confirms the API is untended: to_unit_vector 0 callers, normalize 0 outside MattMath, normalized 2 (both in MovingObject, itself uncalled), unit_vector 3 in ArtAttack plus the tests. The same member/static/by-value/by-ref duplication runs through the whole type: angle() + static angle(vec); dot(other) + static dot(a,b); clamp() + clamped(); rotate() + rotate_vector() + rotate_vector_by_ref(); and RectangleF::intersection has both a member and a static form, Camera::calculate_view_rectangle has four.

**Fix:** Keep exactly two unitisation functions with one documented contract; rename normal()/normal(vec) to perpendicular(). Pick one form per operation (value-returning free functions for pure maths) and implement any second form by calling the first, so the maths exists once.

#### 63. direction_to_8_cardinal_direction maps the zero vector to DIRECTION_RIGHT with no way for the caller to tell

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:1870-1873` — **low** · `correctness`

Verified. `angle()` is `std::atan2(y, x)` (1749-1752) and atan2(0,0) is 0, so a zero-length input falls into the first branch (`angle >= -PI/8 && angle < PI/8`) and is reported as pointing right. I checked all eight sector boundaries against the y-down convention (DIRECTION_UP = {0,-1}) and they are correct and exhaustive; the degenerate input is the only hole.

Live path: Player::on_structure_ramp_collision (Player.cpp:247-250) feeds it the output of CollisionTools::calculate_object_collision_direction, a centre-to-centre vector that is zero when two shapes are exactly concentric. That resolves as a rightward collision.

Secondary, verified: the eight-way sibling `Vector2F::get_direction()` (1662-1714) uses are_equal(x, 0.0f) with the default absolute epsilon and returns MattMath::direction::NONE for the degenerate case. Two functions answering 'which of eight directions is this', one returning Vector2F and one returning the enum, with different degenerate behaviour.

**Fix:** Return direction::NONE (or the enum generally, which would also fix the exact-float comparisons in Player.cpp) and take an explicit minimum-magnitude threshold so a degenerate input must be handled. Then delete one of the two eight-way classifiers.

#### 64. RectangleI's Rectangle and RECT constructors narrow long to int implicitly, unlike every sibling

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:1989-2002` — **low** · `correctness`

Verified:
```cpp
RectangleI::RectangleI(const SimpleMath::Rectangle& rectangle)
{ this->x = rectangle.x; ... }          // long -> int, no cast
RectangleI::RectangleI(const RECT& rectangle)
{ this->x = rectangle.left; ... this->width = rectangle.right - rectangle.left; }
```
SimpleMath::Rectangle stores long and RECT stores LONG; both assigned to int members with no cast. Every other narrowing in these files is explicit: RectangleI(const Vector2F&, const Vector2F&) at 1967-1973, RectangleI(RectangleF) at 1982-1988, RectangleF::get_rectangle_i() at 823-829, RectangleI::get_sm_rectangle() at 2036-2042 all use static_cast. These eight assignments are the odd ones out and produce C4244 at /W4 with nothing failing the build.

No data is currently lost — long and int are both 32-bit on Windows — so this is about consistency and about not training yourself to ignore C4244.

**Fix:** Add static_cast<int> to all eight assignments, and turn on TreatWarningAsError for the engine project so the next one gets caught.

#### 65. Matrix3x3F's element-count check is unreachable — the base constructor already threw

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:2987-2994` — **low** · `correctness`

Verified. `Matrix3x3F::Matrix3x3F(const std::vector<float>& elements) : MatrixF(3, 3, elements)` then checks `if (elements.size() != 9) throw`. The mem-initialiser runs first, and MatrixF(int, int, const std::vector<float>&) (2483-2493) already does `if (rows * columns != elements.size()) throw std::invalid_argument("Number of elements does not match the dimensions of the matrix")`. With rows=columns=3 that is the identical condition, so the derived check can never fire and the caller always sees the less specific base message.

Verified in the same lines: that base check compares `int` (rows * columns) against `size_t` (elements.size()) — a signed/unsigned mismatch at /W4 (C4018/C4389), and TreatWarningAsError is set nowhere in either vcxproj, so it accumulates silently.

**Fix:** Delete the dead derived check; cast both sides of the base comparison after validating rows >= 0 && columns >= 0, or take dimensions as an unsigned type so the invalid state is unrepresentable. Or delete the whole subsystem.

#### 66. Members assigned in constructor bodies instead of member initialiser lists, so they are initialised twice

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:3313-3317, 3405-3426, 3700-3776, 4100-4105, 4201-4207` — **low** · `modern-cpp`

Every member of these types has a default member initialiser, and several constructors then assign over it in the body: `Circle::Circle(float,float,float)` (3313-3317), all three `Triangle` constructors (3405-3426), all five `Quad` constructors (3700-3776), `Camera::Camera(const Viewport&, float)` (4100-4105) and `RectangleRotated::RectangleRotated(const Segment&, float)` (4201-4207). The two-argument `Circle` (3305-3312), the `Segment` constructors (4037-4044), `RectangleF(float,float,float,float)` (667-670) and the 4-arg `RectangleRotated` (4186-4189) right next door do it correctly, so the file is inconsistent with itself. For `Quad`, body-assignment is also what forces the validity check to be a post-hoc `if (!is_valid()) throw` on a half-built object rather than part of construction.

**Fix:** Use member initialiser lists throughout and have the multi-argument constructors delegate to one primary constructor rather than repeating the assignments five times.

#### 67. get_hypotenuse and get_hypotenuse_gradient each re-run find_hypotenuse -- up to 6 sqrt and 3 acos plus a heap allocation to identify one edge

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:3633-3652` — **low** · `performance`

`find_hypotenuse` (3665-3684) calls `get_angle_0/1/2` until one matches PI_OVER_2. Each `get_angle_N` (3512-3527) builds two `Segment`s, takes two directions and calls `angle_between` = 2 sqrt + 1 acos, so the worst case is 6 sqrt and 3 acos. A right triangle's hypotenuse is the longest edge -- three `length_squared` comparisons, no transcendentals. The result is not cached, so calling both accessors pays for it twice, and `get_hypotenuse()` does `this->get_edges()[hypotenuse]` (3641), allocating a three-element vector to read one element when `get_edge_0/1/2()` are right there.

**Fix:** Determine and cache the hypotenuse index once at construction (which is also where right-angled-ness should be validated), using squared lengths. Replace `get_edges()[i]` with a switch over `get_edge_0/1/2()`.

#### 68. TriangleRightAxisAligned::calculate_gradient is a byte-for-byte copy of the base version, declared private so it hides an accessible public base member

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:3685-3694` — **low** · `design`

Merges 3 candidates. `Triangle::calculate_gradient` (3594-3603) is public (MattMath.h:893) and non-virtual; `TriangleRightAxisAligned::calculate_gradient` (3685-3694) has an identical body and is private (MattMath.h:913). Because neither is virtual this is name hiding, not overriding: `TriangleRightAxisAligned t; t.calculate_gradient(0);` fails to compile because the derived private name hides the accessible base one, so the derived class publicly LOSES an operation its base offers. Two copies of the same three lines free to drift apart. In the same class, `int find_hypotenuse(const Triangle& tri) const` (MattMath.h:912) takes a parameter that is only ever `*this` (call sites 3635, 3645) -- a const member function taking itself as an argument.

**Fix:** Delete `TriangleRightAxisAligned::calculate_gradient` outright. Make `find_hypotenuse` a no-argument private const member (or a free function on `const Triangle&`) and share one guard between `get_hypotenuse` and `get_hypotenuse_gradient`.

#### 69. RectangleRotated::get_points() hands out a reference into a member vector that every mutator replaces wholesale

`ArtAttack/MattMath.cpp:4430-4433` — **low** · `design`

It is the only shape accessor in the file returning a container by reference -- `Triangle::get_points()` (3485-3489) and `Quad::get_points()` (3871-3881) both return by value. All nine mutators do `this->_points = this->calculate_points();`, which move-assigns a fresh vector and frees the old buffer, so any caller that takes a `const Point2F*` or an iterator out of the returned reference -- the natural thing to do with a returned container -- is holding a dangling pointer the moment the shape is offset, and `Shape::offset` is called once per bracket iteration per contact. Grep confirms there are currently no callers of `RectangleRotated::get_points()` anywhere in the tree, so this is a live trap rather than a live bug.

**Fix:** Return `std::array<Point2F, 4>` by value (consistent with the array recommendation and with Triangle/Quad). There is no reason to hand out a reference to 32 bytes.

## `ArtAttack/PauseMenu.cpp`

_3 findings: 1 critical, 2 high_

#### 1. PauseMenu subscripts the menu-input vector with an unvalidated player index - guaranteed OOB if any pad drops

`ArtAttack/PauseMenu.cpp:46-113` — **critical** · `memory-safety` · confidence: certain

`PauseMenuInitial::update` does:

```cpp
std::vector<ProcessedMenuInput> inputs = this->get_menu_inputs();
int player_num = this->get_pause_menu_data()->get_player_num();
...
if (inputs[player_num].action == menu_input_action::BACK ||   // PauseMenu.cpp:53
    inputs[player_num].action == menu_input_action::PAUSE)
```

There is no size check anywhere in the function - `inputs[player_num]` is subscripted at lines 53, 54, 59, 82 and 98, and again in `PauseMenuConfirmation::update` at lines 222, 229, 256 and 257.

`player_num` is not a stable pad identity: it is the *compacted index* returned by `GameLevel::check_for_pause_input` (GameStates.cpp:348-358, `return i;` where `i` indexes the already-compacted `player_inputs` vector), stored into `PauseMenuData` at GameStates.cpp:156.

This is the only unguarded menu-input subscript in the codebase - every other page loops `for (i < inputs.size())` (MainMenu.cpp:50, EndMenu.cpp:32, ResultsMenu.cpp:266) or bounds itself with `i < num_inputs && i < player_count` (MainMenu.cpp:1160, 1443, 1790).

Three concrete ways to fire it:
- Player 3 of 3 pauses (`player_num == 2`), then any one pad is unplugged: `MenuInput::update_and_get_menu_inputs` (MenuInput.cpp:139-148) returns 2 entries, `inputs[2]` is OOB.
- Every pad is unplugged (or all batteries die) while paused: `inputs` is empty and `inputs[0]` dereferences the empty vector's null data pointer.
- Alt-tab: `Game::on_deactivated` (Game.cpp:165-169) calls `GamePad::Suspend()` while the main loop (Main.cpp:213-224) keeps calling `tick()` unconditionally, so the pause menu keeps polling a suspended gamepad.

Secondary consequence even without the OOB: the pause menu is only exitable by the pad at that compacted index, so if that specific pad dies the match cannot be resumed, restarted or quit at all.

**Fix:** Guard every access: `if (player_num < 0 || static_cast<size_t>(player_num) >= inputs.size()) return;` at minimum. Properly, carry the XInput slot (not a compacted index) in `PauseMenuData`, index a fixed-size input array by that slot, and add an explicit "controller disconnected - reconnect or press START on any pad" state so the menu never becomes unresponsive.

#### 2. Pause menu indexes the input vector by player number with no bounds check

`ArtAttack/PauseMenu.cpp:48-59, 82, 98, 217-229, 256-257` — **high** · `correctness`

`PauseMenuInitial::update()` (lines 48-59) reads `int player_num = get_pause_menu_data()->get_player_num();` and then does `inputs[player_num].action == ...` at lines 53, 54, 59, 82, 98. `MenuInput::update_and_get_menu_inputs()` (MenuInput.cpp:138-149) only `push_back`s entries for pads where `current[i].connected` is true, so `inputs.size()` is the count of CONNECTED pads, not 4. `player_num` was captured on an earlier frame by `GameLevel::check_for_pause_input` (GameStates.cpp:144-146, 345-357) as an index into a differently-built compacted `PlayerInputData` vector. If a pad disconnects while the pause menu is open, `inputs.size()` shrinks; `operator[]` is unchecked, so this reads past the end. If all pads drop, `inputs` is empty and `inputs[player_num]` dereferences a null data pointer. `PauseMenuConfirmation::update()` repeats the identical pattern at lines 222, 229, 256, 257. `PauseMenuData::_player_num` also defaults to `-1` (PauseMenuData.h:19) with no validation in the setter. Note the rest of the module defends itself by bounding the loop (`i < num_inputs && i < player_count`, MainMenu.cpp:1160, 1443, 1790) — the pause menu is the one place that indexes blind.

**Fix:** Make MenuInput return a fixed 4-slot result so the index is the pad slot (see the MenuInput API finding). Until then, guard at the top of both `update()` bodies: `if (player_num < 0 || player_num >= static_cast<int>(inputs.size())) return;`.

#### 3. Pause menu indexes the compacted menu-input vector with an index taken from a different, independently compacted vector

`ArtAttack/PauseMenu.cpp:53-59` — **high** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

// PauseMenu.cpp:48-59 (same pattern at 82, 98 and in PauseMenuConfirmation at 222, 229, 256)
    std::vector<ProcessedMenuInput> inputs = this->get_menu_inputs();
    int player_num = this->get_pause_menu_data()->get_player_num();
    ...
    if (inputs[player_num].action == menu_input_action::BACK || ...)

`player_num` comes from `GameLevel::check_for_pause_input` (GameStates.cpp:348-359), which returns an index into the vector produced by `PlayerInput::update_and_get_player_inputs()`. Both input classes **compact away disconnected pads**:

    // MenuInput.cpp:139-148 (identical shape at PlayerInput.cpp:127-136)
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++)
        if (current[i].connected) result.push_back(...);

So the index is not a gamepad number, and the two vectors are sampled on different frames. If a pad disconnects between the frame the pause was detected and the next frame's `PauseMenuInitial::update`, `inputs.size()` shrinks and `inputs[player_num]` is an unchecked out-of-bounds read on a heap vector. The same index is also used as a *display* number (`get_player_number_text`, PauseMenu.cpp:135-136), so with pad 0 unplugged, physical player 2 pausing is labelled "Pause Menu P1".

The codebase already knows about this: every main-menu screen guards with `for (int i = 0; i < num_inputs && i < player_count; i++)` (MainMenu.cpp:1160, 1443, 1790). The pause menu — the only screen that indexes rather than iterates — does not. The same latent mismatch exists at `Level.cpp:192` (`object->set_player_input(player_inputs[player_index])`, indexed by position in `_player_objects`).

**Fix:** Put the gamepad slot into `ProcessedMenuInput`/`PlayerInputData` (they already carry a useless `connection` field that is unconditionally set to CONNECTED, MenuInput.cpp:127) and return a fixed 4-entry vector with a `connected` flag instead of compacting. Then look up by slot, not by position. As an immediate patch, bounds-check: `if (player_num < 0 || player_num >= static_cast<int>(inputs.size())) return;`.

## `ArtAttack/Player.cpp`

_28 findings: 1 critical, 5 high, 14 medium, 8 low_

#### 1. Player::draw mutates object state and runs concurrently on the same Player from several thread-pool threads

`ArtAttack/Player.cpp:47-90` — **critical** · `concurrency`

Merges 3 candidates (all reported this). Verified end to end. `Player::draw(SpriteBatch*, const Camera&)` is non-const and writes: `this->_animation_state = new_animation_state;` (:59), `TextureObject::set_sprite_sheet_name(info.sprite_sheet)` (:62), `TextureObject::set_element_name(...)` (:63), `set_animation_strip_and_reset(...)` (:65, which also resets `_frame_index`/`_time_elapsed`), `set_frame_time(...)`/`set_frame_time_to_default()` (:66-73), and unconditionally `TextureObject::set_effects(effects)` (:83) and `AnimationObject::set_effects(effects)` (:86).

The concurrency is real, and it is worse than the candidates described — `Level::draw_active_level` (Level.cpp:382-397) partitions the PLAYER list, not the viewport list: `_partitioner->partition(this->_player_objects->size(), num_threads)` with `NUM_THREADS_MAX = 16` (Game.h:14). `Partitioner::partition` (Partitioner.cpp:10) caps the loop at `i < num_elements`, so an N-player match produces exactly N partitions and N concurrent `ThreadPool::add_task` submissions. `ThreadPool::add_task` uses the real Win32 pool (`SubmitThreadpoolWork`, ThreadPool.cpp:47). Each task then runs `draw_player_view_level`, which loops over EVERY player (Level.cpp:534-540: `for (auto& object : *this->_player_objects) { ... object->draw(sprite_batches->at(i), camera); }`).

So in any 2+ player match, `Player::draw` for the same instance executes on N threads simultaneously. `SpriteSheetObject::_sheet_name` and `_element_name` are `std::string` (SpriteSheetObject.h:25-26); concurrent unsynchronised assignment to a `std::string` is a torn write on the heap pointer / SSO buffer, i.e. potential heap corruption, not merely a stale frame.

Separately, even single-threaded this is a design defect: clip selection belongs in `update()` (called once per frame), not `draw()` (called once per viewport). A player who is off-screen in every viewport never changes animation clip at all, because `Level` guards the call with `is_visible_in_viewport`.

**Fix:** Move the whole `calculate_animation_state()` / strip-swap / effects block into `Player::update()`, and make both `draw` overrides `const` so the compiler enforces purity. Long term `IGameObject::draw` should be const across the engine — a parallel command-list recorder is only safe if the record path is read-only.

#### 2. Player caches a raw SoundBank* that Game::OnDeviceLost destroys underneath it

`ArtAttack/Player.cpp:44` — **high** · `memory-safety`

The constructor ends with `this->_sound_bank = resource_manager->get_sound_bank(SOUND_BANK);` (:44) into the raw non-owning `SoundBank* _sound_bank = nullptr;` (Player.h:168). The owner is `ResourceManager::_sound_banks`, a map of `unique_ptr<SoundBank>`.

`Game::OnDeviceLost()` (Game.cpp:269-280) calls `_resource_manager->reset_all_sounds()`, which is:
```
for (auto& sound_bank : this->_sound_banks) {
    sound_bank.second->reset_all_instances();
    sound_bank.second.reset();          // ResourceManager.cpp:124 — destroys the SoundBank
}
```
OnDeviceLost does not tear down the state machine (only `_sprite_batches`, `_states`, textures, fonts, sounds), so every live `Player` keeps a dangling `SoundBank*`. The next `_sound_bank->play_wave(...)` — Player.cpp:687 (damage), 707 (death), 880 (jump), 1002 (respawn) — is a use-after-free. `OnDeviceRestored` re-runs `load_all_resources()` and inserts NEW SoundBank objects, so nothing re-fetches the pointer and the dangle is permanent, not transient.

Graded high rather than critical only because it requires a device-lost event; the consequence when it happens is memory corruption.

**Fix:** Stop caching. Either look the bank up through the `ResourceManager*` at each call site, or have `reset_all_sounds` reset only the instances (not the owning `unique_ptr`) so device-lost recovery re-initialises in place instead of destroying objects other code points at.

#### 3. draw() is a mutating operation on shared objects, and the same object is drawn concurrently by every viewport thread

`ArtAttack/Player.cpp:47-90` — **high** · `concurrency`

`IGameObject::draw` is non-const (IGameObject.h:11-12) and the render path exploits it.

I verified the dispatch. `Level::draw_active_level` partitions the player list and adds one thread-pool task per partition, each running `draw_player_view_level`. But `draw_player_view_level` then loops over **all** `_player_objects`, `_collision_objects` and `_non_collision_objects` for its viewport, calling `object->draw(...)`. So in 2-4 player split-screen the same `Player` instance has `draw()` entered concurrently by up to 4 threads.

`Player::draw` (Player.cpp:47-90) writes during draw:
```cpp
this->_animation_state = new_animation_state;
TextureObject::set_sprite_sheet_name(info.sprite_sheet);   // std::string assignment
TextureObject::set_element_name(info.uniform_texture);     // std::string assignment
set_animation_strip_and_reset(info.sprite_sheet, info.animation); // 2 more strings + _frame_index + _time_elapsed
set_frame_time(info.frame_time);
TextureObject::set_effects(effects);
AnimationObject::set_effects(effects);
```
while other threads read those same members in `SpriteSheetObject::get_sprite_sheet()` and `AnimationObject::get_source_rectangle()`. Concurrent write/read of a `std::string` that outgrows SSO is a use-after-free of the string buffer, not merely a stale frame. A torn `_frame_index` read makes `AnimationStrip::get_frame_rect` throw (AnimationStrip.cpp:30-33) from inside `ThreadPool::work_callback`, which invokes `(*task)()` with no try/catch (ThreadPool.cpp:60-65) — that terminates the process and leaks the task.

Same shape at `TextDropShadow::draw` (separate finding), `PaintTile::draw` (PaintTile.cpp:34-70, `set_colour` + `_splash.set_rectangle_center` on shared tile state) and `Weapon::draw` (Weapon.cpp:36-66, `set_element_name`/`set_origin`/`set_effects`/`set_draw_rotation`).

This is the single biggest structural obstacle to the engine goal: the renderer is parallel but nothing below `IGameObject` is const or read-only.

**Fix:** Make `IGameObject::draw` and everything it reaches `const`, and move every state transition into `update()` — starting with hoisting the animation-state block out of `Player::draw`. Per-viewport values that genuinely vary (effects, view rect) belong in a draw-parameter struct passed by value. Separately, wrap `ThreadPool::work_callback`'s invocation in try/catch so a task exception cannot terminate the process.

#### 4. The same 32-line is_colliding narrow-phase boilerplate is copy-pasted into 7 classes

`ArtAttack/Player.cpp:148-184` — **high** · `design` · confidence: certain

Identical body — type filter, `AABB_intersects`, "if the other object is a rectangle return true", `Shape::intersects` — appears verbatim at:

- Player.cpp:148-184
- PaintTile.cpp:84-109 (same minus the type filter)
- ProjectileSpray.cpp:56-87
- ProjectileJet.cpp:54-85
- ProjectileBall.cpp:55-86
- ProjectileMist.cpp:56-87
- ProjectileRolling.cpp:48-79

~220 duplicated lines, right down to the comments (`// aabb check`, `// if the other object is a rectangle, then we have a collision`). Note the shared shortcut is also shared-wrong: `if (other_shape_type == shape_type::RECTANGLE) return true;` is only valid when `*this* is also a rectangle — when `this` is a triangle or circle an AABB overlap with a rectangle is reported as a real collision. Because it is copied seven times, fixing that bug means seven edits.

**Fix:** Put the entire algorithm in one free function `bool narrow_phase_collides(const Shape* a, const Shape* b)` (or a non-virtual `ICollisionGameObject::is_colliding` that calls a virtual `should_test_against(other)` type filter). Each class then supplies only its type predicate. Removing the copies also lets the `shape_type::RECTANGLE` shortcut bug be fixed in one place.

#### 5. STRUCTURE_RAMP_LEFT collision branch is an empty // TODO — left ramps are silently non-solid

`ArtAttack/Player.cpp:274-277` — **high** · `correctness`

Merges 2 candidates. `on_structure_ramp_collision` dispatches on ramp type and the left-ramp arm is literally empty:
