```
if (other_type == collision_object_type::STRUCTURE_RAMP_LEFT)
{
    // TODO
}
else if (other_type == collision_object_type::STRUCTURE_RAMP_RIGHT) { ...four near-identical cases... }
```
Anything not caught by `bottom_edge_collision` (UP/UP_LEFT/UP_RIGHT) or `side_wall_collision` (RIGHT && RAMP_LEFT) at :254-269 falls into the empty branch: no `resolve_object_collision`, no `set_move_state`, no velocity zeroing. The player passes through. Worse, `Level::update_level_logic` counts it as a structure contact anyway (Level.cpp:238-241 checks only `is_structure(...)`), so `on_no_collision()` is suppressed and the move state freezes.

Latent today — the only shipped ramp is `STRUCTURE_RAMP_RIGHT` in king_of_the_hill.json — but `LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:152-155` happily accepts the string `"STRUCTURE_RAMP_LEFT"` from JSON, so the first left ramp anyone authors becomes an invisible hole with no assert, log or throw. The half-built `StructureRampLeft.h/.cpp` are entirely commented out yet still listed in the vcxproj, so there is no compile-time signal either.

The RAMP_RIGHT arm is also four copy-pasted identical three-statement bodies (:280-345) differing only in the direction being matched.

**Fix:** Either implement the mirrored case (collapse the RIGHT arm to one `if (direction is any of DOWN/RIGHT/DOWN_LEFT/DOWN_RIGHT)` and parameterise on ramp side), or make `LevelObjectBuilder` reject `STRUCTURE_RAMP_LEFT` so a broken level fails loudly at load rather than silently at play.

#### 6. Dead players keep firing: the weapon is never gated on player_state

`ArtAttack/Player.cpp:696-750` — **high** · `correctness`

`Player::update()` branches on `_state` and only runs movement/animation while ALIVE (:698-711), but the weapon lives entirely outside that branch. `Level::update_level_logic` calls it unconditionally for every player (Level.cpp:204-210), and `Player::update_weapon_and_get_projectiles() const` (:742-750) just forwards `this->get_input()` to `Weapon::update_and_get_projectiles`. I read `Weapon::update_and_get_projectiles` (Weapon.cpp:168-186) and `check_if_shooting_and_ammo_update` (Weapon.cpp:188-233): neither knows anything about `player_state`.

Result: a dead player holding the right trigger keeps spawning projectiles for the whole `RESPAWN_DELAY` (3 s), from `get_center()` — frozen at the death position because `update_movement()` is skipped. `Player::draw` early-returns at :49-52, so the player and gun are invisible. An invisible corpse turret. The weapon's shoot sound also keeps playing (`handle_shoot_sound`, Weapon.cpp:231).

**Fix:** Gate it in `Player::update_weapon_and_get_projectiles()`: return an empty vector when `_state == player_state::DEAD`, or pass a neutral `PlayerInputData{}` so timers still tick but nothing fires. Also call `stop_sounds()` on death (:704-708 currently only plays the death wave).

#### 7. close_quarters ships two 900-unit-tall vertical jump-through 'fences' that teleport falling players to their tops

`ArtAttack/Player.cpp:1-1` — **medium** · `correctness` · confidence: likely

`Player::on_structure_jump_through_collision` only ever resolves a landing-from-above:

    bool was_above = this->_prev_rectangle.get_bottom() <= other_rect.get_top();
    if (moving_down && was_above && move_state != DROPPING_DOWN) {
        MovingObject::set_velocity_y(0.0f);
        this->_rectangle.set_position_y_from_bottom(rect.get_top());
        this->set_move_state(player_move_state::ON_DROP_DOWN_GROUND);
    }

That is correct for a thin horizontal platform. ArtAttack/levels/close_quarters.json:350-378 declares two objects with `"collision_type": "STRUCTURE_JUMP_THROUGH"` whose geometry is the opposite shape:

    "left_fence":  x 1485, y 4350, width 15,  height 900
    "right_fence": x 4500, y 4350, width 15,  height 900

A 15-wide × 900-tall vertical post. Any player descending anywhere in x∈[1485,1500] whose previous bottom was above y=4350 gets snapped to `rect.get_top()` = 4350 — i.e. teleported up to 900 units and left standing on a 15-pixel-wide post in mid-air, with `move_state = ON_DROP_DOWN_GROUND`. Approaching the same fence horizontally, the player passes straight through it, since the handler has no side case.

This is content and code disagreeing about what `STRUCTURE_JUMP_THROUGH` means: the code assumes 'thin horizontal one-way platform', the data uses it as 'vertical fence you can pass through'.

**Fix:** Resolve jump-through collisions against the structure's top *edge* with a max penetration depth (reject if the overlap exceeds a few units), or introduce a distinct one-way-direction field on the collision object so a vertical fence is expressible. Either way the two close_quarters fences need re-authoring.

#### 8. ResourceManager getters return nullptr for a missing key (the catch block is dead), and Player dereferences the result unchecked

`ArtAttack/Player.cpp:44` — **medium** · `robustness`

Merges 3 candidates. `ResourceManager::get_sound_bank` is:
```
try { return this->_sound_banks[sound_bank_name].get(); }
catch (const std::out_of_range&) { ... throw std::out_of_range(error); }   // ResourceManager.cpp:91-102
```
`std::map::operator[]` default-inserts on a missing key and never throws `std::out_of_range`, so the catch is dead code, the function returns `nullptr` for an unknown bank, and the map is polluted with a null entry. `get_texture` (:7-19), `get_sprite_font` (:27-38) and `get_sprite_sheet` (:46-58) have the identical defect. (`get_level_info` at :66-78 correctly uses `.at()`.)

`Player` stores that unchecked at :44 and dereferences it at :687 (damage), :707 (death), :880 (jump) and :1002 (respawn) — a null deref on the first jump if the bank is missing. Not hypothetical: `.gitignore` excludes `*.wav`/`*.xwb`, so a fresh clone has no audio assets.

Compounding it, `player_consts::SOUND_BANK` is the hardcoded literal `"sound_bank_1"` (player_consts.h:55) while the level declares its own bank in JSON (`LevelLoadedInfo::get_sound_bank_name`, used by `Level`). A reusable Player has no business knowing that "sound_bank_1" exists.

**Fix:** Change the getters to `find()` + explicit throw naming the missing key, so a missing resource is a real error at load time. Then null-check `_sound_bank` once at construction and fail loudly, or degrade to a null-sink SoundBank. Longer term the bank name should come from the builder/level data, not from `player_consts`.

#### 9. Player update and draw perform string-keyed std::map lookups every frame to find the sprite sheet and animation strip

`ArtAttack/Player.cpp:702, 47-90` — **medium** · `performance`

`AnimationObject::update()` (called from Player.cpp:702 every frame) goes `get_animation_strip()` → `get_sprite_sheet()` → `ResourceManager::get_sprite_sheet(_sheet_name)`, a `std::map<std::string, ...>` lookup (ResourceManager.cpp:46-58), then a second string-keyed lookup into the sheet's animation strips.

`Player::draw` repeats it: `TextureObject::draw` (:84) resolves the sheet and then the frame by name, and `AnimationObject::draw` (:87) resolves the sheet and the source rectangle via the strip. That is roughly 2 lookups per player per update and ~4 per player per viewport — 4 players × 4 viewports is ~64 red-black-tree traversals with string comparisons per frame for players alone, and the identical path runs for every projectile, which can number in the hundreds. The result is invariant between animation-state changes.

Note this also compounds the draw-race finding: `ResourceManager::get_sprite_sheet` uses non-const `map::operator[]` on a shared map from N threads, so a missing key would be a concurrent insert.

**Fix:** Resolve the `SpriteSheet*` and `const AnimationStrip*` once (at construction and again in the animation-state transition) and cache the pointers. Longer term, key resources by an opaque handle produced at load time rather than `std::string`, and use `unordered_map` at minimum.

#### 10. is_colliding and on_collision disagree: Player only accepts structures but its handler expects projectiles

`ArtAttack/Player.cpp:142-147, 186-244` — **medium** · `design`

`Player::is_matching_collision_object_type` returns `is_structure(other_type)` (:142-147), so `Player::is_colliding` can never return true for a projectile. Yet `Player::on_collision` (:186-244) has a full projectile branch and ends in `throw std::exception("Invalid collision object type.")`.

It only works because `Level::update_level_logic` calls the handler on both participants whenever either predicate passed — Level.cpp:233-236 (`player->is_colliding(other)` → both handlers) and Level.cpp:268-272 (`object->is_colliding(player)` → both handlers). So `Player::on_collision` routinely receives objects that `Player::is_colliding` explicitly rejected, and the callee's correctness depends on the exact shape of the caller's loop. It is also why the same pair is resolved twice per frame.

The fragility is concrete: add any object whose `is_colliding` accepts a player but which `Player::on_collision` does not enumerate, and the game throws from inside the collision loop. (I checked — `PaintTile::is_colliding` (PaintTile.cpp:84-109) has NO type filter at all and would trigger exactly this; it survives only because paint tiles live inside `StructurePaintable::_paint_tiles` rather than in `Level::_collision_objects`.)

The same 25-line 'AABB check, then if other is a rectangle return true, then narrow phase' body is copy-pasted verbatim in Player.cpp:148-185, PaintTile.cpp:84-109 and all five Projectile* classes.

**Fix:** Take collision filtering out of the objects. A `CollisionWorld` with layer/mask bitsets decides candidate pairs, a broad+narrow phase produces a `ContactManifold{a, b, normal, depth}`, and each object gets exactly one `on_contact(const Contact&)` per pair per frame. That deletes seven copies of the same predicate.

#### 11. 'No collision direction' guard is unreachable; a non-intersection is laundered into DIRECTION_RIGHT and resolved as a real ramp contact

`ArtAttack/Player.cpp:245-250, 346-353` — **medium** · `correctness`

Merges 3 candidates (including the dead `is_on_ramp` local). Verified the whole chain:

- `CollisionTools::calculate_object_collision_direction` returns `Vector2F::ZERO` exactly when the shapes are not intersecting (CollisionTools.cpp:128-131).
- Player.cpp:250 immediately feeds that through `Vector2F::direction_to_8_cardinal_direction`, which starts `float angle = direction.angle();` → `std::atan2(0.0f, 0.0f)` → `0.0f` (MattMath.cpp:1749-1752), landing in the first bucket and returning `Vector2F::DIRECTION_RIGHT` (MattMath.cpp:1870-1876). It can never return ZERO.

So the `else if (direction == Vector2F::ZERO) throw` at :346-349 is dead code, the trailing `else throw` at :350-353 is also unreachable (UP/UP_LEFT/UP_RIGHT consumed at :254, LEFT at :258, and DOWN/RIGHT/DOWN_LEFT/DOWN_RIGHT all handled), and the real failure mode is silent: a 'not touching' result becomes DIRECTION_RIGHT, hits the branch at :289-297, and snaps the player down onto the ramp with `set_velocity_y(0)`.

Same function, :271-272: `bool is_on_ramp = ...` is computed and never referenced again, and shadows the member function `Player::is_on_ramp()` (:1246) for the rest of the scope. That is MSVC C4189 under the project's /W4 — evidence warnings are not being read.

**Fix:** Test `direction == Vector2F::ZERO` immediately after :248, before the cardinal snap, and return early. Make `direction_to_8_cardinal_direction` propagate ZERO for a zero-length input instead of silently answering RIGHT — that trap applies to every caller. Delete the dead local.

#### 12. Left-ramp collision is an empty `// TODO` branch while right-ramp is fully implemented

`ArtAttack/Player.cpp:274-277` — **medium** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

```cpp
if (other_type == collision_object_type::STRUCTURE_RAMP_LEFT)
{
    // TODO
}
else if (other_type == collision_object_type::STRUCTURE_RAMP_RIGHT)
{
    ... 60 lines of resolve_object_collision / set_move_state ...
}
```
(Player.cpp:274-345.) `LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:148-155` happily accepts `"collision_type": "STRUCTURE_RAMP_LEFT"` from level JSON and constructs the object, so any level author who places a left ramp gets a silently non-solid one — players fall through it. Today only `king_of_the_hill.json:271` uses a ramp and it is `STRUCTURE_RAMP_RIGHT`, which is why nobody has noticed. This is the same abandoned feature as the six fully-commented `StructureRamp*` files and the unused `is_structure_ramp()` predicate.

**Fix:** Either implement the mirrored case (it is the RIGHT block with the x-direction flipped) or make `LevelObjectBuilder` throw on STRUCTURE_RAMP_LEFT so the gap fails loudly at load time instead of at play time.

#### 13. STRUCTURE_RAMP_LEFT is an empty TODO with no art and no data — the builder accepts it anyway

`ArtAttack/Player.cpp:274-277` — **medium** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

`Player::on_structure_ramp_collision` handles right ramps in detail (Player.cpp:278-354) but left ramps are:

    if (other_type == collision_object_type::STRUCTURE_RAMP_LEFT)
    {
        // TODO
    }

so a left ramp is non-solid for anything that is not a bottom-edge or side-wall hit — the player walks into and through it.

Cross-checking the content confirms the feature was never finished at any layer:
- No shipped level uses it. `STRUCTURE_RAMP_RIGHT` appears exactly once (king_of_the_hill.json:271); `STRUCTURE_RAMP_LEFT` appears in zero level files (levels/*.json and levels/unused/*.json).
- ArtAttack/textures/sprite_sheet_1.json contains `ramp_right_200_100` (line 651) and **no** left-ramp frame at all, so there is nothing to draw one with.
- `StructureRamp.h/.cpp`, `StructureRampLeft.h/.cpp`, `StructureRampRight.h/.cpp` are 100% commented out yet still compiled into the project.

Despite that, `LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:152-155` accepts `"STRUCTURE_RAMP_LEFT"` from JSON and constructs it, so any level author who uses it gets a silently non-solid, un-drawable object rather than a load error.

**Fix:** Either finish the left-ramp case or reject `"STRUCTURE_RAMP_LEFT"` in the builder with a clear 'not implemented' error, and delete the three fully commented-out StructureRamp* translation units from ArtAttack.vcxproj.

#### 14. Ramp collisions resolve via a 40-iteration bisection with a dynamic_cast in the innermost loop

`ArtAttack/Player.cpp:282-345` — **medium** · `performance`

`on_structure_ramp_collision` calls `CollisionTools::resolve_object_collision(&this->_rectangle, other->get_shape(), ...)` at :282, :291, :300 and :339. Ramps are triangles, so the rect/rect fast path at CollisionTools.cpp:244-248 is skipped and it falls into `bracket_object_collision_generic(..., BRACKET_ITERATIONS)` with `BRACKET_ITERATIONS = 40` (CollisionTools.h:7).

Each of the 40 iterations does `collider->intersects(collidee)`, and `Shape::intersects` dispatches through a `dynamic_cast` chain (MattMath.cpp:119-136) — an RTTI lookup in the innermost loop — plus a `pow(1.5f, i)` call (CollisionTools.cpp:40 or :50) and a `get_bounding_box()` returning `RectangleF` by value (:35, :58).

The iteration count is also nonsense at the tail: step size is `1/1.5^i`, so at i=40 that is ~8.6e-8 of the object's size — about 4.5e-6 px for a 52 px-wide player, far below float resolution at world coordinates in the thousands. Everything past roughly iteration 20 is pure waste.

**Fix:** Replace the bisection with an analytic push-out for rect-vs-right-triangle (compute the ramp surface y at the player's x and snap), and give `Shape` a proper double-dispatch or shape-type-indexed function table instead of `dynamic_cast`. If a search must survive, cut it to ~8 iterations with a precomputed step table.

#### 15. Every corner collision heap-allocates a cloned Shape just to measure penetration depth

`ArtAttack/Player.cpp:576-639` — **medium** · `performance`

All four diagonal handlers call `CollisionTools::calculate_object_collision_depth(...)` (:578, :592, :610, :628), which is implemented as:
```
std::unique_ptr<Shape> collider_copy = collider->clone();   // CollisionTools.cpp:275
resolve_object_collision(collider_copy.get(), collidee, collision_direction, amount);
return amount;
```
So each corner contact performs a heap allocation, a virtual clone, and a FULL collision resolution on the copy (including the 40-iteration bisection for non-rectangles) purely to measure a penetration depth that for two AABBs is `RectangleF::intersection(a, b)` — two subtractions. `on_bottom_left_collision`/`on_bottom_right_collision` are the common case of landing on a platform edge, so this runs repeatedly every frame for every player.

**Fix:** Compute the MTV directly: for rect/rect take the intersection extents; for the general case add a non-mutating, non-allocating `Shape::penetration_depth(const Shape*, const Vector2F&)`. Nothing here needs a clone.

#### 16. const member functions mutate the owned Weapon through unique_ptr, where const does not propagate

`ArtAttack/Player.cpp:641-644, 742-750, 1048-1051` — **medium** · `const-correctness`

Merges 3 candidates. `std::unique_ptr::operator->` yields a non-const `Weapon&` from a const `Player`, so three commands are declared as queries:
- `void Player::update_weapon_position() const { this->_primary->set_player_center(...); }` (:641-644)
- `std::vector<std::unique_ptr<ICollisionGameObject>> Player::update_weapon_and_get_projectiles() const` (:742-750) — forwards to `Weapon::update_and_get_projectiles`, a non-const member (Weapon.h:36) that advances shoot timers, spends ammo, plays sounds and constructs projectiles. The most mutating operation in the module, declared const.
- `void Player::stop_sounds() const { this->_primary->stop_sounds(); }` (:1048-1051)

This is what lets `void Level::update_level_logic(...) const` (Level.cpp:180) drive an entire frame of simulation while claiming to be const — it calls `object->update_weapon_and_get_projectiles()` (:205) and `object->update_weapon_position()` (:254) on `const auto&` players. `const` currently carries no information anywhere in this call graph, so the compiler cannot catch a genuine mistake, and it is a direct blocker on ever sharing entities across threads safely (see the draw-race finding). `PlayerBuilder::build_players(...) const` has the same hole via `_weapon_builder`.

**Fix:** Drop `const` from all three. That will correctly force `Level::update_level_logic` and its loop variables to become non-const, restoring `const` as a meaningful signal. If a const-preserving handle is wanted, wrap `_primary` in a small propagate-const pointer.

#### 17. Two divergent damage tables — Player hardcodes its own and ProjectileDetails::player_damage is dead data; health is never clamped at zero

`ArtAttack/Player.cpp:645-690, 696-741` — **medium** · `correctness`

Merges 3 candidates. `on_projectile_collision` (:645-690) is a 35-line if/else chain mapping the collision enum back to constants in `player_consts` (`SPRAY_DAMAGE` … `MIST_DAMAGE`, player_consts.h:65-69). Meanwhile every projectile already carries `ProjectileDetails::player_damage` (projectile_details.h:13), populated per weapon in projectile_consts.h and exposed via `Projectile::get_player_damage()` (Projectile.cpp:295-298). I grepped the whole tree: `get_player_damage` has ZERO call sites outside its own definition — the entire per-projectile damage configuration is dead.

The two tables disagree in sign convention and magnitude: spray 0.01 vs -0.1; jet 0.334 vs -0.5; rolling 0.015 vs **-1000.0**; ball 0.201 vs -0.1; mist 0.01 vs -0.05. Whichever a maintainer edits, half the time nothing happens.

This also forces `Player` to enumerate every weapon type — adding a weapon means editing `collision_object_type`, `Projectile::is_matching_collision_object_type`, `Player::on_collision` (:199-222, which hand-writes 'is this an enemy projectile' as ten enum comparisons duplicating `is_team_a_projectile`/`is_team_b_projectile` in collision_object_type.h) and `Player::on_projectile_collision`. Four places, none compiler-checked, with a runtime `throw` as the fallthrough. That is the game-logic-welded-into-the-entity problem in its purest form.

Also confirmed: `_health` is clamped only on the upper side (:735-738). Nothing clamps at zero, so multiple hits in one frame drive it arbitrarily negative, and that value goes straight to the HUD via `get_health()` (Level.cpp:563).

**Fix:** Delete the `*_DAMAGE` constants from `player_consts.h` and make the projectile the single source of truth — add `get_damage()` to the collision interface (or a small `DamageEvent` payload) so the player does `_health = std::max(0.0f, _health - other->get_damage())`. Fix the sign convention while you are there. Replace the hostility ladder with a `{kind, team}` tag plus an `is_hostile(a, b)` query.

#### 18. Death is detected one frame late, and health regen / debug toggle run while dead

`ArtAttack/Player.cpp:696-741` — **medium** · `correctness`

Merges 2 candidates. `Player::update()` tests `if (this->_health <= 0.0f)` at :704, but damage is applied in `on_projectile_collision`, which `Level` invokes at Level.cpp:271 — AFTER every player's `update()` has already run (Level.cpp:193). So lethal damage taken on frame N is not noticed until frame N+1. During the intervening draw pass in the same tick, the player still renders alive, `get_collision_object_type()` still returns `PLAYER_TEAM_A`/`_B` rather than the `_DEAD` variants, and `is_colliding` still reports live collisions.

Separately, the debug toggle (:726-729) and the health-regen block (:732-740) sit OUTSIDE the `_state` if/else chain, so they execute for dead players too. `_health_regen_timer` accumulates for the whole 3 s `RESPAWN_DELAY`, so on respawn the 5 s `HEALTH_REGEN_DELAY` is already satisfied and regen is live from frame one — the delay only ever applies to the first hit of a life.

I rejected one sub-claim the reviewers made: `_damage_sound_timer` starting at 0.0f does not silence 'the first hit a player ever takes' in general, only a hit landing within the first 0.25 s of the match, since the timer accumulates every alive frame.

**Fix:** Check for death at the point damage is applied (and clamp at zero there) so state, collision type and rendering agree within one frame. Move the regen and debug blocks inside the ALIVE branch and reset `_health_regen_timer` in `respawn()`.

#### 19. respawn() leaves _prev_rectangle and _health_regen_timer stale, and hardcodes 1.0f instead of STARTING_HEALTH

`ArtAttack/Player.cpp:993-1003` — **medium** · `correctness`

Merges 3 candidates, with their consequences corrected. `respawn()` resets position, rotation, velocity, dx, health, ammo and state, but not `_move_state`, `_prev_rectangle`, `_air_time`, `_damage_sound_timer` or `_health_regen_timer`.

I verified that most of the alarming consequences the reviewers claimed do NOT occur:
- The 'free jump on respawn' and 'ramp-gravity slam' claims are WRONG. While dead, `Player::is_colliding` returns false (:151-154), so `player_colliding_with_structure` is false every frame and `Level` calls `on_no_collision()` (Level.cpp:245-248), which converts ON_GROUND/ON_DROP_DOWN_GROUND/ON_RAMP_* to IN_AIR long before the respawn. `_air_time` is only read in the JUMPING branch and is zeroed by `do_jump` on the next jump, so it is harmless.

What IS real:
- `_prev_rectangle` still holds the death rectangle. `respawn()` runs from `update()` at Level.cpp:193, before the collision pass (Level.cpp:222) and before `update_prev_rectangle()` (Level.cpp:255). So for the whole respawn frame `on_structure_jump_through_collision` evaluates `_prev_rectangle.get_bottom() <= other_rect.get_top()` (:372) against a position from wherever the player died — the player can snap onto, or drop through, the platform under the spawn point.
- `_health_regen_timer` keeps accumulating while dead (the regen block at :732-740 is outside the state branch), so on respawn the 5 s `HEALTH_REGEN_DELAY` is already satisfied and regen is live from frame one.
- `this->_health = 1.0f;` (:999) and the regen cap `if (this->_health > 1.0f)` (:735-737) both duplicate `player_consts::STARTING_HEALTH` (player_consts.h:34), which is already 1.0f. Retuning STARTING_HEALTH silently desynchronises all three.

**Fix:** Factor a `reset_transient_state()` called by both the constructor and `respawn()`, covering `_prev_rectangle = _rectangle`, `_health_regen_timer = 0.0f`, `_damage_sound_timer`, `_move_state = IN_AIR`, and `_health = player_consts::STARTING_HEALTH`. That makes it impossible to add a member and forget one of the two paths.

#### 20. on_no_collision() omits ON_CEILING, so the player stays flagged 'on ceiling' for the whole fall

`ArtAttack/Player.cpp:1252-1263` — **medium** · `correctness`

```
void Player::on_no_collision() {
    player_move_state move_state = this->get_move_state();
    if (move_state == ON_GROUND || move_state == ON_DROP_DOWN_GROUND ||
        move_state == ON_RAMP_LEFT || move_state == ON_RAMP_RIGHT)
    { this->set_move_state(player_move_state::IN_AIR); }
}
```
`ON_CEILING` is set by `on_top_collision` (:551) and is as much a surface-contact state as the four listed, but is missing. Once a player bumps their head, `_move_state` stays `ON_CEILING` until they land and `on_bottom_collision` overwrites it. Observable while falling: `calculate_animation_state` returns IDLE for ON_CEILING (:1023-1026) so the idle clip plays while plummeting; `do_jump` has an explicit `else if (move_state == ON_CEILING) { // do nothing }` arm (:882-885) so no jump bookkeeping runs at all; and the debug overlay reports `on_ceiling` throughout.

Related, root cause in Level but the semantics are Player's: `player_colliding_with_structure` (Level.cpp:224-248) is set for ANY structure contact including a pure side-wall hit, and `on_left_collision`/`on_right_collision` (:562-575) never touch the move state. So a player who walks off a ledge while brushing a wall never gets `on_no_collision()` and keeps `ON_GROUND` in mid-air, which does grant a free jump.

**Fix:** Add `move_state == player_move_state::ON_CEILING` to the condition, or better `if (is_on_ground() || move_state == ON_CEILING)` so a newly added grounded state cannot be forgotten here. Separately, have `Level` distinguish 'supported from below' from 'touched any structure' before deciding to call `on_no_collision`.

#### 21. Constructor drops animation_info.frame_time and starts _animation_state inconsistent with the strip it loaded

`ArtAttack/Player.cpp:9-45, 54-74` — **low** · `correctness`

The constructor forwards `animation_info.sprite_sheet`/`animation`/`uniform_texture` to the two sprite bases (:27-31) but silently ignores `animation_info.frame_time`. The only place `frame_time` is ever honoured is `draw()` (:66-73), and only on a state CHANGE — so a caller passing a custom `frame_time` gets it dropped until the state happens to change.

`_animation_state` is declared `= player_animation_state::IDLE` (Player.h:154) while `PlayerBuilder` constructs every player with `DEFAULT_ANIMATION_INFO` (PlayerBuilder.cpp:42), which is the WALK strip (`DEFAULT_ANIMATION_STRIP = "player_right_walk"`, player_consts.h:50/80-86). The object therefore starts claiming IDLE while displaying the walking animation.

Graded low because I traced that it self-corrects: `_move_state` starts as `IN_AIR` and velocity is zero, so the first `calculate_animation_state()` returns JUMPING ≠ IDLE and the transition block repairs it on the first draw. But construct a Player grounded at zero velocity and the walk strip renders while idle indefinitely.

**Fix:** Apply the full `animation_info` — including `frame_time` — through one private `apply_animation_info(const PlayerAnimationInfo&)` used by both the constructor and the state transition, and initialise `_animation_state` from that same info instead of hardcoding IDLE. Point `DEFAULT_ANIMATION_INFO` at `ANIMATION_INFO_IDLE`.

#### 22. The no-camera draw overload omits the team-colour layer, the facing flip and the dead check

`ArtAttack/Player.cpp:91-95` — **low** · `correctness`

```
void Player::draw(SpriteBatch* sprite_batch) {
    AnimationObject::draw(sprite_batch, this->_rectangle, Camera::DEFAULT_CAMERA);
    this->_primary->draw(sprite_batch, Camera::DEFAULT_CAMERA);
}
```
Compared with the camera overload (:47-90) it is missing three things: the `TextureObject` uniform pass (so the player renders with no team colour — the only visual that distinguishes team A from team B), the `SpriteEffects_FlipHorizontally` derived from `get_facing_right()` (so the player always faces right), and the `_state == DEAD` early-return (so a dead player is drawn).

A straightforward copy-paste divergence between two overrides of the same virtual pair. Latent — `Level` only ever calls the camera overload — but any engine code drawing an `IGameObject*` without a camera gets a silently wrong player.

**Fix:** Delegate: `draw(sprite_batch, Camera::DEFAULT_CAMERA);`. Better, drop the two-overload scheme from `IGameObject` entirely — `Camera::DEFAULT_CAMERA` already expresses 'no camera', so one method suffices.

#### 23. get_collision_object_type recomputes a two-level switch, and can throw, on every collision-pair test

`ArtAttack/Player.cpp:96-127` — **low** · `performance`

This virtual re-derives a value from two members that change at most a few times per match, and its default arms `throw std::exception(...)`. `Level::update_level_logic` calls it once per (collision object, player) pair — `Projectile::is_matching_collision_object_type` calls `other->get_collision_object_type()` (Projectile.cpp:96) for every projectile against every player (Level.cpp:268), and `Player::is_colliding` does the mirror for every object (Player.cpp:145). With 4 players and a few hundred live projectiles that is thousands of calls per frame on a throwing function the optimiser cannot inline across the vtable.

It also means an invalid `player_team`/`player_state` surfaces as an exception thrown from a getter deep inside the collision loop rather than at the point the bad value was set. Graded low because the per-call cost is small; the design smell (throwing query, derived-state recomputation) is the real point.

**Fix:** Store the derived `collision_object_type` as a member updated in `set_state`/`set_team` — the only two mutators. Better still, replace the 23-value cross-product enum with a `{category, team}` pair so the type is a trivial field read.

#### 24. const RectangleF& bound to a by-value temporary, then the identical temporary recomputed nine lines later

`ArtAttack/Player.cpp:371-381` — **low** · `correctness`

Merges 2 candidates.
```
const RectangleF& other_rect = other->get_shape()->get_bounding_box();   // :371
bool was_above = this->_prev_rectangle.get_bottom() <= other_rect.get_top();
...
const RectangleF& rect = other->get_shape()->get_bounding_box();         // :380
this->_rectangle.set_position_y_from_bottom(rect.get_top());
```
`Shape::get_bounding_box()` returns `RectangleF` by VALUE (MattMath.h, and every override). Binding a `const&` is legal via lifetime extension, but it reads as a borrowed reference into `other` — the single most common way this pattern becomes a dangling reference when someone later returns it or stores it in a member. `other_rect` and `rect` are the same value under two names, obtained by two virtual calls.

**Fix:** Compute it once as a value — `const RectangleF other_rect = other->get_shape()->get_bounding_box();` — and use it at both sites. Reserve `const T&` for things that genuinely outlive the expression.

#### 25. Debug-overlay visibility is a boolean on the character entity, toggled inside its simulation update

`ArtAttack/Player.cpp:726-729` — **low** · `design`

`if (this->_input.toggle_debug) { this->_showing_debug = !this->_showing_debug; }` inside `Player::update`, read back by `Level::draw_player_view_level` at Level.cpp:572 to decide whether to run `DebugText::draw_debug_info`, and also passed into `_primary->draw(..., this->_showing_debug)` at Player.cpp:89.

Whether a developer overlay is on screen is a property of the debug tooling and the view, not of a simulated character. It forces the flag to replicate per player and forces `get_showing_debug`/`set_showing_debug` into the entity's API (Player.h:115, 246 — the setter is dead).

**Fix:** Give the engine a `DebugOverlay` subsystem owning its own visibility keyed by view index, subscribing to a `toggle_debug` action. `Player` should not know a debug HUD exists.

#### 26. PlayerInputData copied redundantly — once into a local that is then bypassed, and three more times through the by-value weapon API

`ArtAttack/Player.cpp:756-764, 742-750` — **low** · `performance`

Merges 2 candidates. `update_movement` opens with `const PlayerInputData input = this->_input;` (:758), uses it for exactly one field (`input.x_movement`, :759), and then goes back to the member directly for the next two reads (`this->_input.left_analog_stick.y` :762, `this->_input.jump_pressed` :764). The copy buys nothing and misleads.

`Player::update_weapon_and_get_projectiles` passes `this->get_input()` (a `const&`) into `Weapon::update_and_get_projectiles(PlayerInputData input, ...)` — by VALUE (Weapon.h:36, and again in the `RelativeVelocityWeapon` override at Weapon.h:164) — which then passes it by value again into `update_movement_and_rotation(PlayerInputData input, ...)` (Weapon.h:110) and `check_if_shooting_and_ammo_update(PlayerInputData input, ...)` (Weapon.h:106). Three full-struct copies (~56 bytes each) per player per frame for a parameter nobody mutates. Graded low — the cost is trivial; the point is that four signatures are wrong by default.

**Fix:** Delete the local at :758 (bind `const PlayerInputData& input = this->_input;` if a short name is wanted) and change all four `Weapon` signatures to `const PlayerInputData&`.

#### 27. Inconsistent float-zero comparison for the same velocity, plus an unnamed 600.0f walk/run threshold

`ArtAttack/Player.cpp:1004-1021, 756-818` — **low** · `correctness`

Merges 3 candidates. `update_movement` mixes epsilon and exact comparison of the same two values within one if/else chain: `are_equal(MovingObject::get_velocity_x(), 0.0f) && x_input != 0.0f` (:767) versus `MovingObject::get_velocity_x() > 0.0f && are_equal(x_input, 0.0f)` (:802). `calculate_animation_state` then tests the same velocity with a bare exact compare: `if (velocity_x == 0.0f)` (:1010).

The project builds with `<FloatingPointModel>Fast</FloatingPointModel>` in all four configurations (verified in ArtAttack.vcxproj), and `MattMath::EPSILON` is 1e-4, so a velocity of 5e-5 is 'zero' to the movement code and non-zero to the animation code — the player is treated as stopped for physics while playing the walk clip.

`600.0f` (:1014) is an unnamed walk/run threshold sitting between the named `X_INITIAL_VELOCITY` (100) and `MAX_VELOCITY.x` (800) in `player_consts`. Same category: `player_and_weapon_rect.inflate(Vector2F(200.0f, 200.0f))` (:919) is an unnamed culling margin that exists only because the player's `_rectangle` covers the body while `draw` also renders `_primary` — a hand-tuned guess whose failure mode is invisible pop-in rather than a compile error.

Also in the same chain and genuinely wrong: the two opposite-direction branches (:790-800) apply BOTH `X_DEACCELERATION * dt * x_input` and `X_ACCELERATION * dt * x_input` and, unlike the same-direction branches above them, never clamp to `±MAX_VELOCITY.x`.

**Fix:** Use `are_equal(v, 0.0f)` everywhere for velocity. Move `600.0f` and the cull margin into `player_consts` as named constants (and better, derive the cull bounds as the union of `_rectangle` and `_primary->get_draw_bounds()`). Collapse the seven-branch chain into one signed-acceleration computation followed by a single clamp.

#### 28. get_player_move_state_string omits DROPPING_DOWN and allocates a std::string per call

`ArtAttack/Player.cpp:1216-1236` — **low** · `correctness`

Merges 2 candidates. `player_move_state` has eight enumerators (Player.h:22-32); the switch handles seven. `DROPPING_DOWN` is missing, so the debug overlay reports `"invalid"` whenever the player is dropping through a jump-through platform — exactly the state you would be debugging. It is a reachable state, set at Player.cpp:845.

Because there is no `default` label and an enumerator is unhandled, MSVC at /W4 emits C4062 here. The project sets `Level4` but never `TreatWarningAsError` (verified in the vcxproj), which is why this and the C4189 dead local at :271 have gone unnoticed.

The function also returns `std::string` by value from string literals, heap-allocating once per player per frame for the debug overlay. There is a stray `;` after the switch's closing brace.

**Fix:** Add `case player_move_state::DROPPING_DOWN: return "dropping_down";`, return `const char*` (the literals have static storage duration), and keep the switch `default`-less so C4062 keeps guarding it as the enum grows. Turn on warnings-as-errors, or at least read them.

## `ArtAttack/Projectile.cpp`

_14 findings: 1 critical, 6 high, 6 medium, 1 low_

#### 1. get_delete_timer() returns _timer, so the lifetime check is `_timer > _timer` and no projectile ever expires

`ArtAttack/Projectile.cpp:278-288` — **critical** · `correctness`

Verified verbatim. `float Projectile::get_delete_timer() const { return this->_timer; }` (Projectile.cpp:285-288) returns the elapsed timer instead of `_details.delete_timer`. The sole caller is `if (this->get_timer() > this->get_delete_timer())` at Projectile.cpp:278, and `get_timer()` (line 220-223) also returns `_timer` — so the test is a strict self-comparison and is never true. Grep confirms `ProjectileDetails::delete_timer` (projectile_details.h:12) is written at projectile_consts.h:19,32,53,66,79,100 and read nowhere.

Consequences I traced end to end:
- The only removal path left is `Projectile::on_collision` (Projectile.cpp:120-154), which sets deletion on a structure or enemy-player hit.
- `DETAILS_JET` and `DETAILS_MIST` have `gravity = 0.0f, wind_resistance = 0.0f` (projectile_consts.h:50-51, 76-77), so a missed jet/mist shot flies dead straight forever.
- `Level::update_level_logic` responds to anything leaving the level with `throw std::exception("Collision object out of bounds")` (Level.cpp:315-321). I grepped every `catch` in ArtAttack/*.cpp: the only handlers are in Level.cpp:727 (bad_cast), ResourceLoader, ResourceManager and SoundBank. There is no handler on the update path, so a missed shot terminates the process.
- Survivors accumulate in `_collision_objects`, which is walked object-vs-object in a full O(n^2) double loop every frame (Level.cpp:259-293).

Secondary defect confirmed in the same block: the expiry test at line 278 runs before `alter_timer(dt)` at line 282, so even once fixed a projectile survives one frame past its deadline.

Merged from 5 duplicate candidate reports (all naming Projectile.cpp:278-288).

**Fix:** `return this->get_details().delete_timer;`, and move the test after `alter_timer(dt)`. Rename the pair to `get_age()` / `get_lifetime()` (or collapse both into `bool has_expired() const`) so the self-comparison becomes unwritable. Separately, `Level::is_object_out_of_bounds` must mark transient objects for deletion, not throw — an escaped projectile is not an exceptional condition, and today it is a guaranteed process kill.

#### 2. Projectile's hand-rolled structure filter omits both ramp types, so projectiles fly through every ramp in the shipped level

`ArtAttack/Projectile.cpp:93-119` — **high** · `correctness`

Verified. `is_matching_collision_object_type` (Projectile.cpp:98-101) hand-writes:
```cpp
bool structure_collision =
    other_type == collision_object_type::STRUCTURE ||
    other_type == collision_object_type::STRUCTURE_PAINTABLE ||
    other_type == collision_object_type::STRUCTURE_JUMP_THROUGH;
```
`collision_object_type` has five structure enumerators (collision_object_type.h:6-10); this list covers three. For a ramp, `structure_collision` is false and the team switch then asks `other_type == PLAYER_TEAM_A/B`, which is also false. Every projectile's `is_colliding` short-circuits on this predicate first (ProjectileSpray.cpp:59, ProjectileJet.cpp:57, ProjectileBall.cpp:58, ProjectileMist.cpp:59, ProjectileRolling.cpp:51), so no projectile of any kind can hit a ramp.

The correct predicate already exists and is not used: `inline bool is_structure(collision_object_type)` at collision_object_type.h:75-82 lists all five, including the ramps. `Level::update_level_logic` itself calls that function (Level.cpp:238) — the projectile code is the outlier.

This is live content, not theoretical: `ArtAttack/levels/king_of_the_hill.json:271` declares `STRUCTURE_RAMP` collision types. Players collide with ramps; bullets pass through and ramps never take paint.

The identical hand-written list is duplicated 25 lines below in `on_collision` (Projectile.cpp:124-127), so both copies carry the same omission.

Merged from 2 duplicate candidate reports.

**Fix:** Replace both hand-written blocks with the existing `is_structure(other_type)` — it is already `inline` in the header, so there is no call cost. Then delete the duplicate entirely by reducing `on_collision` to `set_for_deletion(is_matching_collision_object_type(other));`. Longer term this should not be an enum whitelist at all — see the collision-filter finding.

#### 3. Each object hardcodes its own slice of the collision matrix, and the resulting relation is asymmetric

`ArtAttack/Projectile.cpp:93-119` — **high** · `design`

Verified. `Projectile::is_matching_collision_object_type` encodes inside the projectile class exactly which of the 23 `collision_object_type` values a projectile may interact with. Two verified consequences:

(a) `PAINT_TILE` is absent from the list, so a projectile always answers 'no' to a paint tile. Painting only works because `PaintTile::is_colliding` (PaintTile.cpp:84-109) has **no type filter at all** — it collides with literally anything. `Level::update_level_logic` calls both orderings (`object->is_colliding(object_2.get())` at Level.cpp:287 inside a loop that visits every ordered pair), so the effective rule is 'collide if either side says yes'. `a->is_colliding(b)` and `b->is_colliding(a)` genuinely disagree here.

(b) `STRUCTURE_RAMP_LEFT/RIGHT` are absent — see the separate ramp finding.

The knowledge of who-hits-what is scattered across every object rather than living in one place, which is precisely why it has already drifted twice.

**Fix:** Move filtering out of the objects and into the collision system: one `CollisionFilter` (layer + mask) per object and one `bool should_test(a, b) { return (a.layer & b.mask) && (b.layer & a.mask); }` evaluated once per pair by the broad phase. That makes the relation symmetric by construction, makes 'projectiles now hit ramps' a one-bit data change, and deletes `is_matching_collision_object_type` from all five projectile leaves plus Player and PaintTile.

#### 4. Every projectile flies straight through the shipped ramp in king_of_the_hill

`ArtAttack/Projectile.cpp:93-119` — **high** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

`Projectile::is_matching_collision_object_type` gates all projectile collision on:

    bool structure_collision =
        other_type == collision_object_type::STRUCTURE ||
        other_type == collision_object_type::STRUCTURE_PAINTABLE ||
        other_type == collision_object_type::STRUCTURE_JUMP_THROUGH;

`STRUCTURE_RAMP_LEFT` / `STRUCTURE_RAMP_RIGHT` are absent, even though `is_structure()` (ArtAttack/collision_object_type.h:75-82) includes them and `Player::is_matching_collision_object_type` (ArtAttack/Player.cpp:142-147) uses that helper. `Projectile::on_collision` (ArtAttack/Projectile.cpp:120-152) repeats the same three-way test, so it would not delete the projectile either. No subclass overrides it — ProjectileSpray.cpp:59, ProjectileJet.cpp:57, ProjectileBall.cpp:58, ProjectileMist.cpp:59, ProjectileRolling.cpp:51 all call the base version.

The shipped content reaches this: ArtAttack/levels/king_of_the_hill.json:257-273 declares `"name": "mountain_level_1_ramp_east"`, `"type": "StructureRamp"`, `"collision_type": "STRUCTURE_RAMP_RIGHT"` with triangle (300,6000)-(1700,6000)-(1700,5550) — a 1400×450 unit slope that is the entire approach from team A's spawn to the central mountain. ArtAttack/LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:144-177 maps that string to `collision_object_type::STRUCTURE_RAMP_RIGHT` and builds a plain `Structure` with a `TriangleRightAxisAligned` shape. Result: players collide with the ramp (Player handles it), but all five projectile types pass through it as if it were air, and are never deleted on it. It is also a plain `Structure`, not `StructurePaintable`, so it cannot be painted either.

**Fix:** Replace the hand-written three-way test with the existing `is_structure(other_type)` predicate in both `Projectile::is_matching_collision_object_type` and `Projectile::on_collision`, so ramps (and any future structure type) are covered by construction. Better still, delete the enum-switch dispatch entirely and put a `bool blocks_projectiles()` on the collision interface.

#### 5. A projectile's only hit response is a bool; its actual effect is implemented by whatever it hits

`ArtAttack/Projectile.cpp:120-154` — **high** · `design`

Verified. `Projectile::on_collision` does exactly one thing — `set_for_deletion(true)` — after re-deriving, for the second time in the same file, the structure/enemy-player predicate that `is_matching_collision_object_type` computed 30 lines earlier (compare Projectile.cpp:98-101 with :124-127; identical text).

Everything a projectile actually *does* lives in the target: `Player::on_projectile_collision` (Player.cpp:645-682) picks the damage by inspecting the attacker's enum; `StructurePaintable::on_collision` decides a paint splat happens and plays the sound; `PaintTile::on_collision` (PaintTile.cpp:114-138) re-derives the attacker's team from the same enum a third time. A projectile therefore cannot introduce a new effect — bounce, explode, splash radius, freeze — without editing every class it might touch. This responsibility inversion is what makes the type enum load-bearing.

Merged with the candidate noting that `on_collision` re-implements the type filter instead of calling the `virtual` predicate declared at Projectile.h:58. Because it duplicates rather than delegates, any subclass that overrides the virtual — the reason it is virtual — collides with the new type but is silently not consumed by it. Both copies also `throw std::exception("Invalid player_team value.")` on `player_team::NONE`, which is the default value of `_team` (Projectile.h:76), from inside the O(n^2) collision loop.

**Fix:** Collapse the body to `if (this->is_matching_collision_object_type(other)) this->set_for_deletion(true);` — one source of truth, and the virtual starts meaning something. Then give the projectile a payload it carries and the collision system applies: `struct HitPayload { float damage; Colour paint_colour; TeamId team; }` exposed as `const HitPayload& get_payload() const`. Targets implement `apply(const HitPayload&)` and stop inspecting the attacker's type. Drop the `NONE` throws by making team a required construction-time invariant instead of re-validating on every collision.

#### 6. collision_object_type is a team x weapon cross-product enum, re-expanded by hand in six places

`ArtAttack/Projectile.cpp:155-195` — **high** · `design`

Verified. `Projectile::get_collision_object_type()` is a 40-line nested switch mapping 2 teams x 5 projectile types onto ten distinct enumerators, with three `throw std::exception` fallbacks (lines 174, 190, 193). Object identity is therefore a flat enum that multiplies class by team, and every consumer re-expands that cross product by hand. I confirmed all the expansion sites:
- `collision_object_type.h:43-73` — three separate predicates `is_projectile`, `is_team_a_projectile`, `is_team_b_projectile`, each listing all ten/five values.
- `Player::on_projectile_collision` (Player.cpp:645-682) — a 5-branch ladder over pairs, ending in `throw std::exception("Invalid projectile type.")`.
- `PaintTile::on_collision` (PaintTile.cpp:114-137) — re-derives the attacker's team from the same ten values, also ending in a throw.
- `StructurePaintable::on_collision`, `Player::on_collision`.

Adding one weapon type means editing at least six files; adding a third team doubles the enum. For a project whose stated goal is a reusable engine, this is the single structural decision that makes the projectile system unextensible.

**Fix:** Replace the identity enum with a collision filter: `get_collision_filter()` returning `{ layer, mask }` bitmasks, where 'projectile' is one layer bit and team membership is a bit in a separate team mask. The cross product disappears. Where a target genuinely needs to know what hit it, give `ICollisionGameObject` a virtual returning a game-side payload pointer rather than forcing the target to reverse-engineer the attacker from an enum. `is_team_a_projectile`/`is_team_b_projectile` and all five hand expansions then delete.

#### 7. get_delete_timer() returns _timer, so the projectile lifetime check is `_timer > _timer` and no projectile ever expires

`ArtAttack/Projectile.cpp:285-288` — **high** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

```
float Projectile::get_delete_timer() const
{
	return this->_timer;
}
```
`Projectile` has no `_delete_timer` member (Projectile.h:69-79); the intended value lives in `_details.delete_timer` (projectile_details.h, populated in projectile_consts.h:19/32/53/66/79/100). The check at Projectile.cpp:278-281 is therefore
```
if (this->get_timer() > this->get_delete_timer())   // _timer > _timer -> always false
    this->set_for_deletion(true);
```
and can never fire. `get_timer()` returns `_timer` (Projectile.cpp:220-222); both accessors return the same field.

REACHABILITY: LIVE, every frame, for every projectile. Level::update (Level.cpp:128) → update_level_logic (Level.cpp:183-186, `object->update()`) → e.g. ProjectileMist::update (ProjectileMist.cpp:34) / ProjectileRolling::update (ProjectileRolling.cpp:33) → Projectile::update_movement (Projectile.cpp:278).

Observable consequences over a 3-minute king_of_the_hill match:
- The only remaining removal paths are `on_collision` with a structure or an enemy player (Projectile.cpp:120-153) and the out-of-bounds check, which **throws** instead of deleting (Level.cpp:315-321).
- MIST has gravity 0 and wind_resistance 0 (projectile_consts.h:76-77) and launches at 300 u/s (weapon_consts.h:120). Designed lifetime 5 s; actual lifetime is however long it takes to cross the 6000-unit level ≈ 20 s. That is a 4× increase in live projectile count, and the collision loop in Level::update_level_logic (Level.cpp:259-293) is O(n²) over `_collision_objects` — so ~16× the pair tests.
- Worst case is ROLLING: `DETAILS_ROLLING` has `delete_timer = 0.000001f` (projectile_consts.h:66), i.e. it is designed as a one-frame hitbox. It also has `starting_vel_length = 0.0f` (weapon_consts.h:92) and `shoot_interval = 0.0001f` (:91), so the Roller spawns a **stationary** 50×50 hitbox with `player_damage = -1000` every frame the trigger is held, and `ProjectileRolling::draw` is empty and `is_visible_in_viewport` returns false (ProjectileRolling.cpp:36-47). With the timer broken, holding the Roller trigger in mid-air leaves a permanent field of invisible instant-kill hitboxes.

**Fix:** `return this->_details.delete_timer;` — or better, drop `get_delete_timer()` entirely and inline `if (this->_timer > this->_details.delete_timer)`. Two accessors on the same field with different names is precisely how this hid. Also add a unit test for projectile expiry; nothing in MattMathTests covers game objects because the engine is not built as a library.

#### 8. Projectile construction can null-deref or throw from inside a constructor when an asset name is wrong, mid-frame with no handler

`ArtAttack/Projectile.cpp:21-22` — **medium** · `robustness`

Verified end to end. `Projectile`'s ctor forwards `details.sheet_name` / `details.animation_strip_name` to `AnimationObject` (Projectile.cpp:21-22), whose ctor body immediately does `this->_frame_time = this->get_animation_strip()->get_frame_time();` (AnimationObject.cpp:21). That chains to `get_sprite_sheet()` -> `ResourceManager::get_sprite_sheet`, which returns `nullptr` on a miss (map `operator[]`, ResourceManager.cpp:51) and is dereferenced unchecked; or, if the sheet exists but the strip name does not, `SpriteSheet::get_animation_strip` uses `.at(name)` and throws `std::out_of_range` **from inside a constructor**.

That exception escapes `std::make_unique<ProjectileSpray>(...)` (ProjectileBuilder.cpp:28-40), then `Weapon::shoot`, then `Level::update_level_logic` (Level.cpp:204-210). I grepped every `catch` in ArtAttack/*.cpp: nothing on that path. So a content rename turns the act of firing into a hard crash rather than a load-time error.

The names are hardcoded string literals in projectile_consts.h — all five projectiles share `"sprite_sheet_1"`/`"projectile_3"` (lines 23-24, 36-37, 57-58, 70-71, 83-84, 104-105), and `DETAILS_DEFAULT` points at a strip literally named `"test"`. Nothing validates them, and nothing validates the `-1.0f` sentinel defaults in `ProjectileDetails` either — a partially-filled struct yields negative gravity and a negative delete timer with no complaint.

Merged from 2 candidate reports.

**Fix:** Validate sheet/strip names once at load time — better, resolve the detail tables into `const AnimationStrip*` handles during resource load so constructing a gameplay object cannot fail. Add a `validate()` on `ProjectileDetails`/`DiffusionDetails` (gravity finite, `delete_timer > 0`, `size > 0`, `end_time > start_time`, names non-empty) reporting every bad field at once. At minimum make the resource getters fail loudly with the missing key named.

#### 9. calculate_diffusion_size() interpolates toward 1+end_scale but clamps to end_scale, so the sprite and hitbox pop down

`ArtAttack/Projectile.cpp:61-89` — **medium** · `correctness`

Verified. The two branches disagree at the join:
```cpp
else if (time >= details.end_time) { multiple = details.end_scale; }
else { ... multiple = Vector2F::ONE + Vector2F(details.end_scale.x * ratio, details.end_scale.y * ratio); }
```
As `ratio -> 1` the interpolating branch converges on `ONE + end_scale`; at `time == end_time` the clamp branch returns `end_scale`. The scale therefore jumps down by exactly 1.0 at `end_time`.
- Spray (`DIFFUSION_DETAILS_SPRAY`, end_scale 1.5, projectile_consts.h:40-46): grows 1.0x -> 2.5x over 0.2s..1.0s, then snaps to 1.5x — a 40% drop.
- Mist (end_scale 5.0, projectile_consts.h:87-93): 1.0x -> 6.0x over 0.2s..2.0s, then snaps to 5.0x.

This is not cosmetic only: the result feeds `_rectangle.inflate_to_size(...)` (ProjectileSpray.cpp:37, ProjectileMist.cpp:37) and `_rectangle` *is* the collision shape (`get_shape()` returns `&_rectangle`), so the hitbox discontinuously shrinks mid-flight.

Secondary issues on the same lines, all verified: the three locals at 77-82 are non-const; `Vector2F(end_scale.x * ratio, end_scale.y * ratio)` hand-reimplements `operator*(const Vector2F&, float)` which exists at MattMath.h:503; and `diff_length` is an unguarded divisor, so a details blob with `start_time == end_time` yields inf/NaN sizes.

Merged from 4 duplicate candidate reports.

**Fix:** `multiple = Vector2F::ONE + (details.end_scale - Vector2F::ONE) * ratio;` — or `Vector2F::lerp(Vector2F::ONE, details.end_scale, ratio)`, which already exists at MattMath.h:468. Make the locals const, and either assert `end_time > start_time` at construction or divide by `std::max(diff_length, epsilon)`. This is exactly the kind of pure function MattMathTests should cover: assert continuity at both `start_time` and `end_time`.

#### 10. get_collision_object_type() re-evaluates a nested switch on every call, inside the O(n^2) collision loop

`ArtAttack/Projectile.cpp:155-195` — **medium** · `performance`

Verified. The function computes its answer from `_team` and `_type` through a nested switch every single call, though both members are fixed at construction. Call sites I traced:
- `Projectile::is_matching_collision_object_type` calls `other->get_collision_object_type()` (Projectile.cpp:96), which is invoked from each leaf's `is_colliding` — and `Level::update_level_logic` runs `is_colliding` for **every ordered pair** of collision objects (Level.cpp:277-292, a full N x N loop, not N choose 2) plus every player-vs-object pair twice (Level.cpp:227-243 and 262-273).
- `Projectile::on_collision` calls it again (line 122).
- `Player::on_projectile_collision` (Player.cpp:647) and `PaintTile::on_collision` (PaintTile.cpp:116) call it on every hit.

So it is O(N^2) nested-switch evaluations plus a virtual call each, per frame, to recompute a constant. With the delete-timer bug letting N grow without bound, this sits on the critical path. The `default:` arms also throw from inside that loop.

**Fix:** Compute the `collision_object_type` once in the `Projectile` constructor and store it; `get_collision_object_type()` becomes a member read. This is a strictly local fix that can land before the larger collision-filter redesign.

#### 11. update_movement() does four unrelated jobs and makes every subclass hand the base its own data back

`ArtAttack/Projectile.cpp:232-283` — **medium** · `design`

Verified. All five leaves open `update()` with the identical two statements (ProjectileSpray.cpp:32-35, Jet:32-35, Ball:32-35, Mist:32-35, Rolling:31-34):
```cpp
const ProjectileDetails& details = this->get_details();
Projectile::update_movement(details.gravity, details.wind_resistance);
```
The base already owns `_details`; making the derived class read two fields out of it and pass them back down is pure ceremony that exists in five places.

The function itself does four unrelated things: gravity integration, clamping against a namespace-scope `projectile_consts::MAX_VELOCITY` that no projectile definition can override (projectile_consts.h:12), wind resistance, and lifetime accounting — despite being named `update_movement`. That naming is part of why the expiry bug stayed hidden.

A real ordering coupling falls out of it, which I verified: `ProjectileSpray::update` calls `update_movement` (which advances `_timer` at line 282) and *then* `calculate_diffusion_size()` (which reads `_timer` at Projectile.cpp:63), so the diffusion is evaluated one frame ahead of the movement it accompanies.

Merged with the candidate noting `update_movement` is declared `virtual` (Projectile.h:67) with no overrides anywhere and all five call sites explicitly qualified — the vtable slot is dead. Same for `virtual bool is_matching_collision_object_type` (Projectile.h:58). The clamp is also written out longhand four times (lines 238-245 and 265-272).

**Fix:** Make `Projectile::update()` a non-virtual template method that integrates from its own `_details`, advances lifetime, applies deletion, then calls a protected `virtual void on_updated()` hook for the one thing that varies. Drop `virtual` from `update_movement` and `is_matching_collision_object_type`. Move `MAX_VELOCITY` into `ProjectileDetails` so it is per-definition data. Collapse the four clamp ladders into one `clamp_abs` helper (or `std::clamp` once the language standard is raised).

#### 12. Wind resistance compares a velocity against an acceleration times a magic 4.0f, then snaps x-velocity to exactly zero

`ArtAttack/Projectile.cpp:247-264` — **medium** · `correctness`

Verified verbatim at Projectile.cpp:248-264. Two distinct problems:

1. **Dimensionally meaningless threshold.** `wind_resistance` is an acceleration — it is multiplied by `dt` two lines below to produce a velocity delta. `wind_resistance * 4.0f` is an acceleration times an unexplained `4`, compared against a velocity in units/s. The threshold has no physical meaning and does not scale if the drag constant is retuned. (The `4` looks like an attempt at 'about four frames of decel', which would only be right at exactly 60 fps.)

2. **Hard snap to zero.** Below the threshold, `set_velocity_x(0.0f)` discards horizontal velocity in a single frame instead of decaying it. With `DETAILS_SPRAY.wind_resistance = 20.0f` the cutoff is 80 units/s and `DETAILS_SPRAYER.starting_vel_length` is 1100 (weapon_consts.h:42), so any sprayer shot within a few degrees of vertical has its horizontal component annihilated on the first update — the shot goes perfectly vertical instead of slightly angled. A projectile can also never asymptotically slow down: it either drags linearly or stops dead.

For JET, ROLLING and MIST `wind_resistance == 0` (projectile_consts.h:51, 64, 77), so the threshold is 0 and the whole block degenerates to a no-op.

Also in the same function: `projectile_consts::MAX_VELOCITY = {5000, 5000}` (projectile_consts.h:12) is applied as four hand-written clamp ladders (lines 238-245, 265-272) with no explanation of why one ceiling suits every projectile type when their launch speeds differ by an order of magnitude.

Merged from 2 candidate reports (severity downgraded from the reviewers' medium/low split to a single medium).

**Fix:** Compare like with like and only zero the velocity when the drag step would overshoot through zero:
```cpp
const float vx = get_velocity_x();
const float delta = wind_resistance * dt;
if (std::fabs(vx) <= delta) set_velocity_x(0.0f);
else                        alter_velocity_x(vx > 0.0f ? -delta : delta);
```
That removes the magic `4.0f` and the discontinuity. If exponential drag is wanted, `vx *= std::pow(damping, dt)`. Move `MAX_VELOCITY` into `ProjectileDetails` so each type caps itself, and factor the four ladders into one helper.

#### 13. get_col_rect_size() and get_base_size() both return `size` instead of `col_rect_size`

`ArtAttack/Projectile.cpp:290-293` — **medium** · `correctness`

Verified. `Vector2F Projectile::get_col_rect_size() const { return this->get_details().size; }` (Projectile.cpp:290-293) returns the wrong field — `ProjectileDetails` has both `size` and `col_rect_size` (projectile_details.h:14-15). The same confusion is in `DiffusingProjectile::get_base_size()` (Projectile.cpp:56-59), which returns `get_details().size` and is the base that `calculate_diffusion_size()` scales — while `_rectangle` was seeded from `col_rect_size` by both the factory (ProjectileBuilder.cpp:30,48,66,98,134) and every leaf constructor (ProjectileSpray.cpp:25 etc.).

So the diffusion path silently mixes the two fields. It is masked today because every `DETAILS_*` sets `size == col_rect_size` (projectile_consts.h lines 21-22, 34-35, 55-56, 68-69, 81-82, 102-103), i.e. the entire render-size/collision-size split the struct promises is unimplemented. The first time anyone gives a projectile a hitbox different from its sprite — the only reason to have two fields — the collision box is wrong.

`get_col_rect_size()` also has zero callers (grep: declaration Projectile.h:50 + this definition only), so nothing would catch it. It returns by value where the neighbouring accessors return `const Vector2F&`.

Merged from 3 duplicate candidate reports.

**Fix:** Return `col_rect_size` from both. Then decide whether the field earns its place: if projectiles should have a hitbox distinct from their sprite, they need two rectangles kept in sync in `update()` with `get_shape()` returning the collision one; if not, delete `col_rect_size` from `ProjectileDetails` and all six initialisers rather than leaving a trap.

#### 14. Rotation is stored twice, in two bases, with no synchronisation — and rotat_origin is never applied

`ArtAttack/Projectile.cpp:20-22` — **low** · `design`

Verified. The single `rotation` argument seeds two separate members: `MovingObject::_rotation` (MovingObject.h:56, via `MovingObject(velocity, rotation)` at Projectile.cpp:20) and `DrawObject::_draw_rotation` (DrawObject.h:38, via the `AnimationObject` base at Projectile.cpp:21-22). They are read through different accessors (`MovingObject::get_rotation()` vs `DrawObject::get_draw_rotation()`) and written through different mutators, and nothing keeps them equal after construction. `AnimationObject::draw` uses `get_draw_rotation()` (AnimationObject.cpp:39), so any future code that spins a projectile via the `MovingObject` API — the natural choice, since that is where the physics lives — rotates the physics rotation while the sprite stays put.

This is latent today because projectiles are never rotated: both `build_projectiles` call sites (Weapon.cpp:319-327 and :565-573) stop at `resource_manager`, so `rotation` is always the `0.0f` default. Which exposes the related dead-data problem — `DETAILS_JET` sets `rotation_origin::CENTER` (projectile_consts.h:52) and nothing reads `rotat_origin` anywhere, so jets are never oriented along their velocity despite the data saying they should be.

Severity downgraded from the reviewer's medium: the desync is unreachable in the current code.

**Fix:** Pick one owner. Since `MovingObject` owns the physics state, keep `MovingObject::_rotation` and have the draw path read it (or push `get_rotation()` into `set_draw_rotation()` each frame in the base `update()`). Then either implement `rotat_origin` — `MovingObject::get_velocity_angle()` already exists at MovingObject.h:31 — or delete the field from `ProjectileDetails` and all six initialisers.

## `ArtAttack/Save.cpp`

_10 findings: 4 critical, 5 medium, 1 low_

#### 1. Save-file parse writes an 8-byte read into a 1-byte heap allocation and never checks anything

`ArtAttack/Save.cpp:12-32` — **critical** · `memory-safety`

NOTE: outside the platform file list, but this is the first thing `wWinMain` does (Main.cpp:99) so it is a platform-startup defect.

```
FILE* fp = fopen(json_path, "rb");             // NULL never checked
auto read_buffer = std::make_unique<char>();    // ONE byte
FileReadStream is(fp, read_buffer.get(), sizeof(read_buffer)); // sizeof(unique_ptr)==8, not the buffer size
Document d; d.ParseStream(is);                  // HasParseError() never checked
fclose(fp);
read_buffer.release();                          // leaks the allocation
auto resolution = Vector2I(d["resolution"]["x"].GetInt(), ...); // unchecked member access
```
rapidjson is told the buffer is 8 bytes when it is 1 — a guaranteed 7-byte heap overflow on every launch. `read_buffer.release()` then leaks it. A truncated or hand-edited `save_data.json` makes `d["resolution"]` assert/UB. `check_if_save_file_exists()` (Save.cpp:33-42) makes the NULL `fp` unlikely but not impossible (file deleted between the check and the open, or unreadable).

**Fix:** `auto read_buffer = std::make_unique<char[]>(N);` and pass `N`. Check `fp != nullptr` and `d.HasParseError()`, guard every member access with `HasMember`/`IsObject`, drop the `release()`, and fall back to default `SaveData` on any failure instead of propagating.

#### 2. Every JSON file is parsed through a 1-byte heap buffer that rapidjson is told is 8 bytes

`ArtAttack/Save.cpp:14-23` — **critical** · `memory-safety` · confidence: certain

All four JSON loaders in the codebase share this exact block:

```cpp
FILE* fp = fopen(json_path, "rb");
auto read_buffer = std::make_unique<char>();          // allocates ONE char
FileReadStream is(fp, read_buffer.get(), sizeof(read_buffer));  // sizeof(unique_ptr) == 8 (x64)
```

`std::make_unique<char>()` allocates a single byte. `sizeof(read_buffer)` is `sizeof(std::unique_ptr<char>)` — 8 on x64, 4 on Win32 — not the buffer size. rapidjson's `FileReadStream::Read()` (external/rapidjson/include/rapidjson/filereadstream.h:66-80) then does `std::fread(buffer_, 1, bufferSize_, fp_)` followed by `buffer_[readCount_] = '\0'`, i.e. it writes up to 9 bytes into a 1-byte allocation, repeatedly, for the entire length of the file. This is a heap buffer overflow on every asset load in the program. It only appears to work because malloc's minimum bucket happens to absorb it.

Secondarily, `read_buffer.release()` (Save.cpp:23) relinquishes ownership *without* deleting — a leak on every call; the author almost certainly meant nothing at all here.

Identical sites: Save.cpp:14-23, LevelLoadedInfo.cpp:98-107, SoundBank.cpp:152-161, SpriteSheet.cpp:72-81. All four must be fixed; there is no shared helper.

**Fix:** Replace all four copies with one shared helper, e.g. `rapidjson::Document load_json_document(const std::string& path)`, that reads the whole file into a `std::vector<char>` / `std::string` and uses `rapidjson::Document::Parse(text.c_str())` (or `FileReadStream` with a real `std::array<char, 65536>`). Delete the `release()` calls.

#### 3. fopen result never checked in any of the four JSON loaders; NULL FILE* reaches fread in Release builds

`ArtAttack/Save.cpp:14-26` — **critical** · `robustness` · confidence: certain

`FILE* fp = fopen(json_path, "rb");` is used with no null check at Save.cpp:14, LevelLoadedInfo.cpp:98, SoundBank.cpp:152 and SpriteSheet.cpp:72. The only thing standing between a missing file and `std::fread(buf, 1, 8, nullptr)` is `RAPIDJSON_ASSERT(fp_ != 0)` in FileReadStream's constructor — and `RAPIDJSON_ASSERT` is `#define RAPIDJSON_ASSERT(x) assert(x)` (external/rapidjson/include/rapidjson/rapidjson.h:437), which is compiled out under NDEBUG. Release builds therefore call `fread` and then `fclose` on a null FILE*, invoking the MSVC invalid-parameter handler and aborting with no message.

The most likely trigger is not exotic: `Save::load_save_file()` (Save.cpp:43-56) writes a default save when the file is missing, but `write_save_file` (Save.cpp:60) will itself fail if the `save/` *directory* doesn't exist (fopen "wb" does not create directories). It returns false, prints "Save was unsuccessful" to a console that does not exist (see separate finding), and `load_save_file` then unconditionally proceeds to `load_from_json` on the still-missing file. A deployed build without a `save/` folder hard-crashes before the window is created (Main.cpp:99 calls `g_save->load_save_file()` with no try/catch).

**Fix:** Check `fp` and throw a typed exception carrying the path, or return an empty/defaulted result. Wrap the whole startup asset load in Main.cpp in a try/catch that shows a `MessageBoxW` naming the missing file instead of aborting silently.

#### 4. 1-byte rapidjson read buffer declared as 8 bytes: heap overrun on every launch (4 sites)

`ArtAttack/Save.cpp:16-23` — **critical** · `memory-safety` · confidence: certain

`auto read_buffer = std::make_unique<char>(); FileReadStream is(fp, read_buffer.get(), sizeof(read_buffer));`

`make_unique<char>()` allocates exactly **1 byte**. `sizeof(read_buffer)` is `sizeof(std::unique_ptr<char>)` = **8** on x64 (4 on Win32), not the size of the buffer.

What rapidjson does with that (verified in the vendored copy, external/rapidjson/include/rapidjson/filereadstream.h:44-81):
- ctor asserts `bufferSize >= 4` — 8 passes, so the guard never fires (and asserts are off in Release anyway);
- `Read()` line 71: `readCount_ = std::fread(buffer_, 1, bufferSize_, fp_);` → **fread of 8 bytes into a 1-byte heap block**, repeated for every 8-byte chunk of the file;
- line 75-76: on the final short read, `buffer_[readCount_] = '\0'` writes at index up to 8.

So it is a **7-byte heap overrun per refill**, not a one-off. Parsing still *works* (rapidjson walks the buffer one char at a time and refills), which is exactly why the game appears to run: in Release the MSVC small-block heap has ≥16-byte granularity so the extra 7 bytes land in slack. Under the Debug CRT heap the 1-byte block gets 4-byte no-man's-land guards, so the overrun smashes the trailing guard *and* 3 bytes of the adjacent block header.

`read_buffer.release()` (line 23) then abandons the pointer without freeing — a leak, and it also means the corrupted block is never passed to `free()`, so the debug heap's damage check never runs and the corruption stays silent.

REACHABILITY: LIVE ON EVERY LAUNCH, before the window exists. wWinMain (Main.cpp:96-99) → `Save::load_save_file()` (Save.cpp:43-56) → `Save::load_from_json` (Save.cpp:12).

Identical pattern at three more sites, all on the startup path via Game::initialize → ResourceLoader::load_all_resources (Game.cpp:258):
- ArtAttack/SpriteSheet.cpp:74-81 (← ResourceLoader.cpp:122, once per sprite sheet)
- ArtAttack/SoundBank.cpp:154-161 (← ResourceLoader.cpp:164, once per sound bank)
- ArtAttack/LevelLoadedInfo.cpp:100-107 (← LevelLoadedInfo ctor, LevelLoadedInfo.cpp:10, once per level file)

All four also call `fopen` without checking for NULL (Save.cpp:14, SpriteSheet.cpp:72, SoundBank.cpp:152, LevelLoadedInfo.cpp:98); rapidjson's `RAPIDJSON_ASSERT(fp_ != 0)` is a no-op in Release, so a missing asset file is a null-deref inside fread.

**Fix:** Replace all four with a real buffer and RAII file handling, e.g. `char read_buffer[65536]; FILE* fp = fopen(path, "rb"); if (!fp) throw ...; FileReadStream is(fp, read_buffer, sizeof(read_buffer));` and delete the `.release()` calls. Better: factor a single `rapidjson::Document parse_json_file(const char*)` helper into one engine-level file and have Save/SpriteSheet/SoundBank/LevelLoadedInfo all call it — the same 10 lines are copy-pasted four times. Note `sizeof(x)` on a smart pointer is a bug pattern worth grepping for globally.

#### 5. load_save_file detects that writing the default save file failed, prints it, then parses the file anyway

`ArtAttack/Save.cpp:43-56` — **medium** · `robustness`

Merged from 3 candidates.

    void Save::load_save_file()
    {
        if (check_if_save_file_exists()) { std::cout << "Save file exists.\n"; }
        else { std::cout << "Save file does not exist.\n"; this->save_to_file(); }
        this->_save_data = this->load_from_json(SAVE_FILE_PATH.c_str());  // unconditional
    }

`write_save_file` (58-83) correctly returns `false` when `fopen(SAVE_FILE_PATH, "wb")` fails — but `save_to_file` (85-99) is `void` and consumes that bool only to choose which of two `std::cout` messages to print, then returns. Execution falls straight through to `load_from_json` on a file that was just proved absent, which is the unchecked-fopen path from the earlier finding: `fread(buf, 1, 8, nullptr)` and `fclose(nullptr)` in Release.

Reachable in the ordinary case: `directory_consts.h:11` is the CWD-relative `"./save/save_data.json"`, fopen does not create directories, and there is no post-build asset copy step (I grepped the vcxproj — no PostBuildEvent, no Copy/xcopy). This is the very first thing the app does.

One candidate called it "guaranteed access violation on first launch outside the VS debugger" — that overstates it slightly (it depends on the CWD lacking a ./save/ directory), so I downgraded from high to medium.

**Fix:** Make `save_to_file()` return `bool` and propagate it. If the write failed, keep the in-memory `SaveData{}` defaults and return WITHOUT parsing. Null-check every fopen. Write saves atomically (tmp file + rename) so a crash cannot destroy existing settings.

#### 6. The pipeline's only diagnostics are std::cout in a /SUBSYSTEM:WINDOWS app, and one of them prints an errno_t

`ArtAttack/Save.cpp:43-99` — **medium** · `robustness` · confidence: certain

`ArtAttack.vcxproj` sets `<SubSystem>Windows</SubSystem>` in all four configurations and nothing calls `AllocConsole`. The five `std::cout` statements in Save.cpp:47, 51, 90, 93, 97 — "Save file exists", "Save was unsuccessful", etc. — go to a stream with no attached console and are invisible in every build. They are the *only* logging in the entire asset pipeline; there is no OutputDebugString, no log file, no error UI (the two DeviceResources.cpp uses are vendor code).

Line 90 is additionally wrong on its own terms:
```cpp
char buffer[30];
std::cout << ctime_s(buffer, sizeof(buffer), &legacy_start) << " Saving...\n";
```
`ctime_s` returns `errno_t` and writes the timestamp into `buffer`. This prints `0 Saving...` — the intended `buffer` is never streamed.

Net effect: when asset loading fails, the user gets a silent process abort and the developer gets nothing.

**Fix:** Add a minimal logging facility (OutputDebugStringA plus a log file) and route load failures to a `MessageBoxW` naming the failing asset before exit. Fix line 90 to stream `buffer`, or drop `<chrono>`/`ctime_s` entirely.

#### 7. std::cout << ctime_s(...) prints the errno_t return code, not the timestamp

`ArtAttack/Save.cpp:87-90` — **medium** · `correctness`

Merged from 4 candidates — all four found it, and it is exactly as described.

    auto legacy_start = std::chrono::system_clock::to_time_t(start);
    char buffer[30];
    std::cout << ctime_s(buffer, sizeof(buffer), &legacy_start) << " Saving...\n";

`ctime_s` has signature `errno_t ctime_s(char*, size_t, const time_t*)` — it returns an error code and writes the text into `buffer`. This prints `0 Saving...`. `buffer`, the thing that actually holds the timestamp the whole `chrono` dance was set up to produce, is written and never read. The return value is also the only failure signal ctime_s gives, and it is being swallowed into a stream insertion. `30` is a magic number (the documented minimum is 26).

Worth noting the whole logging block is invisible anyway: Main.cpp creates a GUI app with no console, so these `std::cout` diagnostics (Save.cpp:47, 51, 93, 97) go nowhere.

**Fix:** `if (ctime_s(buffer, sizeof(buffer), &legacy_start) == 0) std::cout << buffer << ...;`, or drop the C API for `std::put_time`. Route diagnostics through `OutputDebugStringA` or a real logger rather than `std::cout` from an engine class.

#### 8. Save duplicates ResolutionManager's resolution tables verbatim, and the two halves disagree about failure

`ArtAttack/Save.cpp:112-152` — **medium** · `design`

Merged from 3 candidates, with the line numbers corrected. `Save::convert_ivec_to_resolution` (Save.cpp:112-135) duplicates `ResolutionManager::convert_ivec_to_resolution` (ResolutionManager.cpp:152-175), and `Save::convert_resolution_to_ivec` (Save.cpp:136-152) duplicates `ResolutionManager::convert_resolution_to_ivec` (ResolutionManager.cpp:47-63) — one candidate cited 46-61 for the latter; the correct range is 47-63. Same four hardcoded pairs, same silent fallback to S_1280_720, same `default: return {-1,-1}`.

The cause is visible: both ResolutionManager copies are PRIVATE (ResolutionManager.h:24 `private:`, converters at 27 and 35), so `Save` could not call them and copied them instead. ResolutionManager has two further copies of the same table in `convert_resolution_to_string` (81-88) and `convert_vec_to_resolution` (98-119) — four copies of one table across two files.

The two halves also disagree about failure: reading an unrecognised resolution silently downgrades to 720p with no warning, while writing an unrecognised enum emits `{"x":-1,"y":-1}` into save/save_data.json, which the reader maps back to 720p. A user's resolution can be reset with zero diagnostic.

Both Save copies are non-static `const` member functions (Save.h:34-38) that read no member — they are pure functions on `screen_resolution`.

**Fix:** Delete Save's two copies. Own the table once: a `constexpr` array of `{screen_resolution, w, h, label}` next to the enum with free functions `to_extent` / `from_extent` / `to_string`. Serialise the enum by NAME so an unknown value round-trips as an explicit parse error instead of silently becoming 720p.

#### 9. No version or schema field in save or level data; an unrecognised resolution is silently downgraded and then written back
