```cpp
    SubmitThreadpoolWork(work);
}
```

1. `_work_items.push_back` is an unsynchronised mutation of a `std::vector` member. A task that itself calls `add_task` (the obvious way to express nested/recursive parallelism — which an engine will want) corrupts the vector. Nothing in the header says "call from the owning thread only".
2. If `CreateThreadpoolWork` fails, the `new std::function<void()>(task)` is leaked before the throw. This is one of only three raw `new` sites in the codebase.
3. `task` is taken **by value** and then **copied** into the heap allocation instead of moved — two allocations per task where one would do. `Level::draw_active_level` also captures `partitioned_players` by value into each of up to 4 lambdas every frame (Level.cpp:388), so this is per-frame garbage.
4. `wait_for_tasks_to_complete` (ThreadPool.cpp:50-58) is the only synchronisation point and is an all-or-nothing barrier; there is no per-task handle, so you cannot wait on a subset or overlap CPU work with the wait.
5. If `wait_for_tasks_to_complete` is never called, `_work_items` and the `PTP_WORK` objects grow without bound — the class relies entirely on callers being disciplined.

**Fix:** Take the task by value and `std::move` it into a `std::unique_ptr<std::function<void()>>`; release it into the callback only after `CreateThreadpoolWork` succeeds. Guard `_work_items` with a `std::mutex` (or document single-producer as a hard precondition and assert it). Return a handle/`std::future` from `add_task`.

#### 9. Two heap allocations plus a std::function copy per task, plus a full partition-vector copy per closure, every frame

`ArtAttack/ThreadPool.cpp:38-48` — **medium** · `performance` · confidence: certain

`add_task` takes the closure **by value** and then **copies** it again into the heap:

```cpp
void ThreadPool::add_task(std::function<void()> task)          // :38  copy #1 (caller's lambda -> std::function)
{
    PTP_WORK work = CreateThreadpoolWork(work_callback,
        new std::function<void()>(task), &_callback_environment);  // :41  copy #2, not a move
```

`task` is a by-value parameter and is never used again after line 41, so `std::move(task)` is free and correct; as written every submission does a redundant `std::function` copy, which for a non-SBO-sized closure is an extra allocation on top of the `new`.

The caller makes it worse. `Level::draw_active_level` captures the partition table **by value** into each of up to 16 closures:

```cpp
auto partitioned_players = this->_partitioner->partition(this->_player_objects->size(), num_threads);  // :382
for (int i = 0; i < partitioned_players.size(); i++)
    this->_thread_pool->add_task([this, i, partitioned_players, ...]{ ... });   // :388  full vector copy per task
```

Each copy heap-allocates a `std::vector<std::pair<int,int>>` that every task then indexes at exactly one position, `partitioned_players[i]`. Also note `Partitioner::partition` (Partitioner.cpp:4-22) returns a fresh `std::vector` by value on every call, so the table itself is reallocated every frame even though it only changes when the player count does.

Net cost on the hot path, at 60 Hz: per task, one `CreateThreadpoolWork`, one `new std::function`, one redundant `std::function` copy, and one vector copy — for a workload of at most four players. (`partitioned_players.size()` is also `size_t` compared against `int i` at line 386 — C4018 under the project's /W4.)

**Fix:** `std::move(task)` at line 41. Capture only what each task needs — `int start = partitioned_players[i].first, end = ...;` before the lambda, then capture the two ints by value — instead of the whole vector. Cache the partition table in `Level` and recompute it only when the player count changes. Best of all, replace the per-frame submit/drain with a persistent parallel-for that takes an index range, so no closures are allocated on the render path at all.

#### 10. The pool churns a TP_WORK object plus a heap std::function per task per frame, with one global barrier for the whole engine

`ArtAttack/ThreadPool.cpp:38-58` — **low** · `performance`

Per task: one `new std::function` (copy-constructed from a by-value parameter, so two copies of the captures), the std::function's own internal allocation, and a `CreateThreadpoolWork`/`CloseThreadpoolWork` pair. TP_WORK objects are designed to be created once and re-submitted; here they are created and closed every frame.

Separately, `add_task` pushes into a single shared `std::vector<PTP_WORK> _work_items` and `wait_for_tasks_to_complete()` waits on and closes EVERY outstanding item. There is therefore exactly one task group in the entire engine: two subsystems cannot use the pool concurrently and no caller can wait on just its own work. `get_max_num_threads()` exists purely so callers can size their own partitions and index parallel arrays, which is why `Partitioner` exists as a separate injected service at all.

DOWNGRADED from the reviewers' high. One candidate claimed "2,000-6,000 heap allocations per second". I checked the call sites: `Level::draw_active_level` submits one task per partition, and `Partitioner::partition` is called with the player count (at most 4), so gameplay submits ~4/frame; `MenuPage` submits up to 16/frame; `Level::draw_zoom_out_level` submits exactly 1 (and computes an unused `num_threads` at Level.cpp:599). At 60fps that is roughly 240-960 dispatch allocations/second, not thousands. Real, but an order of magnitude smaller than stated.

**Fix:** Return a `JobHandle` from `dispatch(...)` so callers wait on their own group; keep per-group counters rather than one global vector. Pre-create the TP_WORK objects and re-submit them, and allocate job payloads from a per-frame linear allocator instead of `new std::function`. A `parallel_for(count, [](size_t worker_index, size_t begin, size_t end){...})` API would also absorb Partitioner and own the worker-index-to-deferred-context mapping that three call sites currently duplicate by hand.

## `ArtAttack/Weapon.cpp`

_21 findings: 3 critical, 5 high, 7 medium, 6 low_

#### 1. Weapon::draw mutates shared per-object state and is executed concurrently on several render threads

`ArtAttack/Weapon.cpp:36-82` — **critical** · `memory-safety`

`Weapon::draw` is non-const and writes four members of its own base subobjects before issuing the batch call: `TextureObject::set_element_name(get_details().frame_name)` (Weapon.cpp:61, assigns `SpriteSheetObject::_element_name`, a `std::string` - SpriteSheetObject.h:26), `DrawObject::set_origin`, `set_effects`, `set_draw_rotation` (:62-64), and again in the debug branch (:71-78). `WeaponRoller::draw` additionally writes `_colour` (WeaponRoller.cpp:90-97).

That object is shared across threads. `Level::draw_active_level` (Level.cpp:379-399) partitions the players and submits one `ThreadPool` task per partition; `Partitioner::partition` (Partitioner.cpp:4-22) yields one partition per player while players <= threads, and `ThreadPool` is a real Win32 pool with `SetThreadpoolThreadMaximum(16)` (ThreadPool.cpp:15-18). Each task runs `Level::draw_player_view_level`, which at Level.cpp:534-540 loops over **all** `_player_objects` - so with N players, player 0's `Player::draw` (Player.cpp:47-89) and therefore `this->_primary->draw(...)` is entered by N threads simultaneously. Unsynchronised concurrent write/write on a `std::string` is UB and can tear the pointer/size/capacity triple.

Downstream is worse: `SpriteSheetObject::get_sprite_sheet()` reaches `ResourceManager::get_sprite_sheet`, which is `this->_sprite_sheets[name]` - `std::map::operator[]`, a mutating call - from all those threads at once (ResourceManager.cpp:46-58).

**Fix:** Make drawing a pure read. Compute element name / origin / effects / rotation / colour into locals and pass them as arguments to a `const` `TextureObject::draw(...)`, then declare `Weapon::draw` and the whole `IGameObject::draw` chain `const` so the compiler enforces it. Separately, change `ResourceManager::get_*` and `SpriteSheet::draw` to use `find()`/`at()` so lookups cannot mutate the container. Resolving the `SpriteSheet*` and `SpriteFrame` once at construction removes both the race and the per-frame lookups.

#### 2. stop_sounds() throws for Sniper and Bucket, terminating the process at the end of every round

`ArtAttack/Weapon.cpp:252-277` — **critical** · `correctness`

`Weapon::stop_sounds() const` (Weapon.cpp:252-257) is non-virtual and unconditionally calls `get_sound_effect_instance_name()` (Weapon.cpp:258-277), whose switch handles only SPRAYER, ROLLER and MISTER and ends in `default: throw std::exception("Weapon::get_sound_effect_instance_name() - invalid weapon type")`. SNIPER and BUCKET are buildable (WeaponBuilder.cpp:22, :34) and selectable in the weapon-select menu (MainMenu.cpp:1589, :1601). They dodge the throw during play only because WeaponSniper.cpp:28-35 and WeaponBucket.cpp:28-35 override `handle_shoot_sound` to use `play_wave`; neither overrides `stop_sounds`, which is not virtual anyway. The path is unconditional and hit every match: Level.cpp:135 `this->stop_player_sounds();` on the ACTIVE->ZOOM_OUT transition -> Level.cpp:323-329 loops every player -> Player.cpp:1048-1050 -> `_primary->stop_sounds()`. There is no try/catch anywhere on the tick path (grep of Main.cpp and Game.cpp finds none), so the exception reaches std::terminate. Merged from four independent reports.

**Fix:** Stop keying sound identity off `wep_type`. Resolve the looping instance name (or nullptr/empty for wave-based weapons) once in the Weapon constructor from data in `WeaponDetails`, and make `stop_sounds()` a no-op when there is none. A teardown path must never throw. Adding an explicit SNIPER/BUCKET case plus `virtual stop_sounds()` is the minimum patch, but the data-driven fix removes the whole class of bug.

#### 3. Match end throws an unhandled exception if any player picked Sniper or Bucket

`ArtAttack/Weapon.cpp:252-277` — **critical** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

`Weapon::stop_sounds() const` (252-257) calls `get_sound_effect_instance_name()` (258-277), whose switch only handles `SPRAYER`, `ROLLER`, `MISTER` and ends in `default: throw std::exception("Weapon::get_sound_effect_instance_name() - invalid weapon type");` (273-274).

Can Sniper/Bucket actually be equipped? Yes, three independent ways:
- `MainMenuWeaponSelect::cycle_weapons` (MainMenu.cpp:1524-1554) cycles `0..MAX_PRIM_WEP` where `MAX_PRIM_WEP = RANDOM_PRIMARY = 5` (wep_type.h:4-18), i.e. SPRAYER(0), SNIPER(1), ROLLER(2), MISTER(3), BUCKET(4), RANDOM(5). `update_weapon_select_visuals` (MainMenu.cpp:1585-1608) draws icons for all of them, so they are visibly selectable.
- `get_random_weapon()` (MainMenu.cpp:1519-1523) is `rand() % 5` → picks SNIPER or BUCKET with probability 2/5.
- `WeaponBuilder::build_weapon` (WeaponBuilder.cpp:22-25, 34-37) happily constructs `WeaponSniper` / `WeaponBucket`.

Why it does NOT throw every frame (this matters — an earlier reading implied a broader crash): both classes override the *virtual* `handle_shoot_sound` (WeaponSniper.h:22 / WeaponSniper.cpp:28-35, WeaponBucket.h:23 / WeaponBucket.cpp:28-35) and use `play_wave` directly, bypassing `get_sound_effect_instance_name()`. But `stop_sounds` is declared **non-virtual** at Weapon.h:44, so it is not overridable and always lands in the base version.

REACHABILITY: LIVE, and it fires at exactly the 'match ends' step of a normal session. Shortest chain:
Game::tick (Game.cpp:75) → Game::update → StateContext::update → GameLevel::update → Level::update (Level.cpp:126-135, `_timer <= 0` → ZOOM_OUT) → Level::stop_player_sounds (Level.cpp:323-328) → Player::stop_sounds (Player.cpp:1048-1051) → Weapon::stop_sounds (Weapon.cpp:252) → throw at Weapon.cpp:273.

There is no try/catch anywhere on that path (see the separate finding on Main.cpp:211-224), so this is `std::terminate`.

**Fix:** Two fixes, both needed. (1) Make the sound-name lookup total: give SNIPER and BUCKET entries, or better, put the `SoundEffectInstanceWeaponDetails` on `WeaponDetails` so it is data, not a switch — the switch at Weapon.cpp:264-275 duplicates knowledge the subclass already has. (2) `stop_sounds` must be `virtual` and overridden alongside `handle_shoot_sound` in WeaponSniper/WeaponBucket (which have no looping sound to stop, so their override is empty). The real defect is that one half of a two-method protocol was made virtual and the other half wasn't.

#### 4. _sound_bank comes from a lookup that silently returns nullptr on a bad name and is then dereferenced unguarded every frame

`ArtAttack/Weapon.cpp:32-34` — **high** · `robustness`

```
this->_proj_builder = std::make_unique<ProjectileBuilder>();
this->_sound_bank = resource_manager->get_sound_bank(details.sound_bank_name);
```
Neither `resource_manager` nor the result is checked. `ResourceManager::get_sound_bank` (ResourceManager.cpp:90-101) is `try { return this->_sound_banks[sound_bank_name].get(); } catch (const std::out_of_range&) { ... }`. `std::map::operator[]` **default-inserts a null unique_ptr and never throws out_of_range**, so the catch is dead code, a bad name silently yields `nullptr` and pollutes the map. `_sound_bank` is then dereferenced with no guard at Weapon.cpp:242, :249, :256, WeaponSniper.cpp:32 and WeaponBucket.cpp:32 - a null deref on the first frame the trigger is pressed. `weapon_consts.h` hand-writes `"sound_bank_1"` in six places (:25, :47, :81, :97, :125, :159); one typo becomes a crash with nothing pointing at the cause. The identical `operator[]` pattern is in `get_sprite_sheet` (ResourceManager.cpp:46-58).

**Fix:** Fail loudly at construction: `if (!_sound_bank) throw std::runtime_error("weapon sound bank '" + details.sound_bank_name + "' not loaded");`, and assert `resource_manager != nullptr` on the same line. Independently, `ResourceManager::get_sound_bank`/`get_sprite_sheet` must use `find()`/`at()` so a missing key is reported rather than inserted.

#### 5. Dead players keep firing, burning ammo and looping the shoot sound from the corpse

`ArtAttack/Weapon.cpp:188-235` — **high** · `correctness`

`Level::update_level_logic` (Level.cpp:189-212) calls `object->update_weapon_and_get_projectiles()` for every player unconditionally, and `Player::update_weapon_and_get_projectiles` (Player.cpp:742-750) forwards straight to `_primary->update_and_get_projectiles(get_input(), ...)` with no `player_state` check. `Player::update` (Player.cpp:696-721) only branches ALIVE/DEAD for movement and leaves `_input` untouched while dead. `Player::draw` early-returns when DEAD (Player.cpp:49-52), so the weapon disappears visually while `Weapon::check_if_shooting_and_ammo_update` keeps running: it spends ammo, spawns projectiles from the death position, and `handle_shoot_sound` (Weapon.cpp:231, 236-251) keeps the looping effect playing for the whole respawn delay. `Player::respawn` calls `reset_ammo()` (Player.cpp:1000), which hides the ammo half of the symptom.

**Fix:** Gate it in `Player::update_weapon_and_get_projectiles`: `if (_state != player_state::ALIVE) { _primary->stop_sounds(); return {}; }`. Better for the engine goal, give `Weapon` an explicit `set_active(bool)` so "this weapon should not act this frame" is expressible at the weapon API instead of being every caller's responsibility. Note the `stop_sounds()` call must be made non-throwing first.

#### 6. Looping shoot sound is only ever stopped from inside the per-frame update, so it survives pause and outlives the weapon

`ArtAttack/Weapon.cpp:236-257` — **high** · `resource-lifetime`

`handle_shoot_sound` (Weapon.cpp:236-251) is the only place a looping effect is started or stopped, and its sole call site is Weapon.cpp:231 inside `check_if_shooting_and_ammo_update`. `Weapon` declares no destructor, so the acquired looping `SoundEffectInstance` (owned by the `SoundBank`, which outlives the level) has no automatic release path.

Verified consequences:
- Pause: GameStates.cpp:143-148 sets `game_level_state::PAUSE_MENU`, and the ACTIVE branch (GameStates.cpp:181-185) is the only caller of `_level->update`. Pausing while holding fire leaves the loop running for the duration of the pause menu.
- Teardown: `stop_player_sounds()` has exactly one caller, Level.cpp:135, on the round-timer transition. The pause-menu RESTART and QUIT paths (GameStates.cpp:200-207) and the end-menu paths (GameStates.cpp:248, 258, 268, 278, 286) call only `stop_music()`, then destroy the level and its `Player`s and `Weapon`s. Since the `SoundBank` lives in the `ResourceManager`, the instance keeps looping and the only name that could stop it died with the weapon.

**Fix:** RAII: give `Weapon` a small `ScopedLoopingSound` member that stops in its destructor, so every teardown path releases automatically and `Level::stop_player_sounds` / `Player::stop_sounds` become unnecessary. Add explicit `on_activated()`/`on_deactivated()` lifecycle hooks driven by `GameLevel`'s state transitions rather than inferring audio state as a side effect of the shoot check. The destructor must not throw - fix the SNIPER/BUCKET switch first.

#### 7. Weapon::stop_sounds() throws for Sniper and Bucket — crashes at the end of every match

`ArtAttack/Weapon.cpp:252-276` — **high** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

`Weapon::stop_sounds()` unconditionally resolves a SoundEffectInstance name:

    void Weapon::stop_sounds() const {
        const std::string& sound_name = this->get_sound_effect_instance_name();
        this->_sound_bank->stop_effect(sound_name, true);
    }

and `Weapon::get_sound_effect_instance_name()` (Weapon.cpp:258-276) only handles SPRAYER, ROLLER and MISTER:

    default:
        throw std::exception("Weapon::get_sound_effect_instance_name() - invalid weapon type");

The shipped audio data confirms this is by design for shooting: ArtAttack/sounds/sound_bank_1.json:30-129 declares SoundEffectInstances only for `sprayer_a0..b3`, `roller_a0..b3`, `mister_a0..b3` — 24 instances, none for sniper or bucket (see also ArtAttack/sounds/sound list.txt: "wave single play: sniper, bucket"). `WeaponSniper` and `WeaponBucket` correctly override the *shooting* path (`handle_shoot_sound`, WeaponSniper.cpp:28-35, WeaponBucket.cpp:28-35) to use `play_wave` instead. But `stop_sounds()` is **non-virtual** (ArtAttack/Weapon.h:44) and `get_sound_effect_instance_name()` is non-virtual too (Weapon.h:119), with no override in WeaponSniper.h or WeaponBucket.h.

Reachability: `Level::update` calls `stop_player_sounds()` the frame the match timer expires (ArtAttack/Level.cpp:131-137), which calls `player->stop_sounds()` for every player (Level.cpp:323-329) → `Player::stop_sounds()` → `_primary->stop_sounds()` (Player.cpp:1048-1051, `_primary` is `unique_ptr<Weapon>`, Player.h:142). There is no try/catch anywhere above this — the only 11 catch sites in the codebase are in Level.cpp:727, ResourceLoader.cpp:94, ResourceManager.cpp and SoundBank.cpp; `Main.cpp`/`Game.cpp` have none. So any completed match in which a single player chose Sniper or Bucket terminates the process.

**Fix:** Make `stop_sounds()` virtual and override it in WeaponSniper/WeaponBucket to stop the wave (or do nothing), or better: give `WeaponDetails` an optional instance-name provider so `stop_sounds` is a no-op when the weapon has no instance. The switch-on-wep_type in `get_sound_effect_instance_name` should be data on the weapon, not a hard-coded ladder.

#### 8. The base class switches on wep_type to name sounds, so Weapon knows the full list of its own subclasses

`ArtAttack/Weapon.cpp:258-277` — **high** · `design`

`Weapon::get_sound_effect_instance_name()` is `switch (this->get_type())` returning `SPRAYER_SOUND_DETAILS.get_sound_name(...)` / `ROLLER_...` / `MISTER_...` with a throwing default. This is an enum switch standing in for polymorphism, located *in the base class*: adding a sixth weapon requires editing Weapon.cpp, and two of the five existing subclasses deliberately fall into the throwing default. Meanwhile `WeaponDetails::shoot_sound_name` (WeaponDetails.h:47) is populated for all five weapons but read only by Sniper and Bucket (WeaponSniper.cpp:32, WeaponBucket.cpp:32).

The same shape produces two byte-identical 6-line overrides: `WeaponSniper::handle_shoot_sound` (WeaponSniper.cpp:28-35) and `WeaponBucket::handle_shoot_sound` (WeaponBucket.cpp:28-35) are character-for-character the same. The difference they encode - one-shot crack vs continuous hiss - is a property of the *sound asset*, not of the class. It is also why `_sound_bank` and `_details` had to be made `protected` (Weapon.h:47-48).

**Fix:** Add `enum class shoot_sound_mode { NONE, ONE_SHOT, LOOPED; }` plus the resolved instance name to `WeaponDetails`, implement `handle_shoot_sound` once branching on data, and delete both overrides, the type switch, and the three separate `*_SOUND_DETAILS` tables. `_sound_bank`/`_details` can then go back to private, and `stop_sounds()` becomes total (see the critical finding).

#### 9. check_if_shooting_and_ammo_update: a bool-returning 'check' that mutates four subsystems including audio

`ArtAttack/Weapon.cpp:188-235` — **medium** · `design`

The name promises two responsibilities; the body has four: fire-rate gating and ammo spend (:202-215), ammo regen and timer advance (:218-227), the `_shooting_this_update` flag (:229), and starting/stopping a looping sound effect (:231) - all inside a function whose return value is "did we fire". You cannot ask "can this weapon fire?" without playing a sound, which is exactly why the pause and death paths above leak audio. It also carries a vestigial alias chain `bool normal_gun_ok_to_shoot = ...; bool ok_to_shoot = normal_gun_ok_to_shoot;` (:194-197) and two open-coded clamps written as mutate-then-test through four accessor calls (:209-213, :220-224).

**Fix:** Split into `bool FireControl::try_fire(dt)` (pure timing), `AmmoPool::try_consume(amount)` + `AmmoPool::tick(dt)` (pure arithmetic - and unit-testable in MattMathTests, which none of this currently is), and a `WeaponAudio::on_firing_changed(bool)` driven by the coordinator after the fact. The weapon's `update` becomes four readable calls with no hidden side effects.

#### 10. handle_shoot_sound's two bool arguments are bound in the order opposite to their parameter names

`ArtAttack/Weapon.cpp:229-251` — **medium** · `api-design`

The declaration is `virtual void handle_shoot_sound(bool shooting_this_update, bool holding_shoot)` (Weapon.h:52). The only call site is:
```
this->_shooting_this_update = ok_to_shoot && this->get_ammo() > 0.0f;
this->handle_shoot_sound(result, this->_shooting_this_update);
```
So the parameter named `shooting_this_update` receives `result` (a shot was actually fired) and the parameter named `holding_shoot` receives the member named `_shooting_this_update`. The member is itself misnamed - it means "trigger held and ammo remains", deliberately ignoring the fire-interval gate. Because both arguments are `bool`, a transposition compiles silently, and `WeaponSniper`/`WeaponBucket` branch on the first argument only (WeaponSniper.cpp:30, WeaponBucket.cpp:30) - one "tidy-up" swap would make the sniper fire its wave sound every frame the trigger is held. The same unlabelled-bool problem is in `play_effect(sound_name, true, ...)` (:242, `true` = loop) and `stop_effect(sound_name, true)` (:249, :256, `true` = immediate).

Downstream, `WeaponRoller::draw` tints the roller from `_shooting_this_update` (WeaponRoller.cpp:90), so the roller reads as firing on frames where the interval blocked the shot.

**Fix:** Rename the member to `_trigger_held_with_ammo` and the parameters to `fired_this_update` / `trigger_held`, matching the call site - or better, pass a single `enum class shoot_sound_event { fired, held, idle }` so the impossible `(true, false)` combination cannot be expressed. Use named enums (`sound_loop`, `stop_mode`) for the SoundBank booleans.

#### 11. Shoot sound is re-issued or re-stopped every frame instead of on state change, with a tree lookup and XAudio2 round-trips each time

`ArtAttack/Weapon.cpp:236-251` — **medium** · `performance`

`handle_shoot_sound` is called unconditionally once per weapon per tick (Weapon.cpp:231) and does full work on both branches with no edge detection. Firing branch: `get_sound_effect_instance_name()` runs a switch, then `SoundBank::play_effect` (SoundBank.cpp:29-37) does a `std::map<std::string,...>` lookup keyed on e.g. "sprayer_a0" followed by `SetVolume`, `SetPitch`, `SetPan`, `Play`. Idle branch: `stop_effect` -> `SoundEffectInstance::Stop(true)` (SoundBank.cpp:38-41), which in DirectXTK issues `IXAudio2SourceVoice::Stop` + `FlushSourceBuffers` unconditionally on an already-idle voice, plus the same map lookup. Four idle players cost four map lookups and four XAudio2 stop/flush round-trips every frame, forever. None of it is needed - the instance is fixed for the weapon's whole life.

**Fix:** Resolve and cache the `SoundEffectInstance*` in the constructor, keep a `bool _sound_playing`, and touch the voice only on transitions. Zero lookups, zero redundant XAudio2 calls, and it removes the throwing type switch as a side effect.

#### 12. Weapon audio does a string-keyed map lookup plus SetVolume/SetPitch/SetPan/Play on every update tick

`ArtAttack/Weapon.cpp:236-251` — **medium** · `performance`

void Weapon::handle_shoot_sound(bool shooting_this_update, bool holding_shoot)
    {
        const std::string& sound_name = this->get_sound_effect_instance_name();
        if (holding_shoot || shooting_this_update)
            this->_sound_bank->play_effect(sound_name, true, this->_details.shoot_sound_volume);
        else
            this->_sound_bank->stop_effect(sound_name, true);
    }

Called unconditionally from `Weapon::update` (Weapon.cpp:231) — every tick, for every weapon. `SoundBank::play_effect` (SoundBank.cpp:29-38) then does `_sound_effect_instances.at(name)` over 48 entries, followed by SetVolume/SetPitch/SetPan/Play. None of the three level values change between frames, and re-calling Play on an already-looping instance is pure overhead; the else-branch calls Stop(true) on an already-stopped instance 60 times a second.

Same shape at Level.cpp:171: `stop_effect(this->_music_name, true)` runs on every update while the level sits in `level_state::FINISHED`.

One candidate also claimed Level.cpp:73 plays music every frame — that one is WRONG; it is guarded by a first-update check at Level.cpp:71 (`_start_timer >= START_TIMER`). Corrected here.

**Fix:** Cache the `SoundEffectInstance*` on the Weapon (the name is fixed by team + slot + weapon type, none of which change after construction) and only touch it on a state transition — track the previous shooting state and call Play/Stop only when it flips. Set volume/pitch/pan once at setup.

#### 13. End-of-match sound teardown throws for Sniper/Bucket, and nothing anywhere catches it

`ArtAttack/Weapon.cpp:258-277` — **medium** · `robustness` · confidence: certain

const std::string& Weapon::get_sound_effect_instance_name() const
    {
        switch (type) {
        case wep_type::SPRAYER: ... case wep_type::ROLLER: ... case wep_type::MISTER: ...
        default:
           throw std::exception("Weapon::get_sound_effect_instance_name() - invalid weapon type");
        }
    }

`SNIPER` and `BUCKET` are fully selectable (MainMenu.cpp:1589, 1601) and constructible (WeaponBuilder.cpp:22, 34), and `MainMenuWeaponSelect::get_random_weapon()` — `rand() % static_cast<int>(wep_type::MAX_PRIM_WEP)` = `rand() % 5` (MainMenu.cpp:1519-1523) — rolls uniformly over SPRAYER..BUCKET, so "Random" can hand a player a weapon that throws. `Weapon::handle_shoot_sound` (Weapon.cpp:236-250) and `Weapon::stop_sounds` (252-257) both call it; the latter is invoked at the exact ACTIVE -> ZOOM_OUT transition that ends every match (Level.cpp:135, `this->stop_player_sounds()`).

The process has no exception handler at all around the frame loop:

    // Main.cpp:213-224
    while (WM_QUIT != msg.message) {
        if (PeekMessage(...)) { ... } else { g_game->tick(); }
    }

So any of the ~58 `throw std::exception` sites reachable from the end-of-match path — Weapon.cpp:273, Level.cpp:312/319 (out of bounds), Level.cpp:500/590/616/649 (deferred contexts / FinishCommandList), ViewportManager.cpp:150, MenuPage.cpp:96/120, LevelEndInfo.cpp:77 — terminates the process with no message and no save.

**Fix:** Give `Weapon` a sound name for every `wep_type` (or make the name a field of `WeaponDetails`, which already exists in weapon_consts.h) so teardown cannot throw. Independently, wrap `g_game->tick()` in a try/catch that logs and shows a message box before exiting — right now `/W4` warnings are unenforced (no `TreatWarningAsError`) and there is no crash reporting, so these are invisible until a player hits one. Note also `throw std::exception("literal")` is an MSVC-only extension; use `std::runtime_error`.

#### 14. add_player_velocity::NONE silently falls into the Y_ONLY branch and adds the player's vertical velocity

`ArtAttack/Weapon.cpp:537-548` — **medium** · `correctness`

```
if (add_player_vel == add_player_velocity::X_AND_Y) { result += player_velocity * player_vel_amount; }
else if (add_player_vel == add_player_velocity::X_ONLY) { result.x += player_velocity.x * player_vel_amount; }
else //if (add_player_vel == add_player_velocity::Y_ONLY)
{ result.y += player_velocity.y * player_vel_amount; }
```
`add_player_velocity` has four enumerators (WeaponDetails.h:7-13) - the fourth is `NONE`. A weapon configured with NONE, meaning "do not inherit owner velocity", instead gets the owner's Y velocity added. The commented-out `//if (... == Y_ONLY)` shows the author believed the chain exhaustive. `weapon_consts::DETAILS_RELATIVE_DEFAULT` (weapon_consts.h:30-34) is exactly `{ NONE, 1.0f }` and is the NSDMI of `RelativeVelocityWeapon::_rel_details` (Weapon.h:182). Latent today only because all three live relative weapons pass `X_ONLY` (weapon_consts.h:54, :132, :166) and the NSDMI is always overwritten by the constructor - but the failure would be silent, projectiles just flying at the wrong angle.

**Fix:** Use `switch (add_player_vel)` with an explicit `case add_player_velocity::NONE: break;` and no `default:`, so /W4 C4062 flags the next enumerator added. Same treatment for the other exhaustive-by-assumption chains in the module. The `Vector2F inherit_owner_velocity` redesign removes the branch entirely.

#### 15. RelativeVelocityWeapon duplicates Weapon::shoot and Weapon::update_and_get_projectiles wholesale

`ArtAttack/Weapon.cpp:551-595` — **medium** · `design` · confidence: certain

`RelativeVelocityWeapon::shoot` (Weapon.cpp:551-572) repeats the whole 11-argument `build_projectiles` call from `Weapon::shoot` (Weapon.cpp:311-326); the only difference is which `calculate_projectile_launch_velocity` overload computes the velocity. `RelativeVelocityWeapon::update_and_get_projectiles` (Weapon.cpp:574-595) repeats `Weapon::update_and_get_projectiles` (Weapon.cpp:168-186) verbatim apart from passing `player_velocity` into `shoot`. ~45 duplicated lines — and because the two `shoot`s have different signatures they do not override each other, so the base overload is silently hidden rather than replaced.

**Fix:** Make `update_and_get_projectiles` non-virtual on `Weapon` and give it one virtual extension point: `virtual Vector2F calculate_launch_velocity(const Vector2F& dir, const Vector2F& player_velocity) const`. `RelativeVelocityWeapon` then overrides that one function and both duplicated bodies disappear.

#### 16. Weapon::calculate_sprite_origin is a second copy of Drawer::calculate_sprite_origin

`ArtAttack/Weapon.cpp:88-101` — **low** · `duplication`

`Weapon::calculate_sprite_origin(const Vector2F& size, rotation_origin origin)` (Weapon.cpp:88-101) is the same switch as `Drawer::calculate_sprite_origin` (Drawer.cpp:55-67): `CENTER -> Vector2F(size) / 2.0f`, `LEFT_CENTER -> {0, size.y/2}`, else `Vector2F::ZERO`. The only divergence is that Weapon's version spells out a `TOP_LEFT` case that falls through to the identical `default`. This is a pure engine-level sprite helper forked into a gameplay class, and both copies must be kept in sync with `rotation_origin`, which also has a `NO_ROTATION` value neither handles distinctly.

**Fix:** Hoist to a single free function in the draw module - `namespace sprite { Vector2F origin_for(const Vector2F& size, rotation_origin); }` - and have `Drawer` and the weapon renderer both call it. Handle every `rotation_origin` enumerator explicitly so adding one is a compile error, not a silent ZERO. In an engine-first codebase this clearly belongs in shared engine code.

#### 17. get_draw_pos() and get_wep_rotation_origin_offset() are two hand-maintained copies of the same mirroring rule, and neither mirrors the nozzle

`ArtAttack/Weapon.cpp:118-166` — **low** · `correctness`

`get_draw_pos()` (:118-132) computes `facing_left ? (center.x - offset.x, center.y + offset.y) : center + offset`, and `get_wep_rotation_origin_offset(bool)` (:157-166) returns exactly that same offset as a vector. They are arithmetically identical (verified branch by branch) but written in different styles - mutate-in-place vs construct-and-return - so a reader is unlikely to notice, and they must stay in agreement or projectiles stop leaving the barrel, since `draw` consumes one and `get_nozzle_pos` the other.

Two further issues at the same site. (a) `get_nozzle_pos()` (:146-155) rotates `nozzle_offset` by `_rotation` but never applies `_invert_y`/`_invert_x`, even though `update_movement_and_rotation` sets `_invert_y = true` whenever the gun faces left (:302-310) and `draw` turns that into `SpriteEffects_FlipVertically`. The sprite is mirrored about the barrel axis; the computed muzzle is not. Dormant only because every weapon has `nozzle_offset.y == 0` (weapon_consts.h:40, 74, 90, 118, 152). (b) The parameter `bool facing_left` shadows the static member function `Weapon::facing_left(float)` (Weapon.h:94), so three lines apart the same identifier means two different things (:152 the function, :157 the parameter).

**Fix:** Delete `get_wep_rotation_origin_offset` and implement `get_draw_pos()` as `get_player_center() + <the one offset function>`. Better, give the weapon a single `Transform2D` (position + rotation + flip) that both the renderer and the muzzle query derive from, with an explicit `Vector2F muzzle_local` on the definition independent of sprite size - `_details.size.x` currently leaks art dimensions into where bullets spawn (:149).

#### 18. Every shot heap-allocates a transport vector the caller immediately empties, and the mist path never reserves

`ArtAttack/Weapon.cpp:168-186` — **low** · `performance`

`update_and_get_projectiles` returns `std::vector<std::unique_ptr<ICollisionGameObject>>` by value and both `shoot` implementations build a fresh one per call (Weapon.cpp:313-328, :552-574). The caller does `for (auto& proj : new_projs) this->_collision_objects->push_back(std::move(proj));` (Level.cpp:204-210) and destroys the vector - it exists purely as a transport buffer, allocated and freed 60 times a second per player given `shoot_interval == 0.0f` on the sprayer. Inside, `ProjectileBuilder::build_mist_projectiles` (ProjectileBuilder.cpp:131-201) does five `push_back`s on a default-constructed vector with no `reserve(5)`, so it reallocates at capacities 1->2->4->8: three extra allocations plus three moves per mist shot, 10 shots/second/player. Both `return std::vector<std::unique_ptr<ICollisionGameObject>>();` sites (:184, :593) also spell out the full type where `return {};` says the same thing.

**Fix:** Change the signature to append into a caller-supplied container - `void update_and_append_projectiles(..., std::vector<std::unique_ptr<ICollisionGameObject>>& out)` with `Level` passing `*_collision_objects` - so there is no transport allocation and the projectiles land where they are going in one move. At minimum add `projectiles.reserve(5)` in `build_mist_projectiles`.

#### 19. Cluster of unreferenced parameters through the virtual weapon interface (C4100 noise at /W4)

`ArtAttack/Weapon.cpp:188-192` — **low** · `api-design`

Several signatures advertise dependencies their bodies do not have. With /W4 on and no TreatWarningAsError, these accumulate silently:
- `Weapon::check_if_shooting_and_ammo_update(PlayerInputData input, const Vector2F& player_center, const Vector2F& player_velocity)` (Weapon.cpp:188-235) uses only `input.primary_shoot`; both vectors are never referenced. It has no override anywhere, so these are pure noise - and `RelativeVelocityWeapon` faithfully forwards both (Weapon.cpp:585-586).
- `Weapon::update_movement_and_rotation` (:278-311) never uses `player_velocity`.
- `WeaponRoller::update_movement_and_rotation` (WeaponRoller.cpp:29-57) uses neither `input` nor `player_velocity`.
- `WeaponSniper::handle_shoot_sound` (WeaponSniper.cpp:28-35) and `WeaponBucket::handle_shoot_sound` (WeaponBucket.cpp:28-35) never use `holding_shoot`.

`PlayerInputData` is also taken **by value** at every layer (Weapon.h:36, 106, 110, 164; WeaponRoller.h:23) even though the caller already holds it by reference (`Player::get_input()`). It is ~48 bytes - three `Vector2F`, two floats, seven bools, an enum (PlayerInputData.h:7-23) - copied three times per weapon per tick to read two or three fields.

**Fix:** Delete `player_center`/`player_velocity` from `check_if_shooting_and_ammo_update` outright. For genuinely polymorphic signatures where an override ignores an argument, omit the parameter name (`bool /*holding_shoot*/`) so C4100 is suppressed deliberately. Take input by `const&`, or better by a narrow `WeaponIntent`. Turn on TreatWarningAsError.

#### 20. Max ammo is a bare 1.0f in three places and does not track STARTING_AMMO

`ArtAttack/Weapon.cpp:483-486` — **low** · `correctness`

`weapon_consts::STARTING_AMMO = 1.0f` (weapon_consts.h:11) is used in exactly one place - the NSDMI at Weapon.h:126. The regen clamp writes the literal (`if (this->get_ammo() > 1.0f) { this->set_ammo(1.0f); }`, Weapon.cpp:221-224) and `Weapon::reset_ammo()` writes it again (`this->_ammo = 1.0f;`, :485). There is no `MAX_AMMO` constant at all. Change `STARTING_AMMO` to anything other than 1.0 and weapons spawn with ammo they can never regain, and `reset_ammo()` on respawn (Player.cpp:1000) silently *reduces* a full clip. Three independent spellings of one invariant.

**Fix:** Add `constexpr float MAX_AMMO = 1.0f;` to weapon_consts, clamp against it, and make `reset_ammo()` assign `STARTING_AMMO`. Replace both mutate-then-test clamps with a single `set_ammo(std::clamp(...))` once the project is on C++17.

#### 21. Needless local copies in the per-shot path

`ArtAttack/Weapon.cpp:556-558` — **low** · `performance`

`RelativeVelocityWeapon::shoot` opens with `RelativeWeaponDetails rel_details = this->_rel_details;` (:556) followed by `add_player_velocity add_player_vel = rel_details.add_vel;` (:558) - copying a member inside a `const` function that could read `_rel_details.add_vel` and `_rel_details.player_vel_amount` directly. Similarly `Weapon::calculate_sprite_origin` writes `return Vector2F(size) / 2.0f;` (:93) where `size` is already a `const Vector2F&`, so the explicit `Vector2F(...)` is a redundant copy-construct before the division (the same expression is duplicated in Drawer.cpp:61).

**Fix:** Read the members directly, drop the `Vector2F(...)` wrapper, and use `return {};` for the two empty-vector returns.

## `.gitignore`

_1 finding: 1 high_

#### 1. All audio assets are gitignored, so a fresh clone cannot run the game

`.gitignore:365-368` — **high** · `robustness` · confidence: certain

.gitignore lines 366-368 ignore `*.wav`, `*.xwb` and `*.mp3`. I verified with git ls-files: ArtAttack/sounds tracks only `sound list.txt`, `sound_bank_1.json`, `sound_bank_1/XWBTool.exe`, `sound_bank_1/cmd.txt` and `unused/wave_bank_1.json`. The directory on disk confirms it - ArtAttack/sounds/sound_bank_1/ contains XWBTool.exe and cmd.txt and nothing else. The compiled XACT wave bank the SoundBank loader needs is not in the repository. Since player_consts.h:57-64 names DAMAGE_SOUND/DEATH_SOUND/JUMP_SOUND/RESPAWN_SOUND and Level.h:45-49 names COUNTDOWN_SOUND/ZOOM_OUT_SOUND, and the loader throws on missing resources, the project as cloned cannot start a level. This makes the repo unbuildable-to-runnable for anyone but the author, which for a project meant to demonstrate a reusable engine is the single most damaging piece of repo hygiene here.

**Fix:** Either commit the .xwb wave bank (add `!ArtAttack/sounds/**/*.xwb` and `!ArtAttack/sounds/**/*.wav` negations), or use Git LFS for audio, or add a documented fetch/build step (there is already a cmd.txt next to XWBTool.exe describing the build). Whichever you choose, add a README that says how to get a clone into a runnable state - there is currently no README or LICENSE in the repo at all.

## `ArtAttack/AnimatedSprite.h`

_2 findings: 1 high, 1 medium_

#### 1. AnimatedSprite is entirely dead code and a line-for-line fork of AnimationObject — including both of its bugs

`ArtAttack/AnimatedSprite.h:1-49` — **high** · `dead-code`

A repo-wide grep for the identifier finds it only in its own two files, the two `.vcxproj` entries (lines 182 and 296), and `#include "AnimatedSprite.h"` at AnimationObject.h:5 — and `AnimationObject.cpp` never names the type, so even that include is spurious (it serves only to pull in `SpriteSheet.h` transitively).

It is not merely unused, it is a fork of the class that replaced it. Compare AnimatedSprite.cpp:59-122 with AnimationObject.cpp:81-138: `update`, `reset`, `stop`, `play`, `pause`, `is_paused`, `set_frame_index` are the same algorithm over the same five members, including the same `if`-instead-of-`while` timing bug, the same `reset()`-does-not-clear-`_paused` bug, and the same `throw std::exception("Invalid frame index.")`. Every timing fix has to be made twice and one will be missed.

The galling part is that the dead copy is the better design: it is a *component* you hold, and it caches `SpriteSheet*` + `const AnimationStrip*` at construction (AnimatedSprite.h:43-44) instead of doing two string map lookups per call.

I am rejecting one attached sub-claim: a reviewer flagged `set_animation_strip` (AnimatedSprite.cpp:103-109) not resetting `_frame_index` as a live crash when switching to a shorter strip. The analysis is right but the class is never constructed anywhere, so there is no reachable path.

**Fix:** Two coherent options. (a) Delete AnimatedSprite.h/.cpp and their vcxproj entries, and change AnimationObject.h:5 to include `AnimationStrip.h` directly. (b) Keep it, rename to `SpriteAnimator`, delete `AnimationObject`, and have everything that animates *hold* one — which also removes one arm of the `Player` diamond and the per-frame lookups. Do not leave both.

#### 2. AnimatedSprite is a whole class superseded by AnimationObject and never instantiated

`ArtAttack/AnimatedSprite.h:1-48` — **medium** · `dead-code` · confidence: certain

`AnimatedSprite` (AnimatedSprite.h, 48 lines; AnimatedSprite.cpp, 125 lines) is referenced exactly once outside its own two files: an `#include "AnimatedSprite.h"` at `AnimationObject.h:5` — and `AnimationObject` does not use it. `AnimationObject` (AnimationObject.h:7-56) is a verbatim re-implementation: identical private state (`_frame_index`, `_paused`, `_time_elapsed` vs AnimatedSprite.h:44-47) and an identical method set (`update/reset/stop/play/pause/set_frame_index/is_paused/set_animation_strip*`). Both files are compiled into every build (ArtAttack.vcxproj).

**Fix:** Delete AnimatedSprite.h/.cpp, the include at AnimationObject.h:5, and the vcxproj/filters entries. (Note the newer copy is the worse one — AnimationObject makes the animation state a base-class mixin inherited into Player and Projectile rather than a component; that is a separate design problem.)

## `ArtAttack/CameraTools.cpp`

_2 findings: 1 high, 1 low_

#### 1. Camera scroll border clamps min above max, inverting the dead zone at the shipped default resolution

`ArtAttack/CameraTools.cpp:74-91` — **high** · `correctness`

```
clamp_ref(result.top,    MIN_BORDER_TOP,    viewport_size.y / 2.0f);
clamp_ref(result.bottom, MIN_BORDER_BOTTOM, viewport_size.y / 2.0f);
```
`MattMath::clamp_ref` (MattMath.cpp:49-59) is `if (value < min) value = min; else if (value > max) value = max;` — it never validates `min <= max`, and when they are inverted the MIN wins and the result exceeds the requested maximum.

At the default 1280x720 (ResolutionManager.h:25) with a 2-player layout each viewport is 1280x360 (ViewportManager.cpp:166-180). `MIN_BORDER_TOP = MIN_BORDER_BOTTOM = 250` (CameraTools.h:15,17) but `viewport_size.y / 2 = 180`, so top = 0.2*360 = 72 → 250 and bottom = 0.4*360 = 144 → 250; combined 500 inside a 360px viewport. `calculate_camera` (CameraTools.cpp:19-20) then yields `top_edge = ty + 250` and `bottom_edge = ty + 110` — bottom is 140px ABOVE top, so the `else if (player_center.y > bottom_edge)` branch at :29 is unreachable whenever the first fires and the camera pins the player 250px from the top of a 360px viewport instead of following them.

4-player at 1280x720 gives 640x360 viewports, so BOTH axes break (`MIN_BORDER_LEFT/RIGHT = 400 > 320`). I checked 1920x1080: 2-player (1920x540) gives 500 < 540 and 4-player (960x540) gives 800 < 960 and 500 < 540 — both just fit. So this is specifically the default resolution in every multiplayer layout.

**Fix:** Only apply the pixel floor when it fits: clamp the border to at most `0.45f * viewport_size` AFTER applying the minimum, or drop the absolute pixel minimums entirely and keep only the ratios — resolution-independence is what an engine wants. Separately, `MattMath::clamp`/`clamp_ref` should assert `min <= max` instead of silently picking one.

#### 2. Bounds clamping silently returns an out-of-bounds camera when the viewport is larger than camera_bounds, and ignores camera scale

`ArtAttack/CameraTools.cpp:44-71` — **low** · `correctness`

Two related gaps in the bounds correction. (1) It uses `if (left < bounds.left) ... else if (right > bounds.right)` per axis. When the viewport is larger than `camera_bounds` — a small level, or one player at 3840x2160 — both conditions hold; only the first fires and the returned camera still violates the bounds it was asked to respect, with no assert and no way for the caller to know. `Level::update_level_logic` feeds the result straight into `object->set_camera(camera)` (Level.cpp:196-201).

(2) The rectangle is built from raw `viewport_size` (screen pixels) against `camera_bounds` (world units): `RectangleF(new_cam.translation.x, new_cam.translation.y, viewport_size.x, viewport_size.y)`. `prev_camera.scale` is carried into `new_cam` at :23 but never consulted, so the world extent should be `viewport_size / scale`. Currently harmless because per-player cameras always run at scale 1.0, but it is the mirror of the `* scale` bug in `ViewportManager::get_camera_adjusted_player_viewport_rect` and breaks the moment zoom is added or CameraTools is reused.

**Fix:** Compute `const Vector2F world_size = viewport_size / prev_camera.scale;` once at the top (guarding scale == 0) and use it for both the scroll-border edges and the bounds rectangle. Handle the viewport-larger-than-bounds case explicitly (centre on the bounds) and assert the postcondition.

## `ArtAttack/collision_object_type.h`

_5 findings: 2 high, 3 medium_

#### 1. Collision identity is a cross-product of game class x team x weapon, welded into the engine's collision interface

`ArtAttack/collision_object_type.h:4-29` — **high** · `design`

The enum's 23 enumerators multiply three orthogonal concepts: object kind, team, and weapon — PROJECTILE_SPRAY_TEAM_A/B, PROJECTILE_JET_TEAM_A/B, PROJECTILE_ROLLING_TEAM_A/B, PROJECTILE_BALL_TEAM_A/B, PROJECTILE_MIST_TEAM_A/B, PLAYER_TEAM_A/B, PLAYER_TEAM_A_DEAD/B_DEAD, PAINT_TILE, POWER_UP. This is returned by `ICollisionGameObject::get_collision_object_type()`, so the Splatoon team model and weapon roster live inside the engine's collision interface.

Cost is combinatorial and confirmed at the call sites: a third team or a sixth weapon means editing the enum, all seven predicates in this file, and every consuming ladder — Player::on_collision (Player.cpp:186-244), Player::on_projectile_collision (Player.cpp:645+), Level::count_projectiles (Level.cpp:658-682), PaintTile::on_collision, StructurePaintable::on_collision. None of that is engine work; all of it is forced by an engine-level type.

Given the stated goal (reusable engine, game as proof), this is the clearest instance of the anti-goal.

**Fix:** Engine side: a `CollisionFilter { uint32_t layer; uint32_t mask; }` on ICollisionGameObject plus an opaque game-defined type id. Broad phase rejects by `(a.layer & b.mask) && (b.layer & a.mask)`. Team and weapon become game data on the game's own object types, so "is this an enemy projectile" is one expression evaluated in game code with no engine enum to edit.

#### 2. Collision-type predicates are written and never called, while call sites re-implement them as shadowing locals

`ArtAttack/collision_object_type.h:31-73` — **high** · `dead-code` · confidence: certain

`is_player` (:31), `is_dead_player` (:37), `is_team_a_projectile` (:57) and `is_team_b_projectile` (:66) have **zero** call sites anywhere in ArtAttack/ or MattMathTests/. Only `is_projectile` and `is_structure` are used at all (2 and 2 sites). Worse, the code that should be using them re-implements them by hand and shadows them: `Level.cpp:665-676` declares `bool is_projectile = type == PROJECTILE_SPRAY_TEAM_A || ... || type == PROJECTILE_MIST_TEAM_B;` — a local variable with the same name as the inline function declared in the header the file includes, spelling out the identical 10-term disjunction. The same shadowing pattern appears at `Player.cpp:271-272`, where `bool is_on_ramp = get_move_state() == ON_RAMP_LEFT || ... == ON_RAMP_RIGHT;` shadows the member function `Player::is_on_ramp()` (Player.cpp:1246) and is then never read (a /W4 C4189 unreferenced-local). Team-membership checks are likewise hand-written in `Player::on_collision` (Player.cpp:186-244) and `PaintTile::on_collision` (PaintTile.cpp:114-140) instead of calling `is_team_a_projectile`/`is_team_b_projectile`.

**Fix:** Replace the hand-rolled chains in Level.cpp:658-682, Player.cpp:186-244 and PaintTile.cpp:114-140 with calls to the existing predicates, then delete the shadowing locals. Longer term this whole flat 23-value enum is game logic sitting in an engine interface (ICollisionGameObject.h:12-16) and should be replaced by a type-id + team pair or virtual dispatch.

#### 3. Ramp orientation encoded as a collision category, duplicating what the shape already knows, and half of it is an empty TODO

`ArtAttack/collision_object_type.h:9-10` — **medium** · `design`

STRUCTURE_RAMP_LEFT and STRUCTURE_RAMP_RIGHT encode which way a slope faces as a collision *category*, information the triangle geometry already carries. The duplication then drives control flow: Player::on_structure_ramp_collision (Player.cpp:245-358) branches on the enum to decide which face is a solid wall (the `side_wall_collision` expression at Player.cpp:258-261) — a decision the triangle's edge normals answer directly.

Worse, I confirmed the STRUCTURE_RAMP_LEFT branch is an empty `// TODO` (Player.cpp:273-276) while the RIGHT branch is fully implemented, and the `else` falls through to `throw std::exception("Invalid ramp type.")`. So half the feature does not exist while its enum tag is fully wired through the engine's collision interface, and a left ramp silently does nothing after the enum dispatch.

**Fix:** Delete both enumerators and derive slope handling from the contact normal — a surface whose dot with up falls in the walkable band is a ramp regardless of facing, and arbitrary slopes then work for free. If distinct *material* behaviour is needed (jump-through, ice), that is a surface property on the collider, not a collision category.

#### 4. Seven global predicates form a hand-maintained taxonomy the compiler cannot check; five are dead and one is duplicated verbatim elsewhere

`ArtAttack/collision_object_type.h:31-88` — **medium** · `design`

is_player, is_dead_player, is_projectile, is_team_a_projectile, is_team_b_projectile, is_structure, is_structure_ramp are inline free functions at **global** scope, each a hand-written `||` chain. is_projectile lists ten enumerators; is_team_a_projectile and is_team_b_projectile are the same five-element list with the suffix swapped. There is no COUNT sentinel, no static_assert, and no exhaustive switch, so adding an enumerator compiles cleanly while silently dropping out of every predicate — a new projectile type would pass through paint tiles and never be counted.

A repo-wide grep confirms **five of the seven have zero call sites**: only is_structure (Level.cpp:238, Player.cpp:146) and is_structure_ramp (Player.cpp:197) are used. Meanwhile Level::count_projectiles (Level.cpp:665-675) contains a verbatim ten-term reimplementation of is_projectile, with the local variable named identically to the free function it duplicates. So the logic exists in at least two places and the reusable copy is the dead one.

is_player deliberately excludes PLAYER_TEAM_A_DEAD/B_DEAD — a false-negative waiting to happen for any caller that reads the name as "is this a player", with the distinction invisible at the call site. The enum also carries two undocumented null values, DEFAULT and NONE (lines 27-28), with no stated difference.

**Fix:** Replace Level.cpp:665-675 with `if (is_projectile(type)) count++;`. Put the predicates in a namespace, mark them [[nodiscard]] constexpr, and derive them from a single table with a static_assert on its size so adding an enumerator has exactly one edit site. Rename is_player to is_live_player. Longer term these vanish once kind and team are separate data.

#### 5. is_projectile / is_team_a_projectile predicates exist but four call sites re-inline the 10-way disjunction

`ArtAttack/collision_object_type.h:43-73` — **medium** · `design` · confidence: certain

`collision_object_type.h` already provides `is_projectile` (:43-55), `is_team_a_projectile` (:57-64) and `is_team_b_projectile` (:66-73). They are ignored at every site that needs them:

- `Level::count_projectiles` (Level.cpp:665-675) rewrites the exact body of `is_projectile` into a local `bool is_projectile = ...` — and shadows the function name while doing it.
- `StructurePaintable::on_collision` (StructurePaintable.cpp:68-78) rewrites the same 10-term disjunction as `is_offensive_projectile`.
- `Player::on_collision` (Player.cpp:199-221) rewrites both `is_team_a_projectile` and `is_team_b_projectile` inline.
- `PaintTile::on_collision` (PaintTile.cpp:116-133) rewrites both again to derive `other_team`.

~60 duplicated lines, and each is a place a new projectile type must be added by hand. `PaintTile`'s copy also throws `std::exception("...is not a projectile")` on the miss, so it doubles as a type check.

**Fix:** Replace all four bodies with the existing predicates, and add the one missing helper `player_team projectile_team(collision_object_type)` (returns A/B/NONE) so `PaintTile::on_collision` and `Player::on_collision` stop deriving team from the enum by hand. Better still: put `player_team` and a category tag on the object itself rather than cross-multiplying class × team into a 23-value enum.

## `ArtAttack/CollisionTools.cpp`

_12 findings: 4 high, 6 medium, 2 low_

#### 1. Bisection push-out can silently fail to separate, and resolve_object_collision reports success unconditionally

`ArtAttack/CollisionTools.cpp:32-69, 249-260` — **high** · `correctness`

Three interlocking defects verified in the source:

1. Total reachable displacement is bounded. `move_object_by_direction_relative_to_size` (lines 12-30) offsets by `bounding_box_size * relative_amount` where `relative_amount = 1/1.5^i`, i = 1..40. Sum of (2/3)^i over i≥1 = 2, so the collider can never be pushed further than ~2x its own bounding box, and less in practice because the search alternates direction. Anything penetrating deeper than that stays welded inside the geometry, every frame.

2. Failure is undetectable. `bracket_object_collision`'s only `false` return is `else if (i == 1)` (line 42), which is dead: `resolve_object_collision` already verified `collider->intersects(collidee)` at line 235 and nothing has moved yet, so at i==1 `colliding` is always true. The loop never reports the shapes still overlapping after the last iteration.

3. Even that return value is discarded — line 251 calls `bracket_object_collision_generic(...)` as a statement, and line 260 does `return true;` regardless. Every Player call site ignores the bool anyway (Player.cpp:282-339, 548-573), so a stuck player is indistinguishable from a working one.

**Fix:** Derive the push distance from the actual penetration (MTV), not from the mover's own size. As an interim fix: propagate the bracket's result out of `resolve_object_collision`, and make the bracket return false when the shapes still intersect after the final iteration rather than only at i==1.

#### 2. Collision response is an iterative bisection that mutates geometry; there is no contact/manifold concept anywhere

`ArtAttack/CollisionTools.cpp:32-69, 244-254, 270-281` — **high** · `design`

The entire narrow-phase resolution strategy is a numerical search. `bracket_object_collision_generic` runs BRACKET_ITERATIONS = 40 fixed iterations (CollisionTools.h:7); each iteration performs a full `Shape::intersects` (a switch + `dynamic_cast` double dispatch, MattMath.cpp:119-136, which for the triangle path allocates `std::vector<Segment> edges = triangle.get_edges()` at MattMath.cpp:339), a `pow(ITERATION_POWER, i)` call, and a virtual `get_bounding_box()`. It converges only approximately and never produces an exact contact.

Algorithm selection is a shape_type switch (lines 244-254) with the comment "one or both of the sprites are using pixel collision" — pixel collision does not exist anywhere in this codebase. RECTANGLE_ROTATED, which was added to shape_type and to Shape, silently falls into the 40-iteration branch and nobody had to notice.

Measuring penetration depth reuses the same machinery plus a heap allocation: `calculate_object_collision_depth` (270-281) clones the shape via the virtual `Shape::clone()` and runs the whole search on the clone just to read back `amount`. Player.cpp:576-638 calls that on every diagonal contact and then calls the resolver again, inside Level::update_level_logic's quadratic pair loops.

For a project whose stated goal is a reusable engine, the missing abstraction is the important part: there is no `Contact { normal, penetration, point }` anywhere.

**Fix:** Have the narrow phase return a contact manifold computed analytically (SAT/MTV for convex polygons, centre-distance for circles, closest-point for circle-vs-polygon — EricsonMath already has the closest-point building blocks). Resolution becomes `position += normal * penetration`: O(1), allocation-free, exact. BRACKET_ITERATIONS, ITERATION_POWER, both bracket functions, move_object_by_direction_relative_to_size and calculate_object_collision_depth all disappear.

#### 3. "Collision direction" is a centre-to-centre unit vector, not a surface normal, and callers snap it to eight compass points

`ArtAttack/CollisionTools.cpp:109-134` — **high** · `design`

`shape_shape_collision_direction` is literally `Vector2F::unit_vector(collidee_center - collider_center)` (lines 109-123); `calculate_object_collision_direction` just gates it on `intersects`. Centre-to-centre is the correct contact normal only for two circles. A player standing on a wide platform gets a direction pointing at the platform's centre, potentially far off to one side, not straight down.

Every consumer compensates by quantising. Player::on_structure_ramp_collision does `direction = Vector2F::direction_to_8_cardinal_direction(direction)` (Player.cpp:250) and Player::on_structure_collision is an eight-way if/else ladder over DIRECTION_UP … DIRECTION_DOWN_RIGHT ending in `throw std::exception("Invalid collision direction.")` (Player.cpp:490-526). The real geometry is discarded and replaced by a compass rose, with "not a compass point" made a fatal error thrown from inside the per-frame update loop.

This is why ramps need dedicated enum tags and a bespoke handler instead of falling out of the normal.

**Fix:** Produce a real contact normal from the narrow phase. Game code then classifies with a dot product against its own up-vector and a tunable slope threshold. That removes direction_to_8_cardinal_direction, the eight-branch ladder, the eight on_*_collision methods, and makes arbitrary slopes work by construction.

#### 4. Band cases in calculate_object_collision_direction_by_edge resolve on the wrong axis

`ArtAttack/CollisionTools.cpp:176-187` — **high** · `correctness`

Reaching line 176 requires `left_edge && right_edge && !top_edge && !bottom_edge` (I traced all five preceding branches: 152, 156, 161, 166, 171 — none fire in that state). That state means the collidee's AABB crosses both *vertical* edges of the collider but neither horizontal edge, i.e. a horizontal slab strictly inside the collider's y-range. It spans the collider completely in x, so no horizontal displacement can ever separate them — the only meaningful axis is vertical. The code returns `compare_point_collision_depth_horizontal(...)` → LEFT/RIGHT. Line 182 is the exact mirror (vertical slab, must resolve horizontally) and returns UP/DOWN.

Reachable when a platform is thinner than the player and the player has penetrated far enough that its bottom edge is below the platform's bottom — the thin-platform / fast-fall case. Player::on_structure_collision (Player.cpp:488ff) then dispatches on_left/on_right, zeroing velocity_x and shoving the player sideways instead of landing it.

**Fix:** Swap the two helper calls: `left_edge && right_edge` must use `compare_point_collision_depth_vertical`, `top_edge && bottom_edge` must use `compare_point_collision_depth_horizontal`. Add unit tests for both band cases — MattMathTests/CollisionToolsTests.cpp has none.

#### 5. calculate_containing_collision_direction picks the axis opposite to the one its own comment describes

`ArtAttack/CollisionTools.cpp:91-107` — **medium** · `correctness`

```cpp
// calculate the direction of the greatest distance between the two shapes
float x_distance = collider_center.x - collidee_center.x;
float y_distance = collider_center.y - collidee_center.y;
if (std::abs(x_distance) < std::abs(y_distance))
{
	return compare_point_collision_depth_horizontal(collider_center, collidee_center);
}
return compare_point_collision_depth_vertical(collider_center, collidee_center);
```
When |dx| < |dy| the dominant separation is vertical, so by the stated intent the vertical helper belongs here — the branches are inverted. Two shapes whose centres are separated almost entirely in y are reported as a left/right collision. This is the fallback for both the full-containment case (line 154) and the catch-all at line 206 (collider contains collidee, which reaches 206 with all four edge flags false).

The variables are also misnamed: `x_distance`/`y_distance` are signed deltas whose signs are never used.

**Fix:** Invert the comparison to `>` (or swap the two returns), rename to x_delta/y_delta, and add a CollisionToolsTests case for the containment path — the existing tests only cover partial overlaps.

#### 6. Vector2F::ZERO is overloaded as both "no collision" and a legal direction, and exactly-concentric shapes throw

`ArtAttack/CollisionTools.cpp:109-123, 231-239` — **medium** · `correctness`

`shape_shape_collision_direction` returns ZERO when the two centres coincide (lines 117-120); `calculate_object_collision_direction` returns ZERO to mean "not colliding" (line 130). Callers cannot tell them apart.

Consequences verified in the source:
- `resolve_object_collision` (line 235) treats ZERO as no-collision, sets `amount = ZERO`, returns false — so two exactly concentric shapes (a maximally deep overlap) are never separated.
- Player::on_structure_ramp_collision has an explicit `else if (direction == Vector2F::ZERO) { throw std::exception("No collision direction."); }` (Player.cpp:346-349), so a projectile spawning exactly at a ramp's centre takes down the process.

The comparison is exact float equality under /fp:fast (confirmed FloatingPointModel=Fast in all four ArtAttack configurations), while `MattMath::are_equal(a, b, epsilon)` (MattMath.h:59) already exists and is not used here.

**Fix:** Signal failure out of band (bool return + out-param, or std::optional once the standard is bumped) instead of encoding it in the value. For the concentric case pick a deterministic fallback axis rather than reporting no collision.

#### 7. The same narrow-phase intersection test runs three times per colliding pair before any resolution, and each pair is processed twice per frame

`ArtAttack/CollisionTools.cpp:125-134, 231-239` — **medium** · `performance`

For one player-vs-object contact I traced four full `intersects` evaluations before the bracket even starts: Player::is_colliding (Player.cpp:148-185), then `calculate_object_collision_direction`'s guard (CollisionTools.cpp:128), then `resolve_object_collision`'s guard (line 235), then 40 more inside the bracket. Each is a virtual call plus a `dynamic_cast` (MattMath.cpp:119-136) plus, for triangle/quad/rotated-rect, a `std::vector` allocation (MattMath.cpp:339).

On top of that, Level::update_level_logic processes every player↔collision-object pair twice: once in the player loop (Level.cpp:222-241, calling both `player->on_collision` and `other_object->on_collision`) and again in the collision-object loop (Level.cpp:258-273, calling the same two in the other order). The collision-object↔collision-object loop (Level.cpp:275-293) likewise iterates both orderings with only an `object == object_2` self-guard, no i<j.

The redundancy is structural: each function is written to be independently safe, so none can trust its caller.

**Fix:** Produce a contact once in the broad/narrow phase and thread it through on_collision, and dedup pairs so each is resolved exactly once per frame.

#### 8. calculate_object_collision_direction_by_edge never tests intersection, contradicting its documented contract

`ArtAttack/CollisionTools.cpp:136-207` — **medium** · `correctness`

CollisionTools.h:32-33 states "If the objects are not colliding, a zero vector is returned." The implementation never calls `intersects` and has no path returning `Vector2F::ZERO`: for two disjoint shapes all four edge flags are false, every branch falls through, and line 206 returns `calculate_containing_collision_direction(...)`, which always yields one of UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT. A non-collision is reported as a confident direction.

The sibling `calculate_object_collision_direction` (125-134) *does* guard with `if (!collider->intersects(collidee)) return Vector2F::ZERO;`, so two functions documented identically behave differently.

Note the trap for whoever fixes this: Player::on_structure_collision's dispatcher ends with `throw std::exception("Invalid collision direction.")` (Player.cpp:523-526), so making the function honour its own docs would turn a silent phantom resolution into an uncaught exception from the update loop. Both sides need fixing together.

Also: the comment at line 152, "collidee is equal size of collider", is wrong — all four collider edges intersecting means the collidee *contains* the collider.

**Fix:** Add the intersection precondition, and simultaneously change Player's dispatcher to treat ZERO as "no collision, do nothing" rather than throwing. Throwing from a per-frame collision handler is not a recoverable design.

#### 9. std::max over signed direction components inverts the push-out for the up-left quadrant only

`ArtAttack/CollisionTools.cpp:219-228` — **medium** · `correctness`

```cpp
if (collision_direction.x != 0.0f && collision_direction.y != 0.0f)
{
	float larger = std::max(collision_direction.x, collision_direction.y);
	direction = collision_direction / larger;
}
collider->offset(opposite_direction(direction) * amount);
```
The intent is clearly "rescale so the dominant component becomes 1", which needs max of *magnitudes*. I worked all four diagonals: UP_RIGHT (0.707,-0.707) → push (-w,+h), correct; DOWN_LEFT → (+w,-h), correct; DOWN_RIGHT → (-w,-h), correct; UP_LEFT (-0.707,-0.707) → `larger = -0.707`, `direction = (1,1)`, push `(-w,-h)` — up and left, i.e. *deeper into* the collidee. Only that one quadrant is wrong. For non-45° directions the divisor can also be the smaller magnitude, over-scaling the displacement.

Separately, after the division `direction` is (±1,±1), so the offset applies the full `inter.width` **and** the full `inter.height` — every diagonal contact is over-resolved on both axes rather than displaced along the axis of least penetration.

CORRECTION to several reviewers: they claimed this wrongly drives Player's branch choice and shoves the player deeper. It does not. The only live path that passes a diagonal is `calculate_object_collision_depth`, which operates on a `clone()` (line 275) and whose caller only reads `amount.abs_x_greater_than_y()` — sign-insensitive. Every direct `resolve_object_collision` call in Player.cpp passes a cardinal direction, where the `x != 0 && y != 0` guard skips the bug. So this is currently a latent defect in a public engine API, not an observable gameplay bug — hence medium, not critical.

**Fix:** `float larger = std::max(std::abs(d.x), std::abs(d.y));` with an epsilon guard rather than `!= 0.0f` (exact float comparison under /fp:fast). Better: replace the whole routine with an MTV that picks the axis of smaller overlap and displaces only on it, which makes both defects unrepresentable.

#### 10. calculate_object_collision_depth heap-clones a polymorphic shape and runs the full resolver to answer one comparison

`ArtAttack/CollisionTools.cpp:270-281` — **medium** · `performance`

```cpp
std::unique_ptr<Shape> collider_copy = collider->clone();
Vector2F amount;
resolve_object_collision(collider_copy.get(), collidee, collision_direction, amount);
return amount;
```
`Shape::clone()` is virtual returning `unique_ptr` (MattMath.h:85), so this is an allocate + vtable dispatch + free per query — and for RectangleRotated a second allocation, since it stores its corners in a `std::vector<Point2F>` member. Player calls it on every diagonal contact (Player.cpp:578, 592, 610, 628), inside the quadratic pair loops of Level::update_level_logic (Level.cpp:180-300).

What it costs versus what it produces: the callers use the result only for `amount.abs_x_greater_than_y()` — one boolean — and then call `on_top_collision`/`on_left_collision`, which run `resolve_object_collision` a second time. For two rectangles that boolean is four subtractions from `RectangleF::intersection`, which `resolve_object_AABB_collision` already computes at line 214.

The inner bool return is also discarded, so a genuinely non-colliding pair returns a zero vector indistinguishable from a zero-depth touch.

**Fix:** Special-case RECTANGLE/RECTANGLE to `RectangleF::intersection` and skip the clone entirely — that covers the dominant player-vs-structure case. Long term, return depth from the narrow phase so direction, depth and resolution all come from one query per pair per frame.

#### 11. bracket_object_collision: leading bool parameter, magic i==1 sentinel, and per-iteration pow()

`ArtAttack/CollisionTools.cpp:32-53` — **low** · `design`

`bool bracket_object_collision(bool colliding, int i, Shape* collider, const Vector2F& collider_direction)` — the sole caller computes the flag inline (line 62), so the call reads `bracket_object_collision(collider->intersects(collidee), i, collider, dir)` with no indication of what the leading boolean means. The returned bool means "keep going", not "collided": two booleans with opposite senses in one 20-line function. `else if (i == 1)` encodes "first iteration" as a magic loop index (and is unreachable — see the bracket-failure finding).

Lines 40 and 50 call unqualified `pow(ITERATION_POWER, static_cast<float>(i))` — relying on `<math.h>` dumping `::pow` into the global namespace via pch.h rather than `std::pow` — once per iteration, where a running multiply by 1/1.5f would do. (Correcting one reviewer: it is 40 pow calls per resolution, not 80 — only one branch executes per iteration.)

**Fix:** Fold the step function into the loop: hoist the first-iteration early-out above it, then `float step = 1.0f; for (...) { step /= ITERATION_POWER; ... }` — no bool parameter, no i==1 sentinel, no pow.

#### 12. Two dead `collider_aabb` locals, one inside the 40-iteration loop

`ArtAttack/CollisionTools.cpp:35, 58` — **low** · `performance`

`bracket_object_collision` (line 35) and `bracket_object_collision_generic` (line 58) both open with `RectangleF collider_aabb = collider->get_bounding_box();` and never read the variable. Line 35 is inside the function invoked once per bracket iteration, so it is 40 discarded virtual `get_bounding_box()` calls per resolution — and for RectangleRotated that call walks four stored points.

These are C4189 under /W4, which the project sets (WarningLevel=Level4 in all four configs) — but `TreatWarningAsError` appears in neither ArtAttack.vcxproj nor MattMathTests.vcxproj, so the warning has simply been ignored.

**Fix:** Delete both lines. Turn on TreatWarningAsError (or at least /we4189 /we4100 /we4018) so dead locals in hot loops surface at build time.

## `ArtAttack/Colour.h`

_10 findings: 4 high, 6 medium_

#### 1. Colour.h contains no Colour type - only `namespace colour_consts` - and breaks the file-naming rule it sits next to

`ArtAttack/Colour.h:1-469` — **high** · `naming` · confidence: certain

`Colour.h` is 469 lines and its only top-level declaration is `namespace colour_consts` (line 6) holding 149 hex strings and ~153 `MattMath::Colour` objects. The `Colour` struct itself lives in `MattMath.h:586-645`. So `#include "Colour.h"` reads as "give me the Colour type" and gives you constants instead. Meanwhile every other constants-only header in the repo is snake_case and named `*_consts.h`: `directory_consts.h`, `player_consts.h`, `weapon_consts.h`, `projectile_consts.h`. `Colour.h` is the sole PascalCase constants file.

**Fix:** Rename the file to `colour_consts.h` to match its four siblings and its own namespace. Update the ~20 includes. This also removes the ambiguity that produced the case-mismatched `#include "colour.h"` sites (see separate finding).

#### 2. 302 internal-linkage objects defined in a header, every Colour constructed by parsing a hex string at static-init time

`ArtAttack/Colour.h:10-313` — **high** · `performance`

Verified by count: 149 `const std::string` in `colour_consts::html` (lines 10-157) and 153 `const MattMath::Colour` (160-313), all at namespace scope in a header. Namespace-scope `const` has internal linkage, so each including TU gets its own copy and its own dynamic initialisers. Each Colour runs `Colour(const std::string&)` -> `set_from_hex` (MattMath.cpp:2359-2384), which does three or four `hex.substr()` allocations plus `std::stoi(..., 16)` calls — thousands of runtime hex parses before `main` to reproduce compile-time constants.

Correction to the reviewers: they claimed 58 of 81 TUs. I measured 14 files that reference Colour.h directly (DrawObject.h, Level.h, LevelBuilder.h, LevelEndInfo.h, MenuHighlight.h, PaintTile.h, PlayerBuilder.h, player_consts.h, ResultsMenu.h, SpriteSheet.h, StructurePaintable.h, TeamColour.cpp, ViewportManager.h, Weapon.h). The transitive fan-out through DrawObject.h/SpriteSheet.h is large but I did not verify 58, so treat the multiplier as 'most of the drawable hierarchy', not a measured 58.

Real secondary hazard, verified: `std::stoi` throws `std::invalid_argument` on a non-hex digit, and `set_from_hex` has no digit validation. A typo in any of the 149 literals throws out of a namespace-scope dynamic initialiser, which calls std::terminate before main with no attributable diagnostic.

**Fix:** Give Colour a constexpr constructor and define the palette as `inline constexpr Colour ALICE_BLUE{0.941f, 0.973f, 1.0f, 1.0f};` (C++17). That removes the duplication, the pre-main parsing and the terminate risk in one change, and deletes the parallel `html::` string table whose only purpose is to be parsed back into the same numbers. Requires setting <LanguageStandard> in the vcxproj, which is currently unset.

#### 3. Colour.h duplicates 302 dynamically-initialised const objects and a 152-line function into each of 58 TUs

`ArtAttack/Colour.h:10-157,160-307,315-466` — **high** · `performance` · confidence: certain

Colour.h declares 149 `const std::string` at namespace scope (lines 10-157) and 153 `const MattMath::Colour` constructed from those strings (lines 160-307), then a `static MattMath::Colour colour_from_name(const std::string& name)` (lines 315-466) that is a 150-branch chain of `if (name == "ALICE_BLUE") return ...`. Namespace-scope `const` gives internal linkage in C++, and `static` on the function does too, so every including TU gets its own private copy: 149 std::string constructions + 153 Colour constructions running before main() and 302 destructor registrations at exit, plus a full codegen of the 152-line function. I measured Colour.h reaching 58 of 81 TUs, so that is roughly 17,500 duplicated dynamically-initialised objects and 58 copies of the lookup function in the binary. The pattern is repeated across the codebase - I counted ~780 namespace-scope const non-literal objects in 55 headers, concentrated in Colour.h (301), MainMenu.h (53), Weapon.h (28), ResultsMenu.h (25), InterfaceGameplay.h (24), PauseMenu.h (22), player_consts.h (22), Mh.h (21), EndMenu.h (20), Level.h:33-49 and directory_consts.h:9-13. Note directory_consts.h spells it `const static std::string` while Colour.h spells it `const std::string` - the same thing, written two ways.

**Fix:** With C++17 (see the LanguageStandard finding) these become `inline constexpr std::string_view` for the hex literals and `inline constexpr Colour` for the colours - one object, external linkage, zero dynamic init. colour_from_name should move to Colour.cpp as a single non-inline function backed by a static sorted table or a constexpr map, not 150 string compares. The string-keyed colour lookup is itself a smell worth removing.

#### 4. Splatoon team colours are baked into the engine's colour palette header

`ArtAttack/Colour.h:309-313` — **high** · `design`

Verified. `const MattMath::Colour TEAM_BLUE = { 6, 52, 204, 255 };` plus TEAM_YELLOW, TEAM_ORANGE, TEAM_PINK, TEAM_GREEN sit in `colour_consts` immediately after the 149 HTML colours, and are consumed by TeamColour.h to build the team pairings. Any project reusing this engine inherits ArtAttack's team palette in its core colour header — a direct hit on the stated engine-first goal.

Also verified: these five are the only constants in the file that use the `Colour(int,int,int,int)` 0-255 path; every other one goes through the hex-string constructor. Two construction paths in one file, differing only by literal type (see the Colour-constructor-overlap finding).

**Fix:** Move TEAM_* into the game layer next to TeamColour.h (e.g. game/team_palette.h), leaving colour_consts with only standard named colours. The engine should have no concept of 'teams'.
