`ArtAttack/MainMenu.cpp:135-136` — **low** · `robustness`

Every highlight-driven page starts with `std::string highlighted_element = this->get_highlighted_widget()->get_name();` — MainMenu.cpp:135-136, 304-305, 649-650, 884-885; PauseMenu.cpp:50-51, 219-220; EndMenu.cpp:29-30. `MenuHighlight::_highlighted_widget` defaults to `nullptr` (MenuHighlight.h:27), and the class's own `highlight_widget`/`unhighlight_widget` (MenuHighlight.cpp:6-22) both begin with `if (widget == nullptr) return;` — so the author knew it could be null. `get_highlighted_widget()` returns it raw and every caller dereferences it. The only thing preventing a crash is that each `init()` remembers to call `set_highlighted_widget` (MainMenu.cpp:274, 564, 855, 1122; PauseMenu.cpp:174, 330; EndMenu.cpp:210). A new page that forgets, or an `update()` that runs before `init()`, is an immediate null dereference.

**Fix:** Bind the highlight in the `MenuHighlight` constructor or assert it on entry to `update()`. Better, replace the stringly-typed identity with an ordered item list plus index so there is no pointer to be null.

#### 27. Applying options rewrites the whole save file twice and swallows the failure

`ArtAttack/MainMenu.cpp:329-343` — **low** · `robustness`

```cpp
this->get_save()->set_resolution_and_save(this->_resolution_selection);   // line 329
...
this->get_save()->set_full_screen_and_save(fs);                           // line 343
```
Each performs a complete `fopen("wb")` + RapidJSON serialise + `fclose` of the whole save file (Save.cpp:58-83, 101-111), so one Apply truncates and rewrites the file twice; between the two writes the on-disk state is inconsistent (new resolution, old fullscreen flag). The failure path is invisible: `Save::save_to_file()` returns `void` and only `std::cout`s "Save was unsuccessful." (Save.cpp:94-96), which goes nowhere in a `wWinMain` GUI app. The menu then changes the window and the in-memory resolution regardless, so the user sees the setting applied and finds it reverted on next launch with no explanation.

**Fix:** Add a `Save::set_resolution_and_fullscreen(...)` that mutates both fields and writes once, returning a `bool` the menu checks — on failure, revert the in-memory selection and surface an on-screen message. Write to a temp file and rename for atomicity.

#### 28. UI logic branches on opaque string literals "dm"/"tdm" while their siblings are spelled out - and `menu_element` exists but is bypassed

`ArtAttack/MainMenu.cpp:663-733` — **low** · `naming` · confidence: certain

`MainMenu.cpp:663-733` and the widget-name array at `:787-817` identify game modes as `"standard"`, `"tdm"`, `"dm"`, `"practice"` - two spelled out, two reduced to initialisms, in the same if/else ladder (`if (highlighted_element == "standard") ... else if (highlighted_element == "tdm") ... else if (highlighted_element == "dm")`). Nothing in the file expands them. Meanwhile `menu_element.h:14-17` already defines `MAIN_MENU_STANDARD_MODE`, `MAIN_MENU_TEAM_DEATHMATCH`, `MAIN_MENU_DEATHMATCH`, `MAIN_MENU_PRACTICE`, and `MainMenu.cpp:744-753 convert_mode_to_element` converts to them - so the typed enum exists and the comparison logic ignores it in favour of string literals. `MainMenu.cpp:1927` also references widget `"stage_test_1"`, whose level file lives in `levels/unused/test_1.json`.
The `menu_element` enum itself is only half-populated: it has `MAIN_MENU_*` and `PAUSE_MENU_*` prefixes but no entries for the Results or End menus, which exist (`ResultsMenu.h`, `EndMenu.h`) and drive their own string comparisons.

**Fix:** At minimum rename the literals to `"team_deathmatch"` / `"deathmatch"`. Better: finish the job `menu_element` started - key widgets by the enum, add `RESULTS_MENU_*` and `END_MENU_*` entries, and delete the string comparisons (there are ~51 of them per the module recon). A reusable menu system cannot be built on ad-hoc string identity.

#### 29. all_players_confirmed() is vacuously true when player_count is 0

`ArtAttack/MainMenu.cpp:1236-1246` — **low** · `correctness`

`for (int i = 0; i < get_player_count(); i++) { if (...) return false; } return true;` returns true when the count is zero. `MainMenuTeamSelect::update` checks it every frame regardless of whether any input arrived (1215-1222), so a zero-player page would transition to `MainMenuWeaponSelect` on its first update; `MainMenuWeaponSelect::all_players_confirmed()` (1555-1565) has the identical shape and would immediately advance to `MainMenuStageSelect`, whose input loop `for (int i = 0; i < num_inputs && i < player_count; i++)` (1790) never executes with `player_count == 0`, leaving a stage-select screen that ignores all input. `MenuLevelSettings` default-constructs with `_player_count = 0` (MenuLevelSettings.h:34) and `GameStates.cpp:206-208` and `284-286` both build `settings.settings = MenuLevelSettings()`. Not reachable today because both of those pair it with `main_menu_screen::HOME`, but nothing in `GameMenu::init` (GameStates.cpp:19-62) checks that a TEAM_SELECT/WEAPON_SELECT entry point comes with a non-zero player count.

**Fix:** Guard the transition on `get_player_count() > 0 && all_players_confirmed()`, and have `GameMenu::init` assert/reject a mid-way screen whose `MenuLevelSettings` has no players.

#### 30. Select pages rebuild every widget's frame, colour and text from string literals every frame

`ArtAttack/MainMenu.cpp:1258-1309, 1577-1636, 1852-1891` — **low** · `performance`

`MainMenuTeamSelect::update()` ends with an unconditional `update_team_select_visuals()` (1223), which first calls `deselect_and_unconfirm_all_widgets()` (1291-1309) to set all three frames and three colours per player, then immediately overwrites one of them (1262-1289). `set_sprite_frame` takes `const std::string&`, so every literal materialises a temporary `std::string`; `"team_select_center"` (18 chars), `"team_select_a_selected"` (22) and `"team_select_center_selected"` (27) all exceed MSVC's 15-char SSO buffer, so each is a malloc/free pair. That is roughly two dozen string constructions per frame for state that only changes on a button press. `get_player_count()` is also re-evaluated as the loop condition and chains three pointer hops (MainMenu.cpp:22-26) per iteration. Same pattern in `update_weapon_select_visuals` (1577-1626, called unconditionally at 1509) and `update_stage_select_visuals` (1852-1883, called at 1845). Compounding it, `weapon_description(wep_type)` (1736-1755) returns `std::string` **by value** from 70-100 character `const static std::string` constants (MainMenu.h:84-89), and `update_weapon_select_visuals` calls it per player per frame (1623-1624) then copy-assigns into the widget via `TextObject::set_text` (TextObject.cpp:80-82).

**Fix:** Make the visual refresh event-driven — only call `update_*_visuals()` when a select state actually changed this frame. Return `const std::string&`/`const char*` from `weapon_description`, hoist `int player_count = get_player_count();` out of the loop conditions, and store the descriptions in a `constexpr const char*` table instead of dynamically-initialised namespace-scope strings.

#### 31. Unguarded pointer from an enum switch with no default in update_team_select_visuals

`ArtAttack/MainMenu.cpp:1264-1288` — **low** · `robustness`

```cpp
MWidget* selected_widget = nullptr;
switch (this->_select_states[i].team) {
case player_team::A:      ... selected_widget = _player_widgets[i]->player_a.get(); break;
case player_team::NONE:   ... selected_widget = _player_widgets[i]->player_center.get(); break;
case player_team::B:      ... selected_widget = _player_widgets[i]->player_b.get(); break;
}
if (_select_states[i].state == confirmation_state::CONFIRMED) { selected_widget->set_colour(...); }
```
No `default:` and no null check before the dereference at line 1286. Safe today only because `player_team` (player_team.h) has exactly those three enumerators. Adding a fourth — a spectator team, an unassigned sentinel — produces a null dereference with no compiler diagnostic that anyone will see: MSVC's C4062 is a /W4 warning and the project sets `WarningLevel Level4` but no `TreatWarningAsError` in any of its four configurations. The sibling functions `update_weapon_select_visuals` (1609-1612) and `update_stage_select_visuals` (1874-1877) both DO have `default:` branches setting an error frame, so this is an inconsistency, not a deliberate choice.

**Fix:** Add `default: selected_widget = nullptr; break;` plus a guard before the `set_colour`, matching the error-frame handling the two sibling functions already use.

#### 32. Select-page widgets are built with hardcoded placeholder content even though the loaded selection is known one line earlier

`ArtAttack/MainMenu.cpp:1692-1720, 1358-1391` — **low** · `correctness`

`MainMenuWeaponSelect::init()` reads the persisted selection at 1675 (`state.type = get_level_settings()->get_player_weapon(i)`) and then builds all three widgets against a hardcoded Sprayer: `set_sprite_frame("sprayer")` (1695), `"Sprayer"` (1702), `weapon_description(wep_type::SPRAYER)` (1713). The correct values come from `update_weapon_select_visuals()` (1577-1626), which `init()` never calls. It is masked only because `StateContext::update()` runs before `draw()` and `update()` ends by calling `update_weapon_select_visuals()` (1509) — a coincidence of frame ordering, not a design. `MainMenuTeamSelect::init()` has the same gap: it loads `state.team = get_player_team(i)` (1349-1350) but builds the widgets with the unselected frames `"team_select_a"`/`"team_select_center"`/`"team_select_b"` (1371, 1380, 1388) and never calls `update_team_select_visuals()`.

**Fix:** Call `update_weapon_select_visuals()` / `update_team_select_visuals()` at the end of `init()` so the page is correct before its first draw, and construct the widgets from the loaded state rather than a placeholder.

#### 33. Back from weapon select in a 1-player game skips the Player Count page it came from

`ArtAttack/MainMenu.cpp:1445-1462` — **low** · `correctness`

```cpp
if (this->all_players_unconfirmed()) {
    this->play_wave(CANCEL_SOUND);
    if (this->get_player_count() == 1) { transition_to(make_unique<MainMenuModeSelect>(...)); }
    else                                { transition_to(make_unique<MainMenuTeamSelect>(...)); }
    return;
}
```
The forward path for one player is Mode Select -> **Player Count** -> Weapon Select (`MainMenuPlayerCount::update` transitions straight to `MainMenuWeaponSelect` at 910-913 because a single player needs no team). The back path jumps two screens to Mode Select, so the user cannot return to Player Count to change from 1 player to 2 without also re-selecting the game mode. The multi-player branch correctly returns to the immediately preceding screen. Symptomatic of navigation being 'construct the specific class I think I came from' rather than a stack.

**Fix:** Send the 1-player case to `MainMenuPlayerCount` to match the forward path. Structurally, hold a navigation stack so BACK is `pop()`.

#### 34. Bare positional bool arguments at the end of 9-14 parameter constructor calls

`ArtAttack/MainMenu.cpp:1942-1951` — **low** · `api-design`

`MTextDropShadow`'s constructor has fourteen parameters (Mh.h:142-156) with eight defaulted, and the menus routinely pass a naked `true` in the ninth slot to mean 'hidden': `make_unique<MTextDropShadow>("ready", "READY?", ANNOUNCEMENT_FONT, ..., SHADOW_COLOUR, HEADING_SHADOW_OFFSET, true)` (MainMenu.cpp:1942-1951). Same at ResultsMenu.cpp:129-138, 140-149, 155-164, 166-175. Nothing at the call site says what `true` means, and swapping it with an adjacent compatible argument is not a compile error. The habit runs through the module's own APIs too: `MainMenuOptions::apply_fullscreen_setting(bool fullscreen)` (MainMenu.h:181) with its `if (fullscreen) {...} else // windowed` body, and `play_effect(name, bool loop, float volume, ...)` / `stop_effect(name, bool immediate)` (SoundBankObject.h:18-20) called as `play_effect(MUSIC, true, MUSIC_VOLUME)` and `stop_effect(MUSIC, true)` (MainMenu.cpp:107, 1815).

**Fix:** Replace trailing bools with named enums (`enum class visibility { visible, hidden }`, `window_mode`, `playback`), and give `MTextDropShadow` a config struct instead of fourteen positional parameters.

## `ArtAttack/MattMath.h`

_56 findings: 10 high, 31 medium, 15 low_

#### 1. MattMath.h is a god header spanning pure math, collision, colour, D3D11 and camera — and hard-depends on d3d11.h

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:1-1139` — **high** · `design`

Verified by reading the whole header. 1139 lines backed by a 4568-line .cpp declaring: `direction` enum (12-23), Shape (68-89), ~30 free intersection functions (91-182), RectangleF (184-299), Vector2I (354-392), Vector2F (402-498), RectangleI (508-565), Vector4F (567-584), Colour (586-645), Vector3F (655-674), MatrixF with Gaussian elimination and determinant (684-748), Matrix3x3F (750-765), Viewport wrapping D3D11_VIEWPORT (767-806), Circle/Triangle/TriangleRightAxisAligned/Quad/Segment (808-1006), Camera (1007-1045), RectangleRotated (1047-1134).

`#include <d3d11.h>` (line 6) exists for exactly four members of `Viewport` (786, 789-790, 799). `#include "SimpleMath.h"` (line 4) leaks through every type: Vector2F(SimpleMath::Vector2) at 411, RectangleF(SimpleMath::Rectangle)/(RECT) at 198-199, Colour(SimpleMath::Color) at 598, plus matching operator= and get_sm_*/get_xm_* on all of them. So the engine's vocabulary types cannot compile without the DirectX SDK — which is exactly why MattMathTests can only test them by `#include`-ing MattMath.cpp directly (MathTests.cpp:5).

**Fix:** Split with a clear dependency direction: MattMath/Vector.h + Rectangle.h (zero dependencies), MattMath/Colour.h, MattMath/Shapes.h + Intersect.h, and a presentation-layer Viewport.h + Camera2D.h. Move every get_sm_*/get_xm_*/RECT/D3D11_VIEWPORT conversion into a MattMath_DirectXInterop.h of free functions that only the renderer includes.

#### 2. MattMath is a god module: shapes, colour, a general dynamic matrix, viewport and camera in one 1139-line header / 4568-line TU

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:1-1139` — **high** · `design`

Verified contents of the single header: scalar helpers (44-66), a `direction` enum (12-23), the `Shape` hierarchy plus ~30 free intersection functions (68-182), `Vector2I`/`Vector2F`/`Vector3F`/`Vector4F`, `RectangleI`/`RectangleF`, `Colour` with hex parsing and `saturate`/`desaturate`/`brighten`/`darken` (586-645), a dynamically-sized `MatrixF` with `gaussian_elimination`/`determinant`/`is_upper_triangular` (684-748), `Matrix3x3F` (750-765), a D3D `Viewport` (767-806), `Camera` (1007-1045) and the six shape primitives. `Colour` and `MatrixF` have no relationship whatsoever to 2D collision geometry. This is also why MattMathTests cannot test the shapes without `#include "..\ArtAttack\MattMath.cpp"` wholesale (MathTests.cpp:5-6) -- there is no smaller unit to link against.

**Fix:** Break into focused headers behind an umbrella (`Vector2.h`, `Rectangle.h`, `Shapes.h`, `Intersection.h`, `Matrix.h`), move `Colour` into a render module and `Viewport`/`Camera` into a view module, one class per header/source pair. That is also the precondition for making the engine a static library that the test project links against instead of #including .cpp files.

#### 3. The geometry library #includes d3d11.h and DirectXTK, hard-binding a renderer-agnostic module to D3D11

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:4-8, 767-806` — **high** · `design`

Merges 2 candidates. `MattMath.h` opens with `#include "SimpleMath.h"` and `#include <d3d11.h>`, so every gameplay/AI/physics file that wants a `Vector2F` compiles all of `d3d11.h` and `Windows.h`. The coupling is not incidental: `struct Viewport` (767-806) exists solely to convert to/from `D3D11_VIEWPORT` and `SimpleMath::Viewport`, including `const D3D11_VIEWPORT* get_d3d_viewport_ptr()`; `RectangleF` has `RectangleF(const RECT&)`, `get_win_rect()` and `get_sm_rectangle()` (198-199, 230-231); and `Circle` (816), `Triangle` (851-853) and `Quad` (929-932) each carry duplicate constructor sets taking `SimpleMath::Vector2` purely to skip a conversion. For a module whose stated purpose is to be the reusable core of a 2D engine, the geometry primitives must not know the graphics API exists.

**Fix:** Split into a pure-C++ `MattMath/` (Vector2F, RectangleF, Circle, Triangle, Quad, Segment, RectangleRotated) and a `MattMathD3DInterop.h` in the rendering layer providing free `to_d3d(const Viewport&)`, `to_rect(const RectangleF&)`, `from_sm(const SimpleMath::Vector2&)`. Move `Viewport` out of the math namespace -- it is a rendering concept. Delete the `SimpleMath::Vector2` constructor overloads from the shapes.

#### 4. RectangleF — the engine's universal value type and AABB — inherits polymorphic Shape

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:68-89, 184-301` — **high** · `design`

Verified. `struct RectangleF : public Shape` (MattMath.h:184); Shape (68-89) has a virtual destructor plus 11 pure virtuals. `typedef MattMath::RectangleF AABB;` (301). Consequences I checked in the source rather than assumed:
- Not a literal type, so `const RectangleF RectangleF::ZERO` (MattMath.cpp:1134) must be dynamically initialised, and RectangleF can never be constexpr.
- `get_bounding_box()` returns RectangleF **by value** (MattMath.h:71; RectangleF's own is `return *this;` at MattMath.cpp:719-722), so every AABB query materialises a vptr-carrying object. Shape::AABB_intersects (143-146) constructs two per call.
- Shape declares a destructor but no copy control, so its copy-assignment is implicitly public: `Shape& a = circle; Shape& b = rect; a = b;` compiles and silently does nothing.
- 24 bytes instead of 16 on x64, not trivially copyable, arrays of rects cannot be memcpy'd or packed.
Six reviewers raised versions of this; merged here. For a project whose stated goal is a reusable 2D engine, fusing 'is a rectangle' with 'participates in a collision double-dispatch hierarchy' is the single biggest structural problem in this module.

**Fix:** Split the roles: a plain literal `RectangleF`/`AABB` (public floats, constexpr ctors, no base) as the math primitive, and a separate polymorphic or variant-based collision layer. As a zero-cost stopgap today, give Shape `protected: Shape(const Shape&) = default; Shape& operator=(const Shape&) = default;` to close the slicing-assignment hole (Core Guidelines C.67).

#### 5. Shape is an O(N^2) fat interface: adding a primitive forces edits to every existing shape

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:68-89` — **high** · `design`

Merges 2 candidates; severity downgraded from the reported "critical" (nothing crashes -- this is a design cost, not a defect). `Shape` declares seven pure-virtual `intersects` overloads (lines 73-79). Adding an eighth primitive (capsule, ray, convex polygon) requires: a new `shape_type` value, a new pure virtual on `Shape`, an implementation in all five existing concrete shapes, a new `case` in `Shape::intersects(const Shape*)` (MattMath.cpp:119-136), and roughly seven new free functions. That is the classic binary-dispatch explosion and it is the single biggest structural obstacle to MattMath being a reusable collision library. It already shows: `shape_type::NONE` (shape_type.h:11) is a value no shape ever returns, existing only so the `default:` arm can throw.

**Fix:** Collapse the pairwise matrix. Give every convex primitive `Vector2F support(const Vector2F& dir) const` and write one generic SAT/GJK `intersects(const Shape&, const Shape&)` -- N implementations instead of N^2 -- keeping specialised fast paths (AABB-AABB, circle-circle) as an optimisation table rather than as the interface. `Shape` should then carry only `get_bounding_box`, `get_center`, `contains`, `clone` and `support`.

#### 6. Shape::get_edges/get_points/get_triangles return std::vector by value, forcing a heap allocation per narrow-phase call

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:87` — **high** · `performance`

Merges 4 candidates (the "narrow phase heap-allocates dozens" report and three get_edges/std::array reports). `virtual std::vector<Segment> get_edges() const = 0;` forces an allocation for a container that is always 0, 3 or 4 elements. Implementations: RectangleF 808-818, Circle 3340-3344, Triangle 3502-3511, Quad 3943-3953, RectangleRotated 4284-4294. Same for `Triangle::get_points` (3485-3489), `Triangle::get_angles` (3528-3537), `Quad::get_points` (3871-3881) and `Quad::get_triangles` (3965-3973). Verified call sites inside the intersection routines: 219, 234, 288, 321, 369, 393-394 (two per call), 412, 435, 480, 495-496, 516, 533, 549, 599, 646-647 (two per call), plus `Quad::is_valid` at 3835 and `RectangleRotated::edges_valid` at 4541. One quad-vs-OBB query fans out to dozens of malloc/free pairs, and `CollisionTools::bracket_object_collision_generic` (CollisionTools.cpp:53-68) reruns the narrow phase `BRACKET_ITERATIONS` times per contact while `calculate_object_collision_depth` (CollisionTools.cpp:270-281) additionally `clone()`s the whole collider per query. Every shape has a compile-time-known vertex count; nothing here needs dynamic allocation.

**Fix:** Return `std::array<Segment,4>` / `std::array<Point2F,4>` per concrete type, or expose `int edge_count()` + `Segment edge(int)` and index. For the polymorphic path, fill a caller-supplied buffer -- that works under the current (default) C++ standard. Drop `get_triangles()` in favour of two direct calls.

#### 7. Shape::inflate(float) is one virtual with three mutually incompatible geometric meanings and three different failure policies

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:88` — **high** · `design`

Merges 4 candidates. `virtual void inflate(float amount) = 0;` has no documented contract. Verified implementations: `RectangleF::inflate(float)` (946-949) -> `inflate(a,a)` moves each side out by `a`; `RectangleRotated::inflate` (4295-4305) `_hw_extents += (a,a)` -- same perpendicular growth; `Circle::inflate` (3346-3349) `radius += a` -- same; but `Triangle::inflate` (3457-3472) and `Quad::inflate` (3813-3830) do `points[i] = center + dir_i * len_i + dir_i * amount`, pushing each VERTEX radially from the centroid, so the perpendicular edge offset is `amount * cos(theta)` and varies per edge -- for a square, `amount/sqrt(2)`; for a sliver triangle, arbitrarily small. So `shape->inflate(2.0f)` grows a rectangle's boundary by 2 and a triangle's by 1.41 or less. Negative amounts diverge too: RectangleRotated throws, Circle silently produces a negative radius, Triangle/Quad silently invert through the centroid and produce NaN when a vertex sits on the centroid (`edge.normalize()` at 3464-3466 / 3821-3824 divides by zero). StructurePaintable.cpp:118-119 has `//shape->inflate(-THICKNESS);` commented out -- a real caller that wanted the polymorphic negative case and presumably found it didn't work. Graded high rather than medium: this is exactly the kind of undefined interface contract that blocks the engine-reuse goal.

**Fix:** Define the contract as "offset every boundary outward by `amount` along its normal" (Minkowski dilation) and implement Triangle/Quad by offsetting each edge line and re-intersecting adjacent edges -- not by scaling from the centroid. Pick one negative-amount policy for all five. Or drop the virtual and expose shape-specific `expand` free functions with defined semantics.

#### 8. Nine public types in MattMath.h have literally zero tests, including Camera and the entire matrix library

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:684-765, 1007-1045, 586-645, 354-400, 508-565, 767-806, 895-914` — **high** · `test-coverage` · confidence: certain

MattMath.h declares roughly 512 member/free functions; the suite has 33 TEST_METHODs (one empty, two for CollisionTools). Types with no coverage of any kind:
- `MatrixF` + `Matrix3x3F` + free `add/subtract/multiply/divide/gaussian_elimination/transpose/identity/zero/determinant/equal_dimensions` (MattMath.h:684-765, 729-748) — ~40 pure, dependency-free, trivially testable functions. `is_invertible()` (MattMath.cpp:2631-2637) is `determinant(*this) != 0.0f`, exact float comparison on a determinant.
- `Camera` (1007-1045): `calculate_view_rectangle` (4 overloads), `calculate_intermediate_camera`, `calculate_camera_from_view_rectangle`, `calculate_view_position`, `calculate_view_scale`. Every pixel drawn goes through these; a round-trip test (`calculate_camera_from_view_rectangle` then `calculate_view_rectangle` returns the input) is three lines and does not exist.
- `TriangleRightAxisAligned` (895-914): `get_hypotenuse`, `get_hypotenuse_gradient`, `find_hypotenuse` — this is the shape the engine uses for every ramp (LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:144-177).
- `Colour` (586-645), `Vector2I` (354-400), `RectangleI` (508-565), `Viewport` (767-806), `Vector4F`, `Vector3F`: nothing.
- `RectangleF`: ~60 members, and the only thing tested is `rectangles_intersect`. `RectangleF::intersection` is untested despite `CollisionTools::resolve_object_AABB_collision` (CollisionTools.cpp:214) depending on it for every rect-vs-rect push-out.

**Fix:** Prioritise by blast radius, not by ease: Camera round-trips, RectangleF::intersection/union_of/contains, TriangleRightAxisAligned::get_hypotenuse, then the matrix library (which is pure and can be tested exhaustively for small sizes against hand-computed 2x2/3x3 results).

#### 9. Quad() and RectangleRotated() = default bypass every invariant, and a default-constructed OBB makes contains() throw from inside the collision loop

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:922, 1049` — **high** · `robustness`

Merges 3 candidates. Both classes throw `std::invalid_argument` from every user-written constructor and setter (Quad: MattMath.cpp:3710, 3728, 3741, 3756, 3772, 3887, 3897, 3907, 3917; RectangleRotated: 4194, 4209, 4299, 4363, 4374, 4385, 4396, 4407) and then declare `= default` default constructors that check nothing. Traced the failure: a default-constructed `RectangleRotated` has `_hw_extents = ZERO` (so `half_widths_valid()` at 4512-4521 is false -- permanently invalid by the class's own definition) and `_points` = four ZEROs. `contains(point)` (4265-4268) -> `point_rectangle_rotated_intersect` (611-617) -> `get_quad()` (4450-4455) -> `calculate_points()` with zero extents produces four identical points -> `Quad(vector)` (3716-3732) -> `is_valid()` (3832-3849) tests `edges[0].intersects(edges[1])`, both `Segment(ZERO,ZERO)`, and `segments_intersect` short-circuits `if (a == b) return true` (565-570) -> `is_valid()` false -> the Quad ctor throws. So a const query named `contains()` throws out of the middle of `Player::is_colliding` / `CollisionTools::bracket_object_collision_generic`. `Quad(RectangleF(0,0,0,0))` (3734-3745) throws for exactly the same reason. A default `Quad` is likewise invalid by its own `is_valid()`.

**Fix:** Delete the defaulted default constructors, or give them genuinely valid states (unit square / unit extents with `_points` computed). Independently, `contains()` must not be able to throw: implement it as `|dot(p - _center, _x_axis)| <= _hw_extents.x && |dot(p - _center, _y_axis)| <= _hw_extents.y` instead of round-tripping through a validating `Quad`.

#### 10. set_x_axis / set_y_axis can never actually rotate a RectangleRotated -- they validate the new axis against the unchanged other axis

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:1080-1082` — **high** · `design`

`set_x_axis` (MattMath.cpp:4359-4369) assigns `_x_axis = x_axis.normalized()` and then calls `axes_valid()` (4522-4538), which tests `are_equal(Vector2F::dot(_x_axis, _y_axis), 0.0f, EPSILON)` against the OLD, unchanged `_y_axis`. Any new x-axis not already perpendicular to the current y-axis throws, so the only values that succeed are the axis it already had (or its negation). `set_y_axis` (4370-4380) is identical. There is no `set_angle`, no `rotate`, no combined `set_axes` (checked the full public interface at MattMath.h:1056-1111), so an OBB is effectively un-rotatable after construction -- in the one shape whose entire reason for existing is that it rotates.

**Fix:** Replace both setters with `set_rotation(float radians)` deriving both axes from the angle, and/or `set_axes(x, y)` that validates the pair together. Storing a single angle and deriving the axes on demand makes the perpendicularity invariant unrepresentable-as-broken and deletes `axes_valid()`.

#### 11. MattMath.h uses std::unique_ptr and std::string without including <memory> or <string>

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:1-8` — **medium** · `robustness`

Merges 2 candidates. The header includes only `SimpleMath.h`, `shape_type.h`, `<d3d11.h>`, `<cmath>` and `<vector>`, yet declares `virtual std::unique_ptr<Shape> clone() const = 0;` at line 85 (plus five overrides at 206, 822, 859, 937, 1067) and `Colour(const std::string& hex);` at line 600. It compiles only because DirectXTK's `SimpleMath.h` transitively drags in the MSVC STL's memory and string machinery -- an accident of one vendor's header layout, in the most widely included header in the project. A DirectXTK update or a different standard library breaks it, and the failure will look like hundreds of unrelated errors. `<cmath>` is not used by anything in the header and belongs in the .cpp.

**Fix:** Add `#include <memory>` and `#include <string>`; move `<cmath>` to MattMath.cpp. Combine with the D3D split above.

#### 12. MattMath.h declares std::unique_ptr and std::string without including <memory> or <string>

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:4-8` — **medium** · `robustness`

Verified. The header's entire include list is SimpleMath.h, shape_type.h, <d3d11.h>, <cmath>, <vector>. It then declares the engine's ownership primitive at line 85 — `virtual std::unique_ptr<Shape> clone() const = 0;` — plus unique_ptr at 206, 822, 859, 937, 1067, and std::string at 600 and 628. Colour.h includes only MattMath.h yet declares 149 const std::string objects.

It compiles by two separate accidents, both verified: in the game project, pch.h includes <algorithm> (42), <memory> (49) and <stdexcept> (50) and is force-included ahead of everything; in MattMathTests, pch.h is an empty stub (I read it — it contains only the include guard) and MathTests.cpp:5 `#include "..\ArtAttack\MattMath.cpp"` works only because CppUnitTest.h on line 2 drags in <string> and <memory> first. MattMath.cpp itself uses std::min/std::max, std::invalid_argument and std::make_unique with none of <algorithm>, <stdexcept> or <memory> included directly.

For a header meant to be a reusable engine's public interface, a consumer who includes MattMath.h first — the normal thing — gets an error pointing at the header, not at their code.

**Fix:** Add <memory>, <string> and <cstdint> to MattMath.h, <string> to Colour.h, and <algorithm>/<stdexcept>/<memory> to MattMath.cpp. Apply include-what-you-use to every engine header rather than relying on the consumer's PCH ordering.

#### 13. The math library has a D3D11 type baked into it, forcing d3d11.h into 68 of 81 TUs

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:6,786-799` — **medium** · `design` · confidence: certain

MattMath.h:6 includes <d3d11.h>, and the reason is MattMath::Viewport: line 786 `Viewport(const D3D11_VIEWPORT& viewport);`, line 789 `D3D11_VIEWPORT get_d3d_viewport() const;`, line 790 `const D3D11_VIEWPORT* get_d3d_viewport_ptr() const;`, line 799 `Viewport& operator=(const D3D11_VIEWPORT&);`. MattMath.h is the single most-included first-party header (68 of 81 TUs), so one graphics-API-specific struct in an otherwise pure 2D math library taxes the entire build and makes the math module - the one part of the engine that is genuinely reusable and genuinely unit-tested - non-portable. The implementation compounds it: MattMath.cpp:3215 is `return reinterpret_cast<const D3D11_VIEWPORT*>(this);`, i.e. MattMath::Viewport is silently type-punned as a D3D11_VIEWPORT, which is only 'safe' as long as nobody adds a member or changes field order.

**Fix:** Move Viewport out of MattMath into the presentation layer (ViewportManager or a new GraphicsTypes.h), or keep a plain `struct Viewport { float x,y,w,h,minz,maxz; }` in MattMath and put the D3D11 conversion in a free function in the D3D layer. Then delete MattMath.h:6 and drop d3d11.h from 68 TUs. Replace the reinterpret_cast with explicit field-by-field conversion regardless.

#### 14. MattMath gives four types two names each via typedefs, and one struct is camelCase in an all-snake_case namespace

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:33, 301, 1136, 770-775` — **medium** · `naming` · confidence: certain

Alias sprawl: `typedef Vector2F Point2F;` (line 33), `typedef MattMath::RectangleF AABB;` (301), `typedef RectangleRotated OBB;` (1136). The consequence is that the same type is spelled differently depending on which file you are in - `EricsonMath.h:113,119-120` takes `const MattMath::AABB&` while `MattMath.h:96` takes `const MattMath::RectangleF&` for the identical type, and `EricsonMath.h:83-99` uses `Point2F` where `MattMath.h:80` uses `Vector2F`. `Point2F` in particular destroys type safety for the whole shape library (see the RectangleRotated finding).
Separately, `struct Viewport` (line 766) declares `float x, y, width, height` in snake_case and then `float minDepth = 0.0f;` / `float maxDepth = 1.0f;` (774-775) in camelCase - the only camelCase data members in first-party code. The camelCase spelling then propagates through `MattMath.cpp:3152-3294` (`minDepth(minDepth)`, `this->maxDepth`, ~20 sites) and the ctor defaults at `MattMath.h:780,783,785`.

**Fix:** Delete `Point2F` and use `Vector2F` (or make it a real distinct type, not a typedef, if you want point-vs-vector safety). Keep `AABB`/`OBB` only if you commit to them as *the* names and rename `RectangleF`/`RectangleRotated` away; otherwise delete the aliases and fix EricsonMath's signatures. Rename `minDepth`/`maxDepth` to `min_depth`/`max_depth`.

#### 15. No LanguageStandard is set in either vcxproj, so the project builds as C++14 and reimplements clamp/lerp/PI by hand

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:44-66` — **medium** · `modern-cpp`

Verified: grepping `LanguageStandard` across ArtAttack.vcxproj and MattMathTests.vcxproj returns nothing, so MSVC v145 defaults to /std:c++14 and none of `std::clamp`, `std::optional`, `std::string_view`, `if constexpr`, inline `constexpr` statics or `<numbers>` is available. Consequently: `MattMath::clamp` (declared 51/53, defined MattMath.cpp:34-48 and 60-74) is a 15-line if/else reimplementation of `std::clamp`, written twice instead of as a template; `lerp` (66, defined 110-113) is `std::lerp`; `PI` (44) is `std::numbers::pi_v<float>`; `are_equal` (MattMath.cpp:93-96) calls the C global `fabs` rather than `std::fabs`; and `to_radians`/`to_degrees` (101-108) are not `constexpr` despite being pure arithmetic on a `constexpr` constant. Bumping the standard is the single change that unlocks most of the other fixes in this review.

**Fix:** Add `<LanguageStandard>stdcpp20</LanguageStandard>` to all four configurations of both vcxproj files (better: factor the four near-identical ItemDefinitionGroups into a shared .props). Then delete `clamp`/`clamp_ref`/`lerp` and make `to_radians`/`to_degrees`/`are_equal` constexpr.

#### 16. EPSILON is an absolute 1e-4, smaller than one float ULP at the coordinate magnitudes the levels use — and a second EPSILON 100x tighter is visible in the same TU

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:46, 59-61` — **medium** · `robustness`

Verified. `constexpr float EPSILON = 0.0001f;` (MattMath.h:46) is the default for `are_equal(float, float, float epsilon = EPSILON)` (h:59), the codebase's only tolerance primitive (MattMath.cpp:93-96, `fabs(a-b) < epsilon`).

The levels are not unit-scale: close_quarters.json out_of_bounds is {x:-100, y:-100, width:6200, height:6200}. One ULP of a float at magnitude 6000 is about 4.9e-4 — five times larger than EPSILON — so at world scale are_equal is *harsher* than 'equal after one rounding step'. Consumers that rely on it structurally: RectangleRotated::axes_valid (4522-4538), edges_valid (4539-4565, which compares edge *lengths* in world units with the same absolute 1e-4), TriangleRightAxisAligned::find_hypotenuse (3665-3684), Vector2F::get_direction (1662-1714, which applies the absolute epsilon to raw components).

Two smaller defects verified in the same three lines: the Vector2F overload spells its default as the literal `0.0001f` (h:61) instead of naming EPSILON, so the two can drift apart silently; and EricsonMath.h:75 declares a second `constexpr float EPSILON = 0.000001f`, visible in MattMath.cpp because it includes EricsonMath.h at line 3. Unqualified EPSILON inside namespace MattMath resolves to MattMath::EPSILON by inner-scope lookup, which is what each site wants — but the resolution is invisible at the point of use.

**Fix:** Provide a relative-plus-absolute comparison and reserve the absolute form for comparisons against zero. Change h:61's default to `= EPSILON`. Rename the two constants (MattMath::DEFAULT_EPSILON, EricsonMath::INTERSECTION_EPSILON) and qualify every unqualified use in MattMath.cpp. Use std::fabs (float overload) rather than fabs, which forces a float->double->float round trip.

#### 17. Shape is a polymorphic base with public implicit copy construction and copy assignment, so slicing is silent and base-to-base assignment is a no-op

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:68-89` — **medium** · `design`

`struct Shape` (68-89) correctly declares `virtual ~Shape() = default;` but constrains nothing else. It has an implicitly generated public copy constructor and copy assignment, and being a `struct` everything is public. So `Shape& a = *shape_a; a = *shape_b;` compiles cleanly and does literally nothing (`Shape` has no data members and the vptr is not copied), leaving the caller believing one shape was assigned to another. Slicing on construction is equally unguarded and is the supported code path today -- see the `TriangleRightAxisAligned::clone()` finding. For a base used exclusively through `Shape*` / `unique_ptr<Shape>` (`Structure.h:40`, all of `CollisionTools`), leaving value semantics wide open is a standing invitation.

**Fix:** Make the copy operations `protected` (or delete copy assignment) on `Shape` so only derived classes invoke them, force polymorphic copying through `clone()`, and add `protected: Shape() = default;`. That one change would have made the ramp slicing a compile error.

#### 18. Shape is a polymorphic base with public implicit copy-assignment, and every core value type inherits it

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:68-89` — **medium** · `design`

`struct Shape` declares `virtual ~Shape() = default` and nine pure virtuals, but neither deletes nor protects copy construction/assignment, so `Shape& operator=(const Shape&)` is implicitly public. Combined with the raw `Shape*` API CollisionTools exposes, `*collider = *collidee;` inside a resolution routine would compile and silently slice a Circle into a RectangleF's Shape subobject.

The already-paid cost is layout: RectangleF, Circle, Triangle, Quad and RectangleRotated all carry a vptr, so none is trivially copyable or constant-initialisable, and they cannot be passed in registers. These are the engine's fundamental value types and they are copied constantly in the collision path — CollisionTools.cpp:15, 35, 58, 139-140 and EricsonMath.cpp:286-289, 394-395, 426-427, 647-648 each build one or more temporaries per call, and `get_bounding_box()` returns a polymorphic type by value on every invocation. The polymorphism also forces the dynamic_cast double-dispatch chain (MattMath.cpp:119-136) and the `clone()`/unique_ptr dance in calculate_object_collision_depth.

Note this file is outside the math-collision module group but is the direct cause of costs inside it.

**Fix:** Minimal: `protected: Shape(const Shape&) = default; Shape& operator=(const Shape&) = default;` to close the slicing hole without changing layout. Structural, and better for the engine goal: drop the inheritance, make the shapes plain aggregates, and move dispatch to a tagged variant or a free-function overload set — that kills the vptr, the dynamic_casts, and the need for clone().

#### 19. Segment and Point2F participate in the Shape intersects interface but are not Shapes, so two of the seven pure virtuals are unreachable through the polymorphic entry point

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:77-78, 982-1006` — **medium** · `design`

Merges 2 candidates. `Shape` declares `virtual bool intersects(const Segment&)` and `virtual bool intersects(const Point2F&)` (77-78), yet `Segment` (982-1006) does not derive from `Shape` and `Point2F` is a typedef of `Vector2F` (33). `Shape::intersects(const Shape*)` (MattMath.cpp:119-136) switches on `shape_type`, which has no `SEGMENT` or `POINT` value (shape_type.h:4-12), so those two overrides can never be reached polymorphically. `Segment` has only two ad-hoc `intersects` members (`Segment`, `RectangleF`, MattMath.cpp:4054-4062) -- so `circle.intersects(segment)` compiles but `segment.intersects(circle)` does not, and the stubs for exactly those cases sit commented out at 4079-4086. `Segment` also has no `get_bounding_box`, `offset` or `clone`, so it cannot be stored in the `unique_ptr<Shape>` the whole collision system is built on -- even though a segment is the natural shape for a raycast, a paintable edge or a thin projectile.

**Fix:** Make `Segment` (and a distinct `Point` type) first-class `Shape` implementations with their own `shape_type` values so one dispatch path covers everything, or delete `Segment`'s two lopsided members so the asymmetry is at least not advertised.

#### 20. Three parallel public APIs for the same operation, and get_shape_type() leaks so eight call sites bypass all of them

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:80-94, 96-182` — **medium** · `design`

The same intersection is reachable three ways: ~30 free `*_intersect` functions (MattMath.h:96-182), the member `intersects` overloads that merely forward to them (e.g. `Circle::intersects(const Triangle&)` at MattMath.cpp:3372-3375 is `return circle_triangle_intersect(*this, other);`), and `shapes_intersect(a,b)` (157-165) which forwards to the member which forwards to the free function. Argument order is not guessable from the name: `rectangle_rotated_rectangle_intersect(const RectangleF&, const RectangleRotated&)` (MattMath.h:117) takes the axis-aligned rect FIRST. Worse, `Shape::get_shape_type()` is public, so callers route around the polymorphism entirely -- I verified the identical `if (other_shape_type == shape_type::RECTANGLE) return true;` short-circuit in Player.cpp:172, PaintTile.cpp:96, ProjectileBall.cpp:73, ProjectileJet.cpp:72, ProjectileMist.cpp:74, ProjectileRolling.cpp:66, ProjectileSpray.cpp:74, plus CollisionTools.cpp:244-245. The ~30 free functions have zero first-party callers outside MattMath.cpp and the tests.

**Fix:** Publish one entry point -- `bool intersects(const Shape&, const Shape&)` -- and move the pairwise routines into a `detail` namespace or an anonymous namespace in the .cpp. Demote `get_shape_type()` to a dispatcher-only tag; eight call sites using it to skip the narrow phase means the interface is not giving callers what they need.

#### 21. Every derived shape redeclares intersects and none adds `using Shape::intersects;`, so Shape's own convenience overloads are hidden on all of them

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:80-83` — **medium** · `design`

`Shape` declares non-virtual `intersects(const Shape*)` and `intersects(const Shape&)` (80-81). Every derived class then declares its own `intersects` overload set -- RectangleF (241-247), Circle (831-837), Triangle (882-888), Quad (966-972), RectangleRotated (1058-1064) -- and none contains `using Shape::intersects;`. C++ name lookup stops at the first scope with a match, and no `const Shape&` converts to any of the seven parameter types, so `circle.intersects(some_shape_ref)` does not compile even though `Circle` IS a `Shape` with that operation; callers must write `static_cast<const Shape&>(circle).intersects(other)`. It only goes unnoticed because every real call site already holds a `Shape*` (Player.cpp:163/179, PaintTile.cpp:87/103, CollisionTools.cpp:62/235, and the five projectiles). `AABB_intersects` is not redeclared and so is NOT hidden -- two sibling APIs behaving differently for no visible reason.

**Fix:** Add `using Shape::intersects;` to each derived class, or delete the pointer/reference convenience overloads from `Shape` and let callers use the free functions.

#### 22. Shape supports only offset() and inflate() -- no rotate, scale or transform -- which is why RectangleRotated had to be bolted on as a whole new type

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:84, 88, 1047-1134` — **medium** · `design`

Severity downgraded from the reported "high": this is an absence rather than a defect, and a separate OBB type is a defensible (if costly) design. Still real: `Shape` has exactly two mutations, `offset(Vector2F)` (84) and `inflate(float)` (88). There is no `rotate(float)`, no `scale`, no `transform`. So a rotated box could not be expressed as "a RectangleF plus a rotation" and instead needed an 88-line class (1047-1134) plus six new free intersection functions plus a new `shape_type` value plus five new `intersects` overrides in every existing shape. The header already contains `Matrix3x3F::rotation/scale/translation` factories (759-764) that would express this directly and are used by nothing in the tree.

**Fix:** Introduce `struct Transform2D { Vector2F position; float rotation; Vector2F scale; }` with `Matrix3x3F to_matrix()` and `inverse()`, and give `Shape` one `virtual void transform(const Transform2D&)` -- or keep shapes in local space and put the transform on the collider, as most 2D engines do. `RectangleRotated` then becomes `RectangleF` + `Transform2D`, and `Camera` becomes a `Transform2D`.

#### 23. Shape::get_edges() returns std::vector<Segment> by value, forcing a heap allocation per edge query in the narrow phase

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:87, 961` — **medium** · `performance`

Verified. `virtual std::vector<Segment> get_edges() const = 0;` (MattMath.h:87) forces every implementation to allocate for a count that is always 0, 3 or 4 and known at compile time: RectangleF (MattMath.cpp:808-818), Triangle (3502-3511), Quad (3943-3953), RectangleRotated (4284-4293), and Circle returns an empty vector (3340-3344). `std::vector<Triangle> get_triangles()` (MattMath.h:961) and `std::vector<Vector2F> get_points()` (865, 946) have the same shape.

Call sites inside the intersection functions, all verified: 219, 288, 369, 393-394 (two allocations for one triangle-pair test), 435, 480, 599, 646-647 (two per OBB pair). quads_intersect (492-511) allocates two vector<Triangle> then calls triangles_intersect up to 4 times, each allocating two vector<Segment> — up to 10 allocations for one quad-vs-quad test. CollisionTools::bracket_object_collision_generic (CollisionTools.cpp:55-68) then repeats `collider->intersects(collidee)` for `iterations` passes.

Note: the reviewers' claim of an O(n^2) all-pairs loop in Level::update_level_logic is outside this module and I did not verify it; the allocation counts above are verified independently of it.

Also verified: `RectangleF collider_aabb = collider->get_bounding_box();` at CollisionTools.cpp:35 and again at :57 is computed and never read — dead in both functions.

**Fix:** Return a fixed-capacity type: `virtual int get_edges(Segment (&out)[4]) const` returning the count, or std::array from the concrete types with a fill-a-span form on the virtual interface. Note RectangleRotated::get_points() already returns const& while Triangle/Quad return by value — that inconsistency is itself a bug magnet. Delete the dead collider_aabb locals.

#### 24. `rectangle_rotated_rectangle_intersect` parses two ways and its name order is the reverse of its parameters

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:117` — **medium** · `naming` · confidence: certain

`bool rectangle_rotated_rectangle_intersect(const MattMath::RectangleF& rect, const MattMath::RectangleRotated& rotated_rect);` (MattMath.h:117, defined MattMath.cpp:260). The name reads as `rectangle_rotated` + `rectangle` - i.e. (RectangleRotated, RectangleF) - but the parameters are (RectangleF, RectangleRotated). Every sibling in the family puts the types in argument order: `circle_rectangle_rotated_intersect` (141), `triangle_rectangle_rotated_intersect` (156), `quad_rectangle_rotated_intersect` (167), `segment_rectangle_rotated_intersect` (175), `point_rectangle_rotated_intersect` (178). So this one function is backwards, and the call sites prove the confusion is live: `MattMath.cpp:918` calls `rectangle_rotated_rectangle_intersect(*this, other)` from `RectangleF::intersects` while `MattMath.cpp:4239` calls `rectangle_rotated_rectangle_intersect(rect, *this)` from `RectangleRotated::intersects` - two orderings for one function.

**Fix:** Rename to `rectangle_rectangle_rotated_intersect` so it matches both its parameter order and its five siblings. The corresponding test at `MattMathTests/MathTests.cpp:356` should be renamed with it.

#### 25. Redundant `X(const X&) = default;` on every shape suppresses the implicit move operations

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:192, 814, 847, 898, 923, 988, 1013, 1050` — **medium** · `modern-cpp`

Merges 2 candidates. Verified declarations: RectangleF:192, Circle:814, Triangle:847, TriangleRightAxisAligned:898, Quad:923, Segment:988, Camera:1013, RectangleRotated:1050. A user-declared copy constructor suppresses the implicit move constructor AND move assignment. The compiler would have generated an identical copy constructor anyway, so these lines buy nothing and cost the moves. For the POD-ish shapes it is only noise, but `RectangleRotated` holds a `std::vector<Point2F> _points` (1119-1120), so every return-by-value where NRVO does not apply, every `std::vector<RectangleRotated>` growth and every `push_back(std::move(obb))` performs a heap allocation and deep copy a move would have made free.

**Fix:** Delete all eight `X(const X&) = default;` lines and let the rule of zero apply -- the compiler then generates copy AND move correctly. If the intent was to document copyability, use a comment.

#### 26. contains(Point2F) is duplicated non-virtually on five shapes instead of being on Shape, so nothing holding a Shape* can ask the most basic 2D query

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:248, 838, 889, 973, 1065` — **medium** · `design`

`RectangleF::contains` (248), `Circle::contains` (838), `Triangle::contains` (889), `Quad::contains` (973) and `RectangleRotated::contains` (1065) are each declared separately and none is virtual. Four of the five bodies are the identical one-liner `return this->intersects(point);` (MattMath.cpp:912-915, 3392-3395, 3584-3587, 4023-4026); `RectangleRotated::contains` (4265-4268) forwards to the free function instead, for no reason. Because none is on `Shape`, code holding a `Shape*` -- which is how every collider is stored (`Structure.h:40`, `ICollisionGameObject::get_shape()`) -- cannot ask whether a collider contains a point. Point containment is the most basic query a 2D engine needs: mouse picking, spawn validity, trigger volumes.

**Fix:** Add `virtual bool contains(const Point2F&) const = 0;` to `Shape` and delete the five duplicates. `Shape` is also missing `get_area()` (only `RectangleF` has one, MattMath.h:228) despite paint scoring summing shape areas.

#### 27. Not one constructor in MattMath.h is explicit, creating a lossy implicit conversion cycle between the vector types

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:362, 409, 413, 524` — **medium** · `design`

Verified by count: `grep -c explicit ArtAttack/MattMath.h` returns 0. The consequences that compile silently at /W4:
- `Vector2I(const Vector2F&)` (h:362, truncating via static_cast<int> at MattMath.cpp:1375-1379) and `Vector2F(const Vector2I&)` (h:413) are both implicit, so `v2i == v2f` compiles by truncating the float side: `Vector2I(1,1) == Vector2F(1.9f, 1.9f)` is true.
- `Vector2F(float f)` (h:409) broadcasts a scalar into both components (MattMath.cpp:1529-1533). Combined with `typedef Vector2F Point2F` (h:33) and `virtual bool intersects(const Point2F&)` (h:78), `rect.intersects(0.5f)` and `shape->offset(3.0f)` compile and mean the point/vector (0.5,0.5) and (3,3).
- `RectangleI(MattMath::RectangleF rectangle)` (h:524) is not only implicit but takes its polymorphic argument **by value**, unlike every sibling constructor at 515-526 which takes const&. The body (MattMath.cpp:1982-1988) only reads four floats. It also duplicates the existing `RectangleF::get_rectangle_i()` (h:229).
- `RectangleF(const RECT&)` / `(SimpleMath::Rectangle)` (h:198-199) and `Colour(const std::string&)` (h:600) likewise convert implicitly.
Nothing in the type system distinguishes a position from a size from a direction either — all three are Vector2F.

**Fix:** Mark every cross-type converting constructor explicit, and take RectangleI(const RectangleF&) by const reference (or delete it in favour of get_rectangle_i()). Where truncation is intended, replace the constructor with a named conversion so the loss is visible at the call site. Consider making Point2F a distinct type rather than a typedef of Vector2F.

#### 28. Missing `explicit` on converting constructors lets nonsense like circle.intersects(5.0f) compile

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:409, 926-928, 1016` — **medium** · `modern-cpp`

`Vector2F(float f);` (409, defined MattMath.cpp:1529-1533 as `x = f; y = f;`) is a non-explicit single-argument converting constructor, and `Point2F` is a typedef of `Vector2F` (33). Every shape has `bool intersects(const Point2F&) const`. So `circle.intersects(5.0f)` compiles and silently means "the point (5,5)" -- no other overload is viable, so there is not even an ambiguity error. Also non-explicit: `Quad(const std::vector<Point2F>&)` (926), `Quad(const RectangleF&)` (927) and `Quad(const RectangleRotated&)` (928), so a `RectangleF` implicitly becomes a `Quad` via a conversion that THROWS for a degenerate rectangle; and `Camera(const Viewport&, float scale = 1.0f)` (1016), callable with one argument, so any `Viewport` implicitly becomes a `Camera`.

**Fix:** Mark every single-argument (or defaulted-to-single-argument) constructor `explicit`. For `Vector2F(float)`, prefer deleting it and adding a named `Vector2F::splat(float)`.

#### 29. Colour's int and float constructors overlap: Colour(1, 1, 1) is near-black, Colour(1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f) is white

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:586-599` — **medium** · `design`

Verified. `Colour(float,float,float)` / `(float,float,float,float)` take 0..1 (MattMath.cpp:2187-2196); `Colour(int r, int g, int b, int a = 255)` takes 0..255 and divides by 255 (set_from_int_rgba, 2351-2358). With integer literals the int overload is an exact match and wins outright, so `Colour(1,1,1)` gives (0.0039, 0.0039, 0.0039) — visually black — where white was almost certainly meant. `Colour(0,0,0)` happens to be right, which hides the bug. A mixed call like `Colour(1.0f, 0, 0)` is genuinely ambiguous (float->int and int->float are both conversion rank), so the overload set is a compile-error trap too. /W4 issues no diagnostic for the silent case.

Same struct, verified separately: `Colour() = default` leaves `a = 0.0f` (MattMath.h:591) — a default-constructed Colour is fully transparent — while `Colour(r,g,b)` sets a = 1.0f (MattMath.cpp:2188). Two different notions of default alpha in one type; a Colour member left default-initialised draws nothing, which reads as a missing texture rather than an unset colour. Neither the int constructor nor `Colour(const std::string&)` is explicit.

**Fix:** Replace the int constructor with `static Colour from_rgba8(std::uint8_t r, g, b, a = 255)`, update Colour.h:309-313, make the string constructor explicit (or a named try_parse), and change the default member initialiser to `float a = 1.0f`.

#### 30. Colour clamps inside every arithmetic operator, destroying linearity, while its [0,1] invariant is unenforceable through public fields

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:586-645` — **medium** · `design`

Verified. Colour has public `float r,g,b,a` (588-591) *and* a full getter/setter pair per channel (616-624), and calls clamp_colours() from every constructor (MattMath.cpp:2190, 2195, 2200, 2205), every operator= (2221, 2230, 2239), every compound operator (2253-2306), every setter (2326-2349), set_from_int_rgba, set_from_hex, saturate, desaturate, brighten, darken, invert. Every free operator constructs through the clamping constructor (2445-2472). That is roughly 25 defensive calls guarding an invariant that `c.r = 5.0f;` destroys, which makes the 8 accessor methods pure ceremony.

The consequence that actually matters for an engine: clamping inside arithmetic breaks linearity. `(a - b) + b != a`, and `c *= 2.0f; c /= 2.0f;` is not the identity. So the type cannot be used for additive paint/light accumulation, difference or tint computation, or any multi-step blend — which is exactly what a Splatoon-like paint engine needs colour arithmetic for.

**Fix:** Make Colour a plain unclamped linear 4-float value type with constexpr aggregate construction, no clamping in operators, and no getter/setter pairs over public fields. Provide an explicit `Colour saturated() const` and clamp at the single point of conversion to the render target (get_xm_vector/get_sm_colour).

#### 31. Vector3F's seven free operators are declared `static` in the header, giving them internal linkage

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:676-682` — **medium** · `correctness`

Verified. MattMath.h:676-682 declares all seven arithmetic operators `static`, at namespace scope in a header. The definitions at MattMath.cpp:3110-3137 are written without `static`, but per [dcl.stc] the earlier declaration wins and they retain internal linkage. Every TU other than MattMath.cpp sees seven declared-but-never-defined internal functions, so the first TU to write `v3a + v3b` outside MattMath.cpp fails to build.

Confirmed as a copy-paste slip: the structurally identical operator sets for Vector2I (394-400), Vector2F (500-506), Colour (647-653) and MatrixF (729-732) are all correctly non-static. It has not bitten yet because Vector3F's only external use is Drawer, which reads `.x/.y/.z` members directly (Drawer.cpp:34,43) and never uses the operators.

**Fix:** Drop `static` from all seven. Better: once Drawer takes a real Camera instead of abusing Vector3F as {translation.x, translation.y, scale}, delete Vector3F entirely — those four member accesses are its only external use.

#### 32. Sibling shapes disagree on encapsulation and invariants, and the free algorithms reach past the accessors into Triangle's raw array

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:808-1134` — **medium** · `design`

Merges 2 candidates. Within one family: `Circle` has public `center`/`radius` and no invariant (negative radius constructible); `Triangle` has public `Vector2F points[3]` (844) plus accessors on top, and no invariant (degenerate triangles fine); `Quad` has private `points[4]` (978-979) and throws from every ctor and setter; `RectangleRotated` has private members with orthonormality and positive-extent enforcement and throws from setters; `Segment` has public members and no interface. A caller holding a `Shape*` cannot know whether a mutation returns, throws or corrupts. The inconsistency is load-bearing: `triangles_intersect` reads `a.points[i]` directly (386), `triangle_point_intersect` reads `triangle.points[0..2]` (449-450), `triangle_rectangle_rotated_intersect` reads `triangle.points[0..2]` (472-474) -- so `Triangle`'s representation is baked into three free functions and cannot be changed. Both `Triangle` and `Quad` use raw C arrays rather than `std::array`, so there is no `size()`, no `begin()/end()`, and the file uses zero standard algorithms.

**Fix:** Pick one policy family-wide. For value-type geometry the pragmatic choice is public data, no throwing constructors, and opt-in free predicates (`is_valid`/`is_degenerate`/`is_convex`) -- that keeps the shapes trivially copyable and constexpr-able. If enforced invariants are wanted instead, close `Circle`, `Triangle` and `Segment` too and return failure rather than throwing. Use `std::array` in both `Triangle` and `Quad`.

#### 33. TriangleRightAxisAligned does not override clone(), so every level ramp is stored as a sliced Triangle

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:895-914` — **medium** · `correctness`

Verified. `Triangle::clone()` (MattMath.cpp:3453-3456) hard-codes `std::make_unique<Triangle>(*this)`, and TriangleRightAxisAligned (MattMath.h:895-914) adds get_hypotenuse/get_hypotenuse_gradient/find_hypotenuse but no clone() override. LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:161-176 builds a TriangleRightAxisAligned for every ramp and passes `&triangle` to Structure, whose constructor stores `_collision_shape(collision_shape->clone())` (Structure.cpp:22). So every ramp's stored shape is a plain Triangle.

Severity tempered from the reviewers' 'high': the derived class adds no data members, and every consumer of the derived interface is currently commented out — StructureRamp.cpp is entirely commented (lines 1-27), including the `static_cast<const TriangleRightAxisAligned*>(get_shape())` at line 25 that would be UB against a sliced object. So this is a latent trap that fires the moment ramp gradients are re-enabled, not a live bug today.

Also verified in the same type: `TriangleRightAxisAligned::calculate_gradient(int)` (MattMath.h:913) is declared *private* and *hides* rather than overrides the public non-virtual `Triangle::calculate_gradient` (893).

**Fix:** Add `std::unique_ptr<Shape> clone() const override { return std::make_unique<TriangleRightAxisAligned>(*this); }`, and adopt the rule for every Shape leaf. Enforce it structurally with a CRTP ShapeClonable<Derived> mixin so a new leaf cannot forget. Rename or virtualise calculate_gradient so it stops shadowing.

#### 34. TriangleRightAxisAligned does not override clone(), so every ramp's stored collision shape loses its derived type

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:895-914` — **medium** · `design`

Merges 2 candidates, with a correction. `TriangleRightAxisAligned` declares no `clone()` override, so it inherits `Triangle::clone()` (3453-3456) = `std::make_unique<Triangle>(*this)`. LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:161-176 creates a stack-local `TriangleRightAxisAligned`, passes `&triangle`, and `Structure`'s ctor stores `collision_shape->clone()` (Structure.cpp:22). The `unique_ptr<Shape>` a ramp owns for its whole life is therefore a plain `Triangle`, and `get_shape_type()` reports `TRIANGLE`, so nothing downstream can recover the right-triangle identity that is the subclass's entire reason to exist. CORRECTION to the reviewers: this is NOT a memory-safety issue and the "reads past the object" claim is wrong -- `TriangleRightAxisAligned` adds no data members, only member functions, so the slice is value-preserving and the commented-out `static_cast` at StructureRamp.cpp:25-26 would in practice work (formally UB, practically benign). Downgraded from high/memory-safety to medium/design accordingly.

**Fix:** Add `std::unique_ptr<Shape> clone() const override { return std::make_unique<TriangleRightAxisAligned>(*this); }`, and enforce clone-per-leaf with a CRTP mixin so a new subclass cannot forget. Better: delete the subclass -- it is two free functions in a trench coat -- and provide `bool is_right_triangle(const Triangle&)`, `int hypotenuse_index(const Triangle&)`, `Segment hypotenuse(const Triangle&)`. Also have `Structure` take `unique_ptr<Shape>` by value so the ownership transfer is visible at the call site.

#### 35. TriangleRightAxisAligned enforces neither of the two invariants its name promises

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:895-914` — **medium** · `design`

All three constructors (MattMath.cpp:3609-3631) simply forward to `Triangle` and validate nothing. Axis-alignment is never checked at all -- the parameter names `top`, `left`, `right` are the only documentation. Right-angledness is discovered only at USE time, when `get_hypotenuse()` (3633-3642) calls `find_hypotenuse` and throws `std::invalid_argument("Triangle is not a right triangle")` from a const accessor. Since `Triangle` has public data (`Vector2F points[3]`, MattMath.h:844), no virtuals of its own and no invariant, a caller can also break the promise after construction. Inheriting to add two helper functions buys nothing the type system enforces.

**Fix:** Delete the class in favour of free functions, or make it a distinct value type with a factory that returns failure (`static bool try_make(...)`) rather than a subclass that throws on use. Cache the hypotenuse index at construction using squared lengths -- no acos, no sqrt.

#### 36. Camera lives in the math header, writes its transform five times, and is bypassed by Drawer, which reinvents it as a Vector3F

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:1007-1045` — **medium** · `design`

Verified. Camera (translation + scale) is a presentation concept in the maths library, and its core transform `(x - t.x) * scale` is written out five times: calculate_view_rectangle() const (MattMath.cpp:4116-4123), calculate_view_rectangle(RectangleF&) const (4124-4131), static calculate_view_rectangle(rect, camera) (4132-4140), static calculate_view_rectangle(rect, camera, out) (4141-4150), and calculate_view_position (4170-4175).

Meanwhile Drawer does not use Camera at all. Drawer.cpp:42-53:
```cpp
RectangleI Drawer::calculate_draw_rectangle(const Vector2F& position, const Vector2F& size, const Vector3F& camera)
{
    Vector2F draw_pos = (position - Vector2F(camera.x, camera.y)) * camera.z;
```
— a Vector3F whose .x/.y are treated as translation and .z as scale, i.e. Camera with the type information thrown away. That is Vector3F's only external use in the codebase. And Matrix3x3F, which has rotation/scale/translation factories and would have unified all of it, has zero callers.

**Fix:** Move Camera out of MattMath into the presentation layer as Camera2D backed by a single transform. Expose one `Vector2F world_to_view(Vector2F) const` and derive the rectangle overloads from it; delete the other four. Change Drawer::calculate_draw_rectangle to take `const Camera&`, then delete Vector3F.

#### 37. Camera exposes four spellings of the same forward transform, three of them dead, with no inverse and no rotation

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:1007-1045` — **medium** · `design`

Merges 2 candidates. `calculate_view_rectangle` exists as a const value-returning member (1021), a const in-place member (1023), a static (1025) and a static with an out-param (1028); all four bodies (MattMath.cpp:4116-4150) are the same four lines of arithmetic copy-pasted. Grepping ArtAttack/ shows only the first is ever called (AnimationObject.cpp:69, TextureObject.cpp:59). The in-place overload is also a genuine overload-resolution trap: for a non-const lvalue argument, binding to `RectangleF&` is a better match than binding to `const RectangleF&` (less cv-qualified reference wins), so `camera.calculate_view_rectangle(my_rect)` silently picks the MUTATING overload while the reader expects a value. There is no `view_to_world` inverse anywhere -- which any reusable 2D engine needs for mouse picking -- no rotation, and no zoom-about-a-point, all while a fully-built `Matrix3x3F` sits unused in the same header.

**Fix:** Keep only `[[nodiscard]] RectangleF calculate_view_rectangle(const RectangleF&) const` and delete the other three. Replace the class with `struct Camera2D { Transform2D view; }` exposing `world_to_view` / `view_to_world` derived from one matrix and its inverse, and move it into the rendering module (`CameraTools.h` already lives outside, so the split is half done).

#### 38. `RectangleRotated` half-extent API: ambiguous `hw`, self-contradictory `half_y_width`, and axes typed as `Point2F`

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:1072-1117` — **medium** · `naming` · confidence: certain

Three separate naming defects in one struct:
  1. `Vector2F _hw_extents` (line 1117) and `void set_half_extents(const Point2F& hw_extents)` (1083) - `hw` could be half-width, height-width, or hardware. The getter at 1075 says `get_half_extents` while the member says `hw_extents`; pick one word.
  2. `float get_half_y_width() const;` (line 1077) - "the half y width" is a contradiction. Its sibling is `get_half_x_width()` (1076) and there is a `get_half_width(int axis)` (1078).
  3. `Point2F get_x_axis() const;` (1072), `get_y_axis()` (1073), `get_half_extents()` (1075) all return `Point2F` while the backing members are `Vector2F _x_axis` (1115), `_y_axis` (1116), `_hw_extents` (1117). An axis is a direction and a half-extent is a size; neither is a point. This only compiles because `MattMath.h:33` has `typedef Vector2F Point2F`, so the type system cannot catch the mixup.
Also `RectangleF get_rectangle_rotated_to_axis() const;` (1100) - unparseable without reading the body.

**Fix:** `_hw_extents` -> `_half_extents` everywhere including parameter names. `get_half_x_width()` -> `get_half_extent_x()`, `get_half_y_width()` -> `get_half_extent_y()`, `get_half_width(int axis)` -> `get_half_extent(int axis)`. Change the return types of `get_x_axis`/`get_y_axis`/`get_half_extents` to `Vector2F`. Rename `get_rectangle_rotated_to_axis` to say what it produces, e.g. `get_axis_aligned_local_rectangle()`.

#### 39. RectangleRotated::operator== / operator!= are declared but never defined; no test uses them

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:1110-1111` — **medium** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

`bool operator==(const RectangleRotated& other) const;` and `operator!=` are declared in the class body but `grep -rn "RectangleRotated::operator" ArtAttack/` returns nothing — there is no definition anywhere in the repo. Every other shape defines its comparison operators (Circle at MattMath.cpp:3351, Triangle at 3538, Quad at 3975, Segment at 4045, RectangleF at 863). This is a latent LNK2019 for the first caller. It has survived because the RectangleRotated tests only compare *intersection results* (bools) and never compare two rotated rectangles for equality — a gap that is itself worth closing, since `clone()` (4276-4279) and `offset()` (4269-4275) can only be meaningfully tested via equality.

**Fix:** Define the operators (compare center, both axes, and half-extents with `are_equal`, not `==`), then add tests for `clone()` returning an equal-but-distinct object and `offset()` shifting center and all four points by the same amount.

#### 40. RectangleRotated stores exactly 4 points in a heap std::vector and reallocates it on every mutation

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:1119-1120` — **medium** · `performance`

Verified. `std::vector<Point2F> _points = { Point2F::ZERO, ... }` (MattMath.h:1119-1120) with a count fixed at 4 forever — get_point_0..3 (MattMath.cpp:4414-4429) and get_edge_0..3 (4434-4449) index _points[0..3] unconditionally. One heap allocation per RectangleRotated construction, plus one per mutation: every mutator re-runs `calculate_points()`, which itself allocates a fresh `std::vector<Point2F> points(4)` and returns it by value (4487-4499). Sites: offset (4273), set_center (4357), set_x_axis (4368), set_y_axis (4379), set_half_extents (4390), set_half_x_width (4401), set_half_y_width (4412), inflate (4304), both constructors (4199, 4214). `offset()` is what CollisionTools::bracket_object_collision_generic (CollisionTools.cpp:55-68) drives once per iteration.

Separately verified: `get_quad()` (4450-4455) calls `calculate_points()` again — allocating a second vector — instead of using the cache it just maintained.

**Fix:** Change _points to std::array<Point2F,4> and have calculate_points fill it in place (void recalculate_points()), eliminating all allocation and the copy-return. get_points() (MattMath.h:1091) then returns const std::array<Point2F,4>&. Fix get_quad() to use the cache.

#### 41. RectangleRotated caches four fixed corners in a heap std::vector, reallocating on construction, copy, clone and every one of nine mutations

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:1119-1120` — **medium** · `performance`

Merges 4 candidates. `std::vector<Point2F> _points = { ZERO, ZERO, ZERO, ZERO };` -- four 8-byte points in a heap container. Every `RectangleRotated`, including a default-constructed one, allocates; `clone()` (4276-4279) allocates twice; and `calculate_points()` (4482-4499) builds a fresh `std::vector<Point2F> points(4)` that is then move-assigned over `_points` at every one of nine sites: 4199, 4214, 4273 (`offset`), 4304 (`inflate`), 4357, 4368, 4379, 4390, 4401, 4412, plus 4452 in `get_quad()`. `offset()` in particular is called via `CollisionTools::move_object_by_direction_relative_to_size` (CollisionTools.cpp:29) once per bracket iteration per contact per frame. `get_quad()` ignores the cache and recomputes, so the class has two sources of truth for the same four points. Because the copy ctor is user-declared (`= default`, MattMath.h:1050) moves are suppressed, so vector growth and push_back copy rather than move -- see the rule-of-zero finding.

**Fix:** `std::array<Point2F, 4> _points;` and have `calculate_points` return it by value (trivially copyable, no allocation). Build `get_quad()` from `_points`. Then reconsider whether the cache earns its keep at all -- four multiply-adds is likely cheaper than keeping nine mutators coherent.

#### 42. typedef instead of using, and Point2F is a weak alias that lets directions and extents masquerade as points

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:33, 301, 1136` — **low** · `design`

`typedef Vector2F Point2F;` (33), `typedef MattMath::RectangleF AABB;` (301), `typedef RectangleRotated OBB;` (1136). Besides being `typedef` rather than `using`, `Point2F` is a WEAK alias -- the same type as `Vector2F` -- so the distinction it draws carries no meaning and the compiler will never enforce it. The confusion has already leaked into the newest code: `RectangleRotated` uses `Point2F` for things that are unambiguously directions and sizes -- `get_x_axis()`/`get_y_axis()`/`get_axis(int)` (1072-1074), `get_half_extents()` (1075), `set_x_axis`/`set_y_axis` (1081-1082), `set_half_extents` (1083) -- while the corresponding private members are correctly typed `Vector2F` (1115-1117).

**Fix:** Switch all three to `using`. Correct the RectangleRotated axis/extent signatures to `Vector2F` today. Longer term, make `Point2F` a real distinct type so `point + point` does not compile but `point + vector` does.

#### 43. Two different unqualified EPSILON constants 100x apart, and the tests define a third set

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:46` — **low** · `robustness`

`MattMath::EPSILON = 0.0001f` (MattMath.h:46) and `EricsonMath::EPSILON = 0.000001f` (EricsonMath.h:75) -- both `constexpr float EPSILON` at namespace scope, two orders of magnitude apart, with no comment on what either is a tolerance for. MathTests.cpp:9-10 does `using namespace MattMath; using namespace EricsonMath;` in the same file, so an unqualified `EPSILON` there would be ambiguous; the test file works around it by defining a third set -- `MathTestConstants::EPSILON_F` (1e-6), `EPSILON_F_2` (2e-6), `EPSILON_F_100` (1e-4) at MathTests.cpp:14-16 -- which is itself the signal that the tolerance story is unclear. Compounding it, `MattMath::EPSILON` is used as an ABSOLUTE tolerance by `are_equal` (MattMath.cpp:93-99) and applied to unnormalised dot products and world-space lengths (see the edges_valid finding).

**Fix:** Name the constants for what they measure (`ANGLE_EPSILON`, `POSITION_EPSILON`, `UNIT_EPSILON`), add a relative-tolerance overload of `are_equal`, and have the tests use the production constants rather than a private third set.

#### 44. Three separate hand-rolled clamp implementations, and clamp passes NaN straight through

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:51-54, 59-61` — **low** · `modern-cpp`

Verified. MattMath.h:51-54 declares clamp(float), clamp_ref(float&), clamp(int), clamp_ref(int&); the bodies (MattMath.cpp:34-85) are four 12-line if/else ladders that C++17's std::clamp replaces exactly. `Vector2F::clamp`/`clamped` (1739-1748) do not call them — they hand-roll `std::min(std::max(...))` — so one operation exists three ways in one file.

Also verified: `MattMath::clamp` returns NaN unchanged, because `value < min` and `value > max` are both false for NaN. Colour::clamp_colours (2438-2444) is built entirely on it and is the Colour type's only invariant enforcement, so a NaN channel passes through to get_xm_vector() and the sprite batch. The NaN sources (Colour::operator/=(0.0f) at 2298-2306, operator/ at 2465-2468) have no callers, which is why I am grading this low rather than the 'high' one reviewer assigned. There is also no assert that min <= max: clamp(v, 10.0f, 0.0f) returns 10 for every input.

**Fix:** Set <LanguageStandard> and delete MattMath::clamp/clamp_ref in favour of std::clamp; rewrite Vector2F::clamp/clamped in terms of it. Until then, make clamp_colours NaN-safe (`if (!(v >= 0.0f)) v = 0.0f; else if (v > 1.0f) v = 1.0f;`) and guard Colour's division operators against a zero divisor.

#### 45. No [[nodiscard]] anywhere, including on clone() and the pure-query predicates

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:71-88` — **low** · `modern-cpp`

Not one function in the 1139-line header carries the attribute. The places it would actually catch bugs: `virtual std::unique_ptr<Shape> clone() const = 0;` (85) -- discarding it constructs and destroys a shape for nothing; the seven `intersects` predicates per shape plus `contains` and `is_valid` (940, 1108) -- `quad.is_valid();` as a statement is a plausible typo for a check and compiles silently; `RectangleF intersection(const RectangleF&) const` (249), which sits among a pile of mutating `void` members (`inflate`, `scale`, `offset`, `set_*`) so `rect.intersection(other);` reads like an in-place operation and does nothing; `Vector2F normalized() const` (445) next to `void normalize()` (446) -- the same trap; and all the `Camera` factories (1033-1038) and `RectangleF::intersection`/`union_of`/`from_top_left_bottom_right` (290-296).

**Fix:** Mark every const accessor, predicate and factory `[[nodiscard]]`. Mechanical, and the cheapest bug-catching change available in this file.

#### 46. Six pairs of out-parameter / discard intersect overloads where a single optional-returning function belongs

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:99-136, 170-173` — **low** · `design`

Verified. The free API duplicates itself purely to make the contact point optional: rectangle_circle_intersect with and without `Point2F&` (h:99-103), circle_triangle_intersect (123-127), circle_segment_intersect (132-136), segments_intersect with `float& t, Point2F& p` and without (170-173). The discard overloads declare a dummy and throw it away (MattMath.cpp:314, 344, 578-579).

I reject the reviewers' sub-claim that these pass *uninitialised* dummies: Point2F is Vector2F, whose members have default initialisers (`float x = 0.0f;` at MattMath.h:404-405), so `Point2F point;` is value-correct. The `float t;` at 578 genuinely is uninitialised but is never read. So this is API duplication, not a correctness bug — graded low accordingly.

**Fix:** With C++17, collapse each pair into one function returning std::optional<Point2F> (or an optional Contact{point, t}). That removes the parallel overload set and the throwaway dummies in one change.

#### 47. Out-parameters where a return value belongs, each needing a hand-written discarding twin

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:100, 124, 133, 170-171` — **low** · `modern-cpp`

`rectangle_circle_intersect(..., Point2F& point)` (100), `circle_triangle_intersect(..., Point2F& point)` (124), `circle_segment_intersect(..., Point2F& point)` (133) and `segments_intersect(..., float& t, Point2F& p)` (170-171) each require a manually written "I don't care" overload that declares a dummy local purely to throw it away -- MattMath.cpp:312-317, 342-346, 576-581. `MattMath::clamp_ref(float&, ...)` / `clamp_ref(int&, ...)` (52, 54) and `Camera::calculate_view_rectangle(RectangleF&)` (1023) are the same anti-pattern for pure functions.
