CORRECTION to the candidate: it claims `t` is "read uninitialised" in the wrapper at 576-581 -- it is not. `t` is declared uninitialised and passed by reference, but the wrapper never reads it back, so there is no UB, only a pointless local.

**Fix:** Define `struct SegmentHit { float t; Point2F point; };` and return `std::optional<SegmentHit>` (needs the standard bump). That collapses each pair of overloads into one and makes "no hit means no point" unrepresentable. Delete `clamp_ref` in favour of `value = std::clamp(value, lo, hi)`.

#### 48. `X(const X&) = default;` on every type suppresses the implicit move constructor and move assignment

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:192, 687, 1050` — **low** · `modern-cpp`

Verified on 17 types: RectangleF (h:192), Vector2I (360), Vector2F (408), RectangleI (516), Vector4F (575), Colour (594), Vector3F (662), MatrixF (687), Matrix3x3F (753), Viewport (778), Circle (814), Triangle (847), TriangleRightAxisAligned (898), Quad (923), Segment (988), Camera (1013), RectangleRotated (1050). A user-declared copy constructor — `= default` still counts — suppresses both implicit move operations, so all 17 are copy-only.

For the plain-float types this is harmless noise. It costs real work on the only two that own heap memory: RectangleRotated holds `std::vector<Point2F> _points` (h:1119-1120) and MatrixF holds `std::vector<float> _elements` (h:723). Every apparent move of those — vector reallocation, NRVO failures, `*this = MattMath::add(*this, other)` in MatrixF::operator+= (MattMath.cpp:2673) — is a deep copy plus a fresh allocation. Graded low because RectangleRotated should not have a heap vector at all (separate finding) and MatrixF should be deleted.

**Fix:** Delete every `X(const X&) = default;` line. They add nothing — the implicit copy constructor already exists and does the same thing — and they are the sole reason move operations are missing. Rule of zero.

#### 49. No [[nodiscard]] anywhere, on an API built from confusable const/mutating name pairs

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:204-291` — **low** · `modern-cpp`

Verified: `grep -c nodiscard ArtAttack/MattMath.h` returns 0. This API is the textbook case for it, because it deliberately pairs a const version and a mutating version under near-identical names: `Vector2F normalized() const` vs `void normalize()` (h:445-446), `Vector2F clamped(...) const` vs `void clamp(...)` (h:450-451), and `RectangleF intersection(const RectangleF&) const` (h:249) sitting inside a block of mutators (inflate, scale_at_center, offset, h:256-267). Writing `rect.intersection(other);` or `v.clamped(a,b);` as a statement compiles silently and does nothing. Same for every factory: intersection(a,b), union_of, from_top_left_bottom_right, Vector2F::lerp/min_vec/max_vec/unit_vector/rotate_vector, Camera::calculate_*, and Shape::clone (h:85) — discarding a clone leaks nothing thanks to unique_ptr, but silently drops the object.

**Fix:** After moving to C++17, add [[nodiscard]] to every const accessor and static factory in MattMath.h, starting with the const/mutator pairs where the diagnostic maps directly onto a real class of bug.

#### 50. RectangleF exposes ~70 members over four public floats, including a 20-strong hand-enumerated anchor cross-product

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:256-291` — **low** · `design`

Verified. Between h:256 and h:291: inflate x3, inflate_to_size x2, scale_at_center x3, offset x2, scale x2, scale_size_and_position x2, set_position x2, set_position_at_center x2, set_position_x, set_position_x_from_right, set_position_y, set_position_y_from_bottom, set_position_from_top_right x2, set_position_from_bottom_left x2, set_position_from_bottom_right x2, set_size x2, set_width, set_height. That is {which anchor} x {Vector2F or two floats} enumerated by hand — and incompletely: there is set_position_x_from_right but no set_position_from_top_left. h:208-211 also duplicates the public fields with get_x/get_y/get_width/get_height.

I spot-checked the reviewers' zero-caller claims and they hold for union_of, set_position_from_bottom_left/right, set_position_x_from_right, Vector2F::is_contained_within, min_vec, max_vec, angle_between, vec_from_angle_magnitude, cross, sign, rotate_vector_by_ref, Vector4F, MatrixF, Matrix3x3F and Viewport::get_d3d_viewport_ptr.

**Fix:** Delete the zero-caller members. Replace the positioning family with one anchor-based call — `void set_position(Vector2F, anchor = anchor::top_left)` — using a small enum (direction.h already contains a TOP_LEFT..BOTTOM_RIGHT enum that could be repurposed and namespaced). Drop get_x/get_y/get_width/get_height.

#### 51. from_top_left_bottom_right's float overload takes (top, left, bottom, right) while its sibling takes (top-left, bottom-right)

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:293-296` — **low** · `design`

Verified. The Vector2F overload takes a top-left *point* then a bottom-right *point*, i.e. (x,y) then (x,y). The float overload takes (top, left, bottom, right) — y, x, y, x, the opposite pairing. The definition at MattMath.cpp:1129-1133 is internally consistent with its parameter names (`return RectangleF(left, top, right - left, bottom - top);`), but a caller mirroring the sibling will write `from_top_left_bottom_right(left, top, right, bottom)` and get x and y transposed with width/height swapped — no diagnostic possible, all four parameters are float. Zero callers; both live uses (LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:51, 94) take the Vector2F form. A landmine, not a live bug.

**Fix:** Delete the float overload. If a scalar form is wanted, name it so the signature and the name agree: `from_ltrb(float left, float top, float right, float bottom)`.

#### 52. Matrix3x3F publicly inherits MatrixF, which has no virtual destructor and value-semantic operators

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:750-765` — **low** · `design`

Verified. `struct Matrix3x3F : MatrixF` (h:750) where MatrixF (684-727) declares no destructor and no virtual member at all. Three hazards: deleting through a MatrixF* is UB with no protection (no virtual dtor, no protected dtor); MatrixF::operator= is public and implicit, so `MatrixF& r = m3x3; r = MatrixF(5,7);` turns a '3x3' into one claiming 5 rows and 7 columns while still statically typed Matrix3x3F; and the free operators (h:729-732) return MatrixF, so composing two Matrix3x3F transforms yields a MatrixF that cannot be fed back without re-validation.

Graded low rather than medium only because the whole subsystem is unreachable dead code — but combined with the uninitialised _elements defect, Matrix3x3F is not usable as written under any circumstances.

**Fix:** Delete both types. If a 3x3 transform is ever wanted, make it a distinct type over std::array<float,9> — constexpr-friendly, allocation-free, with its own operators returning Matrix3x3F.

#### 53. Inconsistent return conventions across the shape accessors: by-value, by-const-ref and fresh-vector all coexist for the same operation

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:862-865, 942-946, 1087-1091` — **low** · `design`

For the same conceptual operation the three shapes each pick differently. Element accessors: `Triangle::get_point_0..2()` return `const Vector2F&` (862-864); `Quad::get_point_0..3()` return `const Point2F&` (942-945); `RectangleRotated::get_point_0..3()` return `Point2F` BY VALUE (1087-1090) despite `_points` being a stable member. Plural accessors: `Triangle::get_points()` returns a freshly built `std::vector` (MattMath.cpp:3485-3489); `Quad::get_points()` likewise (3871-3881); `RectangleRotated::get_points()` returns `const std::vector<Point2F>&` (1091). A consumer cannot form any expectation about whether a getter costs an allocation, and two of the three silently do.

**Fix:** Standardise: element accessors return `const T&`, plural accessors return `const std::array<T,N>&` over storage the shape already holds. That also removes all three fresh-vector allocations.

#### 54. Untyped int axis/edge selectors validated with a runtime throw, and a -1 sentinel where an optional belongs

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:893, 1074, 1078` — **low** · `design`

`RectangleRotated::get_axis(int)` (MattMath.cpp:4315-4327) and `get_half_width(int)` (4340-4352) accept only 0 and 1 and otherwise throw from a const accessor; `Triangle::calculate_gradient(int edge)` (3594-3603) throws for anything outside 0..2. A two- or three-valued selector passed as `int` and checked at runtime is a compile-time check thrown away -- `get_axis(2)` should not compile, and today it throws from deep inside collision code (that is exactly how `closest_pt_point_OBB` fails). `TriangleRightAxisAligned::find_hypotenuse` (3665-3684) compounds it by returning `-1` for "not a right triangle", which both callers then re-check with two copies of the same three-line guard (3636-3639, 3646-3649).

**Fix:** Introduce `enum class axis { x, y };` and store the axes in a `std::array<Vector2F,2>` so the accessor is total and cannot throw. Return `std::optional<int>` (or an `enum class edge`) from `find_hypotenuse` and share one guard.

#### 55. Namespace-scope shape/camera constants are dynamically initialised, creating cross-TU initialisation-order dependencies

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:1044, 1115-1116` — **low** · `modern-cpp`

Merges 2 candidates. `Camera::DEFAULT_CAMERA` (declared 1044, defined MattMath.cpp:4180 as `{ Vector2F::ZERO, 1.0f }`) is byte-identical to a default-constructed `Camera` (NSDMIs at 1009-1010 already give ZERO and 1.0f); it exists only because no constructor is `constexpr`. Same for `Vector2F::ZERO`/`DIRECTION_*` (MattMath.cpp:1907-1916, where 1913-1916 even call `unit_vector()` at dynamic-init time), `RectangleF::ZERO` (1134), `Vector2I::ZERO` (1495), `RectangleI::ZERO` (2138). These are dynamically initialised statics whose cross-TU ordering is unspecified, and other TUs already read them at namespace scope: `DebugText.h:14` is `const static MattMath::Vector2F DEBUG_POSITION = MattMath::Vector2F::ZERO;`, copied from a static defined in a different TU. Harmless today only because the pre-dynamic zero value happens to be correct. `RectangleRotated`'s NSDMIs (1115-1116) read `DIRECTION_RIGHT`/`DIRECTION_UP`, so any future namespace-scope OBB inherits the hazard.

**Fix:** Give the simple value types `constexpr` constructors and declare the constants `static constexpr` in-class (C++17 makes them implicitly inline). Delete `DEFAULT_CAMERA` in favour of `Camera{}`. Requires the standard bump above.

#### 56. Dead private calculate_points(Segment, float) overload, and neither parameterised overload touches `this`

`ArtAttack/MattMath.h:1128-1129` — **low** · `design`

`std::vector<Point2F> calculate_points(const Segment& center_line, float thickness) const;` (1128-1129, defined MattMath.cpp:4501-4510) is never called from anywhere -- grep across the whole tree finds only its own definition. The constructor it was clearly written for (4201-4215) inlines the same four lines instead, which is exactly how the two copies drifted apart (both carry the same missing-normalisation bug). Both parameterised overloads (4487-4499 and 4501-4510) are `const` non-static member functions that never read a single member; they are pure functions of their arguments.

**Fix:** Delete the Segment/thickness overload and have the constructor delegate to the 4-argument primary constructor. Make the remaining parameterised overload `static` (or a free function in an anonymous namespace in the .cpp).

## `ArtAttack/MenuData.h`

_3 findings: 1 high, 2 medium_

#### 1. Menu data classes inherit a copy of the whole GameData service locator, and publish results by writing through raw out-pointers

`ArtAttack/MenuData.h:7-17` — **high** · `design`

`class MenuData : public GameData` with `MenuData::MenuData(const GameData* game_data) : GameData(game_data)` (MenuData.cpp:4-8) does not reference the master GameData — `GameData::GameData(const GameData*)` (GameData.cpp:4-19) copies all 13 raw pointers field by field. Each `MainMenuData`/`PauseMenuData`/`EndMenuData`/`ResultsMenuData` is therefore an independent frozen snapshot of `ResourceManager*`, `CommonStates*`, `ThreadPool*`, `ViewportManager*`, `Partitioner*`, `vector<SpriteBatch*>*` and `float* _dt`. Those are not stable: `Game::OnDeviceRestored()` (Game.cpp:283-287) calls `create_device_dependent_resources()`, which builds a new `ResourceManager` (Game.cpp:239), `ThreadPool` (236), `ViewportManager` (247), `CommonStates` (252), `Partitioner` (255) and `_dt` (244) and publishes them only on the master GameData. `Game::OnDeviceLost()` (269-279) resets all 16 SpriteBatches and `_states` while `MenuPage::get_point_clamp_sampler_state()` (MenuPage.cpp:180-183) dereferences `get_common_states()` on every page draw. After one device-lost/restore cycle a live page's whole draw path is use-after-free. On top of that each subclass bolts the page's OUTPUT channel on as a raw pointer (`MainMenuData::_is_ready_to_load_level` bool*, `PauseMenuData::_action`, `EndMenuData::_action`, `ResultsMenuData::_action`), so pages publish results by pointer-writing into parent-owned memory (`*get_pause_menu_data()->get_action() = pause_menu_action::QUIT`, PauseMenu.cpp:242-243) that the parent polls after `update()` (GameStates.cpp:188-240). Input, services and output are fused into one inherited bag, so no page can be constructed or tested without the whole engine.

**Fix:** Stop deriving the per-screen data classes from GameData — hold a `const GameData*` (better: a narrow `UIServices` interface with only what menus need). Return the result from `update()` instead of writing it through a raw pointer, so the compiler can tell you a page forgot to set it.

#### 2. Every menu header transitively pulls in D3D11, XAudio2, the thread pool and the save system, and MenuPage.h is not self-sufficient

`ArtAttack/MenuData.h:4-5` — **medium** · `header-hygiene`

`MenuData.h` includes `GameData.h`, which includes ResolutionManager.h, Save.h, ResourceLoader.h, ResourceManager.h, DeviceResources.h, ViewportManager.h, ThreadPool.h and Partitioner.h. `MenuPage.h` includes `MenuData.h`, and every page header includes `MenuPage.h` — so `MainMenu.h`, a file that describes buttons and labels, drags in the entire platform layer. Conversely `MenuPage.h` uses `std::vector`, `std::pair`, `std::string`, `ID3D11DeviceContext`, `ID3D11CommandList`, `ID3D11SamplerState` and `DirectX::SpriteBatch` without including `<vector>`, `<utility>`, `<string>` or `<d3d11.h>`; it compiles only because every .cpp includes `pch.h` first and because MenuData.h happens to pull them in. It also includes `Mh.h` solely for `MObject*` in three declarations. `MainMenu.h:11`, `PauseMenu.h:8` and `EndMenu.h:8` include `StateContext.h` although `State.h:3` already forward-declares `StateContext` and only the .cpp calls `transition_to`.

**Fix:** Include what you use (`<vector>`, `<utility>`, `<string>`, `<d3d11.h>`) and forward-declare the rest (`class MObject; class MenuData; class ResolutionManager; class Save; class ResourceManager; class ViewportManager; namespace DirectX { class SpriteBatch; }`). Move `#include "StateContext.h"` into the .cpps. Introduce narrow UI-facing interfaces so no UI header includes d3d11.h at all.

#### 3. Game UI state classes inherit from the engine's service-locator, so engine wiring is a base class of game data

`ArtAttack/MenuData.h:7 (and MainMenuData.h:8, PauseMenuData.h:7, ResultsMenuData.h:8, EndMenuData.h:7)` — **medium** · `design` · confidence: certain

`class MenuData : public GameData` (MenuData.h:7), then `MainMenuData : public MenuData` (MainMenuData.h:8), `PauseMenuData`, `ResultsMenuData`, `EndMenuData` — a 3-deep inheritance chain rooted in `GameData`, which is the engine's 12-pointer service bag (`Save*`, `ResolutionManager*`, `float* _dt`, `ResourceManager*`, `GamePad*`, `DeviceResources*`, `ViewportManager*`, `CommonStates*`, `std::vector<SpriteBatch*>*`, `ThreadPool*`, `const Partitioner*`, `HWND`; GameData.h:49-61).

This is inheritance used for field concatenation, and it runs the wrong way across the boundary: game screens *are-a* engine service locator. Each level slices a copy of all 12 pointers (`GameData::GameData(const GameData*)`, GameData.cpp:4-20), so `MainMenuData` carries three copies' worth of engine plumbing. Nothing polymorphic is ever done with the base — `GameData` has no virtuals and no virtual destructor, so any `delete` through a `GameData*` is UB.

(Incidentally `GameData::get_thread_pool()` contains a duplicated unreachable `return this->_thread_pool;` at GameData.cpp:144-145.)

**Fix:** Compose, don't inherit: `class MainMenuData { EngineServices* _services; MenuInput* _input; MenuLevelSettings* _settings; bool* _ready; };`. Rename `GameData` to `EngineServices` (or better, split it — most consumers want 2-3 of the 12 pointers, not all of them) and move it engine-side with no game type ever deriving from it.

## `ArtAttack/MenuInput.cpp`

_4 findings: 1 high, 2 medium, 1 low_

#### 1. MenuInput returns a compacted vector, so the input index silently stops matching the player index

`ArtAttack/MenuInput.cpp:131-150` — **high** · `api-design`

```cpp
std::vector<ProcessedMenuInput> result;
for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
    if (current[i].connected) { result.push_back(calculate_menu_input(current[i], _prev_inputs[i])); }
    this->_prev_inputs[i] = current[i];
}
```
Every consumer treats the returned index as a player index: `MainMenuTeamSelect::update` drives `_select_states[i]` from `inputs[i]` (MainMenu.cpp:1160-1213), `MainMenuWeaponSelect::update` (1443), `MainMenuStageSelect::update` (1790), and PauseMenu via `inputs[player_num]`. If pad slot 0 is empty and slots 1/2 are populated, `inputs[0]` is pad 1's state and it drives player 0; unplug a pad mid-menu and every remaining player's controller shifts by one. Compounding this, `calculate_menu_input` unconditionally sets `result.connection = connection_state::CONNECTED;` (MenuInput.cpp:127), so `connection_state::DISCONNECTED` (declared in ProcessedMenuInput, MenuInput.h:41, and in connection_state.h) is unreachable — the one field whose entire purpose is reporting a dropped pad is dead weight. The literal `4` is hardcoded at MenuInput.h:50 and MenuInput.cpp:133, 134, 139 with no named constant even though `menu_input_consts` sits at MenuInput.h:9-13.

**Fix:** Return `const std::array<ProcessedMenuInput, MAX_PLAYERS>&` indexed by gamepad slot, with `connection` set honestly from `current[i].connected`, and introduce `constexpr int MAX_PLAYERS = 4` in a shared header. Index == player becomes true by construction, the bounds hazard disappears, and menus can render "Player 3: controller disconnected" instead of hanging.

#### 2. `throw new std::exception` in two branches that are provably unreachable dead code

`ArtAttack/MenuInput.cpp:60-66` — **medium** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

Two problems in one construct, twice.

First, the branches cannot execute. At MenuInput.cpp:48-70:

```cpp
if (proceed)      { result.action = PROCEED; }
else if (back)    { result.action = BACK; }
else if (pause)   { result.action = PAUSE; }
else if ((proceed && back) || (proceed && pause) || (pause && back))   // line 60 - unreachable
{
    throw new std::exception("2 or more of proceed, back or pause pressed at same time");   // line 64
}
```

Reaching line 60 requires `!proceed && !back && !pause`, which makes every disjunct false. The check is also redundant by construction: `prev_proceed` already requires `!previous.back && !previous.pause` (lines 41-43), so the three flags are mutually exclusive before the chain begins. Identical dead branch for the direction chain at MenuInput.cpp:118-122 (`else if (up && down && left && right)` after `if (up) / else if (down) / else if (left) / else if (right)`).

Second, and worse if either branch were ever reachable: `throw new std::exception(...)` throws a `std::exception*`, not a `std::exception`. No `catch (const std::exception&)` anywhere would match it, so it would propagate to `std::terminate`, and the heap allocation would leak. These are the only two `throw new` sites in the project - every other throw site (58 of them) uses `throw std::exception("...")` by value.

As a bonus, `std::exception(const char*)` is an MSVC-only extension, so none of this is portable off the Microsoft STL.

**Fix:** Delete both branches - they encode an invariant the code above already guarantees. If a real invariant check is wanted, use an assertion. Never `throw new`; and prefer `std::runtime_error`/`std::logic_error` with a message over MSVC's non-standard `std::exception(const char*)`.

#### 3. Menu stick navigation has no hysteresis - PRESENCE and ABSENCE thresholds are both 0.8, so stick jitter repeats moves

`ArtAttack/MenuInput.cpp:72-87` — **medium** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

The two constants exist specifically to form a hysteresis band and are set to the same value:

```cpp
constexpr float DIGITAL_PRESENCE_THRESHOLD = 0.8f;   // MenuInput.h:11
constexpr float DIGITAL_ABSENCE_THRESHOLD  = 0.8f;   // MenuInput.h:12
```

They are then used as the two ends of an edge test that is consequently a bare threshold crossing:

```cpp
bool analog_down = previous.left_analog_stick.y > DIGITAL_PRESENCE_THRESHOLD &&
                   current.left_analog_stick.y  < DIGITAL_ABSENCE_THRESHOLD;   // MenuInput.cpp:72-75
```

With presence == absence this reduces to `prev > 0.8 && cur < 0.8`, i.e. it fires on *any* crossing of 0.8, in either direction of noise. Identical for up (76-79), left (80-83) and right (84-87).

Compounding it, `MenuInput::get_raw_input` deliberately asks for unfiltered axes: `GetState(gamepad_num, GamePad::DEAD_ZONE_NONE)` (MenuInput.cpp:19). So a worn or drifting stick parked around 0.80 produces prev>0.8 / cur<0.8 repeatedly and the menu highlight walks by itself at up to 60 moves/second, each one also firing `play_wave(DIRECTION_SOUND)` (e.g. MainMenu.cpp:172).

Separately, note the navigation is release-triggered (the move fires when the stick returns *below* threshold, not when it is pushed), which makes menus feel laggy and gives no auto-repeat when a direction is held - but that at least is a deliberate choice; the missing hysteresis is not.

**Fix:** Set `DIGITAL_PRESENCE_THRESHOLD` meaningfully above `DIGITAL_ABSENCE_THRESHOLD` (e.g. 0.7 / 0.4) so the edge test has a real dead band, and switch `get_raw_input` to `DEAD_ZONE_CIRCULAR` so drift is filtered before it reaches the comparison. Consider trigger-on-press with a repeat delay rather than trigger-on-release.

#### 4. Two unreachable validation branches, both of which throw a raw pointer

`ArtAttack/MenuInput.cpp:60-66, 118-122` — **low** · `correctness`

```cpp
if (proceed) {...} else if (back) {...} else if (pause) {...}
else if ((proceed && back) || (proceed && pause) || (pause && back))
{ throw new std::exception("2 or more of proceed, back or pause pressed at same time"); }
```
The guard is a tautological false: to reach line 60, all three flags must already be false. It is doubly dead because `prev_proceed`/`prev_back`/`prev_pause` are constructed mutually exclusive at lines 41-43. Identical at 118-122: `else if (up && down && left && right)` after `if(up)/else if(down)/else if(left)/else if(right)`. Both statements also `throw new std::exception(...)`, which throws a **`std::exception*`** — no `catch (const std::exception&)` will ever match it, it can only be caught by pointer, and the allocation leaks. These are the only two `throw new` sites in first-party code; every other throw in the codebase constructs by value. `std::exception(const char*)` is also an MSVC-only extension. Severity is low only because neither branch can execute.

**Fix:** Delete both branches — the mutual exclusivity is established by construction, so there is no error condition left to report. If a defensive check is genuinely wanted, compute it before the dispatch chain and `throw std::logic_error(...)` by value. Never `throw new`.

## `ArtAttack/MenuPage.cpp`

_10 findings: 2 high, 6 medium, 2 low_

#### 1. Menu drawing throws from inside Win32 thread-pool callbacks, which terminates the process

`ArtAttack/MenuPage.cpp:94-121, 140-150` — **high** · `robustness`

`draw_mobject_in_viewports` throws on two paths — `throw std::exception("Deferred context not created")` (line 96) and `throw std::exception("Failed to finish command list")` (line 120) — and is only ever reached from the lambda submitted at lines 142-149. `ThreadPool::work_callback` (ThreadPool.cpp:59-65) is `void CALLBACK f(...) { (*task)(); delete task; }` with no try/catch, so an escaping exception unwinds out of an OS callback and calls `std::terminate`; `delete task` is also skipped and every sibling task's already-created `ID3D11CommandList` leaks because the `Release()` loop at MenuPage.cpp:154-163 never runs. Worse, `DeviceResources::get_deferred_context(int)` — called at MenuPage.cpp:175 from inside the same worker — is declared **`noexcept`** (DeviceResources.cpp:737-738) and unconditionally `throw std::out_of_range("Invalid index.")` on a bad index, which is a guaranteed immediate `std::terminate` rather than a catchable error. `ResourceManager`/`SpriteSheet` lookups reached through `MObject::draw` can also throw. A device reset or a missing asset while a menu is on screen kills the process with no diagnostics.

**Fix:** Wrap the task body in `try { ... } catch (...) { store exception_ptr }` inside `ThreadPool::work_callback` and rethrow on the calling thread after `wait_for_tasks_to_complete()`. Remove `noexcept` from `get_deferred_context` or make it return nullptr. Store `Microsoft::WRL::ComPtr<ID3D11CommandList>` so release is automatic on every path.

#### 2. Menu pages draw once per viewport of a stale screen_layout, tiling the main menu after a multiplayer quit

`ArtAttack/MenuPage.cpp:99-115` — **high** · `correctness`

`MenuPage::draw_mobject_in_viewports` loops over whatever `ViewportManager` currently reports (lines 99-115) and draws the widget once per viewport. That is right for the pause menu; the main menu uses the identical path. `ViewportManager::set_layout` is called from exactly two places in the whole codebase — `GameStates.cpp:122-123` (on level start, sets the match layout) and `Level.cpp:618` (only inside `draw_zoom_out_level_component`, reached on the level-end zoom-out). Nothing resets the layout on the quit path: `GameLevel::update` case `pause_menu_action::QUIT` (GameStates.cpp:203-212) transitions straight to `GameMenu` with `screen = HOME`, and `GameMenu::init` (GameStates.cpp:19-62) never touches the viewport manager. So after a 3- or 4-player match, pause -> Quit leaves `_layout == FOUR_PLAYER` and `MainMenuHome` is rendered four times, once into each quadrant.

**Fix:** Have `GameMenu::init()` call `get_viewport_manager()->set_layout(screen_layout::ONE_PLAYER)`. Longer term split the API: `draw_in_all_viewports()` for in-match overlays vs `draw_fullscreen()` for the front-end, so the front-end does not depend on residual match state.

#### 3. Widget draws do string-keyed std::map lookups on a non-const map concurrently from thread-pool workers

`ArtAttack/MenuPage.cpp:112` — **medium** · `correctness`

`widget->draw(sprite_batch, viewports[i])` (MenuPage.cpp:112) bottoms out in string-keyed lookups on every draw. `TextObject::draw` calls `get_resource_manager()->get_sprite_font(this->_font_name)` (TextObject.cpp:27-30), and `ResourceManager::get_sprite_font` is a NON-const member whose body is `return this->_sprite_fonts[font_name].get();` wrapped in a `try/catch (const std::out_of_range&)` that can never fire because `operator[]` does not throw (ResourceManager.cpp:27-38). `SpriteSheet::draw` does `this->_sprite_frames[frame_name].get_source_rectangle()` (SpriteSheet.cpp:105) — same pattern. Two consequences: (a) a missing key makes `operator[]` DEFAULT-CONSTRUCT AND INSERT, so a misspelled font silently returns nullptr into `sprite_font->DrawString(...)` and a misspelled sprite frame silently draws a garbage source rect, with the dead catch block guaranteeing no diagnostic; (b) `draw_mobjects_in_viewports` dispatches these draws to two thread-pool workers concurrently (MenuPage.cpp:142-149), so two threads call a non-const `std::map::operator[]` on the same map in the same frame — a data race by the standard's rules, and a structural mutation of shared state if a key is ever absent.

**Fix:** Make every ResourceManager/SpriteSheet getter `const` and use `.find()`/`.at()` so a missing key is a diagnosable error rather than a silent insert. Resolve `SpriteFont*`/`SpriteSheet*`/`SpriteFrame` once in the widget constructor and cache the raw pointer, so the per-frame draw does no lookup at all.

#### 4. Every menu frame spins up the thread pool, partitioner and a 16-entry command-list array to draw two objects

`ArtAttack/MenuPage.cpp:124-164` — **medium** · `performance`

Every page's `draw()` builds the same 2-element vector and hands it to `draw_mobjects_in_viewports`, which per frame: allocates `std::vector<ID3D11CommandList*> command_lists(16, nullptr)` (128); allocates a partition vector via `Partitioner::partition(2, 16)` (134-135); submits two thread-pool tasks — and `ThreadPool::add_task` takes `std::function` BY VALUE and then heap-copies it again into `new std::function<void()>(task)` (ThreadPool.cpp:39-40), so four allocations plus two `CreateThreadpoolWork` calls; blocks on `wait_for_tasks_to_complete()` which does `WaitForThreadpoolWorkCallbacks` + `CloseThreadpoolWork` per item; then two `FinishCommandList` + two `ExecuteCommandList` + two `Release`. All to issue on the order of ten sprite draws. On the main menu (one viewport, ~6 widgets) this is pure overhead on the critical path of every frame.

**Fix:** Draw menus directly on the immediate context with one `Begin`/`End` pair per sampler state. If the deferred path must be kept for symmetry with `Level`, skip the thread pool below a threshold and reuse a persistent `command_lists` buffer instead of reallocating per frame.

#### 5. Thread-pool tasks capture caller stack locals by reference with no RAII guarantee that the wait is reached

`ArtAttack/MenuPage.cpp:124-150` — **medium** · `lifetime`

std::vector<ID3D11CommandList*> command_lists(deferred_contexts->size(), nullptr);   // :128 stack local
    auto partitioned_mobjects = partitioner->partition(mobjects->size(), num_threads);   // :134 stack local
    for (int i = 0; i < partitioned_mobjects.size(); i++)
        thread_pool->add_task([this, i, &partitioned_mobjects, mobjects, deferred_contexts,
            &command_lists, sprite_batches]() { ... });                                   // :142-148 BY REFERENCE
    thread_pool->wait_for_tasks_to_complete();                                            // :150

Two stack locals are captured by reference into work items running on OS thread-pool threads; their validity depends entirely on line 150 being reached. It can be skipped: `add_task` itself throws on `CreateThreadpoolWork` failure (ThreadPool.cpp:44), and the task bodies throw (`throw std::exception("Failed to finish command list")`, MenuPage.cpp:120). Either unwinds past line 150 while tasks 0..i-1 are still writing into `command_lists` — a cross-thread write into a destroyed stack frame. Nothing waits on unwind: `ThreadPool` has no scope guard and its destructor is not reached (the pool is owned by Game).

The analogous `Level::draw_active_level` (Level.cpp:386-397) captures `partitioned_players` BY VALUE and `command_lists` as a caller-owned raw pointer. The two sites disagree about the rule, which is the underlying problem: there is no stated contract about what a task may capture.

**Fix:** Make the wait un-skippable with RAII: a `ThreadPool::TaskBatch batch(pool);` whose destructor calls `wait_for_tasks_to_complete()`, with `add_task` on the batch. Then state in the header that tasks may capture references to anything outliving the batch, and stop copying `partitioned_players` at Level.cpp:388.

#### 6. Partition index doubles as object index and as deferred-context / SpriteBatch / command-list index

`ArtAttack/MenuPage.cpp:124-178` — **medium** · `design` · confidence: certain

```cpp
void MenuPage::draw_range_of_mobjects_in_viewports(int start, int end, ...)
{
    for (int i = start; i < end; i++)
        this->draw_mobject_in_viewports(
            this->get_data()->get_device_resources()->get_deferred_context(i),
            command_lists->at(i), sprite_batches->at(i), mobjects->at(i).first, ...);
}
```

The loop variable `i` is simultaneously (a) an index into the *mobject* list and (b) an index into the deferred-context / SpriteBatch / command-list arrays. That is only accidentally safe: it works because partitions are disjoint index ranges *and* because every menu page happens to push exactly 2 mobjects. Push a 17th drawable and `at(i)` throws `std::out_of_range` inside a worker — which, per the missing exception barrier, kills the process.

`Level::draw_player_view_level` has the identical conflation (Level.cpp:496-506): `i` indexes `_player_objects`, `deferred_contexts`, `sprite_batches` and `command_lists` all at once, while `player_num` (from the player object) indexes viewports — two different index spaces silently assumed to line up.

Related inconsistency: `Level` calls `FinishCommandList(TRUE, ...)` (Level.cpp:587, 646) and `ExecuteCommandList(..., TRUE)` (GameStates.cpp:328) — restoring context state on both ends, which is the expensive option — while `MenuPage` uses `FALSE` for both (MenuPage.cpp:117, 161). No comment explains why.

**Fix:** Give each worker a single `RenderThreadContext { ID3D11DeviceContext*; SpriteBatch*; ID3D11CommandList** }` selected by *thread/partition* index, and iterate objects with a separate index. Then the number of drawables is decoupled from the size of the deferred-context pool. Pick one `FinishCommandList`/`ExecuteCommandList` restore policy and document it.

#### 7. The mobject index is silently reused as the deferred-context, sprite-batch and command-list index

`ArtAttack/MenuPage.cpp:166-178` — **medium** · `design`

```cpp
for (int i = start; i < end; i++)
    this->draw_mobject_in_viewports(
        get_data()->get_device_resources()->get_deferred_context(i),
        command_lists->at(i), sprite_batches->at(i),
        mobjects->at(i).first, mobjects->at(i).second);
```
`i` indexes four unrelated containers. The conflation is visible one frame up: `command_lists` is sized from the CONTEXT count (`std::vector<ID3D11CommandList*> command_lists(deferred_contexts->size(), nullptr);`, MenuPage.cpp:128) while the partitioning at 134-135 is over `mobjects->size()`. The unwritten, unasserted invariant is `mobjects.size() <= 16` (`NUM_THREADS_MAX`, Game.h:14). Exceed it and `get_deferred_context(i)` throws `std::out_of_range` from a `noexcept` function inside a thread-pool worker — instant `std::terminate`. There is no assert and no comment. The partitioning is also pointless at this size: `Partitioner::partition(2, 16)` (Partitioner.cpp:4-22, loop bounded by `i < num_partitions && i < num_elements`) yields exactly two single-element ranges, so two OS work items are dispatched to record one sprite each, with a full barrier.

**Fix:** Bind the context/batch/command-list to the partition ordinal, not the mobject index, and assert `mobjects->size() <= deferred_contexts->size()`. For two mobjects, drop the thread pool and record on one deferred context.

#### 8. `get_menu_inputs() const` is a stateful edge-consuming poll disguised as a const getter

`ArtAttack/MenuPage.cpp:185-188` — **medium** · `design` · confidence: certain

```cpp
std::vector<ProcessedMenuInput> MenuPage::get_menu_inputs() const   // declared const, MenuPage.h:53
{
    return this->get_data()->get_input()->update_and_get_menu_inputs();
}
```

`update_and_get_menu_inputs` advances `MenuInput::_prev_inputs` (MenuInput.cpp:147), and every action in the system is edge-detected against that previous frame (`proceed = prev_proceed && no_press_current`, MenuInput.cpp:44). So calling this "getter" *consumes* the edge: a second call in the same frame returns all-NONE, and the caller that would have handled the press silently gets nothing.

The `const` qualifier actively misleads - it advertises that the call is side-effect-free when it mutates the global input state for the whole frame. It compiles only because the mutation happens through a raw `MenuInput*` (`MenuData::get_input()`, MenuData.cpp:16), which const does not propagate through.

Today every page happens to call it exactly once at the top of `update()` (MainMenu.cpp:49, 133, 302, 647, 882, 1156, 1439, 1786; PauseMenu.cpp:48, 217; EndMenu.cpp:28), so the bug is latent rather than live. But it is one refactor away: any page that adds a helper needing input, or any nested `StateContext` that updates two pages in a frame, will silently drop presses with no diagnostic.

Same shape on the gameplay side - `PlayerInput::update_and_get_player_inputs()` is called once per frame at GameStates.cpp:142 and its result threaded manually to both `check_for_pause_input` (line 145) and `Level::update` (line 185), because a second call would eat the pause edge.

**Fix:** Split polling from reading: have the owning state (`GameMenu`/`GameLevel`) call `MenuInput::update()` exactly once per frame and cache the snapshot, then have `MenuPage::get_menu_inputs() const` return a `const&` to that cached snapshot. That makes the const honest and makes double-reads harmless.

#### 9. Viewport list is rebuilt per widget per frame, and Begin/End is issued per widget per viewport

`ArtAttack/MenuPage.cpp:99-115` — **low** · `performance`

```cpp
std::vector<Viewport> viewports = this->get_viewport_manager()->get_all_viewports();
for (size_t i = 0; i < num_viewports; i++) {
    apply_player_viewport(i, deferred_context, sprite_batch);
    sprite_batch->Begin(SpriteSortMode_Deferred, nullptr, sampler_state);
    widget->draw(sprite_batch, viewports[i]);
    sprite_batch->End();
}
```
`ViewportManager::get_all_viewports()` (ViewportManager.cpp:89-103) builds and returns a fresh `std::vector<Viewport>` on every call — once per MObject per frame — even though the layout only changes on `set_layout`. And `Begin`/`End` is issued per widget PER VIEWPORT rather than once per viewport: in four-player split-screen that is 2 widgets x 4 viewports = 8 Begin/End pairs per frame, each setting up and flushing the sprite pipeline, and `MObject::draw(SpriteBatch*, const Viewport&)` (Mh.cpp:18-21) constructs a fresh `Camera(viewport)` per call. The loop nesting is inverted: viewport should be outer, widgets inner, so widgets sharing a sampler state batch into one Begin/End.

**Fix:** Have `ViewportManager` cache the viewport array and return `const std::vector<Viewport>&`, invalidated in `set_layout`/on resolution change. Restructure the draw so viewports are the outer loop and widgets are grouped by sampler state inside a single `Begin`/`End`.

#### 10. If add_task throws mid-loop, already-submitted workers keep references into a stack frame that is unwinding

`ArtAttack/MenuPage.cpp:128-150` — **low** · `lifetime`

The lambdas submitted at MenuPage.cpp:142-149 capture `partitioned_mobjects` and `command_lists` BY REFERENCE; both are locals of `draw_mobjects_in_viewports` (128, 134-135). Correctness depends on reaching `wait_for_tasks_to_complete()` at line 150. But `ThreadPool::add_task` throws `std::runtime_error("Failed to create thread pool work object.")` (ThreadPool.cpp:42-45) when `CreateThreadpoolWork` fails — AFTER earlier iterations already called `SubmitThreadpoolWork` (line 46). That exception unwinds the frame, destroying `command_lists` and `partitioned_mobjects` while live workers are still writing through references to them. The already-created `PTP_WORK` handles also stay in `_work_items`, and the `new std::function` at ThreadPool.cpp:39-40 leaks outright on that path (its `delete` at line 64 only runs on the success path). Low severity because `CreateThreadpoolWork` failing is a rare OOM condition.

**Fix:** Make the wait unconditional with an RAII scope guard whose destructor calls `wait_for_tasks_to_complete()`, so no exit path can leave workers pointing at a dead frame. In `add_task`, hold the task in a `unique_ptr` and only `release()` after `CreateThreadpoolWork` succeeds.

## `ArtAttack/MenuPage.h`

_4 findings: 1 high, 1 medium, 2 low_

#### 1. MenuPage — the base class for all UI — is a D3D11 command-list orchestrator

`ArtAttack/MenuPage.h:38-53` — **high** · `design`

`MenuPage`'s protected API, the surface every UI subclass sees, is raw graphics plumbing: `draw_mobject_in_viewports(ID3D11DeviceContext* deferred_context, ID3D11CommandList*& command_list, DirectX::SpriteBatch*, MObject*, ID3D11SamplerState*)` (38-41), `draw_mobjects_in_viewports(std::vector<std::pair<MObject*, ID3D11SamplerState*>>*)` (43-44), `draw_range_of_mobjects_in_viewports(int, int, vector<pair<MObject*,ID3D11SamplerState*>>*, vector<ID3D11DeviceContext*>*, vector<ID3D11CommandList*>*, vector<SpriteBatch*>*)` (46-50) and `get_point_clamp_sampler_state()` (52). The implementation (MenuPage.cpp:89-183) calls `ViewportManager::apply_player_viewport`, `SpriteBatch::Begin/End`, `FinishCommandList`, `ThreadPool::add_task`, `Partitioner::partition`, `ExecuteCommandList` and `Release()`. For a project whose stated goal is a reusable 2D engine, the UI base class being a renderer means no UI can exist without D3D11, DirectXTK, the thread pool and the partitioner.

**Fix:** Split into two types: `MenuPage`/`UIScreen` owns a widget tree and exposes `build(UIContext&)`, `update(const InputFrame&)` and nothing else; a separate `UIRenderer` owns deferred contexts, sprite batches, sampler states, viewport iteration and command-list submission and is handed to pages as an interface. No UI header should include d3d11.h.

#### 2. get_menu_inputs() is const and get_-prefixed but consumes global input edge state, and heap-allocates every frame

`ArtAttack/MenuPage.h:53` — **medium** · `const-correctness`

`std::vector<ProcessedMenuInput> MenuPage::get_menu_inputs() const` (MenuPage.h:53) forwards to `get_data()->get_input()->update_and_get_menu_inputs()` (MenuPage.cpp:185-188). That is not a read: `MenuInput::update_and_get_menu_inputs` overwrites `_prev_inputs[i] = current[i]` (MenuInput.cpp:147), the edge-detection state the entire menu system depends on. So a `const` accessor named `get_*` silently mutates shared state, and calling it twice in one frame makes the second call see no edges and swallow every button press. Every page's `update()` happens to call it exactly once (MainMenu.cpp:49, 133, 302, 647, 882, 1156, 1439, 1786; PauseMenu.cpp:48, 217; EndMenu.cpp:28; ResultsMenu.cpp:32) — the invariant is real but nothing enforces or documents it. Separately, the vector is built with no `reserve`, returned by value from `MenuInput`, returned by value again from `MenuPage`, and copied into a by-value local at every call site: at least one malloc/free per frame per page for at most four 12-byte PODs.

**Fix:** Split the responsibilities: `MenuInput::update()` (non-const, called once per frame by the owning state) and `const std::array<ProcessedMenuInput, MAX_PLAYERS>& get_inputs() const` returning a reference to a member. `MenuPage::get_menu_inputs() const` then becomes legitimately const and allocation-free.

#### 3. Half-built layout grid in MenuPage that most pages route around with absolute pixel constants

`ArtAttack/MenuPage.h:18-30, 58-60` — **low** · `design`

`MenuPage` offers `_widget_position {150,150}`, `_widget_size {300,75}`, `_widget_spacing {250,150}` (58-60) plus `calculate_widget_position(int h_index, int v_index)` (26) — a notional grid with no concept of alignment, wrapping or content size. Only three of the twelve pages ever set the size (EndMenu.cpp:147, PauseMenu.cpp:130, 286), the value is write-mostly, and the defaults are load-bearing by accident: `ResultsMenuInitial::init` never calls `set_widget_size` yet computes its team-B percentage X from it — `calculate_center_position(this->get_widget_size().x, DEFAULT_RESOLUTION.x) + TEAM_B_PERCENTAGE_X_OFFSET` (ResultsMenu.cpp:150-152) — so the results layout silently depends on the `{300, 75}` literal chosen for main-menu items, and (1920-300)/2 + 325 = 1135 only 'works' because two unrelated magic numbers cancel. Contrast the team-A label two statements earlier (ResultsMenu.cpp:133), positioned correctly from `_team_a_fill->get_rectangle().get_position()`. Meanwhile `MainMenuOptions::init` reads the value into a local it never uses (MainMenu.cpp:457, a C4189 under /W4). Other pages abandon the grid entirely: `PROCEED_POSITION = {725,750}`, `HEADING_POSITION = {800,235}`, `WINNER_POSITION = {750,400}` (ResultsMenu.h:44-46); `_ready` positioned as `_background->get_rectangle().get_center() - Vector2F(400, 100)` (MainMenu.cpp:1946).

**Fix:** Either commit to a real layout system on `MContainer` (stack/anchor + margin, measured content size) or delete the grid and be honest about absolute coordinates. Derive the team-B percentage from `_fill_box`/`calculate_team_b_fill_top_right_position()` like everything else on that page. Delete the unused local at MainMenu.cpp:457.

#### 4. Drawing API uses pointer-to-vector parameters, a reference out-parameter, and a six-argument signature

`ArtAttack/MenuPage.h:38-50` — **low** · `api-design`

The three protected draw helpers are the widest API surface `MenuPage` exposes to subclasses, and every part of the shape is wrong. `draw_mobjects_in_viewports(std::vector<std::pair<MObject*, ID3D11SamplerState*>>* mobjects)` (43-44) takes a POINTER to a container it never modifies and never null-checks; all twelve call sites do `draw_mobjects_in_viewports(&mobjects)` on a local built that frame. `draw_mobject_in_viewports(ID3D11DeviceContext*, ID3D11CommandList*& command_list, SpriteBatch*, MObject*, ID3D11SamplerState* = nullptr)` (38-41) produces the command list through a reference out-parameter written by `FinishCommandList(FALSE, &command_list)` (MenuPage.cpp:117) — a COM object's sole reference deposited into a caller's container slot by a function that cannot know whether the slot already held one; double-assignment would leak silently, prevented today only by `Partitioner::partition` producing disjoint ranges. `draw_range_of_mobjects_in_viewports` (46-50) is six positional parameters, four of them raw container pointers of identical shape, trivially transposable with no compiler complaint.

**Fix:** Take `const std::vector<...>&` (or a span) for inputs, RETURN a `Microsoft::WRL::ComPtr<ID3D11CommandList>` rather than writing through a reference, and bundle the three parallel per-thread resource vectors into a single `DeferredDrawResources` struct passed by reference.

## `ArtAttack/Mh.cpp`

_5 findings: 1 high, 2 medium, 2 low_

#### 1. MTexture::is_visible_in_viewport calls itself — unconditional infinite recursion

`ArtAttack/Mh.cpp:162-165` — **high** · `correctness`

```cpp
bool MTexture::is_visible_in_viewport(const RectangleF& view) const
{
	return this->is_visible_in_viewport(view);
}
```
Unqualified lookup finds MTexture's own member (declared Mh.h:95), so this recurses on itself with identical arguments and no termination — stack overflow on the first call. There is nothing to delegate to either: IGameObject declares it pure (IGameObject.h:13), MObject and MWidget re-declare it `= 0` (Mh.h:25, 69), and TextureObject/SpriteSheetObject/DrawObject do not derive from IGameObject at all (DrawObject.h:7) so no base version exists.

Downgraded from the reviewers' "critical": it is currently unreachable. The only caller is MContainer::is_visible_in_viewport (Mh.cpp:113-123), and a repo-wide grep shows nothing calls that. So it is a landmine, not a live crash — but it detonates the moment anyone adds culling to the menu draw path.

Note the class shape invites this mistake: MTexture::set_colour (Mh.cpp:176-179) is the same forward-to-the-other-base pattern written correctly as `this->SpriteSheetObject::set_colour(colour)`.

**Fix:** `return this->_rectangle.intersects(view);` — the class already stores the rectangle, and Structure::is_visible_in_viewport (Structure.cpp:39-42) does exactly this. Add a unit test asserting an off-screen widget returns false.

#### 2. CONFIRMED infinite recursion in MTexture::is_visible_in_viewport, but it is DEAD CODE - it does not crash the menu

`ArtAttack/Mh.cpp:162-165` — **medium** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

```
bool MTexture::is_visible_in_viewport(const RectangleF& view) const
{
	return this->is_visible_in_viewport(view);
}
```
The claim is factually correct: unconditional self-call, guaranteed stack overflow. It was almost certainly meant to be `return this->_rectangle.intersects(view);` (cf. Visual.cpp:50-53, Structure.cpp:39-42, PaintTile.cpp:149-152, which all do exactly that).

But it is UNREACHABLE, and the prior report's implication that the main menu stack-overflows immediately is WRONG. Exhaustive call-site analysis (repo-wide grep, 40 hits, of which only 4 are calls rather than declarations/definitions/comments):
- Level.cpp:518, :527, :536 — inside `Level::draw_player_view_level`, iterating `_non_collision_objects`, `_collision_objects`, `_player_objects`. None of those ever hold an `MObject`: `LevelObjectBuilder::build_non_collision_object` (LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:182-200) only ever produces `Visual`, and `build_collision_object` only produces `Structure`/`StructurePaintable`. So no `MTexture` reaches these.
- Mh.cpp:117 — inside `MContainer::is_visible_in_viewport` itself, which has **no callers anywhere**.
- Level.cpp:424/432/440 are inside a fully commented-out function.

Menu drawing never culls: `MenuPage::draw_mobject_in_viewports` (MenuPage.cpp:89-122) goes straight to `widget->draw(sprite_batch, viewports[i])` at line 112. That is why the game runs.

The root cause is structural and worth fixing even though the bug is dormant: `MObject : public IGameObject` (Mh.h:8) forces every UI widget to implement `is_visible_in_viewport(const RectangleF& world_view)`, a level-space culling query that has no meaning for screen-space UI. The sibling implementations confirm nobody could implement it either — `MText::is_visible_in_viewport` (Mh.cpp:278-282) and `MTextDropShadow::is_visible_in_viewport` (Mh.cpp:343-347) both just `return true;` with a `// TODO: implement text bounding box` comment.

**Fix:** Fix the body to `return this->_rectangle.intersects(view);` so it is not a landmine, but the real fix is to stop deriving UI widgets from `IGameObject`. Split `IGameObject`'s drawable contract from its world-space/cullable contract: menus need `update()`/`draw()`, not viewport culling. That also removes the `DirectX::SpriteBatch` and `MattMath::Camera` hardwiring in IGameObject.h:11-12 from the UI layer.

#### 3. Text scaling uses scale.x only while position uses both axes, so text drifts out of its layout on non-uniform resolution changes

`ArtAttack/Mh.cpp:252-256, 315-321` — **medium** · `correctness`

```cpp
void MText::scale_size_and_position(const Vector2F& scale)
{
	this->set_position(this->get_position() * scale);   // both axes
	this->set_scale(this->get_scale() * scale.x);       // x only
}
```
Same asymmetry in MTextDropShadow::scale_size_and_position (317-320), where _shadow_offset scales by both axes but _shadow_scale by scale.x alone, while MTexture::scale_size_and_position (180-183) scales its rectangle by both components. A change from 1920x1080 to 1280x1024 gives scale = (0.667, 0.948): textures shrink ~5% more in x than y, glyphs shrink 33% while their y positions shrink only 5%, and drop shadows detach from their glyphs.

Because each call *multiplies* into the existing scale, the error compounds across successive resolution changes and the authored design coordinates are destroyed — the layout cannot round-trip. This runs from 26 call sites across MainMenu/EndMenu/PauseMenu/ResultsMenu.

**Fix:** Author UI once in a fixed virtual resolution and never mutate widget geometry; apply the resolution mapping at draw time as a single scale+letterbox transform folded into the Camera. scale_size_and_position and scale_objects_to_new_resolution both disappear, resolution changes become lossless, and non-uniform aspect gets one explicit policy instead of two accidental ones.

#### 4. scale_objects_to_new_resolution divides by the previous resolution with no zero guard

`ArtAttack/Mh.cpp:78-84` — **low** · `robustness`

```cpp
Vector2F scale_factor = new_resolution / prev_resolution;
this->scale_size_and_position(scale_factor);
```
Component-wise division with no check that prev_resolution is non-zero. A zero component yields inf or NaN, which scale_size_and_position then multiplies into every child's rectangle, position, scale and shadow offset (Mh.cpp:180-183, 252-256, 315-321). Once a widget's geometry is NaN nothing resets it, so the menu is permanently invisible and the corruption survives the next legitimate resize.

Severity lowered from the reviewers' "medium": I did not establish that a zero resolution is actually reachable (that depends on ResolutionManager and the window-resize path, which I did not audit). The missing guard on a public method is real regardless.

**Fix:** `if (prev_resolution.x <= 0.0f || prev_resolution.y <= 0.0f) return;` at the top. Better, store the design resolution and always scale from that base rather than compounding relative factors.

#### 5. MText and MTextDropShadow disable viewport culling with a hardcoded return true

`ArtAttack/Mh.cpp:278-282, 343-347` — **low** · `robustness`

```cpp
bool MText::is_visible_in_viewport(const RectangleF& view) const
{
	// TODO: implement text bounding box
	return true;
}
```
Byte-identical body at Mh.cpp:343-347 for MTextDropShadow. `view` is unused (C4100 under /W4).

This compounds with the MTexture recursion bug: of the three concrete widgets, one stack-overflows when culled and two silently refuse to be culled, so the is_visible_in_viewport contract inherited from IGameObject is honoured by none of the UI classes. Because MContainer::is_visible_in_viewport (Mh.cpp:113-123) short-circuits on the first child returning true, a single MText anywhere in a container makes the entire container unconditionally visible — the failure mode is "culling appears to work but does no work".

**Fix:** Text already knows its font and string; use SpriteFont::MeasureString, cache the extents on set_text/set_scale (they only change then, so it is not a per-frame cost), and test that rectangle. Implement it once on a shared base rather than twice.

## `ArtAttack/Mh.h`

_9 findings: 2 high, 1 medium, 6 low_

#### 1. `Mh.h` and its `M`-prefixed classes are unguessable; the prefix even yields the word "mobject" in API names

`ArtAttack/Mh.h:1-167` — **high** · `naming` · confidence: certain

`Mh.h` declares `MObject`, `MContainer`, `MWidget`, `MTexture`, `MText`, `MTextDropShadow` - the entire UI widget system. Nothing in the file, the filename, or any comment says what `M` or `h` stand for. The prefix has already metastasised into method names that read as a real (wrong) word: `MenuPage.h:38 draw_mobject_in_viewports(...)`, `:43 draw_mobjects_in_viewports(std::vector<std::pair<MObject*, ID3D11SamplerState*>>* mobjects)`, `:46 draw_range_of_mobjects_in_viewports(...)`. Compare the rest of the repo, which never abbreviates a type prefix like this (`SpriteSheetObject`, `TextureObject`, `AnimationObject`, `SoundBankObject`). For a codebase whose stated goal is a reusable engine, a public UI layer named `Mh` is a non-starter.

**Fix:** Rename file to `MenuWidgets.h` (or split per class) and the types to `MenuObject`, `MenuContainer`, `MenuWidget`, `MenuTexture`, `MenuText`, `MenuTextDropShadow`. Method names become `draw_widget_in_viewports` / `draw_widgets_in_viewports`. If the widgets are meant to be engine-general rather than menu-specific, drop the prefix entirely: `UiObject`, `UiContainer`, `UiWidget`.

#### 2. MContainer stores raw non-owning children with no ownership contract, and every menu declares containers before the widgets they point at

`ArtAttack/Mh.h:31-55` — **high** · `ownership`

`std::vector<std::pair<std::string, MObject*>> _children;` (Mh.h:54) with `add_child(MObject* child)` doing `_children.push_back(std::make_pair(child->get_name(), child))` (Mh.cpp:40-43) — no null check, no ownership, no delete. The API is equally consistent with `add_child(new MTexture(...))`, which would leak silently.

The real owners are unique_ptr members of the page classes, and the containers are declared *before* the widgets. EndMenu.h:64-72 verified: `_texture_container`, `_text_container`, then `_box`, `_heading`, `_change_teams`, … Reverse-order member destruction means the containers spend the tail of their lifetime holding pointers to already-destroyed widgets. Same inversion in MainMenu.h, ResultsMenu.h, PauseMenu.h. It does not crash today only because MContainer has no user destructor and nothing touches children during teardown — correctness rests on an undocumented ordering assumption.

The construction side has the mirror hazard: every widget member defaults to nullptr, so calling add_child before make_unique (EndMenu.cpp:214 vs EndMenu.cpp:137) is an immediate null dereference inside add_child.

Secondary defects in the same class: the name is stored twice (in MObject::_name and as the pair key) with no sync mechanism; `remove_child(name)` erases only the first match even though MObject's default name is the shared literal "error_name" (Mh.h:27); `get_children()` (Mh.cpp:74-77) returns the whole vector by value, deep-copying a std::string per child, and is not const.

**Fix:** Make the container own its children: `std::vector<std::unique_ptr<MObject>> _children;` with `MObject* add_child(std::unique_ptr<MObject>)` returning a borrowed pointer. That deletes ~16 unique_ptr members from MainMenu.h, makes destruction order well-defined, and gives remove_child an unambiguous meaning. Drop the duplicated name key and search on `child->get_name()`.

#### 3. The UI widget hierarchy inherits the game-object interface, which hardcodes DirectX::SpriteBatch at its root

`ArtAttack/Mh.h:8` — **medium** · `design`

`class MObject : public IGameObject` (Mh.h:8). IGameObject (read in full) is the simulation-object interface: `update()`, two `draw()` overloads typed on `DirectX::SpriteBatch*` and `MattMath::Camera`, and `is_visible_in_viewport()`. So menu buttons are game objects.

The interface-segregation violation is visible in the implementations: three of the four concrete widgets have a no-op update() — MTexture (Mh.cpp:158-161 `return;`), MText (274-277 `// do nothing`), MTextDropShadow (339-342 `return;`). Only MContainer::update does anything, and all it does is forward.

The deeper problem for the stated goal is that IGameObject bakes a specific D3D11 helper class into the root of both the UI and the simulation hierarchies. There is no rendering abstraction to swap, so nothing below IGameObject is portable. The same leak shows up higher: MenuPage's public API traffics in `std::vector<std::pair<MObject*, ID3D11SamplerState*>>` (MenuPage.cpp:124-125), putting a raw D3D sampler in the UI-tree interface, and z-order is expressed as the arrangement of two container members (_texture_container before _text_container) replicated across eight menu classes rather than as data — while MTexture already inherits an unused layer_depth.

**Fix:** Separate the interfaces: a UI node needs layout/draw/hit_test, a simulation object needs update/draw. Whatever they share should be a narrow `Drawable { void draw(Renderer&) const; }` where Renderer is an engine-owned interface, not DirectX::SpriteBatch*. That single substitution is the prerequisite for the engine being reusable. Then put render state and a sort key on the node so ordering is authored data, not class layout.

#### 4. Mh.h uses Text, ResourceManager, colour_consts and SpriteEffects without including any of their headers

`ArtAttack/Mh.h:1-7` — **low** · `design`

Mh.h includes only IGameObject.h, TextureObject.h and TextDropShadow.h. But `class MText final : public MWidget, public Text` (line 112) inherits Text, whose header is never included — it arrives only because TextDropShadow.h:4 happens to include Text.h (verified). Reorder or refactor that chain and Mh.h stops compiling. Same for `ResourceManager*` (82, 120, 146), `colour_consts::WHITE` (83), `DirectX::SpriteEffects` (87) and `MattMath::Viewport` (15), all reached transitively.

Conversely TextureObject.h is pulled in for MTexture alone and TextDropShadow.h for MTextDropShadow alone, so every TU that only wants MContainer compiles the whole sprite-sheet and font stack.

The filename and prefix are their own problem: Mh.h/Mh.cpp hold the entire retained-mode UI layer (MObject, MContainer, MWidget, MTexture, MText, MTextDropShadow) under a two-letter name, with a one-letter type prefix, in no namespace, flat in the same directory as Level.cpp and CollisionTools.cpp. A consumer of this engine cannot tell from the file tree that a UI system exists.

**Fix:** Include what you use (Text.h, ResourceManager.h, Colour.h). Split the framework (MObject/MContainer/MWidget) from the three concrete widgets, move them under ui/ with matching vcxproj filters, and put them in a namespace.

#### 5. Defaulted default constructors exist solely to build widgets in an invalid state

`ArtAttack/Mh.h:11, 34, 60, 77, 115, 141` — **low** · `lifetime`

`MObject() = default;` (11), `MContainer() = default;` (34), `MWidget() = default;` (60), `MTexture() = default;` (77), `MText() = default;` (115), `MTextDropShadow() = default;` (141). A default-constructed MTexture inherits `DrawObject::_resource_manager = nullptr` and `MObject::_name = "error_name"` — the name literal is itself an admission that the state is invalid, and a widget with no ResourceManager cannot draw anything.

No call site in the codebase default-constructs any of these (every use passes the full constructor: MainMenu.cpp:1322/1368, EndMenu.cpp:137, ResultsMenu.cpp:77, PauseMenu.cpp:120, …), so these constructors exist purely to make a broken object reachable.

Relatedly, none of MObject/MWidget/MContainer declares or deletes its copy operations despite being polymorphic bases. Copying an MContainer duplicates _children, giving two containers holding the same raw non-owning pointers; assigning through an `MWidget&` slices — and MTexture inherits two independent polymorphic hierarchies, so a slice through either leaves the other half stale.

**Fix:** Remove the `= default` default constructors (a user-declared constructor already suppresses the implicit one). Delete the copy operations on MObject — widgets are identity objects referenced by pointer, not values.

#### 6. Non-virtual MObject::draw(SpriteBatch*, Viewport) is hidden by the draw overrides in every derived class

`ArtAttack/Mh.h:15` — **low** · `design`

MObject declares `void draw(DirectX::SpriteBatch*, const MattMath::Viewport&);` non-virtually (Mh.h:15) alongside the two pure-virtual draw overloads (23-24). MContainer (50-51), MTexture (93-94), MText (132-133) and MTextDropShadow (161-162) each redeclare the virtual pair **without** `using MObject::draw;`, so ordinary name hiding removes the Viewport overload from their scope: `MTexture t; t.draw(sb, viewport);` does not compile. It works today only because the sole caller holds an `MObject*` (MenuPage.cpp:112).

Mixing a non-virtual convenience overload into a virtual overload set is a hazard that should not ship in a public base class. Related constness inconsistency in the same interface: is_visible_in_viewport is const but draw is not, even though every implementation only reads — MTexture::draw just forwards to TextureObject::draw.

**Fix:** Make the viewport adapter a free function rather than a member, which sidesteps hiding entirely; the render loop already knows its viewport and should build the Camera once outside the widget loop. Independently, make IGameObject::draw const.

#### 7. Most of MContainer's API is dead, and get_children returns a deep copy of a vector the caller cannot safely hold

`ArtAttack/Mh.h:36-41` — **low** · `design`

A repo-wide grep confirms remove_child(const std::string&), remove_child(const MObject*), remove_all_children(), get_child_count() and get_children() have **zero** callers outside Mh.cpp — only scale_objects_to_new_resolution is used externally (26 sites). Containers are populated once in init() and never modified.

That matters beyond dead code: these are precisely the methods whose semantics the raw-pointer ownership model leaves undefined. remove_child erases the pointer without deleting, so whether it leaks depends on a convention nobody wrote down.

```cpp
std::vector<std::pair<std::string, MObject*>> MContainer::get_children()
{
	return this->_children;
}
```
returns the whole vector by value (a std::string copy per child) and is not const, so a `const MContainer&` cannot enumerate its children at all — while the neighbouring get_child_count() *is* const.

Both remove_child overloads are hand-written iterator loops differing only in the compared field (Mh.cpp:44-65), where two std::find_if calls would do. The file uses no <algorithm> at all.

**Fix:** Delete the unused methods. If they return, define them against an owning `vector<unique_ptr<MObject>>`, drop the duplicated name key, and return `const vector<...>&`.

#### 8. MWidget is a pure pass-through layer whose only content is one setter that all three leaves forward away

`ArtAttack/Mh.h:57-72` — **low** · `design`

MWidget re-declares the same four pure virtuals already pure on MObject — scale_size_and_position (64 vs 20), update (66 vs 22), both draw overloads (67-68 vs 23-24), is_visible_in_viewport (69 vs 25) — and adds exactly one thing: `virtual void set_colour(const MattMath::Colour&) = 0;`. Its only non-declaration content is a constructor forwarding to MObject (Mh.cpp:130-134).

And set_colour is not behaviour either: all three leaves implement it as a one-line forward to a base they already inherit — MTexture → SpriteSheetObject::set_colour (Mh.cpp:176-179), MText → Text::set_colour (283-286), MTextDropShadow → TextDropShadow::set_colour (348-351). Four levels (IGameObject → MObject → MWidget → leaf) all declaring the same four signatures so that one setter can be re-exported under a different name.

The repeated `override = 0` re-declarations at MObject (22-25) and MWidget (64-69) are pure noise — inheriting a pure virtual already keeps a class abstract — and restating draw in MObject is what starts the name-hiding chain above. `~MWidget() override = default;` (62) is the only user-declared destructor among the five classes; it suppresses MWidget's implicit move operations while its siblings keep theirs, and buys nothing since IGameObject already has a virtual destructor.

**Fix:** Delete MWidget and derive the leaves from MObject directly. Delete the redundant `override = 0` lines and `~MWidget() override = default;`.

#### 9. Widget constructors take 11-14 positional parameters with a bool flag buried mid-tail

`ArtAttack/Mh.h:78-88, 116-127, 142-156` — **low** · `design`

MTexture takes 11 parameters, MText 12, MTextDropShadow 14. To set layer_depth you must spell out every preceding default. `bool hidden` sits at position 7 of 11 (position 9 of 14 for MTextDropShadow), so `MTexture(n, s, f, r, rm, c, true)` is unreadable at the call site — and it is the same flag already present on `MObject(const std::string&, bool hidden = false)` and `MWidget(..., bool hidden = false)`. The adjacent floats (rotation, scale, shadow_scale) and the two Colours are positionally swappable with no compile error.

The last several parameters are identical across all three widgets and are only forwarded to DrawObject.

**Fix:** Introduce a `DrawParams` aggregate carrying colour/rotation/origin/effects/layer_depth and pass one struct. Replace `bool hidden` with `enum class Visibility { visible, hidden };`.

## `ArtAttack/MovingObject.h`

_3 findings: 1 high, 2 medium_

#### 1. `_dx` is a 2D vector, producing the nonsense accessors `get_dx_x()` / `set_dx_x()` / `get_dx_magnitude()`

`ArtAttack/MovingObject.h:33-47, 55` — **high** · `naming` · confidence: certain

`MattMath::Vector2F _dx` (MovingObject.h:55) is a per-frame displacement vector, but `dx` universally means "change in x" - a scalar. The result is a whole accessor family that reads as gibberish: `get_dx()` returns a Vector2F, `get_dx_x()` (line 34), `get_dx_y()` (35), `set_dx_x(float x)` (38), `alter_dx_x` (42), `get_unit_dx()` (45), `get_dx_magnitude()` (46), `get_dx_angle()` (47). "the x of the change-in-x" and "the magnitude of the change-in-x" are not sentences. The name also leaks into constants - `player_consts.h:24` has `const MattMath::Vector2F STARTING_DX = { 0.0f, 0.0f };`.

**Fix:** Rename the member and its 14 accessors to `_displacement` / `get_displacement()` / `get_displacement_x()` / `get_displacement_magnitude()` (or `_frame_delta` if you prefer). `STARTING_DX` -> `STARTING_DISPLACEMENT`. This is a mechanical rename with no behaviour change and it makes MovingObject readable for the first time.

#### 2. 27 protected virtual accessors over three fields, with exactly one override in the entire codebase — and it is a no-op

`ArtAttack/MovingObject.h:9, 16-51` — **medium** · `design`

`MovingObject` holds two `Vector2F` and a `float` and declares 27 `virtual` protected one-line accessors plus `virtual ~MovingObject() = default`. I grepped every `override` in the project: the only override of any of them is `Player::get_velocity` (Player.h:104), whose entire body is
```cpp
const Vector2F& Player::get_velocity() const { return MovingObject::get_velocity(); }   // Player.cpp:935-938
```
A pure pass-through whose only effect is to widen access from `protected` to `public` for one caller, `DebugText.cpp:25`. `using MovingObject::get_velocity;` would do that with no vtable.

Cost: a vptr and a 28-entry vtable on every object that mixes it in. `Player` (Player.h:63) and `Projectile` (Projectile.h:19) already carry a vptr from `IGameObject`, so they pay two, and projectiles are spawned continuously (Level.cpp:204-210).

It is also an active trap in two directions. The scalar and derived accessors bypass the virtual entirely — `get_velocity_x()` (:20-23), `get_unit_velocity()` (:52-55), `get_velocity_magnitude()` (:56-59) and `get_velocity_angle()` (:60-63) all read `_velocity` directly rather than calling `get_velocity()`. And most call sites explicitly qualify (`MovingObject::set_velocity_y(0.0f)`, `MovingObject::alter_velocity_y(...)`), suppressing dispatch anyway. If anyone ever writes a *real* override, `obj.get_velocity().x` and `obj.get_velocity_x()` will silently disagree and the qualified call sites will silently ignore it.

The public virtual destructor also advertises `delete static_cast<MovingObject*>(p)`, which for `Player` is a different subobject address than the allocation — yet nothing anywhere holds a `MovingObject*`.

**Fix:** Drop `virtual` from all 27 accessors and define them inline in the header; make the destructor `protected` and non-virtual to document "mixin, never deleted through this base" and remove the vptr. Replace `Player::get_velocity` with `using MovingObject::get_velocity;`. Best: replace the class entirely with a plain aggregate held by composition (`struct Kinematics { MattMath::Vector2F velocity; };`) — in an engine this is a component, not a base class. Note `_dx` is not state at all: it is recomputed and consumed within one integration step (Player.cpp:852-856, Projectile.cpp:275-276), so it and its 12 accessors should be a local variable.

#### 3. MovingObject is 30 protected virtual accessors over three fields, inherited where a member belongs

`ArtAttack/MovingObject.h:16-57` — **medium** · `design`

`MovingObject` has three data members (`_velocity`, `_dx`, `_rotation`, :54-56) and 30 protected `virtual` one-line accessors over them (:17-51). Exactly one is ever overridden anywhere in the codebase: `Player::get_velocity() const override` (Player.h:104), and it is overridden not to change behaviour — the body is `return MovingObject::get_velocity();` (Player.cpp:935-938) — but purely to widen access from protected to public so `DebugText.cpp:25` can read it. The class pays for a vtable and 30 virtual slots to achieve what a public member would.

Worse, the virtual layer is bypassed inconsistently within a single file: Player.cpp calls `MovingObject::get_velocity_x()`, `MovingObject::set_velocity_x(...)`, `MovingObject::alter_velocity_y(...)` with explicit qualification throughout (:767-853), which SUPPRESSES virtual dispatch, while other functions in the same file call the same accessors through `this->` (:606, :624, :910, :1009).

It is also inherited rather than composed: a Player is not a moving object, it has a velocity. Note this is what makes the diamond four-way instead of three-way.

**Fix:** Make it a plain value type (`struct RigidBody2D { Vector2F velocity, delta; }`) held as a member, non-virtual, and delete `Player::get_velocity` and every `MovingObject::` qualification. `_rotation` should not live here at all — it duplicates `DrawObject::_draw_rotation` and is never rendered.

## `ArtAttack/PaintTile.cpp`

_3 findings: 1 high, 2 low_

#### 1. Splash animation is drawn forever after it finishes, permanently doubling sprite count and leaving a 24x24 team-coloured blob on every painted tile

`ArtAttack/PaintTile.cpp:34-53` — **high** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

`PaintTile::draw` draws `_splash` on every frame for any tile whose `_team != NONE` (lines 49-50, and identically at 69-70) with no check for whether the animation has completed. `splash_1` is defined in ArtAttack/textures/sprite_sheet_1.json:108-119 as 5 frames at 0.05s with `"looping": false`, so `AnimationObject::update` (ArtAttack/AnimationObject.cpp:99-103) clamps `_frame_index` to 4 and sets `_paused = true` after 0.25s - and the tile then keeps submitting frame 4 forever.
Geometry makes it visible, not just costly: `SPLASH_RECTANGLE` is `THICKNESS * 2.0f` = 24x24 (ArtAttack/PaintTile.h:20) centred on a tile that is only ~4 wide x 12 tall, so the frozen splash overhangs the structure's surface by 6 world units and overlaps its 5 nearest neighbours. A fully painted 750-tile face carries 750 permanently-drawn overlapping 24x24 quads (6x overdraw) plus a 6-unit team-coloured fringe sticking out of the geometry.
Cost: this is exactly the 2x in the 44,592-sprites-per-frame figure for turbulence - half of those draws are finished animations.

**Fix:** Guard the splash draw with the existing `AnimationObject::is_paused()` (or add a `has_finished()`), and skip `_splash.draw(...)` once the strip has run out. Better: don't give every tile its own animation object at all - a per-structure pool of a few dozen transient splash effects would cover every splash that is actually mid-playback.

#### 2. IGameObject's two draw overloads force every class to duplicate its draw body verbatim

`ArtAttack/PaintTile.cpp:34-75` — **low** · `design`

`IGameObject` (IGameObject.h:11-12) requires both `draw(SpriteBatch*, const Camera&)` and `draw(SpriteBatch*)`. In this module alone that produces four verbatim duplications:
- `PaintTile::draw(sb, camera)` (:34-53) and `PaintTile::draw(sb)` (:54-75) — identical 19-line bodies including the whole team→colour switch, differing only in whether `camera` is forwarded.
- `StructurePaintable::draw` ×2 (:45-52 vs :54-62)
- `Structure::draw` ×2 (Structure.cpp:31-34 vs :35-38)
- `PaintTileSplash::draw` ×2 (PaintTile.cpp:189-192 vs :193-196)

The camera-less overload exists only for UI-space drawing, which the level path never uses — and `MattMath::Camera::DEFAULT_CAMERA` already exists (Level.h:126) to express exactly that.

Related: `PaintTileSplash::set_colour` (PaintTile.cpp:181-184) and `::update` (:185-188) are pure forwarding overrides whose only effect is to widen `DrawObject::set_colour` from protected (DrawObject.h:27) to public (PaintTile.h:40).

**Fix:** Collapse to a single `virtual void draw(DirectX::SpriteBatch*, const MattMath::Camera& = Camera::DEFAULT_CAMERA) const = 0;` and delete the second overload from every implementer. For the access widening, `using AnimationObject::set_colour;` in the public section states the intent and generates no code.

#### 3. PaintTile::is_colliding has no type filter while on_collision hard-throws for anything that isn't a projectile

`ArtAttack/PaintTile.cpp:84-140` — **low** · `robustness`

Unlike every sibling implementation (Player.cpp:148-159 calls `is_matching_collision_object_type` first), `PaintTile::is_colliding` (PaintTile.cpp:84-109) skips the type check entirely — it does AABB then narrow phase and returns true for *any* overlapping object, including players, structures and same-team projectiles.

`PaintTile::on_collision` (PaintTile.cpp:114-140) then does the opposite and hard-throws:
```cpp
else { throw std::exception("PaintTile::on_collision() - other_type is not a projectile"); }
```
The pair only works because the single caller, `StructurePaintable::on_collision` (StructurePaintable.cpp:64-101), pre-filters to offensive projectiles before consulting the tiles. But `PaintTile` implements the full `ICollisionGameObject` interface, so the first time anyone puts paint tiles into `Level::_collision_objects` — the obvious next step for making paint interact with anything — the game throws on the first player-tile overlap, with no handler anywhere on the stack.

The two branches in `on_collision` also hand-rewrite `is_team_a_projectile` / `is_team_b_projectile`, which already exist as inline functions at collision_object_type.h:57-73.

**Fix:** Add the type filter to `is_colliding` so the two functions agree on what a PaintTile collides with, and make `on_collision` ignore non-projectiles rather than throwing. Call the existing predicates instead of respelling them.

## `ArtAttack/pch.h`

_5 findings: 1 high, 4 medium_

#### 1. PCH includes 13 DirectXTK headers that are never used, and omits <string>/<vector>/<map> which almost everything uses

`ArtAttack/pch.h:42-77` — **high** · `performance` · confidence: certain

pch.h is force-included into all 81 TUs. Of its 19 DirectXTK includes (lines 59-77), grepping the entire first-party tree for the corresponding APIs finds zero uses of: BufferHelpers.h (line 59, no CreateStaticBuffer), DirectXHelpers.h (62, no SetDebugObjectName/MapGuard), Effects.h (63, no BasicEffect/IEffect/EffectFactory), GeometricPrimitive.h (65), GraphicsMemory.h (66), Keyboard.h (67), Model.h (68), Mouse.h (69), PostProcess.h (70), PrimitiveBatch.h (71), ScreenGrab.h (72, no SaveDDSTextureToFile), VertexTypes.h (76), WICTextureLoader.h (77, no CreateWICTextureFromFile). Model.h and Effects.h are the two heaviest headers in DirectXTK. Only CommonStates.h, DDSTextureLoader.h, GamePad.h, SimpleMath.h, SpriteBatch.h and SpriteFont.h earn their place. Conversely the PCH's STL section (lines 42-52) omits <string>, <vector> and <map> even though 34 of 81 .cpp files use std::string, 28 use std::vector, and only 5 headers bother to include <string> explicitly - so those are being pulled in accidentally through DirectXTK's own includes.

**Fix:** Delete the 13 unused DirectXTK includes and add <string>, <vector>, <map>, <functional>. Then, since the PCH is the only thing holding the build together (see the self-containment finding), keep it as a build accelerator rather than a dependency-injection mechanism.

#### 2. pch.h forces the whole DirectXTK 3D surface into all 81 TUs of a 2D-only game, and doubles as the engine's error header
