#### 9. Header hygiene: Projectile.h pulls in constants it does not use; ProjectileBuilder.h and projectile_details.h omit includes they do use

`ArtAttack/Projectile.h:1-8` — **low** · `design`

Verified. `Projectile.h:5` includes `projectile_consts.h`, but the header only needs the `ProjectileDetails`/`DiffusionDetails` *types*, which live in projectile_details.h — no `projectile_consts::` name appears in Projectile.h. The consequence is that all eight dynamically-initialised global blobs land in every TU that touches a projectile. The constants are actually used only in Projectile.cpp:238-271 and the five leaf .cpp files, all of which could include projectile_consts.h directly.

Missing includes, also verified: ProjectileBuilder.h uses `std::vector` and `std::unique_ptr` with no `<vector>`/`<memory>` — it gets `<vector>` transitively from MattMath.h:8 and `<memory>` only from each .cpp's pch.h. projectile_details.h uses `std::string` with no `<string>` (MattMath.h does not include it).

Combined with ProjectileBuilder.h:4-9 including all five concrete projectile headers into Weapon.h, touching any leaf projectile header rebuilds most of the project.

**Fix:** In Projectile.h, include `projectile_details.h` and move `projectile_consts.h` down into the .cpp files that read constants. In ProjectileBuilder.h, drop the five concrete includes (move them to the .cpp), forward-declare `class ICollisionGameObject;`, and add `<vector>`/`<memory>`. Add `<string>` to projectile_details.h. Headers should include what they use and nothing more.

#### 10. Polymorphic bases with implicit public copy/move while holding borrowed pointers; rule of 0/3/5 applied inconsistently

`ArtAttack/Projectile.h:19-114` — **low** · `design`

Verified. `Projectile` (Projectile.h:19-80) declares no destructor and no copy/move operations while owning a borrowed `const float* _dt` (line 79) and inheriting a borrowed `ResourceManager*` (DrawObject.h:36). The compiler therefore generates public copy construction and copy assignment that silently duplicate those non-owning pointers; and because `Projectile` is a polymorphic base with public assignment, assigning through a base reference compiles and slices, leaving a `ProjectileSpray` carrying another projectile's team, type and timer.

The inconsistency is one level down: `DiffusingProjectile` *does* declare `~DiffusingProjectile() override = default;` (Projectile.h:99). A user-declared destructor suppresses the implicit move constructor and move assignment, so `DiffusingProjectile` — and hence `ProjectileSpray`/`ProjectileMist` — silently degrades every move to a copy, including its `std::string` members. `Projectile` and the five leaves declare no destructor at all. The redundant destructor is also unnecessary: `IGameObject` (IGameObject.h:9) already supplies a virtual one.

Severity kept low: nothing in the codebase copies or assigns a projectile today.

**Fix:** On `Projectile` and `DiffusingProjectile`: `= delete` the copy constructor and copy assignment (and the move equivalents, or make them protected if a clone path is ever wanted). Remove the redundant `~DiffusingProjectile() override = default;`. Apply one convention across the hierarchy rather than three.

## `ArtAttack/ProjectileBall.h`

_1 finding: 1 high_

#### 1. The collision shape lives in the leaves, so five subclasses exist only to re-declare the same RectangleF

`ArtAttack/ProjectileBall.h:22-31` — **high** · `design`

Verified. Every concrete projectile privately declares `MattMath::RectangleF _rectangle = MattMath::RectangleF::ZERO;` (ProjectileBall.h:31, ProjectileJet.h:31, ProjectileSpray.h:31, ProjectileMist.h:31, ProjectileRolling.h:30) and therefore must re-implement `update`, both `draw` overloads, `is_visible_in_viewport`, `is_colliding` and `get_shape` — all pure boilerplate over that one member. `Projectile` declares five of those as `= 0` (Projectile.h:38-46) purely because it refuses to own the shape.

I diffed the files directly: ProjectileJet.cpp:30-53 and ProjectileBall.cpp:30-54 are identical modulo whitespace; ProjectileSpray.cpp:30-51 and ProjectileMist.cpp:30-51 differ by nothing at all. The complete behavioural difference across four of the five classes is which `DETAILS_*` constant goes to the base constructor, plus one extra `inflate_to_size(calculate_diffusion_size())` line for the two diffusing ones.

The repeated constructor tail is duplicated the same way — `Vector2F size = get_details().col_rect_size; _rectangle.offset(-size.x/2, -size.y/2);` appears verbatim in all five (ProjectileSpray.cpp:25-27 and equivalents), and it also copies the Vector2F instead of binding a const reference. So does the `update()` prologue that reads two fields out of `_details` and hands them back to the base.

Merged with the candidate reporting the `DiffusingProjectile` inheritance level, which adds one member and one function and re-declares four pure virtuals a third time (Projectile.h:102-108) for no effect.

**Fix:** Move `_rectangle` into `Projectile` (all five leaves use a rectangle) and implement `update()`, both `draw`s, `is_visible_in_viewport`, `get_shape` and the centring offset once in the base, with a small protected `virtual void update_shape()` hook for the diffusion case. Fold `DiffusionDetails` onto `ProjectileDetails` behind the already-present `diffusion_type::NO_DIFFUSION` and delete `DiffusingProjectile`. Four of the five subclasses then vanish, replaced by a data record.

## `ArtAttack/ProjectileBuilder.cpp`

_1 finding: 1 high_

#### 1. Projectiles are class-per-variant behind a switch factory, while the rest of the engine is already data-driven

`ArtAttack/ProjectileBuilder.cpp:23-113` — **high** · `design`

Verified. Adding one projectile requires edits in at least five places: an enumerator in `enum projectile_type` (Projectile.h:10-17), a `DETAILS_*` blob in projectile_consts.h, a new `case` block in `build_projectiles` (ProjectileBuilder.cpp:23-113), two enumerators in `collision_object_type`, and two branches in `Projectile::get_collision_object_type`. The four non-mist case bodies (lines 25-42, 43-60, 61-78, 93-110) are the same eight statements four times, differing only in the concrete type and the `DETAILS_*` constant.

Meanwhile the actual variation between the five projectiles is 6 floats, 2 Vector2Fs and 2 strings — precisely `ProjectileDetails`. And the engine already has a data pipeline: levels, sprite sheets and sound banks all load through rapidjson (LevelObjectBuilder.cpp, SpriteSheet.cpp, SoundBank.cpp), yet projectile and weapon tuning is compiled in, so retuning a weapon requires a rebuild.

Merged with the candidate on the hand-unrolled mist spread: `build_mist_projectiles` (ProjectileBuilder.cpp:131-201) is five copy-pasted 14-line blocks differing only in the rotation — `0`, `+PI/12`, `-PI/12`, `+PI/6`, `-PI/6`. 70 lines encoding a 5-element array of angles, with the pellet count and spread baked into the shape of the code. It is also the sole reason `build_mist_projectiles` exists as a separate function. There is no `reserve(5)`, so the vector reallocates three times per shot, and `Level` then re-pushes the results one at a time into the live `_collision_objects` (Level.cpp:207-210).

**Fix:** Load `ProjectileDetails`/`DiffusionDetails` from JSON through the existing rapidjson path into a `std::unordered_map<std::string, ProjectileDefinition>`, and make the factory `spawn(const ProjectileDefinition&, const SpawnParams&)` returning one generic `Projectile`. Add `int pellet_count` and `float spread_radians` to the definition and emit the spread in a loop with a `reserve(pellet_count)`. `enum projectile_type`, the switch, and `build_mist_projectiles` all disappear. In `Level`, use a single `insert` with move iterators instead of the per-element push_back loop.

## `ArtAttack/ProjectileMist.cpp`

_3 findings: 2 high, 1 medium_

#### 1. ProjectileMist constructs its base with `SPRAY` as its projectile_type

`ArtAttack/ProjectileMist.cpp:19-22` — **high** · `correctness`

Verified: ProjectileMist.cpp:19-22 passes `SPRAY` as the fifth base-constructor argument where the type tag belongs. Cross-checked every sibling — ProjectileSpray.cpp:20 `SPRAY`, ProjectileJet.cpp:20 `JET`, ProjectileBall.cpp:20 `BALL`, ProjectileRolling.cpp:20 `ROLLING`. Mist is the only one wrong.

`Projectile::get_collision_object_type()` (Projectile.cpp:155-195) switches on the stored `_type`, so every mist particle reports `PROJECTILE_SPRAY_TEAM_A/B`. Downstream:
- `Player::on_projectile_collision` (Player.cpp:649-654) applies `SPRAY_DAMAGE` instead of `MIST_DAMAGE`. Both are 0.01f today (player_consts.h:65,69), so the bug is currently invisible and will surface the instant either constant is tuned.
- `PaintTile::on_collision` (PaintTile.cpp:118-133) and `StructurePaintable::on_collision` classify mist as spray.
- `collision_object_type::PROJECTILE_MIST_TEAM_A/B` (collision_object_type.h:23-24) are unreachable at runtime, so the mist branches at Player.cpp:673-678 and in every other ladder are dead code.

Contributing cause, verified: `ProjectileBuilder::build_mist_projectiles` takes a `projectile_type type` parameter (ProjectileBuilder.h:36, ProjectileBuilder.cpp:123) that its body never references — the caller at ProjectileBuilder.cpp:86 forwards `MIST` and the function discards it. That is also a live C4100 under /W4.

Merged from 4 duplicate candidate reports.

**Fix:** Pass `MIST`. Then remove the cause: the type tag is a fixed property of the concrete class, so it should not be a hand-copied constructor argument at all — either make it a pure virtual `projectile_type get_type() const` implemented once per leaf, or (better) add the identity to `ProjectileDetails` so `DETAILS_MIST` carries it and the tuning data and the tag cannot disagree. Delete the unused `type` parameter from `build_mist_projectiles`.

#### 2. Copy-paste bug: ProjectileMist registers itself as projectile_type SPRAY

`ArtAttack/ProjectileMist.cpp:19-22` — **high** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

`ProjectileMist`'s ctor initialiser list was copied from `ProjectileSpray.cpp:19-22` and the type tag was never changed:

```cpp
DiffusingProjectile(velocity, team, player_num, team_colour,
    SPRAY, dt, resource_manager,          // <-- should be MIST
    DETAILS_MIST, DIFFUSION_DETAILS_MIST, ...)
```

`Projectile::_type` feeds `Projectile::get_collision_object_type()` (Projectile.cpp:154-192), which switches on `_type`, so every mist projectile in the game reports `PROJECTILE_SPRAY_TEAM_A/B`. Consequences: `collision_object_type::PROJECTILE_MIST_TEAM_A` and `_B` are dead enum values that never occur at runtime; `Player::on_projectile_collision` (Player.cpp:645-690) applies `SPRAY_DAMAGE` instead of `MIST_DAMAGE` to mist hits; every hand-written `PROJECTILE_MIST_*` branch in `PaintTile::on_collision`, `StructurePaintable::on_collision` and `Level::count_projectiles` is unreachable. This is exactly the failure mode the 5-way projectile copy-paste (see the ProjectileSpray/Jet/Ball/Mist/Rolling finding) invites.

**Fix:** Change `SPRAY` to `MIST` at ProjectileMist.cpp:20. Better: remove the parameter entirely — make `projectile_type` a `virtual projectile_type get_type() const` or a static trait on the concrete class so the tag cannot disagree with the class, or drop the enum and put the `collision_object_type` in `ProjectileDetails` next to the rest of the per-projectile data.

#### 3. ProjectileMist registers itself as projectile_type SPRAY; PROJECTILE_MIST_* is unreachable

`ArtAttack/ProjectileMist.cpp:19-22` — **medium** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

```
DiffusingProjectile(velocity, team, player_num, team_colour,
    SPRAY, dt, resource_manager,
    DETAILS_MIST, DIFFUSION_DETAILS_MIST, ...)
```
The 5th argument is `projectile_type`; it should be `MIST`. Compare ProjectileRolling.cpp:19-22 which correctly passes `ROLLING`. Because `projectile_type` is an *unscoped* enum (Projectile.h:10-17) among otherwise scoped enums, `SPRAY` is a bare identifier in scope and the mistake compiles silently.

What actually differs at runtime (traced, not assumed):
- `Projectile::get_collision_object_type()` (Projectile.cpp:155-195) switches on `get_type()`, so a mist projectile reports `PROJECTILE_SPRAY_TEAM_A/B`. `PROJECTILE_MIST_TEAM_A` and `PROJECTILE_MIST_TEAM_B` become **unreachable enum values** — every branch handling them (Player.cpp:673-678, PaintTile.cpp:122/130, StructurePaintable.cpp:77-78, Level.cpp:674-675, Projectile.cpp:165-166/181-182) is dead code.
- Damage: `Player::on_projectile_collision` (Player.cpp:645-682) selects damage by collision type, so mist hits apply `SPRAY_DAMAGE` instead of `MIST_DAMAGE`. **Currently invisible**, because player_consts.h:65 and :69 both define the value as `0.01f`. The bug is latent until someone tunes one of them.
- Painting and team attribution are unaffected — PaintTile.cpp:118-133 and StructurePaintable.cpp:69-78 accept both spellings.
- Debug projectile count (Level.cpp:658-682) still counts it, just as the wrong category.

REACHABILITY: LIVE whenever the Mister is equipped, but with no visible symptom today.

Worth noting alongside: `Projectile::get_player_damage()` (Projectile.cpp:295-298) returning `_details.player_damage` has **zero callers**. So there are two parallel damage systems with opposite sign conventions — `projectile_consts::DETAILS_MIST.player_damage = -0.05f` (dead) versus `player_consts::MIST_DAMAGE = 0.01f` subtracted at Player.cpp:676 (live). The per-projectile damage data in projectile_consts.h is entirely inert.

**Fix:** Pass `MIST`. Then make `projectile_type` an `enum class` so an unqualified `SPRAY` cannot be substituted for a `MIST` at a call site. Longer term, delete the `collision_object_type` cross-product (class × team × weapon, 23 values) — `Player::on_projectile_collision` should ask the projectile for its damage via `get_player_damage()` rather than re-deriving it from an enum, which also deletes the whole if/else ladder and the dead constants.

## `ArtAttack/ProjectileRolling.cpp`

_3 findings: 1 high, 1 medium, 1 low_

#### 1. ProjectileRolling never applies its displacement and never advances its animation — the roller emits stationary invisible hitboxes

`ArtAttack/ProjectileRolling.cpp:29-47` — **high** · `correctness`

Verified. `ProjectileRolling::update()` (lines 29-35) is:
```cpp
const ProjectileDetails& details = this->get_details();
Projectile::update_movement(details.gravity, details.wind_resistance);
```
and stops there. `Projectile::update_movement` only *computes* the displacement into `MovingObject::_dx` (Projectile.cpp:275-276); applying it is each subclass's job. All four siblings do it — ProjectileSpray.cpp:39-40, ProjectileJet.cpp:37-38, ProjectileMist.cpp:39-40, ProjectileBall.cpp:37-38 all call `_rectangle.offset(get_dx_x(), get_dx_y())`, and all four also call `AnimationObject::update()`. Rolling does neither, so its collision rectangle never leaves the spawn point and its animation is frozen.

It is also inert on the render side: both `draw` overloads are `// do nothing` (lines 36-43) and `is_visible_in_viewport` returns a hardcoded `false` (line 44-47).

Surrounding data confirms the weapon is broken end to end: `DETAILS_ROLLER.starting_vel_length = 0.0f` and `shoot_interval = 0.0001f` (weapon_consts.h:91-92), `DETAILS_ROLLING` has `gravity = 0.0f, wind_resistance = 0.0f, delete_timer = 0.000001f, player_damage = -1000.0f` (projectile_consts.h:63-67). The tiny delete_timer shows the intent was a one-frame melee volume; the broken `get_delete_timer()` means that intent is never honoured.

I am tempering one claim several reviewers made: these volumes are NOT permanently immortal in all cases. `Projectile::on_collision` still deletes them on contact with any structure or enemy player, so a volume spawned overlapping the ground dies immediately. Only a volume spawned touching nothing persists indefinitely. The class is still functionally broken.

Merged from 3 duplicate candidate reports (two filed as correctness, one as design).

**Fix:** Decide what this type is. If it is a projectile, apply the offset and call `AnimationObject::update()` like every sibling, implement the draw overloads, and give it non-degenerate velocity/gravity/lifetime. If it is a one-frame melee volume — which the data says — it should not derive from `Projectile`/`MovingObject`/`AnimationObject` at all: an engine-level `HitVolume` (shape + payload + lifetime, no sprite, no velocity) implementing only `ICollisionGameObject` is the right type, and it should `set_for_deletion(true)` at the end of its first update. The reason this was forgettable is that the same `_rectangle.offset(...)` line is duplicated across five subclasses — see the finding on hoisting the shape into `Projectile`.

#### 2. ProjectileRolling is invisible by construction, making both of its draw overrides unreachable

`ArtAttack/ProjectileRolling.cpp:36-47` — **medium** · `dead-code` · confidence: certain

```cpp
void ProjectileRolling::draw(SpriteBatch* sprite_batch, const Camera& camera) { /* do nothing */ }
void ProjectileRolling::draw(SpriteBatch* sprite_batch)                       { /* do nothing */ }
bool ProjectileRolling::is_visible_in_viewport(const RectangleF& view) const  { return false; }
```
Every draw path in `Level::draw_player_view_level` (Level.cpp:516-540) and `draw_zoom_out_level_component` guards on `object->is_visible_in_viewport(camera_view)`, so the two empty `draw` overrides can never be entered — they are unreachable overrides of an unreachable case. The roller weapon is fully wired (`WeaponBuilder.cpp` case `wep_type::ROLLER` → `WeaponRoller`), so the rolling projectile exists in the simulation and collides, it is simply never rendered. Nothing in the code says whether that is intentional (an invisible "paint applicator" entity) or an unfinished art task.

**Fix:** If invisible is intentional, delete both draw overrides and add a one-line comment on `is_visible_in_viewport` saying why. If not, this is a missing feature that the empty bodies are hiding.

#### 3. Four unreferenced formal parameters (C4100 under /W4), and an invisible object paying for full animation state

`ArtAttack/ProjectileRolling.cpp:36-47` — **low** · `modern-cpp`

Verified:
```cpp
void ProjectileRolling::draw(SpriteBatch* sprite_batch, const Camera& camera) { /* do nothing */ }
void ProjectileRolling::draw(SpriteBatch* sprite_batch)                      { /* do nothing */ }
bool ProjectileRolling::is_visible_in_viewport(const RectangleF& view) const  { return false; }
```
Four unreferenced parameters. The project enables `WarningLevel Level4` in all four configurations (ArtAttack.vcxproj:91, 113, 134, 160) but does not treat warnings as errors, so C4100 accumulates silently — the unused `type` parameter at ProjectileBuilder.cpp:123 is the same warning.

Separately, this class still inherits `AnimationObject`, and its constructor resolves `DETAILS_ROLLING.sheet_name`/`animation_strip_name` ("sprite_sheet_1"/"projectile_3", projectile_consts.h:70-71) through `ResourceManager` at AnimationObject.cpp:21 — a full sprite-sheet lookup and animation state for an object that is never drawn.

**Fix:** Omit the parameter names (`void draw(SpriteBatch*, const Camera&) override {}`) so the intent is explicit. Longer term, an invisible collision volume should not be an `AnimationObject` at all — that is the multiple-inheritance hierarchy forcing drawing state onto a non-drawn object; see the HitVolume suggestion on the ProjectileRolling finding.

## `ArtAttack/ProjectileSpray.cpp`

_4 findings: 2 high, 2 low_

#### 1. Five Projectile subclasses are ~90% byte-identical; the whole family should be one class + a data table

`ArtAttack/ProjectileSpray.cpp:8-91` — **high** · `design` · confidence: certain

`ProjectileSpray.cpp` (91 lines), `ProjectileJet.cpp` (89), `ProjectileBall.cpp` (89), `ProjectileMist.cpp` (90) and `ProjectileRolling.cpp` (82) — ~440 lines total — are the same file five times. Each holds a private `MattMath::RectangleF _rectangle`, and each defines byte-identical bodies for `draw(sprite_batch, camera)`, `draw(sprite_batch)`, `is_visible_in_viewport`, `get_shape`, `is_colliding`, plus a ctor that differs only in which `DETAILS_*` constant it forwards and a 12-line `update()` that differs only by an `inflate_to_size(calculate_diffusion_size())` line. The five headers are identical except the class name and base (`Projectile` vs `DiffusingProjectile`); ProjectileSpray.h:9 / ProjectileMist.h:9 even use `= delete` for the default ctor while the other three use `= default`, for no reason.

All the real variation already lives in data: `projectile_consts.h:14-106` holds `DETAILS_SPRAY/JET/ROLLING/MIST/BALL` and `DIFFUSION_DETAILS_SPRAY/MIST`. `ProjectileRolling` is the only genuine behavioural variant (empty draw, `is_visible_in_viewport` returns false).

**Fix:** Delete all ten files. Move `_rectangle`, `draw`, `is_visible_in_viewport`, `get_shape` and the generic `update()` into `Projectile`; keep `DiffusingProjectile::update()` as the one override that inflates. Construct instances as `Projectile(DETAILS_X, ...)` / `DiffusingProjectile(DETAILS_X, DIFFUSION_DETAILS_X, ...)` from a `projectile_type -> details` lookup table, so adding a projectile is a table row rather than two new files.

#### 2. The same 32-line is_colliding() is copy-pasted into all five projectile leaves (and again into Player and PaintTile)

`ArtAttack/ProjectileSpray.cpp:56-87` — **high** · `design`

Verified byte-for-byte identical, including the comments, at ProjectileSpray.cpp:56-87, ProjectileJet.cpp:54-85, ProjectileBall.cpp:55-86, ProjectileMist.cpp:56-87 and ProjectileRolling.cpp:48-79; near-identical (minus the type filter) at PaintTile.cpp:84-109 and in Player.cpp. Nothing in the body is projectile-specific: it is generic narrow-phase dispatch pasted into seven leaf classes.

Because it is duplicated, the 'if other is a RECTANGLE, the passed AABB test means a hit' shortcut — only sound when `this` is itself an AABB — is now wrong in seven places instead of one.

Performance detail confirmed while reading it: each call invokes the virtual `this->get_shape()` up to 3 times and `other->get_shape()` up to 4 times with no hoisting. `Shape::AABB_intersects` (MattMath.cpp:143-146) is `get_bounding_box().intersects(other->get_bounding_box())`, and `get_bounding_box()` is `virtual RectangleF ... const = 0` (MattMath.h:71) returning a **polymorphic RectangleF by value** — two vtable-carrying temporaries per test, when for a projectile `this` already *is* a RectangleF. When `other` is not a rectangle (ramps are triangles), the fall-through reaches `Shape::intersects` (MattMath.cpp:119-136), which performs a `dynamic_cast` per switch branch — an RTTI lookup in the innermost loop of the O(n^2) pass at Level.cpp:277-292.

Merged from 2 candidate reports (one design, one performance).

**Fix:** `is_colliding` should not be a virtual on every game object. Put one `bool shapes_overlap(const Shape&, const Shape&)` in the collision module, have the level call it, and delete the override from all seven leaves. At minimum hoist `const Shape* self = get_shape(); const Shape* o = other->get_shape();`. In `Shape::intersects`, replace the `dynamic_cast` chain with `static_cast` — the switch on `get_shape_type()` has already established the dynamic type.

#### 3. Spawn geometry is split across the factory and the constructor, duplicated in all five leaves

`ArtAttack/ProjectileSpray.cpp:24-28` — **low** · `design`

Verified. The factory builds the rect at the raw nozzle position — `RectangleF(position, DETAILS_SPRAY.col_rect_size)` (ProjectileBuilder.cpp:30, and equivalents at :48, :66, :98, :134-190) — and then every constructor separately re-reads the same constant out of `get_details()` and shifts it to centre:
```cpp
Vector2F size = this->get_details().col_rect_size;
this->_rectangle.offset(-size.x / 2.0f, -size.y / 2.0f);
```
verbatim in ProjectileSpray.cpp:25-27, ProjectileJet.cpp:25-27, ProjectileBall.cpp:25-27, ProjectileMist.cpp:25-27 and ProjectileRolling.cpp:25-27. One conceptual operation — 'place a rect of size S centred on P' — spread across two files and six copies, with the caller required to know the callee will re-centre. The local also copies the `Vector2F` instead of binding a const reference, and the constructor calls a base accessor during its own construction to recover data it was itself handed.

**Fix:** Add `static RectangleF RectangleF::from_centre(const Vector2F& centre, const Vector2F& size)` and let the factory produce the already-centred rect once. The projectile constructor then stores what it is given and does no geometry — a constructor should not be recomputing placement.

#### 4. get_shape() hands out an interior pointer with no documented lifetime contract

`ArtAttack/ProjectileSpray.cpp:88-91` — **low** · `design`

The code is exactly as described: `const Shape* ProjectileSpray::get_shape() const { return &this->_rectangle; }` at ProjectileSpray.cpp:88-91, identical at ProjectileBall.cpp:87-90, ProjectileJet.cpp:86-89, ProjectileMist.cpp:88-91, ProjectileRolling.cpp:80-83. `ICollisionGameObject::get_shape()` (ICollisionGameObject.h:15) documents nothing about validity, and `Level::update_level_logic` both distributes these pointers (Level.cpp:227-293) and destroys projectiles by swap-and-pop in the same function (Level.cpp:296-305).

I am downgrading this from the reviewer's medium. Returning a `const*` to a member is ordinary C++, no current caller retains the pointer past the call, and the swap-and-pop loop runs after all collision testing has finished. The claimed use-after-free is entirely hypothetical — it only materialises if someone later adds a broad-phase cache or a deferred resolution list. Worth a comment, not a rewrite.

**Fix:** Document the contract on `ICollisionGameObject::get_shape()` — non-owning, valid until the next mutation of this object, never store. If a retained copy is ever needed, `MattMath::Shape::clone()` already exists.

## `ArtAttack/ResourceLoader.cpp`

_6 findings: 2 high, 1 medium, 3 low_

#### 1. The engine's resource loader hardcodes this one game's entire asset manifest, including its game-mode enum

`ArtAttack/ResourceLoader.cpp:17-51` — **high** · `design`

Merged from 3 candidates. This is the sharpest engine-reuse blocker in the module.

    void ResourceLoader::load_textures() const { load_sprite_sheet_from_directory(TEXTURE_DIRECTORY, "sprite_sheet_1"); }
    void ResourceLoader::load_fonts() { load_sprite_font_from_directory(FONT_DIRECTORY, "gill_sans_ultra_bold_144"); ...seven names... }
    void ResourceLoader::load_sounds() { load_sound_bank_from_directory(SOUNDS_DIRECTORY, "sound_bank_1"); }
    void ResourceLoader::load_level_info() const
    {
        load_level_info_from_directory(LEVEL_DIRECTORY, "king_of_the_hill", level_stage::KING_OF_THE_HILL);
        load_level_info_from_directory(LEVEL_DIRECTORY, "turbulence",       level_stage::TURBULENCE);
        load_level_info_from_directory(LEVEL_DIRECTORY, "close_quarters",   level_stage::CLOSE_QUARTERS);
    }

`load_all_resources()` (45-51) is the only externally-called entry point in the class, and it is a hardcoded list of twelve Splatoon-clone assets. Shipping a second game means forking this file. The loader is also the only place that knows the asset-file-to-lookup-key association, so nothing outside it can register an asset without a code change. Extensions are hardcoded too (".dds", ".spritefont", ".xwb", ".json" at lines 79, 107, 131-132, 148, 172-173).

It also loads serially on the main thread — the ThreadPool is constructed 22 lines earlier at Game.cpp:236 and sits idle — with no try/catch anywhere, so the first missing file terminates startup, and only `load_sprite_font` (83-101) adds any context to the error at all.

**Fix:** Make the manifest data: `void load_manifest(const std::filesystem::path&)` reading `{type, id, path}` entries. The project already has rapidjson wired up and sounds/sound_bank_1.json proves the pattern works. Wrap each entry individually, collect failures, and substitute a placeholder asset so a missing file degrades rather than terminates.

#### 2. The content manifest is hardcoded C++ inside the engine's loader; adding a level means editing engine code

`ArtAttack/ResourceLoader.cpp:17-51` — **high** · `design` · confidence: certain

```cpp
void ResourceLoader::load_textures() const { this->load_sprite_sheet_from_directory(TEXTURE_DIRECTORY, "sprite_sheet_1"); }
void ResourceLoader::load_fonts() { ... "gill_sans_ultra_bold_144" ... "courier_new_bold_16"; }
void ResourceLoader::load_level_info() const {
    this->load_level_info_from_directory(LEVEL_DIRECTORY, "king_of_the_hill", level_stage::KING_OF_THE_HILL);
    this->load_level_info_from_directory(LEVEL_DIRECTORY, "turbulence", level_stage::TURBULENCE);
    this->load_level_info_from_directory(LEVEL_DIRECTORY, "close_quarters", level_stage::CLOSE_QUARTERS);
}
```

There is no manifest file anywhere in the repo. The complete list of this game's assets lives in these 35 lines of the engine's resource loader. Compounding it, `ResourceManager` keys its level cache on the *game's* enum: `std::map<level_stage, std::unique_ptr<LevelLoadedInfo>> _level_infos;` with `level_stage` values `KING_OF_THE_HILL`, `TURBULENCE`, `CLOSE_QUARTERS` (ResourceManager.h:7,32,34,52; level_stage.h:4-11).

For a project whose stated goal is a reusable 2D engine, this means: a second game cannot use `ResourceLoader`/`ResourceManager` at all without editing them, and adding one level to *this* game requires touching level_stage.h, ResourceLoader.cpp and MainMenu.cpp (which switches on the enum at :1870 and computes `rand() % MAX_STAGE` at :1893-1895).

**Fix:** Move the manifest into data — e.g. `assets/manifest.json` listing textures, fonts, sound banks and levels by name and path — and key `ResourceManager::_level_infos` on `std::string` like every other cache in the class. `ResourceLoader` then becomes generic: read manifest, load each entry.

#### 3. load_sprite_font catches every std::exception and rethrows out_of_range with the original diagnostic destroyed

`ArtAttack/ResourceLoader.cpp:83-101` — **medium** · `robustness`

try { this->_resource_manager->add_sprite_font(font_name, std::make_unique<SpriteFont>(this->_device, ...)); }
    catch (const std::exception&)
    {
        std::string error = "SpriteFont " + font_name + " not found at " + font_path + ".";
        throw std::out_of_range(error);
    }

Three problems. (1) It catches `std::exception`, so a `bad_alloc`, a `DX::com_exception` from a device failure (pch.h:82-105 defines com_exception : std::exception), or any internal DirectXTK error is relabelled "font not found" with the real `what()` discarded — guaranteeing a misleading diagnosis. (2) `std::out_of_range` is a logic_error meaning "index out of range"; a missing asset file is not that. (3) The try block also wraps `add_sprite_font`, so a bad_alloc growing the map reports as a missing file.

Compare `load_texture` (54-73) which does the same job with no handler at all. The five loaders in this class disagree about whether load failure is worth reporting; four of the five report nothing.

**Fix:** Catch narrowly and chain: `catch (const std::exception& e) { throw std::runtime_error("failed to load SpriteFont '" + font_name + "' from " + font_path + ": " + e.what()); }`. Pick one error policy for the whole class and apply it to load_texture / load_sprite_sheet / load_sound_bank / load_level_info too.

#### 4. Only one of five loaders has any error handling, and it destroys the original error; narrow-to-wide path conversion is byte-copied

`ArtAttack/ResourceLoader.cpp:54-101` — **low** · `robustness` · confidence: certain

`load_sprite_font` (:83-101) is the sole loader with a try/catch:
```cpp
catch (const std::exception&) {
    std::string error = "SpriteFont " + font_name + " not found at " + font_path + ".";
    throw std::out_of_range(error);
}
```
It catches *every* exception — corrupt file, out of video memory, device removed — and reports all of them as "not found", discarding the original `what()`. `load_texture`, `load_sprite_sheet`, `load_level_info` and `load_sound_bank` have no handling at all, so `DX::ThrowIfFailed` (:60) and the `WaveBank` constructor (:156) propagate raw HRESULT exceptions out through `Game::initialize`.

Separately, three sites widen a narrow path by copying bytes into wchar_t: `std::wstring(texture_path.begin(), texture_path.end())` at :62, the same for fonts at :91-92 and for the wave bank at :158-159. This is only correct for ASCII; the moment a path picks up a non-ASCII character (an install directory, a user name) it produces mojibake and the file is not found.

Minor: `load_texture` at :66-70 does `resource.As(&texture)` and `texture->GetDesc(&texture_desc)`, then discards `texture_desc` entirely — a pointless second COM QueryInterface plus driver call on every texture load.

Also structural: the ten `load_X` / `load_X_from_directory` pairs (:54-175) each duplicate `directory + name + ".ext"` with the extension hardcoded per asset type.

**Fix:** Use `std::filesystem::path` (available once the project moves off its default /std:c++14) for all path handling and widening. Catch narrowly and chain the original message (`std::throw_with_nested`, or append `e.what()`). Delete the unused texture-desc query. Collapse the from_directory overloads into one helper taking the extension.

#### 5. char-to-wchar_t path conversion via iterator range is wrong for any byte >= 0x80

`ArtAttack/ResourceLoader.cpp:62, 91-92, 158-159` — **low** · `correctness`

std::wstring(texture_path.begin(), texture_path.end()).c_str()

`std::wstring(first, last)` widens each `char` by integral conversion. On MSVC `char` is signed, so any byte >= 0x80 sign-extends into the 0xFF80-0xFFFF range rather than the intended character. It also materialises a temporary wstring on every load. Three sites: line 62 (texture), 91-92 (sprite font), 158-159 (wave bank).

DOWNGRADED from the reviewers' medium. Two candidates described this failing on "an accented user directory" or "any non-ASCII in a user's install path" — that is not reachable here. Every path fed to these calls is built by concatenating a `directory_consts` literal, an asset-name literal and an extension literal (ResourceLoader.cpp:79, 107, 131-132, 148, 172-173), all CWD-relative and pure ASCII. The construct is genuinely wrong, but it cannot misbehave with the current inputs, so this is a cleanup rather than a defect.

**Fix:** Store asset paths as `std::wstring`/`std::filesystem::path` end-to-end so no conversion is needed (`directory_consts` becomes `const wchar_t*`). If a conversion is genuinely required, use `MultiByteToWideChar(CP_UTF8, ...)`.

#### 6. load_texture does a QueryInterface and GetDesc whose results are discarded, and the QI can reject valid textures

`ArtAttack/ResourceLoader.cpp:66-70` — **low** · `correctness`

ComPtr<ID3D11Texture2D> texture;
    DX::ThrowIfFailed(resource.As(&texture));

    CD3D11_TEXTURE2D_DESC texture_desc;
    texture->GetDesc(&texture_desc);

    this->_resource_manager->add_texture(texture_name, m_texture.Get());

`texture_desc` is filled and never read; `texture` is used for nothing else. Leftover debugging code, but not inert: `resource.As(&texture)` is wrapped in `ThrowIfFailed`, so any DDS that is not a 2D texture (a volume texture, a 1D texture) throws a `com_exception` at load time even though the shader resource view was created successfully at lines 60-64 and would work fine. The engine rejects valid assets to compute a value it throws away, plus an extra COM call and refcount round-trip per texture.

**Fix:** Delete lines 66-70 outright. If the dimensions are wanted later, return them from the function rather than computing them into a dead local.

## `ArtAttack/ResourceManager.cpp`

_11 findings: 7 high, 4 medium_

#### 1. All four ResourceManager getters use map::operator[] wrapped in a catch that can never fire, so a missing asset returns nullptr and every render call site dereferences it

`ArtAttack/ResourceManager.cpp:7-102` — **high** · `correctness`

Reported by five reviewers; all correct. `get_texture` (7-19), `get_sprite_font` (27-38), `get_sprite_sheet` (46-58) and `get_sound_bank` (91-102) are all this shape:
```cpp
try { return this->_sprite_sheets[sprite_sheet_name].get(); }
catch (const std::out_of_range&) { throw std::out_of_range("SpriteSheet ... not found."); }
```
`std::map::operator[]` never throws `out_of_range` — it default-inserts and returns `nullptr`. The catch block is unreachable dead code and the documented contract is a fiction. (`get_level_info` at :66-78 gets it right with `.at()`, so the codebase disagrees with itself in the same file.)

Every consumer in the rendering module dereferences the result unchecked: SpriteSheetObject.cpp:33-34, TextureObject.cpp:24-26 and :43-45, AnimationObject.cpp:26, :33, :52, TextObject.cpp:29-30 and :49-50, DebugText.cpp:106-115, InterfaceGameplay.cpp:66-73, 113-120, 153-156, 183-188. So one misspelled or unshipped asset name becomes a null dereference mid-frame on a worker thread instead of a diagnosable load error — and the names involved are hardcoded literals in engine-level headers (`interface_consts::SPRITE_SHEET`, `TIMER_FONT`, `debug_text_consts::DEBUG_FONT`).

It also makes the getters non-const and inserting, which is what turns a missing-name mistake into a shared-map mutation from the parallel draw pass.

**Fix:** Use `.at()` inside the try so the catch becomes live, or better `find()` + an explicit throw naming the key. Then mark all four getters `const` and have them return `const T*`. Add a startup validation pass in `ResourceLoader` that resolves every name the engine hardcodes, so failures surface once at load.

#### 2. Four resource getters use map::operator[] inside a catch(out_of_range) that can never fire — a miss silently inserts a null entry and returns nullptr

`ArtAttack/ResourceManager.cpp:7-19, 27-38, 46-58, 91-102` — **high** · `correctness`

Merged from 5 candidates (all five reviewers found this). Verbatim:

    ID3D11ShaderResourceView* ResourceManager::get_texture(const std::string& texture_name)
    {
        try { return this->_textures[texture_name].Get(); }
        catch (const std::out_of_range&) { throw std::out_of_range("Texture " + texture_name + " not found."); }
    }

`std::map::operator[]` never throws `out_of_range` — it default-inserts. So:
- All four catch blocks are unreachable dead code: get_texture (7-19), get_sprite_font (27-38), get_sprite_sheet (46-58), get_sound_bank (91-102). The "not found" diagnostic the author believes they wrote can never run.
- A misspelled or unloaded name silently grows the map with a null entry and returns `nullptr`, which callers dereference unchecked far away: `SoundBankObject::get_sb()->play_wave(...)` (SoundBankObject.cpp:25) and `SpriteSheetObject::get_sprite_sheet()` (SpriteSheetObject.cpp:31-35) feeding `SpriteBatch::Draw`.
- The lookup MUTATES the container, which is why all four are non-const, which forces every consumer to hold a mutable `ResourceManager*`.

`get_level_info` (66-78) is the counterexample in the same file: it uses `.at()`, it is the only one that reports missing keys, and it is the only one that is `const`. The correct idiom is already present ten lines away.

Same defect one level down in `SpriteSheet::draw`: `this->_sprite_frames[frame_name]` at SpriteSheet.cpp:105 and :126 silently inserts a zero-initialised SpriteFrame for an unknown frame name.

**Fix:** Use `.at()` (or `find()` + explicit throw carrying the key) in all four, mark them `const` and `[[nodiscard]]`, and delete the try/catch wrappers — `.at()`'s own throw is strictly better than one that discards the original message. Collapse the four near-identical bodies into one `template <class Map> auto& lookup(const Map&, const std::string&, const char* kind)`.

#### 3. Resource "getters" use map::operator[] — mutating lookup from render threads, dead catch blocks, silent nullptr on typo

`ArtAttack/ResourceManager.cpp:7-58` — **high** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

```cpp
ID3D11ShaderResourceView* ResourceManager::get_texture(const std::string& texture_name)
{
    try { return this->_textures[texture_name].Get(); }
    catch (const std::out_of_range&) { throw std::out_of_range("Texture " + texture_name + " not found."); }
}
```

Repeated verbatim at ResourceManager.cpp:27-38 (`_sprite_fonts[...]`), :46-58 (`_sprite_sheets[...]`), :91-102 (`_sound_banks[...]`). Three separate problems:

1. **The catch is unreachable.** `std::map::operator[]` never throws `out_of_range`; it default-inserts. So a missing/misspelled resource name silently inserts a null entry and returns `nullptr`, which is then dereferenced (e.g. `sprite_sheet->draw(...)` in TextureObject.cpp:26, `sprite_font->DrawString(...)` in InterfaceGameplay.cpp:156). The intended error message is dead code.
2. **It is a write, not a read.** These "get" functions are non-const and can restructure the map. They are called from the render worker threads: `SpriteSheetObject::get_sprite_sheet()` (SpriteSheetObject.cpp:31-35) is on the hot path of `TextureObject::draw` (TextureObject.cpp:24) and `AnimationObject::draw` (AnimationObject.cpp:33, 52), and `InterfaceGameplay::draw_ammo/draw_health/draw_timer` (InterfaceGameplay.cpp:66, 88, 113, 135, 153, 183) run inside `Level::draw_player_view_level` on N threads simultaneously against the one shared `ResourceManager`.
3. **Same pattern one level down**: `SpriteSheet::draw` (SpriteSheet.cpp:105, 126) does `this->_sprite_frames[frame_name].get_source_rectangle()` — a mutating lookup on a shared sprite sheet, from all render threads, and a missing frame name silently draws a default-constructed `SpriteFrame`.

**Fix:** Make all lookups `const` and use `find()`/`at()` with an explicit not-found path that throws a descriptive exception (or returns an engine-level `Result`). Mark the accessors `const`, which also makes the concurrent-read safety self-documenting. Delete the unreachable try/catch blocks. Consider interning resource names to integer handles so lookups are not string-keyed map probes on the render hot path.

#### 4. Four of five ResourceManager getters use map::operator[] inside a catch(out_of_range) that can never fire

`ArtAttack/ResourceManager.cpp:7-102` — **high** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

```cpp
ID3D11ShaderResourceView* ResourceManager::get_texture(const std::string& texture_name) {
    try { return this->_textures[texture_name].Get(); }        // :12  operator[] never throws
    catch (const std::out_of_range&) { ... throw std::out_of_range(error); }  // dead code
}
```

`std::map::operator[]` default-constructs a new entry for an unknown key and never throws, so the catch block is unreachable and the "Texture X not found" diagnostic is dead. What actually happens on a typo is that the map silently grows a null entry and the caller receives `nullptr`, which is then handed straight to `SpriteBatch::Draw` / `SpriteFont::DrawString`.

Same at get_sprite_font (:31), get_sprite_sheet (:51), get_sound_bank (:95). `get_level_info` (:71) correctly uses `.at()` — so the author knew the right idiom and applied it once out of five times.

**Fix:** Use `.at()` in all five, or better `find()` + an explicit `throw resource_not_found(name)`. Mark all five getters `const` (only `get_level_info` is, purely because it uses `.at()`).

#### 5. Mutating map lookups run concurrently on thread-pool workers during parallel draw — genuine data race

`ArtAttack/ResourceManager.cpp:46-58` — **high** · `concurrency`

`get_sprite_sheet` calls `this->_sprite_sheets[sprite_sheet_name]`, a non-const mutating operation, and it sits on the parallel draw path. I traced the full chain:

  Level::draw_active_level (Level.cpp:386-397) -> ThreadPool::add_task, one task per partition
    -> Level::draw_player_view_level (worker thread) -> object->draw(...)
    -> TextureObject::draw (TextureObject.cpp:24, 43) -> SpriteSheetObject::get_sprite_sheet (SpriteSheetObject.cpp:31-35)
    -> ResourceManager::get_sprite_sheet

Multiple worker threads therefore invoke `operator[]` on the SAME `std::map` simultaneously with no synchronisation. Even when no insertion occurs this is a data race by the standard's rules (non-const member on a shared object); if any name misses, one thread rebalances the red-black tree while others walk it.

`SpriteSheet::draw` is the same shape one level down: non-const, `this->_sprite_frames[frame_name]` at SpriteSheet.cpp:105 and :126, invoked from the same worker threads. `MenuPage::draw_mobjects_in_viewports` (MenuPage.cpp:124-150) reaches the identical path for menus.

**Fix:** Make every read-only accessor genuinely read-only and `const` (`.at()`/`find()` on a const map) and mark `SpriteSheet::draw` const. That removes the race with no lock. Enforce it by handing draw code a `const ResourceManager&` so a mutating lookup will not compile.

#### 6. reset_all_* null out the mapped values but keep the keys, turning "released" into a silent nullptr, and dangle every cached SoundBank*

`ArtAttack/ResourceManager.cpp:104-126` — **high** · `correctness`

Merged from 5 candidates.

    void ResourceManager::reset_all_sprite_fonts() { for (auto& font : _sprite_fonts) font.second.reset(); }
    void ResourceManager::reset_all_textures()     { for (auto& t : _textures) t.second.Reset(); }
    void ResourceManager::reset_all_sounds()       { for (auto& sb : _sound_banks) { sb.second->reset_all_instances(); sb.second.reset(); } }

Every key survives with a null value. Combined with the `operator[]`/`.at()`+`.get()` getters above, a post-reset lookup SUCCEEDS and returns `nullptr`, so failure surfaces as an access violation inside `SpriteBatch::Draw` or `SoundEffectInstance::Play` instead of at the lookup. `SoundBank::reset_all_instances` (SoundBank.cpp:180-187) has the identical shape.

Three further verified problems in these 22 lines, all reachable from `Game::OnDeviceLost` (Game.cpp:269-280):
- `reset_all_sounds()` destroys the SoundBank objects outright, but `Level::_sound_bank` is a raw non-owning pointer cached once at Level.cpp:59 and used at Level.cpp:63, 73, 74, 134, 136, 147, 171. Those are dangling immediately, and Level is never notified.
- Audio has no relationship to the D3D11 device. Tearing down every wave bank and voice because the GPU was lost is simply wrong.
- `sb.second->reset_all_instances()` is redundant — the very next statement destroys the whole SoundBank, which destroys its instances anyway.
- The API is asymmetric: `_sprite_sheets` and `_level_infos` have no reset, so SpriteSheet objects survive holding the raw `ID3D11ShaderResourceView*` that `reset_all_textures` just released.

**Fix:** `.clear()` the maps so lookups fail loudly, remove `reset_all_sounds()` from the device-lost path entirely, and delete the redundant `reset_all_instances()` call. Longer term, give GPU-backed caches a real `reload(ID3D11Device1*)` that restores objects in place so cached pointers stay valid.

#### 7. reset_all_* nulls map entries instead of erasing them, leaving booby-trapped keys that lookups happily return

`ArtAttack/ResourceManager.cpp:104-126` — **high** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

```cpp
void ResourceManager::reset_all_sprite_fonts() {
    for (auto& font : this->_sprite_fonts) { font.second.reset(); }   // key stays, value is now null
}
void ResourceManager::reset_all_textures() {
    for (auto& texture : this->_textures) { texture.second.Reset(); }
}
void ResourceManager::reset_all_sounds() {
    for (auto& sound_bank : this->_sound_banks) { sound_bank.second->reset_all_instances(); sound_bank.second.reset(); }
}
```

After these run, `get_sprite_font("x")` still finds the key and returns `nullptr` — there is no "unloaded" state, no reload-on-demand, and no way for a caller to tell "never loaded" from "released". Combined with the `operator[]` getters above, every failure mode in this class collapses to "returns nullptr, caller dereferences it".

`SoundBank::reset_all_instances` (SoundBank.cpp:180-187) repeats the pattern one level down: it `.reset()`s each `unique_ptr<SoundEffectInstance>` but leaves the map keys, so `get_sound_effect_instance` (SoundBank.cpp:78, which does use `.at()`) succeeds and returns `nullptr`, and `play_effect` (SoundBank.cpp:33-37) immediately calls `sei->SetVolume(...)` on it.

Also: `SpriteSheet::_texture` (SpriteSheet.h:63) is a raw borrowed `ID3D11ShaderResourceView*` that `reset_all_textures()` invalidates without notifying anyone.

**Fix:** Either `clear()` the maps (and make lookups fail loudly) or introduce a real two-phase resource handle with an explicit `is_loaded()` and a reload path. Do not leave null values behind keys that lookups treat as success.

#### 8. ResourceManager is five copy-pasted caches; adding a resource type means editing three classes plus OnDeviceLost

`ArtAttack/ResourceManager.cpp:7-126` — **medium** · `design`

The class is the same six-line pattern instantiated five times — `_textures`, `_sprite_fonts`, `_sprite_sheets`, `_level_infos`, `_sound_banks` — each with `add_X`, `get_X`, and (for three of them) `reset_all_X`. Lines 27-38 vs 46-58 vs 91-102 are identical modulo the member name and one string literal. The three `reset_all_*` bodies (104-126) differ only in the member and the spelling of reset.

Adding shaders or particle definitions requires touching ResourceManager.h, ResourceManager.cpp, ResourceLoader.h, ResourceLoader.cpp, and `Game::OnDeviceLost` (Game.cpp:277-279) which hand-enumerates the reset calls — a list that has already drifted (two of the five caches have no reset at all).

**Fix:** One `template <class T> class AssetCache` plus a type-erased registry (`unordered_map<type_index, unique_ptr<IAssetCache>>`) exposing `get<T>(AssetId)` / `add<T>(...)` / `for_each_cache(fn)`. `OnDeviceLost` becomes one loop instead of a hand-written list.

#### 9. Every ResourceManager lookup uses map::operator[] inside a catch(out_of_range) that can never fire

`ArtAttack/ResourceManager.cpp:7-19` — **medium** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

ID3D11ShaderResourceView* ResourceManager::get_texture(const std::string& texture_name)
    {
        try { return this->_textures[texture_name].Get(); }
        catch (const std::out_of_range&) { throw std::out_of_range("Texture " + texture_name + " not found."); }
    }

`std::map::operator[]` never throws `out_of_range` — it default-inserts. So a misspelled or missing name silently inserts a null entry and returns `nullptr`, and the caller null-dereferences somewhere far away instead of getting the intended diagnostic. The catch block is unreachable dead code. Identical at `get_sprite_font` (line 31), `get_sprite_sheet` (line 51), `get_sound_bank` (line 95). Only `get_level_info` (line 71) uses `.at()` correctly.

This is squarely on the end-of-match path: `SoundBankObject::get_sb()` (SoundBankObject.cpp:16) calls `get_sound_bank` on **every** sound call — `EndMenuInitial::update` alone hits it at EndMenu.cpp:38, 45, 52, 59, 66, 74, 103 — and `EndMenuPage`'s bank name is a bare string literal (`end_menu_consts::SOUND_BANK`, EndMenu.h:36).

A side effect is that all four getters are non-`const` mutating operations on a shared map, which is why `ResourceManager*` can never be handed to the thread-pool draw tasks safely (`MenuPage::draw_mobjects_in_viewports`, MenuPage.cpp:140-150, and `Level::draw_player_view_level`, Level.cpp:491-593, both call into them from workers).

**Fix:** Use `.at()` and let it throw, or `find()` + an explicit error. Make all five getters `const` (the maps then need `mutable`-free const lookup, which `.at()` gives you) so concurrent reads from thread-pool tasks are actually defined. Longer term, resolve resources to handles once at load time instead of doing a string map lookup per draw call per frame.

#### 10. Sprite-sheet lookup uses mutating map::operator[] behind a dead catch, and is called from thread-pool draw tasks

`ArtAttack/ResourceManager.cpp:46-58` — **medium** · `robustness`

Verified, and reached on every projectile draw and every projectile animation tick. `ResourceManager::get_sprite_sheet` is a non-const member whose whole body is:
```cpp
try { return this->_sprite_sheets[sprite_sheet_name].get(); }
catch (const std::out_of_range&) { ... throw std::out_of_range(error); }
```
Two real defects:

(a) **The catch is dead code.** `std::map::operator[]` default-inserts on a miss and never throws `out_of_range`. So a wrong sheet name silently returns `nullptr` instead of the intended diagnostic, and the caller dereferences it unchecked — `AnimationObject`'s constructor does `this->_frame_time = this->get_animation_strip()->get_frame_time();` (AnimationObject.cpp:21) with no null check. Access violation, no message. The identical dead-catch pattern is at ResourceManager.cpp:7-19 (get_texture), :27-38 (get_sprite_font), :66-80 and :91-102.

(b) **The API is not const and is called concurrently.** `Level::draw_active_level` submits one task per player partition to a real thread pool (Level.cpp:375-399), and each task's `draw` path reaches `SpriteSheetObject::get_sprite_sheet()` -> this lookup. I am tempering the reviewers' framing here: with all keys present, `operator[]` performs no tree mutation, so this is a latent race rather than live corruption — but the function's signature permits insertion, so the safety of the entire multi-threaded draw path rests on 'the key always happens to be there'.

Merged from 3 candidate reports; two graded this high/critical on the corruption claim, which I do not think holds for present keys.

**Fix:** Make the getters `const` and non-mutating: `auto it = _sprite_sheets.find(name); if (it == _sprite_sheets.end()) throw std::runtime_error("SpriteSheet " + name + " not found");`. That kills the dead catch, restores the diagnostic, and makes the draw path provably read-only. Then remove the lookup from the hot path entirely — see the caching finding.

#### 11. get_sound_bank uses map::operator[] so an unknown name returns nullptr through a dead catch, and Level dereferences it unchecked

`ArtAttack/ResourceManager.cpp:91-102` — **medium** · `correctness`

```cpp
SoundBank* ResourceManager::get_sound_bank(const std::string& sound_bank_name)
{
    try { return this->_sound_banks[sound_bank_name].get(); }
    catch (const std::out_of_range&) { ... throw std::out_of_range(error); }
}
```
`std::map::operator[]` never throws `out_of_range` — it **default-inserts** a null `unique_ptr<SoundBank>` for the missing key and returns `nullptr`. The catch is unreachable dead code and the map is silently polluted with a null entry. Contrast the correct sibling `get_level_info` (ResourceManager.cpp:66-78), which uses `.at()` inside the same try/catch shape.

The name comes straight from level JSON: `LevelLoadedInfo::get_sound_bank_name()` (LevelLoadedInfo.cpp:72-75) → LevelBuilder.cpp:72 → `Level::Level` stores the result at Level.cpp:59 with no check. The first `update()` then dereferences it at Level.cpp:73 (`_sound_bank->play_effect(...)`) — a null deref with no diagnostic. `StructurePaintable.cpp:34` has the same exposure with the hardcoded `"sound_bank_1"`.

I am reporting this here rather than under Level because the fix belongs in the accessor, but the level module is the sole consumer and the one that crashes.

**Fix:** Use `.at()` inside the try so the catch becomes live, or return by reference and throw a descriptive exception on miss. Independently, Level's constructor should validate its injected dependencies (`resource_manager`, `dt`, `sampler_state`, the resolved sound bank) and fail loudly at construction.

## `ArtAttack/ResourceManager.h`

_7 findings: 2 high, 4 medium, 1 low_

#### 1. The game-mode enum `level_stage` is baked into the engine's asset cache as a map key type

`ArtAttack/ResourceManager.h:7, 32-35, 52` — **high** · `design`

`ResourceManager` — the engine's asset cache — `#include`s `level_stage.h` (line 7) and stores `std::map<level_stage, std::unique_ptr<LevelLoadedInfo>> _level_infos;` (line 52), with `get_level_info(level_stage)` / `add_level_info(level_stage, ...)` (lines 32-35). `level_stage` enumerates this game's three maps plus a menu concept.

Every other resource type in the same class is keyed by `std::string`, so this is not even internally consistent — it exists only so game code can write `get_level_info(settings.get_stage())`. `ResourceLoader.h:6` inherits the dependency, and so does every TU that includes `GameData.h`. The engine literally knows a game mode is called King of the Hill.

**Fix:** Key level definitions like every other asset — by an `AssetId` (string or interned handle). Delete `level_stage` from ResourceManager and ResourceLoader; let the game map its own `level_stage` -> asset id in game-side code (a table in LevelBuilder or in the manifest).

#### 2. The resource cache is keyed on this game's three map names, and the asset manifest is compiled C++

`ArtAttack/ResourceManager.h:7, 32-34, 52 (with ResourceLoader.cpp:17-51)` — **high** · `design` · confidence: certain

`ResourceManager` — the engine's asset cache — includes `level_stage.h` (:7) and keys its level cache on it: `const LevelLoadedInfo* get_level_info(level_stage stage) const` (:32), `void add_level_info(level_stage stage, ...)` (:34), `std::map<level_stage, std::unique_ptr<LevelLoadedInfo>> _level_infos` (:52). `level_stage` (level_stage.h:4-11) is `{ KING_OF_THE_HILL, TURBULENCE, CLOSE_QUARTERS, RANDOM }` — literally the names of this game's three maps. Every other cache in the class is keyed by `std::string`; only levels got a game-specific enum.

Compounding it, the *entire* asset manifest is hardcoded in `ResourceLoader.cpp`: `load_textures()` loads one sheet, `"sprite_sheet_1"` (:19); `load_fonts()` names 7 specific `gill_sans_*`/`courier_new_bold_16` fonts (:23-31); `load_sounds()` loads `"sound_bank_1"` (:35); `load_level_info()` maps three literal filenames to three enum values (:40-42). Shipping a fourth map, renaming a font, or adding a second atlas requires editing engine source and recompiling.

**Fix:** Key `_level_infos` by `std::string` like every other cache, and delete `level_stage.h` from the engine (the game's stage-select menu can carry its own enum or just strings). Replace the hardcoded `load_textures/load_fonts/load_sounds/load_level_info` bodies with a data-driven manifest (e.g. `content/manifest.json` listing textures, fonts, sound banks, levels) that `ResourceLoader::load_all_resources()` iterates.

#### 3. Engine headers are not self-contained — they compile only behind this project's pch — and drag rapidjson into every TU

`ArtAttack/ResourceManager.h:1-11` — **medium** · `header-hygiene`

Merged from 1 candidate, verified against pch.h.

(a) NOT SELF-CONTAINED. `ResourceManager.h` names `Microsoft::WRL::ComPtr<ID3D11ShaderResourceView>` (line 48), `std::unique_ptr` (50-53) and `DirectX::SpriteFont` (line 22) while including only <map>, <string>, SpriteSheet.h, level_stage.h, LevelLoadedInfo.h, <Audio.h>, SoundBank.h. I read pch.h: it is what supplies <wrl/client.h> (line 34), <d3d11_1.h> (36), <memory> (49) and SpriteFont.h (75). `SpriteSheet.h` is worse — it names `ID3D11ShaderResourceView`, `DirectX::SpriteBatch`, `RECT` and `std::unique_ptr` with none of them included. A header that only compiles behind one specific .vcxproj's pch is unusable outside it, which is fatal to the stated engine-reuse goal.

(b) TRANSITIVE WEIGHT. `GameData.h -> ResourceLoader.h -> ResourceManager.h -> SoundBank.h -> <rapidjson/document.h>` compiles a JSON library into every TU that includes GameData.h — which, since `GameData*` is the universal parameter, is nearly all of them — purely so two PRIVATE member declarations (SoundBank.h:45-47) can name `const rapidjson::Value&`. `SoundBank.h:10` includes `MattMath.h` and uses no MattMath type in the header (it is there so the .cpp's `using namespace MattMath;` finds `clamp`). `ResourceManager.h:9` includes <Audio.h> although it names no audio type. `Save.h:4,7` include <iostream> and <rapidjson/document.h> although neither appears in that header. All 13 GameData members are pointers/handles, so GameData.h needs no concrete engine headers at all.

**Fix:** Make every engine header compile standalone (add a self-contained-header check to the build). Forward-declare (`class ResourceManager;`, `namespace DirectX { class AudioEngine; }`) instead of including where only pointers/references appear; use rapidjson/fwd.h — already vendored — for the `Value` parameters; move the .cpp-only includes out of the headers.

#### 4. <Audio.h> (XAudio2) is parsed by 56 of 81 TUs via ResourceManager.h

`ArtAttack/ResourceManager.h:8` — **medium** · `performance` · confidence: certain

ResourceManager.h:8 does `#include <Audio.h>` - DirectXTK's audio header, which pulls in the XAudio2 redist headers via the USING_XAUDIO2_REDIST define from the NuGet targets. Nothing in ResourceManager.h uses a DirectXTK audio type directly; the sound support goes through `std::map<std::string, std::unique_ptr<SoundBank>> _sound_banks;` (line 53) and SoundBank.h is included separately on line 10. Because ResourceManager.h reaches 52 TUs and Game.h adds more, I measured Audio.h being parsed by 56 of 81 translation units. Combined with the rapidjson finding, the two heaviest third-party headers in the project are both in the include closure of three quarters of the build for no reason.

**Fix:** Delete ResourceManager.h:8 and let SoundBank.h own the audio dependency (and forward-declare SoundBank in ResourceManager.h so even that is confined to ResourceManager.cpp).

#### 5. Everything is loaded eagerly at startup and there is no unload API at all — no resource scoping for an engine

`ArtAttack/ResourceManager.h:14-54` — **medium** · `design` · confidence: certain

`ResourceManager`'s entire public surface is `add_*`, `get_*` and three `reset_all_*`. There is no `remove`, `unload`, `erase`, reference count, or resource-set/bundle concept. `load_all_resources()` (ResourceLoader.cpp:45-51) loads *all three* levels' `LevelLoadedInfo` (each keeping its full parsed rapidjson `Document` resident — 21 KB, 22 KB and 13 KB of JSON, plus the DOM overhead), the 2.2 MB sprite sheet, seven SpriteFonts and the entire wave bank at process start, and nothing is ever released until exit. Transitioning between levels (GameLevel/GameMenu in GameStates.cpp) never touches the resource manager.

That is defensible for a three-level student game; it is not defensible for a reusable engine, which is the stated goal. There is no way for a game to say "these assets belong to this level" and get them back.

**Fix:** Introduce a resource-scope/bundle handle (`ResourceScope scope = rm.open_scope("level:turbulence")`) whose destruction releases everything loaded through it, and make level info lazily loaded on first request rather than all three up front. At minimum, add `unload(name)` / `unload_all()` so the API is capable of the thing an engine has to do.

#### 6. No asset-handle abstraction: assets are re-resolved by string map lookup on every draw

`ArtAttack/ResourceManager.h:17-44` — **medium** · `design`

Merged from 2 candidates. Every accessor takes `const std::string&` and returns a raw non-owning pointer, and consumers store the NAME rather than the resolved asset. Verified chain: `TextureObject::draw` (TextureObject.cpp:24, 43) calls `SpriteSheetObject::get_sprite_sheet()` (SpriteSheetObject.cpp:31-35), a `std::map<std::string, unique_ptr<SpriteSheet>>` lookup keyed on `_sheet_name`; `SpriteSheet::draw` then does a SECOND `std::map<std::string, SpriteFrame>` lookup keyed on the frame name (SpriteSheet.cpp:105, 126).

Because `Level::draw_player_view_level` redraws the world once per player viewport, the cost is roughly `objects x players x 2` red-black-tree walks with string compares per frame, all recomputing a constant. There is also no way to detect a typo'd asset name at build time.

All five caches are `std::map` (ordered) although nothing needs ordered iteration.

**Fix:** Introduce `AssetHandle<T>` (index or shared_ptr<const T>) resolved once by the registry. `SpriteSheetObject` should hold `AssetHandle<SpriteSheet>` resolved in its constructor, not `std::string _sheet_name`. Keep the string lookup as a one-time `resolve(AssetId) -> Handle` used at load/build time only. If a name cache remains, `unordered_map` fits better.

#### 7. No [[nodiscard]] anywhere in the project, and Save::get_save_data is entirely dead

`ArtAttack/ResourceManager.h:17-44` — **low** · `api-quality`

A grep for `nodiscard` across all first-party files returns zero hits. The unambiguous candidates in this module are pure accessors whose return value is the point of the call: `ResourceManager::get_texture/get_sprite_font/get_sprite_sheet/get_level_info/get_sound_bank` (ResourceManager.h:17-40), `SoundBank::get_effect_state`/`is_effect_looping` (SoundBank.h:31-32), `ThreadPool::get_min_num_threads`/`get_max_num_threads` (ThreadPool.h:18-19), `Save::get_resolution`/`get_fullscreen` (Save.h:25-26) and all 13 `GameData::get_*`.

Relatedly, `Save::get_save_data()` (Save.h:23, Save.cpp:154-157) returns `SaveData` by value and has zero callers anywhere in the tree — the whole accessor is dead.

(`[[nodiscard]]` is C++17, so this depends on the LanguageStandard finding above.)

**Fix:** Bump the standard, then add `[[nodiscard]]` to every pure getter in the module. Delete `get_save_data` and the redundant `= SaveData()` initialiser at Save.h:29.

## `ArtAttack/ResultsMenu.cpp`

_6 findings: 2 high, 3 medium, 1 low_

#### 1. Results fill bars are sized in 1920x1080 design units after the container was already scaled

`ArtAttack/ResultsMenu.cpp:225-261` — **high** · `correctness`

`ResultsMenuInitial::init()` builds everything in design space and scales once at lines 194-197 (`_texture_container->scale_objects_to_new_resolution(DEFAULT_RESOLUTION, resolution)`). But `update_team_a_fill()` / `update_team_b_fill()` run every frame after that and write raw design-space numbers into the already-scaled rectangles:
```cpp
float max_width = RESULTS_MENU_TEAM_FILL_SIZE.x * score;  // 680.0f, unscaled (ResultsMenu.h:21-23)
this->_team_a_fill->set_width(fill * max_width);
```
`calculate_team_b_fill_top_right_position()` (254-261) is worse — it adds the already-scaled `_fill_box` position and width to the UNSCALED `RESULTS_MENU_TEAM_FILL_BORDER` constant. This happens to be consistent when called from `init()` at line 153 (pre-scale) but is inconsistent when called from `update_team_b_fill()` at line 251 (post-scale). At 1280x720 (scale 0.667) `_fill_box` renders ~466px wide while the bars are driven to 680px, overflowing the box; at higher resolutions a 100% bar underfills. The height IS correct because it was baked in before scaling (lines 114, 125), so the aspect is wrong too. Only 1920x1080 is right.

**Fix:** Derive the bar extent from the live, already-scaled `_fill_box` rectangle every frame — `max_width = _fill_box->get_rectangle().get_width() - 2 * scaled_border.x` — so the animation is scale-agnostic by construction, and delete the design-space constant from the per-frame path.

#### 2. Results-screen fill bars are sized in 1920-space after the widgets have already been scaled to the real resolution

`ArtAttack/ResultsMenu.cpp:225-252` — **high** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

`init()` scales every widget from the 1920x1080 design space to the real resolution:

    // ResultsMenu.cpp:192-197
    const Vector2F resolution = this->get_float_resolution();
    this->_texture_container->scale_objects_to_new_resolution(DEFAULT_RESOLUTION, resolution);

(`MContainer::scale_objects_to_new_resolution` -> `MTexture::scale_size_and_position` -> `_rectangle.scale_size_and_position`, Mh.cpp:78-91, 180-183.)

But every frame afterwards, `update_team_a_fill`/`update_team_b_fill` overwrite the width with an *unscaled* design-space value:

    float max_width = RESULTS_MENU_TEAM_FILL_SIZE.x * score;   // 680.0f * ratio, 1920-space
    ...
    this->_team_a_fill->set_width(width);                      // absolute write, Mh.cpp:212-215

`MTexture::set_width` writes an absolute width into the already-scaled rectangle. At 1280x720 the fill bars come out 1.5x too wide and overflow the fill box; at 2560x1440 they are two thirds too short. The anchor for team B (`calculate_team_b_fill_top_right_position`, lines 254-261) is derived from the *scaled* `_fill_box`, so team B's bar is correctly anchored but wrongly sized — the two bars will not meet.

**Fix:** Cache the resolution scale factor in `init()` (or store the scaled `RESULTS_MENU_TEAM_FILL_SIZE` once) and multiply `max_width` by it, or express the animation as a fraction of the already-scaled `_fill_box` width: `max_width = (_fill_box->get_rectangle().get_width() - 2*border_scaled) * score`. The general bug is that `scale_objects_to_new_resolution` is a one-shot mutation with no record of the scale, so any later absolute setter silently reintroduces design-space units.

#### 3. Results menu polls the pad every update but discards the resulting edge until two timers expire

`ArtAttack/ResultsMenu.cpp:29-70` — **medium** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

```
void ResultsMenuInitial::update()
{
    const float dt = *this->get_data()->get_dt();
    std::vector<ProcessedMenuInput> menu_inputs = this->get_menu_inputs();
    if (this->_delay_timer < RESULTS_MENU_TEAM_FILL_DELAY) { this->_delay_timer += dt; }
    else { ... if (this->_fill_timer >= RESULTS_MENU_TEAM_FILL_TIME) { ... if (this->_show_results_timer >= RESULTS_MENU_SHOW_RESULTS_DELAY) { ... int continue_input = this->check_for_continue_input(menu_inputs);
```

The poll at line 32 always runs — which correctly advances `MenuInput::_prev_inputs` — but the computed PROCEED edge is only *read* at line 58, inside two nested timer gates. Because the edge is derived from a single-frame comparison and is not latched anywhere, a release-edge that lands on the frame before `_show_results_timer` crosses the threshold is destroyed: `_prev_inputs` has already been overwritten, so the same press cannot be seen again. A player mashing A through the fill animation gets one specific press silently eaten and has to press again.

This is the general shape of the problem — edges are consumed by whoever happens to poll, whether or not they act on them — and it is unavoidable while edge state lives inside the poller.

**Fix:** Latch edges in a frame-level input snapshot with an explicit `consume()`, so a PROCEED that arrives while the UI is not accepting input either survives to the next frame or is dropped deliberately, rather than by accident of where the poll call sits relative to the gate.

#### 4. Results screen positions the team-B percentage from a widget size it never sets

`ArtAttack/ResultsMenu.cpp:150-153` — **medium** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

this->_team_b_percentage->set_position(Vector2F(
        this->calculate_center_position(this->get_widget_size().x, DEFAULT_RESOLUTION.x) +
        TEAM_B_PERCENTAGE_X_OFFSET,
        this->calculate_team_b_fill_top_right_position().y));

`ResultsMenuInitial::init()` never calls `set_widget_size` / `set_widget_position` / `set_widget_spacing`, so `get_widget_size()` returns `MenuPage`'s unrelated hard-coded default `{ 300.0f, 75.0f }` (MenuPage.h:59). The x position of the team-B percentage text is therefore `(1920 - 300) / 2 + 325 = 1135` — a number that has nothing to do with this screen and that silently moves if anyone ever tunes the `MenuPage` default. The mirror image of the same smell is in `EndMenuInitial::init` (EndMenu.cpp:147), which *sets* `END_MENU_INITIAL_WIDGET_SIZE` and then never reads it.

`results_menu_consts` also carries five constants that are never referenced anywhere: `RESULTS_MENU_TEAM_FILL_Y_OFFSET` (ResultsMenu.h:25), `RESULTS_MENU_TITLE_Y_OFFSET` (32), `WINNER_TEXT_Y_OFFSET` (34), `TITLE_SHADOW_OFFSET`/`ITEM_SHADOW_OFFSET` (49, 51), `DIRECTION_SOUND`/`CANCEL_SOUND` (55, 57) — leftovers that make it impossible to tell which numbers actually drive the layout.

**Fix:** Either call `set_widget_size(...)` explicitly in `init()` with the value this screen intends, or drop the `get_widget_size()` dependency and write the intended x directly. Delete the unused constants. More broadly, `MenuPage`'s `_widget_position/_widget_size/_widget_spacing` are mutable per-page layout state on a shared base with defaults that no page actually wants — they belong in a small layout value type each page constructs.

#### 5. Score is share-of-painted, not map coverage: fill bar is always exactly full no matter how little of the level was painted

`ArtAttack/ResultsMenu.cpp:225-252` — **medium** · `design` · confidence: certain

`update_team_a_fill`/`update_team_b_fill` set widths to `RESULTS_MENU_TEAM_FILL_SIZE.x * team_a_ratio()` and `* team_b_ratio()` (lines 229 and 242). `team_a_ratio()` is `team_a_area / (team_a_area + team_b_area)` (ArtAttack/LevelEndInfo.cpp:18-33), so the two ratios always sum to 1 and the two bar widths always sum to `RESULTS_MENU_TEAM_FILL_SIZE.x` = 700 - 2*10 = 680 (ResultsMenu.h:17-23). Unpainted area is never computed anywhere - `Level::get_level_end_info` (Level.cpp:706-735) only accumulates painted tile area and never asks a structure for its total paintable area.
Worked example on close_quarters (55,800 units of generated tile area, post-face-bug): A paints `lower_paint`'s 750 top tiles (36,000) and B paints `upper_paint`'s 187 top tiles (9,000); 358 of 1,160 tiles are painted, 19% of the surface. The results screen shows "80.0%" / "20.0%" (LevelEndInfo.cpp:42-61 truncates `std::to_string` at one decimal, which is correct) and a completely full 680px bar - i.e. the identical display you get if the whole map is covered. For a Splatoon-like whose entire point is territory covered, the headline number is measuring the wrong thing.
Degenerate case: if nobody paints anything, `team_a_ratio`/`team_b_ratio` return the hardcoded 0.5 (lines 20-23, 28-31), so an empty map renders as a full bar split 50/50 with "50.0%" on both sides.

**Fix:** Have `IPaintableGameObject` also report total paintable area (it already knows - it is `sum(tile.get_area())` over all tiles regardless of team), aggregate it into `LevelEndInfo::total_area`, and express both percentages over that. The bar then reads as coverage with a genuine unpainted remainder, which is what the mechanic is.

#### 6. const member functions that mutate the objects they own, applied inconsistently

`ArtAttack/ResultsMenu.cpp:214-252` — **low** · `const-correctness`

`const` means nothing here because the mutation goes through an owned `unique_ptr`, so the compiler cannot object. `ResultsMenuInitial::update_fill_box() const`, `update_team_a_fill() const`, `update_team_b_fill() const` (ResultsMenu.h:105-107, .cpp:214-252) call `_team_a_fill->set_width(width)` and `_team_b_fill->set_position_from_top_right_origin(...)` — they are the animation tick, the most mutating thing on the page. `MainMenuOptions::update_full_screen_selection_text() const` (MainMenu.h:180, .cpp:609-622) calls `_full_screen_value->set_text(...)` while its sibling `update_resolution_selection_text()` (602-607) does the identical thing and is NOT const — the qualifier is not even applied consistently to the same operation. `MainMenuTeamSelect::set_level_settings() const` (1225-1235), `MainMenuWeaponSelect::set_level_settings() const` (1511-1518) and `MainMenuStageSelect::set_level_settings() const` (1847-1851) write the shared `MenuLevelSettings` the whole level build depends on. The const propagation is lost in the first place because every `get_*_data() const` returns a NON-const pointer (MainMenu.cpp:18-21, PauseMenu.cpp:35-38, EndMenu.cpp:16-19, ResultsMenu.cpp:18-21).

**Fix:** Drop `const` from anything that changes what the page displays or the settings it feeds forward — the qualifier is actively misleading. Where a genuinely read-only accessor is wanted, return `const T*`.

## `ArtAttack/sounds/sound_bank_1/cmd.txt`

_1 finding: 1 high_

#### 1. Three third-party tool EXEs and their cmd.txt notes are committed, while the audio assets they produce are gitignored — the app cannot run from a clone

`ArtAttack/sounds/sound_bank_1/cmd.txt:1-8` — **high** · `repo-hygiene` · confidence: certain

Committed binaries: `ArtAttack/textures/texconv.exe` (944 KB), `ArtAttack/fonts/MakeSpriteFont.exe` (41 KB), `ArtAttack/sounds/sound_bank_1/XWBTool.exe` (110 KB). Each sits beside a `cmd.txt` holding the single command line that was run by hand — e.g. `ArtAttack/textures/cmd.txt`: `texconv sprite_sheet_1.png -pmalpha -m 1 -f BC3_UNORM`; `ArtAttack/sounds/sound_bank_1/cmd.txt`: the 24-file `XWBTool -f -o sound_bank_1.xwb ...` invocation. That is an asset build pipeline stored as a note-to-self.

The consequence is worse than untidiness: `.gitignore:366-368` ignores `*.wav`, `*.xwb`, `*.mp3`, so `sounds/sound_bank_1/sound_bank_1.xwb` is not in the repo — and it is not in the working tree either (`sounds/sound_bank_1/` contains only XWBTool.exe and cmd.txt). `ResourceLoader.cpp:35` calls `load_sound_bank_from_directory(SOUNDS_DIRECTORY, "sound_bank_1")`, which builds `./sounds/sound_bank_1.xwb` at `:172` and loads it unconditionally during `load_all_resources()`. The tool to rebuild it is committed; the 24 `.wav` inputs are not. So a fresh clone cannot start, and neither can this working tree.

Also in the pile: `ArtAttack/sounds/sound list.txt`, a hand-maintained scratch list of which sounds are 'DONE' with entries like `Title\t?????` — and sure enough `MainMenu.h:78 TITLE_SOUND` is declared and never referenced.

**Fix:** Get the tools from a package (they ship with DirectXTK/DirectXTex) and turn the cmd.txt contents into an actual asset-build step (a script or a vcxproj custom build step), then delete the EXEs and cmd.txt files. Decide whether audio is source-controlled: either un-ignore the .wav/.xwb and commit them, or document how to obtain them. Right now the repo is not buildable-and-runnable by anyone, including its author.

## `ArtAttack/SpriteSheet.h`

_4 findings: 2 high, 1 medium, 1 low_

#### 1. SpriteSheet is three classes in one: atlas data, JSON loader, and sprite renderer

`ArtAttack/SpriteSheet.h:10-69` — **high** · `design`

The class simultaneously holds the data (`map<string, SpriteFrame>`, `map<string, unique_ptr<AnimationStrip>>`, `ID3D11ShaderResourceView*`), parses it (`load_from_json` plus the two static decoders at SpriteSheet.cpp:20-68, which is why `rapidjson/document.h` is in the header), and renders it (five `draw` overloads at :92-174 calling `SpriteBatch::Draw` directly).

That conflation is why the class cannot be `const`, cannot be unit-tested without D3D and a file on disk, and forces RapidJSON on every consumer. It also means the atlas owns the *policy* of how a sprite is drawn: those five overloads are the engine's entire public rendering vocabulary, each a positional list of 6-9 defaulted arguments that every caller re-specifies.

**Fix:** Three types. `SpriteSheet` = immutable atlas (texture handle + `vector<SpriteFrame>` + `vector<AnimationStrip>` + name→index tables, all const after load, safely shareable across render threads). A free `load_sprite_sheet(...)` in a .cpp = JSON → `SpriteSheet`, so the format is swappable and the header has no parser dependency. `SpriteRenderer` = the only thing that talks to `SpriteBatch`, taking `const SpriteSheet&` + a `SpriteDrawParams` struct.
