_2 findings: 2 medium_

#### 1. Drawer is a base class with a public non-virtual destructor whose entire helper API is dead code

`ArtAttack/Drawer.h:9-32` — **medium** · `design`

`Drawer` has no virtual functions and no user-declared destructor, so its implicit destructor is public and non-virtual — yet it is used purely as an implementation-inheritance base (`class DebugText : public Drawer`, `class InterfaceGameplay : public Drawer`). Currently latent because both are held as concrete `unique_ptr`s in `Level`, but `delete static_cast<Drawer*>(p)` is silent UB with no diagnostic, which is a landmine in a codebase meant to be subclassed by others.

Everything it contributes beyond two raw pointers is unused. Grep-verified: `set_resource_manager` and `set_dt` (Drawer.h:14-15) have no callers; both `calculate_draw_rectangle` overloads (Drawer.cpp:33-53) have no callers except each other; `calculate_sprite_origin` (Drawer.cpp:55-67) has no callers. `calculate_draw_rectangle` also reimplements the world-to-screen transform that `Camera::calculate_view_rectangle` already provides, and does it with a *different* camera representation (`Vector3F` packing x/y/zoom) from the `MattMath::Camera` every other renderer uses.

Meanwhile `Weapon::calculate_sprite_origin` (Weapon.cpp:88-101) is a functionally identical reimplementation in a class that does not derive from `Drawer`, called from Weapon.cpp:42, :73 and WeaponRoller.cpp. (Correcting the reviewers: it is not byte-for-byte — Weapon spells out `TOP_LEFT` and adds a `default:` — but it is the same function.) So the inheritance is not even succeeding at sharing the one thing it exists to share, because all three helpers are non-static, non-const members that touch no member state and therefore need an instance to call.

After removing the dead code, `Drawer` is a struct with two raw pointers.

**Fix:** Delete `calculate_draw_rectangle` (Camera owns that transform) and `set_resource_manager`/`set_dt`. Move `calculate_sprite_origin` to a free function in a small rendering-utility header and delete the `Weapon` copy. Then dissolve `Drawer` as a base class — pass a `DrawContext { const ResourceManager* resources; float dt; }` value to the two consumers. In the meantime add `protected: ~Drawer() = default;`.

#### 2. ~140 functions are declared and defined but never called; the largest clusters are Drawer, MovingObject, Colour and MattMath

`ArtAttack/Drawer.h:14-25` — **medium** · `dead-code` · confidence: certain

I extracted every identifier followed by `(` from ArtAttack/*.h and counted occurrences across all first-party .cpp/.h; ~140 names occur exactly twice (declaration + definition) and are therefore never called. Representative clusters:

- `Drawer.h:14-25`: `set_resource_manager`, `set_dt`, and **both** overloads of `calculate_draw_rectangle` (Drawer.cpp:33-53). The latter take `const Vector3F& camera` — a leftover x/y/zoom camera model replaced by `MattMath::Camera`; `Vector3F` now appears nowhere else in the codebase except these four signatures.
- `MovingObject.h:25-51`: `alter_velocity`, `alter_dx`, `alter_dx_x/y`, `alter_rotation`, `get_unit_velocity`, `get_velocity_magnitude`, `get_velocity_angle`, `get_unit_dx`, `get_dx_magnitude`, `get_dx_angle` — all `protected virtual`, none overridden, none called.
- `MattMath.h:616-641` (Colour): `get_red/green/blue/alpha`, `set_red/green/blue/alpha`, `saturate`, `desaturate`, `brighten`, `darken`, `invert`, `make_opaque`, `make_transparent`, `get_sm_colour`.
- One-offs: `GameData.h:46 get_game_data()` (returns `this`), `MenuData.h:14 get_menu_data()` (same), `ResourceLoader.h:19 load_texture_from_directory` (ResourceLoader.cpp:75-81 — its logic was inlined into `load_sprite_sheet_from_directory` at :131 instead), `ThreadPool.h:18 get_min_num_threads`, `Save.h:23 get_save_data`, `TeamColour.h:51 get_team_colours`, `MenuLevelSettings.h:18 get_game_mode`, `ResultsMenuData.h:15 set_level_end_info`, `Mh.h:39-41 remove_all_children/get_child_count/get_children`, `ViewportManager.h:26 get_layout`, `ViewportManager.h:43 get_fullscreen_d3d11_viewport`, `MattMath.h:790 get_d3d_viewport_ptr`.
- Two are dead stubs: `Level.h:152 draw_end_screen` (Level.cpp:696-699, body is `// TODO`) and `DrawObject.h:33 set_draw_rotation_by_rectangle_rotated` (DrawObject.cpp:66-69, body is `// TODO: Implement this function`).

**Fix:** Delete them. The systemic cause is a reflex of writing a get/set pair for every field before there is a caller (182 setters / 344 const getters across the headers) — for a reusable engine the public surface should be driven by what callers actually need, and `protected virtual` one-liners that nothing overrides are pure vtable cost.

## `ArtAttack/DrawObject.cpp`

_1 finding: 1 medium_

#### 1. set_draw_rotation_by_rectangle_rotated is an empty stub and Visual's RectangleRotated constructor silently discards the rotation

`ArtAttack/DrawObject.cpp:66-69` — **medium** · `correctness`

```cpp
void DrawObject::set_draw_rotation_by_rectangle_rotated(const RectangleRotated& rect)
{
	// TODO: Implement this function
}
```
A public API on the root of the render hierarchy with an empty body and (grep-confirmed) zero callers. The unnamed-but-declared parameter is unused, and `TreatWarningAsError` is off so nothing surfaces it.

Its intended consumer is `Visual`'s second constructor (Visual.cpp:22-35):
```cpp
this->_rectangle = rect_rotated.get_rectangle_rotated_to_axis();
```
`get_rectangle_rotated_to_axis()` (MattMath.cpp:4456) returns the OBB's extents re-expressed as an axis-aligned box; the orientation is dropped on the floor even though `RectangleRotated::get_angle()` sits four lines below it at MattMath.cpp:4460. The constructor never calls `set_draw_rotation`, so a `Visual` built from a rotated rect renders axis-aligned — a silently wrong picture. The origin is also never set to the rect centre, so even once rotation is applied it would spin about the top-left corner.

Currently latent: `LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:188` and :236 both use the `RectangleF` overload. But `RectangleRotated` was added specifically for the paintable-ramp work in the recent commits, so this constructor is on the critical path for the next feature.

**Fix:** Implement it — `_draw_rotation = rect.get_angle();` — and call it from the `Visual` constructor along with `set_origin(_rectangle.get_size() / 2.0f)`. If you are not implementing it now, delete both the stub and the `Visual` overload so callers get a compile error rather than a silently wrong image.

## `ArtAttack/EndMenu.cpp`

_1 finding: 1 medium_

#### 1. EndMenuInitial::update reads the highlight once outside the loop, plays the move sound before deciding, and has no back/ownership handling

`ArtAttack/EndMenu.cpp:26-131` — **medium** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

void EndMenuInitial::update()
    {
        std::vector<ProcessedMenuInput> inputs = this->get_menu_inputs();
        std::string highlighted_element = this->get_highlighted_widget()->get_name();

        for (int i = 0; i < inputs.size(); i++)      // C4018 signed/unsigned, /W4, not error-enforced
        {
            ...
            else if (inputs[i].direction == menu_direction::UP)
            {
                this->play_wave(DIRECTION_SOUND);   // fires before any branch is known to match

Four concrete problems:
1. `highlighted_element` is captured *before* the loop and never refreshed, so if two pads produce input on the same frame the second is evaluated against a stale highlight. In practice every branch `return`s, which makes the loop equivalent to "take the first input" — but that is accidental, not stated.
2. `play_wave(DIRECTION_SOUND)` at lines 74 and 103 runs unconditionally at the top of the UP/DOWN branch. If the highlighted name matches none of the five literals (a typo, or a widget added without updating the ladder), the click plays and nothing moves — the failure is silent.
3. `menu_input_action::BACK` is never handled. The pause menu treats BACK as "resume" (PauseMenu.cpp:53-58); the end menu just ignores B, so a player pressing B on the results/end screen gets no response at all.
4. Unlike `PauseMenuData`, which carries `_player_num` (PauseMenuData.h:18), `EndMenuData` has no notion of who owns the menu. Any connected pad — including one belonging to nobody, since `MenuInput` reports all four slots (MenuInput.cpp:139-148) — can select "Exit to Main Menu" and destroy everyone's match.

Separately, `set_widget_size(END_MENU_INITIAL_WIDGET_SIZE)` at line 147 is dead: `get_widget_size()` is never read in this class.

**Fix:** Re-read the highlight inside the loop (or better, index-based selection as suggested for MenuHighlight); move `play_wave(DIRECTION_SOUND)` into `change_highlight` so it only fires when the highlight actually changes; add a BACK case; and decide explicitly whether the end menu is owned by one player (store the index like `PauseMenuData` does) or open to all, rather than leaving it as an accident of the loop. Use `size_t`/range-for for the loop to clear the C4018.

## `ArtAttack/EricsonMath.h`

_5 findings: 3 medium, 2 low_

#### 1. Circular dependency between the geometry-types module and the intersection-algorithm module

`ArtAttack/EricsonMath.h:8` — **medium** · `design`

EricsonMath.h includes MattMath.h (line 8) because every signature takes MattMath types; MattMath.cpp includes EricsonMath.h and implements much of its intersection surface by forwarding down to it — verified at MattMath.cpp:179 (test_AABB_AABB), 185/190 (test_circle_AABB), 249 (test_segment_AABB), 308/315 (test_circle_triangle), 336 (closest_pt_point_segment), 449 (test_point_triangle), 572 (test_2D_segment_segment).

Neither module can be extracted or reused without the other — a direct blocker on the reusable-engine goal. It is compounded by MattMath.cpp being a single ~4500-line translation unit holding the value types, the `Shape` polymorphic dispatch (with its dynamic_cast switch at 119-136), and the free-function intersection table.

**Fix:** Three strictly-upward layers: math/types (Vector2F, RectangleF, Circle, Triangle, Quad, Segment, RectangleRotated — no knowledge of intersection), math/intersect (free functions over those types; the EricsonMath content, renamed for what it does), collision/ (Shape polymorphism, contacts, solver). Only then can the math be lifted out of this project.

#### 2. Two EPSILON constants 100x apart and a duplicated dead clamp, both visible in the same translation units

`ArtAttack/EricsonMath.h:75, 88` — **medium** · `design`

`EricsonMath::EPSILON = 0.000001f` (EricsonMath.h:75) coexists with `MattMath::EPSILON = 0.0001f` (MattMath.h:46), and EricsonMath.h includes MattMath.h. EricsonMath.cpp has file-scope `using namespace MattMath;` and `using namespace EricsonMath;`. The unqualified `EPSILON` at EricsonMath.cpp:665-666 resolves to the 1e-6 value today only because functions defined with a qualified-id search their own namespace first; move that code into a `namespace EricsonMath { }` block and it silently binds the 100x-larger value with no diagnostic. `MattMath::are_equal(a, b, epsilon = EPSILON)` bakes the loose value in as a default, so the two tolerances are already applied inconsistently across the collision code.

EricsonMath::EPSILON is used at exactly one site (test_segment_AABB); every other predicate in the file is exact float comparison under /fp:fast — e.g. `test_2D_segment_segment` uses strict `a1 * a2 < 0.0f` / `a3 * a4 < 0.0f` (705, 712), so segments that touch exactly at an endpoint or are collinear report no intersection.

`EricsonMath::clamp` (EricsonMath.h:88, cpp:354-365) duplicates `MattMath::clamp` (MattMath.h:51) and is dead: grep finds no callers anywhere including the tests, while `closest_pt_point_AABB` (428-448) and `closest_pt_point_OBB` (781-782) each hand-inline the same three lines instead.

REJECTED sub-claim: one reviewer stated MattMathTests/MathTests.cpp would be a hard ambiguity error because it does `using namespace MattMath; using namespace EricsonMath;`. It defines its own EPSILON_F constants (MathTests.cpp:14-16) and never names EPSILON or clamp unqualified, so nothing is ambiguous today.

**Fix:** Delete EricsonMath::clamp and EricsonMath::EPSILON. Keep one tolerance, expressed per-operation and named for its purpose and its world-space units. Route the sign tests in test_2D_segment_segment through it rather than comparing to exact zero.

#### 3. Half the EricsonMath API returns results through out-parameters, several unwritten on the failure path

`ArtAttack/EricsonMath.h:93-142` — **medium** · `design`

Seven of fifteen public functions use non-const reference out-params: test_circle_AABB(…, Point2F& p), closest_pt_point_AABB(…, Point2F& q), test_circle_triangle(…, Point2F& p), intersect_moving_AABB_AABB(…, float& tfirst, float& tlast), test_2D_segment_segment(…, float& t, Point2F& p), barycentric(…, float& u, float& v, float& w), closest_pt_point_segment(…, float& t, Point2F& d).

The file is inconsistent with itself: closest_pt_point_triangle (83-86) returns Point2F by value while closest_pt_point_AABB (99-100) writes into `q`. Point2F is two floats, so there is no efficiency argument.

Worse, the bool+out-param ones do not write on failure. test_2D_segment_segment's comment promises "compute and return intersection t value along ab and intersection position p", but the `return 0` at line 724 leaves both untouched. MattMath.cpp:576-581 already relies on that: `float t; Point2F p; return segments_intersect(a, b, t, p);` — `t` is uninitialised and survives only because the result is discarded. Any future caller of the four-arg form that reads `t` after a false return reads garbage.

**Fix:** Return values: `Point2F closest_pt_point_AABB(...)`, `struct Barycentric { float u, v, w; }`, `struct SegmentHit { float t; Point2F point; }` returned as std::optional. At minimum, write the out-params on all paths so a stale read is impossible.

#### 4. Pure math free functions lack [[nodiscard]], and the header includes <cmath> it does not need

`ArtAttack/EricsonMath.h:9, 77-142` — **low** · `modern-cpp`

Every function in the header is a pure value computation over trivially-copyable structs, yet none is [[nodiscard]] — discarding the result of `test_AABB_AABB` is always a bug and should not compile. Nothing prevents adding it today.

Header hygiene: line 9 `#include <cmath>` — no declaration in the header needs it; the std::abs/std::max/std::min uses are all in the .cpp (579, 583, 656-659), which currently relies on pch.h for them. That dependency is fragile because MattMathTests compiles EricsonMath.cpp directly against its own pch.h. The header also pulls in all of MattMath.h when forward declarations would suffice for a file that only declares functions.

constexpr/noexcept are blocked today by Vector2F's non-constexpr operators (MattMath.h:500-506) and are a follow-up, not an immediate change.

**Fix:** Add [[nodiscard]] to the fourteen non-void functions. Move <cmath> into the .cpp and add the direct includes it needs. Revisit constexpr once MattMath's operators are.

#### 5. test_segment_AABB takes p1 by value while p0 is by const reference

`ArtAttack/EricsonMath.h:119-120` — **low** · `modern-cpp`

```cpp
bool test_segment_AABB(const MattMath::Point2F& p0,
	const MattMath::Point2F p1, const MattMath::AABB& b);
```
Matched by the definition at EricsonMath.cpp:644-645. It is the only by-value parameter in the entire header, so it is plainly a dropped `&` rather than a decision. The top-level `const` on a by-value parameter is also meaningless in the declaration. The one live caller, MattMath.cpp:249, passes `segment.point_1` — a member, so the copy is pure waste.

**Fix:** `const MattMath::Point2F& p1` in both the header and the .cpp.

## `ArtAttack/GameData.cpp`

_3 findings: 1 medium, 2 low_

#### 1. Menu data classes inherit a hand-copied pointer bag; adding one service silently nulls it in every menu

`ArtAttack/GameData.cpp:4-20` — **medium** · `design` · confidence: certain

GameData::GameData(const GameData* game_data) :
        _save(game_data->get_save()),
        _resolution_manager(game_data->get_resolution_manager()),
        ... 13 members copied by hand ...

This reimplements the compiler-generated copy constructor, and takes a *pointer* rather than a reference so it can never be `= default`. `MenuData : public GameData` (MenuData.h:7) then snapshots the whole bag by value, and `EndMenuData`, `ResultsMenuData`, `PauseMenuData` and `MainMenuData` all inherit that. Consequences:

* Adding a 14th service to `GameData` and forgetting to extend this list leaves it `nullptr` in every single menu screen, with no compiler diagnostic. `Save::_dt`-style aliasing bugs are invisible.
* Nothing IS-A `GameData`. `EndMenuData` inheriting a service-locator so it can reach `get_resource_manager()` is inheritance used for `using`-namespace convenience. `MenuData::get_menu_data() { return this; }` (MenuData.cpp:26-29) and `GameData::get_game_data() { return this; }` are pure no-ops that exist only to paper over the confusion.
* Every `EndMenuData`/`ResultsMenuData` is a 13-pointer copy created per menu screen (GameStates.cpp:172, 228) — a snapshot that will silently go stale if anything ever calls a `GameData` setter after construction, which `Game::initialize` does (Game.cpp:36, 60, 253).

For a project whose stated goal is a reusable engine, this is the single biggest coupling problem in the menu layer: no menu screen can be reused or tested without dragging in `DeviceResources`, `ThreadPool`, `Partitioner` and `Save`.

**Fix:** Delete `GameData(const GameData*)` and let the implicit copy constructor do it (take `const GameData&` if a converting constructor is genuinely wanted). Change `MenuData` to *hold* a `const GameData*` instead of inheriting it, and delete `get_menu_data()`/`get_game_data()`. Then narrow what each screen actually needs — `EndMenuInitial` uses only `ResourceManager*`, `ResolutionManager*`, `MenuInput*`, `CommonStates*` and the sprite-batch/deferred-context set; that is the real interface.

#### 2. get_thread_pool contains a duplicated, unreachable return

`ArtAttack/GameData.cpp:142-146` — **low** · `correctness`

Merged from 4 candidates — every reviewer found it.

    ThreadPool* GameData::get_thread_pool() const
    {
        return this->_thread_pool;
        return this->_thread_pool;
    }

A copy-paste artefact. Harmless at runtime, but it is dead code that C4702 would flag in optimised builds at the /W4 the project already sets — direct evidence that the warning output is never read (no TreatWarningAsError anywhere in the project).

Context: GameData.cpp is 156 lines of 26 hand-written one-line accessors over a 13-member pointer bag — exactly the shape where a slip like this hides. Two more pieces of dead weight in the same file: `GameData::get_game_data()` (122-125) returns `this` and has zero callers (grepped), as does `MenuData::get_menu_data()` (MenuData.cpp:26).

**Fix:** Delete line 145 and both `get_*_data()` self-returning accessors. Since the class has no invariants at all — 13 raw pointers, 26 trivial accessors, no validation — consider making it a `struct` of public members and deleting GameData.cpp entirely.

#### 3. Unreachable duplicated return statement — proof that /W4 warnings are being ignored

`ArtAttack/GameData.cpp:142-145` — **low** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

```cpp
ThreadPool* GameData::get_thread_pool() const
{
    return this->_thread_pool;
    return this->_thread_pool;
}
```

The second statement is unreachable (MSVC C4702 at /W4). Both projects compile at /W4 (ArtAttack) / /W3 (MattMathTests) but **neither sets `TreatWarningAsError`**, so warnings like this — and the signed/unsigned comparisons at DeviceResources.cpp:740, Level.cpp:386, MenuPage.cpp:140, and the unused `num_threads` at Level.cpp:599 (C4189) — accumulate silently. For a sweep like this the interesting fact is not the duplicated line, it is that a warning this loud has survived in a hot accessor.

**Fix:** Delete the duplicate line, then turn on `<TreatWarningAsError>true</TreatWarningAsError>` for both projects and fix the backlog. Move the four near-identical `ItemDefinitionGroup` blocks in ArtAttack.vcxproj into a shared `.props` sheet so warning settings cannot drift between configurations.

## `ArtAttack/levels/king_of_the_hill.json`

_1 finding: 1 medium_

#### 1. The 4th team-A spawn point is embedded inside the spawn-room jump-through ceiling in all three shipped levels

`ArtAttack/levels/king_of_the_hill.json:25-28` — **medium** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

`spawn_locations.team_a` entries 0-2 are at y = 4870.0, but entry 3 is:

    { "x": 196.0, "y": 4800.0 }

`PlayerBuilder.cpp:38` builds the player as `RectangleF(position, DEFAULT_SIZE)` where `player_consts::DEFAULT_SIZE = {52, 120}` (ArtAttack/player_consts.h:21) and position is the top-left — so that player occupies y ∈ [4800, 4920], x ∈ [196, 248].

The same level declares `spawn_a_ceiling` (king_of_the_hill.json:163-177) as a `STRUCTURE_JUMP_THROUGH` at x 0-300, y 4855-4865. The 4th team-A spawn point therefore starts the player straddling that one-way platform, whereas the y=4870 spawns start cleanly below it (4870 > 4865). Because `Player::on_structure_jump_through_collision` requires `_prev_rectangle.get_bottom() <= other_rect.get_top()` to resolve, a player spawned already overlapping never gets pushed out and simply falls through — inconsistent with players 1-3.

The identical spawn arrays (including the 4800 outlier) are copy-pasted verbatim into ArtAttack/levels/close_quarters.json:9-49 and ArtAttack/levels/turbulence.json:9-49, and into all four ArtAttack/levels/unused/*.json. It reads as a typo for 4870 that was then propagated by copy-paste.

**Fix:** Change y to 4870.0 in team_a entry 3 of all three shipped levels. Separately, add a load-time validation pass that asserts no spawn rectangle intersects a collision object — this class of authoring error is otherwise invisible until playtest.

## `ArtAttack/MainMenu.h`

_5 findings: 3 medium, 2 low_

#### 1. No UI theme abstraction: four const namespaces redefine the same fonts, colours, shadows and sounds, with drift

`ArtAttack/MainMenu.h:14-90` — **medium** · `design`

`main_menu_consts` (MainMenu.h:14-90), `pause_menu_consts` (PauseMenu.h:11-42), `end_menu_consts` (EndMenu.h:11-40) and `results_menu_consts` (ResultsMenu.h:9-62) independently redefine the same values: `DEFAULT_RESOLUTION = {1920,1080}` x4, `ITEM_FONT = "gill_sans_mt_bold_48"` x4, `HEADING_FONT = "gill_sans_mt_bold_72"` x4, `DETAIL_FONT` x3, `SHADOW_COLOUR` + the four shadow offsets x4, `STANDARD_HIGHLIGHT`/`STANDARD_UNHIGHLIGHT` x3, and `SOUND_BANK`/`DIRECTION_SOUND`/`CONFIRM_SOUND`/`CANCEL_SOUND` x4. The drift is already visible: the heading colour is `TEAM_ORANGE` in Pause/End but `GOLDENROD` in Results. Because these are namespace-scope `const`/`const static` objects they have internal linkage, so every TU that includes the header gets its own copy WITH A DYNAMIC INITIALIZER — `MattMath::Colour` is built from a hex string and every `std::string` constant heap-allocates at static-init time. Several are dead: `pause_menu_consts::TITLE_SHADOW_OFFSET`, `end_menu_consts::TITLE_SHADOW_OFFSET`, `end_menu_consts::DETAIL_SHADOW_OFFSET`, `results_menu_consts::TITLE_SHADOW_OFFSET`, `results_menu_consts::ITEM_SHADOW_OFFSET`, `results_menu_consts::DIRECTION_SOUND`, `results_menu_consts::CANCEL_SOUND`. Spelling is inconsistent even within one block (`const static std::string TITLE_FONT` vs `const std::string SOUND_BANK`). (The original report also listed `end_menu_consts::DETAIL_FONT` — that constant does not exist.)

**Fix:** Collapse into one `struct MenuTheme { FontSet fonts; ColourSet colours; ShadowSet shadows; SoundSet sounds; Vector2F design_resolution; }` reachable from `MenuPage`. Set `<LanguageStandard>stdcpp20</LanguageStandard>` in ArtAttack.vcxproj — it is currently unset, so the project defaults to an old standard — then these become `inline constexpr` with zero startup cost and one definition. Delete the seven unused constants.

#### 2. Four menu *_consts namespaces redefine the same fonts, shadow offsets, colours and sound names

`ArtAttack/MainMenu.h:14-90` — **medium** · `design` · confidence: certain

`main_menu_consts` (MainMenu.h:14-90), `pause_menu_consts` (PauseMenu.h:11-42), `results_menu_consts` (ResultsMenu.h:9-62) and `end_menu_consts` (EndMenu.h:11-40) each independently declare the identical set:

- `DEFAULT_RESOLUTION = {1920,1080}` (MainMenu.h:16, PauseMenu.h:13, ResultsMenu.h:11, EndMenu.h:13)
- `ITEM_FONT = "gill_sans_mt_bold_48"`, `HEADING_FONT = "gill_sans_mt_bold_72"`, `DETAIL_FONT = "gill_sans_mt_bold_36"` (×4)
- `SHADOW_COLOUR`, `TITLE_SHADOW_OFFSET {6,6}`, `HEADING_SHADOW_OFFSET {2.5,2.5}`, `ITEM_SHADOW_OFFSET {1.5,1.5}`, `DETAIL_SHADOW_OFFSET {1,1}` (×4 — a 5-line block repeated verbatim)
- `SOUND_BANK = "sound_bank_1"`, `DIRECTION_SOUND = "UI_Clicks14"`, `CONFIRM_SOUND = "UI_Clicks01"`, `CANCEL_SOUND = "UI_Clicks17"` (×4)
- `STANDARD_HIGHLIGHT = WHITE`, `STANDARD_UNHIGHLIGHT = BLUE` (MainMenu.h:31-32, PauseMenu.h:20-21, EndMenu.h:24-25)

~60 duplicated declarations. Worse, they are namespace-scope `const std::string` / `const Colour` objects in headers, so each of the ~30 TUs that include them gets its own copy with dynamic initialisation at startup.

**Fix:** Create one `ui_theme.h` holding the shared font names, shadow offsets, palette and UI sound names, and leave only the genuinely page-specific values (`MODE_SELECT_WIDGET_SPACING`, `RESULTS_MENU_FILL_BOX_SIZE`, weapon descriptions, …) in the per-menu namespaces. Declare the strings `inline constexpr std::string_view` (or `constexpr const char*`) so there is one object, not one per TU.

#### 3. Four parallel *MenuPage bases exist solely to shadow MenuPage::_data with a duplicate typed pointer

`ArtAttack/MainMenu.h:110-123` — **medium** · `design`

`MainMenuPage` stores `MainMenuData* _data` (MainMenu.h:122) even though `MenuPage` already stores the same object as `MenuData* _data` (MenuPage.h:57) — two members pointing at one object, kept in sync only by the constructor passing `data` twice (`MenuPage(data), ..., _data(data)`, MainMenu.cpp:9-14). The identical pattern is copied in `PauseMenuPage` (PauseMenu.h:61 + PauseMenu.cpp:9-16), `EndMenuPage` (EndMenu.h:53 + EndMenu.cpp:8-14) and `ResultsMenuPage` (ResultsMenu.h:75 + ResultsMenu.cpp:9-16), each with its own `get_X_menu_data()` accessor whose whole job is to return the duplicate. Four near-identical class bodies exist to re-type one pointer.

**Fix:** Make the base generic over its data type — `template <class TData> class MenuPageT : public MenuPage { protected: TData* data() const { return static_cast<TData*>(MenuPage::get_data()); } };` — or drop the typed base and have pages call a checked `get_data<MainMenuData>()`. All four intermediate classes and the duplicated members go away.

#### 4. MContainer stores raw non-owning child pointers, and every page declares containers before the widgets they point at

`ArtAttack/MainMenu.h:133-137` — **low** · `lifetime`

`MContainer::add_child(MObject* child)` (Mh.h:36, Mh.cpp:40) stores raw, non-owning pointers into `std::vector<std::pair<std::string, MObject*>> _children`, undocumented. The children are `unique_ptr` members of the page, and every page declares the containers FIRST, so reverse-order destruction destroys all the widgets before the containers holding pointers to them: MainMenu.h:133-137, 149-155, 166-175, 192-200, 212-220, 245-251, 280-285, 310-316; PauseMenu.h:73-79, 90-97; EndMenu.h:64-72; ResultsMenu.h:86-96. Benign only because `~MContainer` is implicit and a vector of raw pointers touches nothing — but `MContainer` already declares `remove_child`/`remove_all_children` (Mh.h:37-39), so one teardown call in a destructor makes every page a use-after-free. Related and load-bearing but unstated: `MainMenuTeamSelect::init()` (1345-1400) and `MainMenuWeaponSelect::init()` (1671-1728) hand raw pointers to `widgets->player_a` etc. to the containers WHILE `_player_widgets` is still being `push_back`-ed. This survives only because `_player_widgets` is `vector<unique_ptr<PlayerWidgets>>` (MainMenu.h:250, 284) — the extra indirection means reallocation moves the `unique_ptr`s, not the widgets. Change it to `vector<PlayerWidgets>`, the obvious 'simplification', and every registered child pointer dangles on the next `push_back`.

**Fix:** Make ownership explicit: have `MContainer` own its children (`vector<unique_ptr<MObject>>`) with pages keeping observing raw pointers, or at minimum rename to `add_observer`/document non-ownership and declare the containers LAST so destruction order matches the pointer graph. Comment `_player_widgets` explaining that the unique_ptr indirection is required for pointer stability.

#### 5. Three duplicate two-argument constructors whose extra parameter re-does what the caller already did

`ArtAttack/MainMenu.h:227-228, 262-263, 299-300` — **low** · `api-design`

`MainMenuTeamSelect`, `MainMenuWeaponSelect` and `MainMenuStageSelect` each declare a second constructor taking `MenuLevelSettings*`. All three bodies are one line — `this->get_main_menu_data()->set_level_settings(settings);` (MainMenu.cpp:1137-1142, 1420-1425, 1767-1772). But the only caller, `GameMenu::init`, has already stored that exact pointer into the same `MainMenuData` before transitioning: `set_main_menu_data_ptrs()` runs at GameStates.cpp:23 and does `_menu_data->set_level_settings(_menu_level_settings.get())` (GameStates.cpp:65), and then GameStates.cpp:51/55/59 pass `this->_menu_level_settings.get()` — the identical pointer — to the two-argument overload. The overloads are pure noise, and two constructors that differ only in whether they re-assign shared state invite the paths to drift.

**Fix:** Delete the two-argument overloads and use the single-argument form at GameStates.cpp:50-60; the level settings pointer is already installed on the shared `MainMenuData`.

## `ArtAttack/MenuHighlight.cpp`

_1 finding: 1 medium_

#### 1. MenuHighlight null-guards the two methods that cannot crash and leaves the one that can unguarded

`ArtAttack/MenuHighlight.cpp:6-27` — **medium** · `robustness` · confidence: certain

void MenuHighlight::highlight_widget(MWidget* widget) const
    { if (widget == nullptr) return; widget->set_colour(this->_highlight_colour); }
    void MenuHighlight::unhighlight_widget(MWidget* widget) const
    { if (widget == nullptr) return; widget->set_colour(this->_unhighlight_colour); }
    MWidget* MenuHighlight::get_highlighted_widget() const
    { return this->_highlighted_widget; }        // no guard, and every caller dereferences it

`_highlighted_widget` defaults to `nullptr` (MenuHighlight.h:27) and is only assigned in each page's `init()`. Every consumer immediately dereferences the raw result with no check:

    // EndMenu.cpp:29-30, identical shape at PauseMenu.cpp:50-51 and 219-220, MainMenu.cpp:884-885 and ~7 more
    std::string highlighted_element = this->get_highlighted_widget()->get_name();

Any page that forgets `set_highlighted_widget` in `init()`, or that is updated before `init()` runs, null-derefs on the first frame. The defensive checks were added to the two functions where a null is harmless and omitted from the one where it is fatal.

Secondary: `_highlighted_widget` is a raw pointer into `unique_ptr`-owned widgets declared in the *derived* class (e.g. `EndMenuInitial::_change_teams`, EndMenu.h:68, set at EndMenu.cpp:210). Base subobjects are destroyed after derived members, so `MenuHighlight::_highlighted_widget` dangles for the whole of `~MenuHighlight`. Nothing dereferences it today, but the ownership direction is inverted.

Also note the identity model: `change_highlight` and every `update()` compare `widget->get_name()` against string literals (`"change_teams"`, `"restart"`, `"exit"` — EndMenu.cpp:36-127, 51 similar compares in MainMenu.cpp:149-201). A typo in a name literal is a silent dead menu item, not a compile error.

**Fix:** Return early on a null highlight in each `update()`, or make `get_highlighted_widget()` return a reference and assert in `set_highlighted_widget`. Replace the string-name dispatch with a small `std::vector<MWidget*>` of menu entries plus an `size_t _index`, so up/down is `(_index + n - 1) % n` / `(_index + 1) % n` — that single change deletes the 100-line if/else ladders in `EndMenuInitial::update` (EndMenu.cpp:32-130) and `PauseMenuInitial::update` and makes the wrap-around impossible to get wrong.

## `ArtAttack/MenuHighlight.h`

_3 findings: 1 medium, 2 low_

#### 1. MenuHighlight is inherited at three different levels, and per-player selection is re-implemented from scratch twice

`ArtAttack/MenuHighlight.h:8-30` — **medium** · `design`

`MenuHighlight` is inherited by individual pages in MainMenu (`MainMenuHome`, `MainMenuOptions`, `MainMenuModeSelect`, `MainMenuPlayerCount` — MainMenu.h:141, 158, 184, 204), by the SHARED BASE in PauseMenu and EndMenu (`class PauseMenuPage : public MenuPage, public MenuHighlight, public SoundBankObject`, PauseMenu.h:44; EndMenu.h:42), and not at all by `ResultsMenuPage` or by `MainMenuTeamSelect`/`WeaponSelect`/`StageSelect` (MainMenu.h:224, 259, 296). The three that opted out hand-roll multi-player selection instead: `MainMenuTeamSelect` has `TeamSelectState` + `_select_states` + `update_team_select_visuals`/`deselect_and_unconfirm_all_widgets`/`all_players_confirmed`/`all_players_unconfirmed` (MainMenu.cpp:1236-1309), and `MainMenuWeaponSelect` has a near-identical `SelectState` + `unconfirm_all_widgets`/`all_players_confirmed`/`all_players_unconfirmed` (1555-1636). `all_players_confirmed()` and `all_players_unconfirmed()` are literally the same ten lines duplicated in both classes.

**Fix:** Replace the mixin with composition: `std::vector<FocusGroup> _focus` held by `MenuPage`, one group per player slot. Single-cursor pages use `_focus[0]`; per-player pages use one each, and 'all confirmed / all unconfirmed' becomes one method on the collection. That deletes both duplicated pairs and unifies the two visual-refresh routines.

#### 2. MenuHighlight and SoundBankObject are public mixin bases with public non-virtual destructors

`ArtAttack/MenuHighlight.h:8-30` — **low** · `design`

`MenuHighlight` (MenuHighlight.h:8-30) declares no destructor at all, and `SoundBankObject` (SoundBankObject.h:7-36) likewise — both get an implicit PUBLIC NON-VIRTUAL destructor. Both expose nothing but a constructor and protected members, i.e. they are implementation mixins, yet every page inherits them PUBLICLY: `class MainMenuPage : public MenuPage, public SoundBankObject` (MainMenu.h:110), `class MainMenuHome final : public MainMenuPage, public MenuHighlight` (141, and the same at 158, 184, 204), `class PauseMenuPage : public MenuPage, public MenuHighlight, public SoundBankObject` (PauseMenu.h:44), EndMenu.h:42, ResultsMenu.h:64. Destruction through `unique_ptr<State>` is safe because `State` declares `virtual ~State()` (State.h:8), but `delete static_cast<SoundBankObject*>(page)` is UB the public interface permits, and the implicit `MainMenuHome* -> MenuHighlight*` conversion is available to any caller for no benefit. Related: `MenuHighlight::_highlighted_widget` (MenuHighlight.h:27) is a raw pointer into a `unique_ptr` member of the DERIVED page (`set_highlighted_widget(this->_play.get())`, MainMenu.cpp:274), so as a base it is destroyed after the members it points into — dangling for the duration of `~MenuHighlight`, harmless only because that destructor is trivial today.

**Fix:** Make both mixins private bases and give them `protected: ~MenuHighlight() = default;` — deletion through the mixin becomes a compile error while derived use stays legal. Document `_highlighted_widget` as non-owning.

#### 3. MenuHighlight base holds a raw MWidget* into a unique_ptr owned by the derived class

`ArtAttack/MenuHighlight.h:26-29` — **low** · `lifetime`

```cpp
private:
	MWidget* _highlighted_widget = nullptr;
```
MenuHighlight is always used as a *base* (EndMenuPage, the MainMenu page classes, PauseMenu), and the pointer is always set to the address of an object owned by a unique_ptr **member of the derived class** — e.g. `set_highlighted_widget(this->_change_teams.get())` where _change_teams is EndMenu.h:68. C++ destroys derived members before base subobjects, so the pointer is dangling for the whole of ~MenuHighlight, by construction, in every page.

Severity lowered from the reviewers' "high": MenuHighlight has no destructor body and nothing dereferences the pointer during teardown, so there is no live use-after-free. It is a structural hazard — one added log line or assert away from one — not a current defect. There is also no null guard before `get_highlighted_widget()->get_name()` in the update paths.

Note this file is outside the math-collision module group; it surfaced because it consumes Mh.h.

**Fix:** Store the highlighted widget's name (or an index into an ordered navigable list) and resolve against the container — the navigation code already compares get_name() string literals anyway. Or make MContainer own the widgets and hold MenuHighlight as a member declared after the container rather than as a base.

## `ArtAttack/MenuInput.h`

_1 finding: 1 medium_

#### 1. Analog menu edge detection has zero hysteresis — the two thresholds are set to the same value

`ArtAttack/MenuInput.h:11-12` — **medium** · `correctness`

```cpp
namespace menu_input_consts {
    constexpr float DIGITAL_PRESENCE_THRESHOLD = 0.8f;
    constexpr float DIGITAL_ABSENCE_THRESHOLD  = 0.8f;
}
```
The two names exist precisely so the 'pressed' threshold can differ from the 'released' threshold. Set equal, `MenuInput.cpp:72-87` degenerates to a bare sign test around 0.8: `analog_down = previous.y > 0.8f && current.y < 0.8f`. Any stick resting near 0.8 — common when partially deflected or held on a diagonal — crosses the boundary on frame noise and emits a menu-move event, complete with a `play_wave(DIRECTION_SOUND)` each time. Aggravated by `MenuInput.cpp:19`, which reads the pad with `GamePad::DEAD_ZONE_NONE`, so the raw uncleaned axis value is compared; `PlayerInput::get_raw_input` uses `DEAD_ZONE_CIRCULAR` for the same sticks (PlayerInput.cpp:20), so the two input paths disagree about what a stick reading means.

**Fix:** Set `DIGITAL_ABSENCE_THRESHOLD` meaningfully below `DIGITAL_PRESENCE_THRESHOLD` (e.g. 0.8 / 0.4) so the detector is a real Schmitt trigger, use `DEAD_ZONE_CIRCULAR` as `PlayerInput` does, and add a repeat delay so a held direction scrolls at a fixed rate.

## `ArtAttack/MenuLevelSettings.cpp`

_2 findings: 2 medium_

#### 1. MenuLevelSettings keeps _player_count and _player_settings.size() as two independent facts and indexes with unchecked operator[]

`ArtAttack/MenuLevelSettings.cpp:9-25, 62-84` — **medium** · `robustness`

All six per-player accessors (`set_player_setting`, `set_player_team`, `get_player_team`, `set_player_weapon`, `get_player_weapon`, `set_player_num`, lines 62-84) use unchecked `operator[]`. The vector is sized only by `set_player_count` (9-25), and `_player_count` (MenuLevelSettings.h:34) is stored SEPARATELY from `_player_settings.size()`; the invariant that they agree is established in one function and asserted nowhere. Callers drive their loops from `get_player_count()` while indexing containers sized in a different call on a different frame: `MainMenuTeamSelect::set_level_settings` (MainMenu.cpp:1227-1234), `MainMenuTeamSelect::init` (1345-1351), `MainMenuWeaponSelect::init` (1671-1677). `MenuLevelSettings` is also copied by value into `MainMenuMidwayLoadSettings` (MainMenu.h:107) and back out (GameStates.cpp:12-16, 247, 257, 267), crossing several boundaries with nothing revalidating. A default-constructed `MenuLevelSettings` has `_player_count == 0` and an empty vector, so `get_player_team(0)` on one is UB — reachable today only via the HOME entry point which never indexes. The redundant loop in `set_player_count` (15-19) also shows the confusion: `resize()` already value-initialises the new elements, then the loop assigns `MenuPlayerSettings()` over them again (and `MenuPlayerSettings` has default member initialisers for all three fields, MenuPlayerSettings.h:8-11).

**Fix:** Delete `_player_count` and make `get_player_count()` return `static_cast<int>(_player_settings.size())` — one source of truth, invariant unbreakable. Collapse `set_player_count` to a single `resize()`. Use `.at()` (or an assert) in the accessors so an out-of-range index fails loudly.

#### 2. MenuLevelSettings is shared mutable state with an order-dependent API and stored derived data

`ArtAttack/MenuLevelSettings.cpp:62-84` — **medium** · `design`

The per-player setters index `_player_settings[player_index]` unchecked while the vector is sized only by the separate `set_player_count` (9-25), so the object carries an implicit protocol — count first, then per-player fields — that the caller must know. `MainMenuPlayerCount::update` performs the dance four times over: `set_player_count(1); set_player_team(0, A); set_screen_layout(ONE_PLAYER); set_player_num(0, 0);` (MainMenu.cpp:899-913, repeated at 915-950 for 2/3/4 players). `screen_layout` is pure derived data — it is a function of player count — yet it is stored (MenuLevelSettings.h:35) and hand-set at four sites, so the two can disagree. Meanwhile `MainMenuData` holds a `MenuLevelSettings*` that eight pages read and write across transitions, and three page constructors reassign it as a side effect (MainMenu.cpp:1137-1142, 1420-1425, 1767-1772).

**Fix:** Make it an immutable value produced by a builder, compute `screen_layout` from `player_count` at the point of use, and pass the finished value to `GameLevel` instead of sharing a pointer to a half-filled object across the whole menu flow.

## `ArtAttack/MenuLevelSettings.h`

_2 findings: 1 medium, 1 low_

#### 1. `level_mode` is accessed as "game_mode"; `player_num` vs `player_index` vs `num` means three things across the codebase

`ArtAttack/MenuLevelSettings.h:17-18, 24-29` — **medium** · `naming` · confidence: certain

Two related naming lies in one small class:
  1. `void set_game_mode(level_mode game_mode);` / `level_mode get_game_mode() const;` (lines 17-18) storing `level_mode _game_mode` (32). The type is called a *level* mode, the accessor a *game* mode, and the enum values are `STANDARD_MODE, TEAM_DEATHMATCH, DEATHMATCH, PRACTICE` (`level_mode.h:6-9`) - note `STANDARD_MODE` carries a redundant `_MODE` suffix its three siblings do not.
  2. `void set_player_num(int player_index, int player_num);` (line 29) takes both concepts as ints in one call, and `MenuLevelSettings.cpp:82-84` shows they are genuinely different (`_player_settings[player_index].num = player_num`). `MenuPlayerSettings.h:48` names the field just `num`. Meanwhile `ViewportManager.h:78-90` uses `player_num` as a 0-based viewport *index*, `Player.h:113,156` stores `_player_num` seeded from `player_consts::DEFAULT_PLAYER_NUM = 0`, and `Weapon.h:19,58,136` passes `player_num` through to sound-instance selection (`shoot_sound_name_a0..b3`).
  Also `void set_screen_layout(screen_layout screen_layout);` (line 22) - the only parameter in the repo that shadows its own type name.

**Fix:** Pick `level_mode`/`get_level_mode` or `game_mode`/`game_mode` and be consistent; drop the `_MODE` suffix from `STANDARD_MODE`. Then split the player identifiers: `player_index` (0..3 slot, used for arrays/viewports) vs `gamepad_index`, and rename `MenuPlayerSettings::num` accordingly. Rename the shadowing parameter to `layout`.

#### 2. Aggregate getters return by value where const& belongs, forcing whole-container and struct copies

`ArtAttack/MenuLevelSettings.h:14, 24` — **low** · `performance`

`std::vector<MenuPlayerSettings> MenuLevelSettings::get_player_settings() const` (MenuLevelSettings.h:14, .cpp:4-7) copies the entire vector; its one caller iterates it read-only — `PlayerBuilder.cpp:27` `for (auto& setting : settings.get_player_settings())` — a full heap copy per level build, bound by non-const reference so any write would be silently discarded into a temporary. `set_player_setting(int, MenuPlayerSettings)` (h:24) takes the struct by value then copies it again into the vector (.cpp:62-65). `ResultsMenuData::get_level_end_info() const` (ResultsMenuData.h:14) and `ResultsMenuInitial::get_level_end_info() const` (ResultsMenu.h:101, .cpp:275-278) each return `LevelEndInfo` by value — a copy of a copy of an aggregate containing a `TeamColour` plus two floats — and `update_team_a_fill`/`update_team_b_fill` call it every frame (ResultsMenu.cpp:228, 241) just to read one float that is fixed from `init()` onward. `init()` itself already holds `const LevelEndInfo end_info` at line 75 and then re-fetches two more full copies at 116 and 127. `ViewportManager::get_all_viewports()` (ViewportManager.cpp:89-103) likewise builds a fresh vector and is called once per MObject per frame from MenuPage.cpp:99-100.

**Fix:** Return `const std::vector<MenuPlayerSettings>&` and `const LevelEndInfo&`; take `const MenuPlayerSettings&` in the setter; use `const auto&` at PlayerBuilder.cpp:27; reuse the `end_info` local at ResultsMenu.cpp:116/127; cache the viewport list in `ViewportManager` and invalidate it in `set_layout`.

## `ArtAttack/PaintTile.h`

_2 findings: 1 medium, 1 low_

#### 1. PaintTile is a heavyweight polymorphic object with four std::strings and a full animation object, instantiated thousands of times

`ArtAttack/PaintTile.h:51-84` — **medium** · `performance`

```cpp
class PaintTile final : public TextureObject, public ICollisionGameObject
{
    MattMath::RectangleF _rectangle;
    player_team _team = player_team::NONE;
    TeamColour _team_colours = TeamColour();   // identical for every tile in the level
    const float* _dt = nullptr;                // stored and never read
    PaintTileSplash _splash;                   // a whole AnimationObject
};
```
Each tile carries two vtable pointers, a `ResourceManager*`, colour/origin/rotation/effects/depth from `DrawObject`, **two `std::string`s** from `SpriteSheetObject` (`"sprite_sheet_1"`, `"pixel"`), and an embedded `PaintTileSplash` with two more strings (`"sprite_sheet_1"`, `"splash_1"`) plus its own full copy of the DrawObject state. Every one of those strings holds the same literal, per tile. `TeamColour` is a level-wide constant duplicated per tile.

Counts from the shipped data: king_of_the_hill's `boundary_floor` alone is 1,500 tiles; turbulence has that plus eight more paintable structures. `StructurePaintable::update` (:37-43) walks all of them every frame just to tick `_splash.update()`, which for a paused splash is a virtual call that returns immediately.

`_dt` (PaintTile.h:82) is stored from the ctor and never read — I grepped PaintTile.cpp and the only hit is the initialiser at line 23; the splash gets its own copy of the pointer.

`_splash` is also two-phase constructed: default-constructed then assigned in the constructor body (PaintTile.cpp:25-28), which is the only reason `PaintTileSplash() = default` has to exist.

**Fix:** Replace `std::vector<PaintTile>` with a grid: `{ Vector2F origin; float tile_w, tile_h; int nx, ny; std::vector<uint8_t> team; }` — per-cell storage drops from ~300 bytes to 1, and position/colour/sheet/frame are all derivable. Keep a small list of *active* splashes so `update` iterates those, not every cell. Meanwhile: delete `_dt` and move `_splash` into the member-init list.

#### 2. A level-wide-constant TeamColour is stored by value in every PaintTile

`ArtAttack/PaintTile.h:81` — **low** · `performance`

`TeamColour _team_colours = TeamColour();` — 32 bytes (two 4-float `Colour`s), copied into every paint tile. `StructurePaintable` holds `std::vector<PaintTile> _paint_tiles` (StructurePaintable.h:53), generated as a grid over every paintable surface, and `PaintTile::on_collision` reads `_team_colours.get_team_colour(...)` on the collision path (PaintTile.cpp:39-64).

The value is fixed for the entire level — chosen once at LevelBuilder.cpp:36 — so the same two colours are duplicated across every tile and pulled through cache in the tile update/draw/scoring loops. `Level` (Level.h:128) and `StructurePaintable` (StructurePaintable.h:54) each hold their own copy too.

Graded `low` because I have not measured the tile count; the fix is cheap either way and `PaintTile` is the most numerous object type in the game, so its footprint is worth auditing as a whole.

**Fix:** Store a `const TeamColour*` (8 bytes) or a small palette index in `PaintTile`, with the single `TeamColour` owned by `Level`. Better still, resolve the tile's colour once when its team changes rather than looking it up through a per-tile copy on every collision.

## `ArtAttack/Partitioner.cpp`

_3 findings: 2 medium, 1 low_

#### 1. partition() divides by num_partitions with no validation — zero is a hardware fault, negative silently returns nothing

`ArtAttack/Partitioner.cpp:4-22` — **medium** · `robustness`

```cpp
int elements_per_partition = num_elements / num_partitions;
int remainder = num_elements % num_partitions;
```
Neither argument is checked. `num_partitions == 0` is integer division by zero — undefined behaviour, a fault on x86. `num_partitions < 0` gives a negative quotient, the loop condition `i < num_partitions && i < num_elements` is false immediately, and an **empty** vector is returned; the callers then dispatch zero draw tasks and render nothing, with no diagnostic. This is a public utility in a library that is supposed to be reusable, with no stated precondition anywhere.

REJECTED sub-claim, repeated by four reviewers: that this path is live because `ThreadPool::_max_num_threads` is default-initialised to -1 (ThreadPool.h:26). ThreadPool has no default constructor — the only declared one is `ThreadPool(int min, int max)` (ThreadPool.h:12) — and the sole construction site passes NUM_THREADS_MAX (Game.cpp:236). The -1 member initialiser is never observable. The missing validation is real; the claimed live trigger is not.

The partition arithmetic itself is correct: I checked remainder distribution and the `i < num_elements` guard for 0, 5/3, 17/16 and n < partitions.

**Fix:** `if (num_partitions <= 0) throw std::invalid_argument(...)` (or clamp to 1) and `if (num_elements <= 0) return {};` at the top. Also give ThreadPool's members a sane default rather than -1, and make them const.

#### 2. Partitioner + ThreadPool + index ranges is a hand-rolled parallel_for duplicated at both call sites

`ArtAttack/Partitioner.cpp:4-27` — **medium** · `design`

Both users perform the identical six-step ritual. Level::draw_active_level (Level.cpp:378-399): read num_threads, partition(size, num_threads), loop over result, add_task capturing the index, wait_for_tasks_to_complete. MenuPage::draw_mobjects_in_viewports (MenuPage.cpp:125-150): the same code with a different body function. Both then rely on the partition index implicitly lining up with a deferred-context index and a SpriteBatch index in parallel vectors — a correspondence expressed nowhere in a type.

The two sites also disagree about capture semantics: Level captures `partitioned_players` **by value** into every lambda (Level.cpp:388, a vector copy per task per frame), MenuPage captures `partitioned_mobjects` and `command_lists` **by reference** (MenuPage.cpp:142-143). Both are correct only because of the join four lines later, which is documented nowhere. One site pays for safety it does not need; the other relies on an invariant it does not state.

A further note on the MenuPage site: `command_lists` holds raw owning COM pointers released by hand at MenuPage.cpp:162, and draw_mobject_in_viewports throws (`throw std::exception("Failed to finish command list")`, MenuPage.cpp:120), so an exception between creation and release leaks every command list. ComPtr is already used elsewhere in the codebase.

**Fix:** Put `parallel_for(size_t count, fn(begin, end, worker))` on ThreadPool. It owns the split, the dispatch and the join, and passing `worker` explicitly stops the deferred-context/SpriteBatch lookup being an implicit index correspondence. Both call sites collapse to one line and Partitioner disappears. Use ComPtr for the command lists.

#### 3. partition() returns fewer partitions than requested, without reserve, and the result is copied per task

`ArtAttack/Partitioner.cpp:4-22` — **low** · `performance`

The loop guard is `i < num_partitions && i < num_elements`, so the result size is min(num_partitions, num_elements) — the function silently does not honour its own parameter, and nothing in the header says so. Both call sites happen to iterate `result.size()` and survive, but any caller that indexes a per-thread resource array by num_threads would be wrong.

The final size is known exactly up front yet there is no `reserve`, so this reallocates two or three times per call, once per draw pass per frame. `push_back(std::make_pair(start, end))` constructs a temporary where `emplace_back(start, end)` would construct in place. Level then captures the whole returned vector by value into each of N lambdas (Level.cpp:388), so with N partitions that is N more copies per frame of data that is constant for the frame.

**Fix:** `reserve(min(num_partitions, num_elements))` and `emplace_back`. Document (and assert) the shortfall behaviour, or pad with empty ranges so the result size always equals the requested count and the worker-index correspondence holds. Capture only `partitioned[i]` in each lambda, not the whole vector.

## `ArtAttack/Partitioner.h`

_3 findings: 3 medium_

#### 1. A stateless one-function class is heap-allocated and threaded through four layers as a non-owning pointer

`ArtAttack/Partitioner.h:6-16` — **medium** · `design`

`class Partitioner` has zero data members; both methods are const and pure. Despite that it is heap-allocated once (Game.cpp:255 `std::make_unique<Partitioner>()`), stored as `std::unique_ptr<Partitioner>` (Game.h:75), published into the service locator (GameData.h:43-44, 61; GameData.cpp:148-156), threaded through LevelBuilder's constructor and member (LevelBuilder.h:24, 38; LevelBuilder.cpp:14, 21, 82), into Level's constructor and member (Level.h:80, 147; Level.cpp:30, 52), fetched ad hoc by MenuPage (MenuPage.cpp:130), and passed again at GameStates.cpp:120. GameData.h includes Partitioner.h, so effectively every TU sees it.

Four non-owning `const Partitioner*` aliases exist whose validity rests on the undocumented assumption that Game::_partitioner outlives every Level and MenuPage; none is documented as non-owning and none is null-checked before use (Level.cpp:383, MenuPage.cpp:135). The payoff for that surface is nothing, because there is no state to share.

For the engine-reuse goal specifically: a partitioning utility should not require an object graph to call.

**Fix:** Delete the class. Free functions in a namespace. That removes a member from GameData, a constructor parameter and member from LevelBuilder and Level, and an include from three headers.

#### 2. The class named "Partitioner" does no spatial partitioning, and the engine has no broad phase at all

`ArtAttack/Partitioner.h:6` — **medium** · `design`

In a 2D engine, "partitioner" names a spatial index. This class splits [0, n) into contiguous index ranges for thread scheduling. Meanwhile the thing the name promises does not exist anywhere: Level::update_level_logic (Level.cpp:180-293) is three nested loops — players x collision_objects, collision_objects x players, collision_objects x collision_objects — with no acceleration structure and no ordering. Every pair is narrow-phase tested, and because the first two loops cover the same pairs in both orderings, each player/object pair is tested and dispatched to `on_collision` **twice per frame**; the object/object loop likewise runs both orderings with only an `object == object_2` self-guard.

Each of those tests is the virtual + dynamic_cast + (for non-rect shapes) allocating path, and each resolved contact then triggers the 40-iteration bracket. With a paint-heavy level dominated by projectiles, the quadratic term caps projectile count long before rendering does. Note also that ThreadPool/Partitioner are used only to parallelise *drawing* (Level.cpp:374-399); the genuinely quadratic part of the frame is single-threaded.

**Fix:** Rename the current class to what it is (RangeSplitter / IndexRange) and build the abstraction the name was reserving: a uniform grid broad phase producing a deduplicated candidate pair list, queried per object. Level bounds are already known (Level::is_object_out_of_bounds), so a grid is the cheapest correct fit.

#### 3. The int/size_t partition overload pair narrows silently and is ambiguous for every other integer type

`ArtAttack/Partitioner.h:11-15` — **medium** · `correctness`

```cpp
std::vector<std::pair<int, int>> partition(int num_elements, int num_partitions) const;
std::vector<std::pair<int, int>> partition(size_t num_elements, int num_partitions) const;
```
The size_t overload's entire body is `return partition(static_cast<int>(num_elements), num_partitions);` (Partitioner.cpp:26) — an unchecked narrowing cast, so a container larger than INT_MAX yields a negative count and the silent-empty behaviour above. The overload exists only so call sites can pass `.size()` without a warning; it suppresses the warning rather than fixing the type.

The pair also only disambiguates for exactly `int` and exactly `size_t`. Any other integer type (unsigned int, long, uint32_t on this toolchain) needs an integral conversion to reach either candidate, both at the same rank, so the call is ambiguous and fails to compile — a trap for the next caller.

Returning signed pairs then forces signed/unsigned comparisons at both call sites: `for (int i = 0; i < partitioned_players.size(); i++)` (Level.cpp:386) and `for (int i = 0; i < partitioned_mobjects.size(); i++)` (MenuPage.cpp:140), both C4018 under /W4 — advisory only, since TreatWarningAsError is set nowhere.

**Fix:** One function taking and returning size_t, and a named result type: `struct IndexRange { size_t begin; size_t end; };` — `.first`/`.second` at Level.cpp:391-392 and MenuPage.cpp:146 tell the reader nothing. Delete the int overload; mark it [[nodiscard]].

## `ArtAttack/PlayerBuilder.h`

_1 finding: 1 medium_

#### 1. build_players returns unique_ptr<vector<unique_ptr<Player>>> — a heap allocation and a null state wrapping an already-movable container

`ArtAttack/PlayerBuilder.h:15-21` — **medium** · `design`

Merges 2 candidates. `PlayerBuilder.cpp:21` does `auto players = std::make_unique<std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Player>>>();` and `:66` returns it. The outer `unique_ptr` adds an allocation, an indirection, and a nullable state that no caller checks, around a type that is already move-only and cheap to move — a plain local plus `return players;` would be identical in cost thanks to NRVO.

The cost is paid at every use site: `Level.h:95-105` stores four members this way (`_non_collision_objects`, `_collision_objects`, `_player_objects`, `_viewport_dividers`), all defaulted to `nullptr`, and Level.cpp dereferences them everywhere (`*this->_player_objects` at :190, 222, 252, 262, 308, 639; `->at(i)` at :503, 508, 555-577). `Level() = default;` exists (Level.h:57), so a default-constructed Level with null members is a reachable state and every one of those dereferences is a null deref waiting to happen.

**Fix:** Return `std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Player>>` by value and store it by value in `Level`. The container can never be null and `*this->_player_objects` becomes `_player_objects` everywhere.

## `ArtAttack/projectile_consts.h`

_3 findings: 1 medium, 2 low_

#### 1. Namespace-scope const/static const aggregates with std::string members in a header: per-TU copies, dynamic init, and a cross-header init-order dependency

`ArtAttack/projectile_consts.h:6-107` — **medium** · `modern-cpp`

Verified. Every constant in `namespace projectile_consts` is a namespace-scope object defined in a header. Both plain `const` (lines 8-12) and `static const` (lines 14-106) give internal linkage at namespace scope, so every TU including this header gets its own private copy — and the file itself is inconsistent about which spelling it uses, for no reason.

`ProjectileDetails` holds two `std::string` members (projectile_details.h:16-17) and `Vector2F`'s constructors are defined out-of-line in MattMath.cpp, so none of these are literal types: all eight aggregates are **dynamically initialised** globals doing 12 string constructions per TU at static-init time, plus destructors at exit. projectile_consts.h is pulled in transitively through Projectile.h -> the five projectile headers -> ProjectileBuilder.h -> Weapon.h -> Player.h -> Level.h, reaching most of the game.

A real init-order hazard falls out of it, which I verified: `weapon_consts.h` initialises its own namespace-scope statics by *reading* these ones — `{ projectile_consts::DETAILS_SPRAY.size.x / 2.0f, 0.0f }` at weapon_consts.h:40, and the same at :74, :90, :118, :152. One dynamically-initialised object depends on another. It works only because weapon_consts.h includes projectile_consts.h first, so declaration order within each TU saves it — a guarantee that breaks silently the day someone reorders an include.

Five constants are entirely dead, confirmed by grep: `DEFAULT_STARTING_POSITION` (:8), `DEFAULT_SIZE` (:9), `STARTING_DX` (:10), `STARTING_VELOCITY` (:11) and `DETAILS_DEFAULT` (:14-25, whose animation strip is literally named "test"). The four Vector2F names are verbatim duplicates of `player_consts::DEFAULT_STARTING_POSITION/DEFAULT_SIZE/STARTING_DX/STARTING_VELOCITY` (player_consts.h:20-25).

Merged from 3 candidate reports.

**Fix:** Delete the five dead constants. Make `ProjectileDetails` a literal type (`std::string_view` or `const char*` for the two names), give `Vector2F` constexpr constructors, and declare every blob `inline constexpr` — one object program-wide, zero dynamic init, zero allocation, no init-order question. That needs `<LanguageStandard>` set (see the C++14 finding). If the standard must stay put, at minimum use `extern const` in the header with a single definition in a .cpp.

#### 2. projectile_consts::DETAILS_DEFAULT names an animation strip 'test' that does not exist in the atlas

`ArtAttack/projectile_consts.h:14-25` — **low** · `correctness` · confidence: certain

static const ProjectileDetails DETAILS_DEFAULT =
    {
        ... "sprite_sheet_1",  //sheet_name
            "test",            //animation_strip_name
    };

ArtAttack/textures/sprite_sheet_1.json declares exactly nine animation strips (lines 2-121): `player_right_walk`, `player_right_idle`, `player_right_jumping`, `player_right_falling`, `player_test`, `projectile_1`, `projectile_2`, `projectile_3`, `splash_1`. There is no `test`. Because `SpriteSheet::get_animation_strip` uses `.at(name)` (SpriteSheet.cpp:15-18), this would be an uncaught `std::out_of_range` rather than a silent miss.

It does not currently fire — grepping the tree, `projectile_consts::DETAILS_DEFAULT` has no users (only `weapon_consts::DETAILS_DEFAULT`, which names the real frame `error`, is used, at Weapon.h:48). So this is a landmine rather than a live bug, but it is exactly the kind of thing that detonates the first time someone adds a projectile type and copies the default.

Related dead atlas content found in the same cross-check — 15 entries in sprite_sheet_1.json are referenced by nothing in the codebase: `square_white_32`, `paint`, `dirt`, `grass`, `cloud`, `sky`, `proj_roller`, `splatter_20/40/60/80`, `player_1_right`, `player_2_right`, `pause_menu_box` (PauseMenu.cpp:122-123 draws `pixel` instead), and the strips `projectile_1`, `projectile_2`, `player_test`. `player_test` (json:56-68, x0 y1300 100×100 ×4) additionally overlaps the live `player_right_idle` and `player_right_jumping` strips in the texture.

**Fix:** Point DETAILS_DEFAULT at `error`/`projectile_3` like the other entries, or delete it since it is unused. Prune the 15 dead atlas entries, and add a startup validation that every name constant in *_consts.h resolves in the loaded sheet — it is a dozen lines and would have caught all of this.

#### 3. A single float silently becomes a Vector2F in the diffusion constants, under a comment that names the wrong field

`ArtAttack/projectile_consts.h:40-46` — **low** · `robustness`

Verified. `DIFFUSION_DETAILS_SPRAY` (projectile_consts.h:40-46) and `DIFFUSION_DETAILS_MIST` (:87-93) initialise the third member with a bare `1.5f` / `5.0f`, but that member is `MattMath::Vector2F end_scale` (projectile_details.h:31). This compiles only because `Vector2F(float f)` (MattMath.h:409) is a non-explicit converting constructor. It happens to do what was meant, but nothing at the call site says so — and the trailing comment reads `//end_size` while the field is named `end_scale`, so the source of truth for what `1.5f` means is wrong twice. Non-uniform diffusion is silently unexpressible at these call sites even though the field is a vector.

The same implicit conversion means any `float` binds to any `const Vector2F&` parameter across the whole codebase.

**Fix:** Write `MattMath::Vector2F(1.5f, 1.5f)` here, as the `DETAILS_*` blobs already do for `size`, and fix the comment to `//end_scale`. Mark `Vector2F(float)` `explicit` in MattMath.h:409 — the compiler will then point at every other site relying on the silent conversion.

## `ArtAttack/projectile_details.h`

_2 findings: 1 medium, 1 low_

#### 1. Four of nine detail fields are never read, and damage has a second, sign-inverted source of truth in player_consts.h

`ArtAttack/projectile_details.h:7-33` — **medium** · `design`

Verified by repo-wide grep. Dead fields:
- `rotation_origin rotat_origin` (line 11) — set by all six constants (projectile_consts.h:18,31,52,65,78,99, including a meaningful `rotation_origin::CENTER` for the jet) and read by nothing. The only repo hits are the declaration and those six initialisers. Jets are never oriented along their velocity despite the data saying they should be.
- `diffusion_type type` (line 32) — set to `LINEAR_SIZE_AND_COL_RECT` by both diffusion blobs and never consulted. `calculate_diffusion_size` (Projectile.cpp:61-89) never branches on it, so `NO_DIFFUSION` does not disable diffusion and all three enumerators (lines 20-25) behave identically.
- `float delete_timer` (line 12) — dead because of the `get_delete_timer()` bug; see that finding.
- `float player_damage` (line 13) — the only reader would be `Projectile::get_player_damage()` (Projectile.cpp:295-298), which has zero callers.

The damage duplication is the worst of it, and I verified both tables. projectile_consts.h uses **negative** values (`-0.1f` spray :33, `-0.5f` jet :54, `-1000.0f` rolling :67, `-0.05f` mist :80, `-0.1f` ball :101), implying `health += damage`. The live values are the **positive** `player_consts.h:65-69` (`SPRAY_DAMAGE = 0.01f`, `JET_DAMAGE = 0.334f`, `ROLLING_DAMAGE = 0.015f`, `BALL_DAMAGE = 0.201f`, `MIST_DAMAGE = 0.01f`), applied with `-=` in an 11-branch enum ladder (Player.cpp:645-682). Two tables, opposite sign conventions, magnitudes differing by up to 5 orders of magnitude (rolling: -1000.0 vs 0.015), and the one that lives with the projectile — the obvious place to tune — is the dead one.

One reviewer additionally claimed the `-1.0f` sentinel defaults in `DiffusionDetails` (lines 29-31) produce a negative-size rectangle through `inflate_to_size`. The mechanism is real (I checked MattMath.cpp:957-963 — it writes width/height straight through), but no code path constructs a `DiffusingProjectile` with default `DiffusionDetails`, so I am not reporting that as a live defect.

Merged from 4 candidate reports.

**Fix:** Damage belongs to the attacker: delete `player_consts.h:65-69`, fix the sign convention in projectile_consts.h, and have `Player::on_projectile_collision` do `this->_health -= projectile->get_player_damage();`. That collapses a 38-line ladder to one line and removes the `throw std::exception("Invalid projectile type.")` at Player.cpp:681. Then either honour `rotat_origin` in the draw path and branch on `diffusion_type`, or delete both fields and the enum. Do not leave aspirational fields that read as working features.

#### 2. The snake_case-file/PascalCase-file split has a rule, and two files break it - plus abbreviated struct fields

`ArtAttack/projectile_details.h:1-33` — **low** · `naming` · confidence: certain

The de-facto convention is: PascalCase filename = declares a class/struct of that name (`WeaponDetails.h` -> `WeaponDetails`, `PlayerInputData.h` -> `PlayerInputData`, `MenuPlayerSettings.h` -> `MenuPlayerSettings`, `BorderThickness.h` -> `BorderThickness`); snake_case filename = enums and constants only (`shape_type.h`, `wep_type.h`, `player_team.h`, `weapon_consts.h`, ...). Two files break it: `projectile_details.h` declares `struct ProjectileDetails`, `enum class diffusion_type` and `struct DiffusionDetails`, and `player_consts.h:8-16` declares `struct PlayerAnimationInfo` inside a constants header. Compare `WeaponDetails.h`, which is the exact same kind of file, correctly named.
Inside `ProjectileDetails` the fields are also abbreviated inconsistently: `rotation_origin rotat_origin` (line 11 - "rotat" is not a word) and `Vector2F col_rect_size` (15 - "col" reads as column or colour, it means collision) sit beside fully spelled `wind_resistance`, `player_damage`, `animation_strip_name`.

**Fix:** Rename `projectile_details.h` -> `ProjectileDetails.h` and move `PlayerAnimationInfo` out of `player_consts.h` into `PlayerAnimationInfo.h`. Fix the fields: `rotat_origin` -> `rotation_origin_mode` (it cannot be `rotation_origin`, that is the type), `col_rect_size` -> `collision_rect_size`.

## `ArtAttack/ProjectileBuilder.h`

_2 findings: 2 medium_

#### 1. Stateless ProjectileBuilder is heap-allocated per weapon, takes 12 positional parameters, and drags all five concrete headers into most of the game

`ArtAttack/ProjectileBuilder.h:11-45` — **medium** · `design`

Verified. `ProjectileBuilder` has zero data members (ProjectileBuilder.h:11-44). `build_projectiles` is a non-static `const` member that touches no state; `build_mist_projectiles` is already `static` — which the class half-acknowledges by calling `this->build_mist_projectiles(...)` on a static function (ProjectileBuilder.cpp:80). Yet `Weapon` owns one on the heap: `std::unique_ptr<ProjectileBuilder> _proj_builder = nullptr;` (Weapon.h:122), allocated at Weapon.cpp:32 — one allocation per weapon per player per level for an empty object.

The signature is 12 positional parameters written out four times (ProjectileBuilder.h:15-27 and :30-42, ProjectileBuilder.cpp:9-21 and :117-129). Both real call sites — Weapon.cpp:319-327 and Weapon.cpp:565-573 — pass only the first eight, so `rotation`, `origin`, `effects` and `layer_depth` are always defaults, threaded down through every leaf constructor to `DrawObject` for nothing. With 12 same-shaped neighbours an argument-order mistake compiles cleanly, which is precisely how the `SPRAY`-instead-of-`MIST` bug survived. `build_mist_projectiles` additionally takes a `projectile_type type` it never reads (C4100 under /W4).

Header coupling: ProjectileBuilder.h:4-9 includes `Projectile.h` plus all five concrete projectile headers, and Weapon.h:11 includes ProjectileBuilder.h, so every TU reaching Weapon.h — Player.h, Level.h, the game states — parses all five projectile classes, though nothing in the builder's interface names a concrete type (the return is `vector<unique_ptr<ICollisionGameObject>>`).

Correction to the reviewers: two of them claimed `Weapon::get_projectile_builder()` has zero callers. That is **false** — it is called at Weapon.cpp:565. The rest of the finding stands. Merged from 4 candidate reports.

**Fix:** Make these free functions in a `projectile_builder` namespace (or plain statics) marked `[[nodiscard]]`, delete `_proj_builder`, the `make_unique` at Weapon.cpp:32 and the `get_projectile_builder()` accessor. Replace the 12 positional parameters with one `ProjectileSpawnParams` struct by const&, and drop the four unused draw parameters from the whole chain. Move the five concrete `#include`s into ProjectileBuilder.cpp and add the missing `<vector>`/`<memory>`. Also: `ProjectileBuilder.cpp:113` has a stray `;` after the switch's closing brace.

#### 2. The project sets no <LanguageStandard>, so it silently builds as C++14 and blocks the idioms this module most needs

`ArtAttack/ProjectileBuilder.h:15-27` — **medium** · `modern-cpp`

Verified: I grepped ArtAttack.vcxproj for `LanguageStandard` and there is no such element in any of the four `ItemDefinitionGroup` blocks, so MSVC defaults to /std:c++14. `WarningLevel Level4` and `ConformanceMode true` are set (lines 91/96, 113/117, 134/141, 160/166), and `/Zc:__cplusplus` is already in AdditionalOptions.

Concretely, within this module that costs:
- `inline constexpr` variables — the correct fix for the eight per-TU dynamically-initialised globals in projectile_consts.h.
- `std::string_view` for `ProjectileDetails::sheet_name`/`animation_strip_name`, which are compile-time literals in all six blobs yet force heap allocations per TU per blob.
- `std::clamp` for the four hand-rolled clamp ladders at Projectile.cpp:238-245 and 265-272 (`<algorithm>` is already in pch.h).
- `[[nodiscard]]` on `build_projectiles` — today, silently dropping the returned volley of `unique_ptr`s compiles without a peep.
- `std::size` for the spread-angle array that should replace the five copy-pasted mist blocks.

Nothing in this module depends on pre-C++17 behaviour.

**Fix:** Add `<LanguageStandard>stdcpp20</LanguageStandard>` (or `stdcpp17` as a first step) to all four ItemDefinitionGroup blocks in ArtAttack.vcxproj, and to MattMathTests.vcxproj. Then land the `inline constexpr` / `string_view` / `std::clamp` / `[[nodiscard]]` changes the other findings call for.

## `ArtAttack/ResolutionManager.cpp`

_5 findings: 4 medium, 1 low_

#### 1. convert_resolution_to_ivec returns {-1,-1} for an unknown value while every sibling converter falls back to 1280x720

`ArtAttack/ResolutionManager.cpp:47-63` — **medium** · `correctness`

`default: return {-1, -1};` (:60-62). The three sibling converters all fall back to a valid resolution: `convert_string_to_resolution` → S_1280_720 (:119), `convert_vec_to_resolution` → S_1280_720 (:148), `convert_ivec_to_resolution` → S_1280_720 (:173). `convert_resolution_to_string` returns the literal string `"-1x-1"` (:90), which round-trips back through `convert_string_to_resolution` to 1280x720 — so the two halves of one round trip disagree about the sentinel.

A `{-1,-1}` flows straight into `RECT rc = {0, 0, -1, -1}` and `CreateWindowExW(..., -1, -1, ...)` (Main.cpp:146-164) and into `SetWindow(hwnd, -1, -1)` (Game.cpp:38-40), where `static_cast<UINT>(m_outputSize.right - m_outputSize.left)` (DeviceResources.cpp:275) becomes 0xFFFFFFFF before the `std::max<UINT>(…, 1u)` clamp lets it through. It also poisons every viewport division in ViewportManager. Nothing checks for a negative extent anywhere.

**Fix:** Make all five converters agree on one policy. `screen_resolution` is a scoped enum with four values, so `default:` is unreachable for well-formed input — make it loud (assert / `throw std::invalid_argument`) plus a 1280x720 fallback. Silently returning a negative size is the worst of the options.

#### 2. The resolution table is hand-written five times here and duplicated again in Save

`ArtAttack/ResolutionManager.cpp:47-175` — **medium** · `design`

Five parallel encodings of the same four rows: `convert_resolution_to_ivec` (:47-63), `convert_resolution_to_string` (:76-92), `convert_string_to_resolution` (:94-121, an if/else chain calling the previous function four times, each returning a fresh heap `std::string` — up to four allocations per lookup), `convert_vec_to_resolution` (:123-150), `convert_ivec_to_resolution` (:152-175, which hard-codes 1280/720/1920/… a second time so the pixel dimensions live in two places that can drift). `Save.cpp:112-152` duplicates two of them again, declared as private members of an unrelated class in Save.h.

All four private converters are `const` non-static member functions that never touch `this` — free functions wearing a `this` pointer. (Note: `convert_resolution_to_string` is correctly `static` in ResolutionManager.h:21, contrary to what some reviewers claimed.)

**Fix:** One `static constexpr std::array<ResolutionInfo, N>` of `{screen_resolution id, int w, int h, std::string_view name}` with lookup helpers over it. Save serialises the id or the name and calls the shared lookup. Supporting 21:9 or arbitrary sizes becomes a table edit rather than seven function edits.

#### 3. Resolution is a closed hardcoded list of four 16:9 modes, never validated against the actual display

`ArtAttack/ResolutionManager.cpp:47-121` — **medium** · `robustness`

Nothing in the codebase queries the display: I grepped all of ArtAttack/ for `GetSystemMetrics`, `EnumDisplaySettings`, `GetMonitorInfo`, `MonitorFromWindow` and `GetDisplayModeList` — zero hits. The only adapter/output enumeration that ever existed is commented out at Main.cpp:39-81.

So the options menu walks the enum blindly (`MainMenu.cpp:572` reads `static_cast<int>(screen_resolution::MAX)` and cycles), and selecting 3840x2160 on a 1080p panel creates an oversized window with no check. A user whose native mode is not one of the four hardcoded 16:9 entries can never match it, and a saved resolution is never validated on load. Combined with the `{-1,-1}` sentinel above, an out-of-range value produces a negative window size rather than a clamp.

**Fix:** Enumerate supported modes from `IDXGIOutput::GetDisplayModeList` at startup, populate the options menu from that list, validate any saved resolution against it, and clamp to the monitor's current mode on mismatch.

#### 4. Five parallel conversion ladders over the same four-entry resolution table

`ArtAttack/ResolutionManager.cpp:47-175` — **medium** · `design` · confidence: certain

The set {1280x720, 1920x1080, 2560x1440, 3840x2160} is written out five separate times in 130 lines:

- `convert_resolution_to_ivec` (:47-63) — switch returning `{1280,720}` etc.
- `convert_resolution_to_string` (:76-92) — switch returning `"1280x720"` etc.
- `convert_string_to_resolution` (:94-121) — 4-branch if-chain
- `convert_vec_to_resolution` (:123-150) — 4-branch if-chain
- `convert_ivec_to_resolution` (:152-175) — 4-branch if-chain that *re-hardcodes the literals a second time* (`if (vec.x == 1280 && vec.y == 720)`), so the numbers now live in two places and can drift.

Adding a resolution requires five edits plus an enum entry.

**Fix:** Declare one `static constexpr struct { screen_resolution e; int w, h; const char* name; } RESOLUTIONS[]` and implement all five functions as linear scans over it (the string form can be built with the width/height rather than stored). ~130 lines collapse to ~30, and a new resolution becomes one table row.

#### 5. convert_vec_to_resolution compares floats with == under /fp:fast, and both vec overloads are dead code

`ArtAttack/ResolutionManager.cpp:123-150` — **low** · `correctness`
