`if (vec == this->convert_resolution_to_vec(screen_resolution::S_1280_720))` — `Vector2F::operator==` is exact float equality (the codebase has `MattMath::are_equal(a, b, EPSILON)` for the epsilon case and does not use it here), and the project compiles with `FloatingPointModel=Fast` in all four configurations. The specific values 1280/720/1920/1080/2560/1440/3840/2160 are all exactly representable in binary32 so it works today, but only by accident — it stops working the moment a value such as 1366x768 scaled by a DPI factor is added.

Both `set_resolution(const Vector2F&)` and `set_resolution(const Vector2I&)` are additionally dead: a grep for `set_resolution` across ArtAttack/ finds only Main.cpp:100 and MainMenu.cpp:324, both passing a `screen_resolution` enum.

**Fix:** Delete the `Vector2F` and `Vector2I` overloads and their two private converters — ~50 lines of untested dead code with a latent float-equality trap. If a vec lookup is needed later, compare integer dimensions against the single constexpr table proposed above.

## `ArtAttack/ResolutionManager.h`

_2 findings: 1 medium, 1 low_

#### 1. Three different naming schemes for "the screen resolution as a vector", plus a duplicated private converter

`ArtAttack/ResolutionManager.h:12-13` — **medium** · `naming` · confidence: certain

The same two operations are named three ways across three classes:
  - `ResolutionManager.h:12-13`: `get_resolution_ivec()` -> Vector2I, `get_resolution_vec()` -> Vector2F. "vec" silently means float; "ivec" is GLSL vocabulary that appears nowhere else here.
  - `MenuPage.h:54-55`: `get_float_resolution()` -> Vector2F, `get_int_resolution()` -> Vector2I. Adjective moved to the front, abbreviations expanded.
  - `Save.h:34-37`: private `convert_ivec_to_resolution` / `convert_resolution_to_ivec`, byte-identical in name and purpose to `ResolutionManager.h:27,35` - the same converter written privately in two classes.
A fourth spelling shows up in `MainMenu.cpp:448` where the local is `res_i`.

**Fix:** Settle on one pair - `get_resolution_pixels()` returning Vector2I and `get_resolution_size()` returning Vector2F - and expose them only on `ResolutionManager`. `MenuPage` should forward, not rename. Move the `screen_resolution <-> vector` conversions into one place (they belong with `screen_resolution.h`, not duplicated in `Save` and `ResolutionManager`).

#### 2. No [[nodiscard]] on any observer in the platform layer, including ones that allocate or throw

`ArtAttack/ResolutionManager.h:12-22` — **low** · `modern-cpp`

Every query in this module is discardable: `ResolutionManager::get_resolution_ivec/get_resolution_vec/get_resolution_string/get_resolution/convert_resolution_to_string` (ResolutionManager.h:12-22); `ViewportManager::get_layout/get_player_viewport/get_all_viewports/get_camera_adjusted_player_viewport_rect/get_viewport_dividers/get_fullscreen_d3d11_viewport` (ViewportManager.h:26-43); `CameraTools::calculate_camera` (CameraTools.h:24); `DeviceResources::get_deferred_contexts/get_deferred_context` (DeviceResources.h:87-88). Several are non-trivial — `get_all_viewports` builds a vector, `get_viewport_dividers` builds a vector and can throw (ViewportManager.cpp:150). This matters more than usual here because `apply_*` vs `get_*` naming is the only signal distinguishing commands from queries, and the three `apply_player_viewport` overloads are easy to confuse with the getters.

**Fix:** Once /std:c++17 is set (see the vcxproj finding), mark all of the above `[[nodiscard]]`.

## `ArtAttack/ResourceLoader.h`

_2 findings: 1 medium, 1 low_

#### 1. ResourceLoader's entire public API is dead code, and GameData carries a ResourceLoader* nobody reads

`ArtAttack/ResourceLoader.h:15-54` — **medium** · `design`

Merged from 2 candidates. Ten public methods exist (`load_texture`, `load_texture_from_directory`, `load_sprite_font`, `load_sprite_font_from_directory`, `load_sprite_sheet`, `load_sprite_sheet_from_directory`, `load_level_info`, `load_level_info_from_directory`, `load_sound_bank`, `load_sound_bank_from_directory`). I grepped the whole first-party tree: the ONLY external call into this class anywhere is `Game.cpp:258 this->_resource_loader->load_all_resources();`. Every other reference is ResourceLoader calling itself.

Meanwhile `GameData` stores, sets and exposes a `ResourceLoader* _resource_loader` (GameData.h:27-28, 53) whose only reader in the entire codebase is `GameData`'s own copy constructor (GameData.cpp:9) — so a useless dependency and its transitive headers are propagated to every TU that includes GameData.h.

There is also a confusing overload set split across access levels: public `load_level_info(const std::string&, level_stage) const` (line 35) and private `load_level_info() const` (line 53).

The `*_from_directory` twins double the API purely to concatenate a directory, a name and a hardcoded extension.

**Fix:** Decide what the class is. If lazy/streaming loading is wanted, expose it through the registry (`AssetRegistry::load(AssetId)` / `load_async(...) -> JobHandle`) and drop the per-type public methods. If not, make everything private except `load_all_resources()` and remove `ResourceLoader*` from `GameData` entirely.

#### 2. ResourceLoader's const qualifiers are arbitrary — identical operations are half const, half not

`ArtAttack/ResourceLoader.h:15-54` — **low** · `const-correctness`

void load_texture(...) const;        // :17
    void load_sprite_font(...);          // :22   not const
    void load_sprite_sheet(...) const;   // :28
    void load_level_info(...) const;     // :35
    void load_sound_bank(...);           // :40   not const

All five do the same thing — build a resource and hand it to `_resource_manager->add_*` — and none mutates a `ResourceLoader` member. The split is a coin flip and it propagates: `load_textures()`/`load_level_info()` are const (lines 51, 53) because what they call is, while `load_fonts()`/`load_sounds()` (52, 54) are not, which forces `load_all_resources()` (15) to be non-const.

`const` here is also actively misleading: `load_texture(...) const` writes into the shared ResourceManager through a raw pointer. Marking a member const while it mutates the entire asset cache communicates the opposite of the truth.

**Fix:** Make them all non-const (they all mutate the world), or better, take the ResourceManager as a parameter so the mutation is visible in the signature: `void load_texture(ResourceManager& out, const std::filesystem::path&) const;`. The latter also makes ResourceLoader stateless and testable.

## `ArtAttack/Save.h`

_2 findings: 1 medium, 1 low_

#### 1. `Save` conflates persistence, schema, display policy and console logging; it is really an unversioned settings file

`ArtAttack/Save.h:11-39` — **medium** · `design`

`SaveData` contains exactly `{screen_resolution resolution; bool fullscreen;}` — application display settings, not save-game data. I read the on-disk form: save/save_data.json is a single line, `{"resolution":{"x":1920,"y":1080},"fullscreen":false}`, with no schema version field, so the format can never be migrated.

The class simultaneously does file I/O (`load_from_json`, `write_save_file`), owns the resolution enum<->pixel mapping (the duplicated tables above), and logs to `std::cout` from a windowed app with no console. `set_resolution_and_save` / `set_full_screen_and_save` (Save.cpp:101-111) hard-wire the write policy into every setter, so changes cannot be batched or deferred. The path is a fixed relative constant, so multiple profiles or a per-user location are impossible.

Minor in the same header: `SaveData _save_data = SaveData();` (line 29) spells out a redundant copy-initialisation where the members' default initialisers already do the job.

**Fix:** Split into (a) a POD `Settings` struct with a `version` field, (b) a `SettingsStore` serialising it to a path supplied at construction (resolved through a platform path service), and (c) a logging facade. Setters mutate `Settings`; an explicit `store.save(settings)` performs I/O.

#### 2. `fullscreen` vs `full_screen` inconsistent inside a single class

`ArtAttack/Save.h:14, 26-27` — **low** · `naming` · confidence: certain

`SaveData::fullscreen` (Save.h:14, one word), `Save::get_fullscreen()` (26, one word), `Save::set_full_screen_and_save(bool full_screen)` (27, two words). `MainMenu.h:177` then stores `bool _full_screen_selection` and `MainMenu.cpp` uses widget names `"full_screen"` / `"full_screen_value"`, while `Main.cpp` branches on `Save::get_fullscreen`. Also note `set_full_screen_and_save` and `set_resolution_and_save` (line 24) encode a side effect in the name, which means there is no way to set the value without persisting - a design smell the name is honest about but should not need to be.

**Fix:** Standardise on the one-word `fullscreen` (matching the Win32/DXGI vocabulary): `set_fullscreen(bool fullscreen)`, `_fullscreen_selection`, widget name `"fullscreen"`. Separate the persistence: `set_fullscreen()` + an explicit `save_to_file()` call, which already exists at line 22.

## `ArtAttack/screen_layout.h`

_1 finding: 1 medium_

#### 1. The viewport abstraction is hardwired to 'players' and to exactly four split-screen arrangements

`ArtAttack/screen_layout.h:4-10` — **medium** · `design`

`enum class screen_layout { ONE_PLAYER, TWO_PLAYER, THREE_PLAYER, FOUR_PLAYER }` is the only vocabulary the viewport service has, and it propagates through the whole API: `apply_player_viewport(int player_num)`, `get_player_viewport(int player_num)`, `get_camera_adjusted_player_viewport_rect(int player_num, …)`, `get_player_count_from_layout` (ViewportManager.h:27-52). The game sets it from a menu choice and `Level::draw_zoom_out_level_component` flips it mid-render (Level.cpp:619).

A reusable engine cannot express a picture-in-picture minimap, a security-camera view, a render-to-texture pass or a 6-player layout with this API, because a viewport is *defined* as 'the thing player N looks through'. This is game-specific vocabulary welded into what should be the platform layer.

**Fix:** Model views generically: a `ViewSet` of indexed `View { Viewport rect; Camera camera; }` with `add_view` / `view(i)` / `count()`. Split-screen for N players becomes a game-side helper that populates a ViewSet from a generic layout table; the word 'player' disappears from the platform layer.

## `ArtAttack/SoundBank.h`

_5 findings: 3 medium, 2 low_

#### 1. SoundBank conflates immutable asset data with runtime voices, forcing per-team/per-player-slot voice names into the data file

`ArtAttack/SoundBank.h:12-50` — **medium** · `design`

`SoundBank` owns both a `unique_ptr<WaveBank>` (an immutable asset, line 39) and `map<string, unique_ptr<SoundEffectInstance>> _sound_effect_instances` (mutable runtime voices, line 41), keyed by name. Because there is no voice pool, the game must pre-declare one instance per emitter BY NAME. I read sounds/sound_bank_1.json: lines 32-127 declare `sprayer_a0..a3`, `sprayer_b0..b3`, `roller_a0..b3`, `mister_a0..b3` — the cross product of weapon x team x player slot, 24 hand-written entries.

Supporting a fifth player, a third team, or a fourth weapon means editing a JSON asset plus the code tables that mirror it. `decode_sound_effect_instances_json` (SoundBank.cpp:99-148) additionally creates an instance for EVERY wave when `create_effect_instance_for_each_wave` is true (it is, line 29 of the JSON), so all 24 waves get voices whether or not anything plays them — 48 live SoundEffectInstances at startup.

**Fix:** Split the concepts. `SoundAsset` = immutable wave data, shared and const. `AudioSystem` = runtime, owning a voice pool: `VoiceHandle play(SoundId, const PlayParams&)`, `stop(VoiceHandle)`, with voice stealing when exhausted. An emitter holds a handle acquired at fire time; nobody names a voice, and the data file lists sounds only.

#### 2. No mixer or bus concept: music is just a looping sound effect and there is no master or category volume

`ArtAttack/SoundBank.h:20-32` — **medium** · `design`

The whole audio API is per-instance: `play_effect(name, loop, volume, pitch, pan)`, `set_effect_volume(name, volume)`. Music goes through the identical path — `Level::update` does `this->_sound_bank->play_effect(this->_music_name, true, this->_music_volume);` (Level.cpp:73) with the track name and volume stored as plain Level members, and menus do the same with hardcoded constants.

I grepped the entire first-party tree for `SetMasterVolume` — zero hits — and there is no category/bus anywhere. An Options screen therefore physically cannot offer a working volume slider without touching every call site, and music is held fully decoded in a wave bank rather than streamed.

**Fix:** Add buses (`Master`, `Music`, `SFX`, `UI`), each with a gain multiplied into every routed voice, and persist the gains through the settings store. Play music through a streaming path (DirectXTK `SoundStreamInstance`) owned by a small `MusicPlayer` with `play(track, fade)` / `stop(fade)`, so Level and every menu page stop carrying a track name and a magic volume constant.

#### 3. const is meaningless on SoundBank: const methods start and stop playback and hand out mutable pointers to owned state

`ArtAttack/SoundBank.h:20-35` — **medium** · `const-correctness`

Merged from 2 candidates. `play_wave`, `play_effect`, `stop_effect`, `pause_effect`, `resume_effect`, `set_effect_volume/pitch/pan` are all declared `const` (SoundBank.h:20-30) yet every one mutates the audio objects the class owns. They get away with it because `get_sound_effect_instance(...) const` (SoundBank.cpp:74-84) returns a NON-const `SoundEffectInstance*` obtained from `_sound_effect_instances.at(...).get()` — a const member handing out a mutable handle to its own state.

The fiction is copied wholesale into `SoundBankObject` (all 12 methods const, SoundBankObject.h:16-30) and then propagates outward: `void Level::stop_music() const` (Level.cpp:61-64) is a const member that stops audio. `const` in this codebase therefore carries no information — a reader cannot use it to reason about what a call does, and the compiler cannot help.

**Fix:** Drop `const` from every method that changes playback state, and give `get_sound_effect_instance` a const overload returning `const SoundEffectInstance*` plus a non-const overload for the mutable pointer. If a component needs to trigger audio from a const context, that is the const context's bug.

#### 4. Abbreviation-alias accessors (get_sb, get_sei) are pure forwarders with no external callers

`ArtAttack/SoundBank.h:34-35` — **low** · `design`

DirectX::SoundEffectInstance* get_sound_effect_instance(const std::string&) const;
    DirectX::SoundEffectInstance* get_sei(const std::string&) const;   // identical

mirrored in SoundBankObject.h:13-14 (`get_sound_bank`/`get_sb`) and :29-30. `SoundBankObject::get_sb` is literally `return this->get_sound_bank();` and `get_sei` is `return this->get_sound_effect_instance(...);`.

I grepped all first-party files: `SoundBank::get_sei` (SoundBank.cpp:85) and `SoundBankObject::get_sei` (SoundBankObject.cpp:69) have ZERO callers anywhere. `get_sb` is called only from inside SoundBankObject.cpp's own forwarders. Four declarations exist for nothing, and they leak `DirectX::SoundEffectInstance*` out of the abstraction — the one thing that ties consumers to DirectXTK.

**Fix:** Delete `get_sei` at both declaration sites and `get_sb` (fold it into `get_sound_bank`, or better into a cached member per the performance finding). Also drop `get_sound_effect_instance` from both public/protected surfaces.

#### 5. _wave_names is effectively a parameter promoted to a member

`ArtAttack/SoundBank.h:40` — **low** · `design`

`std::vector<std::string> _wave_names;` is assigned exactly once, at SoundBank.cpp:168 (`this->_wave_names = decode_wave_names_json(waves);`) and read exactly once, at SoundBank.cpp:107 (`for (auto& wave : this->_wave_names)`) from `decode_sound_effect_instances_json`, which is called on the very next statement (line 169) inside the same function. Nothing else in the codebase touches it. It keeps the 24 wave-name strings from sounds/sound_bank_1.json alive for the whole process lifetime for no reason, and it is the only thing preventing `decode_sound_effect_instances_json` from being `static` like its sibling `decode_wave_names_json` already is.

**Fix:** Make it a local in `load_from_json` and pass it to `decode_sound_effect_instances_json(json, wave_names, create_for_each)`, which then becomes static.

## `ArtAttack/SoundBankObject.cpp`

_1 finding: 1 medium_

#### 1. Every audio call re-resolves the SoundBank by string through ResourceManager — two tree lookups per sound operation

`ArtAttack/SoundBankObject.cpp:14-21` — **medium** · `performance`

SoundBank* SoundBankObject::get_sound_bank() const
    { return this->_resource_manager->get_sound_bank(this->_sound_bank_name); }

All twelve wrappers (SoundBankObject.cpp:23-72) call `get_sb()` individually, so every `play_wave`/`play_effect`/`get_effect_state` first walks `ResourceManager::_sound_banks` — a `std::map<std::string, ...>` and, via `operator[]`, a MUTATING call, which is also the concurrency finding — and then walks `SoundBank::_sound_effect_instances` (48 entries per sound_bank_1.json). Two string-keyed red-black tree traversals per sound operation, for a pointer that is fixed at construction.

`Level` and `Weapon` already do the right thing and cache the pointer once (Level.cpp:59, Weapon.cpp). `SoundBankObject` is the outlier.

**Fix:** Resolve once in the constructor (and in `set_sound_bank_name`) into a `SoundBank*` member; `get_sound_bank()` becomes a member read.

## `ArtAttack/SoundBankObject.h`

_3 findings: 3 medium_

#### 1. SoundBankObject is inheritance-as-implementation-reuse: 12 one-line forwarders grafted onto four UI page classes, public base with a non-virtual destructor

`ArtAttack/SoundBankObject.h:7-36` — **medium** · `design`

Merged from 3 candidates. The whole class is a `std::string` + a `ResourceManager*` plus twelve protected members that each forward one call. SoundBankObject.cpp:23-72 is 50 lines of nothing but:

    void SoundBankObject::play_wave(const std::string& wave_name, float volume, float pitch, float pan) const
    { this->get_sb()->play_wave(wave_name, volume, pitch, pan); }

Every signature is a second copy of the corresponding `SoundBank` signature, so any API change is a two-file edit.

It is inherited PUBLICLY by four unrelated UI classes, which I verified by grep:
  MainMenu.h:110    class MainMenuPage : public MenuPage, public SoundBankObject
  PauseMenu.h:44    class PauseMenuPage : public MenuPage, public MenuHighlight, public SoundBankObject
  EndMenu.h:42      class EndMenuPage : public MenuPage, public MenuHighlight, public SoundBankObject
  ResultsMenu.h:64  class ResultsMenuPage : public MenuPage, public SoundBankObject

Its entire interface is `protected`, so it exists solely to be inherited — the `is-a` relation public inheritance advertises is false (a menu page is not a sound bank object). It declares no destructor, so it gets a public non-virtual one and `delete static_cast<SoundBankObject*>(page)` compiles as UB. Safe today only because pages are owned as `unique_ptr<State>` and `State` has a virtual destructor.

**Fix:** Composition: give the page a member holding the resolved `SoundBank*` (or an `AudioSystem&`) and call `_audio->play_effect(...)`. That deletes SoundBankObject.cpp entirely and removes a base class from four multiple-inheritance hierarchies. If the mixin survives, at minimum make its destructor `protected: ~SoundBankObject() = default;`.

#### 2. Default constructors on SoundBankObject and SoundBank leave dependencies null with no way to repair them

`ArtAttack/SoundBankObject.h:10-11, 33-35` — **medium** · `design`

Merged from 4 candidates.

`SoundBankObject() = default;` (SoundBankObject.h:10) leaves `_resource_manager == nullptr` (line 35). Every method funnels through `get_sound_bank()` (SoundBankObject.cpp:14-17), which is `return this->_resource_manager->get_sound_bank(...)` with no null test. The class provides `set_sound_bank_name` (line 32) but NO setter for the resource manager, so a default-constructed object can never be made valid.

`SoundBank() = default;` (SoundBank.h:15) is the same: `_wave_bank` stays null (line 39) while `play_wave` does `_wave_bank->Play(...)` (SoundBank.cpp:21) and `decode_sound_effect_instances_json` does `_wave_bank->CreateInstance(...)` (line 113). No setter exists.

Even the intended path is two-phase: `SoundBank(std::move(wb))` then a separate `sb->load_from_json(...)` (ResourceLoader.cpp:161-164), so the object exists with no waves in between.

All four current derived classes pass both arguments, so this is latent rather than live — but it is a trap left armed. The half-initialised case composes badly with the `operator[]` finding: a valid manager plus the default `_sound_bank_name == ""` makes `get_sound_bank("")` INSERT an empty-named entry and return nullptr.

Minor in the same header: `std::string _sound_bank_name = "";` (line 34) — the default constructor already yields an empty string.

**Fix:** Delete both `= default` constructors and the `= ""` initialiser. Take `ResourceManager&` so null is not expressible, and make SoundBank construction total via a factory that returns a fully-loaded object or fails.

#### 3. Cryptic acronym aliases `get_sb()` and `get_sei()` duplicate the spelled-out getters, and both forms are in live use

`ArtAttack/SoundBankObject.h:65-66, 81-82` — **medium** · `naming` · confidence: certain

`SoundBankObject.h:65-66` declares both `SoundBank* get_sound_bank() const;` and `SoundBank* get_sb() const;`. Lines 81-82 do the same for `get_sound_effect_instance()` / `get_sei()`. `SoundBank.h:34-35` repeats the `get_sound_effect_instance` / `get_sei` pair. These are not deprecated leftovers - call-site counts across the .cpp files are `get_sb()` 12 vs `get_sound_bank()` 8, and `get_sei()` 2 vs `get_sound_effect_instance()` 14. So a reader must learn both spellings, and `sei` is an acronym that appears nowhere else in 28k lines.

**Fix:** Delete `get_sb()` and `get_sei()`; rewrite their 14 call sites to the full names. If the motivation was line length, that is what a local `auto* bank = get_sound_bank();` is for.

## `ArtAttack/SpriteFrame.h`

_3 findings: 2 medium, 1 low_

#### 1. SpriteFrame parses origin and rotated-packing from the atlas JSON and then throws both away; _source_rectangle2 is never even written

`ArtAttack/SpriteFrame.h:19-31` — **medium** · `correctness`

`SpriteSheet::decode_sprite_frames_json` (SpriteSheet.cpp:34-44) carefully parses two optional fields and passes them to the constructor, which stores them (SpriteFrame.cpp:11-12, 18-19). Nothing ever reads them back — the class's only accessor is `get_source_rectangle()` (SpriteFrame.h:19), there is no `get_origin()` or `is_rotated()`, and grep finds no other use of `_origin`/`_rotated` anywhere.

So an atlas entry marked `"rotated": true` — meaning the packer stored it turned 90 degrees to save space — is drawn unrotated, i.e. visibly wrong, with no warning. The schema is live: sprite_sheet_1.json:141 already carries a `"rotated": false` entry, so the first `true` produces a corrupt sprite. Per-frame authored pivots are likewise ignored, which is part of why `Weapon` and `Drawer` each hand-roll a `calculate_sprite_origin`.

Separately, `MattMath::RectangleI _source_rectangle2` (line 23) is declared, default-initialised to `ZERO`, and never written by either constructor or either `set_source_rectangle` overload (SpriteFrame.cpp:28-38). It is a half-finished duplicate representation; the `2` suffix is the tell. The second constructor (`SpriteFrame(position, size, ...)`, SpriteFrame.h:14-18) also has no callers — only the `RectangleI` one is used, at SpriteSheet.cpp:43.

**Fix:** Either implement or delete. To implement: expose `get_origin()`/`is_rotated()`, use the pivot as the default draw origin, and in the draw path add -pi/2 to the rotation and swap the destination extents when rotated. To delete: strip `_origin`, `_rotated`, the unused constructor, the JSON parsing at SpriteSheet.cpp:34-42, and `_source_rectangle2`. Silently ignoring data you bothered to parse is worse than not parsing it.

#### 2. SpriteFrame stores three fields it never exposes, silently discarding per-frame origin and rotation from the atlas JSON

`ArtAttack/SpriteFrame.h:21-25` — **medium** · `dead-code` · confidence: certain

`SpriteFrame` has exactly one accessor, `get_source_rectangle()` (SpriteFrame.h:19). Its private members `_origin` (:24) and `_rotated` (:25) are written in both constructors (`SpriteFrame.cpp:11-12, 18-19`) and never read by anything. `_source_rectangle2` (:23) is never written *or* read — grep returns one hit, the declaration. Upstream, `SpriteSheet.cpp:27-44` goes to the trouble of parsing `frame["origin"]["x"]`, `frame["origin"]["y"]` and `frame["rotated"]` out of `sprite_sheet_1.json` and passing them into the constructor. So the sprite-atlas format supports rotated/offset frames, the loader reads them, and the data is dropped on the floor — a second dead data pipeline in the same codebase.

**Fix:** Delete `_source_rectangle2`. Then either add `get_origin()`/`is_rotated()` and honour them in SpriteSheet's draw calls (which is what the atlas format implies), or delete `_origin`/`_rotated` and stop parsing them in SpriteSheet.cpp:27-44.

#### 3. `_source_rectangle2` - a numeric-suffix placeholder name shipped as a member

`ArtAttack/SpriteFrame.h:21-23` — **low** · `naming` · confidence: certain

`SpriteFrame.h:21-23`:
```
RECT _source_rectangle = { 0, 0, 0, 0 };

MattMath::RectangleI _source_rectangle2 = MattMath::RectangleI::ZERO;
```
Two members holding the same rectangle in two representations, the second distinguished only by the digit `2`. `get_source_rectangle()` (line 19) returns the `RECT` one; `_source_rectangle2` is written by `set_source_rectangle` (27-30) and never read outside. The `2` tells a reader nothing about which to use or why both exist.
Similar numeric-placeholder naming in the assets: `textures/sprite_sheet_1.json` frames `projectile_1`, `projectile_2`, `projectile_3`, `cloud_1`, `cloud_2`, `player_1_right`, `player_2_right`, `splash_1`, `square_white_4`, `square_white_32` - the trailing numbers mean size in some cases and variant index in others.

**Fix:** If both representations are genuinely needed, name them for their type/purpose: `_source_rect_win32` and `_source_rect` (or store only `MattMath::RectangleI` and convert on demand in `get_source_rectangle`). Given `_source_rectangle2` appears to be write-only, deleting it is likely correct - verify against `SpriteFrame.cpp` first.

## `ArtAttack/State.h`

_2 findings: 1 medium, 1 low_

#### 1. The entire codebase contains exactly one forward declaration - the root cause of the header coupling

`ArtAttack/State.h:4` — **medium** · `design` · confidence: certain

`class StateContext;` at State.h:4 is the only forward declaration in all 105 headers (verified by grep for a leading `class X;` pattern). Everything else includes the full definition, whether it needs it or not. The measurable result: mean transitive header closure per TU is 21 headers; Main.cpp reaches 105 and GameStates.cpp 103; MattMath.h and shape_type.h reach 68 of 81 TUs, SpriteFrame.h/AnimationStrip.h/Colour.h 55-58, SoundBank.h and LevelLoadedInfo.h 53-56, ResourceManager.h 52. Editing SpriteFrame.h - a small value type - rebuilds two thirds of the project. The codebase already proves it knows how (State.h works fine), it just never applies the technique anywhere else.

**Fix:** Adopt the rule 'include only what the header's declarations require by value/base; forward-declare everything used only by pointer or reference'. The highest-leverage targets are GameData.h, ResourceManager.h, Level.h (17 includes), Player.h (11), LevelBuilder.h (10) and Weapon.h (9). A single fwd.h for the DirectXTK types used by pointer (SpriteBatch, SpriteFont, GamePad, CommonStates) covers most of the remainder.

#### 2. set_context is public with one legitimate caller, get_context() const hands out a mutable pointer, and neither class suppresses copy/move

`ArtAttack/State.h:14-18` — **low** · `design`

`void set_context(StateContext* context);` is public (State.h:14). A grep across all first-party files shows exactly one caller: `StateContext::transition_to` (StateContext.cpp:23). Any code holding a `State*` can silently re-parent a state to a different context.

`StateContext* get_context() const;` (State.h:16, protected — several reviewers wrongly called it public) is a const member returning a **non-const** pointer, so a `const State` can call `get_context()->transition_to(...)` and replace itself; the const is meaningless.

Neither `State` nor `StateContext` deletes copy or move, so the invariant "`_context` points at the object whose `_state` unique_ptr holds me" has no type-system protection. `Game` then explicitly opts in with `Game(Game&&) = default; Game& operator=(Game&&) = default;` (Game.h:22-23) — moving a `Game` would move the `StateContext` base's unique_ptr to a new address while the state's `_context` still pointed at the moved-from husk, and would leave `_device_resources->RegisterDeviceNotify(this)` (Game.cpp:20) pointing at that husk too. `Game` is `final` and constructed once (Main.cpp), so the move operations exist for no reason and are wrong.

**Fix:** Make `set_context` private with `friend class StateContext;`, or remove it and pass the context to the `State` constructor. Return `const StateContext*` from the const overload. Delete copy and move on both `State` and `StateContext`, and remove `Game(Game&&) = default;` / `operator=(Game&&) = default;` — a device-notify registrant is not movable.

## `ArtAttack/Structure.cpp`

_1 finding: 1 medium_

#### 1. Structure::is_colliding unconditionally returns false — the collision contract is asymmetric and undiscoverable

`ArtAttack/Structure.cpp:43-50` — **medium** · `design`

```cpp
bool Structure::is_colliding(const ICollisionGameObject* other) const { return false; }
void Structure::on_collision(const ICollisionGameObject* other) { /* do nothing */ }
```
Structures — the majority of every level's collision objects, including StructurePaintable which inherits this `is_colliding` — report that they never collide with anything. All structure collision behaviour lives in the *other* participant. `StructurePaintable` then *does* override `on_collision` (StructurePaintable.cpp:64) and depends on the projectile's `is_colliding` returning true for it.

So whether a collision is noticed depends entirely on which participant is the loop's initiator, and the loops are written as though `is_colliding` were symmetric — Level.cpp:259-273 tests `object->is_colliding(player)` and :277-292 tests both orderings, and for structures both are dead. Any future object type whose `is_colliding` filter does not name structures will pass through every wall in the level with no diagnostic.

`other` is also an unused parameter in both functions (C4100 under /W4).

The interface itself is the problem: `ICollisionGameObject::is_colliding` (ICollisionGameObject.h:12) makes every implementer answer a question about geometry, which is why the identical AABB-then-narrow-phase body is copy-pasted in PaintTile.cpp:84-109, Player.cpp:148-185 and every Projectile subclass.

**Fix:** `is_colliding` belongs on a `Collider` (shape + layer mask) resolved once by a CollisionSystem, not as a virtual on every game object. Response should be a handler keyed on the layer pair, called exactly once per pair with a documented (a,b) ordering. Failing that, at minimum implement `Structure::is_colliding` properly so the contract is symmetric.

## `ArtAttack/Structure.h`

_2 findings: 1 medium, 1 low_

#### 1. Shape ownership is unstatable from the signature: a raw const Shape* that is silently cloned, with no null check

`ArtAttack/Structure.h:14` — **medium** · `design`

`Structure`'s constructor takes `const MattMath::Shape* collision_shape` (Structure.h:14) and quietly deep-copies it in the member-init list: `_collision_shape(collision_shape->clone())` (Structure.cpp:22). Nothing in the signature says whether the callee retains, adopts or copies, and there is no null check before `->clone()`.

Because the contract is invisible, callers pass the address of stack locals and it only works by luck: LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:62 passes `&rectangle` (local declared at :37), :136 passes `&rectangle` (local at :80), :173 passes `&triangle` (local at :161). Each dies at the end of `build_collision_object`. If the constructor ever stops cloning, or a subclass caches the argument, every structure in every level holds a dangling `Shape*` and nothing at the call site would look wrong. `StructurePaintable` forwards the same raw pointer (StructurePaintable.h:32 → .cpp:25).

Note also that LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:61-62 passes the *same* rectangle as both the sprite rectangle and the collision shape, while :172-173 passes a bounding box and a triangle — the API gives no hint that these may legitimately differ, which is precisely what makes the StructurePaintable face-mapping bug possible (it reads tile positions from `get_rectangle()` and the face set from `get_shape()`).

**Fix:** Make the contract part of the type: `const MattMath::Shape& collision_shape` (clones internally, cannot be null) or `std::unique_ptr<MattMath::Shape>` (caller gives it up). The reference form fits the builder, which always has a stack shape it wants copied. Also rename `Structure::get_rectangle()` to `get_sprite_rectangle()`.

#### 2. Level objects inherit their rendering implementation instead of composing a sprite, and polymorphic bases allow slicing assignment

`ArtAttack/Structure.h:7` — **low** · `design`

`class Structure : public TextureObject, public ICollisionGameObject` (Structure.h:7) and `class PaintTile final : public TextureObject, public ICollisionGameObject` (PaintTile.h:51) both inherit an *implementation* base (TextureObject → SpriteSheetObject → DrawObject) alongside an interface; `PaintTileSplash : public AnimationObject, public IGameObject` (PaintTile.h:23) does the same with the other rendering base.

Consequences visible here: `Structure` inherits five protected `draw` overloads it doesn't want (TextureObject.h:19-32) and must disambiguate with `this->TextureObject::draw(...)` (Structure.cpp:33, PaintTile.cpp:52/72); an object cannot have two sprites, or a sprite *and* an animation, without inheriting the same base twice; and `Structure`'s `_sprite_rectangle` doubles as both draw geometry and visibility bounds (Structure.cpp:39-42), so visual and collision extents cannot diverge.

Separately, none of these polymorphic bases suppresses assignment. `Structure` is a public base of `StructurePaintable`, declares no copy/move operations, and so gets a public implicit move-assignment — meaning `Structure& a = ...; a = std::move(b);` on two references that are actually StructurePaintables compiles and silently slices, stealing the collision shape and discarding `_paint_tiles`/`_team_colours`/`_sound_bank`. Same hole in `IGameObject` (IGameObject.h:6-14), `ICollisionGameObject` (ICollisionGameObject.h:8-17), `IPaintableGameObject` (IPaintableGameObject.h:10-15) and `DrawObject` (DrawObject.h:9-11), all of which have a public defaulted virtual destructor and no suppressed assignment. Not currently exercised, but free to close.

**Fix:** Compose rather than inherit: `Structure` should *hold* a `Sprite` and a `Collider`, not *be* a TextureObject. Meanwhile give every polymorphic base the standard non-sliceable shape (protected copy/move, public virtual dtor).

## `ArtAttack/StructureRamp.cpp`

_2 findings: 1 medium, 1 low_

#### 1. Six ramp source files are 100% commented out yet still compiled and listed in the vcxproj

`ArtAttack/StructureRamp.cpp:1-26` — **medium** · `dead-code` · confidence: certain

`StructureRamp.h/.cpp`, `StructureRampLeft.h/.cpp`, `StructureRampRight.h/.cpp` contain nothing but `//`-prefixed lines (every line of all six files except `#include "pch.h"` at the top of each .cpp). They are still declared in `ArtAttack/ArtAttack.vcxproj:252-254` (`<ClInclude>`) and `:348-350` (`<ClCompile>`), and in `ArtAttack.vcxproj.filters`. Every build therefore compiles three empty translation units. `LevelObjectBuilder.h:10-11` also carries the corresponding `//#include "StructureRampLeft.h"` / `//#include "StructureRampRight.h"` lines. Ramps are actually built as plain `Structure` with a `TriangleRightAxisAligned` in `LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:144-176`, so the class hierarchy these files describe was abandoned.

**Fix:** Delete all six files and their vcxproj/filters entries and the two commented includes in LevelObjectBuilder.h. If the ramp abstraction is wanted later, recover it from git history — that is what history is for.

#### 2. Six StructureRamp files are 100% commented out but still compiled and still listed in the vcxproj

`ArtAttack/StructureRamp.cpp:1-27` — **low** · `design` · confidence: certain

`StructureRamp.cpp` (27 lines), `StructureRamp.h` (23), `StructureRampLeft.cpp` (20), `StructureRampLeft.h` (21), `StructureRampRight.cpp` (20), `StructureRampRight.h` (21) contain nothing but `#include "pch.h"` followed by the entire class commented out with `//`. They are still in `ArtAttack.vcxproj`, so three empty translation units are compiled every build. The live ramp code is elsewhere: `LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:227-259` builds ramps as a plain `Structure` with a `TriangleRightAxisAligned` shape and a `STRUCTURE_RAMP_LEFT/RIGHT` enum tag, and `StructureRampLeft`/`Right` were themselves already duplicate-by-copy — identical ctors differing only in which enum they pass to `StructureRamp`.

This matters for the reusable-engine goal: a fresh reader has to work out which of the two ramp representations is real.

**Fix:** Delete all six files and their `<ClCompile>`/`<ClInclude>` entries from ArtAttack.vcxproj. If the class is wanted later, git history has it. If ramps do become first-class, the Left/Right split should be one class with a `bool` or an axis enum, not two subclasses that differ by one constructor argument.

## `ArtAttack/StructureRamp.h`

_3 findings: 1 medium, 2 low_

#### 1. Six files named after classes that do not exist - StructureRamp/Left/Right are 100% commented out but still in the vcxproj

`ArtAttack/StructureRamp.h:1-23` — **medium** · `design` · confidence: certain

`StructureRamp.h` (23 lines), `StructureRamp.cpp` (26), `StructureRampLeft.h` (21), `StructureRampLeft.cpp` (20), `StructureRampRight.h` (21), `StructureRampRight.cpp` (20). I counted non-comment non-blank lines: 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0. There is no `StructureRamp` class anywhere; ramps are actually built as plain `Structure` with a `TriangleRightAxisAligned` shape at `LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:144-177`. All six files are listed in `ArtAttack.vcxproj:252-254` and `:348-350`, so the build compiles six empty translation units and anyone browsing Solution Explorer sees a ramp class hierarchy that is fiction. Note the JSON level format at `LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:144` also keys on `type == "StructureRamp"`, a type name with no corresponding class.

**Fix:** Delete all six files and their vcxproj entries. If ramps deserve a class later, add it then. Meanwhile rename the JSON discriminator from `"StructureRamp"` to something honest like `"ramp"`, since the JSON `type` strings elsewhere (`"Structure"`, `"StructurePaintable"`, `"Visual"`) are C++ class names and this one is not.

#### 2. Three ramp classes are 100% commented out but still in the build, while ramps are faked as a Structure carrying an enum tag

`ArtAttack/StructureRamp.h:1-24` — **low** · `design`

StructureRamp.h is entirely commented out (all 23 lines) and StructureRamp.cpp is a lone `#include "pch.h"` followed by 26 commented lines. StructureRampLeft.h/.cpp and StructureRampRight.h/.cpp are the same. Yet all six files are still listed in ArtAttack.vcxproj (lines 252-254 and 348-350), and LevelObjectBuilder.h:10-11 still carries their commented-out includes.

Meanwhile the real ramp construction (LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:144-177) builds a plain `Structure` from a `TriangleRightAxisAligned` and distinguishes ramp-ness only by `collision_object_type::STRUCTURE_RAMP_LEFT/RIGHT`. So "ramp" is a behavioural variant expressed as an enum tag on a base class, which forces `Player::on_collision` to branch on the tag (Player.cpp:236-238) to get ramp movement. The one genuinely ramp-specific behaviour, `get_gradient()`, exists only in the commented-out code (StructureRamp.cpp:23-27).

This is also the direct cause of the projectiles-pass-through-ramps bug reported separately.

**Fix:** Pick one: delete the six dead files and their vcxproj entries, or finish the type and give it `get_gradient()`/`get_surface_normal()` so ramp behaviour is polymorphic instead of an enum branch inside Player. Given the wider collision_object_type problem, the right destination is a slope/material property on the collider.

#### 3. Six fully commented-out game-object files are still compiled by the project

`ArtAttack/StructureRamp.h:1-8 (and StructureRamp.cpp, StructureRampLeft.*, StructureRampRight.*)` — **low** · `design` · confidence: certain

`StructureRamp.h`, `StructureRampLeft.h`, `StructureRampRight.h` contain zero non-comment lines; the three matching .cpp files contain exactly one each (the `#include "pch.h"`). All six are still listed in `ArtAttack.vcxproj` (ClInclude at lines 252-254, ClCompile at 348-350), so three empty TUs are compiled every build. `LevelObjectBuilder.h:10-11` still carries the commented-out includes.

Meanwhile ramps *are* shipped, as plain `Structure` with a `TriangleRightAxisAligned` shape and a `STRUCTURE_RAMP_LEFT/RIGHT` enum tag (LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:144-177) — so the enum values in the engine-level `collision_object_type.h:9-10, 84-88` exist to tag objects whose dedicated classes were abandoned. The dead-class graveyard makes the engine/game split harder to reason about because it is unclear which abstractions are live.

**Fix:** Delete the six files and their vcxproj entries. If ramps stay as tagged `Structure`s, drop `STRUCTURE_RAMP_LEFT/RIGHT` and `is_structure_ramp()` from the shared enum in favour of the shape type (which already distinguishes triangles).

## `ArtAttack/TeamColour.cpp`

_3 findings: 2 medium, 1 low_

#### 1. throw std::exception("literal") is an MSVC-only extension, used at 58 sites — a hard portability wall for the engine

`ArtAttack/TeamColour.cpp:22` — **medium** · `portability`

`default: throw std::exception("Invalid team.");` The standard `std::exception` has **no `const char*` constructor**; the one-argument form is an MSVC extension. A grep for `throw std::exception` across the first-party tree returns **58** occurrences, including on live paths: this one is reached from `PaintTile::on_collision` (PaintTile.cpp:39-64) and `PlayerBuilder` (PlayerBuilder.cpp:50, 56), and `Level::update_level_logic` uses it for out-of-bounds (Level.cpp:312, 319).

For a project whose stated goal is a reusable 2D engine, none of this compiles on gcc/clang. Interestingly the newest code in the repo already knows better — `RectangleRotated::set_x_axis` (MattMath.cpp:4365) throws `std::invalid_argument`, so the correct pattern exists and just has not been applied backwards.

Separately, this particular throw is questionable on its merits: `player_team` has only A, B and NONE, and NONE is a legitimate value (`PaintTile::_team` defaults to it), so "invalid team" is a programming error rather than a runtime condition.

**Fix:** Replace all 58 with `std::runtime_error` / `std::invalid_argument` / `std::logic_error` taking `std::string`, which compile everywhere. For this specific function, decide once what NONE means: either it is a precondition violation (assert) or it has a defined neutral colour — currently it is treated as both, depending on which of the two same-named functions you call.

#### 2. rand() is never seeded anywhere in the project, so every random choice is identical on every launch

`ArtAttack/TeamColour.cpp:29` — **medium** · `correctness`

There are exactly three `rand()` call sites in the whole first-party tree — TeamColour.cpp:29, MainMenu.cpp:1521 (random weapon), MainMenu.cpp:1894 (random stage) — and a repo-wide grep for `srand` returns **zero** hits. `rand()` without seeding behaves as if `srand(1)` was called, so the team colour, the RANDOM_PRIMARY weapon roll and the random stage produce the exact same sequence on every run of the game.

Secondary issues at the same line: `rand() % n` is biased when `n` does not divide `RAND_MAX+1` (MSVC's `RAND_MAX` is only 32767), the global generator is not injectable so no test can control it, and `rand()` shares hidden global state with a codebase that runs a Windows thread pool.

**Fix:** Do not seed `rand()` — replace it. Put one `std::mt19937` in the engine, seeded once from `std::random_device`, behind `int random_int(int lo, int hi)` using `std::uniform_int_distribution`, and route all three call sites through it. An engine should own its RNG so gameplay is reproducible and testable.

#### 3. Two same-named team-to-colour lookups with opposite failure policies — but the divergent one is dead code

`ArtAttack/TeamColour.cpp:13-24, 58-70` — **low** · `correctness`

```cpp
// member, :13-24
const Colour& TeamColour::get_team_colour(player_team team) const {
    case A: return team_a;  case B: return team_b;
    default: throw std::exception("Invalid team.");     // loud failure on NONE
}
// static, :58-70
Colour TeamColourTools::get_team_colour(TeamColour team_colours, player_team team) {
    case A: ...;  case B: ...;
    default: return team_colours.team_a;                // silently reports team A
}
```
Identical name, identical inputs, opposite behaviour on `player_team::NONE`, which is a real enumerator (player_team.h:8) used for unassigned players and neutral paint. `get_team_colours` (:43-56) is a third policy again (silent BLUE_ORANGE fallback).

**Two reviewers escalated this to "NONE quietly counts as A is a scoring bug".** That is wrong: the static overload has zero callers, so no scoring path can reach it. It is dead-code inconsistency, not a live defect, hence `low`. The live member function's `throw` on NONE is the more interesting half — see the portability finding.

**Fix:** Delete `TeamColourTools::get_team_colour` and `get_team_colours` entirely. Keep one lookup, on the data type. Decide the NONE contract explicitly — for a palette lookup a neutral colour is the more useful answer than an exception, given `PaintTile::_team` defaults to NONE.

## `ArtAttack/Text.cpp`

_1 finding: 1 medium_

#### 1. Class Text exists only to widen the access of four setters, implemented as pointless forwarding overrides

`ArtAttack/Text.cpp:22-37` — **medium** · `design`

The entire class body is four one-line forwards:
```cpp
void Text::set_text(const std::string& text)      { this->TextObject::set_text(text); }
void Text::set_colour(const Colour& colour)       { this->TextObject::set_colour(colour); }
void Text::set_scale(float scale)                 { this->TextObject::set_scale(scale); }
void Text::set_position(const Vector2F& position) { this->TextObject::set_position(position); }
```
No state, no behaviour. The only semantic effect is that these four are `public` in `Text` (Text.h:21-24) while `protected` in `TextObject`/`DrawObject` (TextObject.h:31-34, DrawObject.h:27) — which is what lets `Level.cpp` call `_countdown_text->set_text(...)`.

The cause is that the mutators are `protected virtual` for no reason other than to make this access-widening override legal, and that virtualness then costs every drawable in the engine. `Text` also adds a layer to an already five-deep chain (`DrawObject` → `TextObject` → `Text` → `TextDropShadow` → `MTextDropShadow`).

(Correcting one reviewer: these are overrides of existing virtuals, so they do not add vtable slots — the cost is the pointless indirection and the extra layer, not extra entries.)

**Fix:** Replace the whole body with `using TextObject::set_text;` etc. and delete Text.cpp. Better: decide whether those setters should be public on `TextObject` in the first place — a text object you cannot set the text of is odd — and delete `Text` entirely, reparenting `TextDropShadow` and `MText` onto `TextObject`.

## `ArtAttack/TextObject.cpp`

_1 finding: 1 medium_

#### 1. SpriteFont's UTF-8 DrawString overload uses a per-font conversion buffer, and fonts are shared singletons drawn from every render thread

`ArtAttack/TextObject.cpp:27-62` — **medium** · `concurrency`

Both `TextObject::draw` overloads pass `this->_text.c_str()` — a `const char*` — which selects DirectXTK's UTF-8 `DrawString` overload (SpriteFont.h:51-55). That overload converts UTF-8 to UTF-16 into a scratch buffer owned by the font's pImpl, lazily allocated and grown on demand.

The buffer is per-`SpriteFont`, and fonts are shared singletons handed out by `ResourceManager`. Text drawing happens inside `draw_player_view_level`, which runs as one task per partition on the thread pool: `Level::draw_countdown_text`, `InterfaceGameplay::draw_timer`/`draw_respawn_timer` (InterfaceGameplay.cpp:156-198) and `DebugText::draw_debug_info` (DebugText.cpp:115-131) all call `DrawString` on the same font from different threads. Concurrent conversions would overwrite each other's buffer, and a grow would reallocate under another thread's feet.

I am marking this uncertain rather than confirmed: only the DirectXTK *header* is vendored here (packages/directxtk_desktop_2019.2023.10.31.1/include/SpriteFont.h), so I could confirm the const UTF-8 overloads exist and that only a `unique_ptr<Impl>` backs them, but I could not read the implementation to verify the shared-buffer claim in this tree. The threading exposure is confirmed; the library-internal mechanism is not.

**Fix:** Store text as `std::wstring` (or cache a converted wstring alongside `_text`, invalidated in `set_text`) and call the `wchar_t` overload, which does no shared-buffer conversion. That also removes a `MultiByteToWideChar` call from the hot path. Confirm against the DirectXTK source you are actually linking before deciding how urgent this is.

## `ArtAttack/TextureObject.cpp`

_2 findings: 1 medium, 1 low_

#### 1. TextureObject and AnimationObject duplicate the same five draw overloads

`ArtAttack/TextureObject.cpp:21-69` — **medium** · `design` · confidence: certain

`TextureObject::draw` ×5 (TextureObject.cpp:21-69) and `AnimationObject::draw` ×5 (AnimationObject.cpp:98-147) are the same 49 lines twice. The only real difference is the second argument handed to `SpriteSheet::draw`: `this->get_element_name()` vs `this->get_source_rectangle()`. The last three overloads in each class are byte-identical:

```cpp
void X::draw(SpriteBatch* sb, const RectangleF& r) const { this->draw(sb, r.get_rectangle_i()); }
void X::draw(SpriteBatch* sb, const RectangleF& r, const Camera& c) const
{ RectangleF rect = c.calculate_view_rectangle(r); this->draw(sb, rect); }
void X::draw(SpriteBatch* sb, const Vector2F& p, const Camera& c, float s) const
{ Vector2F vp = c.calculate_view_position(p); float vs = c.calculate_view_scale(s); this->draw(sb, vp, vs); }
```

Both classes derive from `SpriteSheetObject`, which is where this belongs.

**Fix:** Move the camera-to-view conversion overloads into `SpriteSheetObject` as non-virtual, expressed in terms of two pure-virtual primitives `draw_primitive(SpriteBatch*, const RectangleI&)` and `draw_primitive(SpriteBatch*, const Vector2F&, float)`. `TextureObject` and `AnimationObject` then implement one function each instead of five.

#### 2. Destination rects truncate position and size independently rather than rounding edges, giving seams and an asymmetry across x=0

`ArtAttack/TextureObject.cpp:35-39` — **low** · `correctness`

Everything textured funnels through:
```cpp
void TextureObject::draw(SpriteBatch* sprite_batch, const RectangleF& destination_rectangle) const
{
	this->draw(sprite_batch, destination_rectangle.get_rectangle_i());
}
```
`RectangleF::get_rectangle_i()` (MattMath.cpp:823-829) is four independent `static_cast<int>` — truncation toward zero, not floor — and `RectangleI::get_win_rect()` (MattMath.cpp:2043-2052) then reconstitutes edges as `right = x + width`. Truncating origin and extent separately is the classic tiling defect: two abutting tiles at `x=10.6,w=4.5` and `x=15.1,w=4.5` become `[10,14]` and `[15,19]`, a 1-pixel gap. And because truncation is toward zero rather than floor, the mapping is not uniform across x=0, so a sprite scrolling left across the origin jumps a pixel.

Same pattern at AnimationObject.cpp:44-48, Drawer.cpp:42-53, and the four HUD rects in InterfaceGameplay.cpp.

I am grading this low rather than medium: the reviewers asserted visible shimmering seams across every painted surface, which depends on the paint grid producing fractional edges and which I did not verify. The rounding defect itself is unambiguous.

**Fix:** Round the *edges*, not the position and size, so abutting tiles share an edge whenever their float edges coincide:
```cpp
inline RECT to_pixel_rect(const RectangleF& r) {
    return { std::lround(r.x), std::lround(r.y), std::lround(r.x + r.width), std::lround(r.y + r.height) };
}
```
Put it on `RectangleF` and route every destination-rect conversion through it. Alternatively use the float position + scale form of `SpriteBatch::Draw` and preserve sub-pixel motion entirely.

## `ArtAttack/textures/old textures/bucket.dds`

_1 finding: 1 medium_

#### 1. Roughly 20 MB of superseded and source-only assets are tracked, including four parallel 'unused' directories

`ArtAttack/textures/old textures/bucket.dds:1` — **medium** · `repo-hygiene` · confidence: certain

`ResourceLoader::load_textures()` (ResourceLoader.cpp:17-20) loads exactly one thing: `./textures/sprite_sheet_1.dds` (+ `.json`). Everything else under the asset tree is dead weight tracked in git:
- `ArtAttack/textures/old textures/` — 41 `.dds` + matching `.png` pairs, 8.3 MB, superseded by the atlas.
- `ArtAttack/textures/sprite_sheet_1.png` (9.1 MB) and `sprite_sheet_1.xcf` (176 KB, GIMP project) sitting in the *runtime* asset directory next to the 2.2 MB `.dds` that is actually loaded.
- `ArtAttack/textures/new player textures/` — 13 PNGs, referenced by nothing.
- `ArtAttack/fonts/unuseed fonts/` [sic] — 24 `.spritefont` files, 2.4 MB. `ResourceLoader::load_fonts()` (ResourceLoader.cpp:21-33) loads 7, all from `fonts/`.
- `ArtAttack/levels/unused/` — base.json, level_0.json, structure_test_old.json, test_1.json.
- `ArtAttack/levels/*.pub` — three 113-121 KB Microsoft Publisher documents (352 KB total), one of them misspelled `turebulence.pub` against `turbulence.json`. Nothing in the code opens `.pub`.
- `ArtAttack/sounds/unused/wave_bank_1.json` — an obsolete copy of the sound-bank schema.
- `ArtAttack/save/save_data.txt` — a legacy two-line save format (`1920x1080` / `false`) alongside the live `save_data.json`. `directory_consts.h:11` only knows about the .json; nothing reads the .txt.

**Fix:** Delete all of the above from the working tree. Move genuine source art (the .xcf, the source PNGs) out of the runtime asset directory into an `art/` folder outside the copy-to-output path, or out of the repo entirely. A directory named 'unused' checked into a repo is a decision that was deferred rather than made.

## `ArtAttack/WeaponBuilder.cpp`

_1 finding: 1 medium_

#### 1. wep_type is both the factory discriminator and a constructor parameter, so a weapon can be built with the wrong type tag

`ArtAttack/WeaponBuilder.cpp:16-40` — **medium** · `api-design`

`build_weapon` switches on `type` to choose the class and then hands the same `type` back into the constructor, which stores it in `Weapon::_type` (Weapon.h:138):
```
case wep_type::SPRAYER:
    return std::make_unique<WeaponSprayer>(team, player_num, team_colour, type, player_center, resource_manager, dt);
```
Nothing prevents `WeaponSprayer(team, num, col, wep_type::ROLLER, ...)` from compiling and running - it would produce a sprayer that plays and stops `"roller_a0"`, two weapons fighting over one `SoundEffectInstance`, because `_type` is the sole key used by `get_sound_effect_instance_name()` (Weapon.cpp:258-277). The class already knows what it is: `WeaponSprayer` hardcodes `DETAILS_SPRAYER` (WeaponSprayer.cpp:20). The parameter is a redundant second source of truth for the same fact, kept in sync only because `WeaponBuilder` is the only caller and happens to pass what it dispatched on.

**Fix:** Drop `wep_type` from all five concrete constructors and have each subclass pass its own literal up to `Weapon` alongside its `DETAILS_*`, exactly as it already does for the details - or fold the tag into `WeaponDetails` so the two cannot disagree at all. Best: remove `_type` entirely once the audio configuration is data-driven; a class knows what it is.

## `ArtAttack/WeaponBuilder.h`

_1 finding: 1 medium_

#### 1. WeaponBuilder is a stateless static switch that must be edited to add a weapon, yet is heap-allocated and called through a pointer

`ArtAttack/WeaponBuilder.h:10-22` — **medium** · `design`

Three verified problems in 15 lines. (1) `build_weapon` is `static` (WeaponBuilder.h:14) and the class has no state, yet `PlayerBuilder.h:23` holds `std::unique_ptr<WeaponBuilder> _weapon_builder`, `PlayerBuilder.cpp:10` does `make_unique<WeaponBuilder>()`, and `PlayerBuilder.cpp:47` calls `this->_weapon_builder->build_weapon(...)` - an instance call to a static function through a heap-allocated empty object. (2) `WeaponBuilder.cpp:16-40` is a hardcoded switch over five `wep_type` values with `default: throw std::exception("Invalid weapon type")`; adding a weapon means editing this file, so the factory is closed for extension. (3) `WeaponBuilder.h:4-8` includes all five concrete weapon headers, so touching WeaponMister.h recompiles PlayerBuilder, Player and everything downstream.

The same anti-pattern is one level down: `ProjectileBuilder` (ProjectileBuilder.h:11-44) has zero data members, a defaulted ctor, one `const` method and one `static` method, yet every `Weapon` heap-allocates its own (`std::make_unique<ProjectileBuilder>()`, Weapon.cpp:32), stores it (Weapon.h:122), and hands it out as a raw borrowed pointer via `get_projectile_builder()` (Weapon.h:115, Weapon.cpp:488-491). `Weapon.h:11` includes ProjectileBuilder.h, which includes all five concrete projectile headers - so every TU that touches a weapon compiles the entire projectile hierarchy.

**Fix:** Replace `WeaponBuilder` with a registry the game populates: `register_weapon(id, factory_fn)` at startup (or from the weapons JSON), so concrete weapon headers are included only by the one TU that registers them. Make `ProjectileBuilder`'s functions free functions in a namespace and delete `_proj_builder`, `get_projectile_builder()` and the ProjectileBuilder.h include from Weapon.h. Both classes are namespaces wearing a class costume.

## `ArtAttack/WeaponDetails.h`

_2 findings: 1 medium, 1 low_

#### 1. SoundEffectInstanceWeaponDetails hardcodes 2 teams x 4 players as eight named string fields plus a throwing nested switch

`ArtAttack/WeaponDetails.h:21-33` — **medium** · `design`

```
struct SoundEffectInstanceWeaponDetails {
    std::string shoot_sound_name_a0 = ""; ... shoot_sound_name_b3 = "";
    const std::string& get_sound_name(player_team team, int index) const;
};
```
`WeaponDetails.cpp:4-40` resolves it with a `switch(team)` wrapping two `switch(index)` blocks - 36 lines, eight returns, three `throw std::exception`. The maximum player count is baked into *struct field names*, and the same 2x4 shape is repeated three times in weapon_consts.h (:58-68, :102-112, :136-146) where every entry is mechanically `"<weapon>_<team><index>"`. Supporting a fifth player or a third team means editing a struct, a 36-line accessor, and three positional aggregate tables in which one misplaced line silently gives team B's sound to team A. `int index` is an unchecked raw index in a public API with no documented range, and the function is called on *every* update of a sprayer/roller/mister (Weapon.cpp:238), so any bad index is an uncaught throw out of the render loop rather than a missing sound.

**Fix:** Delete the struct and the accessor. The naming convention is perfectly regular, so derive the name: `sound_id + '_' + team_char + std::to_string(index)`. Better, have the audio layer hand the weapon an opaque `SoundEffectInstance*` handle resolved once at construction, so no per-frame string naming happens at all and the 2x4 limit disappears with the three constant tables.

#### 2. Unscoped projectile_type enum leaks SPRAY/JET/BALL/MIST/ROLLING into the global namespace

`ArtAttack/WeaponDetails.h:45` — **low** · `modern-cpp`

`WeaponDetails` stores `projectile_type proj_type = SPRAY;`, and weapon_consts.h initialises it with bare global identifiers at :24 (`SPRAY`), :46 (`SPRAY`), :80 (`JET`), :96 (`ROLLING`), :124 (`MIST`), :158 (`BALL`). These come from `enum projectile_type` (Projectile.h:10-17), which is unscoped - the only unscoped enum in a codebase that otherwise uses `enum class` consistently (`wep_type`, `add_player_velocity` in this very header at :7, `rotation_origin`, `player_team`, `diffusion_type`). Five extremely generic names are injected into the global namespace of every TU that includes Weapon.h, and they implicitly convert to `int`. That last part makes the positional aggregate initialisers more dangerous than they look: `projectile_type` sits between `float ammo_usage` and `std::string sheet_name` in the member order, so a misordered brace-list can silently initialise a float from an enumerator.

**Fix:** Change it to `enum class projectile_type` and qualify the six use sites in weapon_consts.h. Six edits, and it removes an implicit-conversion hazard from every aggregate initialiser in both consts headers.

## `ArtAttack/WeaponRoller.cpp`

_2 findings: 2 medium_

#### 1. WeaponRoller::draw is a 57-line copy-paste of Weapon::draw for an 8-line colour tint

`ArtAttack/WeaponRoller.cpp:59-115` — **medium** · `duplication`

`WeaponRoller::draw` reproduces `Weapon::draw` (Weapon.cpp:36-82) line for line - same `get_draw_pos()`, same `calculate_sprite_origin(..., LEFT_CENTER)`, same invert_x/invert_y -> `SpriteEffects` ladder, same four `set_*` calls, same debug-nozzle block. The only difference is WeaponRoller.cpp:90-97, choosing `get_team_colour()` vs `colour_consts::WHITE`. `_shooting_this_update` was made a protected data member of `Weapon` (Weapon.h:50) solely to feed this. Both copies also carry the identical unreachable `invert_x` branches (see the dead-state finding). The override is declared `private` in WeaponRoller.h:28-29 while the base declaration is public (Weapon.h:31), and it drops the base's `bool debug = false` default argument - default arguments on virtuals bind statically, so the effective default depends on the static type of the pointer used.

**Fix:** Add `protected: virtual MattMath::Colour get_draw_tint() const { return colour_consts::WHITE; }` to `Weapon`, override that in `WeaponRoller`, and delete `WeaponRoller::draw` entirely. Keep override access identical to the base declaration and never redeclare or omit a default argument on a virtual.

#### 2. WeaponRoller re-implements Weapon::draw and update_movement_and_rotation instead of overriding a small hook

`ArtAttack/WeaponRoller.cpp:59-115` — **medium** · `design` · confidence: certain

`WeaponRoller::draw` (WeaponRoller.cpp:59-115, 57 lines) is a verbatim copy of `Weapon::draw` (Weapon.cpp:35-82, 48 lines) — same `get_draw_pos`/`RectangleF`, same `calculate_sprite_origin(..., LEFT_CENTER)`, same 12-line `SpriteEffects` flip ladder, same debug-nozzle block — with exactly one addition, lines 90-97:

```cpp
if (this->_shooting_this_update) DrawObject::set_colour(this->get_team_colour());
else                             DrawObject::set_colour(colour_consts::WHITE);
```

Similarly `WeaponRoller::update_movement_and_rotation` (:29-57) copies `Weapon::update_movement_and_rotation` (Weapon.cpp:274-306); only the two `set_rotation` values differ (`PI/4` / `3PI/4` vs `0` / `PI`) plus one `set_gun_player_aligned(true)`.

Separately, `Weapon::calculate_sprite_origin` (Weapon.cpp:88-101) is a byte-for-byte duplicate of `Drawer::calculate_sprite_origin` (Drawer.cpp:55-67), which already exists as a shared helper.

**Fix:** Keep one `Weapon::draw` and add a `virtual Colour get_tint_colour() const` hook that the roller overrides; add `virtual float get_aim_rotation(bool facing_right) const` for the rotation. Delete `Weapon::calculate_sprite_origin` and use `Drawer::calculate_sprite_origin` (or promote it to a free function in a `sprite_tools` header, since neither class needs to be a base for it).

## `ArtAttack/WeaponSprayer.cpp`

_1 finding: 1 medium_

#### 1. Five Weapon subclasses are pure data forwarding; the SoundEffectInstance details struct triples the same 8-string table

`ArtAttack/WeaponSprayer.cpp:8-27` — **medium** · `design` · confidence: certain

`WeaponSprayer.cpp:8-27`, `WeaponMister.cpp:8-27` and `WeaponBucket.cpp:8-27` are byte-identical 20-line ctors apart from the `DETAILS_*` / `DETAILS_RELATIVE_*` pair they forward; `WeaponSniper.cpp:9-27` and `WeaponRoller.cpp:9-27` are the same minus the relative details. Their headers (WeaponSprayer.h, WeaponMister.h, WeaponBucket.h, WeaponSniper.h, WeaponRoller.h) are identical 12-line ctor declarations with the class name swapped. `WeaponSniper::handle_shoot_sound` (WeaponSniper.cpp:28-35) and `WeaponBucket::handle_shoot_sound` (WeaponBucket.cpp:28-35) are byte-identical 7-line bodies.

Related data duplication: `SoundEffectInstanceWeaponDetails` (WeaponDetails.h:21-33) declares eight separately-named string fields `shoot_sound_name_a0..a3, b0..b3`, requiring the 36-line nested switch `get_sound_name` (WeaponDetails.cpp:55-91) to index them; `weapon_consts.h` then writes the same `{weapon}_{team}{index}` table out three times as literals (`SPRAYER_SOUND_DETAILS` :58-67, `ROLLER_SOUND_DETAILS` :102-111, `MISTER_SOUND_DETAILS` :136-145).

**Fix:** Delete all ten Weapon* files and construct weapons directly from a `wep_type -> {WeaponDetails, RelativeWeaponDetails*, sound-instance prefix}` table in `WeaponBuilder`. Where `handle_shoot_sound` genuinely differs (one-shot vs looped), make it a `bool looping_shoot_sound` flag in `WeaponDetails` rather than a subclass. Replace the eight named strings with `std::array<std::string, 8>` indexed by `team * 4 + index` — `get_sound_name` becomes one line — or drop the table entirely and build the name as `prefix + (team == A ? "_a" : "_b") + std::to_string(index)`, since the strings are already mechanical.

## `ArtAttack/wep_type.h`

_2 findings: 1 medium, 1 low_

#### 1. wep_type mixes implemented weapons, unimplemented weapons, a menu sentinel and an array bound in one enum

`ArtAttack/wep_type.h:4-18` — **medium** · `design`

```
enum class wep_type { SPRAYER, SNIPER, ROLLER, MISTER, BUCKET, RANDOM_PRIMARY,
                      GRENADE_STD, MINE, CURLING, WATER, NONE,
                      MAX_PRIM_WEP = RANDOM_PRIMARY };
```
Only five can be built (WeaponBuilder.cpp:18-37 throws for the rest), yet `GRENADE_STD` is passed as a live value at PlayerBuilder.cpp:55 and stored in `Player::_secondary_type` with no weapon object behind it. `RANDOM_PRIMARY` is not a weapon but a menu option, resolved at MainMenu.cpp:1499. `MAX_PRIM_WEP` is an aliased sentinel used as an *exclusive* bound - `rand() % static_cast<int>(wep_type::MAX_PRIM_WEP)` (MainMenu.cpp:1521, also :1527) yields 0-4, correct only because the name says MAX when it means COUNT; it is also written last, after `NONE = 10`, so it reads as the largest enumerator. Enum ordering is therefore load-bearing for the menu's random pick: inserting a weapon before RANDOM_PRIMARY silently changes it.

The same enum simultaneously means "class to instantiate", "menu option", "stored identity tag" and "array bound".

**Fix:** Split the concerns: an engine-side opaque `weapon_id` resolved by a registry for instantiation, and a separate game-side menu enum including RANDOM, with an explicit `constexpr std::array<weapon_id, N> SELECTABLE_PRIMARIES` for the random pick instead of enum arithmetic. Rename the sentinel `PRIMARY_WEAPON_COUNT` or move it out of the enum entirely.

#### 2. `wep`/`proj` truncations appear only where the full word would have been just as short

`ArtAttack/wep_type.h:1-18` — **low** · `naming` · confidence: certain

`wep_type.h` declares `enum class wep_type` with member `MAX_PRIM_WEP = RANDOM_PRIMARY` (line 17) - in a codebase whose classes are `Weapon`, `WeaponBucket`, `WeaponSprayer`, `WeaponBuilder`, `WeaponDetails`, and whose constants namespace is `weapon_consts`. So the type is `wep_type` but literally everything around it says `weapon`. The truncation spreads: `Weapon.h:141 get_wep_rotation_origin_offset` (defined `Weapon.cpp:157`), `Weapon.h:122 std::unique_ptr<ProjectileBuilder> _proj_builder` (a `ProjectileBuilder` in a file that spells `Projectile` out everywhere else), `WeaponDetails.h:45 projectile_type proj_type`, `Weapon.h:68 get_starting_vel_length`, `Weapon.h:174-175 add_player_vel / player_vel_amount`, `Weapon.h:91-92 get_draw_pos / get_nozzle_pos`, `Weapon.h:116 get_dt_ptr`, `MainMenu.cpp:1693,1712` widget suffixes `"_wep_icon"` / `"_wep_desc"`. `player_consts.h:48` has `DEFAULT_SECONDARY = wep_type::GRENADE_STD`.
Relatedly, `main_menu_consts` (MainMenu.h) contains both `WEAPON_DESCRIPTION_FONT` (line 26) and `SPRAYER_DESC`/`SNIPER_DESC`/... (84-89) plus `WEAPON_DESC_X_OFFSET` (73) - the same word abbreviated and not, three lines apart.

**Fix:** Global rename: `wep_type` -> `weapon_type` (and the file to `weapon_type.h`), `MAX_PRIM_WEP` -> `MAX_PRIMARY_WEAPON`, `_proj_builder` -> `_projectile_builder`, `proj_type` -> `projectile_type_id`, `get_starting_vel_length` -> `get_starting_velocity_length`, `add_player_vel` -> `add_player_velocity_mode`, `get_draw_pos`/`get_nozzle_pos` -> `..._position`, `GRENADE_STD` -> `GRENADE_STANDARD`, `*_DESC` -> `*_DESCRIPTION`. None of these truncations save a meaningful number of characters.

## `ArtAttack/CameraTools.h`

_1 finding: 1 low_

#### 1. CameraTools is a stateless class used as a namespace, heap-allocated per Level through a unique_ptr

`ArtAttack/CameraTools.h:21-32` — **low** · `design`

`CameraTools` has no data members. `calculate_camera` is a `const` non-static member that reads only its four parameters (CameraTools.cpp:8-72) — the only reason it is not already `static` is that it was not marked. `calculate_camera_scroll_border` already is static. Yet `Level` owns one on the heap: `std::unique_ptr<CameraTools> _camera_tools` (Level.h:113), constructed with `std::make_unique<CameraTools>()` (Level.cpp:56) purely to call a pure function at Level.cpp:80 and :196. Same shape as `CollisionTools` elsewhere in the codebase: a namespace written as a type, then given an owner because everything else in the file has one.

Its policy is also unconfigurable: the border ratios and pixel minimums are `constexpr` in `camera_consts` (CameraTools.h:9-17), so no game or level can supply its own follow behaviour.

**Fix:** `namespace camera_tools { MattMath::Camera calculate_camera(...); }` — the `camera_consts` namespace is already right there — and delete `Level::_camera_tools` and the make_unique. If a real camera abstraction is wanted, make it a `CameraController` owning target/bounds/translation/scale with injectable policy and explicit modes (Follow, FitRect, Lerp), which would also absorb the zoom logic currently inlined in `Level::update` (Level.cpp:150-159).

## `ArtAttack/dimension.h`

_2 findings: 2 low_

#### 1. dimension.h and direction.h are dead headers declaring maximally generic names at global scope, one of which collides with MattMath::direction

`ArtAttack/dimension.h:1-10` — **low** · `design`

Verified. dimension.h declares `enum class dimension { X, Y }` at global scope. It is included by nothing: grep for `dimension.h` and for `dimension::` across ArtAttack and MattMathTests returns zero hits. It exists only as ArtAttack.vcxproj:194. Same for direction.h (vcxproj:195): zero includers, and it declares a global `enum class direction` (anchor positions TOP_LEFT..BOTTOM_RIGHT) that collides by name with `MattMath::direction` (MattMath.h:12-23, the eight compass points returned by Vector2F::get_direction()).

That collision is a live hazard, not a stylistic one: Player.cpp writes unqualified `direction` under `using namespace MattMath;`, so the moment anyone includes direction.h in that TU the name becomes ambiguous or silently resolves to the wrong enum. For an engine that is meant to be reusable, leaking `dimension` and `direction` into the global namespace is a problem in its own right.

**Fix:** Delete dimension.h and its vcxproj entry. Either delete direction.h or rename its enum to `anchor` and move it into MattMath. Rename MattMath::direction to something that says what it is (cardinal_direction / direction_8), since Segment::get_direction() already returns a Vector2F under the same word. Also convert the three typedefs (Point2F h:33, AABB h:301, OBB h:1136) to `using`.

#### 2. Three headers are in the project and included by nothing at all

`ArtAttack/dimension.h:1-11` — **low** · `dead-code` · confidence: certain

I searched every .cpp and .h under ArtAttack/ for `#include "<name>"`. Three headers have zero includers: `dimension.h` (enum class dimension {X, Y}), `direction.h` (enum class direction {TOP_LEFT..BOTTOM_RIGHT}) and `direction_lock.h` (enum class direction_lock {LOCKED, UNLOCKED}). The enum names themselves also appear nowhere else — `grep -rn "\bdimension\b"` returns only the declaration. All three are listed in ArtAttack.vcxproj and .filters, so they show up in the Solution Explorer as if they were live engine types. `direction.h` is additionally a name collision trap: `MattMath.h:12` declares a *different* `direction`-flavoured concept, and a future `#include "direction.h"` would be ambiguous with it.

**Fix:** Delete dimension.h, direction.h and direction_lock.h and their vcxproj/filters entries.

## `ArtAttack/Drawer.cpp`

_1 finding: 1 low_

#### 1. calculate_sprite_origin silently folds NO_ROTATION into TOP_LEFT, and the rotat_origin field it exists for is never read anywhere

`ArtAttack/Drawer.cpp:55-67` — **low** · `correctness`

```cpp
switch (origin)
{
case rotation_origin::CENTER:      return Vector2F(size) / 2.0f;
case rotation_origin::LEFT_CENTER: return { 0.0f, size.y / 2.0f };
default: // rotation_origin::TOP_LEFT
    return Vector2F::ZERO;
}
```
`rotation_origin` has four enumerators — `CENTER, TOP_LEFT, LEFT_CENTER, NO_ROTATION` (rotation_origin.h:4-10). The `default:` swallows both `TOP_LEFT` and `NO_ROTATION` while the comment claims only `TOP_LEFT`, and because `default:` is present MSVC emits no C4061/C4062, so the unhandled enumerator is invisible under /W4. `NO_ROTATION` means "do not rotate this sprite", which an origin function cannot express at all; it is being answered with a pivot point.

And the enumerator is not theoretical: `projectile_details.h:11` declares `rotation_origin rotat_origin = rotation_origin::NO_ROTATION;` and `projectile_consts.h` sets it on five of six projectile types (lines 18, 31, 65, 78, 99). A grep across every .cpp finds **zero reads** of `rotat_origin` — the field is written by the content tables and never consumed, so all projectile sprite origins silently fall back to `DrawObject::_origin`'s default of ZERO.

`Weapon::calculate_sprite_origin` (Weapon.cpp:88-101) spells out `TOP_LEFT` explicitly and then adds a `default: return Vector2F::ZERO;` — same silent fold, arrived at by copy-paste drift.

**Fix:** Make the switch total and let the compiler police it — drop `default:`, list all four cases, and have `NO_ROTATION` assert or map explicitly. Then either wire `ProjectileDetails::rotat_origin` into the projectile draw path or delete the field and its six initialisers.

## `ArtAttack/level_mode.h`

_2 findings: 2 low_

#### 1. level_mode is stored on MenuLevelSettings but no code ever reads it — there is no rule-set abstraction

`ArtAttack/level_mode.h:4-10` — **low** · `design`

`enum class level_mode { STANDARD_MODE, TEAM_DEATHMATCH, DEATHMATCH, PRACTICE };` is stored on `MenuLevelSettings` (MenuLevelSettings.h:32) and set from the mode-select menu. I grepped the whole tree: `MenuLevelSettings::get_game_mode()` (MenuLevelSettings.h:18, .cpp:37) has **zero callers**. `LevelBuilder::build_level` (LevelBuilder.cpp:30-83) never asks for it and `Level` never sees it.

This is the symptom of the missing abstraction: there is exactly one hardcoded rule set (paint-area scoring on a 240s timer) spread across `Level::update`, `Level::get_level_end_info` and `LevelEndInfo`, so a second mode has nowhere to live.

I am **downgrading** this from the reported medium and correcting the reported consequence: one reviewer claimed "the player can pick Deathmatch and get a paint-area match". That is false — MainMenu.cpp:673-680 plays `ERROR_SOUND` and refuses to advance for the `"tdm"` and `"dm"` elements; only `"standard"` proceeds (MainMenu.cpp:663-671). The menu does not lie; the enum values are simply unimplemented placeholders.

**Fix:** Introduce a `GameMode` interface owned by the level (`on_start`, `update`, `is_finished`, `build_results`) and have `LevelBuilder` select the implementation from `settings.get_game_mode()`; `PaintCoverageMode` becomes one implementation. Until then, either remove the unimplemented enumerators or leave them — but delete the unreachable `get_game_mode` accessor so it stops looking wired up.

#### 2. Three game modes, four weapon types and three collision-object types exist in enums with no implementation anywhere

`ArtAttack/level_mode.h:4-10` — **low** · `dead-code` · confidence: certain

`level_mode.h` declares STANDARD_MODE / TEAM_DEATHMATCH / DEATHMATCH / PRACTICE. `MainMenu.cpp:667` unconditionally calls `set_game_mode(level_mode::STANDARD_MODE)`; `MenuLevelSettings::get_game_mode()` (MenuLevelSettings.cpp:37) is never called by anything, so the mode is written and never read; `MainMenuModeSelect::convert_mode_to_element` (MainMenu.cpp:744-758), which switches over all four, is itself never called. Similarly `wep_type::MINE`, `CURLING` and `WATER` (wep_type.h:12-14) have zero references outside the enum, and `WeaponBuilder::build_weapon` throws on anything but the five real weapons. `collision_object_type::POWER_UP`, `DEFAULT` and `NONE` (collision_object_type.h:26-28) are never produced by any object. `Player::_secondary_type` (Player.h:159) is set from `PlayerBuilder.cpp:55` to `wep_type::GRENADE_STD` and never read; `PlayerInputData::secondary_shoot` (PlayerInputData.h:16) is read off the gamepad right-shoulder at `PlayerInput.cpp:30` and consumed by nobody — the whole secondary-weapon feature is an unwired stub.

**Fix:** Trim the enums to what is implemented. Aspirational enum values are worse than a TODO because switch statements and if-chains grow branches for them (MainMenu.cpp:744-758) that can never execute, and readers cannot tell reachable from unreachable.

## `ArtAttack/LevelBuilder.h`

_1 finding: 1 low_

#### 1. Heap-allocated instance of an all-static class; build_level should be const and [[nodiscard]]

`ArtAttack/LevelBuilder.h:29` — **low** · `design`

