```cpp
std::unique_ptr<TeamColourTools> _team_colour = nullptr;          // LevelBuilder.h:29
this->_team_colour = std::make_unique<TeamColourTools>();         // LevelBuilder.cpp:23
const TeamColour team_colours = _team_colour->generate_random_team_colour();  // LevelBuilder.cpp:36
```
`TeamColourTools` (TeamColour.h) has no data members and all its functions are static. The `unique_ptr`, the `make_unique` and the `->` are ceremony around what could be `TeamColourTools::generate_random_team_colour()`.

Relatedly, `LevelBuilder::build_level` (LevelBuilder.h:26) is non-`const` although it mutates nothing — it reads pointer members and calls LevelObjectBuilder's `const` methods — and it is the module's principal factory with no `[[nodiscard]]`, so discarding its result silently builds and destroys an entire level.

**Fix:** Turn `TeamColourTools` into a namespace of free functions, delete the member and its allocation, and mark `build_level` `[[nodiscard]] ... const` (which requires raising the language standard — see that finding).

## `ArtAttack/LevelEndInfo.h`

_1 finding: 1 low_

#### 1. LevelEndInfo mixes a score record with UI string formatting and hardcoded English copy

`ArtAttack/LevelEndInfo.h:7-27` — **low** · `design`

A 3-field struct with 14 member functions. Alongside the legitimate score queries it carries presentation:
- `winning_team_string()` (LevelEndInfo.cpp:62-78) returns the literal UI copy `"Team A Wins!"` / `"Team B Wins!"` / `"Draw!"` — no localisation seam.
- `team_a_percentage_string()` and `team_b_percentage_string()` (:42-61) are byte-identical apart from which field they read, and format by `std::to_string` then `find('.')` then `substr` rather than with a formatting facility.

That is presentation policy living in the scoring record, with the two teams hardcoded into both the field names and the copy — the same two-team assumption flagged on `IPaintableGameObject`.

**Fix:** Reduce to a plain results record (per-team scores keyed by TeamId, plus `winner()`), and move string production into the results-menu UI where font, language and rounding policy live. Deduplicate the two percentage-string functions into one taking a `player_team`, formatted with `std::ostringstream << std::fixed << std::setprecision(1)`.

## `ArtAttack/menu_element.h`

_1 finding: 1 low_

#### 1. menu_element, both its converters, MainMenuTitle::_music, and two data-class accessors are entirely unreferenced

`ArtAttack/menu_element.h:1-32` — **low** · `dead-code`

`menu_element.h` defines a 22-value enum whose ONLY references in the codebase are `MainMenuModeSelect::convert_mode_to_element` (MainMenu.h:201, MainMenu.cpp:744-759) and `MainMenuPlayerCount::convert_player_count_to_element` (MainMenu.h:221, MainMenu.cpp:1010-1026) — both `private static` and both called from nowhere. This is the half-finished ID-based widget identity system the string comparisons should have used; it was started, abandoned, and left in the build. As written it is also a project-global enum hardcoding one specific game's screens (`MAIN_MENU_TEAM_DEATHMATCH`, `PAUSE_MENU_CONFIRMATION_NO`), which does not scale past this project. Other dead code in the same module: `MainMenuTitle::_music` (MainMenu.h:138), never assigned, only mentioned in the commented-out `//this->_music->Stop();` at MainMenu.cpp:55; `MenuData::get_menu_data()` (MenuData.h:14, MenuData.cpp:26-28) and `GameData::get_game_data()` (GameData.cpp:122), both of which just `return this` and have zero callers; and the unused local `Vector2F widget_size = this->get_widget_size();` at MainMenu.cpp:457.

## `ArtAttack/MovingObject.cpp`

_2 findings: 2 low_

#### 1. get_unit_velocity()/get_unit_dx() divide by zero for a stationary object — but both are dead code

`ArtAttack/MovingObject.cpp:52-55, 100-103` — **low** · `correctness`

```cpp
Vector2F MovingObject::get_unit_velocity() const { return this->_velocity.normalized(); }
Vector2F MovingObject::get_unit_dx() const       { return this->_dx.normalized(); }
```
`Vector2F::normalized()` (MattMath.cpp:1724-1728) has no zero guard:
```cpp
float length = this->length();
return Vector2F(this->x / length, this->y / length);
```
Both members default to `Vector2F::ZERO` (MovingObject.h:54-55), so calling either on an idle object yields `(NaN, NaN)`.

**Six reviewers overstated the consequence.** I grepped the whole tree: `get_unit_velocity`, `get_unit_dx`, `get_velocity_angle` and `get_dx_angle` have **zero callers** outside their own definitions. Nothing consumes the NaN, so the claims that it "silently poisons positions, collision directions and camera targets" are false. Downgraded to `low`: this is latent dead code, and the real defect is one layer down in `MattMath::Vector2F::normalized()`/`normalize()`, which other code does call (PlayerInput.cpp:99 guards it with a deadzone check; RectangleRotated::set_x_axis, MattMath.cpp:4361, validates afterwards).

Worth noting alongside: `FloatingPointModel=Fast` is set in all four ArtAttack configurations (ArtAttack.vcxproj:94, 116, 139, 165), which licenses the compiler to assume operands are not NaN — so if a caller is ever added, the failure will be silent rather than loud.

**Fix:** Delete the four unused accessors, or guard in `Vector2F::normalized()`/`normalize()`: if `length_squared()` is below an epsilon, return `Vector2F::ZERO`. Do not paper over it at the MovingObject layer only — `normalized()` has other callers.

#### 2. Unqualified atan2 can silently round-trip through double

`ArtAttack/MovingObject.cpp:62, 110` — **low** · `modern-cpp`

`return atan2(this->_velocity.y, this->_velocity.x);` (:62) and the same for `_dx` (:110). `atan2` is unqualified. `<cmath>` comes in via pch.h and MattMath.h, and MSVC also injects the C `<math.h>` names into the global namespace, so this resolves — but which overload wins is implementation-dependent. If `::atan2` (the `double(double,double)` C function) is selected, both float arguments are promoted to double, the computation happens in double, and the result is narrowed back to float.

Graded `low` in part because both functions are dead code (see the get_unit_velocity finding — `get_velocity_angle` and `get_dx_angle` have zero callers), so there is no measurable cost today.

**Fix:** Use `std::atan2(...)` and include `<cmath>` in MovingObject.cpp directly rather than relying on the precompiled header — or delete both functions, since nothing calls them.

## `ArtAttack/PauseMenu.h`

_1 finding: 1 low_

#### 1. A generic confirmation dialog is hardcoded to two questions via an enum declared in a protected section

`ArtAttack/PauseMenu.h:55-59, 85` — **low** · `api-design`

`PauseMenuPage` declares `protected: enum class confirmation_type { RESTART, QUIT };` (55-59) purely so `PauseMenuInitial` can name it when constructing `PauseMenuConfirmation` (PauseMenu.cpp:70-79). `PauseMenuConfirmation` then switches on it twice — once for the prompt text (`get_question_text`, PauseMenu.cpp:362-374) and once for the resulting action (233-245). A yes/no dialog is the most obviously reusable widget in any UI toolkit, and this one cannot ask a third question without editing an enum in a base class it does not belong to plus two switches. Worse, `PauseMenuConfirmation`'s constructor is PUBLIC but its parameter type is protected in the base (PauseMenu.h:85), so no code outside the hierarchy can name the type — a public API that no public caller can invoke. The name also collides conceptually with the unrelated `confirmation_state` (confirmation_state.h) used for per-player select state.

**Fix:** `ConfirmationPage(std::string question, std::function<void()> on_yes, std::function<void()> on_no)` — no enum, no switches, reusable by every screen. Move the type to namespace scope if it must stay, and rename one of the two to remove the `confirmation_type`/`confirmation_state` collision.

## `ArtAttack/PauseMenuData.h`

_1 finding: 1 low_

#### 1. Include guards: 10 files whose `#endif` comment names a different macro, one of them a typo, plus two spelling schemes

`ArtAttack/PauseMenuData.h:1-2` — **low** · `naming` · confidence: certain

I compared the `#ifndef` macro to the trailing `#endif // !X` comment in all 88 headers. Ten disagree, so the comment misdirects anyone matching up a long file:
  `PauseMenuData.h`: guard `PAUSEMENUDATA_H`, comment `PAUSEMENUDATE_H` ("DATE" typo)
  `GameStates.h`: `GAMESTATES_H` vs `GAMELEVEL_H` | `StateContext.h`: `STATECONTEXT_H` vs `STATECONTEXTGENERIC_H` | `MenuHighlight.h`: `MENUHIGHLIGHT_H` vs `MENUPAGEHIGHLIGHT_H` | `TeamColour.h`: `TEAMCOLOUR_H` vs `TEAM_COLOURS_H` | `IPaintableGameObject.h`: `IPAINTABLEGAMEOBJECT_H` vs `IPAINTABLE_H` | `LevelLoadedInfo.h`: `LEVELLOADEDINFO_H` vs `LEVEL_LOADED_INFO_H` | `PlayerInput.h`: `PLAYERINPUT_H` vs `PLAYER_INPUT_H` | `ResolutionManager.h`: `RESOLUTIONMANAGER_H` vs `RESOLUTION_H` | `ViewportManager.h`: `VIEWPORTMANAGER_H` vs `VIEWPORT_H`.
The guards themselves also use two schemes for PascalCase filenames - run-together (`LEVELLOADEDINFO_H`, `MENUPAGE_H`, `SOUNDBANKOBJECT_H`) and underscored (`LEVEL_END_INFO_H`, `MENU_PLAYER_SETTINGS_H`, `THREAD_POOL_H`, `WEAPON_DETAILS_H`) - so `PlayerInput.h` guards `PLAYERINPUT_H` while `PlayerInputData.h` guards `PLAYER_INPUT_H`, a name that by the other scheme belongs to `PlayerInput.h`. `BorderThickness.h` guards `BORDER_THICKNESS` with no `_H` at all, and `CollisionTools.h:1` is `#ifndef  COLLISION_TOOLS_H` with a double space.

**Fix:** Replace all of them with `#pragma once` - MSVC v145 supports it, it is what `Game.h`/`StepTimer.h`/`DeviceResources.h` effectively want, and it makes every one of these divergences unrepresentable. If guards must stay, generate them mechanically from the filename (underscored + `_H`) and drop the `#endif` comments.

## `ArtAttack/ResultsMenu.h`

_1 finding: 1 low_

#### 1. check_for_continue_input returns an int sentinel of -1 that the caller only tests for presence

`ArtAttack/ResultsMenu.h:104` — **low** · `api-design`

`static int ResultsMenuInitial::check_for_continue_input(const std::vector<ProcessedMenuInput>&)` (ResultsMenu.h:104, .cpp:263-274) returns the index of the first proceeding input or `-1`. The sole caller throws the index away: `int continue_input = this->check_for_continue_input(menu_inputs); if (continue_input != -1) { ... }` (ResultsMenu.cpp:58-60). The return type encodes information nobody wants, in a form the type system cannot check — nothing stops a future caller from subscripting with the sentinel. The same anti-pattern is `GameLevel::check_for_pause_input` (GameStates.cpp:345-357), whose result IS consumed as an index and feeds directly into the pause-menu out-of-bounds hazard.

**Fix:** Return `bool` here since only presence is used (`std::any_of` expresses the whole body in one line). Where the index genuinely is needed, return `std::optional<size_t>` so 'no input' cannot be accidentally used as a subscript.

## `ArtAttack/save/save_data.json`

_1 finding: 1 low_

#### 1. A file the program rewrites on every run is tracked in git, so the tree is dirty after each launch

`ArtAttack/save/save_data.json:1` — **low** · `robustness` · confidence: certain

git ls-files ArtAttack/save returns save_data.json and save_data.txt. Save.cpp opens SAVE_FILE_PATH (directory_consts.h:12, "./save/save_data.json") for writing and rewrites it whenever resolution or fullscreen changes, and Main.cpp calls load_save_file() at startup. Running the game therefore modifies a tracked file, so `git status` is dirty after every session and real changes get lost in the noise. save_data.txt appears to be a superseded copy of the same data that nothing reads. Related repo clutter, all verified tracked: 84 of the 103 files under ArtAttack/textures live in a directory literally named "old textures"; ArtAttack/fonts/"unuseed fonts" (sic) holds 20 unused .spritefont files; ArtAttack/levels/unused/ and ArtAttack/sounds/unused/ are tracked; and three third-party tool executables are committed - ArtAttack/textures/texconv.exe, ArtAttack/fonts/MakeSpriteFont.exe, ArtAttack/sounds/sound_bank_1/XWBTool.exe.

**Fix:** Ship a save_data.default.json as the tracked template, gitignore the live save, and have Save::load_save_file() copy the default on first run (it already has check_if_save_file_exists()). Delete the 'old textures', 'unuseed fonts', levels/unused and sounds/unused directories and the three committed EXEs - document the tool versions in a README instead. While you are in .gitattributes, note it is the untouched VS template (`* text=auto` with every other rule commented out); add explicit `*.dds binary`, `*.spritefont binary`, `*.xwb binary`, `*.exe binary` so line-ending normalisation can never be attempted on assets.

## `ArtAttack/save/save_data.txt`

_1 finding: 1 low_

#### 1. Orphan plaintext save file, plus a git-tracked save file the game rewrites at runtime and a silent resolution downgrade

`ArtAttack/save/save_data.txt:1-2` — **low** · `design` · confidence: certain

Three separate problems around the save data, all visible from the shipped files:

1. `ArtAttack/save/save_data.txt` contains `1920x1080\nfalse` — a plaintext predecessor of the JSON format. It is tracked in git (`git ls-files ArtAttack/save` returns both files) and **no code reads it**: the only save path in the codebase is `directory_consts::SAVE_FILE_PATH = "./save/save_data.json"` (ArtAttack/directory_consts.h:11), used at Save.cpp:35, :55, :60. Dead file.

2. `ArtAttack/save/save_data.json` is tracked *and* rewritten at runtime (`fopen(SAVE_FILE_PATH.c_str(), "wb")`, Save.cpp:60) by `set_resolution_and_save` / `set_full_screen_and_save`. Changing a setting dirties the working tree. Runtime-mutable state does not belong in version control.

3. `Save::convert_ivec_to_resolution` (Save.cpp:112-135) hard-codes four resolutions and its `else` returns `S_1280_720`. A save file holding any other resolution — including one written by a future build, or hand-edited — is silently downgraded to 1280×720 with no message and without correcting the file, so the value stays wrong until the user changes it in the options menu. The counterpart `convert_resolution_to_ivec` returns `{-1,-1}` for an unknown enum (Save.cpp:150), which would then be written into the JSON.

Minor, same file: Save.cpp:90 is `std::cout << ctime_s(buffer, sizeof(buffer), &legacy_start) << " Saving...\n";` — `ctime_s` returns an `errno_t`, so this prints `0 Saving...`, never a timestamp. (And `std::cout` in a `wWinMain` GUI app with no console goes nowhere regardless.)

**Fix:** Delete save_data.txt; add `ArtAttack/save/save_data.json` to .gitignore and generate it on first run (the code already does this via `check_if_save_file_exists`). Replace the resolution if/else ladder with a table lookup and log/repair an unrecognised value instead of silently substituting. Fix the ctime_s line to print `buffer`.

## `ArtAttack/screen_resolution.h`

_1 finding: 1 low_

#### 1. screen_resolution::MAX aliases a real enumerator rather than being a past-the-end sentinel

`ArtAttack/screen_resolution.h:4-11` — **low** · `design`

```
enum class screen_resolution
{
    S_1280_720, S_1920_1080, S_2560_1440, S_3840_2160,
    MAX = S_3840_2160
};
```
`MAX` is an alias for a valid value, and `MainMenu.cpp:572` relies on that (`int enum_max = static_cast<int>(screen_resolution::MAX);` then wraps inclusively). Adding a fifth resolution *after* MAX silently drops it from the menu cycle; adding it before silently changes MAX's meaning. There is also no fixed underlying type, and the enumerator names encode pixel dimensions that ResolutionManager.cpp:47-63 and :152-175 then hard-code a second and third time.

**Fix:** `enum class screen_resolution : std::uint8_t { S_1280_720, …, S_3840_2160, COUNT };` and iterate `< COUNT`, updating MainMenu.cpp:572 accordingly. Better still, drive the menu from the single constexpr resolution table proposed for ResolutionManager rather than from enum arithmetic.

## `ArtAttack/shape_type.h`

_1 finding: 1 low_

#### 1. shape_type::NONE is produced by no shape but is the only way to reach the dispatcher's throwing default branch

`ArtAttack/shape_type.h:4-12` — **low** · `robustness`

Grepping `shape_type::NONE` across ArtAttack/ and MattMathTests/ returns zero hits -- no `get_shape_type()` override ever returns it (RectangleF:725, Circle:3327, Triangle:3445, Quad:3797, RectangleRotated:4235 all return their concrete tags). Meanwhile `Shape::intersects(const Shape*)` (MattMath.cpp:133-134) handles it only via `default: throw std::invalid_argument("Shape type not recognized")`, thrown from inside the per-frame collision loop. So the enum advertises a "no shape" state that the dispatcher treats as fatal, reachable only through a programming mistake the type system could have prevented. `Segment` has no `shape_type` value at all despite being one of the seven `intersects` overloads.

**Fix:** Delete `shape_type::NONE`. If a null-shape concept is needed, model it as a null `Shape*`. Decide whether `Segment` is a `Shape` and make the enum consistent either way.

## `ArtAttack/sounds/unused/wave_bank_1.json`

_1 finding: 1 low_

#### 1. The unused wave_bank_1.json omits a field SoundBank::load_from_json reads unconditionally, and carries three fields nothing reads

`ArtAttack/sounds/unused/wave_bank_1.json:1-16` — **low** · `robustness` · confidence: certain

`SoundBank::load_from_json` (ArtAttack/SoundBank.cpp:163-166) reads three top-level members without checking existence:

    Value& waves = d["waves"];
    Value& sound_effect_instances = d["sound_effect_instances"];
    bool create_effect_instance_for_each_wave = d["create_effect_instance_for_each_wave"].GetBool();

The live bank ArtAttack/sounds/sound_bank_1.json:29 supplies `"create_effect_instance_for_each_wave": true`. The sibling file ArtAttack/sounds/unused/wave_bank_1.json does **not** contain that key at all — it has only `waves` and `sound_effect_instances`. Loading it would hit `operator[]` on a missing member, guarded only by the NDEBUG-disabled `RAPIDJSON_ASSERT`.

Conversely, wave_bank_1.json's instance entry declares `"volume": 1.0, "pitch": 0.0, "pan": 0.0` — `SoundBank::decode_sound_effect_instances_json` (SoundBank.cpp:123-146) reads only `name` and `wave`, so those three fields are silently ignored. The two files are the same schema drifted in two directions, and neither the reader nor the writer of the data knows which fields are contractual.

(I verified every sound name in the code against the live bank and they all resolve: the three `music_name` values `dragostea_din_tei` / `holly_dolly` / `caramelldansen` from the level files, `smash_countdown` and `slide_whistle_up` from Level.h:47-51, `WaterSplashing` from StructurePaintable.h:13, all five weapon shoot sounds from weapon_consts.h, the four player sounds from player_consts.h:56-62, `Top_Of_The_Morning`/`UI_Clicks01`/`UI_Clicks14`/`UI_Clicks17`/`UIerror2`/`Whoosh2` from MainMenu.h:74-82, and `party_horn`/`DrumRoll` from ResultsMenu.h:58-60. Only `Steamboat` is shipped and unreferenced.)

**Fix:** Delete `ArtAttack/sounds/unused/`. Make `load_from_json` use `HasMember`/`FindMember` with an explicit default for `create_effect_instance_for_each_wave`, and either honour `volume`/`pitch`/`pan` or remove them from the schema.

## `ArtAttack/StepTimer.h`

_1 finding: 1 low_

#### 1. StepTimer.h is an unmodified vendor template: unmarked, not self-contained, no interpolation alpha, fixed 100 ms clamp

`ArtAttack/StepTimer.h:1-13` — **low** · `design` · confidence: certain

I compared this file line-by-line against the stock DirectX 11 VS-template / DirectXTK `StepTimer.h`: the constructor member-init order, the `m_qpcMaxDelta = m_qpcFrequency.QuadPart / 10` comment, the 1/4-millisecond snap block at lines 120-130, the `TicksPerSecond = 10000000` constant and the whole `Tick()` template are all byte-identical to upstream. **There are no local edits.** That is itself worth reporting for three reasons:

1. Nothing marks it as third-party. It sits flat among the 193 first-party sources with no `// vendored from ...` banner and no version note, unlike `external/rapidjson`, so a future reader cannot tell it is not the author's code and will not know it can be re-synced upstream.
2. It is not self-contained: it uses `LARGE_INTEGER`, `QueryPerformanceFrequency` and `QueryPerformanceCounter` but includes only `<cmath>`, `<cstdint>`, `<exception>`. It compiles only because `pch.h:32` pulls in `<Windows.h>` first. A reusable engine header must not depend on the consumer's precompiled header.
3. Because it was never adapted, it lacks the two things this codebase actually needs: an accessor for the fixed-step remainder (`m_leftOverTicks / m_targetElapsedTicks`) to drive render interpolation, and a setter for `m_qpcMaxDelta`, which is a hard-coded private (line 40) that fixes the maximum catch-up burst at exactly 6 steps with no way to tune it.

Minor precision note: `SetTargetElapsedSeconds(1.0/60)` truncates to `m_targetElapsedTicks = 166666`, i.e. 60.00024 Hz rather than 60 — harmless here only because the snap window at line 127 (2500 ticks) is far larger than the error.

**Fix:** Move vendored files (`StepTimer.h`, `DeviceResources.h/.cpp`, `pch.h`) into an `external/` or `vendor/` folder with a provenance comment giving upstream URL and version, matching how `external/rapidjson` is already handled. Add `#include <Windows.h>` (or a minimal `<profileapi.h>`) to `StepTimer.h` so it stands alone, then add `double GetInterpolationAlpha() const` and `void SetMaxDelta(double seconds)` as clearly-marked local extensions.

## `ArtAttack/Visual.h`

_1 finding: 1 low_

#### 1. Visual and MTexture are the same class written twice, and Visual is final yet exposes a protected member

`ArtAttack/Visual.h:8-41` — **low** · `duplication`

`Visual` (Visual.h:8-41) and `MTexture` (Mh.h) have the same shape: both are `IGameObject` + `TextureObject` plus a `RectangleF _rectangle`; both implement `update()` as a no-op; both implement the two `draw` overloads by forwarding to `TextureObject::draw(batch, _rectangle, camera)`; both implement `is_visible_in_viewport` as `_rectangle.intersects(view)`. `MTexture` adds only a name and a hidden flag.

Smaller contradiction in the same header: `class Visual final` (line 8) declares `_rectangle` as `protected` (line 40). Nothing can derive from it, so protected is meaningless — it should be private.

**Fix:** One `SpriteInstance` type — `{ Sprite visual; RectangleF bounds; float rotation; }` — used by both level content and UI, with the UI layer adding name/visibility by *wrapping* it rather than re-deriving. Make `_rectangle` private in the meantime.
